stories.headline: ru-wiki: temp user swaps "Белоруссия" for "Беларусь" in Nazi SS official's bio
stories.summary: This is a naming-convention edit on a historical article, not a real-world event. The ru-wiki biography of Karl Zenner, the SS and Police Leader in Belarus in 1941–42, got three edits in about a minute. A temporary account (~2026-56034-98) changed "Белоруссия" to "Беларусь" twice: once in the infobox and once in the body (rev 155687030). The edit summary says "Белоруссия" sounds offensive, "as a reminder of the colonial past". EyeBot automatically reverted the change because it scored as likely vandalism. Patroller Beonus then undid the bot's revert (rev 155687057), so the "Беларусь" wording is what the page currently says. The same temporary account also edited another bio (Бабосов, Евгений Михайлович) seconds later with no edit summary. I didn't read that diff, but it may be the same terminology change. On ru-wiki the Белоруссия/Беларусь wording is a long-running style dispute, so the change could still be reverted. One undo of a bot doesn't make this an edit war between people. I didn't read EyeBot's revert diff; I'm relying on its edit summary for what it did.

stories.headline: West Virginia vandalism has stopped; no new edits since admin's last revert
stories.summary: Nothing has happened since our last brief. The graph shows no edits to English Wikipedia's West Virginia article, or to the linked Ibrahim Isaac Sidrak page, after Zzuuzz's revert at ts 1792445878. The four reverts the Scout flagged are the same churn we already covered. Throwaway temporary accounts kept re-adding one +160-byte block of sexual slurs, and patrollers 45dogs and administrator Zzuuzz removed it within seconds. I read Zzuuzz's rev 1381076764. It brings back the nickname "Mountain State," the real motto and the lead paragraph, and removes the incest-themed lines and a stray Green Day link. It's one-way vandalism cleanup on one English page, not a two-sided dispute, and nothing points to a real-world event. The quiet period suggests the page was protected or the accounts were blocked, but I haven't checked either. I recommend merging this into the existing West Virginia vandalism story and closing it.

stories.headline: Serie A: it.wiki records Fiorentina 1-3 Como; no new activity since last brief
stories.summary: This is the same story as the earlier routine brief on it.wiki's "Serie A 2026-2027" page, and nothing has changed since then. The graph still shows five small edits by four temporary accounts on 18 Oct 2026, with no reverts. I re-read rev 152957251, which replaces the Fiorentina–Como kickoff time ("15:00") with a 1-3 result in the "Girone di andata" fixture list. I tried to re-check the other four diffs (152956574, 152957155, 152957171, 152957183), but none of them loaded. So the table and infobox details in the earlier brief (Como up to 14 points and 4th place, the infobox going to 66 matches and 192 goals) were not checked again this time. Rev 152956574 ("Primati stagionali", +10) came about 50 minutes before the score edit and may be about a different match. There are no reverts, editors on other pages, or other-language pages involved, so this looks like routine season-page upkeep, not vandalism. The score comes only from the edits; no outside source or other-language page confirms it.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un enwiki: 'current event' tag pulled pending reliable sources; death still unverified
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the existing Kim Jong Un death-rumor story, not a new event. The scout's "four editors, 729 churn" covers enwiki housekeeping since the last brief. The one substantive move: TheAwesomeHwyh removed the {{current event}} tag that Augmented Seventh had added minutes earlier, with the summary "removed current event tag until reliable sources pick this up" (rev 1381094826). The graph marks this as a revert, but it undoes the tag, not a death claim, and it is not an edit war. The bulk of the churn is Super Goku V's -679 edit (rev 1381094264). It renamed a duplicated "Early life" heading back to "Personal life" and removed a repeated sentence about his birth date (1982 per Pyongyang, 1983 per South Korean intelligence). That edit is structural and has nothing to do with the rumor. Extended-confirmed protection (Rsjaffe) stays in place. Experienced enwiki editors are now saying outright that reliable outlets have not picked up the rumor. As far as the graph shows, no death claim stands on enwiki, eswiki or fawiki, and the rumor (social media and tabloids: brain hemorrhage, 19 October) remains unverified.

stories.headline: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary gets routine upkeep on Wikipedia after release
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia article on "You Can See Everything" is getting maintenance edits, not new content. It is a 2026 A24 documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The recent edits I read add nothing newsworthy. One changes dates to the month-day-year format using a script, one renames references, one adds a link to Billy Evans' article, and one bumps the Rotten Tomatoes review count from 134 to 135 (still 98%; Metacritic 97). The roughly 552 bytes of churn the Scout flagged come from these formatting changes, not from a new article or new information. The film itself is not new to the wiki: the article already describes a surprise Telluride premiere (September 7, 2026) and an October theatrical opening, citing a Variety box-office preview dated October 14 that projected an $8M opening. The film is in release, but there is no fresh event here, no reverts and no edit war. I only checked the English page, not other language versions.

stories.headline: Raphaël Arnault fr-wiki: no new activity; unsourced-smear revert war stays contained
stories.summary: This is a recheck of the tracked dispute, and nothing new has happened. The graph still holds the same 8 edits on fr:Raphaël Arnault. The last one is HaguardDuNord's revert (rev 240557967), and no edits came after it. I read the latest addition (rev 240557856). The temporary account ~2026-56241-09 added text to the lead calling the far-left MP "triple fiché S" (on a French state-security watchlist three times). It also says his parliamentary aide Jacques-Élie Favrot was involved in a "lynching" that killed "the patriot Quentin Deranque", and that he is close to a suspect in an arson attack on Limoges town hall. None of it cites a source. The revert removed exactly that text. Gyrostat had already reverted the same insertion three times, calling it POV-pushing. A search of all pages in the graph turns up nothing on Deranque, Favrot, Limoges or other-language versions of the Arnault article, so nothing backs up the claimed incidents. This looks like one account pushing possibly defamatory claims about a living person, and the main editors stopped it each time. It's not evidence of a real-world event. A real incident could still be behind the claims, but so far the graph doesn't show one.

stories.headline: James L. Easton bio gets infobox and succession-box update; no news
stories.summary: I read three of the four edits; all are routine changes to the article's structure. A temporary-account editor (~2026-54850-06) switched the infobox to an officeholder template. It now lists Easton as IOC Vice-President from 2002 to 2006 and as World Archery president from 1989 to 2005, between Francesco Gnecchi-Ruscone and Uğur Erdener (rev 1381070821). The same editor also added a matching succession box (rev 1381074968). Davemck then removed duplicate infobox parameters (rev 1381075053), and Itzcuauhtli11 did the same kind of cleanup with a script (rev 1381075334, not read). Nothing adds dates of death, new appointments or recent events. The editor's comment says Easton "is the President," but the terms they entered are historical and closed. There are no reverts, no other languages and no linked pages, so I see no sign of a real-world event.

stories.headline: Ramayana: Part 1 page: temp-account cleanup rolled back as vandalism; no news signal
stories.summary: I found no sign of real-world news here. This is upkeep on an upcoming film's English Wikipedia article. Over about 50 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-55775-56) made 9 small edits. It removed what it called duplicate references, cutting an NDTV citation from the Origins section (rev 1380880476). It also reworked the soundtrack infobox (rev 1380882217): it renamed the album to "Ramayana: Part 1", changed the recording date from 2025 to 2024, added studios in Chennai and Santa Monica, and removed the T-Series label and Namit Malhotra as producer. In a later edit summary the same account says it added a label back. Separately, Onedirectiongod619 removed a wikilink on "crore" in the budget line (rev 1380884665), a 4-byte formatting change. Vestrian24Bio then restored the earlier revision by Mattgelo, labelling it "Rvv" (revert vandalism), which undid the whole sequence (rev 1380886487). The restored version carries an {{AI-generated}} cleanup tag pointing to a case on Wikipedia's AI-content noticeboard. Every edit was about formatting, sources or soundtrack credits. No edit adds a release date, box-office figure or other news, and there is no back-and-forth reverting, no activity in other languages and no outside editors. The infobox changes are unsourced, so they don't count as evidence of a real update to the soundtrack.

stories.headline: Bournemouth season page logs first league win of 2026–27, a 2–0, moving them up to 15th
stories.summary: On about 18 October 2026, a few registered editors and one temporary account made routine post-match updates to the English Wikipedia page for AFC Bournemouth's 2026–27 season. There were no reverts. The edits show Bournemouth's first Premier League win of the season, in their seventh league match: the record changes from W0 D3 L3 to W1 D3 L3, and goals scored rise from 7 to 9 while goals conceded stay at 13. That points to a 2–0 win. The squad statistics credit one goal each to Evanilson (43rd minute) and Marcus Tavernier, which makes Tavernier the top scorer in the league and all competitions (4). The infobox league position changes from 19th to 15th. Later edits are small fixes: a booking minute, a link to Sunderland, a kick-off time changed from 15:00 to 17:30 GMT, and an average-attendance figure added by an anonymous editor. I couldn't confirm who Bournemouth played or the exact date from the diffs I read. This is ordinary sports-page upkeep with no wider news significance.

stories.headline: Luke McCaffrey page: self-insertion vandalism reverted, no new activity since
stories.summary: I rechecked this story and found no new edits in any language since the last brief. All activity is still the same 3 edits to the English article on Commanders wide receiver Luke McCaffrey. HunterStrayer changed the lead to say McCaffrey switched to wide receiver "with Hunter Strayer at Rice", which is the editor adding his own name (rev 1381105039). Rencoolguy reverted it within about a minute (rev 1381105236). ParallelX made a one-character comma fix in the personal-life section (rev 1381106098). No edit mentions a trade, injury or roster move, and no other-language versions moved, so this shows no real-world event. It is minor vandalism that has already been fixed, and this story duplicates the tracked one.

stories.headline: Patrol cluster quiet: no new edits since Derderian cleanup; nothing to report
stories.summary: Nothing has changed in this cluster since the last brief. A graph query for edits after the last recorded revision (ts 1792462663) on the six English pages found none. The latest Derderian revision I read, rev 1381111035, only rewrites the lead: Derderian is "Primate of the Western Diocese of the Armenian Church of North America since 2003", cited to a 2003 LA Times archive story. That cements the paid-editing/LLM trim; it doesn't report a new event. The Warren BLP attack is still reverted, and Hannah Pearl Davis, Cheezels, Otra Nota and Emma Maembong have all stopped moving. It's English only, among the same few patrollers (CreativeLibrary460, EndTheWikiEditor, ESkog), with no real-world event behind it. This agrees with the scout's note about routine patrol cleanup. Only risk: the temp accounts could come back to the Warren page.

stories.headline: pt-wiki Notre Dame list: newcomer blanks page a third time to plead for talk; reverted
stories.summary: There is no news here. On the pt-wiki page "Colégio Notre Dame", the same new account, O cara legal01, blanked the list of Brazilian Notre Dame schools for a third time (rev 73250782). In its place they wrote a message on the article itself. It accuses the people reverting them of using "multiple accounts, bots" and says they study at the school and know a lot about it ("Eu sei muito sobre essa escola, estudo lá"). It ends by asking for a reply. Little Sunshine reverted it within about 30 seconds (rev 73250793), and the list is back. The scout's note is wrong in two ways. These are not new routine edits: they continue the same dispute as the earlier promo overwrite (73250672) and blanking (73250722). And "no reverts" is also wrong: three edits are reverts (73250693, 73250730, 73250793), but they show up only in the edit comments, not in the graph's revert field. This is one student pushing content about their own school, which counts as low-level disruption, against two established editors. It is not a two-sided edit war, and nothing has happened in the real world. If the user keeps going, the likely next step is a warning or a block, not anything worth reporting.

stories.headline: Victor Marx recordings paragraph unchanged; linked pages show only vandalism and copyedits
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The only real-world content in this cluster is still Bovidbeauty's paragraph on Victor Marx (rev 1381210360). It says 2026 recordings resurfaced in which Marx describes pushing his wife into a door, throwing his toddler son across a room, and says God gave him "a gift for violence". The paragraph cites a single International Business Times UK article from 1 October 2026 that calls him the Colorado GOP nominee. No edits have touched the Marx page since patrollers reverted a temporary account's test edit. There is still no second source and no coverage in other languages. On the other pages: Will Ross Gjede again wrote personal names into the Disinformation lead (rev 1381222158), and the graph shows no revert of it yet. The Confectionery store redirect to "Feces" (rev 1381221358) was reverted. The only edit since then is HouseBlaster removing the English-variety suggestion from the improvement banner, since the article now uses British English (rev 1381223110), which is routine. These pages are linked only through shared patrollers (Dr vulpes, MarioWonderExpert). Still unclear: whether the Marx story will spread to other editors or sources.

stories.headline: Minor vandalism on Italian Wikipedia's Vita nuova article, reverted within minutes
stories.summary: A single temporary account (~2026-56054-61) made two edits to the itwiki article on Dante's Vita nuova. The first put gibberish into the opening sentence ("la prpoppi ciao dante ama boh opera..."). The second swapped the displayed title of the sonnet "Tanto gentile e tanto onesta pare" for a mock version ("...non sembra"). The bot Moderatore Automatico undid the first edit within seconds, and user Yiyi undid the second within about 90 seconds. The graph's revert flag is false for both, but the edit comments ("Annullata la modifica...") show they were reverts. This looks like schoolroom-style vandalism with no link to any real-world event. The page now matches its earlier version, and nothing has happened in other languages.

stories.headline: Mozambican FRELIMO politician Ana Rita Sithole reported dead on 18 October
stories.summary: Wikipedia editors have updated the page on Ana Rita Sithole, a Mozambican FRELIMO MP and 2023 co-president of the ACP-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly, to say she has died. Her death date is given as 18 October 2026. The news first showed up in a Deaths in 2026 entry (rev 1380898167). It cites a Portuguese-language article from Mozambique's O País titled "Morreu Ana Rita Sithole, vítima de doença", which says she died of an illness. Within minutes, three separate editors updated her biography: a category swap to 2026 deaths, a change from present to past tense, and a +350 rewrite adding the death date and a source (rev 1380901228). There were no reverts or signs of vandalism, and no other-language pages moved. Two things are uncertain. The source rests on one outlet, and I saw only its headline as quoted, not the article itself. The records also disagree on her years as an MP: the death list says 1994–2004, while the article says she served from 2000. This looks like a routine obituary update with low wider news value.

stories.headline: France unrest: en infobox now shows 1 dead, 500+ police hurt and ~1,800 arrests after 17 Oct
stories.summary: This update answers the open question from the last brief: the infobox on enwiki "2026 French student protests" has been brought up to date. The Egyptian Journalist1234 (rev 1380906507) replaced the 1 October figures with numbers cited to Reuters and AP, both dated 18 October. One demonstrator died of cardiac arrest during the Paris protests, and police gave no further details. More than 500 police, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, according to the interior minister. Nearly 1,800 people were arrested across France according to Reuters; AP says at least 1,800. These figures are lower than the ones in the reverted duplicate copy (600+ injured, 2,000+ arrests), and I am using the version that is live now. The same edit also removed the older numbers: 1,949 arrests on 1 October, and the Justice Ministry figure of 6,100 people taken into custody since the protests began. The title of the cited AP story says Macron is to address the nation after riots and looting. That comes from a headline and has not been confirmed independently here. The other two edits were cosmetic: Brotherxaoop reformatted the same figures (rev 1380907315) and RickMorais fixed a typo (rev 1380906197). There were no reverts, three editors acted independently, and none of these edits touched the page title or the requested move.

stories.headline: One admin's cleanup patrol links three unrelated pages; no news event
stories.summary: The only thing tying these three pages together is one experienced editor, Drmies, doing routine maintenance across all of them. On Obradoiro CAB (a Spanish basketball club), Drmies made three reverts. The first undid 23 edits by WikiCreative123 as "huge amount of unverified content, test edits." The last undid a single +7,985-byte re-addition by the same user. That re-added text expands the infobox, adds unsourced fan nicknames and season write-ups, and claims the club was relegated in May 2024 and promoted back to Liga ACB on 8 May 2026 as Primera FEB champions. Those results might be true, but the edits cite no source and we have not checked them. On John Burroughs School, Drmies trimmed the alumni and faculty lists after another editor added names. On Nick Mowbray, Drmies reverted an unsourced addition naming a child. This is one editor reverting another, not a back-and-forth edit war, and there is no sign of a real-world event.

stories.headline: Strawberry Prince ja page: same vandal blanks article, admin-side revert restores it
stories.summary: This is more of the same activity on the Japanese Wikipedia article すとぷり (Strawberry Prince), not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-55856-14 has already been flagged for sexual spam and an unsourced "dissolved" claim. In rev 111431094 (−4,030 bytes) it removed the infobox, the activity overview and the remaining four-member table, and replaced them with repeated sexual slang ("パコモリ…"). Its edit summary falsely called this a "fix for the members' graduation". About four minutes later, registered editor 大夫将監 reverted both of the account's recent edits with TwinkleGlobal (rev 111431116, +4,033), which restored the page. Just before that, in rev 111431006, 大夫将監 took the "【卒業】" (graduated) tags off the names of ななもり。(Nanamori) and さとみ (Satomi). They now appear only in the former-members table that editor created earlier. The real-world fact behind all this, the announced graduation of Nanamori and Satomi, is unchanged, and nothing I read adds a source for it. This is one account's vandalism being cleaned up by one patroller, not an edit war.

stories.headline: Photo-swap vandalism on fr-wiki Florentin bio reverted a third time; page now restored
stories.summary: Update to s_29ddc4f0. The third infobox image swap on the fr-wiki bio of Jordan Florentin, a far-right publicist, came from temporary account ~2026-56031-17 (rev 240548412, comment "les modo de wikipédia sont pas drôles"). It replaced the photo with "Jordanfloflo.jpg". About 50 seconds later R3L3ct3ur49 reverted it (rev 240548433), putting back the original image file ("Jordan Da Rocha à la manifestation du 22 novembre 2025 à Paris…"). So the swap is no longer live, which corrects the previous brief. The pattern is unchanged: three accounts swapped the photo with activist taunts in the edit comments, and three different patrollers (Goodshort, GF38storic, R3L3ct3ur49) reverted them. No edits have been logged since the last revert, and there is no sign of a real-world event behind the activity. Still open: whether the page gets protected, what Jordanfloflo.jpg shows, and whether the restored file is correctly labelled, since its filename names "Jordan Da Rocha".

stories.headline: Amici 26 itwiki page: no new activity since last brief; still routine
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened on this story since the last brief. The Italian Wikipedia page for the 26th edition of "Amici di Maria De Filippi" still has 11 edits from 4 editors: Dominikcapuan and three temporary accounts. All edits are small (-2 to +27 bytes), and none is a revert. No other pages or languages are involved. A graph query found no edits after rev 152955945. I re-read the two most recent content edits. One adds the song title "A noi non serve far l'amore" to the episode table (152955879). The other changes "Jed ottiene il banco" to "I Jed ottiengono il banco" (152955945), treating Jed as a group; the verb is misspelled. This is viewers logging details of an episode while it airs or just after, with no sign of vandalism, an edit war or real-world news. This story duplicates the existing routine story on the same page and could be merged into it.

stories.headline: Temporary account swaps "monofisismo" for "miafisismo" on es.wiki pages; bot reverts
stories.summary: Over about 3.5 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-55841-36) made three unexplained edits on Spanish Wikipedia: Justiniano I, Makuria and Monotelismo. In the two diffs I read, it replaced "monofisismo/monofisitas" with "miafisismo/miafisitas", the term Oriental Orthodox churches prefer. Some instances were left unchanged. On Monotelismo, the edit also deleted a sentence about Sergius's talks with Cyrus of Phasis, which accounts for the -305 bytes. The anti-vandalism bot SeroBOT reverted both pages within seconds, restoring the previous versions. Only one human was involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. The scout's "4 editors / large expansion" reading is wrong: the large delta was a deletion, and two of the four edits are bot reverts. This looks like a one-person terminology change, not vandalism in the usual sense. I didn't read the Makuria diff, but its -4 delta fits the same swap.

stories.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI article: routine expansion of development section, no news event
stories.summary: Seven edits by four registered editors on the enwiki Grand Theft Auto VI article over about an hour. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors. The largest change (+1,892 bytes, Riarutaimu) adds a "Gameplay" subsection under Development. It is built from GamesRadar+ pieces dated August–October 2026 about Rockstar balancing realism, including a cut grocery- and fridge-restocking mechanic. The other edits are small tidy-ups: Riarutaimu trimming the Technology/NPC paragraph, a link added to "NPC" under MOS:ACRONYM (Tbhotch), copyedits and links in Gameplay (SleepyRedHair), and category formatting (OrbitalVoid49). Nothing new gets announced: no release date change, delay or sales figure, and the sources cited are weeks old. This looks like normal upkeep of a high-interest article, not a reaction to breaking news. I didn't check other-language versions of the article.

stories.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: 'Libro de los muertos' vandalism still live after bot revert
stories.summary: This is still school-style vandalism with no news behind it. I disagree with part of the scout's note, though: these edits are not routine, and there were reverts. Since the last brief, temporary account ~2026-56376-29 added "beltran y maria son novios" ("Beltrán and María are a couple") to the start of the article (rev 175929927). Automoderador reverted it 8 seconds later (rev 175929928). But that revert went back to ~2026-56459-05's version, which already had the earlier fake credit "(creado por Lucas Agosti)" ("created by Lucas Agosti") in the opening sentence. The latest edit, rev 175929939 by ~2026-56159-87, only adds a double space, and the Lucas Agosti text survives it. So as of the last edit in the graph, the false claim is still on the page. The account behind it, ~2026-56459-05, also tried changing the title to "Libro de los vivos" ("Book of the Living") and the date to 2050 (rev 175929905). Several temporary accounts are making similar edits within minutes of each other, which suggests one group, possibly classmates. The Darwin and Saif al-Adel pages haven't changed since the prior brief. Next step: someone needs to remove the Lucas Agosti text by hand.

stories.headline: Joke vandalism on es.wiki page for Spanish village Mazarulleque; bot put it back
stories.summary: No real-world event here. This is small-scale vandalism on the Spanish Wikipedia article for Mazarulleque, a village in Cuenca. Temporary account ~2026-55804-97 added two nonsense lines (rev 175914329, +135 bytes): a border with "El Lago Del Rats" and a claim that "En 2024 El Rats se proclamó como el diputado de la textura" ("In 2024 El Rats proclaimed himself the deputy of texture"). Two minutes later a second temporary account (rev 175914343, -3230) removed that nonsense but also deleted the long, sourced 19th-century Madoz gazetteer quote. The anti-vandalism bot Automoderador treated that large removal as blanking and reverted it (rev 175914344), which restored the Madoz text but also put the "El Rats" vandalism back. The 6595-byte churn the scout flagged is just this delete-and-restore cycle. As of the last edit we have, the nonsense seems to still be on the page. It's unclear whether the second editor was trying to clean up or was blanking too.

stories.headline: Lamine Yamal it.wiki: third vandal name-swap reverted; stats update stands
stories.summary: Since the last brief there is one new act of vandalism on Italian Wikipedia's Lamine Yamal article. Temporary account ~2026-55923-30 changed the infobox name a third time, this time to an insult ("Zio mino compare cornuto"), in rev 152988489. Amirzat reverted it within about 50 seconds (rev 152988497). That makes three reverted edits from one throwaway account. It's a minor vandalism spree, not an edit war. Contrary to the scout's note, there were reverts. Popsi's stats update (rev 152988462) is still in place. Stats now run to 18 October 2026, and his 2026-27 numbers are 9 league appearances and 8 goals, and 2 Champions League appearances and 1 goal. Across all competitions this season that's 11 appearances and 9 goals, and his Barcelona totals are 162 appearances and 58 goals. This is consistent with routine stats upkeep after recent matches. No other pages or languages changed, so there's no sign of a wider news event.

stories.headline: Italian 'Tower of Hanoi' article hit by temp-account vandalism; reverted twice
stories.summary: This is schoolboy-style vandalism on it.wikipedia's 'Torre di Hanoi' article. It does not point to any real-world event. Temporary account ~2026-56340-28 made four edits in about 8 minutes. It swapped the intro's 'Torre di Lucas' attribution for the name-like string '(abdel halal)' (rev 153000256), then renamed the subject 'Torre di Amine fatah'. It finally blanked the opening paragraph that explains the puzzle's rules (rev 153000376, −555 bytes). Experienced editor Torsolo restored an earlier version once. Editor .mau. then undid all of the temp account's changes (rev 153000493), and the article's original intro is back. The scout's note missed something: the graph's revert flag is false on every edit, but the edit comments ('Ripristinata', 'Annullate le modifiche') show two reverts. Nobody else is involved and nothing changed in other languages. Unless the account comes back, no follow-up is needed.

stories.headline: NZ Antarctic Heritage Trust page: promotional rewrite reverted; no news event
stories.summary: Over about 80 minutes, new account PenguinExplorer97 (3 edits total) rewrote the en-wiki article on the Antarctic Heritage Trust (New Zealand) in the organisation's own marketing voice. The edits added "vision of inspiring explorers" wording, trademarked programme names (Inspiring Explorers Education™, Young Inspiring Explorers™), claims like "world's largest cold-climate conservation project", a mention of a new phase of conservation work at Cape Adare, and citations only to nzaht.org. The rewrite also removed the charity-register citation and the sourced 2013 CNN item about the photo negatives found at the huts. MaxLorax made one small bolding fix. Viewmont Viking then undid all four revisions (−2707 bytes), citing "Unsourced, poorly sourced, promotional, MOS". This was a single revert, not an edit war. The pattern looks like a likely conflict-of-interest or PR update, not a reaction to news. The Cape Adare programme comes only from the Trust's own site and has no independent confirmation in the edits.

stories.headline: Noni Madueke page updated after league goal; vandalism and formatting tiff reverted
stories.summary: Edits to Noni Madueke's English Wikipedia page look like routine matchday upkeep, plus one act of vandalism and a small formatting dispute. An anonymous editor raised his league goals for the current club from 3 to 4 ("madueke scored"). Regular editor Arsenal1973 then raised his appearances from 29 to 30 and changed the club-stats timestamp to 18 October 2026. Together these suggest he played and probably scored in a league match that day. The same anonymous editor later changed his international goals from 1 to 1,000,000, which is clear vandalism, and Mattythewhite reverted it. Separately, another anonymous editor wrapped his full name in a {{nowrap}} template. GiantSnowman undid that ("not needed"), and the anonymous editor put it back, which is the start of a small edit war over formatting only. The edits contain no claims of a transfer or injury. I haven't independently confirmed the goal: no source is cited, and the stats edits don't name the opponent.

stories.headline: Oberon High School vandalism: Neriah reverts fake principal, then a new account hits the motto
stories.summary: The student vandalism on the English Wikipedia article for Oberon High School is still going. Patroller Neriah undid Yubbleslvl's quieter edits (rev 1381168399), which removed the fake principal "Adrian Herbert" and the "[[9 Seal Street]]" address and put Warren Dawson back. About four minutes later, a temporary account not seen before, ~2026-56187-41, made rev 1381168791 with no edit summary. Its +284 size is mostly the infobox spacing being widened, but it also replaces the real motto, "Shape your future, go one better", with a taunt about "the two wings of the herberts" coming to the school. That repeats the "Herbert" name Yubbleslvl used, so it is very likely the same person or group of friends switching accounts. The graph shows no edits after this one, so the fake motto is probably live right now. This is the fifth round of a schoolyard prank, not a real-world event. Correcting the scout: the pattern is sustained account-hopping with repeated reverts, not just three editors and four edits.

stories.headline: Ukrainian Wikipedia adds article on Bolsonaro's 2003 'rape' remark; one vandal edit reverted
stories.summary: On Ukrainian Wikipedia, NachtReisender created an 8.8 KB article on Jair Bolsonaro's 2003 remark to deputy Maria do Rosário, which he repeated in 2014: "She doesn't deserve to be raped" (Portuguese: "Não merece ser estuprada"). The article covers the 11 Nov 2003 argument in the Chamber of Deputies, quotes the exchange, and covers the incitement-to-rape case that followed. It cites a July 2023 Poder360 report that the case was archived. The same editor then added three categories. A temporary account deleted "не" ("not") from the opening line, which flipped the quote to "She deserves to be raped". Its edit summary was just "clarification". Renvoy reverted it about 70 seconds later. This is vandalism of one sentence, not an edit war. The graph shows no linked versions of the article in other languages and no edits there, which fills the gap left by the earlier brief. Nothing in the edits points to anything new in the case. This looks like an editor translating an old topic, not a reaction to news. One small inconsistency: read_diff gives the article's title as "Вона не гідна бути зґвалтованою", a slightly different wording from the tracked title. That may just mean the page was renamed.

stories.headline: West Virginia article vandalism appears to have stopped; no new edits since last revert
stories.summary: This is still the same vandalism-and-revert cycle on enwiki's West Virginia article. It is not news and not a content dispute. The graph shows no edits after PhilKnight's revert at 1792467118 (rev 1381120567), so nothing has happened since the previous brief. The vandal's last attempt was temporary account ~2026-56033-01 using "undo" to put the text back (rev 1381120482). Before that, Hdhajaj restored it four times (revs 1381119754, 1381119829, 1381119907, 1381119941). HMSLavender, through AntiVandal, and PhilKnight reverted each of those within about a minute. Four reverting editors and several throwaway accounts fit one block-evading vandal; there is no two-sided edit war. I couldn't re-read any diffs this round, including the latest ones. That fits revision deletion of the obscene text, but I can't confirm it. This brief therefore relies on edit metadata and the content of earlier briefs, so it cites no revisions. Whether the page has been protected is still unknown. The quiet since the last revert suggests protection or blocks, but I haven't checked either.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on Palatine priest Richard Schäfer (1872–1932); no current event
stories.summary: AF666 created the German Wikipedia article "Richard Schäfer (Pfarrer)" from scratch (rev 271440835, +3,090 bytes). It is a historical biography of a Catholic priest and teacher from the Diocese of Speyer, born 1872 in Wattenheim and died 4 July 1932 in Ludwigshafen. The article is sourced to the German National Library (DNB), an 1899 Speyer diocesan directory and the Lexikon Pfälzer Persönlichkeiten. The other four edits are normal cleanup after a new article is created. Ephraim33 added authority-control data (GND/VIAF) and fixed punctuation (rev 271440966), and M2k~dewiki and Ephraim33 made small typo fixes. There were no reverts, all three editors are registered accounts, and the subject died more than 90 years ago, so these edits don't point to anything happening in the world now. One thing I can't rule out: the article may have been written for an anniversary or local commemoration, but nothing in the edits says so.

stories.headline: Temporary account tries 3 times to delete Salesians' abuse section on es-wiki; bots revert
stories.summary: The roughly 10.9k of churn isn't a rewrite. Within about 12 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56065-70) deleted the same ~1.8 KB "Abusos sexuales" section of the Spanish article on the Salesians three times, and anti-vandalism bots (Automoderador twice, SeroBOT once) put it back each time. The section is old, sourced content: it cites El País's 2023 database, which counts 123 reported cases and 196 victims in Spanish Salesian schools, plus EFE and Público. One deletion summary calls the section "highly politicized and biased", and another removal left a garbled heading ("exuales"). The edit flags show no reverts, but the bot edit summaries say they are reversions, which is why the scout missed them. Nothing points to a new real-world event: no new content, no other languages, and no human editors on the other side. This is one account whitewashing the page, contained so far. It could flare up again or lead to page protection.

stories.headline: New dewiki bio of 16th-century Nuremberg merchant Linhart Tucher; patrollers also tidy Pencereci page
stories.summary: Linhart Tucher was added to this story, but it has nothing to do with Turgut Pencereci in the real world. The only link is that the same new-page patrollers, M2k~dewiki and AxelHH, worked on both German articles within minutes of each other. A temporary account (~2026-56308-12) created the Tucher article with a 3.7k-byte biography (rev 271471003). It covers Linhart II. Tucher (1487–1568), a Nuremberg patrician, merchant and senior Losunger (one of the city's top officials), and draws mainly on a 2018 "450 years since his death" piece from the Stadtarchive Metropolregion Nürnberg plus bavarikon exhibition pages. M2k then added person data, categories and authority-file IDs (rev 271471170), and AxelHH removed a Deutsche Biographie link (rev 271471259). On the Pencereci page, AxelHH only reformatted the image into a captioned thumbnail (rev 271471268). There are no reverts, no versions in other languages and no news hook for Tucher; the death dates are centuries old. The open questions about Pencereci from earlier briefs are unchanged: the death date has not been checked independently, it is unclear whether he is notable enough for an article, and a conflict of interest is possible. Tucher should probably be split out of this story, since he has nothing to do with Pencereci.

stories.headline: Alex Dunne page quiet after infobox photo revert; no new edits
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened on the English Wikipedia page for Irish F2 driver Alex Dunne since the last brief. The most recent edits are still Lana8171's swap of the infobox photo, replacing the 2025 Zandvoort image with "File:Alex dunne in truck.jpg" using the wrong markup (rev 1380921438), and Knitsey's revert about 45 seconds later as "Not an improvement" (rev 1380921523). I read both diffs: the revert puts the original image back exactly. The graph has no edits on this page or on Barrett M82 after that revert. The page has no linked articles in other languages. This was a short burst of fan edits ("Goat" puffery and the "#DunnetoAlpine2027" hashtag) that patrollers cleared, and nothing points to a real-world event. Fans may come back, but for now the article is back to the clean version and things are quiet.

stories.headline: Temporary account's genealogy additions to two frwiki Crusader bios undone
stories.summary: This isn't news. It's routine housekeeping on two French Wikipedia biographies from the Crusader era (Onfroy IV de Toron and Alix de Champagne-Jérusalem). There was no coordinated expansion, and the scout's "no reverts" note was wrong. A temporary account (~2026-55688-85) added large blocks to both pages (+1857 and +2965 bytes): collapsible ancestry trees (Ancêtres-compact6), maps of the Crusader states for 1165–1240, and small wording and formatting changes. In the same roughly 15-minute session it also worked on related pages (Aboul Gharib plus three redirects to it, Mleh, Stéphane d'Arménie, and Isabelle Ire de Jérusalem). A registered editor, Baptiste de Lusignan, then used the standard "Annulation" (undo) function to reverse the edits on both pages within minutes, with no reason given. The graph's revert flag is false, but the edit comments make clear these were undos. The content looks like good-faith genealogy work, not vandalism, and nothing ties it to a current event. So far there's just one undo per page and no back-and-forth, so it isn't an edit war. That could change if the temporary account restores its additions.

stories.headline: Two unrelated fawiki edits reverted by AI anti-vandal bot; no news trigger
stories.summary: This "story" is two unrelated edits by temporary accounts, and an automated bot reverted both within about a minute. On Iraj Mesdaghi (rev 44764534), the edit changed the text from saying he is a former supporter and now a staunch opponent of the People's Mojahedin Organization (MEK) to saying he is a supporter. It went against the cited source. The same edit removed a link to the Iranian student Confederation and misspelled "Pahlavi" as "Pakhlavi", which looks like a deliberate insult. That makes it a point-of-view edit or vandalism, not news. Dexbot's AI-based anti-vandal system reverted it (rev 44764541). On Qaher-313 (rev 44764466), a different temporary account added an unsourced line saying Defense Minister "Akhlaghi" claims the aircraft will fly in 1406 (2027–28). Dexbot reverted that too (rev 44764477). The claim might trace back to a real statement, but nothing in the edit sources it. The pages share only the bot, and the edits are about 10 minutes apart. Older article text mentions Reza Pahlavi's March 2026 transitional-justice committee, but no one changed it in this activity. Unless Qaher-313 claims come back with sources, there's no real-world trigger here.

stories.headline: Turkish wiki generals' pages: no new activity since tribute edits were removed
stories.summary: This is not a separate story. It has the same four trwiki edits as the tracked story on Osman Erbaş and Metin Gürak. The graph shows nothing after Afurkanakin's clean-up at ts 1792557135. The scout's note says "no reverts", but that only reflects the revert flag. Afurkanakin's edits remove exactly what the temporary account ~2026-53392-15 added (+60/−60 on Erbaş, +23/−23 on Gürak), each within about 2–4 minutes. So in practice they are reverts, just not tagged as such. The earlier brief, based on the diff text, found these were personal tribute or greeting messages with no new facts. Erbaş's death in the 2021 helicopter crash was already on his page. I could not re-read the diffs this time because the diff fetch failed for all four revisions, so this brief relies on graph metadata and the earlier brief. There is still no sign of a real-world event, and this story should be merged into s_7a5a3b85's earlier brief or closed.

stories.headline: Bournemouth beat opponent 2–0 in Premier League round 7; season page updated
stories.summary: Three editors updated the 2026–27 AFC Bournemouth season article within about 15 minutes, filling in a Premier League round 7 result. The diffs record a 2–0 Bournemouth win: Marcus Tavernier scored in the 6th minute and Evanilson in the 48th. Kevin Danso was sent off in the 17th minute, apparently for the opponent. Craig Pawson refereed, attendance was 12,004, and five players were booked. A later edit moved Bournemouth from 19th to 15th in the league and made Tavernier the outright top scorer with 4 goals. The other edits were small fixes, such as a misspelled link. I don't know who the opponent was from the diffs I read. There were no reverts or disputes, and one of the editors is a temporary account. This is routine sports-results upkeep, not breaking news.

stories.headline: German article on chemist E. J. Corey gets copyedit; still no news event
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. The dewiki article on Nobel laureate Elias James Corey still has only five edits, from three registered editors in about 12 minutes. None of them were reverts, and nothing new was added after the last edit (ts 1792329426). The main edit is Mister Pommeroy's +820 "kl. Überarbeitung" (small revision). It rewrites the lead for grammar and style, renames the section "Forschungsarbeiten" (research work) to "Werk" (work), and replaces a duplicated citation with a reference to an existing one. Invisigoth67's later edit only removes a double space and a stray space in a wikilink. None of the text I read mentions a death, an award or any other current event. Other-language versions of the article (Wikidata Q135171) show no activity in the graph. The large diff is still cut off in the tool, so a small addition near its end is possible but unlikely given the edit summaries.

stories.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: student vandalism on WWI article reverted; joke 'Noa Cordero' page gone
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news, and there is nothing new since the last brief. On es-wiki 'Primera Guerra Mundial', temporary account ~2026-56138-66 added made-up leaders to the lead: 'Rubén Rayon, cientifico experto en nanotecnología' for the Allies and 'Alvaro Almela' for the Central Powers (rev 175914794). Patroller Nuria, the witch took it out with "rvto más" (rev 175915524), and I confirmed both diffs. Three temporary or new accounts then edited the joke page 'Noa Cordero'. Its revisions (175915550, 175915568, 175915577) now return "no revision" from Wikipedia, which most likely means the page was deleted after the speedy-deletion tag. That is an inference, not something I confirmed. The graph shows no edits on either page after that tag. Nothing here points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Confectionery store: duplicate M&M's World link removed; AFI copyediting continues
stories.summary: Since the last brief there has been one new edit to English Wikipedia's Confectionery store page. ShrimpsAreTasty unlinked "M&M's World" in the Merchandise section's sentence on stores that became tourist attractions, with the summary "Previously linked" (rev 1381151899, −4 bytes). That is a standard fix for a link that already appears earlier in the article. The sentence and its sources (Hersheypark, M&M's World, Minnesota's Largest Candy Store, Ghirardelli Square) are otherwise unchanged. There are no reverts, no new language editions and no sign of a real-world event. I'm calling it routine because of what the diff shows, not because the page is already tracked elsewhere. The other edits in the dossier (the History paragraph split and the White Rabbit link) were covered in the previous brief.

stories.headline: Vi-wiki "2 Ngày 1 Đêm" prank continues: student name moved to creative-director field
stories.summary: The pranking on the Vietnamese Wikipedia article for the show 2 Ngày 1 Đêm hasn't stopped. Three more edits came from three temporary accounts, and they go both ways. In rev 75655597, ~2026-56149-89, the same account that created the fake "Phạm Phi Hoàng 11a1" page, put the student's name in the infobox as creative director, replacing Đinh Trung Chính (edit summary "thích", meaning "like"). In rev 75655557, another account replaced the "[[Phạm Phi Hoàng 11a1]]" link with "[[Giang Won't Young]]", a pun on the K-pop singer Jang Won-young and on the earlier "Giang" nickname gag. So that edit swaps one joke for another rather than cleaning up. In rev 75655558, a third account replaced the cast birth date that had been set to "Chưa rõ" (unknown) with 20/04/1983, which looks like a partial repair of the earlier vandalism. I haven't checked that this is the cast member's real birth date. No patroller has reverted any of these edits, and the student's name is still in the article in a new spot. This is not a real-world news event.

stories.headline: ptwiki editor works to save new Italian university translation tagged for deletion
stories.summary: This update adds to the earlier brief on the new Portuguese article about Università degli Studi della Campania Luigi Vanvitelli (Q3551649). Napol2027 created it by translating the Italian page (rev 73241253), and patroller Leirbag reib then proposed it for semi-speedy deletion (rev 73241277). After that, a third editor, Daniel G Rego, started cleaning it up. He localised the infobox into Portuguese (Caserta, Campania, founded 1991, formerly the Second University of Naples), added a cited source for the founding year, and added "Ver também" (see also) and external-links sections, categories and authority control (rev 73241297). He then tagged the page as "em tradução" (being translated) and "em construção" (under construction) (revs 73241320, 73241321). This looks like a regular editor trying to get the article past deletion, not a sign of any real-world event. There are no reverts and the editors don't disagree. I haven't checked whether the deletion tag is still on the page.

stories.headline: New dewiki biography of Jena bioinformatician Reinhard Guthke created; no news event
stories.summary: The 11.4k churn comes from one edit: Rolandhs15 created a new German Wikipedia article (rev 271443049) on Reinhard Guthke. Guthke is a German bioinformatician and systems biologist born in 1950 in Kyritz. He worked at the Zentralinstitut für Mikrobiologie und experimentelle Therapie in Jena and its successor, the Leibniz-Institut für Naturstoff-Forschung und Infektionsbiologie, and retired in 2017. The article describes him as living ("ist ein"), so this is not a death update. The other three editors only did small routine cleanup within about 20 minutes: authority data (Normdaten), a link fix and a spacing fix. None of the edits were reverts. Only the German page moved, and nothing points to a real-world trigger. One caveat: the article's main source is a 2026 portrait book by Roland Hensel, and the creator's username "Rolandhs15" suggests the author may have created the article himself. That is a possible conflict of interest or book promotion, but it is not news.

stories.headline: Jaguars rookie TE Nate Boerkircher logs first NFL touchdown, per Wikipedia edits
stories.summary: Two editors updated the article on Jaguars rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher to show his first NFL touchdown. Gmc190188 changed the infobox TD stat from blank to 1, then fixed the formatting a minute later (revs 1380892596, 1380892692). A temporary account then added prose saying he scored his first touchdown on Oct 18 against the Houston Texans in a game played in London, on a "leaping, one handed grab" (rev 1380893550). Materialscientist removed that line within minutes as unsourced (rev 1380893898). This was an anti-vandalism tool removing unsourced text, not an edit war, and the infobox TD=1 stayed. The 371 churn mostly comes from that one sentence being added and taken out. This is routine game-stat upkeep, with no sign of a trade or injury. The touchdown is consistent across two independent editors but has no source yet, and the London/Texans detail rests on a single unsourced edit.

stories.headline: Italian 'Buco nero' article hit by fringe anti-gravity edits; reverted twice
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is low-level vandalism on the Italian Wikipedia article for black hole ('Buco nero', Q589). One temporary account (~2026-55982-55) made three edits within about 8 minutes. The edits insert fringe commentary into the lead, saying gravity "is only a theory", the article is "SCIENCE FICTION", space doesn't exist, and we live in a "holographic universe". The bot Moderatore Automatico reverted the first edit (rev 152984178) and the editor Sayatek reverted the second (rev 152984287). The scout's note said there were no reverts, but those two are reverts: the revert flag simply wasn't set. The large churn number comes from this add-and-undo cycle, not from any rewrite of the article. As of the latest data, the third edit (rev 152984321) had not yet been reverted, but it probably will be. Nothing on other pages or in other languages points to a real-world trigger.

stories.headline: Bad Arolsen school article gets infobox, sourcing tag and a link-in; still routine
stories.summary: This is a follow-up on the new German article about the Christian-Rauch-Schule, a Gymnasium in Bad Arolsen, now at its hyphenated title. Since the last brief, Kurator71 added an Infobox Schule (founded 1852, about 800 pupils, head Markus Wagner, Große Allee 73), a "Gegründet 1852" category and a {{Belege fehlen}} (missing sources) tag, which reflects the informal sourcing noted earlier. Tom md fixed small typos, including "Christian Rach" changed to "Christian-Rauch-Schule". A separate editor, Wheeke, linked the new article from the article on the sculptor Christian Daniel Rauch, whom the school is named after. The redirect left at the old title is still tagged for speedy deletion, which is normal after a move. There are no reverts, no other languages and no sign of a real-world event behind the edits. This is routine article building. The only open question is whether the article survives later sourcing or notability checks.

stories.headline: French student protests article: Catalan festival photo removed from infobox, citations trimmed
stories.summary: This window had about 10 edits to the enwiki article "2026 French student protests" by registered editors (Telovemi97, Kind Tennis Fan, Vitorperrut555), all in English, with no formal reverts. No new events were added. The most interesting edit is about a photo. Telovemi97 replaced an infobox image that Darouet had added, "Correfoc de La Mercè 2026", which shows Barcelona's fire-run festival, not the Paris protests. In its place they put back a photo of a crowd breaking into a Chanel boutique in Paris on 17 October (rev 1381248422), then added a sixth image of a man holding a République–Voltaire sign (rev 1381249365). That undoes part of Darouet's earlier move away from riot and looting images. It's a framing dispute to watch, but not an edit war yet, because Darouet hasn't responded. Kind Tennis Fan did reference cleanup. They cut nine stacked citations on the 2 October Paris school fires (rev 1381251700). They also removed an Amnesty citation as "incorrectly sourced" from the lead sentence saying the police response maimed students and led to 6,800 arrests (rev 1381252249), leaving a 19 October NYT report on a 14-year-old maimed by a tear-gas grenade as the source. The 6,800 cumulative arrest figure is much higher than the earlier counts (1,949 on 1 October, about 1,200 on 17 October). I couldn't tell from these diffs when it was added, and now only one source supports it, so it should be checked.

stories.headline: Update: fr-wiki \"Kitack Lim\" vandal page creation, no new activity or other-language moves
stories.summary: This is an update to the existing story, not a new one. A temporary account (~2026-56173-18) created the French Wikipedia page "Kitack Lim" with the word "caca" as its only content (rev 240545288, diff read). Anti-vandalism bots tagged it within seconds: first RevolucioBot (rev 240545289), then Salebot (rev 240545290). There have been no further edits since. A fulltext search of the graph finds no other "Kitack Lim" page, in French or any other language, so nothing else has moved. Only three accounts are involved: one vandal and two bots, with no human editors working on the topic. Nothing suggests a real-world event involving the former IMO Secretary-General.

stories.headline: Robert Hosie page: two small vandal edits, both reverted within about a minute
stories.summary: Robert Hosie is a historical Scottish inside forward who played in the NAFBL and the American Soccer League (1921–33). One temporary account (~2026-56209-40) made two edits to his en-wiki page. The first inserted junk into "one season", making it "one seas has on" (rev 1381246021). The second swapped "his/he" for "her/she" (rev 1381246088). Manualbadeditfix reverted the first as inappropriate humor, and Discospinster reverted the second with Huggle. Each revert came about a minute after the edit it undid. This is one page, with no edits in other languages and nothing tied to a current event, and it repeats the already-tracked Hosie vandalism story. It is not news.

stories.headline: Schlitzie article: minor vandalism by one account reverted twice
stories.summary: Not news. This is small-scale vandalism on the English article about the sideshow performer Schlitzie (1901–1971), and it has already been cleaned up. One account, Avlokkolva, made two edits to the lead sentence. First it changed the closing period to a comma (rev 1381059108), which the anti-vandalism tool Interceptor reverted as non-constructive. Twenty minutes later it misspelled the subject's name and alternate spellings ("Schlitzie"→"Schlitzi", "Schlitze"→"Schlitz", "Schlitze Surtees"→"Schlitz Surtees") (rev 1381059815), and Johnj1995 undid that within 21 seconds. No other languages and no other pages are involved, and nothing in the edits points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Helen Haines: no new facts since last update; only new edit adds "Dr" to her name
stories.summary: There has been only one edit to Helen Haines's English Wikipedia article since our last brief. A temporary account (~2026-45828-43) changed her infobox name to "Dr Helen Haines" (rev 1381128294). That's a cosmetic change and tells us nothing about the attack. The Scout's "three editors" are the same edits we already covered last time. I re-read the key ones. Patrick Cristiano's edit still only adds "Category:Australian amputees" and cites a France 24 report that she lost a leg (rev 1381127705). The amputation is still not in the article text, so it rests on one editor and one second-hand media report. 5225C's "2026 attack" section still says she was hit outside her Wangaratta electorate office at 15:35 AEDT on 19 October. It cites a Victoria Police release saying a man was arrested, Albanese saying it "wasn't an accident", and an AAP report of a counter-terrorism probe (rev 1381124659). There are no reverts, no other-language pages and no separate attack article. Still unconfirmed: her current condition, the suspect's identity and charges, and the motive.

stories.headline: sv-wiki 'Jordens kärna' (Earth's core): two vandal edits, both reverted, nothing new since
stories.summary: This is still vandalism and nothing has happened since the last brief. The graph has the same four edits as before and no later activity on the page. Temporary account ~2026-55891-13 made two edits that added text after the sentence about Inge Lehmann's 1936 discovery of the inner core. Rev 59783792 added "Jag är bäst" ("I am the best"). Rev 59783800 added a racial slur. Established editors undid both quickly. Nalle&Lisa undid the first after about 90 seconds and tagged it "klotter" (graffiti). Nirmos rolled back the second about 40 seconds after it was made. The vandal edited no other pages, no other language versions moved, and nothing points to a real-world event. No further action needed unless the account comes back.

stories.headline: Finnish Wikipedia gets new, likely chatbot-drafted stub on psychologist Richard M. Ryan
stories.summary: A temporary account created the fi.wikipedia page "Richard Ryan", a stub on US psychologist Richard M. Ryan, co-creator of Self-Determination Theory. The first revision opens with the line "Tässä on lyhyt Wikipedia-tyylinen artikkeli…" ("Here is a short Wikipedia-style article…"). That reads like text pasted from an AI chatbot. The revision also cites only English Wikipedia and ends with a stray "Gangsta rap" item in the list of works. Patroller MikkoK tagged the page as unsourced (its edit was not read). Luurankosoturi then removed the Wikipedia citations ("Wikipedia is not a valid source"), wikified the text and added categories, and the page now carries a proposed-deletion tag for being unsourced. Nothing in the edits points to a real-world event involving Ryan. This is ordinary new-page creation and cleanup, with no edit war and no spread to other languages.

stories.headline: Peter Skapetis page: one unsourced school detail reverted, then citation upkeep; no news
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia biography of Australian footballer Peter Skapetis was edited three times by three different registered accounts. First, AvonRSC added an unsourced line saying he attended Rowville Secondary College's sports academy football program (rev 1381234214). About 30 seconds later, DollarStoreBa'al reverted it as unsourced, in good faith (1381234266). Perpetually Blooming Rose then added Wayback Machine archive links to existing citations about his past moves (Stoke City, trials, Dover Athletic, Dandenong Thunder) (1381235098). None of these edits adds a transfer, retirement or other new event. Nothing points to an edit war or vandalism, since the revert happened once and wasn't contested, and the edits stayed on English Wikipedia. Pages in other languages weren't checked.

stories.headline: Kanika Mann page: Google-search 'source' removed; filmography upkeep, no news event
stories.summary: This update adds to the routine story already tracked on the enwiki biography of Indian actress Kanika Mann. Since the last brief, ERcheck removed the raw Google search URL that a temporary account had added as a reference for the "Flight Attendent" (2024) web-series credit, calling it not a reliable source (rev 1381061011). That leaves the credit, which SAR FILM added earlier, with no source at all. I could load the Skywatcher68 diff this time: it changed only a citation byline, replacing the bogus author name "Team / IndianTelevision.com" with an "author not stated" placeholder (rev 1381059146). The temporary account also added the surname "Tyagi" to a character name, "Shakti" (rev 1381059807). Four editors made eight edits on one page, with no reverts, no other languages and nothing linking this to a real-world event. Open question: the username SAR FILM may point to a conflict of interest, which I have not checked.

stories.headline: U-17 Women's World Cup: Group A/B tables, scorers, attendance updated; NZ eliminated
stories.summary: This is routine match-day upkeep on the en-wiki page for the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. There are no reverts and no conflict: Tomrtn made most of the edits, with single edits from Angolaiscool and Metalpipe. Angolaiscool marked New Zealand as eliminated from Group A (0–2, goals 0–6), and the edit summary cites FIFA. Tomrtn changed Germany's status code from "Q" to "a" (2–0, goals 6–3). Tomrtn also cleaned up goal notation (og→o.g., P→pen.), updated the third-placed-teams table to 20 October (the Group A and B third-place teams each moved to 1–0–1, and A now ranks first), and added an attendance of 231 for a Group B match. North Korea leads Group B on 2–0 with goals 12–1. Metalpipe's goalscorers edit lists Argentina's Mercedes Diz and Morocco's Nessma Mouradi on 3 goals each, followed by several German, Nigerian and Polish scorers. Uncertain: the exact meaning of the lowercase "a" status code, and I didn't check other language editions.

stories.headline: Linus Torvalds es-wiki page vandalized by temporary account, reverted twice by bots
stories.summary: The roughly 6.5k of churn on Spanish Wikipedia's "Linus Torvalds" page comes from vandalism and bot reverts. It is not a rewrite and does not point to anything happening in the real world. Temporary account ~2026-56158-52 made two edits with no summary, about five minutes apart. I read both diffs. The first (rev 175918433) deleted the infobox and changed the lead to call Torvalds "Gorila sabroso" ("tasty gorilla") and "un desconocido" ("a nobody"), with garbled text about "páginas raras" ("weird pages"). The second (rev 175918516) deleted the infobox and lead paragraph again. SeroBOT (rev 175918435) and Automoderador (rev 175918518) each restored the earlier version within about 10 seconds. I did not open those two diffs, but their edit summaries say they are reverts and their size changes (+1004 and +2265) exactly cancel out the vandal's edits. The graph's revert flag missed them, which is why the scout saw "no reverts". Only this one page and this one non-bot account are involved, and nothing points to a coordinated campaign or any news about Torvalds.

stories.headline: France 17 October riots: death toll disputed on en-wiki; Macron to address nation
stories.summary: The English '17 October riots' page is still being worked on, mostly through tidying. The one revert is about the death toll. A temporary account (~2026-56083-52) changed the infobox from "2 (1 police officer, 1 protester)" to "1 protester" with the comment "wrong", and OrdinariusFingius undid it, putting back 2 deaths. Neither edit cites a source, so treat the police officer's death as unconfirmed. In the body text, Limoges is still there, which settles a doubt from the last brief. The article says the 19th-century Hôtel de Ville was set on fire in the evening, burned into the next morning and was partly destroyed. It cites Euronews ("Spire collapses at historic Limoges town hall") and AP. The same text says Lyon's tourist office was burned, Marseille city hall's lobby was briefly entered, and a demonstrator lost a hand in Saint-Étienne. Interior Minister Nuñez said an investigation was open and did not confirm reports that a police grenade caused the injury. A Le Monde live-blog citation dated 18 October says Macron will address the French people at 8 p.m. London3Calling also removed causes from the infobox ("poor school conditions", "chronic underfunding of education", "police brutality", "reintroduction of conscription") with a comment that pushes back on the education-underfunding claim. That is a change of framing to keep an eye on, not a new fact. Other figures (1,200 arrests, 150 police hurt, 550,000 marchers) have not changed.

stories.headline: France national team page: old October 2025 qualifier results removed, reverted, removed again
stories.summary: This is routine housekeeping, not news. Editor Chelsdog removed two old match boxes from the "Recent results" section of the English Wikipedia France national football team article: France 3–0 Azerbaijan (10 Oct 2025) and Iceland 2–2 France (13 Oct 2025), both 2026 World Cup qualifiers. TonySt reverted the first removal, which had no edit summary, calling it "unexplained content removal". Chelsdog then made the same removal again with the explanation "over one year": the edit timestamps put these edits in October 2026, so the matches had just passed the one-year mark. No match scores or facts were changed. Only two editors and one language edition were involved, there has been one revert, and nothing has happened since. This looks like the same kind of results-trimming already being tracked on the France U-21 page. It is not an edit war unless TonySt reverts again.

stories.headline: Revert loop over 2023 DTPM citation continues on Santiago Los Libertadores station page
stories.summary: This is not a real-world event. It is the same small edit war already being tracked on the es-wiki article for Estación Intermodal Los Libertadores, a transit hub in Santiago, Chile. Temporary account ~2026-55933-43 again removed the single <ref> on the bus-route line "Caletera Autopista Los Libertadores … Cerro Portezuelo" (rev 175919561). That ref cites a February 2023 DTPM "Programa de Operación" routes zip file. 18 seconds later, Aroblesm, who originally added the ref, restored it with a rollback (rev 175919566). Counting both temporary accounts, the citation has now been removed three times and restored three times, each time a ±277-byte change. Every removal used the undo tool and gave no reason, and none of the removing accounts has edited any other page, which points to disruption or an unexplained objection rather than a sourced content dispute. It is unclear whether the two temporary accounts are the same person. If removals continue, the page may need protection or admin attention.

stories.headline: Jasmine Sokko page: apparent label account rewrites bio, reverted as promotional COI
stories.summary: An account called JSJFJ, with only 3 edits, made three edits to English Wikipedia's Jasmine Sokko article. Each had the comment "Official company update of artist bio to reflect recent changes." The name and the text point to her label, JFJ Productions (JJ Lin's company). The first edit (−11,283 bytes) removed her birth name "Jasmine Wong Chu Qing" and the sourced lead text. In their place it put marketing copy ("multi-hyphenate creative director... Draped in monochromatic ensemble"), her December 2024 debut as a JFJ artiste on JJ Lin's JJ20 tour, the album "Burnout Dynasty" (March 2025), her NDP2026 song "You'll Be Okay," and a single released 5 June 2026. Two experienced editors, APK and Celjski Grad, reverted all three edits as unsourced, promotional, conflict-of-interest changes. This is a common pattern of a label or PR account editing an artist's page. There is no new real-world event here: the facts it cites are already known or minor releases. Three reverts in about 20 minutes could become an edit war if JSJFJ keeps going. For now it's a one-sided COI cleanup, not a two-way edit war or malicious vandalism.

stories.headline: Subtle factual tampering on Fergie's "Clumsy" article reverted within minutes
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts made small, misleading changes to the English Wikipedia article on Fergie's 2007 single "Clumsy". ~2026-56033-76 changed the "Composition" section so that Digital Spy's comparison was to Cassidy's "I'm a Hustla" instead of Tweet's "Oops (Oh My)" (rev 1381134480). ~2026-56080-52 then credited an MTV News quote to BET, renaming the citation without changing its MTV source link (rev 1381135151), and made a -41 byte edit to the chart section; the visible part of that diff showed no clear change. Within about 10 minutes, the established editor Tbhotch reverted both edits by ~2026-56080-52 and then restored his own earlier revision, which undid the Tweet/Cassidy swap too (rev 1381135379). This looks like sneaky vandalism, not a news event or an edit war: the changes went one way, with no back-and-forth. Nothing points to anything happening in the real world. I didn't see exactly what the chart-section edit changed, and I didn't check whether these accounts were active on other pages.

stories.headline: Simon Fraser vandalism reverted; pages quiet since, no news event
stories.summary: The scout's read holds: this is minor vandalism, and nothing has changed since the last brief. I checked the graph and found no edits to Simon Fraser (explorer), Aye-aye or Paper Wars after Smallestredboy's revert (rev 1381234790). The last activity came from temporary account ~2026-56278-91. It renamed the subject in the lead "kurt kobain" (rev 1381234640) and changed the "Early life" heading to "late life" under the summary "fixed some minor mistakes" (rev 1381234718). EditWarCriminal and Smallestredboy undid both edits, each within about 40 seconds, and the diffs confirm the page is back to normal. The pages are linked only by anti-vandalism patrollers, and nothing points to a real-world event. The only loose end is the possibly mistaken proposed-deletion notice still on Paper Wars (rev 1381234046), which is wiki housekeeping, not news. I recommend folding this into the existing vandalism story and lowering its priority.

stories.headline: Vandalism on English 'Uraeus' page is over: reverted, no new edits
stories.summary: This repeats the vandalism story already on file. It is not a new event. The same six edits are involved. Temporary account ~2026-55935-45 vandalised the Symbolism section of the English Wikipedia 'Uraeus' article three times; the last edit (rev 1381088316) changed the opening sentence to "Poopie is uraeus,a symbol for the goddess Wadjet... :)". Patrollers SuperPianoMan9167 and Nil NZ reverted each edit within about a minute. Nil NZ's final revert (rev 1381088396, made with the WikiShield tool) brought the original text back word for word. The graph shows no edits to the page since that revert, no other language versions involved, and none of the three editors touching any other page. Nothing here points to a real-world event. Recommend merging into the existing vandalism story or closing this one.

stories.headline: Brnabić vandal pastes Diana conspiracy text; Bosnian Cyrillic label dispute hits third revert
stories.summary: The vandalism on English Wikipedia's Ana Brnabić article is still going, but it no longer has anything to do with her. Temp account ~2026-55886-45 came back (rev 1380891652, +608) and pasted Serbian-language text into the infobox. The text sets out the conspiracy theory that MI6 killed Princess Diana on royal orders, and it ends with a chatbot-style offer to "tell you more", so it looks like pasted AI chat output. MarioWonderExpert reverted it within about 17 seconds. The real event in this cluster is on Bosnian Cyrillic: Arolaq made his third attempt (rev 1380891862) to change the infobox language from Serbo-Croatian to Bosnian. This time he also reworded the lead and argued in the edit summary that Serbo-Croatian is no longer official. Shadow4ya undid it within about 70 seconds. Three changes and three reverts in about 22 minutes (two by Shadow4ya, one by Materialscientist) is now a slow edit war on a nationalist sore point, though I see no talk-page or other-language activity. Nancy Ajram is incidental: temp account ~2026-56036-78 replaced "singer" in the lead with an apparent slur (revs 1380891926, 1380891998), and Paul Erik, ClueBot NG and Materialscientist reverted each attempt. Nothing here points to a real-world event, and every bad edit has been undone.

stories.headline: Prank vandalism on German Burj Khalifa article reverted twice
stories.summary: This is not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-56116-74) vandalised the German Wikipedia article on Burj Khalifa twice in about 5 minutes, and two established editors reverted both edits within seconds. First (rev 271482534), it made "Leo Benning und sein Hund Lukas Kränzle" (Leo Benning and his dog Lukas Kränzle) the building's main tenant in the infobox. Der.Traeumer reverted that. Second (rev 271482647), it swapped the height-comparison image caption for a crude joke about "Leo", while its edit summary falsely claimed to be correcting misinformation. Carol.Christiansen reverted that. The graph did not flag the reverts, but the edit comments show they were standard rollbacks. Nothing happened on other pages or in other languages. The likely source is a schoolkid prank naming a friend. The Scout called this routine, but it's vandalism, and it's already contained.

stories.headline: Galician Wikipedia gets two new translated articles: Gaza square and Malayan Communist Party
stories.summary: Wikimoder26 created two new articles on Galician Wikipedia within minutes of each other. Both are translations of the lead sections of Spanish Wikipedia articles, and both edit summaries say so. One is 'Praza do Soldado Descoñecido', on the Unknown Soldier Square in Gaza City (rev 7731663, already covered in an earlier routine brief). The other is 'Partido Comunista de Malaisia', on the Communist Party of Malaya (rev 7731689). It gives encyclopedic background: the party was founded in 1930, played a role in the Malayan Emergency and gave up its weapons in 1989. Nothing in it is new or tied to a current event. The rest of the burst is cleanup by regular Galician editors. MAGHOI added categories and marked the Malaya article as too short. Breogan2008 added wikilinks and an authority-control template (rev 7731734), then added a History section to the Gaza square article, translated from the English article (rev 7731769). That section includes the square becoming a camp for displaced people in 2025, with a sourced report dated May 2025. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors, only four named editors, and only Galician pages changed. The pages have no clear link in the news beyond one translator's choice of topics. This is routine translation work, not a news event.

stories.headline: Joke edits on ja.wiki page for former Hiroshima town Ōgaki reverted; no new activity
stories.summary: This story is the same one as the earlier vandalism brief on 大柿町 (Ōgaki), a former town in Hiroshima Prefecture that merged into Etajima City in 2004. One temporary account (~2026-56244-55) made three small joke edits. I read two of them: one says the town's land "was launched by rocket and is now sea" (rev 111446241), and another adds "this is non-fiction" to the paragraph on where the name comes from (rev 111446275). Two established editors, Black Oar and Daiyamond (using TwinkleGlobal), reverted the edits within about 7 minutes. The graph shows no edits since the last revert, and no other pages, languages or editors are involved. Nothing points to a real-world event, and this can be closed as a duplicate of the earlier story.

stories.headline: Indonesia adds powerlifting and judo bronzes at 2026 Asian Para Games; tally at 17 bronze
stories.summary: Results-tracking continues on English Wikipedia's "Indonesia at the 2026 Asian Para Games". Since the last brief, Yogwi21 added three bronze medals dated 20 October: Margono (powerlifting, men's −65 kg), Shebrioni (powerlifting, women's −61 kg) and Fajar Pambudi (judo, men's J1 −95 kg) (rev 1381167417). Kwetiau then raised the infobox bronze count from 16 to 17 (rev 1381167800). That leaves the tally at 4 gold, 4 silver and 17 bronze, and the rank was last given as 9th. The infobox now shows fewer bronzes than the medalist table implies, which suggests editors are not keeping the two in step. It does not look like a dispute: there are no reverts, all the editors have accounts, and edits are still coming in. Uncertainty: I have not checked the figures against an official medal table.

stories.headline: Arsenal win 1–0 away in Premier League round 7, stay second (routine update)
stories.summary: Three editors updated the en-wiki 2026–27 Arsenal F.C. season page with one Premier League round-7 result dated 18 October 2026. The match entry shows a 0–1 away score, an 80th-minute goal and a booking for Noni Madueke, a booking for Neco Williams, and an attendance of 30,893. The first editor marked the result as "L". Publicwalrus changed it to "W", which matches the 0–1 away score and the other edits: the away record went from 2 to 3 wins, the form string added a W, and points rose from 15 to 18. Alexthebat901 kept Arsenal 2nd in the league position row. The opponent isn't in the diffs I read. Williams's booking suggests Nottingham Forest, but I haven't confirmed that. The page logged no reverts and no other languages moved, so this is a routine match-result update, not a distinct news event.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on Ryūkyū princely houses (Udun) gets images, cleanup; routine
stories.summary: The only activity here is a new German article, "Udun (Ryūkyū)", being built out. It covers the princely houses of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, their residences and their tombs. Bosse Nor created it (rev 271488924, +11,575 bytes, "Neuanlage", meaning a new page) and has now posted one follow-up edit (rev 271489207, +274). That edit adds four images (Nakagusuku Udun, Shikina Udun, and the Ie and Ginowan Udun tombs) and fixes double periods in the list of houses.
