Two other editors made small cleanup edits: M2k~dewiki added the category "Königreich Ryūkyū" (rev 271488949), and another editor added non-breaking spaces (rev 271489047). The story still covers one page in one language, with 3 editors, 4 edits, no reverts and nothing tied to current events, so this is ordinary article growth, not news.

stories.headline: New it-wiki article created on Rembrandt's 1637 Louvre painting of Tobias and the angel
stories.summary: An Italian Wikipedia article on Rembrandt's 1637 panel "L'arcangelo Raffaele che lascia la famiglia di Tobia" (Louvre, Paris) was created from scratch. The first revision (152985552, +2147) built the stub: an infobox (oil on oak panel, 52×68 cm), a lead sentence, and categories. A second revision by the same temporary account (152986850, +3414) added Description, History (the painting entered Louis XV's collection in 1742) and "Tobias in other works" sections, with book citations. The remaining edits are small: a 9-byte tweak by a second temporary account, and a citation-template fix by an experienced editor (Egidio24, 219 edits). There are no reverts, no conflict, and no sign of any real-world news trigger. This is ordinary content creation, as the scout expected. I did not read the two smallest diffs.

stories.headline: Kira Kosarin YouTube link spam continues with a third numbered account; all reverted
stories.summary: This is still vandalism, not a news event. Since the last brief, a third account in the same name series, "Mark Goldstein2", added the same bare YouTube link (watch?v=eNMzaV9P5N8) to the top of the Kira Kosarin article twice. Both edits carried the comment "Please Watch Video Sponsored by LTA" (rev 1380904106). On Wikipedia, "LTA" usually means "long-term abuse", which suggests a known repeat vandal, but I haven't confirmed that. Mark Goldstein1 had earlier added the same link (rev 1380903894). SuperPianoMan9167 and Ser Amantio di Nicolao reverted each insertion within about 40 seconds. The last revert was rev 1380904175, with the comment "rats, thought I could beat it to here". Across 16 edits there are 8 spam insertions by three accounts and 8 removals, but only 5 of the removals are flagged as reverts in the data. None of the accounts edited other pages in the graph and no other language versions were touched. This is spam being cleaned up by patrollers, not an edit war between two editors. More numbered accounts may follow until the page is protected or the accounts are blocked.

stories.headline: Michael Rockefeller page: patroller reverts new account's edits; no news event
stories.summary: Over about 3 minutes, a low-activity account (Olliebones23, 4 edits in total) made two edits to the English Wikipedia article on Michael Rockefeller. One changed the short description with no change in size. The other removed 13 bytes from a section and left a blank section comment. Vandal patroller Discospinster reverted both edits, the second time using the Huggle anti-vandalism tool (HG). This is not two editors trading reverts: the account did not push back after the second revert, and no other editor or language version moved. The same account made similar short-description and small edits to unrelated pages (Harry Houdini, Two-Face) in the preceding half hour, which fits unconstructive or test edits being cleaned up. I couldn't check what the text said because every diff fetch failed, so I'm calling this vandalism from the metadata pattern alone, and I don't see any sign of a real-world event.

stories.headline: Third emoji edit on Turkish page for volleyball player İlkin Aydın, reverted in a minute
stories.summary: The same temporary account (~2026-56033-95) came back for a third edit to the tr-wiki biography of volleyball player İlkin Aydın. Rev 38293949 replaced the "== Kariyeri ==" ("Career") section heading with heart and kiss emojis. Patroller SHIFT64 undid it about a minute later (rev 38293959), and the diff shows the heading put back. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but that is wrong. The graph's revert flag is false, yet SHIFT64's edit is a standard undo of that revision. As with the earlier edits, no facts about the subject were changed, no other language versions moved, and only one vandal and two patrollers are involved. This is persistent low-level fan vandalism, not a sign of a real-world event. If it keeps up, the page may get protection or the account a block, but nothing yet suggests news about the player.

stories.headline: US 'No Kings' protests under way Oct. 17; Wikipedia article moves to past tense
stories.summary: Editors on the English Wikipedia article "October 2026 No Kings protests" are treating the nationwide US rallies as happening now. An unregistered editor removed the {{Update}} tag, whose reason was "they have begun" (rev 1380888453). ItalianAce rewrote the Demonstrations section and changed it from future to past tense (rev 1380889445). The section that edit replaced said events were planned in many states, including Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas and Kentucky. It cited local outlets that describe Oct. 17 rallies tied to early voting before the midterms. Lorax added a photo dated 2026-10-17 of a No Kings protest at Friendship Heights on the Maryland/DC border (rev 1380890548), which is first-hand evidence that the events took place. Activity is light so far: 4 edits from 4 editors on one page, no reverts, and no other language editions checked. Turnout, size and any incidents have not appeared in the edits yet. This is a separate US event from the tracked France Oct. 17 protests, even though it falls on the same date.

stories.headline: Vietnamese '2 Days 1 Night' page protected after nickname vandalism; et-wiki eKool hit with slurs
stories.summary: Update. The vandalism wave on the Vietnamese Wikipedia article for '2 ngày 1 đêm' kept going. Temporary account ~2026-56131-10 put in more mocking names for host Trường Giang ("mét sáu thích làm màu", "Giang Đẫm bé bỏng") and renamed the criticism section to "Giang Lùn" ("Short Giang"). Patroller Veritas Sapientiae undid the edits and then added a {{pp-vandalism}} protection tag, which should slow the throwaway accounts down. The scout's note is wrong about the Estonian eKool page: this is not routine maintenance. Temporary account ~2026-54734-65 blanked the article three times in about five minutes, replacing it with racist slurs, number spam and a jab at a school. Veritas Sapientiae and Morkoz reverted each time. The two pages share no real-world event. They are linked only because one cross-wiki patroller (Veritas Sapientiae) cleaned up both, so the eKool part counts as separate, unrelated vandalism. None of these edits points to anything happening in the real world.

stories.headline: Hebrew page for kids' show 'HaSidratiyim' sees cleanup edit reverted as season 2 airs
stories.summary: The large churn on the Hebrew Wikipedia article for 'הסדרתיים' (a Kan Educational series) comes from one edit and its reversal. A temporary account (~2026-55928-69) copyedited the character list, cut about 2.5k bytes of plot detail (including an episode-17 detail about Ron), and added that Ron loses his powers in season 2 (rev 44084637). User חובב תחבורה ציבורית then undid it with the summary 'reverting vandalism', putting the removed text back plus a long episode-7 plot summary, net +4448 (rev 44084722). A third editor only added an explanatory-notes section (rev 44084710). The removed edit reads as a good-faith trim and copyedit, not vandalism. That makes this a small content disagreement on a fan-maintained page, not a news event. The one real-world fact on the page is that season 2 premiered on 18 October 2026, which probably explains why people are editing it now. There is one revert and no back-and-forth, so it isn't an edit war yet.

stories.headline: Jan Crawford page: 'shill' vandalism reverted in 46 seconds; disputed El-Sayed line stays
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the earlier brief. The one new edit is a revert by Materialscientist using an anti-vandalism tool (rev 1380873182). It came 46 seconds after the edit it undid. That revert takes out the temporary account's addition to the lead sentence calling Crawford a "Trump administration shill masking as a television journalist" (1380873081), so the lead again simply calls her a television journalist, author and attorney. The earlier brief said the vandalism was still on the page; that is no longer true. The disputed Career sentence is still there. It says that on Oct 18, 2026, she praised a "Christian nationalist" for asking Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to denounce the Muslim Brotherhood. It cites her X post and a Handbasket article that names the questioner as a former staffer for Sen. Hawley (1380871914). The sentence's wording is loaded, and its main source is her own post. There are no edits after the revert, no new editors, and nothing on El-Sayed pages or in other languages. That points to a small online controversy that has calmed down, not a developing event.

stories.headline: India Asian Para Games page adds powerlifting silver for Kasthuri Rajamani; tally 12-17-18
stories.summary: Live results editing continues on 'India at the 2026 Asian Para Games' (en). Mr Gupta 18 and Neeelzzz20, both established editors, are still working together, with no reverts. Since the last brief, Mr Gupta 18 added a 21 October silver for Kasthuri Rajamani in the women's 67 kg powerlifting (rev 1381266830). That raised India's silver count from 16 to 17 and its total from 46 to 47, with golds at 12 and bronzes at 18. A follow-up edit adds her lift attempts: 103, a failed 106 and a best of 108 kg (rev 1381266937). An earlier edit added a time of 11.50 marked as a personal best to Rakeshbhai Bhatt's bronze in athletics (rev 1381266161). This is normal good-faith updating during a live event. The results come only from Wikipedia and haven't been checked against outside sources.

stories.headline: Hoax "Prayturnia" sleep condition twice inserted into Insomnia article, reverted
stories.summary: This is a small hoax incident, not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-55799-03) twice added a paragraph to English Wikipedia's Insomnia article about a made-up related condition called "Prayturnia". The text claimed that people with it can go days without sleep with no ill effects, that about 1 in 173 million people have it (1 in 137 million in the second version), and that it is mostly found in mountainous areas like Nepal. Both versions cited a general Sleep Foundation page on sleep deprivation that doesn't back up the claim. Drchriswilliams reverted the first addition as nonconstructive, and MrOllie reverted the second as a hoax. Each revert came within about 10 minutes. There was no back-and-forth edit war, no other pages or languages were involved, and the 2,712 churn figure is just the two insertions plus their two reverts.

stories.headline: New Hebrew Wikipedia biography of Virginia congressman Thomas W. Harrison (d. 1935)
stories.summary: The heavy churn comes from a brand-new article, not from a rewrite of an existing one. Hebrew Wikipedia editor על הטוב created 'תומאס הריסון' (rev 44092987, +7,556 bytes, comment "creating new page"). It is a full biography of Thomas Walter Harrison (1856–1935), a Democrat who served in the Virginia Senate, as a state judge, and in the U.S. House for Virginia's 7th district (1916–22 and 1923–29). Its structure and sourcing look like a translation of the English article. The two follow-up edits are routine cleanup: YoavR changed a category using HotCat, and Assayas swapped one dash style for another (rev 44093051, −12 bytes). The subject died in 1935, nothing in the text points to anything happening now, and there are no reverts or edits in other languages. This is routine editing with no news hook.

stories.headline: Patrol cluster: San Sebastián article blanked, Montezuma spam; no new event
stories.summary: This time the diffs loaded, and they back up the earlier vandalism reading. Nothing has been edited on the five pages since the last update (the newest edit is ESkog's revert at ts 1792459994). The pages are linked only because the same patrollers worked on them (Augmented Seventh on all five). On San Sebastián Street Festival, temp account ~2026-56117-51 deleted the article's lead and history sections (-10,186 bytes, no edit summary), and ClueBot NG restored them. On Carlos Montezuma, temp account ~2026-56069-53 added the bolded line "thank you for reading you help our team wikipedia . com enjoy reading…", which is plain vandalism, and Augmented Seventh reverted it. On Long Beach, Mississippi, a temp account keeps adding complaints about an "ordinance 676" placed in the article's opening paragraph. One version links to legiscan's Mississippi state bill HB676 (2023), not a city ordinance, so the edit is unsourced and confused, though the anger behind it may be real. On Moksha, temp account ~2026-55295-24 has now made its fourth attempt to add "liberation from prakriti (nature and matter)" wording to the lead (rev 1381103010). The graph shows no revert of it yet, and the edit-by-edit dispute is already covered by story s_2b6c075a. Nothing here points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Zumbi dos Palmares (pt-wiki): one account's vandalism reverted twice; no new activity
stories.summary: This is still minor vandalism by one account. It points to no real-world event. The account Frfansciois made three edits to the lead of the pt-wiki article. First it relabelled the [[cerca do Barriga]] link as 'Serra do Barriga', which may have been good faith. In rev 73255712 it changed how Zumbi's 1695 death year displays, making it read 2026. In rev 73255768 it relabelled the same link 'cerca do renanzinho', a joke name. Uchoa rolled back the first two edits and Little Sunshine reverted the third, all within about 10 minutes. The article is back to its stable text. The scout says there were no reverts, which is wrong: the revert flag wasn't set, but both patroller edit comments are rollbacks. The scout also says this belongs in an existing story, but the graph has only one story on this page, this one (s_67f6af68), so there is nothing to merge it into. There have been no edits since my earlier brief. I'd suggest closing it unless the account comes back.

stories.headline: One temporary account blanked big chunks of five articles, including the Serbian protests page; all reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Temporary account ~2026-56102-20 cut large blocks of text with no edit summary from five unrelated English Wikipedia articles in about 30 minutes: Phnom Penh (−10,150), GoDaddy (−3,578), Preply (−3,288), Suno (−16,844) and 2024–present Serbian anti-corruption protests (−37,192). The two diffs I read show the infobox, the lead and long sourced sections deleted in each case, with broken template pieces left behind. Nothing new was added and no real-world event is mentioned. Patroller KH-1 reverted both the Suno and the Serbian protests edits within minutes. There's no sign of other editors or other language versions moving, and this isn't a back-and-forth revert fight. The only reason Suno and the protests page were grouped together is that the same account hit both. One thing worth noting is a maintenance tag on the protests page saying it has no coverage of 2026 events. That points to an article that's falling behind, not to anything new happening right now.

stories.headline: Reverted vandalism on Stefon Diggs and Hopi; It's Jeff redirect change is unrelated
stories.summary: This repeats the story already being tracked. There is no real-world event behind it. One temporary account (~2026-56045-94) added "they were 67rizzers" to the Hopi article (rev 1381088856). It then replaced the whole Stefon Diggs infobox with "he was born in ohio and had 27 moms" (rev 1381089316, -1,899 bytes, edit summary "hgjjg"). SuperPianoMan9167 reverted the Hopi edit and ClueBot NG restored the Diggs page within seconds. The scout's note says there were no reverts, but that is wrong: there were three. The It's Jeff edits come from a different temp account (~2026-56203-53). It repointed a redirect from "Jeff the Land Shark#Comic books" to "It's Jeff!" (rev 1381089691). ClueBot NG reverted that change, and the account made it again with an "R from misspelling" tag (rev 1381089771). That looks like a good-faith redirect fix, possibly a false positive by the bot, not vandalism. The deleted infobox listing Diggs with the Washington Commanders for 2026 was already on the page before the vandalism, so it is not new information. Recommend merging this into the existing vandalism story and closing it.

stories.headline: Chwalińska's Wuhan win added to prose; early No. 11 ranking claim reverted
stories.summary: This updates the tracked Wuhan Open story. The result hasn't changed: Maja Chwalińska beat Sonay Kartal in three sets in the 2026 Wuhan Open final. Since the last brief, Chwalińska's English article has added prose saying "She went on to win the final, beating Sonay Kartal in three sets," citing a Sky Sports highlights page. The section heading now says "first WTA Title" (rev 1380878695). That edit also says she rose to No. 11 the following week. The one revert is about that ranking, not the result. Kapnonian changed her infobox to No. 11 as of 19 October 2026 (rev 1380874767). Moscow Connection undid it with the note "Come back when the ratings are updated" (rev 1380877668), because the new ranking hasn't been published yet. That's normal housekeeping, not an edit war. Polish Wikipedia shows the same thing: an editor's comment reads "Ranking nie został opublikowany" ("ranking not published"), though I couldn't load that diff. Other new edits are formatting on Kartal's page (rev 1380875566) and a stats tweak (rev 1380880224). Treat the No. 11 ranking as unconfirmed until WTA publishes it; the prose still says No. 11, which contradicts the reverted infobox.

stories.headline: Polish Wikipedia records Maja Chwalińska winning Wuhan Open 2026, her first WTA title
stories.summary: Polish Wikipedia's article on tennis player Maja Chwalińska says she won the Wuhan Open 2026 final on 18 October, beating Sonay Kartal 2:6, 6:4, 6:2. The article calls it her first career WTA title. It also says she is the third Polish woman to win a WTA 1000-level event (or equivalent) and the first Polish player to win in Wuhan. Editor Mareczekkk added these lines (rev 80999998, 81000038), along with her route to the title: wins over Sherif, Bouzková, Jović, Sakkari, and Iga Świątek 7:5, 6:1 in the semifinal, described as her first win over a top-10 player. Editors are being careful rather than fighting. RafaEl030794 first added a one-line "tournament winner" sentence (80999973). Mareczekkk had earlier hidden an unsourced lead mention of reaching the Wuhan final (80999884), and later undid an early ranking update to No. 11, saying the new ranking had not been published yet (81000054). There were no reverts by other editors, and all three editors are named accounts. The only source cited for the final is a live-match page on Sport.pl, and no other language versions are moving in the graph, so the result is not independently confirmed here.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV page on Italian Wikipedia: vandalism reverted, no further activity
stories.summary: This update finds no new activity. The graph still shows the same 4 edits on it.wiki's "Papa Leone XIV" page, and nothing came after Titore's revert (rev 153000750). The scout called this routine editing, but it is vandalism: one temporary account (~2026-54751-20) and two editors who undid its changes. Its second edit (rev 153000718) changed "primo papa... proveniente dagli Stati Uniti" (the first pope from the United States) to "secondo papa" (the second). Titore restored "primo" in rev 153000750. The text of the first vandal edit (rev 153000669) and the content of Moderatore Automatico's revert of it (rev 153000677) can no longer be retrieved. The likeliest reason is that administrators hid the revision because it was offensive, which fits the prior brief's description of insults and drug slang, but I have not confirmed this. Nothing points to a real-world event. Watch for repeat attempts that might lead to page protection.

stories.headline: De-wiki housekeeping: Stratz bio tidied up; new Kirk T. McDonald page tagged for speedy deletion
stories.summary: This is routine German Wikipedia maintenance, not a news event. Heinz Stratz is a writer and translator who lived 1897–1941. Experienced maintainers are tidying a new biography of him. M2k~dewiki added the Personendaten template, Normdaten IDs (GND/LCCN/VIAF), a sort key and categories (rev 271486638). Magipulus added categories and fixed links. According to his edit summary, Magipulus also changed the place of death because "Herzberg bei Murmansk" seems to have been a Wehrmacht nickname for a hill, not a real town. The big churn on Kirk T. McDonald (Wikidata Q105708212, probably the Princeton physicist) comes from one new article: Alexandre Vendryes, an account with 19 edits, created it at about 5 KB and then cut about 770 bytes. M2k~dewiki made a small fix, and Flossenträger then posted "SLA+", meaning a speedy-deletion request. None of the three McDonald revisions can be fetched any more and the page has no summary, so it was most likely deleted. That inference is my only uncertainty, and I could not read those diffs. There are no reverts, no other language versions involved, and nothing points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Simple English 'Ku Klux Klan' article hit by vandalism from one temporary account, reverted
stories.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56022-80) added racist, sexually explicit insults to the Simple English Wikipedia 'Ku Klux Klan' article three times in about 8 minutes. None of the added text was encyclopedic content. ChenzwBot automatically reverted the first insertion (rev 11035809). The account then added two more (revs 11035817, 11035824), and Spiderone reverted both, putting back the bot's clean version. Only one page in one language was affected, and nothing suggests a real-world event behind it. The dossier lists 9 edits by this account, but all of them are on this page. I read the three insertions.

stories.headline: BBC to close BBC Three, BBC Scotland channel and Radio 4 Extra in spring 2027, edits say
stories.summary: Three registered editors (VernardoLau, Benmathieson901, Benjamintchip) edited the English BBC Three and BBC Scotland (TV channel) articles in parallel over about 50 minutes, with no reverts. The BBC Radio 4 Extra article was also edited in the same window by VernardoLau plus two other editors, which makes six distinct editors across the cluster. On BBC Three, Benmathieson901 added a section saying the BBC announced on 20 October 2026 that the BBC Three and BBC Scotland linear channels will close in spring 2027 and go online-only, as part of a plan to cut £500m by 2028. On the BBC Scotland channel page, VernardoLau rewrote the lead and History section to give the same news, adding that the content will move to BBC iPlayer and some programmes will air on the Scottish versions of BBC One and BBC Two. Benjamintchip added "Spring 2027 (planned)" as the closing date in both infoboxes. Every addition cites the same BBC News article dated 20 October 2026, with an archived copy and a byline later added as Steven McIntosh. This looks like a real corporate announcement. I haven't checked the BBC article itself or read the Radio 4 Extra diffs, and the exact closure date is still only "spring 2027".

stories.headline: ALCS page wrap-up: Rays beat Guardians 4–2 to reach World Series vs. Brewers
stories.summary: The 2026 ALCS article is getting wrap-up edits after the series ended, not live in-game updates as the scout guessed. BaseballFanatic1 added a Game 6 recap: Yandy Díaz hit a two-run homer in the eighth to make it 7–3, and Bryan Baker pitched a scoreless ninth. The same edit says the Rays are heading to their third World Series, citing an MLB.com piece headlined "Rays finish off Guards to set up World Series clash vs. Crew". That editor also bolded the Rays as winners (4–2) in the composite line score and raised total attendance from 197,475 to 207,475. Smitty Smitty added that Junior Caminero was named ALCS MVP, then removed it about 14 seconds later, so the MVP award is unconfirmed by these edits. The other changes are small copyedits and wikilinks, with no reverts between editors and no vandalism. The Brewers–Rays matchup already shows up in tracked stories about the 2026 World Series page (s_a9b43062, s_5a8fb50c), so this is follow-up to a known result rather than new news. That supports a routine, low-priority story, and it could be linked to the World Series story.

stories.headline: Ivar Aasen article on no.wiki hit by schoolyard-style vandalism, quickly reverted
stories.summary: Over about 20 minutes, two temporary accounts vandalised the opening sentence of the Norwegian Wikipedia biography of Ivar Aasen (1813–1896), the creator of Nynorsk. Neither edit relates to any real event. Account ~2026-56235-93 first changed his life dates to "1967–1969" (rev 26005573, labelled "En feil", meaning "an error"), then piped the link for "språkforsker" (linguist) to an insult meaning "sex offender" (rev 26005581). Patandor, an experienced patroller with 66 edits on the page, reverted both. Minutes later a second temporary account, ~2026-56144-51, swapped "språkforsker" for a vulgar phrase (rev 26005592), and Patandor reverted that within 5 minutes (rev 26005597). The scout read this as routine maintenance with no reverts, but that was wrong: the "no reverts" count came from the revert flag not being set on Patandor's rollbacks. Two separate temporary accounts doing the same thing could mean a classroom or coordinated prank, but nothing suggests a news hook. The article is clean now.

stories.headline: Routine cleanup of de-wiki bio of MDR presenter Henriette Fee Grützner
stories.summary: Three registered editors made five small edits to the German Wikipedia article on presenter and actress Henriette Fee Grützner over about 15 minutes. None were reverted. Andim filled in her full birth date (21 October 1987) in the person-data template. Hahnenkleer added a link to her personal website and changed her MDR stint on "Einfach genial" from "since April 2019" to "between 2019 and 2023", citing the show's own article. A third editor added a stage role at Boulevardtheater Dresden ("Die Weihnachtsgans Auguste", since 2024). All of these changes are maintenance or catch-up edits that bring older facts up to date. They show no sign of a new event, and no pages in other languages are involved.

stories.headline: Philip Dwyer vandalism and Birthmark self-linking both reverted; no new activity
stories.summary: Nothing has happened on either page since the last brief. The last edit in the graph is IrisChronomia's revert on Birthmark (film) at ts 1792346067. On Philip Dwyer (English Wikipedia), the temporary account ~2026-46936-96 made two more edits. One changed the short description to "far-right anti-immigration "activist" and dole sponger" (rev 1380905651). The other changed the infobox name to "Angry Phil" (rev 1380905761). SuperPianoMan9167 reverted both about 16 seconds later. That makes four vandal edits from this one account, and each was undone within about 25 seconds. On Birthmark (film), an account named Vikram Shreedharan, the film's credited director, writer and producer, turned that name into an external-style link to Draft:Vikram_Shreedharan (rev 1380905847), and IrisChronomia reverted it. This was the third self-linking attempt, so it looks like a conflict of interest, but we can't confirm the account is really the filmmaker. Only English Wikipedia is involved, and there's no sign of a real-world event behind either page.

stories.headline: 2026 World Series page: routine copyediting before Brewers–Rays Game 1
stories.summary: The English article "2026 World Series" is getting small, low-stakes edits ahead of the series. Its text describes a matchup between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays, citing Oct. 15–16, 2026 sources, including a Brewers sweep of the Dodgers for the NL pennant. The diffs I read are all minor: a likely Rays Game 1 starter (Drew Rasmussen) added inside a hidden comment while the infobox still reads TBD; wikilink fixes (1957/1958 World Series, COVID-19 pandemic); and a clause added that Milwaukee is chasing its first title since 1957. A cluster of edits labeled "cleaned up", "clarification" and "redundant" came from one editor. There are no reverts and no fights over content, and no other pages or languages are moving with this one. The page has about 104 edits from a wider pool of regular sports editors, which is normal for an upcoming event. Nothing here suggests news beyond the series being scheduled. Expect bigger activity once games are played and scores get added.

stories.headline: Temp account's push to remove Greek Jewish history fails as patrollers restore all four pages
stories.summary: This is the same campaign we already track, now winding down, and not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56372-73 made one last round of removals on English Wikipedia between about 1792539099 and 1792539142. It cut the 8 KB Ioannina "Jewish community" section a fifth time (rev 1381244163). That section covers the 1829 Romaniote synagogue and the deportation of 1,870 Jews to Auschwitz in March 1944. This time the account argued that "religious texts are not valid historical sources". It also again removed the clause "reaches back two thousand years" from the opening of History of the Jews in Thessaloniki (1381244231), and again removed the synagogue image on Larissa. All three were reverted within about a minute: EndTheWikiEditor on Ioannina (1381244273), AriuCH on Larissa, and Discospinster on the Jewish-history article. The graph shows no edits on any of the four pages since then, so all the content stands restored and the account looks to have stopped, or been stopped, though we can't confirm a block from here. Over the whole campaign it was one account against six patrollers, with 18 edits by the remover across four pages, no other language editions affected and no outside trigger visible. News value is low; only watch for a renewed attempt or page protection.

stories.headline: Russian 2026 deaths list adds ex-UK MP Andy King; routine upkeep continues
stories.summary: Since the last brief, ru:Список умерших в 2026 году has had two new edits that matter. An editor added former British MP Andy King, aged 78, under 19 October (rev 155708739), sourced to a Warwickshire World obituary for the "former Rugby MP". A second editor then changed only the dash in that line (rev 155708792). Another editor added French rapper Prince Waly, aged 34, sourced to Le Figaro (rev 155708703). Prince Waly was already in the prior brief, so this is the same entry, not a new death. The graph has no Andy King page in any language, and editing is still limited to this one list, with 4 editors, 9 edits and no reverts. This is normal upkeep, not a major breaking death. One uncertainty: I have not independently checked that Andy King is the Labour MP for Rugby (1997–2005); that identification rests on the source headline.

stories.headline: "Silenced" film hatnote dispute over Tommy Robinson wording; no news event in cluster
stories.summary: The only new activity is on the English page "Silenced (2011 film)". There, "Arts culture editor" kept rewriting the hatnotes at the top of the page. One change relabelled Tommy Robinson's film as "the libellous film produced by the far-right, anti-Islamic activist" (rev 1380871975, then rev 1380874833). That edit cited a Guardian story from October 2024 about Robinson admitting contempt of court. Three different patrollers using the Interceptor tool reverted the edits: Theeverywhereperson, Celjski Grad as non-neutral (rev 1380875585) and MarioWonderExpert (rev 1380876920). The same user also kept changing the link for a 2026 Australian documentary from "Silenced (documentary film)" to "Silenced (2026 film)", saying the page had been moved (rev 1380876769). They also edited the "Silenced (2026 film)" page itself. So this is a one-person neutrality and link dispute over hatnote wording, not an edit war between equals, and the source it relies on is old news. Telangana, "Walk On (U2 song)" and Luny Tunes were covered in the earlier brief: unrelated patrol cleanup. They share no subject, and the only link between them is patroller Celjski Grad. Everything is on English Wikipedia, and nothing points to a new real-world event. The 2026 documentary's release may explain why that editor is interested, but I couldn't confirm that.

stories.headline: Unsourced family detail added to NSW Premier Chris Minns page, quickly reverted
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56297-75), making its only edit, added one unsourced sentence to Chris Minns's English Wikipedia biography. It named a daughter ("Tyla Minns") and a wife ("Mel Minns"). The edit summary was "About his family in the Northern beaches". About 70 seconds later, Qwerty123M, a registered editor with 17 edits on the page, reverted it as a good-faith but unsourced change. The existing sourced sentence about his brother Jim was left as it was. Nothing suggests a real-world event: there was one edit, no follow-up, and no activity on the article in other languages. The added names are unverified, and we should not report them. This is routine maintenance on a biography of a living person, not an edit war or a vandalism spree.

stories.headline: 49ers beat Commanders 23–17 to go 6–0, season page shows
stories.summary: Three registered editors made four quick edits to the English 2026 San Francisco 49ers season article, updating it after the Week 6 home game against the Washington Commanders. Bluejay14 marked the game as a win, 23–17, and linked the NFL.com recap (rev 1381119531). Useight changed the infobox record from 5–0 to 6–0 (1381119737) and filled in a box score that adds up to the same result: 49ers 13-7-3-0, Commanders 3-0-7-7 (1381119812). TheGoodGeneral 1 then linked the Week 7 game at Atlanta in the schedule (1381120012). The editors agree with each other, nobody reverted anything, and only one language edition was edited. This looks like normal post-game upkeep, not a disputed or breaking story. The score comes only from Wikipedia edits and hasn't been checked against an outside source, but the three editors' changes all match.

stories.headline: Fake 'Jack Voss' AFL profile grows again and stays live after patrol reverts restored it
stories.summary: This update belongs in the existing schoolkid vandalism story. It is not a new event. The latest large edit on 'Jack Voss' (rev 1381087356, +1021) is not a blanking. Temporary account ~2026-56201-43 added a mostly empty AFL season-stats table and changed a games figure from 21 to 26, building out the fake "Voss the Boss" Richmond profile. I need to correct my earlier brief. Rev 1381086467 shows this same account blanking the page to "#redirect [[A]]", and the removed text includes the made-up infobox (born 2008, "2026 draft", 2027 debut) sitting under a broken "#redirect [[Jock Voss ]]" line. The Dr vulpes and ClueBot NG reverts went back "to version by Afltubes", so they put the fake profile back rather than removing it. As of the last edit in the graph, nobody has reverted the fabricated content and it is still live. Castle Hill High School has had no edits since Dr vulpes' revert. The account switching between blanking and expanding the page is probably the same prankster or a classmate, but I can't confirm that. The page needs to be restored to a clean redirect and watched for BLP problems, since it may name a real minor.

stories.headline: Minor wording tweaks on itwiki Akira Tozawa page, one reverted; no news event
stories.summary: Three edits to the Italian Wikipedia article on wrestler Akira Tozawa in about 15 minutes. A temporary account changed the lead from "In carriera ha detenuto" to "In WWE ha vinto" and shortened the championship link label (rev 152955778). Amirzat, a registered editor, reverted that change word for word (rev 152955996). A second temporary account deleted one line listing the 2018 NXT North American Championship Invitational (rev 152955814), and that deletion has not been reverted. None of these edits adds a new title, match result, injury, release or any other real-world development. The graph shows no linked pages in other languages and no edits to them. This looks like routine copy-editing with a single revert, not an edit war or a news event. There is a little uncertainty: the line removal has no explanation, but it is small and doesn't point to anything happening off-wiki.

stories.headline: New ru-wiki stub on 1990s Moscow electronic band 'Spirali' tagged for deletion
stories.summary: The churn comes from a page being created, not from anything happening in the world. On ru-wiki, user Дальных created 'СПИРАЛИ' (+1808 bytes), a page with nothing but infoboxes. It describes a Moscow electronic group (big beat, breakbeat, trip hop) active 1997–2003, with labels and members listed. It has a blank, duplicated infobox template and no prose. A temporary account (~2026-54331-87) then deleted the empty infobox and added a {{Db-nn}} speedy-deletion tag for lack of notability. EyeBot automatically reverted that edit based on an ORES score (+919). The bot's revert is not a revert pair between people, so this is not an edit war. The 3646 churn is just these three edits added up. I see no sign of a real-world event behind the page. The page will probably be re-tagged for deletion or cleaned up.

stories.headline: Old Kharkiv war-crimes material restored to ruwiki page on Russian Gen. Makovetsky
stories.summary: The ruwiki article on Lt. Gen. Oleg Makovetsky, commander of Russia's 6th Air and Air Defence Army, had five edits from three accounts. A temporary account added "Ukraine" to his combat record (rev 155689864) and a line saying he "is accused of war crimes in Ukraine" (rev 155689885). The anti-vandalism bot EyeBot reverted both, and neither edit cited a source. Then BFD-69 undid an older edit, 153404646 by Shluzzzoid (rev 155690163, +3494). That restored a lead sentence and a section saying Makovetsky ordered the bombing of Kharkiv and Kharkiv Oblast, and that Kharkiv regional prosecutors have named him a suspect. All of the restored sources are from March 2022 (LB.ua, Volynnews, Futura News). Nothing points to a new event such as a death, award, arrest or new charges. This looks like an ongoing content dispute over Ukraine-related allegations, not a news trigger. Uncertainty: one more removal and restore would make this an edit war, and a new development could still be behind the anonymous edits, but nothing in the text shows one.

stories.headline: Lithuanian Wikipedia: patroller reverts new user's additions to business/marketing pages
stories.summary: This is routine maintenance, not a news event. A new account, Mazasisatlas4s, made its only two edits to two Lithuanian Wikipedia pages about 13 minutes apart. On "Verslo administravimas" (Business administration) it added 614 bytes; the edit summary describes text about accreditation of study programmes. On "Rinkodara" (Marketing) it added 807 bytes; the summary describes text on how specialist training in Lithuania has developed since 1990. The patroller Homo ergaster undid both edits within about 2 minutes each. That account was doing the same to other pages at the time (Wii U, Mario, Lego, Imunoanalizė and others). Nobody re-added the text, so this is not an edit war, and there's no sign of an outside event. The topic and style suggest a student or someone adding material about their institution, but that's a guess: none of the diffs would load, so this account rests only on edit metadata and summaries, and I can't say why the text was removed. The scout's "four editors" doesn't match the dossier, which shows two.

stories.headline: Vandalism on es-wiki "Sexualidad" and "Nelson Mandela"; bots revert most of it
stories.summary: This is vandalism by temporary accounts on Spanish Wikipedia. Nothing happened in the real world. I disagree with the scout's note on one point: the large change on "Sexualidad" (−1883 bytes) was not a cleanup. The account ~2026-56166-73 (edit summary "Errores") deleted most of the opening section, including cited text on animal sexual behaviour, and replaced part of it with "NUNJAMASSASSSSSSS USES WIKIPEDIA". Automoderador put the text back 8 seconds later. Earlier, the same account had swapped "técnicas" for "tung tun sahurr", a meme phrase, and SeroBOT reverted that within 8 seconds. On "Nelson Mandela", ~2026-56166-32 added a stray comma, which Automoderador reverted. ~2026-55928-03 then inserted "peo" before the birth date. The graph shows no revert of that edit, so it may still be live; that should be checked on the wiki itself. Mandela's dates (1918–2013) were not changed. The two pages are not about the same topic. The likely link is the editors: the temporary-account names ~2026-56166-32 and ~2026-56166-73 look very similar, so they may have been created close together, perhaps by the same person or the same place (e.g. a school). That link is a guess, and it does not extend to ~2026-55928-03.

stories.headline: Barbera Thornhill page: small dispute over YouTube-sourced claim about her son
stories.summary: On the en-wiki biography of Barbera Thornhill (US Ambassador-at-Large to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons since Oct 2026), a temporary account added one sentence: "She has a son named Hale Thornhill-Wilson." Its only source was a YouTube video titled "This Woman Eerily Appeared Out Of Nowhere" from the channel MinutesOfHorror (rev 1381173524). Realcosmixyt, a regular patroller, removed it as unsourced. A single-edit account (H1234ek) put it back, saying the information was correct but not the original source. Realcosmixyt removed it again because YouTube is not a reliable source (rev 1381175366). All the churn is that one 245-byte sentence going in and out four times within about 20 minutes. There's no sign of a real-world event and no movement on other languages or pages. Uncertain: it's a claim about a family member on a living person's biography, it's still unverified, and it could come back if more single-edit accounts keep pushing it.

stories.headline: zhwiki Our Lady's College (HK) page: school vandalism fully reverted, no new activity
stories.summary: This is the same vandalism already tracked on the zhwiki article 聖母書院 (Our Lady's College, Wong Tai Sin, Hong Kong). It is not a news event. One account, Nickychinnnnnn, made four edits in about 10 minutes. Patrollers BanSpdRunOrMaybeNot and XiaoFui undid each one within about 1–5 minutes, and the page is back to its earlier version. The two diffs I read show the vandalism: one inflated the campus from 6,600 to 100,000 m², with 10 playgrounds, 30 labs and "lucky swimming pools", and the other added a current history department head as a notable alumna. A small correction to the scout's note: only one revert carries a revert flag, but the comments show all four edits were undone. The graph has no edits after the last revert (rev 95181665), and the pattern is two patrollers against one vandal, not an edit war.

stories.headline: UFO sightings list: same temp account re-adds unsourced text after revert
stories.summary: This is the same low-level churn on English Wikipedia's 'List of reported UFO sightings' that we are already tracking. Temporary account ~2026-56176-35 first added a +50-byte "sighting of two boys who saw a alein" (rev 1381290431). AndyTheGrump reverted it as "unsourced nonsense". A second temporary account's +7-byte edit was also reverted, as "rvv". After both reverts, ~2026-56176-35 came back with a new +112-byte, unsourced and ungrammatical sentence (rev 1381291325): "Since them there has been very few amounts of sightings if so a lot have been put online on different websites". The graph does not yet show that edit as reverted. There are only 3 editors, one page and no other languages, and no edit names a dated or sourced incident, so nothing points to a real-world event. It looks like persistent novice or test editing that will probably be reverted again. It is not an edit war: one experienced editor is reverting a temporary account that keeps re-adding content.

stories.headline: Demervall sv-wiki bio: temp account's rewrite rolled back twice, page now quiet, no news
stories.summary: Nothing has been edited since the last brief. EPIC's rollback (rev 59785662) is still the latest edit on sv:Magnus Demervall. The diffs confirm what happened. Temporary account ~2026-56289-70 put its shorter rewrite back (rev 59785656). The rewrite replaced the infobox and the detailed lead with a short "organisationschef" lead sourced to Riksdagen, and removed his birth name (Andersson), his home in Segersta, his Egyptian father and the Centre Party career section. EPIC then restored Yger's version (rev 59785662). This was one temporary account against two patrollers, two rollbacks in total. It looks like an attempt to tidy up or curate the biography, possibly with a conflict of interest. It is not a real-world event: the only facts in it (CEO of Företagarna since February 2025) are old news. The scout's 'no reverts' reading is wrong because the rollbacks aren't flagged as reverts in the graph. The scout is right that the story has no broader significance. Things to watch: whether the account comes back, or whether the rewrite turns up on other language versions.

stories.headline: Cuti Romero (es): no new activity; sourcing edits and bot reverts remain routine
stories.summary: I re-checked the story and found no new edits since the prior brief. The page still has six edits from three accounts: temporary account ~2026-44405-78, SeroBOT and Automoderador. The user's edits were reverted twice by bots and restored both times. No humans pushed back and no other language editions changed. In rev 175884041 the user adds press citations to claims the article already made: that Romero plays for Atlético de Madrid and captains Argentina. The citations are Infobae (2026-10-18), Clarín (2026-10-13) and La Gaceta (2026-09-25), which say Scaloni named him captain after Messi's farewell. In rev 175884004 the user flattens the career list and removes the loan markers. That leaves Genoa as 2018-20, drops the Juventus row, and adds a typo-ridden claim that he never played for Juventus. The edits add no new real-world event. The open risk is that a human patroller undoes the lower-quality rewrite.

stories.headline: France fuel protests page logs 17 Oct riots and Macron crackdown vow; Reformation vandal reverted
stories.summary: The scout called the fuel-protests edits "routine". The diffs show the opposite: enwiki '2026 French fuel protests' is recording a major escalation. Rev 1380921375 contains text, cited to AFP, CNN, ABC and Al Jazeera, saying that on 17 October 2026 protests spread to about 110 cities, joining student protests and a revived yellow-vest movement. Turnout figures are 550,000 from the Interior Ministry and 800,000 from the CGT union. PM Sébastien Lecornu reported 1,200 arrests and 150 police officers injured, and Limoges's Hôtel de Ville was firebombed and burned down. Rev 1380919091 adds that Macron promised a "firm response" to the rioting (KATV, dated 18 Oct). Most of this text was already on the page before these edits, which polish it (one editor is fixing the transcription of a slogan on a yellow vest). The page has only one active content editor (OrdinariusFingius) and no other-language pages linked in the graph, so the facts rest on the cited sources, not wide editor activity. Separately, '~2026-55882-34' tried to insert "Palestinian" into an image caption (rev 1380920053) and was reverted as unsourced. The Reformation thread is still plain vandalism: temporary account ~2026-55860-40 kept re-adding a 27-byte change ("suck it"; rev 1380920471, text cut off in the tool) and four patrollers/bots reverted it. The two pages are linked only by patroller Celjski Grad.

stories.headline: Lua Blanco article: follow-up edits only tidy up; cancer death account unchanged
stories.summary: This is the same ptwiki page as the breaking story on the death of Lua Blanco, the 'Rebelde' actress, and the new edits add nothing to it. They are housekeeping. Francisco Leandro made the death category more specific, changing it to "deaths from cancer in Rio de Janeiro state" (rev 73241414). Guedexx tidied the infobox and cut the family list down to the relatives who have their own articles (rev 73241172). Lord Zaxor fixed a spelling error ("descrição" to "discrição", meaning "privacy") and complained in his edit summary (rev 73241408): 79a's earlier undo of the Creutzfeldt-Jakob vandalism had also brought the typo back (rev 73241381). That summary was annoyed, but it was a single fix, not a back-and-forth edit war. The scout's "no reverts" note is slightly off because of that one undo, which was a correct one. The article still says she died on 18 October 2026, aged 39, of intestinal cancer, citing Quem, CNN Brasil and Jornal de Brasília. I have not checked those outlets independently. I suggest merging this into the tracked breaking story rather than treating it as a separate event.

stories.headline: Estonia football page: old Oct 2025 results pruned, briefly reverted, then removed again
stories.summary: This is routine maintenance on the English Wikipedia page for the Estonia national football team, not news. Chelsdog, an established editor with 335 edits, removed two match boxes from October 2025: the 1–3 home loss to Italy on 11 October and the 1–1 draw with Moldova on 14 October, both 2026 World Cup qualifiers. TonySt reverted this as "unexplained content removal". Chelsdog then removed the same 1,589 bytes again with the explanation "over one year", which fits the usual practice of keeping only the last 12 months of results in the recent-results section, since the edit timestamps fall about a year after those matches. The scout's 4,767 churn figure is just the same block counted three times, and no new facts were added. There was one revert and one re-removal, so this is not yet an edit war, but it could become one if TonySt reverts again. I didn't read the first removal (rev 1381261390), but its size matches the other two.

stories.headline: Spanish Armada article hit by two schoolyard-style vandal edits, both reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. About 22 minutes apart, two different temporary accounts each replaced the lead paragraph of en-wiki's Spanish Armada article with nonsense. The first claimed the Armada "never happened" and talked about Alvin and the Chipmunks and Eric Cartman. The second was "RICARDO KILLLED HGENRY TYHE 8". Editor RFNirmala reverted the first within about 4 minutes, and ClueBot NG reverted the second within 10 seconds. The large churn the scout flagged is just these blankings and their reverts adding up. There's no real dispute and no sign of other language versions being touched. The pattern looks like classroom vandalism, possibly students working on a history lesson, but that's a guess. Worth a semi-protection watch, not a story.

stories.headline: Wikipedia editors list Brock Purdy ahead of Lamar Jackson as NFL career passer rating leader
stories.summary: This is not an edit war. The flurry on the Lamar Jackson article was a short, one-sided disagreement that settled itself, apparently prompted by a stats update. Tb101202 removed Jackson's "Career passer rating (minimum 1,500 attempts): 102.7" record line. GOAT Bones231012 restored it, calling it an unexplained removal, then undid their own restore within about two minutes. They then changed the lead from saying Jackson "ranks first" on the all-time regular-season career passer rating list to "ranks second." In the same few minutes, Tb101202 edited "List of NFL career passer rating leaders": they changed a rating from 105.4 to 105.6 and replaced the lead image and caption to say Brock Purdy "is the all-time leader in career passer rating for the regular season." This most likely means Purdy recently passed Jackson, perhaps after a game or after reaching the minimum number of attempts. But no edit cites a source or a specific game, only two editors were involved, and no other languages have moved, so the trigger is unconfirmed.

stories.headline: ISL 2026–27 page updated after Match 10; East Bengal win 4–0 at Churchill Brothers
stories.summary: This is the same set of 8 edits the prior brief covered, on the English 2026–27 Indian Super League page. Three registered editors (Sherifkk, Iampavan19, HelloWorld8800) made them in about 12 minutes, and none were reverted. No edits have come in since the last one at ts 1792331389. The infobox diff shows matches going from 9 to 10 and total goals from 23 to 27. It also adds a new biggest away win, Churchill Brothers 0–4 East Bengal (18 October 2026), and names Bipin Singh as joint top scorer on 2 goals. The latest edit only shortens a link label to "Mohun Bagan SG". This is ordinary result-tracking with no dispute or vandalism. The score and scorer come only from the diffs and were not checked against outside sources.

stories.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: temp account renames birthplace Poyo→Poio, likely good faith
stories.summary: There has been one new edit to Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography since the last brief, and I read it. Temporary account ~2026-55802-76 changed the infobox birthplace from [[Poyo]] to [[Poio]], with the summary "correct name of city of birth" (rev 175887487). Poio is the official Galician name of the town, so this looks like a good-faith naming fix rather than trolling. It contains no insults or "Quintana" jokes. The edit also pulled several infobox fields onto the same lines as wikitext comments, and moved the club list onto the "equipos =" line. That is the same formatting side-effect as the earlier unsourced shirt-number edit (rev 175886406), so it may be an editor-tool artefact; it probably doesn't break how the page displays, but I haven't confirmed that. I agree with the scout that this isn't a new event. I disagree with "no reverts": Saloca's rev 175887360 just before this was a rollback, even though the graph doesn't mark it as one. As noted in earlier briefs, the infobox name "Rodríguez Parera" and the unsourced shirt-number change 32→20 may still be live; I haven't checked the current page. This is still small-scale activity on one page in one language, and the vandalism spree seems to be dying down into cleanup.

stories.headline: Edits say Tennessee Rep. Dennis Powers lost Aug. 6 GOP primary to Noah Smith (unsourced)
stories.summary: The scout called the side pages in this cluster unrelated noise. One of them is actually the most newsworthy item here. Editor Easttnlover added a paragraph to Dennis Powers' article (rev 1381088112, comment "election results"). It says challenger Noah Smith beat Powers in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee House District 36, 8,034 votes (66.97%) to 3,963 (33.03%). That would end Powers' bid for a ninth term. Patroller F0malhaut42 reverted it for lacking a reliable source. Easttnlover then changed the infobox to show his term ending in November 2026, with Noah Smith as successor (rev 1381088402), and started a new "Noah Smith" article (3 edits, diff not readable). Everything comes from one low-edit account, with no citation and no other editors or languages backing it up, so I can't confirm it. That said, the vote totals are specific and add up, and the timing fits a primary night. The School District 43 Coquitlam edits are routine principal updates, as the earlier brief said. The LTE Advanced edits were a test edit (an email address added) that was reverted.

stories.headline: No new activity on Ruhainies page; the 3,540 "churn" is the same three vandal edits
stories.summary: This is a re-flag, not new activity. The page has no edits since the prior brief. The graph shows only three edits on ms:Ruhainies: 6987545, 6987548 and 6987549, made by three single-edit temporary accounts in about 6 minutes. Their sizes (+62, +3443, +35) add up to the 3,540 churn the scout flagged. I re-read two of those diffs. Rev 6987545 changes her name to "Rusak Rumah Tangga Org" ("wrecker of people's marriages") and adds mocking notes to her occupations. Rev 6987548 pastes in an unsourced gossip timeline of the Bella Astillah and Aliff Aziz marriage, which ends with the March 2024 khalwat (close-proximity) arrest and the June 2024 divorce, so no new real-world event. None of the edits have been reverted, and no linked pages in other languages exist or moved. The earlier finding stands: targeted vandalism of a living person's biography that is still live. It needs patroller attention, but it isn't news.

stories.headline: No new activity on Greek 'Hare' article; name-insertion vandalism still reverted
stories.summary: This is an update on the earlier brief, and nothing has changed. The last edit to the Greek Wikipedia article Λαγός (hare) is still Fotis A.'s DEFAULTSORT edit (rev 11887251). No temporary account has edited the page since. I re-read two diffs. In rev 11887239, a temporary account added "Αγρια:Βασιλης / Επιθετικα:Σταυρος / Ηρεμα:Σωτηρης" ("wild: Vasilis / aggressive: Stavros / calm: Sotiris"). In rev 11887250, Fotis A. removed the names and labels that were still on the page. The graph shows the three temporary accounts edited only this page. Fotis A. was working through Greek film articles before and after, so the cleanup looks like routine patrolling, not a targeted dispute. There is no sign of a real-world trigger and no edit war. One small loose end: the editor totals for two temporary accounts (4 and 3 edits) are higher than the edits the graph shows. That may be a counting quirk, but it means some of their edits may be missing from the graph.

stories.headline: Rivonia Trial vandalism reverted; no new edits since cleanup
stories.summary: This is a follow-up on a vandalism burst already tracked on the English "Rivonia Trial" article. There is no news event. Re-reading the diffs confirms the earlier brief. In rev 1381291938, a temporary account replaced the trial's location (Pretoria's Palace of Justice and the Old Synagogue) with a joke: "Miss Zhomes class room", a trial lasting 3.5 years, and a line about homosexuality "in the United States". Four minutes later, in rev 1381292185, a second temporary account fixed the joke's spelling and added Donald Trump, Joe Biden, Joseph Stalin and "Doctor Disrepsepct" to the list of men convicted. In rev 1381292210, 21 seconds after that, Lynch44 restored PhotographyEdits' last good version, which removed both edits. The graph shows no edits to the page after the restore, no other language versions moved, and no related pages were involved. The mention of a teacher points to students, but that is a guess.

stories.headline: Knecht page protected after Lakers release; latest edits are only formatting
stories.summary: This is the same story as the tracked Lakers–Dalton Knecht waiver, with no new development. Since the last brief, which covered the New York Post citation added in rev 1381074631, only two edits have landed, not three. Vic Hawk changed how the infobox writes his Lakers years, from {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2026|start}} to {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} (rev 1381076221). That fixes the season notation and does not change the facts. Ymblanter then added a {{pp-protected}} tag (rev 1381076601). The tag suggests an administrator has protected the page, likely because several temporary accounts were editing it during the news spike, but I did not check the protection log. Nothing has been reverted since Bagumba's first revert, and the sourced waiver line still stands. The graph still shows no activity on the Lakers team or season pages or in other languages.

stories.headline: K-pop singer Ejae reported married to Sam Kim in Seoul; Wikipedia adds Vogue source
stories.summary: Two editors updated the English Wikipedia article on singer-songwriter Ejae (KPop Demon Hunters) to say she has married her fiancé, former music producer Sam Kim. First, a temporary account (~2026-56339-92) rewrote the Personal life section to say they married on October 17, 2026 at her grandfather's estate in Seoul. In doing so it removed a February 2026 Chosun Daily citation that had described a planned November 7 wedding in Los Angeles. The same account added no new source and changed the infobox from "partner" to "spouse". About 15 minutes later, registered editor Jamie Eilat cleaned up the infobox ({{marriage|Sam Kim|2026}}) and added a citation to a Vogue piece dated October 19, 2026, titled "Inside Ejae and Samuel Kim's Garden Wedding at Her Grandfather's Former Home in Seoul". The article now says simply "They married in October 2026." Uncertain: I have not checked the Vogue article myself, and the exact date (Oct 17) currently comes only from the unsourced edit. There are no reverts and nothing suggesting vandalism. This is celebrity personal news, so it is a low-stakes routine update.

stories.headline: Vandalism spree on ko-wiki: artist page blanked, '케이팝모터스' page spammed
stories.summary: The scout's guess of "routine expansion" doesn't hold up. The edit metadata shows coordinated vandalism, not content work. On 정은혜 (미술가), the user '아정당' made five removals in a row ending in "문서를 비움" (page blanked). After a +3665 restore by a temporary account, '에스아이네트 본사' removed text four more times. The page 케이팝모터스 has been created over and over with the text "반달" (Korean slang for vandal) repeated. It was also briefly made a redirect to 찰스 폰지 (Charles Ponzi). Several accounts are involved: '아정당' and '아정당모바일' (names that look like an impersonation pair), '에스아이네트 본사', and three temporary accounts. The same accounts also hit unrelated pages: 주체사상탑 (the Juche Tower), 전남광주통합특별시체육회 and 두일신풍연립. That pattern points to a vandal or sockpuppet campaign, not a real-world event. Two caveats: none of the revision diffs could be fetched (they may have been deleted by admins), so this rests on edit summaries, size changes and editor patterns. No language versions in other wikis moved.

stories.headline: Troy Denning forum-feud vandalism with slurs reverted again; page clean for now
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The en.wiki biography of Star Wars novelist Troy Denning was hit twice by temporary accounts. Each one added an unsourced "2024 SI Controversy" section about a faked forum screenshot (UnuThul vs. Caedus). The section also named forum users and piped their names to slur articles (Faggot, Nigger, Retard (pejorative), Autism). BOZ removed the first insertion by hand as "obvious vandalism" (rev 1381116548). A second temporary account put it back (rev 1381116867). Admin PhilKnight then rolled that back (rev 1381118406, -1078); I read the diff and it removes the whole slur-laden section. The graph shows no edits after the rollback, so the page should be clean. The only remaining question is whether the same people come back, which could lead to page protection or revision deletion. The scout's note is correct: there are 2 vandal accounts and 2 reverts, all on one page in one language, and it continues the story already being tracked.

stories.headline: Timelash: vandal returns as protection lapses, reverted in seconds and page re-protected
stories.summary: This is vandalism on the English Wikipedia article for the 1985 Doctor Who serial Timelash, not a news event. A new account, 'TheProtectionlashHasExpired', made one edit (+169 bytes) whose edit summary pinged admins (Yamla, Ponyo, Zzuuzz, Pppery, Staraction, HJ Mitchell) to say "the protection has now expired". That fits a returning long-term abuser. SuperPianoMan9167 reverted it 7 seconds later. About six minutes after that, Dualcerb added {{pp-extended|small=yes}}, which I confirmed in the diff and which signals extended-confirmed protection is back on. I couldn't read the vandal's revision or the revert diff because Wikipedia returns no content for them, which suggests admins hid (revision-deleted) the vandal's text, so I don't know what it added. A graph search found no other edits in this window with the same taunting summary, so it hasn't spread so far. This matches the prior brief, and nothing new has happened.

stories.headline: Willards, Maryland: unsourced musician claim re-added once, reverted; page now quiet
stories.summary: This is minor vandalism with no real-world event behind it. Temporary account ~2026-56394-08 restored the line that ~2026-56393-78 had added to the lead, which I confirmed by reading that diff. The line says Willards is "home of the famous guitarist and lead singer of 7 Spirits Rd, Fender Kottemann, who also created Neon", and it has no source. DonnieNova had reverted the first insertion. Komethere reverted the restore with VandalHandle, citing "unsourced". The page has had no edits since Komethere's revert, it is back to its stable census-based lead, and only this one English-language page is involved. The two temporary accounts have consecutive numbers and each made a single edit, so they are probably the same person. That is an inference I haven't confirmed.

stories.headline: New dewiki article on 18th-century Hanoverian general Pufendorf; author copyedits
stories.summary: This update adds one edit to the story: A1000, who created the German article "Georg Siegmund von Pufendorf", removed 13 bytes with no edit summary. The diff shows a grammar fix only: a duplicated "das Regiment" was dropped from the sentence about him handing the Wendish territorial regiment to Johann Friedrich von Quernheim in 1788. The creation diff (+2,844), which I could read this time, confirms the article's content. Pufendorf was a Brunswick-Lüneburg major general, born in Minden in 1715 and died in Döhren in 1799. He rose from ensign (1738) to inspector of all the territorial regiments (Landregimenter) in 1788 and was made a noble of the Holy Roman Empire with his brothers in 1756. The article cites Poten's 1902 list of Hanoverian generals and a 1796 state calendar. One small error: the creation edit put him in the death-year category "Gestorben 1759" while the text gives 1799. I haven't confirmed whether a later small fix (for example M2k~dewiki's "k" edit) corrected it. There are still only three editors, all logged in, no reverts and no other languages, and nothing links the article to any current event. This is routine article creation and cleanup.

stories.headline: France imposes local curfews incl. Paris after weekend riots, per English Wikipedia edits
stories.summary: The English article "2026 French student protests" was created about 32 hours ago. It already has 42 edits from 13 named editors, which is more activity than the scout's 3-edit window showed. The most important recent edit (rev 1381068920) added that curfews were imposed in several cities, including Paris, and that PM Sébastien Lecornu called them "partial" and "very locally limited". It cites a Yahoo News piece dated 19 Oct. The surrounding text, credited to the BBC and the Interior Ministry, says about 2,400 people were arrested and about 1,000 police were injured (seven seriously) during Saturday's demonstrations. It says about 550,000 people took part and that looting continued on a smaller scale in Paris and Lyon on Sunday. The one revert was a single wording dispute: one editor removed "mostly peaceful" (rev 1381077449) and another put it back (rev 1381078771). That is one back-and-forth, not an edit war, and the other recent edits are cleanup. Caveats: these figures come from what the article says its sources report, and I have not checked them independently. The page also has no other-language versions linked in the graph, which is surprising for an event this size in France and worth checking for a missing French article.

stories.headline: Gwamba rapper page: one-off self-insertion vandalism, already reverted; no new activity
stories.summary: This story covers the same four en-wiki edits as the existing vandalism brief on "Gwamba", the page about Malawian rapper Duncan Zgambo. There has been no new activity since then. In rev 1381142938, the account "Yahaya Usman Gwamba" replaced the infobox details with his own: born 27/7/2000 in Argungu, studied at Kebbi State University, occupation "Billionaire Farmer". In rev 1381143102 the same account renamed the lead subject "YahayaUsmanGwamba" and deleted "Malawi". F0malhaut42 and Itsjuenyin (using the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool) reverted both edits within about two minutes. The graph doesn't flag these as reverts, but the edit comments show they were. No other pages, languages or editors are involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. I agree with the scout: this is minor, already-resolved churn and should be folded into the existing story rather than opened as a new one.

stories.headline: Routine itwiki edits: Aeneid image swaps and a page move for astronomer Cassini IV
stories.summary: Two unrelated Italian Wikipedia articles are getting ordinary maintenance edits, and nothing points to a real-world event. On 'Eneide', temporary account ~2026-52083-13 keeps rearranging and replacing illustrations (Ferdinand Bol, Pinelli and Carracci captions). M7 undid one round of these changes with a single revert. The editor then made the swaps again, and they are cosmetic, not vandalism. On 'Jean-Dominique Cassini (astronomo 1748)', Gambo7 finished a naming-convention move: the edit removed the {{Sposta}} move tag and stub tags, and the move comment points to a redirect from 'Jean-Dominique Cassini (1748-1845)'. One temporary account (~2026-56296-04) touched both pages, but only with 1-character whitespace fixes, so the overlap looks like chance. A small correction to the scout's note: there was one revert on Eneide, but it isn't an edit war.

stories.headline: Theranos article gets routine short-description and template tidy-ups; no news signal
stories.summary: Three registered editors made five small edits (deltas from -9 to +13) to the English Wikipedia Theranos article over about 90 minutes. No other language editions moved and nothing was flagged as a revert. GhostInTheMachine added the company's active years to the short description ("American health-technology company, 2003–2018"). Yedaman54 then changed it to "Defunct American health-technology company (2003–2018)" and re-dated the Use mdy dates and Use American English templates. GhostInTheMachine's next edit (-9, comment cites WP:SDDATES, diff not read) most likely returned it to the guideline's comma format. That is a small style disagreement, not an edit war. Hsw542 made a one-character grammar fix in the 2015–16 regulatory section without changing any substance. None of the edits adds new facts, sources, or current events, so this looks like ordinary maintenance. One caveat: I didn't read the -9 diff, so the exact wording that ended up on the page isn't confirmed.

stories.headline: Former Swedish ambassador Sven Hirdman dead at 87, Swedish Wikipedia says
stories.summary: The Swedish Wikipedia article on diplomat Sven Hirdman already says he died on 9 October 2026 in Stockholm. That claim cites a death notice in Dagens Nyheter and an SVT report headlined "Diplomaten Sven Hirdman är död" ("Diplomat Sven Hirdman has died"), dated 2026-10-18. Hirdman was a former ambassador and state secretary. The 2024 photo caption in the article shows him at a protest against the DCA agreement, which is presumably the Russia link the scout mentioned. The three edits in this window are follow-up cleanup, not the first report of the death. Belairroad2 added wikilinks (Sergels torg, Norge), Tekannan fixed a typo ("Stockolm" to "Stockholm") in the place-of-death field, and Disembodied Soul added the {{nyligen avliden}} ("recently deceased") template. There are no reverts and nothing suggests vandalism or a dispute. No other-language versions of the page are linked in the graph, so I couldn't check whether other wikis are reflecting the death. I didn't see the edit that first added the death, but it has two mainstream Swedish sources, so the death looks real. Coverage is low-intensity.

stories.headline: Russian boxer Denis Boytsov dead; ruwiki cites Championat for 17 Oct 2026 date
stories.summary: This update corrects the earlier brief, which said there was no corroboration from other languages. The Russian Wikipedia article on heavyweight Denis Boytsov (Q327073) already lists his death date as 17.10.2026. A revision by Vitedg (rev 155682928) shows that date and a citation to a championat.com article. The cited headline reads "Умер «русский Тайсон». Не стало Дениса Бойцова" ("'The Russian Tyson' has died. Denis Boytsov is gone"). The URL mentions his beating in Germany, a head injury, an induced coma and his recovery. That edit itself is a small cleanup: it unlinks some dates, and in the visible part of the diff the reference is taken off the death-date line. I couldn't confirm whether the reference was moved elsewhere or removed. On German Wikipedia, a temporary account added the same exact date, 17.10.2026 (rev 271435294). Irraza1910 reverted it within two minutes because it had no source (rev 271435362), not because it was wrong. The year 2026 stays in the German article. The two language versions now agree on the death, and Russian Wikipedia has a named sports-media source for it. I haven't checked the source directly, and the Russian page shows just this one edit, so there's no sign of a wave of editing.

stories.headline: Nancy Ajram page quiet after vandalism; only link cleanup since last brief
stories.summary: There has been no new vandalism on en-wiki's Nancy Ajram page since the last brief. The only two edits since then are wikilink tidying by established editors. PixelsRCool removed a duplicate link to "World Music Awards" on the "WMA winner" phrase and cut some links further down the article (rev 1380894703). Calmira90 then changed a piped link to point straight to "World Music Award", citing WP:NOPIPEDLINK (rev 1380896292). Neither edit changes any facts or adds new events. The page's only revert is still PixelsRCool's undo of the "RANI yehya" infobox vandalism covered before, and nothing new has happened on the Mahmoud Ouertani page. This was vandalism that has since stopped, followed by routine upkeep; there is still no sign of a real-world event.

stories.headline: Helen Haines attack: no new facts since suspect was named and charged
stories.summary: This updates the tracked story on the alleged vehicle attack on independent MP Helen Haines outside her Wangaratta office. It is not a new event. The scout counted "three editors with sizeable churn", but MrActiniuM's and Neegzistuoja's edits were already covered in the last brief: suspect Brendan Nugent named and charged with three offences, per a single ABC report from 20 Oct. Since then there have been only two small edits on English Wikipedia, with no reverts. Rev 1381156862 by Laterthanyouthink only adds a wikilink for Chiltern Bush Nursing Hospital in her nursing background. Rev 1381156083 by Schestos (+1 byte, no edit summary) is in the attack section's opening paragraph, but the diff tool cut off before the change. At one byte it is almost certainly a typo or formatting fix, though I couldn't confirm that. The paragraph still says she was struck twice on 19 Oct at 15:35 AEDT, that PM Albanese called it deliberate, and that the AFP, ASIO and the joint counter-terrorism team are investigating. Nothing new on her condition, which stays critical but stable at the Alfred, or on court dates. I tried rev 1381154815 again, and the text of the "Pauline" reaction is still cut off, so it remains unconfirmed.

stories.headline: New page on a non-notable individual tagged for speedy deletion; not news
stories.summary: A single-sentence English Wikipedia article was created by a new account (ARGFNorway, 1 edit) describing a private individual, apparently a teenage Norwegian high-school student, with a self-supplied portrait. A temporary account added only the note "(This article is currently under work)". New-page patroller DonnieNova reverted that and tagged the page for speedy deletion under CSD A1 (no context) and A11 (obviously invented or non-notable). The "revert" is ordinary page patrolling, not a dispute: no back-and-forth, no other language versions, no other pages involved. Nothing here points to a real-world event. The subject appears to be a minor, so the brief leaves out identifying details.

stories.headline: VisionQuest article: routine fixes to air dates and sourcing, no edit war
stories.summary: Four editors made a small burst of edits to the English article on Marvel's Disney+ series VisionQuest (which premiered in October 2026), all on the same day. Kucingb1rah moved every episode release date one day later (Oct 13→14 through Nov 10→11), saying the change matched Disney+. Trailblazer101 undid both edits as "Inaccurate, see cited sources." The article cites a release schedule giving a Disney+ premiere of October 13, after a BFI London Film Festival screening on October 12. The originally announced date was October 14. The one-day gap is most likely a time-zone difference (a US-evening release falls on the next day in Asia) or the old announced date, not a real schedule change. Separately, Marco camino 10 removed a 787-byte addition by MillenniumGeneration because it relied on Murphy's Multiverse, which the reverting editor said is not a reliable source. I only saw a truncated part of that addition, so I can't say exactly what it claimed. There's no back-and-forth reverting, no anonymous accounts and nothing in other languages. This is ordinary upkeep of an article about a show that's airing, not news.

stories.headline: Corneille fr.wiki page: minor test edits by temporary account, cleaned up and reverted
stories.summary: Four edits in about 15 minutes on the French Wikipedia biography of Pierre Corneille. There is no sign of any real-world news. A temporary account (~2026-56250-63) made two edits. In rev 240541362 it added a useful wikilink to "avocat" and, judging by the next cleanup diff, also put a 👍🏻 emoji after a bibliography entry. Csar62 removed the emoji (rev 240541448). The same temporary account then put the emoji back and replaced the "avocat du roi" wikilink with a raw Google search URL (rev 240541562). R3L3ct3ur49 reverted that, per the edit comment. This is low-grade test or vandal editing, typical of a student on a school-curriculum author's page, with no other pages or languages involved. I didn't read the revert diff itself; the description of it comes from its edit comment.

stories.headline: World Series page: copyedits to Rays background on Peralta's Mets stint; no new event
stories.summary: This adds to the existing Rays–Brewers World Series story and doesn't change it. The Scout is right: this is routine upkeep. Since the last brief, three named editors made four small edits to the 2026 World Series page, with no reverts and nothing outside English Wikipedia. DeMarcusCousinsCousin changed the description of Freddy Peralta's Mets stint from "poor season and a half" to "half a season" (1381135150, -4 bytes).
