That matches the cited Aug. 2, 2026 MLB.com trade story. CoDeX0206 then linked Peralta's name (1381135606) and made a further +18-byte tweak to the same paragraph (1381135789). I couldn't see that last change because the diff came back truncated. Allen2 made a "minor grammar fix + template tweak" to Background (1381135749). That paragraph now says this is the third World Series in which both teams play home games under a dome or retractable roof, after 2023, with a footnote explaining that the neutral-site 2020 Series doesn't count. This settles the trivia line editors fought over earlier in a sourced-adjacent form, but that sentence itself still has no citation. The ALCS Game 6 attendance (40,230 vs 30,230) is still unresolved.

stories.headline: Vandalism on ru-wiki 1986 Transformers film article quickly reverted
stories.summary: One account, Skyfire0 0, made two bad edits to the Russian Wikipedia article on the 1986 animated film "The Transformers: The Movie." The first edit renamed the film "Трансформеры в Казахстане" ("Transformers in Kazakhstan"), added a Kazakh "original title" that is actually a machine translation, listed Kazakh as a language and credited "animators from Kazakhstan." EyeBot, an anti-vandalism bot that scores edits with ORES, undid that edit about 30 seconds later (ORES score 0.75). The same account then garbled the plot summary, saying Unicron's next victim was "itself" rather than the planet Lithone. The editor Beonus rolled that back within a minute. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but two of the four edits are reverts: the graph didn't flag them as reverts, though their edit summaries show it. This was a small vandalism incident that was cleaned up fast, and there's no real-world news here. The article is back to its earlier version, and nothing suggests edits in other languages or coordinated activity.

stories.headline: New de-wiki biography of theologian Johannes Rüster gets routine tidying
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the earlier brief. The German Wikipedia article on Johannes Rüster has the same six edits by three registered editors, and none of them are reverts. Rüster is a religious educator and fantasy-literature scholar at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, born in Nuremberg on 16 September 1976. The diffs I read are all maintenance work. Gortfather added a sort key and categories (Lutheran theologian, FAU lecturer, born 1976). Murkus69 renamed "Links" to "Weblinks" and added a references section. M2k added the GND authority record, the Personendaten metadata template and the "Deutscher" category. None of the edits add or change facts, and nothing points to a death, an appointment or a dispute. This looks like a newly created article being cleaned up, not a news event.

stories.headline: France 17 Oct protests: frwiki article quiet since last update, no new facts
stories.summary: I found no new edits to the frwiki article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026" since the last brief. The latest revision in the graph is still Olevy's 240488602 (ts 1792333558), which the last brief already covered. The page has 14 edits from 7 named editors, no reverts and no SAME_AS pages in other languages. The scout's "631 churn" figure appears to add up the edits already reported, not new activity. I re-read two diffs. Rev 240488602 cites La Voix du Nord and Le Parisien for "insurrection" and TF1 Info for "urban guerrilla", and adds a Le Parisien piece ("C'est apocalyptique") on police being overwhelmed by rioters and looters. It now presents critics as divided: some say the police response was too weak, others say it was too violent. Rev 240488416 shortens the death passage: a protester collapsed on boulevard Magenta in Paris's 10th arrondissement and died outside the Château-d'Eau emergency post before he could be treated (CNews). It still reads as a medical death. The earlier caution stands: the claim that arson destroyed Limoges's city hall has no source. Everything is still on one page in one language and has not been checked independently.

stories.headline: Ru-wiki attack page on a minor reverted to redirect again by patroller
stories.summary: This is an update, not news. Patroller Енс Боот has now undone the temporary account's restoration of the attack page (rev 155720107, −2392 bytes). The diff confirms "Даниил Жуковский" once again redirects to [[Жуковский, Даниил Дмитриевич]]. All of the abusive fake biography of a schoolchild born in 2012 is removed: the mocking nickname, insults about his looks, and social-media links. So the earlier concern that the attack text was left live is resolved. Енс Боот's earlier rollback of the "slander" speedy-deletion tag was a step on the way to restoring the redirect, not a decision to keep the page. The graph shows no edits since then. Still unknown: whether ~2026-55919-40 tries a third time, and whether admins will hide the revisions or protect the page. Neither shows up in the edit graph. Do not repeat the content.

stories.headline: Prazosin article: PTSD section rewritten, minor revert friction over citation formatting
stories.summary: A temporary-account editor rewrote the en-wiki Prazosin lead and expanded the PTSD section (+2,750 bytes). The new text calls prazosin's use against PTSD nightmares off-label, says it is usually taken three times a day for blood pressure and prostate symptoms, and cites newer sources, including a 2024 Psychiatrist.com article on three-times-daily dosing. Established editor Boghog then made two cleanup edits: one normalised the citation templates and the other trimmed a lead "becoming way too long". A second temporary account reverted both within minutes with the summary "was not finished", restoring the old reference names and formatting. The reverts appear to be about formatting rather than medical substance, and the first temporary account went on to make small wikilink and organisation edits afterwards. There are no signs of a news trigger: one page, one language, no regulatory or safety language in the diffs. The two temporary accounts may well be the same person in different sessions, but that is unconfirmed. If Boghog reverts again this could turn into a small edit war, but for now it is routine article improvement.

stories.headline: Rays lead Guardians 7–3 after eight innings of ALCS Game 6, per live edits
stories.summary: Fans are still updating the enwiki 2026 ALCS page inning by inning during Game 6. Since the last brief, mainly Smitty Smitty, BaseballFanatic1 and Allen2 have made edits, with no reverts. The game summary now says Nathaniel Lowe hit an RBI single in the top of the 6th that made it 3–1, Freddy Peralta pitched 5⅓ innings and allowed one run, and Junior Caminero hit a two-run homer in the bottom of the 7th for 5–1 (revs 1381108142, 1381112763). Next, a walk to Patrick Bailey and a hit-by-pitch to Ángel Martínez brought in two Guardians runs, cutting the lead to 5–3 (rev 1381115766). Allen2 then raised the Rays' total to 7 with the comment "Rays scored 2 runs in the 8th" but left the 8th inning cell empty. Smitty Smitty filled in H8=2 and added a Yandy Diaz home run (revs 1381116756, 1381116831). Smitty Smitty is also updating the series composite line score (rev 1381115437). The diffs I read show only the Rays' innings and part of the Guardians' line, so the 7–3 score is pieced together from those edits. All of it comes from unsourced fan edits during the game, and I don't know the final result or what it means for the series.

stories.headline: Titans get first 2026 win, 26–20 at Colts, to go 1–5, per season page edits
stories.summary: Two registered editors updated the 2026 Tennessee Titans season article within 16 seconds of each other. One changed the infobox record from 0–5 to 1–5 (rev 1380921423). The other filled in the Week 6 schedule row as a win, "W 26–20", at the Colts, with a 1–5 record and an NFL.com recap link to titans-at-colts-2026-reg-6. That editor also un-hid the Week 7 entry against the Cleveland Browns (rev 1380921456). Both edits agree with each other, so this looks like an ordinary post-game update and not vandalism or an edit war, with no reverts and no other pages involved. It suggests the Titans won their first game of the season after an 0–5 start. The score comes only from the Wikipedia edits and hasn't been checked against another source.

stories.headline: Persian Wikipedia: bot restores Gilan–Ardabil border line removed from Hiran tourism-area article
stories.summary: The 1,468-byte "churn" is really one 734-byte deletion followed by a bot undoing it. It is not a content expansion. A temporary account (~2026-55789-21) deleted the phrase saying the Hiran model tourism area (Astara County, Gilan) sits "on the border of Gilan and Ardabil provinces", along with its ILNA citation (rev 44768045). Dexbot's AI-based anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) reverted it word for word 19 seconds later (rev 44768047), so the article is back where it started. The removal could be a good-faith edit about the region's provincial identity, since Hiran sits on the Gilan–Ardabil line, rather than vandalism, but one edit with no explanation can't settle that. No other editors, languages or real-world event are involved.

stories.headline: Taniec z gwiazdami S32 Week 7 'Disney Night' scores entered live on English Wikipedia
stories.summary: Two registered editors (Łukasz...wrocław, ~36 edits; Serecki, ~8) are updating the English page for season 32 of Polish TV's Taniec z gwiazdami (Dancing with the Stars) in what looks like real time during the Week 7 'Disney Night' broadcast. The dossier lists far more than the six edits in the scout's note. Each batch follows the same pattern: a judges' score goes into the week table (e.g. '50 (10,10,10,10,10)', '48 (9,10,10,9,10)'), then the scoring, average and highest/lowest charts are updated, with one 50 marked as the night's highest score. Serecki added the 18 October 2026 guest performances (Edyta Górniak singing 'Kolorowy wiatr', Natalia Kukulska singing 'Ani słowa', and an orchestra number with Donald and Daisy Duck) and corrected a film link to Snow White (2025). There are no reverts, no anonymous editors and no activity on other-language pages. This is routine fan tracking of the show, not news. Which couple is eliminated this week is not yet clear from these edits.

stories.headline: Vandalism on 'The Bonnie Blue Flag' article reverted within a minute
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56013-63) undid an earlier revert (rev 1362834767). That put back an older vandal edit on the enwiki article about the Civil War-era song 'The Bonnie Blue Flag'. The edit replaced the Project Gutenberg sheet-music cover with an image file named 'Bonnie Blue, July 2025.jpg', apparently a photo of the internet personality who shares the name. It also added the sentence 'This flag has everything to do with the ykw star.' Patroller T430s reverted it about 34 seconds later, restoring the last version by NinjaRobotPirate. This is a name-confusion prank that someone tried before, not a content dispute or a news event. No other pages, languages or editors are involved.

stories.headline: Two quickly reverted schoolyard-style vandal edits on Rhythm Tengoku and Vesuvius pages; no news
stories.summary: Nothing in this cluster points to a real-world event. It is two small vandalism episodes on English Wikipedia, both cleaned up within minutes. On Rhythm Tengoku, the account Unpaidwikieditor twice added a personal attack on another user ("Evantch10 is a menace to society... the reason I got a 0 on my assignment in my class"). ClueBot NG removed the first, and RadioactOlive removed the second using WikiShield. The scout called the Vesuvius edits harmless, but they are vandalism too. A temporary account (~2026-55863-76) twice added a made-up story about a "Mr. Munch" singing Bastille's "Pompeii" while the city was buried in 79 AD. 420yeahh removed the first ("removed possible vandalism") and RadioactOlive reverted the second. The two pages are grouped mainly because RadioactOlive patrolled both. The two vandal edits came within about five minutes of each other and both read like student pranks, so they may come from the same classroom. The graph cannot confirm that link. Both articles are back to their earlier versions. This should be merged with the existing Rhythm Tengoku vandalism story.

stories.headline: New temporary account vandalizes Spanish 'Medieval music' article; reverted in 90 seconds
stories.summary: This is a follow-up on the vandalism we're already tracking on es:Música de la Edad Media. Nothing has happened in the real world. A new temporary account, ~2026-56483-07, put a Spanish vulgarity ("polla") at the start of the article's opening sentence (rev 175930233). It is the only edit that account has made. The patroller Maragm rolled it back about 90 seconds later (rev 175930235), which put the opening paragraph back to its clean text. This is a different temporary account from the ~2026-56477-37/Zebniga pair. It may be the same person on a fresh session, but that is a guess: the edit history alone can't show it. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but there were. As before, the graph's revert flag doesn't catch them; Maragm's rollback summaries show them. Only this one page and one language are involved, and semi-protecting the page would likely end this.

stories.headline: Laurent Nuñez enwiki vandalism: no new activity, both insults stay reverted
stories.summary: This update adds no new activity. The page still shows the same 4 edits in English only: temporary account ~2026-56054-65 added two crude insults, and both were reverted within seconds. I re-read both diffs. Rev 1380920602 ("political status", +39) added a "citern of piss" line to the lead sentence, and ClueBot NG removed it about 2 seconds later. Rev 1380921344 ("last status", +71) added a similar line about a "yellow smelly liquid" to the career paragraph, and ESkog reverted it about 6 seconds later with AntiVandal. Neither edit changed any facts: his office as Interior Minister in the second Lecornu government since 12 October 2025, his earlier posts and his dates were left as they were. A graph query found no edits after the last revert on any version of the article in another language (same Wikidata item Q30729111). One person vandalised the page and it has already been cleaned up. This is not an edit war and gives no sign of anything happening in the real world. I've dropped the earlier brief's guess about the timing, because nothing in the evidence supports it.

stories.headline: One temporary account's changes to two caste pages reverted by a patroller; no edit war
stories.summary: This isn't a real dispute. One temporary account (~2026-56036-30) made poorly formatted edits to two small English Wikipedia caste/tribe pages within about 12 minutes. On Rajar (tribe), it removed 834 bytes (rev 1381092366), deleting the lead sentence, infobox and Rajasthan text and leaving loose citations. Its edit summary is in Sindhi and names one person as a member of the tribe. On Babbar (tribe), it rewrote the infobox (rev 1381091908) to add Hindu/Indian places and Punjabi, and removed the Baloch/Balochistan links. Patroller KuyaMoHirowo reverted both pages within minutes, citing an "ECR violation" (the restriction that limits South Asian caste topics to established editors; revs 1381092504, 1381092610). Each page has a single revert and the account didn't come back, so this is routine cleanup, not an edit war or a news event. What's unclear: whether the Babbar change reflects a real disagreement over the group's origins (Baloch vs. Rajput/Punjabi). But only one account was involved, so it doesn't count as evidence of a wider dispute.

stories.headline: Footnote sections deleted from four ja-wiki animated film pages, quickly reverted
stories.summary: Over roughly 2.5 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56447-07) made unexplained edits to four Japanese Wikipedia film pages: Frozen 3, Coco 2, the Shaun the Sheep pumpkin-patch film and Trolls Band Together. Each edit removed 26–49 bytes. The two diffs I read (Frozen 3, Trolls) show the account deleting the footnotes section heading (脚注), the help template and the reference list. Within about 7 minutes, patroller しのしん used TwinkleGlobal to revert all four edits as vandalism ("Rvv"), restoring the earlier versions. The scout counted 8 editors, but only two accounts were active in this burst. No release dates or other content changed, and nothing points to a real-world event. This is low-level disruptive editing that has already been cleaned up. I could not load the diff for the revert itself, but the edit summary and byte counts (+46 back against −46) match a full restore.

stories.headline: Jeff the Killer page: unsourced sexuality claims added by temp account, reverted twice
stories.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56097-97) made two edits to the enwiki article on the creepypasta character Jeff the Killer. Both added unsourced claims that the character is "LGBTQIA+"/"Homosexual": an infobox field, a change to the lead, and a rewrite of the backstory so it reads that he went on a killing spree after "coming out of the closet" and being burned by "homophobic bullies". The cited Pacer source was left as it was. Patroller Cannolis reverted the first edit for having no reliable source (WP:RS). ClueBot NG reverted the second as possible vandalism. The scout was wrong on one point: two of the four edits are reverts. But this is one person pushing unsourced content, not a back-and-forth edit war. Nothing points to a real-world event: no other languages or pages were involved, and no other editors joined in. This is low-level vandalism that was quickly handled, with no news value.

stories.headline: Notre Dame loses 28–24 at No. 8 BYU, drops in polls; Miami stays No. 1
stories.summary: Notre Dame's 2026 season page now joins the Miami/Pittsburgh cluster, and these edits are more than routine upkeep: they record a game result. Rev 1380905124 by KingDLR2006 filled in the box score for "at No. 8 BYU". By quarter it reads Notre Dame 3-7-6-8 = 24 and BYU 7-14-0-7 = 28. BYU took the lead on a 6-yard Walker Lyons TD catch from Bear Bachmeier with 1:47 left. Some of the running-score labels inside that diff are garbled, so the result comes from the quarter totals. Later edits fit a loss: Notre Dame is listed at 6–1 in the Navy preview (rev 1380908351), and its AP rank went from 2 to 4 (rev 1380908224 by KingSkyLord; rev 1380907740 by Blue Heron Football). One oddity: Torlek's rev 1380900587 enters Notre Dame at No. 8 in the week-7 Coaches Poll, which is a big gap from the AP No. 4 and may be an error. On Miami, rev 1380907663 adds 40 first-place votes to its week-7 AP No. 1 ranking. All the edits are on English Wikipedia by a few regular college-football editors, with no reverts. This is upkeep of a real ranked-team upset, not an edit war, but I haven't confirmed the score outside Wikipedia.

stories.headline: Italian 'Guerra d'Iran' article churn is cleanup, not news
stories.summary: The 303-byte churn on itwiki's 'Guerra d'Iran' comes from six edits by three accounts, and none of them adds a new development. Registered editor Carlo Dani made link maintenance edits. One relinks the SIGINT article to skip a redirect in the section on CIA coordination with Israel before the 28 February strikes (rev 152959745). Another unlinks the IAEA article in the nuclear-background section (rev 152959922). Two temporary accounts reformatted the infobox's list of allied groups operating in Lebanon (Hezbollah, Huthi, PMF, Hamas, PIJ, PFLP, Amal and others). They added flag borders and merged the lines into one block; the existing sources were carried over and no new combatants were added (revs 152959752, 152959917). There are no reverts and no back-and-forth between editors, and no SAME_AS pages in other languages are tracked, so nothing points to an edit war or a breaking event. The underlying 2026 Iran war is clearly a live topic, but these particular edits contain no new facts.

stories.headline: Douglas Stephan update: 2026 Davy Medal entry holds steady, no new edits
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. There are no new edits on Douglas Stephan, Otto Carius or Utah Transit Authority after the last tracked revision (1381251999). The Stephan entry still says he won the Royal Society's 2026 Davy Medal for chemistry. It is cited to a University of Toronto Arts & Science news piece by Sean McNeely dated 2026-08-27 (rev 1381251519). That same edit moved the Order of Canada citation to the right sentence. The later edit only fixed a misspelled citation-needed tag on "He currently lives in Toronto" (rev 1381251999). Activity is small, all English-language, and no one has disputed or reverted the award claim. I have not checked the award against anything outside Wikipedia. The other two pages are still just routine cleanup by patrollers.

stories.headline: Hoax Python Steering Council names repeatedly inserted, reverted on enwiki
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56033-10) made four edits to English Wikipedia's Python article. Each one attached five names (Findlay Noble, Quincy Ting, Noah Lima Grainger, Izaac Lye, Michelangelo Bianchi) to the sentence about the January 2019 Steering Council election, saying "the council came out public this morning". The real 2019 council was Barry Warsaw, Brett Cannon, Carol Willing, Guido van Rossum and Nick Coghlan, as set out in PEP 8100. The added names match none of them and look made up. Three established editors (Gadfium, Untamed1910, T8y) reverted the claim as unsourced or as contradicting PEP 8100. The account then added a "source": a Real Python glossary URL with an invented citation title ("Python Council changed to new members..."). Cleanup is incomplete. T8y's last revert (1381270716) removed the names but kept the fake Real Python citation, and the original PEP 8100/PEP 13 references appear to have been dropped. There is no sign of a real-world governance change. Only one page and one language are involved, and the activity is a single account's hoax or vandalism, not news.

stories.headline: Two unrelated vandalism attempts on ru-wiki Blok and Transformers pages, both reverted
stories.summary: These are two separate cases of low-level vandalism on Russian Wikipedia. They don't point to any real-world event. On the Alexander Blok biography, temporary account ~2026-55774-71 added a joke about the game "Block Strike" (Блок Страйк). It renamed the poet to "Блок Страйк" / "Блок страйкович" and wrote that he "began thinking about the game Block Strike back in the 19th century" (revs 155685834, 155685880). EyeBot automatically reverted the first edit and TheReallyThings rolled back the second. On the 1986 Transformers film page, Skyfire0 0 renamed the film "Transformers in Kazakhstan", gave it a Kazakh co-production and a Kazakh title, and then garbled the plot summary (revs 155685718, 155685746). EyeBot and Beonus reverted both edits. The two pages share only the anti-vandal bot EyeBot, and the edits came from different accounts with different themes, so the clustering is coincidental. No cross-language spread was checked, because nothing in the content suggests a real event.

stories.headline: No story: two unrelated es-wiki vandal edits, linked only by anti-vandal bots
stories.summary: This cluster is not a real-world event. Two separate temporary accounts edited different pages, and their edits were reverted within minutes. On Barcelona, ~2026-56374-47 twice inserted a political insult ("ciudad de rojos independentistas") into the lead sentence (revs 175920550, 175920579). Automoderador reverted the first and human editor Varondán undid the second. On DirecTV, ~2026-56366-65 first added junk infobox parameters ({{www.directvla.com}}, {{www.lider.com}}) and Automoderador reverted it. The same account then made a -419 byte edit that brought back old content, including an outdated "AT&T 70% / TPG Capital 30%" ownership line in place of the current TPG Capital, an old Telam citation format and older wording. SeroBOT reverted that too. The two pages share no editors except the bots Automoderador and SeroBOT, which is the only thing tying them together. Nothing in the diffs points to sports broadcast rights or any other link between DirecTV and Barcelona. Recommend closing the story.

stories.headline: zh.wikipedia Hakka-origins dispute stays quiet after protection; no new edits
stories.summary: There has been no new activity since the protection, so there is nothing to add to this story. Contrary to the scout's note, no edits to 客家民系, 衣冠南渡 or 建炎南渡 appear after Manchiu added {{pp-dispute}} templates (rev 95200461 at ts 1792568767, rev 95200468 at ts 1792568785). The diffs show each template expiring 2026-10-28. The graph has only 4 editors on these pages (Cjsyr12345, ~2026-56323-48, ~2026-56490-98, Manchiu), not 6. The last edit by either warring account was at ts 1792568623, and none of the four has edited any other page since then. The "no reverts" count is misleading: the graph's revert flag is false on all of these edits, but the comments show more than 30 manual undos before protection. 建炎南渡 was not given a template; Manchiu only tagged the other two pages. I still can't confirm whether the protection is technically enforced or only tagged. This is not a real-world event. I'd suggest closing this follow-up and re-alerting only if either party edits these pages again or the protection lapses.

stories.headline: Two temporary accounts vandalize de.wiki electrical-meter pages; patroller reverts
stories.summary: Over roughly 30 minutes, two temporary accounts (~2026-55970-25 and ~2026-55949-88) made small edits to three German articles on measuring instruments: Digitalmultimeter, Dreheisenmesswerk and Drehspulmesswerk. The diffs show juvenile vandalism. One edit inserts what looks like a name, "Pasci", plus a crude phrase ("Pascis Riesen Glied") and the nickname "Shelter" into the opening sentence. Another cuts the Quantisierungsabweichung section and part of a paragraph (rev 271476089). A third adds "zur befriediegung des Shelters" to Dreheisenmesswerk. The two accounts build on each other's edits, which suggests classmates, possibly during a physics lesson on these instruments. That is a guess. Patroller Ot reverted all three pages to clean versions within minutes. This is not a coordinated technical cleanup and there is no real-world news here. I did not read the Drehspulmesswerk diffs, but they follow the same pattern and were also reverted.

stories.headline: Ex-Guatemalan prosecutor Solórzano Foppa reported shot dead at Guatemala City stadium; two held
stories.summary: This follow-up backs up the earlier brief and adds detail. The Spanish Wikipedia biography of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa (former prosecutor and former head of the tax agency SAT) has a "Muerte" (death) section citing LA Times en Español, Publinews and Prensa Libre, alongside the DW and La Jornada sources reported earlier. According to that section, he was killed in a gun attack on the morning of Saturday 17 Oct 2026, aged 43, at the government-run "Campo Marte" stadium in zone 5 of Guatemala City, even though government security staff were protecting him. It also says a second person was found dead and five were wounded. Hours later the National Civil Police (PNC) reported arresting two suspects and recovering the weapon, which a preliminary report said was found in a "PedidosYa" delivery backpack. Editor Hard's two new edits (175886420, 175886400) only reword the casualty sentence and add an internal link; this text was added earlier, and that edit isn't in our graph. No editor disputes the death and there are no reverts. Uncertain: the page is still es-wiki only (no other-language versions, no en-wiki, no family pages or Huité massacre page moving in our graph), only 4 editors are involved, and I have not checked the cited outlets myself. The arrest and backpack details are preliminary police reports.

stories.headline: No news: patrol reverts on two unrelated biographies (Staggie, Schall)
stories.summary: These two English Wikipedia biographies have nothing to do with each other. What ties them together is one recent-changes patroller, F0malhaut42, who made 33 edits across many pages using the RedWarn tool. There is no new death or event. On Rashied Staggie, the Cape Town gang leader shot dead in December 2019, user RealtalkME cut about 125 bytes from the "Death" section, which already covers that killing. F0malhaut42 reverted it as unexplained removal, and RealtalkME then made a small, harmless wording change to "Early years" (noting the twin brother). On Roger Schall, the French photographer who died in 1995, Daisy61470 said she was a family member and added text giving credit to his brother Raymond Schall. F0malhaut42 reverted this for lack of reliable sources. The edits are a conflict-of-interest problem, not news. I couldn't see exactly what the Staggie removal cut because the diff text was truncated. Nothing here needs follow-up unless the Schall family edits keep coming back as an edit war.

stories.headline: Account rewriting Dubai page with government sources reverted again; crime section kept
stories.summary: This is an edit war on one Wikipedia page, not a news event. Assembly2026, an account that has edited only the English page Emirate of Dubai (6 edits), is trying to cut critical material from it and replace it with text sourced to the Dubai government. Its edit 1381158994 deleted the whole "International crime hub and criminal haven" section, which cites OCCRP's "Dubai Unlocked", the Carnegie Endowment and the press, calling it "highly inappropriate". Patroller IrisChronomia reverted that as a neutrality (NPOV) problem. Assembly2026 then made a bigger cut of 9,321 bytes (1381159862): it rewrote the lead, governance and geography sections around dubai.ae and digitaldubai.ae, with a 2025 population figure of 4.58M and "Arabian Gulf" wording. IrisChronomia undid that too (1381160591), so both sides have now reverted each other twice, and nothing has been edited since. Uncertain: the diff text I could see was cut off, so I can't confirm the second cut also removed the crime section, though the byte count suggests it did; and whether Assembly2026 has a conflict of interest is a guess, not proven. The other two pages share only the patroller and are small disputes: "Zionism" was added back to De Nederlandse Alliantie's ideology infobox after being reverted (1381159974), and a "marital rape" wording change on Arranged marriage was reverted.

stories.headline: Cleanup continues on new dewiki biography of ORF presenter Larissa Rausch; no news
stories.summary: This is still a newly created German Wikipedia biography being tidied up. Nothing suggests a real-world event. Since the last brief, three editors have made only small cosmetic edits, with no reverts. AxelHH removed bold formatting from the section headings and linked the birth year (rev 271471993). AxelHH also swapped the broad "Journalismus" category for "Journalist (Österreich)" (rev 271472018). The article's creator, Wikithunder1848, added links to FHWien der WKW (rev 271472002) and Radio Arabella (rev 271472054). The -12/+12 byte pair from AxelHH is two unrelated edits, not a revert. The page exists only in German. Two problems remain: the ORF Stars citation URL still carries "utm_source=chatgpt.com", which hints the draft was written with AI help, and the subject's notability could be challenged later. Neither is newsworthy right now.

stories.headline: Songtsen Gampo edit war on French Wikipedia has gone quiet after bot revert
stories.summary: This updates the tracked frwiki "Songtsen Gampo" edit war. It is not a new event and has nothing to do with current news. Nothing has been edited since the last brief. The last two edits are still the garbled-name account's third swap (240570804) and Salebot undoing it 3 seconds later (240570805). That was about 20+ minutes before this check, and the page has been quiet since. The diff of 240570804 confirms the swap is the same as before. It deletes the passage sourced to Kuzmin, which says Taizong was "acculé" (cornered) by Gampo's conquests, and the Songzhou passage. It puts in "Old Tang Book 196" text instead, calling Tibet "un pays qui se soumet à la dynastie Tang" (a country that submits to the Tang dynasty) and the Wencheng marriage a "compromis mutuel" (mutual compromise). In 240570760, Rédacteur Tibet cited a China Intercontinental Press history of Tibet to support the contested invasion sentence. The scout's "no reverts" is wrong again. The revert flags are false, but the edit summaries show undo cycles. This page has no linked pages in other languages in the graph, so the dispute is limited to French Wikipedia. Earlier briefs suspected one person behind several accounts. That is still unconfirmed. The account may try again or move to the talk page, so the war may not be over.

stories.headline: Man City season page logs 5–1 Champions League league-phase win on 20 October
stories.summary: Three registered editors made four edits to the English 2026–27 Manchester City F.C. season page within about 15 minutes. There were no reverts. The edits record a Champions League league-phase match, the club's third, played 20 October 2026. Rev 1381228304 enters a 5–1 City win: Foden scored a hat-trick (34', 65', 76'), with goals from Anderson (12') and Cherki (57'). Pilios scored for the opponent at 52', and Willy Delajod of France refereed. The same edit marks the result as a W and moves City to 6th in the table. Rev 1381228583 only removes a wikilink, and rev 1381229959 updates the squad statistics table to match the new result. This is routine post-match upkeep: there is no controversy, no other pages are involved, and I checked no other languages. One unknown is the opponent, which these diffs don't name.

stories.headline: New de-wiki stub on 1920s songwriter Jesse Greer (d. 1970); not news
stories.summary: Konrad Lackerbeck created a new German Wikipedia article on Jesse Greer, an American songwriter (1896–1970) known for "Just You, Just Me." The article is sourced to Wölfer's Lexikon der Unterhaltungs-Musik (2000). Three other edits followed: a whitespace fix, a minor change to the external links, and M2k adding Commonscat and authority-control templates (GND/LCCN/VIAF). The +1445 "large churn" is just the page being created, not a rewrite or a death update. He died in 1970, so nothing here points to a current event. There are no reverts and no other languages are involved. This is routine article creation.

stories.headline: Unsourced death claim for Croatian singer Jakov Jozinović removed from hr-wiki
stories.summary: On hr-wiki, editor Martin Kuljak added a death date and place to the lead of the article on 20-year-old Croatian pop singer Jakov Jozinović: "Beč [Vienna], 18. rujna 2026." (rev 7620284). The edit cited no source and did not link or mention the death anywhere else in the article. About seven minutes later a temporary account deleted the claim (rev 7620286), and a minute after that the experienced editor Ponor used Twinkle to restore the last good version (rev 7620287). The page is not linked to any other-language Wikipedia article, and no other pages show any matching activity. The edits came about a month after the claimed death date, with no source and no follow-up from other editors, so this looks like a death hoax or vandalism that was quickly reverted, not a real-world event. Some uncertainty remains: if real reports of his death appear, this page should be checked again.

stories.headline: Unsourced Kim Jong-un death claims on it.wiki reverted; page protected
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts on Italian Wikipedia added a death date for Kim Jong-un to his article, about 30 minutes apart. The first said he died on 20 October 2026 in Pyongyang (rev 152983744). The second gave the same date and place and added "brain haemorrhage" as the cause (revs 152984330 and 152984365). Neither edit cited a source. Editor Osnenzo removed each one, saying there was no source and no official confirmation (rev 152984468). Popsi then protected the page, and Osnenzo added a sourced birth year (rev 152984525), which is ordinary upkeep. The Scout's note said there were no reverts, but these were manual undos that the graph didn't flag as reverts. Nothing backs up the claim elsewhere: the only English edit was a date-format template (rev 1381140272). On Persian Wikipedia, a "death rumours" section that was described as AI-generated was cut, and a joke edit was reverted (rev 44784298). This looks like a hoax or rumour-driven vandalism, not news. The one open question is the timing: two separate accounts gave the same date, which could mean a rumour is going around off-wiki. It's worth checking again if other languages pick it up.

stories.headline: Patrol cleanup across three unrelated en-wiki pages; no real-world event detected
stories.summary: The only thing linking these three pages is one patroller, Materialscientist (using the Interceptor/rollback tools), cleaning up edits within about 15 minutes. They are not one news story. Hashim Amla: a temporary account's unsourced +63-byte addition (rev 1380894318) was reverted by Interceptor; separately, "User from Serbia" made an unexplained +44-byte edit (1380894908) that a prior brief describes as adding the "OIS" honour suffix. That honour is still unconfirmed, and no other honours-related pages moved. Fugazi: a temporary account blanked 298 bytes with no reason given (1380894591), and Interceptor restored them. Latin epsilon: I disagree with the scout's "routine churn" reading. An account named "Ɛ＝Ð Cum God the Second Attempt Ɛ＝Ð" (an offensive name, and "Second Attempt" points to a returning/sock account) undid an earlier editor's change (1380895438), then added content with the summary "Ɛ＝Ð" (1380895770). Both were rolled back to the earlier editor's version (1380895828), which fits a vandalism account more than a content dispute. Caveat: the diff fetch failed for every revision, so this rests on edit metadata only (comments, deltas, revert flags, usernames). No revisions are cited.

stories.headline: Kim Ho-ryeong page vandalism: false Hanwha version still live after self-undone revert
stories.summary: There has been no new activity since the last brief. The newest edit on kowiki 김호령 is still Ykhwong's rev 42687456. The diffs confirm what we reported before. Temporary account ~2026-56200-36 left no sources and changed the Kia Tigers outfielder's current club, his 2015 draft team and his career line to "한화이글스" (Hanwha Eagles), and broke the markup doing it (rev 42687444). A real trade could never change a player's 2015 draft team, so this is vandalism, not trade news. Nt reverted twice. Ykhwong reverted, then 16 seconds later reverted his own revert (42687456). That put the vandal's text back word for word, so the live page wrongly says Hanwha and needs one more revert. The scout's note says "no reverts," which is wrong: there were three revert edits. Nothing in other languages or elsewhere backs up a real move.

stories.headline: Routine copyediting of Polish Wikipedia article on the 'Rule 63' internet meme
stories.summary: Over about 30 minutes, four registered pl-wiki editors (Xarys777, NiktWażny, Wcalenieja, IOIOI) made six small edits to "Zasada 63", the article on the "Rule 63" internet meme about gender-swapped versions of fictional characters. The diffs I read show only maintenance work. Wcalenieja fixed Polish inflection and capitalization, reformatted citations, wrapped English titles in templates, and removed the {{Przetłumaczony}} template marking the page as translated from en-wiki. IOIOI added a sister-projects box (Commons/Wiktionary) and the "Memy internetowe" category, and removed a red link from "See also". There were no reverts and no disputed content, and no other language versions or related pages moved. This looks like a recently translated article being tidied up through normal community cleanup, not a sign of any real-world event. The net churn is small (each edit changed fewer than 160 bytes), and I didn't read the first two minor edits.

stories.headline: New pt-wiki biography of Haitian anthropologist Suzanne Comhaire-Sylvain created
stories.summary: On Portuguese Wikipedia, user Oitocentistas created a new article (+5,482 bytes) on Suzanne Comhaire-Sylvain (1898–1975), described as Haiti's first Black woman anthropologist and an early linguist of Haitian Creole. The article cites 2023–2024 scholarship (Ethnologies, Archipélies). The creator then added categories. Two other experienced editors, Daniel G Rego and Leirbag reib, followed with small cleanups: infobox image and caption formatting, punctuation before refs, and naming a reused reference. There were no reverts and nothing contested. The subject died in 1975, and no edit points to a current event, so this looks like ordinary content creation, maybe tied to an editing campaign on women or Haitian figures. That last part is a guess the graph doesn't confirm. The 'large churn' the scout flagged is just the page being created; it isn't a rewrite.

stories.headline: French Wikipedia gets new article on Norwegian cyclist Simen Evertsen-Hegreberg
stories.summary: This is a routine new-article story, not breaking news. Zubeldia3764 created the frwiki biography of Simen Evertsen-Hegreberg (rev 240487498, +6.9 kB). He is a Norwegian rider born in 2004 in Würzburg, Germany, son of former pro Morten Hegreberg. He rode for Tirol-KTM from 2023 to 2025 and rides for Lucky Sport in 2026. The creator then added detail on his 2022 junior season (rev 240487843: second at Nokere Koerse juniors behind Jarno Widar; second in the Norwegian junior criterium championship). FromZeFild (rev 240488126) removed several infobox fields, which looks like infobox cleanup, possibly so the data comes from Wikidata instead; it is not a dispute. A third editor made a small edit to the rankings section. The newest source cited is an August 2026 local article saying he would ride the Arctic Race of Norway. The page has no reverts and no other language versions moving with it, and nothing in what I read points to a current news event. The likeliest explanation is a cycling-project editor writing up a rider before the 2026 season.

stories.headline: es-wiki Total Drama page: user's redirect and deletion bids reverted by bot and patroller
stories.summary: This is a low-stakes editorial fight on es:Drama Total Todos Estrellas, not a real-world event. Only three accounts edited the page. Brunocrac4 tried three times to replace the roughly 34k article with a redirect to "Drama Total: Todos Estrellas e Isla Pahkitew" (rev 175924261), along with smaller copyedits: "quinta temporada" became "primera parte de la quinta temporada" and "será lanzado" became "fue lanzada" (rev 175924090). Each time the anti-vandal bot SeroBOT restored the article. The scout said there were no reverts, but that is wrong: the edit comments record at least five revert actions, even though the revert flag was never set. Brunocrac4's own comments warn of an edit war and call it a bot that "no entiende" (doesn't understand). Brunocrac4 then added an {{Eliminar}} deletion tag, arguing the page is redundant and outdated (rev 175924345). Patroller Ontzak removed the tag. The merge question is a fair one, and it will probably be settled through a deletion or merge discussion. There has been no activity since the previous brief.

stories.headline: Northwestern moves up to No. 24 in AP poll; 2026 season pages get weekly updates
stories.summary: The newest activity in this story is three small, non-reverted edits by three registered editors to the English Wikipedia page for the 2026 Northwestern Wildcats football team. IPlayToWin changed the team's AP ranking from 25 to 24 and filled in No. 24 for week 7. KingSkyLord added rank 24 to the schedule. Torlek updated the header of the upcoming Rutgers game summary to read "Rutgers (2–4) at No. 24 Northwestern (5–1)". These edits follow the same weekly upkeep already seen on the Wake Forest page (AP No. 17, 6–1) and the Wisconsin page (hosting No. 16 USC). Torlek and KingSkyLord make these edits across all three pages, the usual pattern for poll and schedule maintenance. There's no sign of vandalism or an edit war, and nothing beyond the new week-7 poll and last weekend's results. I didn't check the AP figures against an outside source; they come from the edit text only.

stories.headline: Arch Manning page: stats now show 6th Texas start was a loss; one vandal edit undone
stories.summary: I found no new activity since the last brief. The graph still holds only the same three English Wikipedia edits, all within about 3 minutes, and no Texas Longhorns pages moved. Marist72's edit (rev 1380878386) changes the season row from 5 games, 5 starts and a 4–1 record to 6 games, 6 starts and 4–2. The career row goes from 16–4 to 16–5. The difference points to one new game: 14 of 20 passing, 173 yards, 1 TD, no interceptions, and 10 rushes for 0 net yards. That suggests Manning started a sixth game for Texas this season and lost it. An unregistered account then replaced "Manning" with "Smith" for Arch and his relatives (rev 1380878646). MarioWonderExpert undid it a minute later with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool (rev 1380878789). That was a single act of vandalism, not an edit war. What's still unknown: the opponent, the score and the date. The stats rest on one editor; the career row links to Sports-Reference, but that link was already there and doesn't confirm this update.

stories.headline: UCL Matchday 3 wrap: late games end 4–2; attendances and minute fixes added
stories.summary: This updates the earlier brief on the en-wiki page for the 2026–27 Champions League league phase. At full time, JacksonAlex92 (rev 1381228770) moved the hidden scorer lists into view and entered two 4−2 final scores. From the scorer names, one game looks like PSG (Doué 38', Vitinha 81', Fabián Ruiz 86') against Barcelona (Espart 55', Lamine Yamal 79'). The other looks like Napoli (Politano 1', McTominay 41' and 75', and a Bjørtuft own goal 89') against Bodø/Glimt (Hauge 27', Helmersen 63'). Leprazoori then added UEFA-sourced attendances: 40,124 at Fenerbahçe v Slavia Prague and 47,221 at Sabah v Dortmund in Baku. He also moved some goal times by a minute (Hermoso 21', Pisilli 52', Helmersen 62'). Three editors are working together with no reverts, so this is routine sports updating. Not confirmed: which team was at home in each 4−2 game, and whether a fourth PSG scorer sits on a line the diff didn't show. The fixtures above are worked out from the players' names, not from team fields I could see.

stories.headline: Torbeši article: small edit war over "Macedonian-speaking" vs "Slavic-speaking" wording
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia article on the Torbeši, a Muslim ethnoreligious group, saw a small revert cycle over how to describe them. A temporary account restored a version (rev 1381148599) that changes "Macedonian-speaking" to "slavic-speaking", adds Kosovo to the regions where they live (Podgora/Prizren, Sredačka Župa), replaces Romani with Vlachs in a list of other groups, and switches to the spelling "Torbeshi". A new account, Skorobishta12, then added unsourced lists of villages in Albania (Kukës/Luma) "with Torbesh roots" and removed "Macedonian" from the census wording (rev 1381149132). Established editors pushed back. Jingiby had already reverted these changes earlier ("not an improvement... gain a consensus", rev 1381139934), and StephenMacky1 put that version back, calling the changes "Disruption" (rev 1381149894). This is a familiar Balkan dispute over labels and identity, not a sign of any real-world event. It's low volume: one page, four editors, no other languages involved. The temporary account and the new account may be the same person, but I can't confirm that.

stories.headline: Catherine Doherty article: second sneaky vandal edit reverted, no news event
stories.summary: The English article on Catherine de Hueck Doherty (1896–1985), founder of Madonna House, is still drawing low-level vandalism. Earlier, account LXR111 added a sexual insult to the lead (rev 1381263333), and patroller Nil NZ reverted it. The new activity comes from temporary account ~2026-54424-47. That account made its second bad edit (rev 1381263630), labeled "spelling error". The edit changed "He died in 1991" to "They died in 1991" in the line about her son George, which falsely implied other people died in 1991. Nil NZ undid it within about 80 seconds with WikiShield, noting "not a spelling error" (rev 1381263700). The page is back to its correct text. There are still only three editors on one page, no other-language activity, and nothing pointing to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Lucas Digne page: repeated BLP vandalism to personal-life section, reverted
stories.summary: This is not a transfer or club story. One temporary account (~2026-43477-40) made the same 8-byte change three times, inserting the word "traitor" before "girlfriend Tiziri" in the Personal life section of Lucas Digne's English Wikipedia biography. Three different established editors undid it each time: Ser!, Mattythewhite, and Cannolis, who cited the policy on biographies of living people (WP:BLP). No sources were added and nothing about his club, contract or career changed. The edit could be a reaction to gossip about Digne's private life, but there is no evidence for that. The graph shows no linked pages in other languages and no activity on related pages. Status is vandalism. If the account keeps going, the page may get protected.

stories.headline: JOA disambiguation page hit by repeated joke insertion; patroller reverted it twice
stories.summary: This update adds the JOA disambiguation page to the existing Anubis vandalism story. Two different temporary accounts (~2026-56142-99, then ~2026-55884-90 about four minutes later) each added the same fake entry, "A gentleperson's club in the BD07 district." BD07 is a UK postcode area in Bradford, so this looks like a local in-joke. The first edit used the summary "brief addendum". Both times Materialscientist removed the line within about 90 seconds, using the Interceptor tool. The scout's note says there were no reverts on JOA, but there were two; the graph doesn't flag them as reverts. The same exact line coming back from a new account suggests one person switching accounts, though I can't confirm that. The only link to Anubis is that the same patroller cleaned up both pages, so these are probably separate incidents rather than a coordinated campaign. Both pages are back to their clean versions, no other languages were touched, and nothing points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: ru-wiki 1943 date dispute spreads to "Poland" and "Home Army" pages; new edits still live
stories.summary: This update adds two pages. Temporary account ~2026-55727-16 was reverted on the Yalta Conference and Operation Tempest pages; Sand Kastle 17's undo in rev 155684444 put back "1 октября 1943". The account then made the same one-figure change on two more ru-wiki pages. On "Польша" (Poland), rev 155684479 changes the date of the London government's instruction to the Home Army from "1 октября 1943" to "26 октября 1943", with no source and the same comment as before ("исправление, уточнение", "correction, clarification"). On "Армия Крайова" (Home Army), rev 155684530 (+1 byte, comment "исправление") targets the same passage. That diff was cut off: the old line "[[1 октября]] 1943" is visible but the new line isn't, so I'm inferring the 1→26 change from the matching byte count. Neither new edit had been reverted when the graph last updated. This is one account pushing a single date across four pages while patrollers undo it, not a real-world event. The scout's note of "no reverts" is wrong, as the earlier brief also found: the graph's revert flag is off, but the edit comments show the undos. One caveat: some historians date this instruction to late October 1943 (about 26–27 October), so the change may be a real correction made without a source rather than vandalism. Talk-page discussion with a source would settle it. The batfish half of this story has had no new activity.

stories.headline: Romania: Parliament reportedly elects Luca Niculescu PM, ending months-long crisis
stories.summary: On English Wikipedia's "2026 Romanian political crisis" article, editors added that on 20 October Parliament voted in Luca Niculescu as prime minister. The text says PSD, PNL and UDMR backed him, "effectively ending the crisis that held for nearly half a year" (revs 1381211296, 1381211915). The article now gives the crisis an end date of 20 October 2026. It traces the crisis back to the no-confidence vote that removed PM Ilie Bolojan, followed by failed bids by Eugen Tomac, Adrian Veștea and Siegfried Mureșan (rev 1381210422). Other wikis back this up: Niculescu cabinet pages were active in the same hours on fr, ro, pl and en, a new Polish page "Rząd Luki Niculescu" was created, and Niculescu's biography was edited on fr, pl, simple and cs. Uncertainty: almost all of the English edits came from one editor, VityaPeti, and the vote sentence I read has no reference attached. Materialscientist reverted one of VityaPeti's edits as unsourced, but what that revert touched was the start date (25 April vs 5 May). VityaPeti then put the 25 April date back (rev 1381214779), so there is a small open dispute over the start date, not a full edit war. There are no other reverts and no sign of vandalism.

stories.headline: Karol G tour page on es-wiki: tour-date table reworked, unsourced cancellations added
stories.summary: The candidate headline is wrong. "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour" is Karol G's concert tour, not a travel show. Three accounts made 7 edits with no reverts. Registered editor Paiap reformatted the tour-date table to show attendance and gross per show (for example, Chicago Soldier Field 85,300 and $18.0M; SoFi Stadium 139,000 and $34.1M, citing Billboard Boxscore). Paiap also changed the counts to 64 shows and 1 cancelled, and the edit comment says a Poland date was dropped because it isn't on sale or listed on Karol G's official site. Temporary account ~2026-55869-88 then moved Lyon (21 Jul 2027) in the cancelled-dates section, added Lisbon's Estádio da Luz (18 Jun 2026) as cancelled, and gave "logistics problems" (with a typo) as the reason for both. That account cited no source and also made small formatting edits that broke the España flag template. This looks like routine fan upkeep of the page. The only possibly newsworthy claim is the cancellations, and nothing in the edits confirms them, so I'd treat them as unverified.

stories.headline: No new activity on Vincent Boesen page; reverted Samui United stats remain at 0/0
stories.summary: This is the same set of edits the tracked story already covered, and nothing has happened since. The page's only edits are the four already logged on the German Wikipedia article for Vincent Boesen, a striker who joined Samui United FC in Thailand in 2026. I've now read the 0-byte edit by Zikrul Kari (rev 271484561), which the earlier brief skipped. It changed his Samui United record from 3 games and 3 goals to 1 game and 3 goals. RoBri's rollback (rev 271484579) undid the anonymous edit and both of Zikrul Kari's, restoring Siam.Soccer's version, which shows 0 games and 0 goals. The diff shows the rollback also put back the infobox formatting the anonymous edit had changed. One correction to the earlier brief: the rollback came about 38 seconds after the last edit and about 5 minutes after the first, not about 30 minutes later. The numbers never agreed with each other, no source was given, and nobody has tried again or edited the matching pages in other languages. It's possible Boesen scored a hat-trick in one match, but the edits don't confirm it. This is routine and needs no further follow-up unless the stats are re-added with a source.

stories.headline: Pro Asyl article refreshed with 2025 figures; account named for the group adds a source
stories.summary: A temporary account rewrote the English Wikipedia article on German refugee-advocacy NGO Pro Asyl. It updated the infobox to 25,000 members and a budget of €6,020,618 (2025), up from 25,209 members and €5.85m in 2022. The edit also copy-edited the lead and, according to its edit summary, deleted an "outdated" Positions section (net −649 bytes). Editor CantReadRunes did a partial "revert" that only fixed a duplicated bold name and a broken interlanguage link. The same editor then swapped a broken citation for a citation-needed tag. An account named "ProAsyl" then cited the organisation's own 2025/2026 activity report for the figures. The "reverts" were cleanup, not an edit war, and there is no sign of a real-world event. The only point worth noting is a possible conflict of interest: the new numbers rest on Pro Asyl's own report, and the account name suggests the organisation edited its own page. Removing the Positions section could also be read as image management, but I did not check what that section said.

stories.headline: Prank edits on Cruz Alta (Córdoba) eswiki page spread to its history and notable-people sections
stories.summary: This is still schoolyard vandalism, not a news event. Two temporary accounts kept going after the last brief. ~2026-56015-61 changed the 1966–69 mayor "Pratta" to "Fernández-Rosalez, Paul" (rev 175909866). It also added an "honorable mention" for a teacher at the Instituto Privado Diocesano San Luis and his greyhound "Galgo Salvaje" (rev 175909993), and slipped made-up names ("Valentin Bruno", "Bastian Martinez Miranda") into the colonial history section (rev 175910068). ~2026-56106-69 changed how the link to the singer Pablo Funes displays, so it now reads "giustiiix arda" (rev 175910013). It then described that name as an adult-website actress (rev 175910056). That is a crude and possibly defamatory joke, which makes it a cleanup priority. The history and notable-people text also contains other odd names ("Renzo Pratto", "ivo ilari", "Tanque massei", "Massi Fratta77", "ciudad de suiza") that look like earlier vandalism from the same group. I didn't check when those went in. No reverts have happened since SeroBOT's earlier one, so as of the last edit everything above is still live. The school reference suggests a group of students is behind this.

stories.headline: Albanian protests page: temp account returns, swaps in new image and 'riots' subtitle
stories.summary: This is a small follow-up, not a new story. About six minutes after Pattersonuwu restored PancakeGuy20's version (1381073858), the same temporary account (~2026-55646-41) edited the 2026 Albanian student protests infobox again (1381074423). It added the subtitle "2026 Albanian riots" and replaced the existing AlbProtest.png with "File:Flamingo Reveloutin.jpg", captioned "Craziest riots in Albania". This time it did not touch the casualty figures, and no one has reverted the edit so far. Calling the protests "riots" has no source, and the misspelled image name and the caption look like low-quality or joke editing rather than a report of escalation. The page has five edits in total, no other-language versions in the graph and no sources in any diff I read, so it says nothing reliable about what is happening on the ground. The protests themselves still look like a real, ongoing event. Expect a patroller to revert this edit.

stories.headline: Albania student protests: no new facts since last brief, only cleanup on en-wiki
stories.summary: The only edit to "2026 Albanian student protests" since the previous brief is rev 1381239682. In it, admin DMacks removed a duplicate "Flamingo Revolution" link from See also under the style rule against repeating links already in the article, so it changes no facts. The "1,347 churn" in the scout's note is the "Finished wip (up to 18 Oct)" edit (rev 1381238882), which the prior brief already covered. That edit dates the clashes from 13 October, adds rubber pellets to tear gas and water cannon as police methods, and says there have been daily Tirana protests since 31 May as part of the Flamingo Revolution, sourced to Top Channel and DW. The Prince Rupert's drop change is an unrelated grammar revert by DMacks of a one-comma edit by a temporary account. There are still no reverts on the protests page and no other-language versions of it in the graph, and most new content comes from one editor (Hduensixojnrwjzz). The underlying story is still developing, but this update adds nothing new. The cited news sources are still unchecked.

stories.headline: Russian talk-show page 'Вопрос ребром': tag work continues, one 'See also' link undone
stories.summary: This is still routine maintenance on the Russian Wikipedia article about the talk show 'Вопрос ребром'. It's on the same page as the routine story we're already tracking. Temporary account ~2026-55836-54 re-added the 'no poster image' tag to the infobox (rev 155688744). The same account then added a 'See also' section linking to [[MC Taxi]] (rev 155688809). The edit summary named the 'Резонансные выпуски' (notable episodes) section, but that section got no new text. Within a minute, experienced editor Skepsiz undid the link (rev 155688828), saying the linked article doesn't exist and its notability is doubtful. One undo isn't an edit war. No new facts were added, no other language versions changed, and nothing points to a real-world event. MC Taxi might be connected to a recent episode, but the edits give no evidence of that.

stories.headline: Not a story: Nathan Tella vandalism, unsourced American Bitcoin claim; no new edits
stories.summary: There has been no new activity since the earlier brief on these pages. The graph shows the same seven edits, and the latest is KuyaMoHirowo's revert on Nathan Tella. The only link between the two pages is patroller Materialscientist, who reverted unrelated edits on each. On Nathan Tella, a temporary account added a made-up line saying he "won a Bundesliga title… after scoring 5 goals in 5 minutes against Bayern Munich", then tampered with the infobox, and both edits were reverted. On American Bitcoin, a temporary account wrote that the company was "trademarked by Christopher Connor in 2014. Eric Trump stole it". Materialscientist reverted that. An account named ChristopherJohnConnor then rewrote the History section to say the company was "founded in 2014 by Christopher Connor, and taken in March 2025 by Eric Trump". That rewrite cites only the existing Wired source, which doesn't support it, and the graph shows no revert yet. This looks like an unsourced claim pushed by someone with a personal stake (the account is named after the person it credits), not a news event. The remaining open question is whether patrollers will remove that History edit.

stories.headline: Callina Liang page: juvenile 'Chun-Li thighs' edits removed, page protected
stories.summary: This is minor vandalism, not a news event. The 'Street Fighter' (2026) press cycle seems to be drawing attention to Callina Liang, the actress playing Chun-Li. Gadfium, an experienced editor, removed a sentence citing a Barstool Sports blog that said Liang "added 3 inches to her thighs" for the role, calling the source unreliable (rev 1381102757). A temporary account then added "thick legged" to the lead's description of Chun-Li (1381109545). ClueBot NG reverted it within seconds, and Gadfium then added a page-protection icon (1381112273), which means the page was semi-protected. There are no substantive biographical changes and nothing in other languages. A promotional or news hook for the film is likely behind the attention, but the edits don't confirm one.

stories.headline: Fievel Goes West soundtrack page: patroller reverts unsourced Intrada reissue text
stories.summary: This is routine page patrol, not an edit war. Over about 5 minutes, a temporary account (~2026-54338-41) made two additions to the enwiki article on the 1991 An American Tail: Fievel Goes West soundtrack. The first (+107) added "Intrada Records (2026)" to the label field and placeholder sections. The second (+5288) pasted what reads word for word like a label press release ("Intrada announces an expanded 2-CD set of James Horner's score... View the album trailer here."), along with a full track list for CD 1. Patroller Discospinster used Huggle to revert both edits for lacking a reliable source. The pasted text is promotional and probably copied from elsewhere, which also explains the large churn. The only real-world point is that Intrada may have announced an expanded 2-CD reissue of Horner's score. That is a minor niche release, and I haven't checked it outside Wikipedia. Only one page, one language and two editors are involved, with no back-and-forth so far.

stories.headline: Kate, Princess of Wales page: vandalism spree reverted, no new edits since the restore
stories.summary: This story covers the same 5 edits as the tracked vandalism story on the English Wikipedia article about Catherine, Princess of Wales. Querying the page's full edit history found nothing after MSincccc's restore (rev 1381125722). The account Ana Maria Gallizi Debetio emptied infobox fields and changed the royal navbox to read "HIGHNESS ANA MARIA GALES OF UNITED KINGDOM" (rev 1381125264, diff read). ClueBot NG reverted that. The account then gutted the infobox again and blanked about 175k bytes. MSincccc restored the bot's clean version, which brought back the title, image, spouse, children and mother fields and the article body (diff read). No other languages or pages moved, and nothing points to a real-world event. I'd fold this into the existing story rather than treat it as a new one. The Scout's "no reverts" reading came from the revert flag, which isn't set on these edits, but the edit summaries show two restorations.

stories.headline: Cube film series page: block-evasion edit war over a films table, no news hook
stories.summary: Still no real-world event here. There have been no new edits since Untamed1910's revert (rev 1381080244), and the article now reads as it did before the table was added. A temporary account (~2026-56041-90) spent about 20 edits building a table of the four Cube films: release dates, directors, writers and producers. The first draft (rev 1381068430) had empty rows plus a 2021 row with leftover details from an unrelated 2008 film, which were later replaced. The table adds nothing new, and the remake sentence and its Variety source were already in the article. AriuCH and then Untamed1910 removed the table as block evasion by Didaka90. AriuCH also undid an earlier edit by a different temporary account, ~2026-51961-07 (rev 1381078274), which suggests the same person may have come back more than once. The temporary account put the table back twice, with summaries attacking AriuCH (rev 1381079626). A correction: the previous brief said the insults were in rev 1381080244, but that is Untamed1910's revert. I haven't checked the sockpuppet claim itself.

stories.headline: Arabic pastry war: Sarra69 tries again on both pages; sixth editor reverts
stories.summary:
There is still no real-world event. This is the same Tunisia-vs-Algeria origin dispute on the Arabic Wikipedia articles مشموم (mechmoum) and مقروض (maqrout). The scout's "no reverts" is wrong again: the window has three rollbacks, and the graph's revert flag is set on none of them.

- **The temporary account's edit was undone:** Doaa970 rolled back the temporary account ~2026-55998-36 on مشموم (rev 77025646). That restored "Algerian sweets" and the infobox with the "gâteau algérien" image.
- **Sarra69 tried again on مشموم:** Sarra69 changed the lead to "Tunisian sweets", the portal bar from Algeria to Tunisia, and the image to a non-existent "gateau tunisien" file (rev 77025742). Sarra69 then removed the infobox entirely (rev 77025773).
- **Sarra69 tried again on مقروض:** Sarra69 set the origin to Kairouan and the creator to "Tunisia" (rev 77025801). The rollback diff shows this edit also changed "Maghrebi" to "Tunisian pastry" in the lead.
- **A new reverter:** Within about two minutes a sixth editor, Mohamed Belgazem, undid both. The مشموم rollback is rev 77025840 and the مقروض one is rev 77025844.

Both rollback comments call Sarra69's edits "pending" changes, which suggests both pages are under pending-changes review. I didn't check the protection log to confirm that. As of ts 1792445446 both pages are back on the Algerian (مشموم) or neutral (مقروض) wording. Across two hours Sarra69 has now been reverted roughly 18 times by six editors. I still can't confirm a link between Sarra69 and the temporary account, and I didn't check blocks or talk pages.

stories.headline: Deaths in 2026 list: copy edits only since last brief; nothing new on Tsuchida
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened in this story since the last brief. In the graph, the only edits since then are two small ones to English Wikipedia's "Deaths in 2026" list, both in the 20 October section. Bhinkins changed Noah Musingku's description from "Papuan" to "Bougainvillean" and kept the same ABC News citation (1381143511). There is also a 10-byte "replace slang term" edit by Refsworldlee (1381143019), which I didn't read. Neither edit touches the Hiroshi Tsuchida entry. The English and Chinese Tsuchida articles have had no edits since the last brief. The facts are unchanged: he died of heart failure on 11 October 2026, aged 54, and his agency announced it on 20 October. One open question from earlier briefs is now confirmed. Rev 1381125630, by an unregistered editor, swapped "Living people" for "1954 births" and "2026 deaths", but he was born in 1972. No later edit in the graph appears to fix this, though I haven't checked the live page. There are no reverts and no disagreement.

stories.headline: Horrid Henry TV page protected after link spam; Tina Batson edits are a separate birth-year dispute
stories.summary: The Horrid Henry cluster on English Wikipedia is still vandalism with no real-world event behind it, and it now looks contained. After the Nicholas Cruise accounts kept pasting a YouTube link, admin MCE89 added a {{pp-vandalism}} template to "Horrid Henry (TV series)" (rev 1381232103). That means the page has been protected, the same step taken earlier on Pororo. I disagree with the scout on Tina Batson, a Venezuelan pageant contestant: it is not part of the Henry vandalism. Temporary account ~2026-56417-67 twice changed her birth year from 1999 to 2000 (revs 1381231885, 1381232554; the first edit's comment, "la edad", is Spanish for "the age"). Equivalent-Text2598 reverted the first change and Inzessin the second, noting that the cited Globovisión source says 1999 (rev 1381232670). This is a small, unsourced factual dispute, not juvenile vandalism. The account's only other edit was to Miss Earth 2026, which fits a pageant follower rather than the Henry vandals. Nothing new happened on Montrose, Nana (manga) or Paulo Retre since the last brief. There are no other language versions involved. The Batson birth-year change may come back, but it isn't news.

stories.headline: MTK Global page gets 'Legacy' section on 2021 Panorama film plus promo text; no news
stories.summary: Two temporary-account editors added a new "Legacy" section to the English article on MTK Global, the defunct boxing management firm. The main addition (rev 1381270410, +1200) restates old coverage: the 2021 BBC Panorama documentary "Boxing and the Mob" about Daniel Kinahan, threats against the journalists who made it, and MTK's denial that Kinahan controlled the company. It also adds what looks like promotional filler about an "MTK Global On Everipedia" audiobook, hardcover and Facebook group. The two "reverts" are the second editor undoing their own small edits (+66, +100), so this is not an edit war. The same editor that made the first addition then added another +692 to the Legacy section. I couldn't read that diff or the other small diffs (the tool returned errors), so I can't say what they contain. Nothing suggests a new real-world event: no other pages or languages moved, and the sourced content describes events from 2021.

stories.headline: France U-21 page: year-old qualifier results pruned, briefly reverted, then removed again
stories.summary: This is routine page upkeep, not news. The only edits are on the English page for the France national under-21 football team. Chelsdog, a regular editor, deleted the match boxes for two U21 Euro 2027 qualifiers from October: a 6–0 away win over the Faroe Islands and a 6–1 home win over Estonia. TonySt undid this as "unexplained content removal" (rev 1381262284). Chelsdog then deleted the same 1,497 bytes again with the note "over one year" (rev 1381263060), meaning the results are more than a year old and no longer belong in the recent-results section. That is a common cleanup on national-team pages, and the edit dates fit those October matches being about a year old. The diffs only move the results around and don't change them, and no new result or squad news shows up. The second removal hasn't been challenged so far, so this looks like a one-time misunderstanding rather than an edit war. That could change if TonySt reverts again.

stories.headline: Wu Kangmin (吳康民) zhwiki bio gets sourced early-life expansion; no news event
stories.summary: This story covers the same burst of 7 edits as the earlier routine brief: three registered editors (Gnonich, Will629, 919sth.) working on the Chinese Wikipedia biography of Hong Kong educator Wu Kangmin, long-time principal of Pui Kiu Middle School. Most of the change is one edit by Gnonich (rev 95148194, +1640). It adds sourced early-life material (birth in Shantou, his family's part in the anti-Japanese resistance, the drama troupe he started at age 12, entering Sun Yat-sen University at 16) and an alma mater field. The sources are his own Wen Wei Po columns and a 2012 book. The follow-up edit (95148203, +4) only fixes a broken wikilink bracket ([[梅縣]), and Will629's 95147215 adds a category for Hong Kong secondary-school principals. 919sth. added the Hong Kong centenarians category and then removed it (95148239). That looks like a category correction, but it shows the subject is very old, which is why I'd watch for a later death-related spike. None of the edits I read add a death date, obituary wording or any recent-event source. There have been no edits since 1792333626, and the graph has no other-language versions of the page (no SAME_AS links), so there are none to check for activity.

stories.headline: Houston, BYU season pages updated after week's games and new AP poll
stories.summary: This looks like routine weekly maintenance on two English Wikipedia pages, 2026 Houston Cougars and 2026 BYU Cougars football. A small group of regular sports editors works on both (Torlek, Smitty Smitty, KingSkyLord, Blue Heron Football), and there are no reverts. On the Houston page, TNNSUH added a scoring summary (+1473 bytes) for a home win over No. 18 Oklahoma State. The last score listed is 35–32 Houston, but that may not be the final score. The same editor then retitled the next game as No. 14 Houston (6–1) at No. 10 Utah (6–0). On the BYU page, the AP poll entry now shows BYU at No. 2 with 20 first-place votes, and the upcoming UCF game lists BYU as 6–0. These are pages the two teams' fans keep up to date, not a news event. One open question: the 6–0 record seems to clash with the separate BYU story about a Notre Dame loss, so that game may have happened later or appear in another section. I didn't check this.

stories.headline: EMD SD70 article blanked to redirect a second time; patroller rolls it back again
stories.summary: This is still vandalism, not news. About seven minutes after the first incident, "Bernardo Games oficial" wiped the roughly 89.5k-byte English article "EMD SD70 series" again (rev 1381068429). As before, it was replaced with "#REDIRECT [[Wikipedia]]" and a 1024px LG logo, the same content as the earlier blanking in rev 1381067729. Within 35 seconds, patroller 45dogs used rollback tagged "Vandalism" and the full article came back (rev 1381068508). Before that, the similarly named "Bernardo4565" had undone the first blanking, and 45dogs had reverted an image swap. Three accounts and one page, with no other languages moving. This is a single repeat vandal, not an edit war or a sign of any real-world event about the locomotives. More attempts are possible until the account is warned or blocked.

stories.headline: Sandra Day O'Connor page: minor test edits and name vandalism, reverted
stories.summary: There is no real-world news here. This is small-scale vandalism on the English Wikipedia article about Sandra Day O'Connor, and it has already been reverted. First, temporary account ~2026-56189-06 deleted a letter, turning "Sandra Day" into "Sandra Dy" (rev 1381180507, labelled "spelt wrong"), then put it back (rev 1381180914). Those two edits look like a test. About nine minutes later, temporary account ~2026-56191-76 replaced her name in the opening sentence with "Homer let the barts out" (rev 1381181913), with the misleading summary "it was spelled wrong". Ampil reverted that within about 40 seconds (rev 1381182010). Her dates (March 26, 1930 – December 1, 2023) were never changed, so this has nothing to do with her death. No other languages and no other pages were involved.

stories.headline: Grande Fratello VIP 9 page updated live during day-33 episode; flash vote result still blank
stories.summary: This continues the routine story already being tracked: the same Italian Wikipedia page is being updated live during a Grande Fratello VIP 9 episode. All edits come from a few temporary accounts, mainly ~2026-44750-62, and none are reverts. The newest diffs add more detail about the "televoto flash", a quick public vote. The housemates voted Carmen, Giacomo and Jonathan as the people who get least involved in life in the house. Jonathan was left out of the flash vote because he is already up for the next elimination, so only Carmen and Giacomo face it. Whoever of the two gets fewer votes becomes the second candidate for elimination (revs 152979591, 152979554). The vote result is still a placeholder ("con il ()%, ()"; "%, %"). The other edits are small fixes: a typo correction ("Carnen" to "Carmen") and some rewording. The results will probably be filled in later in the broadcast. This has no news value beyond the show itself.

stories.headline: New dewiki bio of Bonn biodiversity professor Scherber gets routine metadata edits
stories.summary: This is the same story as the tracked creation of the German Wikipedia biography of biologist Christoph Scherber (University of Bonn / LIB). The later edits are all metadata maintenance by experienced editors, with no reverts. Murkus69 added the category "born in the 20th century" (rev 271469773). M2k~dewiki added authority data with his GND number, a sort key and the person-data template (rev 271469789), then added his VIAF identifier (rev 271469796). None of these edits changes the article's content or adds a news hook such as a death, appointment or award. The article is on one language edition only, and three editors have touched it. Routine; no follow-up needed unless new substantive edits appear.

stories.headline: De-wiki page for unreleased novel "Die letzte Königin" appears deleted after SLA
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the routine new-page story.
