The graph has no edits on the German article "Die letzte Königin" since the three already logged: the creation by temporary account ~2026-56392-15, which described an unreleased debut novel about the anti-colonial rebel leader Muhumusa due in January 2027; a HotCat category edit by M2k; and Horst Gräbner's speedy-deletion (SLA) tag. Wikipedia now says both the creation and the SLA revisions don't exist, and the page summary comes back empty. That strongly suggests the speedy deletion went through, but I couldn't check the deletion log directly. I couldn't re-read any diffs, so I'm citing none and relying on the earlier brief for what the page said. There's no sign of a real-world news event, of other languages, or of a dispute. Recommend closing.

stories.headline: Alberta referendum: remain ~76% at 47.6% reporting; results for other ballot questions posted
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked results story. On the independence referendum page, DRWiki1102 is still posting live counts about once a minute. The latest edit shows 1,072,509 for Remain to 332,835 for Referendum, with 47.56% of polls reporting (rev 1381143904). That is about 76.3% remain out of roughly 1.41 million votes. At 43.83% it was 1,027,550 to 319,879 (rev 1381141300), so the share has stayed near 76% since the first numbers at 19% reporting. There is something new on the companion page, "2026 Alberta referendum", which covers the whole multi-question ballot. Muaza Husni added percentage results for Questions 1 to 9 (rev 1381143116) and cited Global News (rev 1381143326). Questions 1 to 5 pass with 56% to 61% for. Questions 6 and 8 are narrowly behind at 49.2% and 48.7% for. Question 7 is at 52% for, Question 9 is tied 50-50, and Question 10 is blank. The table doesn't say what each question asks or how many polls had reported, so treat these as partial figures. On the same page, Atle164 corrected the infobox, which had the 76.4% / 23.6% split under the wrong options (rev 1381142060). There are no reverts and no new Turki al-Maliki edits, and that page should still be split out of this story. Caveats: the independence counts are still uncited, there is no sourced projection, about half of polls are still to be counted, and I haven't checked the other ballot-question figures against the Global News source.

stories.headline: "Shoulder Lean" song page: one temporary account's small edits reverted three times; no news
stories.summary: Over about 6 minutes, the enwiki article "Shoulder Lean" (a 2005 hip-hop single) got 5 small edits (−27 to +5 bytes) from the temporary account ~2026-56080-52. Established editor Tbhotch reverted each batch: 3 reverts, all using the standard rollback summary. Graph history shows the same temporary account spent the previous ~15 minutes making similar small or zero-byte edits to the music video, chart and track-listing sections of other mid-2000s hip-hop/pop song articles (Clumsy, Bring Em Out, Hero, I Can, Get Away, Hey Luv, Burn, Best Thang Smokin'). That looks like one editor's tweaking spree being cleaned up, not a reaction to anything in the real world. There was no talk-page back-and-forth, no other editors, and no other-language pages moved. Caveat: I couldn't fetch any of the diffs (the diff service returned errors), so I can't say what text changed or whether the edits were vandalism or good-faith format/data changes. This judgement rests only on edit metadata.

stories.headline: No new activity on NFL referee Scott Novak page; one-account vandalism remains reverted
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. The graph shows no edits to the Scott Novak article after Gorkypickeral's revert (rev 1380917009). One temporary account, ~2026-55776-01, made all four vandal edits, and each was undone within seconds to about a minute. I read two of the diffs. Rev 1380916860 put the nickname "Holding on the offense" into the lead sentence. Rev 1380916962 changed the infobox name to Scott "Angel Hernandez" Novak, a jab comparing him to the much-criticized MLB umpire. The page is back to its earlier text. The editors who reverted the vandal never reverted each other, so this isn't an edit war. The edits look like an angry fan reacting to a game Novak refereed, but the graph doesn't show which game, and nothing points to separate real-world news.

stories.headline: Hoax 'hamster' line on Carl Bildt page restored by same account after two reverts
stories.summary: New account Asdf1223344 keeps adding a made-up sentence to Carl Bildt's early-life section. The English version reads: "In 1956 Carl was gifted a hamster by his father Daniel Bildt, this hamster would come to play a vital role in his humanitarian research." The first English version said 1951, and a follow-up edit changed it to 1956. A Swedish version went into svwiki. The line has no source and is a joke, not news. Tegel rolled it back on both wikis. The account restored it on en, Bugghost reverted it, and the account then undid that revert too (rev 1380897575). As of the latest edit in the graph, the hoax line is live on enwiki; the svwiki rollback has stayed in place. This is a one-account vandalism campaign turning into a small edit war against two patrollers, not a real-world event about Bildt. The diffs confirm the text, so confidence is higher than in the previous brief.

stories.headline: Dutch actor Maarten Spanjer dead at 73, per new English Wikipedia article
stories.summary: This is two unrelated page creations, not one Olympic story. They were grouped together only because a new-page patroller (Ansgar Slopsbane) tidied both. The main item is a new English article on Dutch actor and presenter Maarten Spanjer, created by MoviesandTelevisionFan. Its first-revision text, which the graph shows as the edit comment, gives his dates as 24 October 1952 – 17 October 2026. That points to a death about a day before these edits. Follow-up edits I read only add an image ("Spanjer in 1977") and an IMDb link. The Dutch Wikipedia summary also describes him as an actor (1952–2026). No other-language edits were linked in the graph, there is no source for the death in any diff I could read, and I could not load the creation diff itself, so the death needs outside confirmation. The second page, "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the 2028 Summer Olympics," is a small new stub by a low-activity account (Hlidk, 5 edits). The patroller's edit adds navboxes and categories, including a "Japan–Russia sports relations" category that looks copied from the Tokyo 2020 page. It looks speculative or boilerplate rather than a sign of any real roster news.

stories.headline: VisionQuest article gets new episode plot summaries; routine TV-series upkeep
stories.summary: Almost all of the activity on the enwiki "VisionQuest" page (a Marvel TV series) is editor Jal11497 adding plot summaries to two episode entries in the Episodes table: +1472 and +1729 bytes. The summaries cover the Butcherbird Killer/Jocasta storyline and Ultron turning on Vision. About an hour later, Marco camino 10 cut one of those summaries by 482 bytes, with the comment "Removing completely unnecessary details." The rest are tiny fixes: a typo fix and a 12-byte "Minor Change". There are no reverts, no edits in other languages and no sign of a dispute. This is the usual pattern after episodes are released: people write up the plot, then others trim it. My guess is that new episodes recently came out, but I didn't check air dates, so that's an inference. Nothing here points to a real-world news event beyond that.

stories.headline: Temporary account swaps "fictional" for "cartoon" on My Little Pony pages; patrollers revert
stories.summary: A single temporary account (~2026-50731-87) made four edits in about 20 minutes to Rainbow Dash (twice), Pinkie Pie and Applejack (My Little Pony), all with the edit summary "NON." I read the diffs. Each edit changed "fictional character" to "cartoon character" in both the short description and the first sentence of the lead. That word swap accounts for the −4 bytes, and nothing else was removed. Patrollers Silvers Rayleigh (rollback) and Augmented Seventh (Interceptor tool) reverted every edit within minutes. The account redid the Rainbow Dash change once after it was reverted, so there is a small amount of repeat editing, but no back-and-forth between established editors, no other languages and no real-world trigger. This looks like an unexplained wording preference that patrollers treated as disruptive, not malicious vandalism and not news. Correcting the scout's note: this story covers 8 edits by 3 editors across 3 pages, and it is the only story tracking these pages, not a duplicate of a separate My Little Pony story.

stories.headline: Italian ex-footballer and coach Angelo Pierleoni reported dead at 63
stories.summary: The Italian Wikipedia biography of Angelo Pierleoni, a former footballer and coach, now says he died on 18 October 2026, aged 63. The main edit (rev 152959542, +413, by Marica Massaro) adds the date to the death fields and a death sentence to the article. It cites a local news report, Marsica Live's "Lutto nel mondo del calcio, è morto il calciatore Angelo Pierleoni", dated the same day. Three other editors followed with small changes that accept the death as fact. One added Fermo as the place of death (152960177). An editor with a temporary account changed "ex calciatore" to "calciatore" (152960021), which is the usual it-wiki style for someone who has died. There was also a wikilink fix (152960273). Nobody reverted anything and no other language editions were involved. The only source is one regional outlet, and nothing else confirms the place of death in Fermo. One diff (152960072) couldn't be read.

stories.headline: French protests: Nice adds curfew for minors, third city after Paris and Lyon (en-wiki)
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked French protests story, not a new event. Since the last brief there are five edits from five editors on en-wiki and fr-wiki, and no reverts. The one new fact comes from Emperorpenguinn on en-wiki's 19 October entry: Nice's mayor set a 9 pm–6 am curfew for minors in the city centre, saying it would protect residents from "hordes of thugs" who had held the streets that weekend. That makes Nice the third city with night curfews, after Paris (10 pm–6 am, applies to everyone) and Lyon (Presqu'île). This fits the earlier signs of a tougher state response, but every curfew claim still rests on the same single Anadolu article. The other edits are housekeeping. Xantxo removed an infobox photo that showed a Correfoc event in Barcelona labelled as a Paris protest. Olevy reworded the Limoges paragraph so it says protesters set fire to the town hall, where it had read as if the fire started by itself; the sources are unchanged (France 3, CNews, France Info), and they say the 1883 building is "largely lost". Salmon Of Ignorance fixed "propoganda" to "propaganda" in the paragraph about Saint-Denis mayor Bally Bagayoko. B-noa's fr typo fix was not read.

stories.headline: Ice Cream Man (2026 film): two joke edits to reviews line, both reverted within a minute
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-55276-33) rewrote the reception sentence twice. The first edit (rev 1381182207) changed "negative reviews" to "positives" and added made-up quotes: "THE BEST HORROR MOVIE OF ALL TIME" and "IT WAS FUNNY KEVIN". The second (rev 1381182365) added "but was funny as a mofo so go watch it". Celjski Grad undid the first through the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, and ClueBot NG undid the second about 7 seconds after it was saved. The edits weren't flagged as reverts in the data, but the edit summaries show both were. The stable text still says the film opened in US theatres on August 7, 2026, through Iconic Events Releasing, to negative reviews. Only one English page is involved, there have been no edits since the bot revert, and nothing points to a real-world event. This matches the earlier brief.

stories.headline: An-225 Mriya article: one vandal edit reverted, then a wikilink fix; no news
stories.summary: There were five small edits to English Wikipedia's Antonov An-225 Mriya article in about six minutes. Three accounts were involved, and all five edits were in the Development section. A temporary account added 3 bytes. Netstars22 reverted it about 30 seconds later with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, labelling it non-constructive. Canadayay then made three edits (+16, −20, +20) that its edit comments describe as adding a link to "Buran". The diff text could not be fetched this session, so this account is based on edit metadata and comments. A prior brief that did read the diffs said the same: a "The"→"тнε" vandal edit, and a caption link to the Buran programme. The graph shows no other-language pages linked to this article and no edits beyond this one page, so nothing points to a real-world event. Routine; I recommend closing.

stories.headline: Honda's 2027 MotoGP lineup: Alonso to LCR, Moreira promoted to factory team with Quartararo
stories.summary: This is a follow-up on the existing Honda 2027 lineup story, not a new event. MotoFan9373 replaced the TBA Honda placeholders on the 2027 MotoGP World Championship article (rev 1381145554). David Alonso goes to Pro Honda LCR and Diogo Moreira goes to Honda HRC Castrol alongside Quartararo. Both changes cite MotoGP.com articles dated 20 October 2026. The same editor then changed the "Rider changes" prose to match (rev 1381147211) and removed a Notes section that was no longer needed after the "subject to HRC placement" footnotes came out (rev 1381147323). New editor Itsabrori added that Álex Rins "retired from motorcycle racing", with no source (rev 1381146841). An experienced editor reverted it over grammar (rev 1381146953), so the Rins retirement claim is still unverified. There was one revert and no back-and-forth: these are routine roster updates on one English-language page.

stories.headline: Schoolyard vandalism spreads to Radio Venceremos; El Salvador 'RIP' edit still live
stories.summary: This is a small, low-level vandalism spree on en-wiki, not a news event. The newest edit is on Radio Venceremos. Temporary account ~2026-56256-69, with the edit summary "Added key info", inserted "LeBron decided that it was time for a change" into a sentence about the station after the 1992 end of the war (rev 1381223555). Joyous! reverted it within about two minutes (rev 1381223783). Joyous! also cleaned up the Birth of Venus vandalism earlier, and that page and History of El Salvador are both pages a Salvadoran school group might target, which fits the scout's note. On History of El Salvador, BLOSSOM1295 put "Rest in peace the" in front of the lead in two edits (revs 1381222782, 1381222838). No later edit to that page shows up in the graph, so it is probably still live and needs a revert. Nothing in it points to a real death or event. The Birth of Venus diffs I tried to re-read this time didn't load, so the details there come from the previous brief. One caveat: no single editor vandalized more than one page, so the link between the pages is inferred from the subject matter and the shared patrollers.

stories.headline: Not news: temp-account vandalism and a stray train edit, all reverted
stories.summary: Nothing here points to a real-world event. The cluster is several new temporary accounts making unrelated low-quality edits on en and es Wikipedia, and patrollers reverted each one within minutes. Since the last brief, ~2026-55800-34 has kept editing en:Mumbai CSMT–Solapur Vande Bharat Express. In revs 1380897895 and 1380898194 it put Hinglish notes about a Lucknow–New Delhi Vande Bharat departure ("subah 6 10 per chalegi", meaning it will run at 6:10 in the morning) into the infobox name and the hatnote. Annh07 reverted both. This looks like a confused editor using the wrong article, not news about this train. However, the account did make the edit several times, so it could hint at a Lucknow service, and nothing here confirms that. On en:Elmopalooza, ~2026-55856-82 twice replaced Kenny Loggins with "Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz" (rev 1380896773), a joke. ClueBot NG reverted it, then IrisChronomia, who flagged possible block evasion. The earlier prank edits to en and es Yeremay Hernández and the small edits to Ochoa, Nino Bravo and Teófilo Gutiérrez are unchanged since the last brief (that brief also read revs 175886380 and 1380896646). These pages don't share any editors apart from the patrollers.

stories.headline: Soth Kevin page restored after second blanking; same spree also hit Phnom Penh, Suno
stories.summary: The blanking of en:Soth Kevin, a Cambodian Kun Khmer boxer, has been undone. JavaHurricane reverted the second temporary account's blanking (rev 1381279184) with a WikiShield revert (rev 1381279249), which put back the lead and the full boxing-career section. Before that, the account ~2026-56301-19 went on to blank pages beyond the Cambodia theme. It cut the whole infobox and opening of en:Phnom Penh (rev 1381279316, −10,158 bytes). That is the exact byte count that the earlier account ~2026-56222-16 removed from the same page, which makes it much more likely that both temporary accounts are one person, though we still can't prove it. It also removed the infobox and lead of en:Suno (rev 1381279504, −25,671 bytes), leaving a broken fragment, and made two cuts to en:Talkpal AI (−2,572 and −5,711 bytes; not read). The edits are destructive and give no reason or new information, so I see no real-world event behind them. We don't know whether the Phnom Penh, Suno and Talkpal AI edits have been reverted yet. This is vandalism, not news.

stories.headline: Unrelated vandalism on Airbus A340, Dallas and Scott Novak pages, linked only by patrol bots
stories.summary: These three en-wiki pages are tied together only by the anti-vandal patrollers ClueBot NG and Cannolis. No vandal account touched more than one page, so this is coincidence, not coordination. Dallas: Kevinvalles209 blanked large parts of the article twice (−33.5k, then −65.4k bytes), and ClueBot NG and Cannolis restored it both times. The scout's "no reverts" note is wrong: those restorations are reverts, even though they aren't flagged as such. Scott Novak (an NFL referee): temporary account ~2026-55776-01 replaced the lead with "sucks at being a referee", then added the nickname "holding on the offense". Both edits were reverted. That's typical fan anger after a game and hints that he worked a recent NFL game, but nothing here confirms which one. Airbus A340: on top of the vandalism in the existing story, Emirloves67chickennuggets added a farewell "editor message" thanking the A340-600 and naming "TC-JDM" (a Turkish registration). ClueBot NG reverted it. This one user's sentiment is weak evidence of a real A340-600 retirement, possibly at Turkish Airlines, and I can't confirm it. Recommend folding this into the existing A340 vandalism story. Dallas and Novak are separate low-value vandalism with no news event.

stories.headline: Korean Wikipedia gets new article on Sept. 21 DMZ mine blast that injured three ROK soldiers
stories.summary: On ~Oct 20, 2026, user Legacy of Justinian created a new kowiki article (+6,087 bytes, rev 42683042) on the "25th Infantry Division DMZ mine explosion." It says that on 21 Sept 2026, in the DMZ in Yeoncheon county, Gyeonggi province, a ROK Army reconnaissance team was clearing a path ahead of a UN Command site inspection when a mine went off. A second blast followed as others moved in to evacuate the injured; three soldiers were hurt. Citing a Ministry of National Defense/JCS joint task-force final report (korea.kr), the article says the mine was a North Korean-made plastic anti-personnel mine planted south of the MDL, and Seoul calls that deliberate. It also says Kim Yo Jong called the incident staged and threatened to reinforce against the 21st Division. A follow-up edit (rev 42683047) adds that the team had 3 officers/NCOs and 15 enlisted. The editor also added a DPRK military-incidents navbox to the article on North Korea's involvement in the Ukraine war (rev 42683068). That edit is housekeeping, not a separate development. This is a write-up of an incident about a month old, sourced to Korean press and government briefings, not breaking news. Only 2 editors appear (not the 4 the scout noted), there are no reverts, and no other-language pages have moved. I have not independently confirmed the facts beyond the article's cited sources.

stories.headline: Patroller reverts two unrelated POV edits on Manusmriti and US racial unrest pages
stories.summary: These two pages are not one story. The only thing connecting them is the patroller Tankishguy, who undid one edit on each page within about 11 minutes. On Manusmriti, temporary account ~2026-56112-88 added about 2,170 bytes of unsourced advocacy to the Controversies section (rev 1381113538). It argued that the text's offensive verses were inserted later "during the era of Muslim rule", and recast sati and the Shudra category in its own terms. The edit summary complains that earlier attempts had been removed, so this person has probably tried before, but it is a one-person push, not a two-sided edit war. Tankishguy reverted it about 2 minutes later (rev 1381113891). On United States racial unrest (2020–2023), a different temporary account, ~2026-56354-02, changed "murder of George Floyd" to "overdose death of george flloyd" (rev 1381115522). This was plain vandalism, reverted within a minute as such (rev 1381115583). Neither edit points to anything happening in the world, and no other languages or editors are involved.

stories.headline: NZ 2026 election polling page: cleanup edits around recent Labour-led polls
stories.summary:
This latest burst on the English Wikipedia page "Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election" is housekeeping. No new polls were added. AusYou and a temporary account (~2026-56089-54) made about eight small edits (deltas between −2 and +138 bytes), and none were reverts. The edits:
- Reordered the Whakaata Māori–Curia Te Tai Tokerau electorate poll (5–15 Oct, n=500, Te Ao Māori News, 20 Oct) so the party vote row comes first. That poll has Labour leading the party vote 27 to 25, and its source headline credits Hūhana Lyndon with leading the electorate.
- Corrected a publication name in the Ikaroa-Rāwhiti poll citation.
- Filled empty electorate table cells with n/a.
- Adjusted a 9–19 Oct national poll (n=1,458): AusYou changed the Labour lead row from 28.7 to 29.7, then put it back to 28.7. That is one editor correcting their own change, not an edit war.
The polls already on the page suggest Labour is narrowly ahead in mid-October 2026 polling, but this batch of edits adds no new information.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on sculptor Herbert Gebauer (1925–2010) still getting routine cleanup
stories.summary: This is still the newly created German Wikipedia biography of Herbert Gebauer, a Stuttgart-Sillenbuch sculptor who died in 2010. It is the same story as the routine brief already on file. The newest edits are standard cleanup by experienced editors. Kurator71 removed a link to a portrait photo that doesn't exist on Commons. AHZ linked the article on his father, the painter Paul Gebauer. M2k added authority data (GND and VIAF) and a link to the Commons category. Together with the earlier quality-check tag and the categories added before, that makes 8 edits by 4 editors, all on one language and with no reverts. Nothing in the text adds a new event: the death date is still 4 April 2010, and the main source is still a 2024 publication from a private collection of his work. The only open question is whether the article is kept after the relevance check.

stories.headline: Boca Juniors win 3–1 away at Vasco da Gama to reach Copa Sudamericana 2026 final
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked Boca story on es-wiki "Copa Sudamericana 2026". The new edit, by AMBlanco25 (rev 175927508), adds the scorers for the semifinal leg: Rodríguez (66') for the home side, and Di Lollo (4'), Merentiel (34') and Paredes (88') for the visitors, who are Boca. That matches VicenteTGO99's result line of 1:3 (rev 175927496), the same edit that turned on the Final section with Boca Juniors (ARG) as the home side. So Boca appear to have won the leg 3–1 away in Brazil and gone through to the final. One detail doesn't add up: two Boca goals came before half-time (4' and 34'), but the half-time score is listed as 0:1, so one of those entries is probably a typo. The aggregate score, the first-leg result and the final's opponent are still not confirmed in the edits. There are three registered editors, no reverts, no other languages and no sign of vandalism.

stories.headline: 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs page: wording edits undone in one revert, no new results
stories.summary: Nothing has been edited on the English article on the 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs since the last brief. The latest revision is still Conyo14's revert (rev 1381209128), which undid four small edits by two temporary-account editors, giving the reason "unnecessary edits/unexplained removal of content". I read the first-round edit (rev 1381208555). It rewrote the Lightning–Canadiens and Penguins–Flyers write-ups, adding tiebreaker scores and two errors: it gave Pittsburgh and Philadelphia 106 points (the article says 98) and said Tampa Bay won the Metropolitan Division tiebreaker. The revert put the earlier text back. The text saying Vegas swept Colorado in the Western Conference final was already in the article before these edits and was not changed. This is one revert on one page in one language, with no back-and-forth, so it is routine upkeep rather than an edit war or a new real-world development.

stories.headline: Lua Blanco: en-wiki dispute over death claim quiet; editors now only doing cleanup
stories.summary: The scout's signal (a revert and 758 bytes of churn) mostly comes from edits we covered in our last brief: SuperFastSpellChecker's "unsourced" rollback and the restorations by StarDeg and Jkaharper. Since that brief there are two en-wiki edits we hadn't read, and neither one challenges the death. StarDeg changed the lead from "is" to "was", so it now reads "March 5, 1987 - October 18, 2026 ... was a Brazilian actress" (rev 1380903113). Seasider53, an experienced registered editor, copyedited the early-life section. He also removed the names of her non-notable siblings, citing WP:BLPPRIVACY, and left the death material in place (rev 1380904395). No one has reverted the death again since the rollback about 15 minutes earlier, so there is no edit war. Two caveats from earlier briefs still stand: en-wiki still has no news source for the death, and the "intestinal cancer" detail and Rio de Janeiro place of death have not been verified. pt-wiki still cites CNN Brasil and Quem, which supports the death itself being real.

stories.headline: Crown Jewel 2026 page: editors cut speculation that WWE may move event from Riyadh
stories.summary: Four editors made five edits to the en-wiki page for WWE's upcoming Crown Jewel (2026) event. The one edit that matters (rev 1381092140, -1,261 bytes) took out a "Security concerns" section. That section cited the "October 2026 attacks on Saudi airports" and "2026 Yemen offensives". It also quoted Dave Meltzer via 411Mania (Oct 2 and Oct 12, 2026): no promotion for the event had appeared at Money in the Bank, WWE had back-up plans including Las Vegas, and he thought the event would most likely be moved. The editor who removed it called it WP:CRYSTALBALL speculation and said the source never mentions "security concerns". Separately, one editor removed and another restored footnotes about pending title matches (Zayn vs Rhodes on Raw Oct 19, Green vs Bella on SmackDown Oct 30). That was one removal and one restoration, not yet an edit war. The page itself is routine event-card upkeep. The cut text hints at a bigger real-world story (attacks on Saudi airports, a possible relocation), but I can't find a page for those attacks anywhere in the graph, so the claim is unconfirmed here. Two diffs failed to load (JDC808, GodofDemonwars); both were small edits.

stories.headline: Jamar, Gujarat: schoolboy vandalism by temporary account reverted twice
stories.summary: This is vandalism with no news hook. Temporary account ~2026-56137-71 edited the lead of the en-wiki stub on Jamar, a village and former princely state in Gujarat, twice in about two minutes. Both edits replaced the village description with joke text about a student at "Youngker HS" named Jamar (rev 1381196125, 1381196423). The edit summaries passed these off as "context" about the city's history. Anti-vandalism patrollers undid both within about a minute each: Celjski Grad with the Interceptor tool, and HundredVisionsAndRevisions with WikiShield. The two editors didn't revert each other, so this isn't an edit war, and no other pages or languages were involved.

stories.headline: Simple English 'Hello Kitty' blanking vandalism continues; page restored for now
stories.summary: This is still page-blanking vandalism by one temporary account (~2026-56234-44) on Simple English Wikipedia's Hello Kitty article. It is not a real-world event. Since the last brief, the account made two more rounds of the same pattern. First it cut the article down to its images and the bare title (rev 11036561 / 11036565, -3.7k), then it blanked the page completely (11036562 / 11036566). Each round was rolled back with Twinkle by Spiderone and tagged as vandalism (11036563, and 11036567, which restores the full ~4k article text). No later edits show up in the graph, so the page is in its restored state for now. The removed text was standard, long-standing content about the character and Sanrio, with no new claims. The story stays on one page in one language, with three editors (the vandal, ChenzwBot, Spiderone). There is no sign of a block yet, and the account could come back.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on 19th-century Polish general Józef Rautenstrauch
stories.summary: This is a new historical biography, not a news event. Asdrubal created the German Wikipedia stub "Józef Rautenstrauch" (rev 271439890, +1535 bytes). The stub describes a Polish general (1773–1842) who served under Józef Poniatowski in 1812 and at Leipzig, did not take part in the November Uprising of 1830, and then joined the Russian army. About 10 minutes later M2k, a regular de-wiki maintenance editor, added an image, a Commonscat link, VIAF authority data and a sort key, and changed the birth date in the Personendaten from "7. Mai 1773" to just "1773" (rev 271440097). Saliwo then fixed a one-character typo. There are no reverts, no other languages and no link to current events. The edit churn is simply the article being created, which is what the scout expected.

stories.headline: Sex shop vandalism reverted by Drmies; article restored, no new edits since
stories.summary: This is an update to the vandalism run on the English "Sex shop" article. The edit the last brief flagged as still live has now been reverted. Experienced editor Drmies reverted temporary account ~2026-56238-27 (rev 1381082476) about three and a half minutes after its edit. The diff shows the restore was complete: the first sentence again says the retailer "sells products related to sexual or erotic entertainment" instead of "forces kids to use products". Léon Vidal's Paris shops are back to the 1920s, which matches the cited book "City of Pleasure: Paris Between the Wars". A graph query shows no edits after this revert on either Sex shop or The Mask (1994 film), so the article looks clean as of this check. The full run was three bad-faith edits from three accounts in about 19 minutes, each reverted by a different patroller. There was no back-and-forth between two editors, only one language was involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. The "Chuck Engelman" producer line on The Mask (rev 1381079643) has no recorded revert in the graph. I haven't checked it against a source.

stories.headline: Ota Jirák death entry trimmed to one source; place of death removed from article
stories.summary: Update to the breaking story. Czech Wikipedia still reports that actor and presenter Ota Jirák died on 17 October 2026, aged 77. No one has disputed the death or reverted it. Experienced editor David V. (rev 26309576) has since taken out the temporary account's sentence saying Jirák died "on Saturday at his cottage in the Mladá Boleslav area." He also removed the Blesk.cz citation ("Legendární Hele přišlo o hlas. V 77 letech zemřel herec Ota Jirák"). His edit comment says he could not find the place of death in the source. The article now says only "Zemřel 17. října 2026 ve věku 77 let" ("He died on 17 October 2026, aged 77"), backed by the Novinky.cz piece "Zemřel herec Otakar Jirák" (18 Oct 2026). The other new edits are housekeeping: fixes to the Kinobox film-database link by Petrsv and Jindřich Rubeš. Taken together, the death and date are stable, but the place of death is unconfirmed. Earlier edits had said both Prague and the Mladá Boleslav area, and the article now gives neither. A graph query found no linked articles in other languages for this page.

stories.headline: Suvendu Adhikari page: no new edits since two reverted blankings
stories.summary: Nothing has happened on en.wiki's Suvendu Adhikari article since the last brief. The graph shows only the same four edits: two single-edit temporary accounts (~2026-53924-48 and ~2026-56119-04) each deleted the same 8,470-byte block, and ClueBot NG and IrisChronomia restored it within 13 and 42 seconds. The page ends up unchanged. Nothing has been edited since the last revert, so the blanking has not continued for now. I tried to read all four diffs again and none would load ("missing content"). That could mean an administrator has hidden those revisions, but I can't confirm it. So this update rests on edit history and summaries only, and I cite no diffs. This isn't news about Adhikari himself. I'd suggest folding this into the existing vandalism story rather than tracking it separately.

stories.headline: Test-style vandalism on ja.wiki Elon Musk page reverted twice; no news event
stories.summary: Over about 14 minutes, a temporary account (~2026-56073-43) made three small edits to the Japanese Wikipedia article イーロン・マスク (Elon Musk). The edit summaries were keyboard filler ("あ", "あいうえお", "おｎ"). One of these edits (rev 111446464) cut into the lead paragraph, which describes Musk's background, his role in the Trump administration and DOGE, and the companies he co-founded. Black Oar rolled back the account's first edit. Kugelschreibers then reverted the rest with Twinkle, tagging it "荒らしの差し戻し" (vandalism revert). The restored lead (rev 111446498) matches the earlier text and adds no new facts. The same Wikidata item (Q317521) has no edit activity in other languages over this period, so nothing points to a real-world trigger. This looks like isolated test edits or vandalism by one account, already cleaned up, not an edit war or breaking news.

stories.headline: Routine upkeep on fa-wiki page for Iranian streaming series 'Taxi'; no news hook
stories.summary: Three edits hit the Persian Wikipedia article on 'Taxi' (تاکسی), an Iranian 12-episode streaming series. It is directed by Hassan Nouri and adapted from a book by Soroush Sehat. A temporary/anonymous account added six cast names (Amir Nouri, Seyed Ali Salehi, Hamed Vakili and others; +209). Dexbot's AI anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) automatically undid that edit about a minute later. The graph does not mark this as a revert, but the bot's comment says it is one. Editor Carl then made a cleanup pass (−572): he trimmed long encoded reference URLs, removed a duplicate wikilink and emptied the IMDb template ID. The page already says filming ran from 17 Mordad to 29 Shahrivar 1405 (Aug–Sep 2026), and none of these edits add new real-world facts. The churn looks like ordinary maintenance, not a reaction to an event. The only open question is whether the cast addition was accurate, and the bot removed it without checking.

stories.headline: Racist vandalism spree on Simple English ethnic-group pages, quickly reverted
stories.summary: This is not a content dispute. One temporary account (~2026-56022-80) added one-line racist and sexually explicit slurs to Simple English Wikipedia's "Manx Americans" and "Cornish Americans" pages, twice on each, over about 7 minutes. Every insertion was reverted within seconds to minutes by patrollers Spiderone and NDG and by the anti-vandalism bot ChenzwBot, and Spiderone tagged them as vandalism. The diffs I read (11035821, 11035825, 11035835, 11035837) contain only abusive text, with no real claims and nothing citing a source. In the same short window the graph shows this account also touched Norwegian Americans, Irish Americans, Ku Klux Klan and Trumpism. I didn't read those diffs, but the pattern fits a single trolling spree rather than a reaction to any real-world event. There is no news signal here, and no more monitoring is needed unless the account or similar ones keep going.

stories.headline: France 17 Oct: Rouen added to riot-hit cities in lead; Marseille church smoke from bin fires
stories.summary:
Two small edits have come in since the last brief, both on fr-wiki's "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026", from registered editors and with no reverts. They are folded into this story rather than opening a duplicate.
- **Rouen in the lead (rev 240495881, Jerome misc):** Rouen was added to the list of cities with major riots and looting. This brings the lead in line with the Rouen looting section reported earlier.
- **Limoges:** the same lead sentence says Limoges's town hall, a listed historic monument, was "destroyed" by arson. That text was already there and this diff doesn't show its source, so treat it as unconfirmed until a citation is found.
- **Marseille (rev 240495930, Gottseidank):** a photo caption now says the black smoke around the Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul came from bin fires. That plays down any suggestion the church itself was attacked. It is only a caption, with no press source.
There are no new casualty, arrest or turnout figures and still no versions in other languages, so the story remains steady but quiet. Earlier open points still stand: the Vance quote and the looting summary have no source, the Magyar quote is cited to an article that predates it, and the Nancy figures depend on a single source.

stories.headline: cs.wiki "Satanic panic" article: copy-paste move to Czech title undone
stories.summary: The large churn is Czech Wikipedia housekeeping and does not point to anything happening in the world. Editor K.i.f copied the roughly 32 kB article "Satanic panic" into a new page, "Satanská panika" (+31,547), then replaced the original with a redirect (-31,944). The redirect carried a move-proposal template citing Czech media that use the Czech term. About six minutes later, OJJ used TwinkleGlobal to restore the full article under the old title (+32,021, summary "Špatně", meaning "Wrong"). OJJ then removed the move template from "Satanská panika" with the summary "Přesunuto" ("Moved"). The diff tool now labels these revisions under "Satanská panika", which suggests a proper page move that keeps the edit history replaced the copy-paste. Only two editors were involved, there was no back-and-forth reverting, and no other language versions changed. This is a disagreement over how to retitle the page, not an edit war or news. The one open question is the article's final title, which the history-preserving move seems to have settled.

stories.headline: Vandalism on two ja.wiki pages (Manga Mura, Shuhei Kojima) reverted by patroller
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is low-level vandalism on two unrelated ja.wiki pages, and the same patroller, Black Oar, cleaned up both. On 漫画村 (Manga Mura), the defunct pirate-manga site, temporary account ~2026-56040-46 replaced the lead and several paragraphs with the name "黒柳徹子" (Tetsuko Kuroyanagi, a TV host), with the edit comment "くろや" (rev 111448499, −1918 bytes). Black Oar reverted it about 2 minutes later. So the "large churn" the scout flagged is one blanking and its revert, not real content change. On 小島脩平 (Shuhei Kojima, a retired baseball player), another temporary account added a line break in the lead. The joke phrase "応援歌が良いよ" ("his cheering song is good") was already in the article before that edit (rev 111448603), and Black Oar's rollback removed it (rev 111448623). The only link between the pages is Black Oar's patrol run: there are no other editors and no other languages involved.

stories.headline: Same temp account vandalises Rohan (name) after Internet challenge; both edits reverted
stories.summary: The scout was mostly right, with one correction: the Rohan edit was not random churn. It came from temp account ~2026-56450-07, the same account that vandalised Internet challenge with "tung c" and "TTT" earlier in this story. On Rohan (name), it rewrote the lead to say Rohan "is a name for tuffs and tungs" and added "indian, chinese, LOTR" to the list of origins (rev 1381267402). That is the same "tung" joke as on Internet challenge. Nil NZ reverted it with WikiShield about 7 minutes later (rev 1381267831, revert diff not read). On List of people from St. Petersburg, Florida, a different temp account (~2026-56118-78) changed the page's short description from "None" to "Tiffany S. Black" (rev 1381267730), most likely a name drop. Nil NZ reverted it about 2 minutes later (rev 1381267835). Nothing new on Bacchus Marsh Grammar or Cmune in this window, and nothing here points to a real-world event. Still unchecked: whether the leftover Bacchus Marsh vandalism ("eqsuitute" and the sentence-style heading) has been fixed.

stories.headline: Anti-government vandalism hits Indonesian pages; Satyam Audios link is a coincidence
stories.summary: This cluster is two unrelated things, joined only because ClueBot NG reverted edits on all four pages. Within about four minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56076-24) added Indonesian-language insults to Prabowo Subianto (a fake death date and a "resign" rant), Government of Indonesia ("criticize it and you get silenced") and the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (complaining that critics' social-media accounts get taken down while online gambling sites stay unblocked). ClueBot reverted each edit within seconds. Earlier, a separate temporary account added "love epstein" to Prabowo's infobox, and KuyaMoHirowo reverted it. The vandalism complains about censorship and account takedowns, which may reflect current anger online at Komdigi, but the edits contain no factual claims, and the matching pages in other languages show no recent activity. The Satyam Audios churn (an Indian record label) is a good-faith cleanup by KlWI, who cut promotional text. ClueBot mistook it for vandalism and restored it, and KlWI reverted it again. That's a bot false positive, not an edit war, and it has nothing to do with Indonesia.

stories.headline: No news: one editor's wikilink spree on footballer pages, partly reverted
stories.summary: This is not a transfer or squad story. All six edits come from two accounts. "Aliyu baba goni" added small wikilinks (+4 to +33 bytes, with comments like "wiki link") across 13 football-related pages in about 17 minutes. Those pages include Nigerian figures (Osimhen, Lookman, Iwobi, Musa, Bala Mohammed) and Portuguese-league players (Tormena, Galeno, Lima, Rúben Micael), so this looks like editing practice rather than a reaction to something that happened. Experienced editor GiantSnowman reverted two of the links as "OVERLINK" and "inappropriate link" and reworded Galeno (−43). There are only two editors, no other languages involved, and no back-and-forth reverting, so it isn't an edit war or vandalism. One caveat: the diff text could not be fetched, so this conclusion rests on edit sizes, edit comments and the editor's history in the graph.

stories.headline: New UK channel 5Drama's Wikipedia page gets tidied as its 21 Oct launch nears
stories.summary: Three registered editors made routine improvements to the English Wikipedia article on 5Drama, a new Paramount UK/Channel 5 channel. According to the article, the channel was announced on 24 September 2026 and launches on 21 October 2026, taking over from 5Select and swapping programme-guide slots with 5Action. The article's sources are a Paramount press release and a Deadline story. Most edits came from Benmathieson901 (37 edits in total, all on this one page). They added the press-release citation, which replaced an 'unreferenced' tag, and added then removed a website link pointing to the 5Select page. Andreworkney made style fixes: switching to British spelling ('programme'), removing Freesat from the terrestrial channel list, and correcting bold text. EighteenFiftyNine added a wikilink. There were no reverts or conflicts, and nothing reads as vandalism. The page activity simply reflects the channel launch, which is minor news. Whether the single-page editor is linked to the broadcaster is unknown. The text is mildly promotional ('popular original British dramas') but has sources.

stories.headline: Small dewiki content dispute over Helmut Neunzert bio ends in admin reset
stories.summary: The four edits on the German article about mathematician Helmut Neunzert are a small content dispute, not a news event or a death update. In rev 271468785, editor Michael Hilden reverted an earlier removal by Horst Gräbner (rev 271428446) and restored about 1 KB of text. The restored text covers a reunion of Neunzert's doctoral students in Inzell after his 90th birthday (25–27 Sept 2026), a group photo, a claim of more than 250 academic descendants in the Mathematics Genealogy Project, and an upcoming talk on 21 Oct 2026 at the Fraunhofer ITWM's 30th-anniversary colloquium. Administrator Mpns then reset the page to the version before the edit war (rev 271469245) and removed that text again. Another editor followed with an image-size tweak. The graph has no revert flags on these edits, but the edit summaries show a back-and-forth over whether the material is notable enough. Only one page and language moved. Nothing suggests a change in Neunzert's status, and the text describes him as alive and scheduled to speak.

stories.headline: Aaron Judge ja.wiki vandalism reverted; tie to new 'THE LUV BUGS' page is just a patroller
stories.summary: This is minor vandalism, already cleaned up, with nothing new on the Aaron Judge page since the last brief. One temporary account (~2026-56106-07) made two false edits to the lead of the Japanese Aaron Judge article. The first (111447627) changed Yankees to Dragons and turned his AL home run record into an NPB record. The second (111447645), labelled "content correction," made him Samurai Japan's manager at the 2026 WBC. Daiyamond (via Twinkle) and Black Oar (111447653) reverted them within about a minute each. The scout's note says there were "more reverts," but there are none after 111447653. The only link to THE LUV BUGS is Daiyamond, a patroller who also tidied that page. It is a brand-new article about a Japanese music label (started September 2024, Shibuya WOMB events), created from a sandbox template by Todorokigotarou. It cites only the label's own sites, and its release list runs to 2026-09. Daiyamond removed leftover sandbox markup (111447688) and North Pacific tagged the page Uncategorized. That is routine work on a new page, not news, so the two pages should not be treated as one story.

stories.headline: Spanish Wikipedia vandalism hits Torvalds, Martínez-Bordiú pages; hoax death reverted
stories.summary: This is a prank spree on Spanish Wikipedia (eswiki), not news. On the Carmen Martínez-Bordiú article, temporary account ~2026-56315-78 added a death date of 21 Oct 2026 and a death place of "Pionyang (Corea del Norte)" (rev 175930900, summary "Fecha"). The same account padded her full name with a long string of joke names (rev 175930971). Another account replaced Franco with "Adolf Hitler" as her grandfather and moved her birthplace to Beijing (rev 175930873). Dcaminop added "alias el tio Paquito de mi padre" and changed her birth year and place (rev 175931086). On Linus Torvalds, Holawe3e293 added "hola estrella" in front of his name (rev 175931445), following the "kissed/married" prank edits covered in an earlier brief. Every edit was undone within minutes by patrollers Castellónenred, Geom and Nuria, the witch. The death claim is the only edit that looks like news. I treat it as a hoax because the place is absurd, it cites nothing, the same account was making joke edits at the same time, and the graph tracks no other-language versions of her page, so there is no sign the change spread to other wikis. One gap: I have no outside confirmation that she is alive. The style, the new and temporary accounts and the timing fit one group of friends, probably at a school.

stories.headline: Łukasz Gibała recorded as taking office as Kraków mayor on 20 October 2026
stories.summary: Three editors updated Polish Wikipedia's list of Kraków mayors (Prezydent Miasta Krakowa) the same way, with no reverts. In rev 81016973, the current officeholder changes from Stanisław Kracik, marked "p.f." (pełniący funkcję, meaning acting), to Łukasz Gibała, with a term start of 20 October 2026. Rev 81017004 removes Gibała's "elekt" (mayor-elect) label, gives him a start date of 20 October 2026, and ends the acting period that began on 26 May 2026. Revs 81017063 and 81017124 add Gibała's photo to the infobox and start a days-in-office counter from 20 October. The graph shows matching edits on related pages within hours: plwiki "Stanisław Kracik" ("zakonczyl pelnienie funkcji", meaning his acting term ended), plwiki "Łukasz Gibała" ("objął urząd", meaning he took office) and dewiki "Łukasz Gibała" ("Aktualisierung", meaning update). I didn't read those diffs. Taken together, this points to a real and expected handover from an acting mayor to the elected one, not vandalism or an edit war. The edits don't explain why Kraków had an acting mayor from May or how Gibała was elected (possibly an early election), so that background is unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Routine dewiki: church article gets altar photo and link; Koblenz ultras recreation appears deleted
stories.summary: This is an update to a story already rated routine, and nothing suggests a news event. The only edits since the last brief are two small, non-minor additions by EoNy to the new article 'Dorfkirche Sandhagen (Galenbeck)'. One adds an interior photo of the pulpit altar (Kanzelaltar) (rev 271505111). The other adds a footnote linking the altar to the 'Liste von Kirchen mit Kanzelaltären', a list of churches with pulpit altars (rev 271505215). This is normal article building. On 'Kamikaze Koblenz', AsepTisch's second speedy-deletion tag (rev 271505036) can no longer be retrieved. That suggests the recreated ultras page has been deleted again, the same way the first version was. I'm inferring this; I haven't confirmed it in a deletion log. Nothing new has happened on the footballer page 'Marcel Leon Gauss', which is still expected to be deleted. There are no reverts, no other language editions involved, and all the editors are familiar maintenance and author accounts. The scout's note holds.

stories.headline: Vandalism on eswiki '19 de octubre' resumes; latest bad edit not yet reverted
stories.summary: This is still the vandalism spree on Spanish Wikipedia's date page '19 de octubre'. It is not a news event. After Gelo DemonPlayer restored the standard intro (rev 175906846, 'vandalismo eliminado'), the account Vores452 came back about 7 minutes later (rev 175906908). It again replaced the opening sentence with the same personal sexual remark. No later edit shows up in the graph, so this vandalism may still be live on the page. All the edits come from one account plus one temporary account, which reverters Ontzak, SeroBOT and Gelo DemonPlayer have been undoing. No births, deaths or events entries were touched and no other language versions changed. The page needs another revert, and Vores452 is a likely candidate for a block.

stories.headline: Hilltop High School (California): prank edits reverted, no new activity, no news
stories.summary: This is the same activity as the existing vandalism story. There are no edits newer than the last brief: the page has only six revisions in the graph, and the latest is Meters removing an empty History section. One temporary account, ~2026-56136-17, made three unsourced additions. The first said the swim team won state titles "over 30 times in a row under coach Ethos Pathos-Pythagorean", which is an obviously made-up name. The second called the student body the "most reportedly islamic" public school in San Diego County. The third said a named student started the district's first mosque or Islamic club. Patrollers Nil NZ (using the WikiShield tool) and Meters reverted the additions as unsourced, and Meters also cited the rule against naming students who aren't notable. The activity is on one page in one language, by one account, and nobody re-added anything, so there's no edit war and no sign of a real-world event. This should be merged with or closed as a duplicate of the prior story.

stories.headline: Korean Wikipedia: new Bundaberg drinks stub blanked and redirected; Sprite article expanded
stories.summary: Two editors account for all of this activity on Korean Wikipedia: a temporary account (~2026-56049-73) and the experienced editor Ykhwong. The scout's note said 4 editors, but the dossier shows only these two. The temporary account created a new page, 분다버그, about the Australian soft-drink brand Bundaberg Brewed Drinks. Over about 20 edits it added an unsourced overview, written in a promotional tone, with a list of flavours, a reference to the brand's 10 years in Korea, and serving tips (rev 42682403). It then cut the page down and blanked it itself (rev 42682535, "문서를 비움", page blanked). Ykhwong then made the page a redirect to the existing article on the town, 번더버그 (rev 42682545). On the Sprite page, Ykhwong added about 37 KB, apparently translated from English Wikipedia, with a 2026 logo, origin in 1959 in West Germany, and a marketing section (rev 42682468). The temporary account also added small "see also" links there. There are no reverts and no conflict between editors, and nothing in the edits points to a real-world event. This looks like ordinary article creation and cleanup with no news hook.

stories.headline: CFB Wainwright fire: 7 dead per media sources, not officially confirmed; fire "being held"
stories.summary: A new edit to the English article "CFB Wainwright fire" corrects how the death toll is sourced (rev 1380891851, Patternbuffered). The article had said Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed "at least seven" deaths. It now says he confirmed "both fatalities and injuries" but gave no numbers and no cause, citing CBC. The figure of seven is now credited to Global News, which cites unnamed military sources, and to a CBC report on October 18 based on its own sources. That CBC report says National Defence had not confirmed the number. The same edit replaces an outdated line saying it was unclear whether the fire was contained: around 10:45 pm on October 17, the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was "being held." The other recent edits are minor: Jukitaa added a Global News citation for the word "explosion" (rev 1380890189), and Slaughter-echo added a wikilink and fixed capitalisation (rev 1380890114). The article also says search-and-rescue technicians parachuted in, citing CTV and Canadian Press photos. There is no edit war or vandalism in this window. Still unconfirmed: the official death toll, the cause (the article's "accidental, not terrorism" line rests on one reference I have not opened), and the injury count. I have not checked any of the cited sources directly.

stories.headline: Vandalism on Travis Walton and Daryl Dixon pages reverted by one patroller
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Two unrelated temporary accounts made joke edits to two English Wikipedia pages. On "Travis Walton incident", ~2026-56092-76 renamed a heading from "allegations of a hoax" to "allegations of a fart" and changed the displayed name of Raymond E. Fowler to "Pharter". On "Daryl Dixon", ~2026-56012-91 rewrote the opening paragraph to call him "the worst" character, credit the role to Chadwick Boseman, and add partisan jokes. The same patroller, SuperPianoMan9167, reverted every one of these edits within about a minute. The patroller is the only link between the two pages. No other languages moved, and there was no back-and-forth over the reverts. Nothing here points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Lil Keed slur edit still not undone; no cleanup edits found after the earlier revert
stories.summary: The scout thought three editors might have cleaned up the slur. They didn't. These are the same three edits from the tracked vandalism story, and the graph has no other edits on the page. Rev 1381134668 by a temporary account changed "one daughter named Naychur" to a made-up son's name containing a racial slur, and kept the HotNewHipHop citation. Rev 1381134880 by Theeverywhereperson, using the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, only put back the legal name "Raqhid Jevon Render" after a second temporary account's joke-name edit. It did not touch the personal-life sentence. Based on the graph, the slur is probably still live on English Wikipedia. I can't confirm that without checking the current page, and an edit the graph missed could have fixed it. This is vandalism, not news, and it should probably be merged with the existing tracked story. Someone should check the live article and revert if needed.

stories.headline: Promotional push on Mike McGlone page continues from new temp account; no news event
stories.summary: This is still routine English-only patrol work, and nothing points to a real-world event. On Mike McGlone (the actor known for the GEICO "rhetorical questions" ads), temporary account ~2026-55788-83 made a third attempt to add the uncited "Success Guidebook/Peace Guidebook" essay claims and the albums HERO, To Be Down and SPEED (rev 1381067184). This time the music source was a Google search link. A second temporary account, ~2026-56015-00, then added a link to michaelmcglone.com and swapped an internal wiki link for a long Google search URL (rev 1381068694). That suggests one person, possibly the subject or someone close to him, editing through rotating temporary accounts. Wolfwolfnuke reverted the 56015 edits with AntiVandal (rev 1381068826). But the diff shows the revert only rolled back to the 55788 version, so the promotional discography line with the Google link still appears to be on the page. On Moksha, the same temporary account re-added its uncited sentence on liberation from prakriti and samsara (rev 1381068529). JimRenge undid it ("try to convince fellow editors instead of edit warring"), as Joshua Jonathan had done before. This is a slow edit war against several patrollers, not a two-person ping-pong. I can't tell whether the two McGlone temporary accounts are the same person. That rests on the matching style and the Google-link habit.

stories.headline: Unsourced category tag on two ja-wiki actress bios reverted citing WP:V
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56374-53) added the category "ハーフのAV女優" (mixed-heritage AV actresses) to two Japanese Wikipedia biographies, 夏木りん (AV女優) and 愛弓りょう, about a minute apart (revs 111456446, 111456454). Both edits added only that category line, with no source. Within about 4 minutes, registered editor 侵入者ウィリアム undid both. The revert of 111456446 (rev 111456471) cites WP:V, and I am assuming the second revert, 111456473, is the same kind of edit because its comment and size are identical. Neither side edited again, so this was not an edit war. Nothing points to a real-world event. The only thing that matters is the risk of putting an ethnicity label on living people without a source, and that was quickly fixed. One open question is whether the temporary account is adding this category to other pages too; I did not check.

stories.headline: 2026–27 Primeira Liga page: matchday results plus unsourced coaching changes
stories.summary: This is routine upkeep on the English 2026–27 Primeira Liga page by three editors, with no reverts. Wikizin entered the Braga–Vitória de Guimarães result as 1–2 and moved the "results updated" date to 19 October 2026 (rev 1381079354). A temporary account updated Porto's position-by-round, showing them still 1st after round 9 (rev 1381079670). The large 797-byte edit (rev 1381078065, also from a temporary account) changes the managerial-changes table. It says Rio Ave sacked Sotiris Sylaidopoulos on 4 October and hired Vasco Seabra, and that Arouca then appointed Vítor Severino to replace Seabra. It also adds unfinished rows for Estoril Praia and for Famalicão, marked "Sacked", 13th, with the outgoing manager left blank and the date commented out. The edit cites no sources and those rows are half-filled, so treat the coaching changes as unverified, especially Famalicão and Estoril. There is no sign of a major event; the coaching moves are worth checking against Portuguese sources.

stories.headline: U-17 Women's World Cup group results logged live: 2–4 in Group A, Nigeria 2–0 Puerto Rico
stories.summary: Several editors, mostly temporary accounts, are filling in match results on the English article for the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup as games end. In Group B, Embele moved the standings date to 20 October 2026 and recorded a 2–0 win with goals from Adegbuyi (25') and Oscar (90+2'). The standings table now gives Nigeria 1W 1L and Puerto Rico 0W 2L, 0–8 on goals, so the 2–0 match appears to be Nigeria vs Puerto Rico (rev 1381222103). In Group A, a temporary account entered a 2–4 result. Mouradi scored twice (64' and a 90+5' penalty) for the side that lost. Kleemann (27'), Martens (34'), Choisy (45+2') and Giesen (50' penalty) scored for the winners (revs 1381223919, 1381224768). TheArabizedHelper991 then only changed the formatting to use goal templates (rev 1381226046). The edits show no reverts, vandalism or disputes. The diffs I read don't name the teams in the Group A match, and the scores come from Wikipedia editors rather than official sources.

stories.headline: Masked Singer Israel S5 page gets routine contestant-table updates after latest episode
stories.summary: The Hebrew Wikipedia page for season 5 of Israel's "The Masked Singer" (הזמר במסכה) got about nine small edits from four registered accounts over roughly an hour. One account, שעה טובה, made most of them. The diffs I read are routine contestant-table changes. Cohoma23 added sources to two unmaskings: a Mako/Keshet 12 piece (17 Oct 2026) reporting that singer Eden Fines was the "fire ant" mask, shown to viewers at home first, and a Maariv piece about Maya Buskila. שעה טובה added a new "Elephant" (פיל) mask row in Group B. Another account then renamed that entry "Elephant in a china shop." There are no reverts, no other language editions and no editors working across other pages. This is fan upkeep after a broadcast, not a news event. The scout counted three edits, but there were about nine, and one diff (44091021) wouldn't load.

stories.headline: Promi Big Brother 14 finale being logged live: Nadja Benaissa 4th, third place in flux
stories.summary: Four registered editors made six edits in about 30 minutes to the dewiki page for Promi Big Brother season 14. The edits read like someone updating the page while the finale airs. Samuelgarcia22 (rev 271468247) put No Angels singer Nadja Benaissa in 4th place with an exit date of 19 October, and Frarenatin (rev 271468360) marked her "Viertplatzierte" (fourth place) in the nominations table. Third place is less clear. Frarenatin (rev 271469428, "Runde 3") marked Gia Georgina as third, but a Samuelgarcia22 edit made about 40 seconds earlier (rev 271469417) appears to give former boxer Axel Schulz the "3" in the contestant table, and ThorstenThorstig3 (rev 271469489) moved Axel's row above Nadja's in the nominations table. That could be a real contradiction or just a row swap that is hard to read in the diff. There are no reverts and no other languages involved, so this is ordinary live-show updating rather than a dispute. The winner isn't recorded yet, so expect more edits.

stories.headline: No new edits on pt.wiki Vandro Família page since patroller's rollback
stories.summary: This is an update to the vandalism story we were already tracking on the pt.wiki biography of former Rio state deputy Vandro Família. There has been no activity since the last brief. The most recent edit in the graph is still Rkieferbaum's rollback of DonJK (rev 73251975, comment "Desfeita(s) uma ou mais edições de DonJK"), and a query for anything newer returned nothing. I read that diff again. It brings back the real infobox: name Vandro Lopes Gonçalves, office as Rio de Janeiro state deputy, Magé, born 1977, Brazilian, occupation politician, and the sourced lead. It also removes the vandal text: the "Alemanha Nazista" (Nazi Germany) title, the made-up legal names, the "boliviano" nationality line, the spouse field filled with group usernames, the fake "CDS" party and the "Prostituta" occupation. The diff output is cut off partway through the cassação paragraph, so I still can't confirm from the diff alone that Babinelson0512's made-up claim of a 67-year sex-abuse sentence is gone. Someone should check the live page. All of this is on one page in one language, nothing points to a real-world event, and the 2026 PSDB affiliation is still sourced only to an Instagram reel.

stories.headline: JKT48 article hit by joke infobox edits from a temporary account, quickly reverted
stories.summary: The English JKT48 article had two edits from the temporary account ~2026-56039-01, both with the edit summary "idk". The first changed the infobox name from "JKT48" to "Fufuritsu" (rev 1381125945). The second swapped the group's parent in the infobox from AKB48 Group to the Indonesian streamer Windah Basudara, and listed internet personalities as past members: Windah Basudara, DeanKT, Reza Arap and Luthfi Halimawan (rev 1381126143). Editor KH-1 reverted each edit within minutes. This is not an edit war between two sides. It is plain vandalism, probably a fan or meme joke, and it does not point to any real-world news. No other languages or pages were involved, so I don't think it needs watching beyond normal patrol.

stories.headline: Small vandalism run on three ja.wiki biographies changed infobox names; all reverted
stories.summary: In about 90 seconds, one registered account (デンジスパーク) made unexplained edits to the infobox name fields on three Japanese biography pages. It cut the last character off 水野貴雄 (→水野 貴) and 天神林ともみ (→天神林 とも), and changed ただの いっこ to ただの いつこ, swapping っ for つ. About six minutes later, a patroller (Syunsyunminmin) rolled back all three edits within the same second, restoring the earlier versions. In the graph, the account has touched only these three pages. There is no sign that the pages are connected to each other, there was no other editing activity, and no other language versions changed. This looks like low-grade vandalism or a test, not a news event or a shared template edit, and the Scout's 'six editors' really comes down to two people who matter here.

stories.headline: Akmal Saleh page: infobox blanking reverted; editor tags and trims unsourced BLP content
stories.summary: The latest edit is cleanup and does not signal a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56064-09 added {{citation needed}} tags to the Early life and political career text on the en-wiki biography of UMNO Youth chief and Malacca exco member Muhamad Akmal Saleh. It also removed 781 bytes it called "potentially libellous unsourced claims" (rev 1381179876). It did not change any office, term or status facts. This follows the pattern from earlier: a one-edit temporary account blanked the full infobox (rev 1381179085), Serols reverted it within about 30 seconds, and the same cleanup editor then removed an unsourced spouse/children line under WP:BLP. All of this is on one page in one language, and the single revert is part of anti-vandalism work, not an edit war. Caveats: the diff I read was cut off, so I can't confirm exactly what the "libellous" text was. Removing possibly defamatory claims could also be a sign of outside controversy around him, but the edits show no such event.

stories.headline: New YouGov poll put One Nation first on primary vote (27%) and Labor–Coalition level at 50–50
stories.summary: A routine poll-table update on en-wiki's "Opinion polling for the next Australian federal election" includes a notable figure. Rev 1381157737 added a YouGov poll taken 13–20 Oct (1,500 respondents, online). It has One Nation first on primary vote at 27%, then Labor 24%, the Coalition 23%, the Greens 14% and others 12%. The two-party-preferred (2PP) split between Labor and the Coalition is 50–50, and a second matchup, most likely Labor vs One Nation, is 53–47. The cited headline reads "Albanese loses two-party-preferred lead as One Nation remains ahead in primary vote", which suggests One Nation already led earlier polls rather than this being a new first. The other two edits are cosmetic: one changed party abbreviations (L-NC→L/NP, etc.) and one fixed a dash in the date range. There are 3 editors, no reverts, one page, and no activity in other languages. Caveats: the citations point to "news24.com.au", which I could not confirm as an established Australian outlet. The edit comment ("You're all goving") is odd, and I am inferring the second 2PP matchup from the table layout. Treat the figures as unverified until a second source or editor confirms them.

stories.headline: Dallas Brodie bio: lone editor re-adds unsourced spouse claim five times; no news hook
stories.summary: This has grown past the earlier routine dispute and past the scout's count. On the English Wikipedia page for BC MLA Dallas Brodie, temporary account ~2026-56265-64 has now added "spouse (David ash)" to the Personal life section five times in about two hours. Editors removed it each time: Katerdactyl once, Fingray7 three times (revs 1381274735, 1381278500, 1381280064, with comments like "Once again, this is unsourced"), and JavaHurricane with the WikiShield tool (rev 1381281185, labeled vandalism). That is four editors and four reverts, not three and two. In the latest re-add (rev 1381280210), the account points to family obituaries as proof in the edit comment, but the article text still cites no source. The reverts all go one way, a single account against several editors, so this is a slow edit war and likely a 3RR breach, not a two-sided ping-pong. There is still no sign of a news event: one page, one language, nothing about her politics or career, and no other editors joining in. I can't check if the claim is true. The likely next step is a warning or page protection, not news coverage.

stories.headline: Hungarian Masked Singer season 5 page gets routine episode-table edits
stories.summary: Nearly all the activity on huwiki's 'Álarcos énekes (5. évad)' (the Hungarian Masked Singer, season 5) comes from one editor, Ermic6666667, with 18 edits. They are rebuilding the tables for episode 1 (11 October) and episode 2 (18 October): moving duel rows, adding mask names such as 'Szupergomba' and 'Jégkirálynő' to the episode 2 table, and later adding a wiki link for Kovács István (filmproducer). A temporary account added Kovács István, filmproducer, to the 'Nyomozók' (panel/investigators) section. A third editor swapped one category for three: Álarcos énekes, 2026 in music and 2026 in television. There are no reverts, all edits are small, and none of the diffs I read reveal an unmasking or any other newsworthy event. This looks like ordinary fan upkeep of a TV season page while it airs. I did not read every one of the small table edits.

stories.headline: Mehdi Tartar page on Persian Wikipedia vandalized, then automatically reverted
stories.summary: The activity on the Persian Wikipedia article for football coach Mehdi Tartar is vandalism. It does not reflect real-world news. Temporary account ~2026-56228-07 inserted made-up infobox facts: birth year 1209 SH, made-up goal totals, and national teams (Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Spain) in place of his real coaching clubs (rev 44779872). A second temporary account then blanked the whole infobox, after it had been changed to list Barcelona, Real Madrid and Chelsea and a 3.45 m height (rev 44779918). Within seconds, Dexbot's AI anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) reverted the page to the clean version (rev 44779920). The clean infobox lists Tartar as Persepolis head coach from 1405 SH. That entry was already there before this burst, so it is not new here. The large churn figure comes from the blank-and-restore pair, not from a real rewrite. Two small edits by the first account (revs 44779838, 44779859) were not read, but they come before the reverted state. No other languages or pages are involved.

stories.headline: India at 2026 Asian Para Games: results upkeep continues; one archery edit reverted
stories.summary: Results-tracking on the English article "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" is continuing, almost all of it by Neeelzzz20. Since the last brief, Neeelzzz20 has edited the Archery, Badminton, Shooting and Medalists sections. The only new event is a single revert. Abesh2023, a newer account with 5 edits, filled the 20 October archery placeholders with opponent flags for Malaysia and Mongolia (rev 1381132803). About 14 minutes later Neeelzzz20 undid that edit (rev 1381134463), giving no reason. This is a one-off disagreement over an unconfirmed fixture, not an edit war. I couldn't check the newest additions because the diffs for revs 1381131559, 1381132036, 1381131605, 1381132602 and 1381134703 wouldn't load. So it's unclear whether more medals or results were recorded after the four table-tennis bronzes in the last brief. As before, the edits cite no sources.

stories.headline: DeviantArt "Closed" edit made again on enwiki, reverted within 74 seconds
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked DeviantArt story. There is no new real-world event. About seven minutes after Celjski Grad's restore, temp account ~2026-56322-35 made the full shutdown edit again with no edit summary (rev 1381285712). The edit set current_status to Closed, added a dissolved date of 21 Oct 2026, changed commercial to No, marked the planned languages as cancelled, changed "is" to "was" in the opening line, and added the "Companies disestablished in 2026" category. ~2026-56061-30 undid all of it 74 seconds later (rev 1381285803), so the page reads Active again. I read both diffs. No sources have been added at any point, and a graph check shows no edits to other-language versions (Q46523) since the last brief. This is a slow vandalism loop: one persistent pusher, probably the same person behind several temp accounts (my inference), against at least five editors reverting. The scout's "ongoing dispute" reading is right, but nothing here supports a shutdown. The page probably needs semi-protection. Whether DeviantArt is down for maintenance is still unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Clifford film page: third false Illumination credit reverted; account hit ~20 kids-TV pages
stories.summary: This is still vandalism, not news. The same temporary account (~2026-55856-82) came back a third time to the en-wiki 'Clifford the Big Red Dog (film)' page. This time it swapped the production credit "Scholastic Entertainment" for "Illumination Entertainment" (rev 1380899042). Magitroopa, who had already flagged the account as LTA (long-term abuse), undid it 14 seconds later (1380899067), and the page is back to the correct credits. The graph shows that between about 1792340778 and 1792342217 (roughly 24 minutes), the account touched about 20 other en-wiki pages, mostly Nickelodeon/Disney kids' TV shows plus the pages for Illumination (company), Dan Povenmire and Kenny Loggins. That fits the spree pattern behind the LTA tag. I didn't read diffs on those other pages, so I can't say whether they were vandalised too. There is no real-world event: it's one language, the reverts are quick, and nothing has changed in the real credits.

stories.headline: '9-1-1' season 9 split dispute escalates to second revert; page back to a redirect
stories.summary: The fight over whether "9-1-1 season 9" should be its own article or a redirect has gone a step further. Since the last brief, Magical Golden Whip reverted JoyfullySmile's restored 36 KB article for a second time (rev 1381064049, "take to talk page"). Within about 45 seconds he made a self-revert that brought the article back (1381064095), then undid that too (1381064141). The self-revert looks like a misfired rollback, not a change of mind. The page is now a redirect to List of 9-1-1 episodes#Season 9 (2025–26) again. Lonniemitchell22 then added an italic-title template, a sort key and season categories (1381064333), which now sit on the redirect. Taken together, that's two content reverts by Magical Golden Whip and one by JoyfullySmile, all on English Wikipedia only, and nobody has said in the edit history that they've gone to the talk page. This is a small edit war about page structure between two editors, not real-world news. It's below the three-revert threshold, and it could die down or move to the talk page. Watch for JoyfullySmile undoing it again or creating other season pages.

stories.headline: NZ 2026 polling page: formatting fix to unsourced Mongrel Mob timeline entry
stories.summary: The only new edit on the en Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election page is housekeeping. The temporary account ~2026-48399-43 added an unsourced 15 Oct timeline row (rev 1381065517) saying the Green Party and Te Pāti Māori were photographed with the Mongrel Mob at a wellbeing day. That row had been inserted by rewriting the existing 14 Oct row, which is probably why the system marked the edit as a revert. Its follow-up (rev 1381065762) corrects the sort date to 2026-10-15 and adds matching grey shading to the restored 14 Oct row, which records the NZ Herald leaders' debate between Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins. No new polls, no reverts by other editors and no sign of an edit war. The Mongrel Mob claim still has no source, and it is unclear whether other editors will keep it. The earlier poll additions (Freshwater Strategy national poll, Curia Te Tai Tokerau poll) stand as in the prior brief.

stories.headline: New de-wiki biography of journalist Oswald Zenkner (1901–1963) gets routine cleanup
stories.summary: This is a new German Wikipedia article on Oswald Zenkner (1901–1963). The article describes him as a German newspaper journalist, Wehrmacht war correspondent and book author. Three registered editors made six edits, with no reverts and no activity in other languages. Murkus69 moved the draft into the main article space and removed the {{Baustelle}} (under construction) tag (rev 271440554). M2k~dewiki, a maintenance editor, added the person-data template, sorting key, categories and authority-file IDs GND 116979976 and VIAF 122298495 (rev 271440477).
