One small detail: Murkus69's move also wiki-linked the birth date, and the author EposImages removed those links a minute later (rev 271440574). That is a style difference, not an edit war. The person-data template still has no death date, although the article text gives 1 August 1963. The subject died decades ago and nothing points to a news trigger; this matches the earlier routine brief.

stories.headline: ru-wiki 2026 deaths list adds Kyrgyz soprano Sartbaeva, geochemist Glazunov
stories.summary: Routine upkeep of the Russian Wikipedia "List of deaths in 2026" by several editors, all logged in except one temporary account, with no reverts. Diffs add Kyrgyz opera soprano Kairgul Sartbaeva (90), a People's Artist of the USSR, sourced to a Lenta.ru item dated 20 Oct 2026 (rev 155721372). Two editors added Soviet/Russian geochemist Oleg Glazunov (99) within ten seconds of each other, citing baikal24.ru and VK (revs 155721686, 155721682). Krokusse then cleaned up formatting and removed one of the two Glazunov entries (rev 155721748). The same diff also shows Soviet dissident Boris Kochubievsky (90) and ex-Lokomotiv footballer Oleg Garin (60) already on the list. Garin's line is among the removed lines in that diff, probably because it was moved within the page, but I haven't confirmed that. None of these people's own pages show activity in the graph, so there's no sign that any of these deaths is driving wider editing. It's a regional notable-deaths story at most.

stories.headline: Liechtenstein vandalism spree quiet after Cannolis rollback; page stays clean
stories.summary: There has been no new activity on en:Liechtenstein since the last brief. The graph has no edits after Cannolis's rollback at rev 1381110647, so the page is still clean. That rollback put back the real flag and coat of arms, which Freyaconnolly123 had replaced with uploads named "Lp image.jpg" and "Freyag123.jpg". It also restored the infobox GDP figures, for example per-capita PPP from "$2.10" back to $210,600, and changed "all of the debt" back to "no debt". Rev 1381109172 by ~2026-56101-99 cut the GDP figures down and also edited the "no debt" sentence. The added text was cut off in the diff, but that is the only edit since ClueBot NG's revision that touched the sentence, and the rollback reverted it, so it was almost certainly the source of the "all of the debt" wording. Overall, four throwaway or temporary accounts made juvenile edits over about 40 minutes, and five patrollers and bots reverted them. Only this one page moved: no other language versions and no related articles, and there is no sign of a real-world event. The vandalism could start again, but for now it is over.

stories.headline: Hebrew 'Eggplant' bullying vandalism: one last hit reverted, page now looks clean
stories.summary: This update covers the same schoolyard vandalism of the Hebrew Wikipedia articles חציל (Eggplant) and מגה-מוח (Megamind). It isn't news. After the main cleanup, temporary account ~2026-56318-51 came back one more time (rev 44096521). It changed the bolded subject at the start of the Eggplant intro from 'חציל' to the first name 'אביב' (Aviv), which looks like another jab at a peer. Idoiz rolled it back about 17 seconds later (rev 44096524), returning the page to שעה טובה's last version, which had already undone the earlier insults. The graph shows no Eggplant edits after that rollback. That answers the open question in the earlier brief: the latest revision appears clean. There are still no other languages involved, no tie to any real-world event, and no back-and-forth between established editors. The vandal could come back, and I haven't checked whether either page was protected or the temporary accounts blocked.

stories.headline: FNaF 3 article: copied game transcript removed and revision-deleted; no news event
stories.summary: On the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 article, StoopidPieForU added about 2.8 KB of text to the Plot section. Their edit summary says it was the full transcript of the night 1 phone call from the game, with more transcripts to come. About eight minutes later NegativeMP1 put the page back to the earlier revision by SleepyRedHair, saying a transcript is not what plot summaries are for and that it was a copyright violation. NegativeMP1 then added a {{Copyvio-revdel}} tag covering revisions 1381122139 through 1381122729 (I read this diff). An admin, Mfield, completed the revision deletion and removed the tag. I couldn't read the added text itself because those revisions now return "missing content", which fits the deletion. The large churn figure comes from this one add-and-remove, and the page is back where it started. This is ordinary copyright cleanup, not a real-world event or an edit war.

stories.headline: ja-wiki sunflower festival article stripped of its sources, then its sourcing tag undone
stories.summary: There have been no new edits since the earlier brief, and the diffs I re-read confirm it. Shin-Nippori created the Japanese article on the Akeno Sunflower Festival in Chikusei, Ibaraki (rev 111451078). Two minutes later the same editor removed every inline citation (local-government research institute, Ministry of Agriculture and Chikusei city PDFs) and the references section, leaving the text word for word the same (rev 111451098). そもそもーる added a "needs sources" tag ({{出典の明記}}). Geogie took it out with a pop-up undo (rev 111451166), so the article now has no sources and no warning. There are three named editors, one revert, no pushback, one language and nothing tied to a current event, so this is not news and not an edit war. It is unclear why the sources and the tag were removed; it looks like housekeeping on a new article, not an attempt to mislead.

stories.headline: Es-wiki page on amateur Buenos Aires five-a-side team tagged for deletion; no news
stories.summary: On es-wiki, user Elpibejanson created "Mantequinha", which the creation summary describes as an amateur football club founded in 2026 in Buenos Aires by a group of friends who play in "TIFA". Patroller CarlosEduardoPA added a deletion template with Twinkle Lite about 80 seconds later. After that the creator made two small edits ("puse un cuadro") and a new temporary account made one ("nada importante"), which look like tries to remove or work around the tag. I couldn't read any of the five diffs: Wikipedia says none of the revisions exist, which most likely means the page has already been deleted. So this rests on the graph's metadata and edit summaries only. It's a non-notable self-promotional page, not a real-world event, and there's no reason to keep watching it.

stories.headline: Cherokee councilor page: no new activity after unsourced allegation was reverted
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened on the English Wikipedia page for Daryl Legg, the Cherokee Nation District 6 council member, since our last brief. The graph still holds only four edits. A temporary account (rev 1380882650) and a new account, Stanleeew (rev 1380883112), each added an unsourced claim that a family member caused a fatal drunk-driving crash and that a "cover up" was under way. The patroller Materialscientist reverted both within minutes (revs 1380882715 and 1380883347). I read the second addition and its revert, and the page is back to its one-sentence stub. No sourced edits, no other-language pages and no related pages have moved, so nothing confirms a real event. We're treating this as a BLP attack (unsourced claims about a living person) that has been contained, not as news. The scout was right not to open a new story; this one should stay merged with the tracked vandalism story.

stories.headline: Genre edits by one temporary account on three pop pages, reverted; no news trigger
stories.summary: This cluster comes from one temporary account (~2026-55473-37). It added "Teen pop" to the genre lists on Jessica Simpson (rev 1381271877) and Fantasy (Mariah Carey song) (rev 1381271460). On Cry Me a River (Justin Timberlake song) it went further, replacing "Funk" and "pop" with "Teen pop" (rev 1381269814). Tbhotch, an experienced editor, reverted the Simpson change ("Teen pop is pop") and the Cry Me a River change ("unsourced claim"). The Fantasy addition was still in place as of the last edit in the story. The rest is routine upkeep: Wherelovelives renamed a chart row to "Poland Airplay" on Fantasy (rev 1381272560) and made a similar "fix" edit on Cry Me a River. Nothing points to a death, anniversary or release: only English Wikipedia is involved, the changes are small, and no facts about a real-world event were added. This is a common kind of low-level unsourced genre editing, not news.

stories.headline: fa-wiki adds unsourced "262 kg world record" claim to Iranian weightlifter Alireza Yousefi
stories.summary: Seven edits in about 10 minutes on the Persian Wikipedia biography of Alireza Yousefi, an Iranian super-heavyweight lifter who won gold at the 2018 Youth Olympics. Editor "Guard active" added a photo of him in a Foolad Khuzestan shirt captioned "world heavyweight record holder" (rev 44791515). The same editor then added a lead sentence saying Yousefi holds the world heavyweight clean-and-jerk record at 262 kg (rev 44791527), with no new source. The other edits are punctuation fiddling by a temporary account. Dexbot's AI filter auto-reverted one of them, which only removed extra full stops (rev 44791577), so this is not an edit war or real vandalism. The 262 kg claim could point to a recent real result, such as a record in the new IWF weight classes, but I can't confirm it: no other language versions or related pages are moving, and the claim is uncited. Treat it as an unverified claim worth a quick check, not as confirmed news.

stories.headline: Two unrelated new German Wikipedia articles: historic Neustadt mill and vendor 'Pakera Score'
stories.summary: This cluster is two unrelated new articles on de.wikipedia, and neither is tied to a news event. First, AF666 created "Kronenmühle (Neustadt)" (rev 271442722), a sourced local-history stub about a medieval watermill on the Floßbach in Winzingen, Neustadt an der Weinstraße. It covers the mill's ownership by the Branchweiler hospital and later the Jesuits, and its 1823 auction. M2k~dewiki then removed the infobox status "abgerissen" (demolished) because it contradicts the article text saying the premises are now used commercially (rev 271443036). Zollernalb made small fixes. Second, the "Pakera Score" vendor article was already covered in the earlier brief. After it, Lutheraner added an edit with the comment "SLA+", which on de.wikipedia means a speedy-deletion request (rev 271442941). Wikipedia now reports that revision as missing, which suggests the promotional article has already been deleted. I couldn't read that diff, so this is inferred from the edit comment and the missing revision. There were no reverts, only one language and no outside hook, so this is routine wiki housekeeping.

stories.headline: Persian Wikipedia's Kazan article hit by short-lived vandalism, not news
stories.summary: All five edits to the fawiki article on Kazan (Q900) over about 4.5 minutes were vandalism and its cleanup, with no link to any real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-56063-54) tacked a derogatory phrase onto the lead paragraph saying the city "has many paid girls" (rev 44780314). Dexbot's Shahbaz AI anti-vandalism system reverted it automatically. Klaser35 then put a similar slur into the article's opening sentence ("Kazan, full of paid girls") under the misleading edit summary "typo fix" (rev 44780339), and took it out again in two steps (44780353, 44780356). The article now looks clean, apart from a leftover double space. There is no other-language activity in the graph and no factual content changed. The one open question is whether Klaser35 and the temporary account are the same person; the timing and wording suggest so, but that isn't proven.

stories.headline: Raúl Rangel page vandalism reverted, but fake height of '1.50 cm' may still be live
stories.summary: This is still plain vandalism, with no real-world news behind it. One temporary account (~2026-55859-59) made three unsourced edits to the infobox of Chivas goalkeeper Raúl Rangel on en-wiki. It changed his birthplace to "Tel Aviv", his height to "1.40/1.50 cm", the caption to an insult ("El Pendejo Tala") and his club to rival "Club America" with made-up shirt numbers 67 and 41. Ceilingbumps undid the first edit and Asukite rolled back the third. The earlier brief said the page was fully restored, which looks wrong. Asukite's rollback (rev 1380899712) restores the caption, birthplace, club and number but not the height. The middle edit (rev 1380899480, -50 bytes, height 1.90 m → "1.50 cm" with its source tag removed) was never reverted. The byte changes add up to -50, which fits that edit still being in place. I couldn't check the live page, and the diffs for 1380899480 and 1380899679 overlap oddly, so this is likely but not confirmed. It needs a manual check and a fix if the height is still wrong. Note: no other story is tracked on this page, so this task is about the tracked story itself, not a second incident. No other pages or languages were involved.

stories.headline: es-wiki 'Frente Obrero' vandalism stays removed; no new edits since last check
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked cleanup and has no real-world news hook. The graph shows the same five edits on es-wiki 'Frente Obrero (España)' and nothing after Blitzo170's rev 175885172, so the anti-vandal bot SeroBOT has not put the text back a third time. I read all five diffs. Temporary account ~2026-55781-26 twice undid antisemitic changes to the lead: "organizaciones" had become "razas gentiles", and an added line spoke of the «goyim» of Núcleo Nacional and "Antisionismo" (revs 175885025, 175885087). Each time, SeroBOT restored the vandalised version within seconds (175885027, 175885091). Blitzo170 then made the same fix. The first removal was larger (−1313 bytes against −904 later), so it probably also cut some sourced text that the second fix kept. I can't confirm that because the diff output was truncated. Also unconfirmed: the source cited for "Antisionismo" is about a banner reading "Fuera el Islam", so the original word may have been changed too. This is a bot false-positive pattern, not an edit war between people. Close it unless the page moves again.

stories.headline: Small revert dispute over Air Canada route listing on BWI Airport page
stories.summary: Two registered editors swapped one revert each on the English Wikipedia article for Baltimore/Washington International Airport, about five minutes apart. Mrgoggins90 undid an earlier removal by Danners430 (rev 1381197694) and put back a 345-byte destinations-table row saying Air Canada serves Toronto–Pearson and Montreal–Trudeau. That row cites a WBAL-TV story headlined "Air Canada to resume service at BWI-Marshall this spring". Danners430 then removed the same row again, saying "once again" unsourced content was being added "along with the good additions". The diff I could see shows only the cited Air Canada row, so it is unclear which part Danners430 considers unsourced. It may have been in the earlier edits that I could not see. This looks like a low-intensity content dispute between two people on one page, with no other languages or editors involved, not a breaking event. If the WBAL report is accurate, Air Canada restarting BWI flights is ordinary airline route news, and I have not checked it independently.

stories.headline: Thai Wikipedia adds full royal title for Wat Arun abbot's Somdet elevation; other monk's 2569 entry cites Gazette
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked story. On Thai Wikipedia, an anonymous editor expanded the BE 2569 (2026) ecclesiastical-titles entry for Somkiat Kowito, the abbot of Wat Arun (rev 13355802, +831). The new text says he was raised to Somdet Phra Ratchakhana, the senior monk rank, and gives his full title as written on the royal appointment plate (suphannabat): "Somdet Phra Wachirakowitthamet ... residing at Wat Arunratchawararam, Bangkok". The same editor then removed a shorter duplicate line that another editor had added minutes before (13355793 added it, 13355805 removed it). This was cleanup, not a revert war. A later edit by อมฤตาลัย changed formatting only (13355808). On the "Somdet Phra Ratchakhana" list page, two other registered editors added him to the Mahanikai table with a BE 2569 date and a birth date of 6 Sept 1943 (BE 2486), and to the current-reign list (13355806, 13355809). The edits agree with each other and nobody reverted anything. New this round: someone edited the page of another monk, Somdet Phra Maha Wachirathibodi (Phi Suchato), whose own BE 2569 Somdet elevation was already listed. The edit (13355816) swapped a reused reference for a direct link to a Royal Gazette (Ratchakitcha) proclamation of title appointments. That suggests the abbot's elevation may be part of a wider royal batch in 2026, but I can't confirm that from the edits: the abbot's own entry still cites no source, and the activity is Thai-only.

stories.headline: German Harz ditch article expanded; small revert fight over castle studio section
stories.summary: The scout's note is out of date. Since the last brief, Ludengraben has been edited again, and a third German page, Schloss Bodenburg, has seen reverts. Sarkana, who created Ludengraben, greatly expanded it (rev 271493296, +3890 bytes). The article is now titled by its other name, Kochs-Graben, and gains an infobox (9.5 km long, built from the mid-1720s to 1745), plus a sourced history: mine director Koch built the ditch without permission from the Stolberg counts, and it only began operating in 1745. On Schloss Bodenburg, a temporary (effectively anonymous) account, ~2026-56092-95, deleted the section on the 2007 Corten-steel artist's studio twice with no explanation (revs 271493632, 271493710). It also changed the text to say visitors can see only "parts of" the castle park, not the whole park (rev 271493681). AxelHH and Aspiriniks reverted each change within minutes. It looks like a small edit war or unexplained-deletion vandalism by one account. Nothing ties it to a real-world event, though the park-access wording could reflect a local change I can't verify. No other languages moved, and the Wächter biography had no new edits.

stories.headline: Student workshop on pt-wiki hearing-rehab article stops at 16 edits; one bad link remains
stories.summary: There has been no new activity on pt-wiki "Habilitação e reabilitação auditiva" since rev 73259681. The UNINASSAU "Oficina Semana Ubíqua" class exercise, supervised by Profa Natalia Garcia, ended at 16 small edits by 8 registered accounts. The scout counted 4 editors, but the dossier shows 8, and none of them edited any other page. Diffs show wikilinking only. I can now answer the open question from the earlier brief: Melyssa Rodrigues first linked "linguagem oral" (spoken language) to "Língua brasileira de sinais" (Brazilian Sign Language) in 73259590, and Adriel Micael da Silva later removed that link. The one problem still standing is Weslem Henrique Lima Da Silva's 73259676, which links "linguagem" to "Linguagem brasileira de sinais". That is the wrong topic and probably a red link, so it is worth a quick cleanup. This is not a news event, not vandalism and not an edit war.

stories.headline: Raw milk article: lone editor's pro-raw-milk rewrite reverted twice by patrollers
stories.summary: On English Wikipedia's "Raw milk" article, one account (Brazilianhistory, 2 edits total) made two edits to the lead. The first, about 6 minutes in, turned "Proponents have said that raw milk has better flavor, nutrition..." into a flat factual claim ("The raw (unpasteurised) milk has better flavor..."). The second edit, logged as "lait cru" (French for "raw milk"), did the same and also deleted the sourced sentences on medical consensus about milk-borne disease risk and on countries regulating raw milk sales. Two different patrollers reverted the edits within minutes: Leaf.Sheap ("Should not be in wikivoice") and Knitsey ("Unexplained removal"). This is a single editor pushing one point of view and being reverted by the usual patrollers. It is not a two-sided edit war and doesn't show any real-world news event. The scout's "1071 churn" is the same text being added and then removed again. I didn't read the two reverts' diffs; their edit summaries and size changes match the edits they undo.

stories.headline: New id-wiki bio of streamer Reza Auditore used for religion-based meme vandalism
stories.summary: Jengglot created a new Indonesian Wikipedia page on Kick/YouTube streamer Reza Auditore (rev 30093563). It reads like a fan profile, cites a single ggwp.id article, and includes a paragraph about a community joke that he is Jewish ("Yahuditore"). Later edits push the joke further. A temporary account added "Reza auditore beragama yahudi" ("Reza Auditore is Jewish") at the top of the page (30093602). Jengglot then captioned a generic stock-style "Traditional Jewish Portrait in Tallit and Kippah" image as "Foto Diri Reza Auditore" ("photo of Reza Auditore") (30093616). This looks like a fan community trolling the page with a religion-based meme about a living person, not a news event. Nothing has been reverted yet, and the page is likely to be deleted or need BLP cleanup. Two small diffs (30093610, 30093617) could not be retrieved.

stories.headline: New Galician article on gay pride flags translated from Spanish, then tidied
stories.summary: User Kd6awi25t created the Galician Wikipedia article "Bandeiras do orgullo gai" by translating the Spanish article "Banderas del orgullo gay" (+9,758 bytes). It covers the history of Gilbert Baker's rainbow flags from 1978 and gay men's flag designs proposed online since 2018. About two minutes later the same user removed 2,260 bytes: an image gallery whose file links were broken (the Spanish "Archivo:" prefix had been left in) and one paragraph about the Tumblr-designed gay men's flag. Since the creator made this cut to their own text, it reads as self-correction, not a dispute. After that, regular editor Breogan2008 (446 edits) and two others made small fixes, including adding a portal and an LGBTIQ+ category. There were no reverts, nothing points to a real-world event, and no other languages were involved. This is routine content creation and cleanup.

stories.headline: Zh-wiki Ringling Bros. page: temp account keeps adding fake "2024 animal show" list
stories.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. This is low-level vandalism or a hoax on the zh-wiki article 玲玲馬戲團 (Ringling Bros. circus). A temporary account (~2026-56261-74) added about 3.3k bytes. A patroller, Ghostingb, rolled it back with AdvancedRollback; Ghostingb's recent edits are quick single touches across many unrelated zh pages, which is how patrollers work. The account then re-added the same material, 3,250 bytes under the heading "Yes Lives World Of Animals (2024 Show)" (rev 95195558). That edit swaps out the page's existing related-films section (The Greatest Showman) for an English-language numbered list of roughly 200 wild species, including great white sharks, a sperm whale, a colossal squid and a narwhal, none of which a touring circus could plausibly show. The account's later edits (95195584, 95195612) just add and then remove two entries (Australian Pelican, Wisent). The Scout guessed a rewrite or translation, but this is neither: it's one account's repeated insertion, with no sources and no matching activity in other languages. Uncertain: I couldn't load the diffs for the first insertion, the rollback, or the final +33 edit by 外掛系統123 (rev 95195674), so I don't know whether the list was removed again or is still on the page.

stories.headline: Brighton beat Crystal Palace 5–0 in Premier League round 7; season and league pages updated
stories.summary: The edits now confirm the opponent that the earlier brief could only guess at. On the 2026–27 Premier League page, rev 1380884880 fills in the results grid as Brighton 5–0 Crystal Palace, linked through the Brighton–Palace rivalry article. Rev 1380884646 makes that game the season's biggest home win, dated 18 October 2026. The same edit adds two more results from that round: Bournemouth 2–0 Sunderland and Leeds 1–1 Manchester United. Another edit (rev 1380885607) logs a red card for Sunderland's Kevin Danso. On Brighton's season page, the summary table now shows three home wins and a draw (13 goals for, 1 against) and adds a seventh straight "W" to the form line (rev 1380884819). Six editors across two English Wikipedia pages made small, consistent edits with no reverts, so this is routine post-match upkeep. The only open question is a "pos4" position line extended with "16p". It may track another team, possibly Palace, and I couldn't work out what it refers to.

stories.headline: Daniel Levy page: one unexplained edit reverted, no sign of news
stories.summary: An edit labelled "HI" by temporary account ~2026-56112-43 added 50 bytes to the English article on former Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy (rev 1381150582). DoggieLicc undid it about 2.5 minutes later (rev 1381150784). Fourteen seconds apart, PhilKnight restored the edit by reverting DoggieLicc (rev 1381151719), then reverted his own change (rev 1381151743). The page now matches DoggieLicc's version. A revert followed almost at once by a self-revert looks like a misclick on the rollback button, not an edit war. The diff tool cut off the text before the changed part, so I couldn't see the 50 added bytes. Still, the "HI" summary, the quick undo and the lack of follow-up suggest a test edit or minor vandalism. The paragraph shown in the diffs already says Levy stepped down as executive chairman on 4 September 2025, which is old news. Only one language and one page are involved, so there's no sign of a new real-world development.

stories.headline: Brandon McNulty recorded as 2026 Veneto Classic winner on three Wikipedias
stories.summary: Editors on three Wikipedias recorded American cyclist Brandon McNulty as the winner of the 2026 Veneto Classic, all within about 15 minutes of each other. On enwiki, a temporary account added McNulty (USA, team UEX) to the Veneto Classic winners list under 2026 (rev 1380882587). About a minute later, Walterwiki updated nlwiki to make McNulty the latest winner of the race's 6th edition (rev 72094983). On frwiki, a temporary account added "Veneto Classic (2026)" to the main wins in McNulty's infobox, along with Tour de Croatie and Tour du Luxembourg wins (revs 240489041, 240489164). Philasc then cut the infobox back, citing the guideline on which races belong there (rev 240489290). Experienced editor FromZeFild re-added the Veneto Classic 2026 win in the year-by-year results instead (rev 240489379). That trim was a cleanup, not an edit war. Several separate accounts reported the same result in three languages, so this looks like a real race result. But I didn't check any source outside Wikipedia, and none of the edits I read cites one. This is a small sporting result, not breaking news.

stories.headline: Routine cleanup on two Harry Bosch novel pages; no news hook
stories.summary: Two registered editors made small maintenance edits to two English Wikipedia articles on Michael Connelly's Harry Bosch novels, The Concrete Blonde and Angels Flight. Lieutenant Cotton put each release date into the {{Start date}} template (1994-06-01 and 1999-01-28). The dates themselves did not change. Itzcuauhtli11 added a {{long plot}} cleanup tag to Angels Flight. The same editor's "revert" on The Concrete Blonde undid an earlier removal of an existing {{long plot|date=June 2026}} tag, which restores the tag. It is not a content dispute. There was no back-and-forth reverting, no anonymous or vandal activity, and no other languages were involved. These look like typical edits from people working through a series of novel articles, not a reaction to anything happening in the world.

stories.headline: Persian Wikipedia: bot-reverted vandalism run spreads to a fourth page, "Verse of Stoning"
stories.summary: I'm updating this story with a fourth Persian page, آیه رجم (the "Verse of Stoning," a disputed Quranic verse). It fits the same pattern of single edits by temporary accounts, each auto-reverted within seconds by Dexbot's Shahbaz anti-vandalism system. A new temporary account (~2026-56049-84) deleted a sourced passage of 1,383 bytes. The passage cited al-Kafi and Majlisi's Mir'at al-Uqul, and reported that Shia scholars fall into three camps on the verse. The account replaced it with one unsourced line claiming "Shia scholars unanimously reject this" (rev 44781129). Dexbot restored the original text 15 seconds later (rev 44781131). This is a one-sided POV deletion on a religiously sensitive page, not a news event. The "large churn" is just one removal and its revert, and only two editors touched the page. Earlier in this story, unchanged and drawn from the prior brief rather than re-read diffs: edits on the Jalali Naini biography, Ghoorbagheh (The Frog) and Noah pages were self-insertion or nonsense vandalism, all reverted. This edit came from a different temporary account than those, so I see no sign of a coordinated campaign, though I can't rule out that the same person is behind more than one temporary account.

stories.headline: It-wiki Vanvitelli University page: history section moved out after bot reverts
stories.summary: The large churn on the Italian Wikipedia article for Università degli Studi della Campania Luigi Vanvitelli comes from a structural editing dispute, not a news event. Temporary account ~2026-56209-09 tried three times to remove a roughly 6 KB "Le origini" history section about the Primo Policlinico di Napoli, Sant'Andrea delle Dame and the Santa Patrizia cloisters. Each time the comment said the material belonged in related articles (Primo Policlinico di Napoli, then Azienda Ospedaliera Universitaria "Luigi Vanvitelli"). The automated bot "Moderatore Automatico" undid the first two removals (e.g. rev 152996184). The third (rev 152996196) has not been undone so far. Another temporary account then toned down promotional wording in a photo caption (rev 152996226, "Toni celebrativi"). The removed text is sourced, uncontroversial background history, and no other pages or languages are involved. The removals look like cleanup, not vandalism, though nobody has confirmed the content was actually added to the target articles. This could turn into a small edit war if the bot or a human puts the section back.

stories.headline: Bigg Boss Malayalam S8: Nilina evicted on Day 42, editors update the page
stories.summary: A few fans are updating the en-wiki page for Bigg Boss Malayalam season 8 after a Week 6 episode. Bijzindia's edits say housemate Nilina, who entered on Day 28, was evicted on Day 42 after the public vote. They mark her as evicted in the housemate status table, the weekly summary and the nomination table. The same editor added Day 42 guests Mithun Ramesh and Asian Paints CEO Amit Syngle, who appeared on stage with host Mohanlal as part of a sponsor promotion. Separately, a temporary account and Ashok Gopi Vazhoor renamed contestant "Santhosh" to "Tashi", citing his stage name and the host saying he would call him that. This is a minor naming change, not an edit war, and there have been no reverts. Routine fan editing of a TV show; all of it is unsourced on-air detail, so the eviction claim is likely but not independently confirmed.

stories.headline: Confectionery store: unexplained removal of 1787 Japanese image reverted
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia Confectionery store article is still going through good-faith cleanup. Nothing points to a real-world event, and only English Wikipedia is involved. There is one new edit since the last brief. Ser Amantio di Nicolao put back the 1787 woodblock image "The Great Buddha Sweet Shop" from Ritō Akizato's Miyako meisho zue in the History section, with the summary "why?" (rev 1381272779, +314). The image had been removed without explanation a few minutes earlier by temporary account ~2026-56289-79 (rev 1381272394). The restore puts back exactly the same image, caption and alt text, and the text next to it is unchanged. So far that is one removal and one revert. If the temp account takes the image out again it would be worth watching, but this is not an edit war and stays routine.

stories.headline: Sarah Storey third to leave Strictly Come Dancing series 24 after Icons Week dance-off
stories.summary: Editors on the English page for Strictly Come Dancing series 24 are recording the result of Week 4 ("Icons Week"). Onyou45 added the Week 4 results, with two couples marked "Bottom two" and the rest "Safe" (rev 1380911730). Minutes later, Girlypop Magnemite changed Paralympian Sarah Storey and her partner Julian Caillon from "Participating" to "Eliminated 3rd on 18 October 2026" (rev 1380913186). The same editor marked their bottom-two entry as "Eliminated" (rev 1380913350) and closed their scoring row after a Week 4 score of 21 (rev 1380913072). The edits come from three established accounts, none were reverted, and they match each other, so this looks like normal live updating after the results show. However, these are not edits from the broadcaster, and the diffs I read don't name the other bottom-two couple. Only one page and one language are involved, so this is a small entertainment story, not a major event.

stories.headline: 1 News–Verian NZ poll (15–19 Oct): preferred-PM row added after the party-vote row
stories.summary: This updates the earlier brief. AusYou has now added the matching preferred prime minister row for the 1 News–Verian poll (15–19 Oct 2026, n=1,003) on en-wiki's "Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election". It cites the same 1news.co.nz story from 20 Oct. In that row, the leader is in a blue cell at 20%, then 17, 7, 5 and 8, with a 3-point lead. The blue shading suggests the leader is the National-aligned figure, probably Christopher Luxon, but I have not checked the table header to confirm who each column is. AusYou also made a cosmetic edit, adding a colour to the Te Tai Tokerau Party header in the Māori-roll table. Earlier activity stands as reported: the party-vote row was added (National reportedly 32%, a 5-point lead), and Fungalinfection fixed a footnote. The only revert was JamesNZguy undoing his own edit, so this is routine upkeep of a poll table, not an edit war. I have not checked any of the figures against 1 News directly.

stories.headline: Luis Malagón page: vandal edit blanking infobox reverted within a minute
stories.summary: The churn on the English Wikipedia page for Club América goalkeeper Luis Malagón came from routine maintenance and one act of vandalism. It is not a transfer or other news. Intruder007, a regular editor, made a stats update (rev 1380899269). It moved the club-update date from 10 to 17 October 2026 and added one appearance, taking his América league caps from 121 to 122. That points only to a match played on 17 October. About 10 minutes later, temporary account ~2026-55824-54 deleted the whole infobox (−2873 bytes, edit summary "/* */") and changed his birthplace in the text from Zamora, Michoacán to "Tel Aviv, Israel" (rev 1380900302). Staticspector reverted that 38 seconds later (rev 1380900353), putting the page back to Intruder007's version. All three editors touched only this page, and nothing suggests the edits link to a real-world event beyond the routine match update.

stories.headline: Routine upkeep on article for Fielder–Oppenheim Elizabeth Holmes documentary
stories.summary: Three editors made small edits within about 8 minutes to the en-wiki article for "You Can See Everything", a 2026 A24 documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim about Elizabeth Holmes. This looks like normal upkeep on a film that is out in theaters now, not a news event. Nope251 changed the Rotten Tomatoes review count from 110 to 113 (still 99%; Metacritic 99). Guz13 copyedited and reordered the plot section, mainly about the 2025 reenactments with Amanda Seyfried and Christopher Abbott. A temporary account added "epic" to the opening line with no source ("The film's considered an epic"). That is a mild, unsourced change in tone, not vandalism, and someone may undo it. There were no reverts, no other languages involved, and no factual claims about real-world events. The only thing that ties to the news is the film's ongoing release and the attention it is getting from critics.

stories.headline: NZ 'Moon Man' forecaster Ken Ring has died, family says; Wikipedia updated
stories.summary: Editors are updating English Wikipedia to report the death of Ken Ring, the Auckland writer known for weather and earthquake predictions based on lunar cycles. Ebalia Nux changed the article to past tense and added a death line citing a Stuff report dated 21 October 2026 ('Moon Man' weather forecaster Ken Ring dies after short illness). The same editor also added Ring to the deaths list on the 2026 in New Zealand page. A few minutes later, Ebalia Nux changed the wording to say only that his family announced the death on 21 October through one of his social media pages, and took out the exact date of death because it is not confirmed. Gadfium added the 2026 deaths category; I did not read that edit's diff. The two pages are only linked by this death. The other October edits by Andykatib (job cuts, Colleen Ngarewa's death) are separate news items, and despite the revert flag on one of them there are no signs of an edit war or vandalism. The only source is one Stuff report I can see cited, and the exact date of death is unknown. Only English Wikipedia is involved, with three named editors.

stories.headline: Scorpion stub on fr.wiki: wrong-photo cleanup settled; nothing new, no news
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. The French stub on the scorpion Birulatus astartiae has had no edits since R3L3ct3ur49's revision 240539657. Antp 92 started by blanking the image slot in the taxobox because the photo was wrong ("photo incorrect", 240539169). A clumsy follow-up (240539485) deleted the whole taxobox and put broken [[Fichier:]] code into the reference link. RevolucioBot undid that automatically. R3L3ct3ur49 then reverted Antp 92's last edit and put the taxobox back. They said they had removed the bad image on Wikidata, which is where the taxobox was pulling it from. That fixes the complaint at its source. There were two reverts, but they came from a bot and a patroller fixing one editor's mistakes. This is not an edit war or vandalism. Only one page in one language is involved, and there is no real-world news here.

stories.headline: New es-wiki bio of Puerto Rican author Carlos Colón Rodríguez tagged for speedy deletion
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is a newly created article working its way through deletion review. Wikinor24 created the Spanish-language Wikipedia biography (rev 175886438). It describes Carlos Colón Rodríguez, a self-published writer born in Cayey, Puerto Rico, in 1958, and lists his books up to "El Perfil de un Dictador" (2025). The only sources are an Amazon listing and a 2011 book-fair notice. A.piquerasm then tagged it for speedy deletion as lacking encyclopedic relevance ({{Destruir|A4}}, rev 175886926). Another account, General de brigada Antonio, deleted the tag without giving a reason and removed the infobox photo (rev 175886938). A.piquerasm put the tag back (rev 175886952), and the creator then re-added the official photo. Nothing in the article mentions a death or any recent event. The one removal of the tag doesn't count as an edit war, but it may be a conflict of interest or promotion. I haven't checked whether the accounts are connected, and the most likely outcome is that the page gets deleted.

stories.headline: Swedish diplomat Lars Bergquist's dewiki page: wrong link fixed, no news event
stories.summary: All three edits to the German article on Swedish diplomat Lars Bergquist were about one wrong link. The article linked Sweden's foreign ministry to "Utenriksdepartementet", which is Norway's foreign ministry. A temporary account (~2026-56005-23, edit summary "Falsche Verlinkung", i.e. "wrong link") replaced it with a link straight to the Swedish Wikipedia article on Utrikesdepartementet (+75). Horst Gräbner removed that link (-75) because German Wikipedia doesn't allow visible links to other-language Wikipedias in article text. CaroFraTyskland then made a final -1 fix, noting that "uten..." is the Norwegian ministry. The diff text I could see was cut off, so I'm assuming that fix replaced the Norwegian name with the correct Swedish one. None of the edits touch dates, death or career details, and the three editors agreed on the fix rather than fighting over it. This isn't a real-world event.

stories.headline: Helen Haines attack suspect remanded in custody until Feb 2027; no bail sought
stories.summary: This is a continuation of the tracked Helen Haines car attack story, not a new event. The only new fact comes from PliskorCor's edit (rev 1381247137), which cites ABC News from 21 Oct 2026. It says that at an initial hearing the accused, Brendan Nugent, made no bail application, and his lawyer said he has a neurological disorder and a concussion. He was remanded in custody until 4 Feb 2027, and the magistrate asked that a medical professional see him immediately. The edit sits next to text already on the page: on 20 Oct, Victoria charged him with intentionally causing serious injury and dangerous driving causing serious injury, and the Commonwealth charged him with causing harm to a public official. Since the earlier brief, the page has had only routine changes, such as Blainster adding the 18 May 2019 election date (rev 1381247917). The rest of the window is good-faith profile expansion by established editors, with no reverts or vandalism, and only English Wikipedia moved. The court details rest on one cited ABC report that I have not checked independently.

stories.headline: Deaths in 2026: routine additions incl. Iranian archaeologist Yusef Majidzadeh, 90
stories.summary: Normal upkeep of English Wikipedia's "Deaths in 2026" list, with no reverts or disputes. About 7 named editors made edits in roughly 1.5 hours. New entries, each with a source: Iranian archaeologist Yusef Majidzadeh, 90 (Persian-language ISNA/Entekhab; first filed under 17 October, then moved to 19 October per the edit comment); Argentine actor Antonio Grimau, 82 (Canal26, later swapped for an El País Uruguay source); Mexican telenovela actor Carlos Miguel Suárez (López-Dóriga); Kenyan Equity Group payments head Eva Ngigi-Sarwari, 45, who reportedly died on a business trip to China (TechCabal); and US racehorse Early Voting, 7, of colic (BloodHorse). The removals followed by re-additions were date or format fixes, not an edit war. None of these looks like a major breaking story. Ngigi-Sarwari's death abroad is the only one that may draw more coverage. I didn't check whether other-language pages are moving.

stories.headline: En-wiki patrol churn: unsourced celebrity romance claim and small vandalism reverted
stories.summary: This is routine anti-vandalism patrol, not a news event. The update adds two pages since the last brief. Josef Newgarden: a one-edit temporary account changed his birth year from 1991 to 1990 with no explanation. Patroller KuyaMoHirowo restored 1991 in both the infobox and the lead (diffs 1381274954 and 1381275019). WAZE-TV: a regular editor added to the History section, then KuyaMoHirowo fixed a broken page-number template in a citation. That is ordinary cleanup. The earlier items stand. A two-edit account added an unsourced claim that Miles Joris-Peyrafitte is dating, and then engaged to, actress Kelsey Asbille. Both edits were reverted under the rules for unsourced claims about living people. Nothing in the graph supports the claim. Also reverted: stripped links and a press-release citation on Open Software Foundation (diff read), a football taunt on Jorginho Paulista, and an edit on The Old Manor, Croscombe that was reverted as spam. Caveat: the diff tool failed for the romance-claim edits and the WAZE-TV History edit, so for those I'm relying on edit summaries.

stories.headline: Routine: unit-template edits to MD-90 and BAe 146 pages reverted by patroller
stories.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. One temporary account (~2026-56033-60) made two small formatting edits about five minutes apart, and an established editor (Seasider53) reverted both. On British Aerospace 146 the edit added a knots unit to a {{Convert}} template in the old 1987 PSA Flight 1771 entry. On McDonnell Douglas MD-90 it rewrote the cabin width × height {{cvt}} template. Neither edit changed any facts or added any events, and there was no edit war: one revert per page and no back-and-forth. The only thing linking the two pages is that the same editor touched both. I didn't open the two reverts; I'm treating them as exact undos based on their sizes (-3 and -11) and their 'Reverted 1 edit' comments.

stories.headline: Czech Wikipedia cleans up "Josef Polášek" disambiguation pages; no news trigger
stories.summary: This is page housekeeping, not news. On cs.wikipedia, RomanM82 turned the base title "Josef Polášek" from a redirect into a disambiguation page. It lists four people with that name: a priest (1866–1948), a Brno functionalist architect (1899–1946), an actor (born 1965) whose page is now "Josef Polášek (herec)", and a former dean at Tomas Bata University in Zlín. RomanM82 also redirected "Josef Polášek (rozcestník)" (the old disambiguation page) to the base title. Harold undid that redirect ("takhle ne", meaning "not like this") and reverted the base page to an older list, which still includes the new dean entry. Paul E's add-and-undo of a surname template was a self-revert. The one change to the dean's article fixed a missing "a" ("and"). It describes events from 2011–2012, not anything new. All this happened within about 12 minutes, in one language. It looks like a disagreement over how to organise the pages, not an edit war or vandalism. I see nothing that points to a current event.

stories.headline: New de-wiki biography of pianist Gabriele Baldocci, then routine cleanup
stories.summary: This is a new article, not a news event. Rastlyn, an account with only 8 edits, created the German Wikipedia article on Italian-British pianist and composer Gabriele Baldocci (born 1980 in Livorno) in one 13,454-byte edit (rev 271494750). The article covers his early life and training, his work with Martha Argerich and his recordings of Liszt's piano versions of Beethoven's symphonies, citing reviews and interviews. Within minutes, two experienced editors made standard new-article fixes: M2k~dewiki added the person-data template (Personendaten) and authority-control data (Normdaten) and fixed a link to a disambiguation page, and AxelHH edited the external-links section. There were no reverts. Nothing points to a news trigger: the newest source cited is a July 2026 concert report, and no other-language versions of the page showed up in the graph. One uncertainty: a new, low-activity account wrote a long, polished, promotional-leaning biography, which could mean a conflict of interest. The diff alone can't show that.

stories.headline: Puna teal page hit by minor vandalism from one temporary account; quickly reverted
stories.summary: The four edits on the English "Puna teal" article are juvenile vandalism, not a content dispute and not a real-world event. A single temporary account (~2026-56184-67) made two edits. First it swapped a Clements (2007) citation for "Hey its me its Verity" (rev 1381180737), which DonnieNova reverted. Then it replaced the lead's species description with "the best duck in the world. I love it sooooooo much and I want to hug one please" (rev 1381181019), which ClueBot NG reverted 9 seconds later. There is one page in one language, no back-and-forth between established editors, and both edits have been undone. The vandal may come back, but nothing here is newsworthy.

stories.headline: Japan's MMX Phobos probe page now says it "launched in 2026"; details unverified
stories.summary: On 19 Oct 2026 (UTC), several registered editors updated the English Wikipedia article on JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which aims to return samples from Phobos. None of the edits were reverted. The current article intro describes MMX as a probe that "launched in 2026." The edit comments support that: one editor added an "elapsed mission duration" (+71 bytes) and then added +508 bytes with no comment, another added citations (+781), and a third "changed some future tense to past/present tense." Together these point to a launch that has just happened. One anonymous edit also hit the Japanese article (火星衛星探査計画, -1572 bytes, no comment) about 1.6 hours before the English activity. That edit could be a launch-related update or something unrelated. The edits on the Phobos article are style cleanups and have nothing to do with the launch. Every diff fetch failed again, including the Japanese one. So the launch date, time and early status (successful separation, contact with the probe) remain unconfirmed by edit text. The evidence is the article's current intro plus the edit comments.

stories.headline: DWTS S35: Week 6 'no elimination' now stated and sourced; Stiles' tribute to Ledger added
stories.summary: The last brief inferred that nobody was eliminated in Week 6. The en-wiki season 35 article now says so directly. TSDS25 added "No elimination took place this week" (rev 1381256480). JoyfullySmile extended it to "all scores were carried over to the following week" (rev 1381256639). DiaMali then cited a Hollywood Reporter Week 6 recap dated October 20, 2026 for the line (rev 1381256961). Johnny0929 added that Julia Stiles was joined at the end of her dance by her 10 Things I Hate About You co-stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Andrew Keegan, Gabrielle Union and Susan May Pratt, as a tribute to Heath Ledger (rev 1381256599). DiaMali reworded and wikilinked that sentence; the Stiles detail doesn't have its own citation in the diffs I read (rev 1381257040). All edits are by established accounts on one page in English only, with no reverts. They build on each other and don't conflict, so this is routine episode coverage that confirms the prior brief rather than adding a new story.

stories.headline: New ar-wiki bio of Egyptian academic tagged for speedy deletion over notability
stories.summary: This isn't a news event. It's a newly created Arabic Wikipedia page about Dr. Nadia Abdel Fattah El-Bagoury, an Egyptian anthropology and education researcher. The intro says she studied at Al-Azhar, got her MA and PhD from Cairo University's Institute of African Studies, and worked in school libraries for the Education Ministry. The account "Mohamed elbagory81" created the page (rev 77037293, +2315 bytes, "adding sources and references"). The username shares her family name, which may mean a conflict of interest, but that is not confirmed. Within about 4 minutes, patroller "زين العابدين 22" added a speedy-deletion request because the article doesn't meet the notability rules for people (77037297). A third editor followed with a 2-byte edit using the same notability reason (77037300). The 2451 churn the Scout flagged is just the page being created plus the tag, not an expansion of an existing article, and nothing was reverted. Caveat: the diff text couldn't be fetched, so this comes from edit summaries, byte counts, the new-page flag and the page intro.

stories.headline: CFB Wainwright fire: editor widens toll to "4–7 dead", reviving the unconfirmed media figure
stories.summary: Not all of the new en-wiki edits are cleanup. HowlingWolven changed the lead to say "at least four service members and as many as seven people were killed" (rev 1380911125), citing Global News's unofficial report next to CBC's "Carney confirms 4 deaths". The same editor changed the infobox from deaths = 4 to deaths = 4-7 (rev 1380911443); the edit summary admits the 7 comes from "anonymous sources". The official count is still 4 and these diffs don't show any new confirmation, so the article now gives more weight to the unconfirmed number than before. Other editors may challenge this, but so far there have been no reverts. The rest is routine: David O. Johnson removed an honorific and fixed date style (rev 1380916299), an anonymous editor fixed a typo (rev 1380915651), and Slaughter-echo added McGuinty's title as Defence Minister in Reactions (rev 1380917713). That diff was cut off before the stated purpose of the edit, a note that Poilievre is the base's local MP, so I couldn't check it. Caveats: I haven't opened the Global News or CBC sources, and nothing new about the cause appeared.

stories.headline: Dennis Feldman filmography: minor dispute over Species sequel credits
stories.summary: This is a small content dispute on one English page, Dennis Feldman, the screenwriter who created the Species franchise. It is not a news event. A temporary account removed Species III (2004) and Species – The Awakening (2007) from his filmography table, citing IMDb as saying he didn't write them, and added a note that he only has a "based on characters created by" credit on Species entries he didn't work on. Editor 420yeahh put the two films back and removed that note, with the edit summary "unsourced". The first editor then undid that change. A third account made a 2-byte tweak afterward. The dispute is one round of revert so far, not a running edit war, there's no vandalism, and no other language versions changed. I can't confirm which version is right, and the dispute could start up again.

stories.headline: Edits to cut stale 2026 Duma candidacy from Yaroslavl Yabloko politician's page undone by bot
stories.summary: The page is the ru-wiki biography of Sergei Balabaev, a Yabloko politician who used to sit in the Yaroslavl regional duma. It has had four edits and no new activity since the last brief. A temporary account and then registered user Markusha17 each deleted the same line, which calls him a 2026 State Duma candidate in district No. 194 and cites Kommersant (10 Aug 2026) and the Yaroslavl electoral commission. Both gave "outdated information" as the reason. EyeBot, an automatic anti-vandalism bot, put the line back within minutes both times. There's no human edit war. Most likely the September 2026 election is over and someone is tidying up wording that's no longer true. The edits say nothing about how he did, and no other pages or languages have changed. This is routine and adds nothing to the existing story.

stories.headline: Routine sourcing and cleanup on it-wiki "Nisser" (Scandinavian folklore)
stories.summary: Four edits by three registered editors on the Italian Wikipedia article about nisser, the household spirits of Scandinavian folklore, and nothing else in the graph is involved. Salnitrum added the alternative name "tomte" to the lead, sourced to a 2022 Portuguese book (rev 152959029), then made a small follow-up edit of +24 bytes. Egidio24 fixed a citation-template parameter, and Tras changed the case of the portal names. There are no reverts, no anon editors and no other languages involved, so this does not point to any real-world event. The seasonal (Christmas) subject may explain why someone is editing it, but that is a guess. I didn't read the two small edits (152959063 and 152959174); their comments and byte sizes suggest housekeeping.

stories.headline: Street Fighter (2026) opening weekend: Wikipedia box-office figures shift from $13M to $51.1M
stories.summary: Paramount's Street Fighter came out in the US on October 16, 2026. Over its opening weekend, editors of its English Wikipedia article have been updating the box-office numbers. Wikieditor9117 changed the infobox worldwide gross from $13 million to $51.1 million, and The Media Expert made the same change in the lead, from $31M to $51.1M. Viotic0230 added that the film was projected to open to $31 million from 3,575 North American theaters. That citation points only to The Numbers' homepage, not a page for this film. Earlier, an anonymous editor changed the infobox gross from $13M to $31M, and David O. Johnson reverted it as "incorrect info." That $31M may have been the domestic projection mistaken for the worldwide gross, so the figures are still settling. There is one revert but no edit war, and the rest is small copyedits, such as removing a redundant year from the plot summary. This is routine release-weekend tracking on one English-language page. The exact gross figures are unconfirmed until the final weekend numbers are published.

stories.headline: Spanish 'Xantolo' vandalism continues; repeat temporary account adds new insult
stories.summary: This updates the earlier brief on the Spanish Wikipedia article on Xantolo, the Day of the Dead celebration of Mexico's Huasteca region. Temporary account ~2026-56273-78, which made one of the earlier vandal edits (175909038), came back about 17 minutes later with rev 175909258. That edit replaces the opening line's "Jeffrey Epstein created Xantolo" with "created by Michi Lote together with the God Tupu Tamadre", a pun on a Spanish obscenity. The word "dildos" stays in the lead. The graph shows no reverts since Aldair's earlier cleanup, so the vandalised text appears to still be live. It is still confined to one page in one language, and nothing points to a real-world event. Uncertain: whether anyone is about to revert it, and whether the page will be protected. A revert or protection would likely end this.

stories.headline: Latvian surname-page vandalism (Pētersons, Bite) fully reverted; no new activity
stories.summary: This is the same vandalism story already being tracked, with nothing new. The graph shows exactly 8 edits on lvwiki "Pētersons" and "Bite (uzvārds)", all made within about 6 minutes, and nothing after Egilus's final undo (rev 4537885). Temporary account ~2026-55979-91 added a joke entry, "Ričards Pētersons (2011)", calling him a schoolboy, floorball player, e-sports player and "2025 revolution participant" (rev 4537879). Temporary account ~2026-56057-44 deleted the real list of people named Bite: Erasts, Inga, Mariss and Miķelis (rev 4537876). Established editor Egilus reverted every change. Two corrections to the scout's note: only 3 editors were involved, not 6 (the two temporary accounts plus Egilus), and Egilus actually made 4 reverts, though only one is flagged as a revert. Neither temporary account edited any other page in the graph. There's no real-world event behind this; the two temporary accounts are probably one person, but I haven't confirmed that.

stories.headline: Fr-wiki "Nouvelle-Guinée": small revert dispute over the island's world size rank
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is a small content dispute on the French Wikipedia article about New Guinea, and it involves three edits that went back and forth. A temporary account (comment "Pr mon exposé", meaning "for my school presentation") changed the opening sentence from "deuxième plus grande île du monde après le Groenland" (second-largest island, after Greenland) to "troisième… après l'Australie et le Groenland" (third, after Australia and Greenland) (rev 240551781). Experienced editor Ariel Provost undid this with the comment "lire la note !" ("read the note!"). The article already has a footnote explaining that Australia and Antarctica are counted as continents, not islands. A second temporary account then put the "third-largest" wording back (rev 240552118), arguing in the edit comment that no continent is called "Australia". The scout's note said there were no reverts, but two of the three edits are undos, even though the graph's revert flag is false for all of them. This is a small revert cycle on one sentence, in one language, with one page involved. It could grow into a real edit war if it keeps going. I did not read the middle diff (rev 240552027). Its comment and its -37 byte change suggest it is the exact reverse of the first edit. I haven't checked whether the two temporary accounts are the same person.

stories.headline: Baie-D'Urfé (fr): temporary account vandalized article, both edits reverted; nothing new
stories.summary: This task covers the same four edits already in story s_053daa08, so I've added it there rather than opening a new story. The scout's guess of a content rewrite is wrong: the churn is vandalism and its cleanup. Temporary account ~2026-56095-29 added "W Ecole Joseph Henrico mon gars" to the end of the lead (rev 240530114, +33). Utilisateur ouikipedia undid it about 30 seconds later. The same account then removed about 7.2k bytes of body text: toponymy, history, geography, demographics/languages and politics (rev 240530192). RevolucioBot reverted that within 4 seconds as non-constructive. The graph shows no edits after the bot's revert, no other pages touched by this account, and no other languages involved. It looks like a one-off schoolyard prank with no sign of a real-world event. The revert flags in the graph are wrong: both undos are marked as non-reverts.

stories.headline: Third wave of prank vandalism on it-wiki Marcandalli page, reverted again
stories.summary: This is a continuation of the vandalism story already being tracked, not a new event. A third temporary account (~2026-56160-40) made three edits to the infobox of footballer Alessandro Marcandalli on it-wiki. In rev 152989209 and rev 152989245 it swapped his name, birthplace and sport for made-up entries, including what look like personal names and the sport "Basket". In rev 152989250 it changed his sport to "Latino". Maybe75 reverted the first of these through LiveRC (152989221), and Amirzat rolled back the rest in rev 152989305, which puts the real name, Calcio (football) and Ponte San Pietro back. The edit log's revert flags are all false even though these are reverts, which is why the scout counted none. The swapped-in names and "Latino" look like a schoolroom prank. I have left them out of this brief because they may belong to real private people, possibly minors. The page has now been hit by three temporary accounts in about 25 minutes, so a short semi-protection may be worth it. There is no sign of any real-world news about the player.

stories.headline: Self-described grandson disputes death date of pre-WWI footballer Ginger Owers
stories.summary: This is a small dispute about a historical fact. It is not news. A temporary account that says it is the grandson of Ginger Owers, an English centre forward active before WWI (born 1888), changed his death date in the lead from June 1951 to June 1964 (rev 1381154896). Patroller Celjski Grad reverted this within minutes as unsourced (rev 1381155128). The same account then edited the infobox to say he died in June 1964 in Epping rather than Bristol (rev 1381155340). A second temporary account restored the 1951/Bristol version (rev 1381156062). The graph didn't flag that last edit as a revert, but in practice it was one. The page is now back to 1951/Bristol. Nobody added a source on either side, and the family claim can't be checked from the graph. If the account keeps trying, this could turn into a small edit war.

stories.headline: New de-wiki bio: Hanau mayor Isabelle Hemsley (CDU) reportedly named Hesse state secretary
stories.summary: I found nothing new since the earlier brief. The graph shows no edits to the page after 1792517967. The 9 edits by 4 editors are the creation of a German Wikipedia biography and the tidy-up that followed. None of them are reverts. Derrobin154 created the page (rev 271490787, +2,845 bytes). It says Isabelle Hemsley (CDU, born 1989 in Hanau) became mayor of Hanau on 1 Oct 2026, after losing the 15 March 2026 runoff for chief mayor to Maximilian Bieri (SPD). It also says she will become state secretary in Hesse's interior ministry under Roman Poseck, replacing Martin Rößler, who is due to head the Gießen regional government office from 1 Nov 2026. The source for that is one Stadt Hanau press release on presse-service.de, which I did not open. The later edits are housekeeping: person data and a sort key (rev 271490970), a references tag (rev 271490867), and comma and grammar fixes by a temporary account (rev 271490880). None of them changed what the article claims. No other pages about Rößler, Poseck, Bieri or the Gießen office are moving in the graph, so nothing else backs up the appointment yet. Confidence is moderate because it all rests on one cited source.

stories.headline: Unrelated low-level disruption on Pixar and 'Fifth grade' pages, reverted by patrollers
stories.summary: This is not a news event. Two different temporary accounts made small, unsourced edits on two unrelated en-wiki pages, and patrollers reverted each one within minutes. On Pixar, ~2026-55847-47 replaced the "Untitled third Monsters, Inc. film" entry with a made-up 2030 title, "IU". After ClueBot NG reverted that, the same account deleted the whole Filmography timeline (-1179 bytes), and Streetr4 restored it. On Fifth grade, ~2026-55860-26 changed the typical age from "10–11" to "9–11". Streetr4 and Materialscientist reverted it twice as disruptive or unsourced. The only link between the two pages is the patroller Streetr4, who touched both; there is no film reference or real-world connection. The 'no reverts' flag is misleading: these were anti-vandalism reverts that the graph didn't tag as reverts. I didn't read the restoring revisions themselves.

stories.headline: Latvian singer's Wikipedia bio hit by defamatory rewrite, reverted twice by patrollers
stories.summary: This is not a death or news update. It is BLP vandalism on the Latvian Wikipedia article about singer and teacher Indra Lintiņa-Lučka (b. 1961, Liepāja), who became known in the Atmoda period (1988–1992) performing with Eduards Rozenštrauhs. One temporary account (~2026-56213-67) twice replaced the lead with unsourced attacks: that she "schemed" her fame off Rozenštrauhs, used the "old, naive composer as a springboard", and as a teacher psychologically terrorised pupils, sourced only to "rumours among parents". Both times the account called the original text "flattering and false". Patrollers Meistars Joda and Egilus each reverted to the original lead (±377 bytes each). The scout's churn figure is the sum of four ±377-byte edits, not new content, and the "no reverts" flag missed them because they were made with undo-style comments. Nothing points to a real-world event. The motive may be a personal grievance, but that is unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Helen Haines car attack: page edits now copyedits only, no new facts
stories.summary: This is a follow-up on the story we're already tracking, and nothing new of substance has come in. The only edit since the last brief is a grammar fix by Limblr (rev 1381088652) that adds "of" to a 2022 election-margin sentence. It doesn't touch the attack section. The core account is unchanged in rev 1381086441, which I re-read. It says Haines was hit by a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta at 15:35 AEDT on 19 October 2026 and taken to hospital with critical injuries. It also says Albanese called it apparently "a deliberate act" and that the national joint counter-terrorism team (AFP and ASIO) is investigating with state police. These claims are cited to Victoria Police, ABC, BBC, AAP and 7NEWS, with archived links. Several named editors are making small edits, with no reverts and no vandalism. I searched the graph for related titles (Haines, Wangaratta, Indi) and found no new pages or other-language versions. Still unknown: Haines's current condition, the suspect's motive and any charges.

stories.headline: Recent-changes patroller reverts low-level vandalism on three unrelated enwiki pages
stories.summary: This isn't a news event. Three unrelated temporary accounts vandalised three English Wikipedia pages, and the only link between them is patroller APK, who reverted all three. On 'Percy Jackson & the Olympians', one account added a made-up line saying Percy "is reportedly dating his half sister, Liron Gosman" (rev 1381273587). APK reverted it, and the same account put it back (rev 1381274464). In the edit data I have, that re-added line has not been reverted again. On 'Alex G', another account changed the musician's occupation field to "record producer philosopher" (rev 1381274341), and APK reverted it as unsourced. On 'All men are created equal', a third account cut the lead paragraph about the Declaration of Independence (rev 1381274014). APK restored it, and that account kept making small edits afterwards. No other languages are involved, and none of the edits point to anything happening in the real world.

stories.headline: No new activity on it-wiki Ecuadorian Communist Party page; rewrite looks finished
stories.summary: The scout's note says the history rewrite is continuing, but the graph shows no edits after the tracked story was filed. The page has 7 edits in total, and the last one, SurdusVII's "+categoria", came at ts 1792518990, before the prior brief. The only edit the earlier brief didn't describe is Jamessil's −4 byte rev 152992922. Its diff shows only formatting or markup changes, no change to the text. I re-read the main +7359 rev 152992834. It adds a table of presidential election results from 1940 to 2021, sourced to academic books and election archives. Nothing in it mentions a current event, though the access dates of "20 ottobre 2026" match when it was edited. The graph links this page to no other-language versions, so I found no matching activity elsewhere. It's still one page in one language: a single content editor plus two routine maintainers, no reverts and no anonymous editors. This is ordinary article improvement, and this story should be merged with or closed against the tracked routine one. Data-quality caveats remain: the 1944 row shows "91 votes / 91%", and the 1992 FADI candidate is given as Gustavo Jalkh. Both look doubtful, but I haven't checked them against sources.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on Jeff Parker ETA IVtet live album 'Happy Today'; routine
stories.summary: The 9 KB jump is a new German Wikipedia article, not a rewrite. Freimut Bahlo created it in a single edit (rev 271497928). It covers 'Happy Today', a live jazz album by Jeff Parker's ETA IVtet. According to the article, the band recorded it on 20 Aug 2025 at the Lodge Room in Highland Park, Los Angeles, and International Anthem released it with Nonesuch in May 2026. Since then two other editors have made only small changes: Atirador fixed formatting, and LegoFCB made a wording fix and swapped in a fuller Discogs citation (rev 271498709). There are no reverts and no disputes, and nothing points to a breaking news event. This looks like ordinary coverage of an album that came out months ago. I didn't check whether articles in other languages changed.

stories.headline: Washington Post film critic Ann Hornaday reported dead at 66; Wikipedia updates her page
stories.summary: The scout called this routine list upkeep, but the newest entry on EN 'Deaths in 2026' is a well-known person. Rev 1381059139 (DarkStarHarry) added Ann Hornaday, 66, an American film critic at The Washington Post. It cites a washingtonpost.com obituary whose URL is dated 2026/10/19 and titled "Ann Hornaday, longtime Washington Post film critic, dies at 66." A second editor, Griffter12, then rewrote the entry and added a {{paywall}} tag (rev 1381059333). That suggests someone else looked at the source too, but the edit doesn't prove they read it. On her own article, DarkStarHarry switched her to past tense, added a death date of 18 October 2026, swapped Living people for 2026 deaths (rev 1381058900), and added Baltimore as the death place (rev 1381059974). Caveats: one editor made every change to the biography. The birth date he gave, 1960-01-01, looks like a placeholder, not a sourced date. I haven't confirmed the date she died, and the list entry was first posted under the 16th and then edited under the 18th. Earlier items still stand, including the Ivorian politician Louis-André Dacoury-Tabley, 81 (rev 1381058661, single French source). No reverts and no edit war.

stories.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: Stumble Guys and Samurái vandalism; Samurái damage may still be live
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It's schoolyard vandalism by temporary accounts on two unrelated Spanish Wikipedia pages, and this story is already the schoolyard-vandalism story. The graph shows no other story on these pages, so there's nothing to merge. On Stumble Guys, ~2026-56174-90 kept changing a French insult about "jean raphe" in the lead (rev 175921732). Eddy Wardian reverted it back to SeroBOT's clean version (rev 175921766), and there have been no edits since. On Samurái, the last edit in the graph is ~2026-56137-36's rev 175921661. It broke the lead image caption, added "aseituna" and removed the recorded-audio template, and the graph shows no revert after it. So unlike Stumble Guys, that damage may still be live, though the graph could be behind the wiki. Contrary to the scout's note, there are reverts: SeroBOT, Automoderador and Eddy Wardian undid edits on both pages. The data just doesn't flag those edits as reverts. No new activity since the last brief.

stories.headline: NRA article vandalism stops after semi-protection; no further edits
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not a content dispute, which confirms the earlier brief. A temporary account (~2026-56319-52) and then the account Sbsbbab kept putting the same insertion into the English NRA article. It renamed the infobox to "Terrorist Organization" and added "mass murdering terrorist organization" to the opening sentence and the image caption (revs 1381071455, 1381071956). Cannolis, Untamed1910 and Slatersteven reverted it each time. Untamed1910's restore (1381071971) put it down to a long-term abuser ("LTA calebhughes"). Administrator Mfield then added semi-protection (1381072337, {{pp-semi}}). The graph shows no edits to the page since then, so the semi-protection appears to have stopped it. The scout's "no anonymous edits" point is misleading: temporary accounts aren't flagged as anonymous, and the "reverts" are mostly the vandal undoing the patrollers. That makes it one-sided, not two editors trading reverts. Nothing changed in other languages, and nothing points to a real-world event. The Fog edits in the dossier are a separate, minor vandal and have nothing to do with this.

stories.headline: Fog and Curse LLC: small vandalism by two temporary accounts, quickly reverted
stories.summary: This is not news. Two unrelated temporary accounts made small vandal edits on English Wikipedia. One added junk text ("jevil") to Fog over and over, with comments like "gro" and "mimi". The other changed a section heading on Curse LLC from "2006–2010" to "2000–2010" and left the comment "find and see what i changed HEHE". The same anti-vandalism patrollers (DonnieNova, Ivebeenhacked, Cannolis) reverted every edit within minutes, and that is the only thing linking the two pages. No real-world event, content dispute or edit war between established editors is involved.

stories.headline: Pickleball in the United States: schoolyard vandalism, only partly cleaned up
stories.summary: This is still minor vandalism on one English Wikipedia page. It has nothing to do with real-world news, and nothing has changed since the earlier brief. In rev 1381186024, a temporary account using the edit note "better image" changed the line about 166 college pickleball clubs to end with "actively seeking dillan pham". The same edit deleted the USA Pickleball citation and the "Collegiate Pickleball Tour" heading. A second temporary account added "|last=GYH IS PRO" to a citation. Patroller DonnieNova removed that in rev 1381186554, but only rolled the page back to the first vandal's version. Going by the diffs, the "dillan pham" text and the removed citation and heading are still on the page. The graph has recorded no edits since the rollback, so nobody has fixed it yet. This involves one page in one language, and the inserted text looks like student in-jokes, so there's no sign of a wider event.

stories.headline: Sanda Island Lighthouse: one vandal edit reverted in 70 seconds, then routine copyedits
stories.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. On the en-wiki article for Sanda Island Lighthouse (Argyll and Bute, Scotland), a temporary account (~2026-56028-75) made one edit (rev 1381178080, -590 bytes). It deleted the infobox and changed the lead: "United Kingdom" became "libia", the 1850 founding date became "1700 with his wife", and "operated by the Northern Lighthouse Board" became "was abandoned". Jeppiz fully reverted it about 70 seconds later (rev 1381178197). Apart from that, Cripesohblimey and Minturn made small style edits: paragraph whitespace, and "Early wrecks" changed to "Earlier wrecks" (rev 1381178704). There was no back-and-forth and no other pages or languages were involved. This was a single act of vandalism that was quickly fixed, not a dispute or news event. Recommend closing.

stories.headline: New Italian Wikipedia biography of ex-Shin Bet chief Carmi Gillon, no news trigger
stories.summary: The 6,439-byte churn comes from one edit. User Stefantiz created a new itwiki article on Carmi Gillon (+6,371 bytes). Gillon is a former Shin Bet director (1995–96) who resigned after Yitzhak Rabin's assassination and later served as ambassador to Denmark. The new text is a sourced biography covering his career, the Shamgar Commission findings and his later posts. The other three edits are small cleanups: a note fix, an image caption from Sedlex, and Bio "Epoca" parameters from AndreA. There are no reverts, and the graph has no linked pages in other languages showing activity. The part of the creation diff I read mentions no new event such as a death or appointment. So this looks like normal article creation, not a reaction to news. One caveat: the end of the creation diff was cut off, so I can't fully rule out a recent development mentioned there.

stories.headline: Schoolyard vandalism on es-wiki Bruno Philippi bio fully reverted; no news
stories.summary: Update to the earlier brief: the vandalism on the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Chilean businessman Bruno Philippi has now been fully cleaned up. Account ~2026-56193-02 came back and made more junk edits. One of them removed a heading it had added earlier, "pollo lagos tdh kl" (rev 175922081). Editor Montgomery then undid 10 revisions in one go (rev 175922104), which restored the clean heading "Primeros años de vida". That removes the "rodrigo nunez" change the earlier brief flagged as still live. There is no real-world news about Philippi. On the second page, Cristel Sandí (a Costa Rican footballer), temporary account ~2026-55977-00 first replaced the infobox and changed her club to Waybe-Sport Extremadura CD in Spain's Primera Federación (rev 175921901). It then added a career path of Dimas Escazú until 2025, Real Estelí (Nicaragua) 2025–26, and Extremadura from 2026 (rev 175922017). Eddy Wardian reverted the first edit, and Casisgaal reverted the second as "sin referencias" (no references). The transfer could be real, but it has no source, is unconfirmed, comes from one anonymous account in one language, and is not linked to the Philippi vandalism.
