stories.headline: Alberta referendum: no new results since ~76% "Remain" at 73% reporting; edits are cosmetic
stories.summary: The scout's note doesn't hold up. The edits since the last brief don't update the results tally. There are two new revisions. Rev 1381161708 by PortiaIsPolitical is labelled "Fixed the number of votes", but it only makes a formatting change to the Referendum vote line. The figure is still 420,038. Rev 1381162008 by Lukey2jedi is a copyedit ("researcher" to "researchers") in the section on alleged Russian and US foreign-influence campaigns. The latest results on the page are still the ones from revs 1381160763 and 1381161419: Remain 1,315,426 and Referendum 420,038 with 73% reporting, about 75.8% Remain. No source is cited for those numbers, so treat them as provisional. There is no edit war, and activity is still on one English page only. Expect another update when the reporting share moves past 73%.

stories.headline: Two unrelated vandalism edits on English Wikipedia, both reverted by one patroller
stories.summary: This is not a news event. Two different temporary accounts each made one edit, on two pages that have nothing to do with each other, and both edits were undone within minutes by patroller Somepinkdude. On "Zacharia", which normally just redirects to "Zechariah", rev 1381113142 replaced the redirect with a 4 KB joke article. It describes a made-up "unit of time" equal to five business days, named after a private individual and mocking how short their time at a job was. The reverter called it a BLP (biography of a living person) violation, unsourced and probably AI-generated, and restored the redirect in rev 1381113748. On "Genoveva Matute", rev 1381114054 changed the Filipino writer's death date from March 21, 2009 to March 4, 2024 without a source. The article's own cited Inquirer obituary is from 2009, so the change is false, and it was reverted in rev 1381114183. Nothing links the two edits except the patroller who cleaned up both, and no other languages or editors were involved.

stories.headline: Unrelated eswiki pages linked only by anti-vandalism bot; no news event
stories.summary: The three pages in this cluster (Nefertiti, Señorita Colombia 2026, Esto es guerra) are connected only by SeroBOT, eswiki's automated anti-vandalism bot, which reverted one edit by a temporary account on each page within roughly 13 minutes. A different temporary account made each edit, and none of them touched more than one page. The one diff that loaded, rev 175912097, is plain joke vandalism: it adds "nombre real Fabiana Silva" and "amiga del Sebita" to Nefertiti's lead, and SeroBOT reverted it 3 seconds later. The other diffs wouldn't load. The Señorita Colombia edit blanked 614 bytes, was reverted, and was followed by a zero-byte edit to the "Candidatas" section by the same account, which is in line with low-level tampering on a live pageant article but is not confirmed. There's no sign of coordination or of a real-world event, and nothing points to an edit war. Señorita Colombia 2026 may be getting normal attention around the pageant, but that isn't shown here.

stories.headline: Patroller reverts vandalism by four temporary accounts on unrelated es-wiki pages
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is routine counter-vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia. In about 13 minutes, four different temporary accounts each made one edit to an unrelated page. Patroller "Nuria, the witch" reverted every one within about a minute. On Sara García Alonso, someone changed "Oncológicas" to "Ginecologicas" and changed Pedro Duque's 1992 ESA selection year to 1967. On Tormenta Daniel, someone removed the "Impacto/Grecia" headings and put in "NACHO EL NANO". On Villapene, the parish name was swapped for a crude pun ("Villapollon"). On Bradypus tridactylus, someone added "Se drogan y fuman hierba" ("they get high and smoke weed"). The graph doesn't flag these edits as reverts, but the patroller's comments ("Revertida una edición…") make clear they were. The pages have nothing in common except the patroller, and nothing points to a real-world trigger. It is unclear whether the four accounts are one person.

stories.headline: No new activity: Pledge, Kai and Sliced bread joke edits all reverted; one stray typo left
stories.summary: This is still the same schoolyard vandalism on three English pages, and nothing has happened since the last brief. A graph query found no edits on Pledge of Allegiance, Kai or Sliced bread after rev 1381186163. On Pledge of Allegiance, Pickersgill-Cunliffe's revert (rev 1381186067) took out "yet useless," and put the lead back to "a patriotic recited verse". On Kai, Raptor123456 removed his own innuendo line (rev 1381186083). In the same edit he cut the last letter off "Khakassia", leaving "Khakassi" in an unrelated entry. Temp account ~2026-56185-92 then added a similar line (rev 1381186150), and ClueBot NG reverted it back to Raptor's version, so the typo is probably still on the page. Everything is in English, nothing is going back and forth between two editors, and there is no real-world news hook. The scout's call of continued churn rather than a new event holds.

stories.headline: Pitch and putt: minor vandalism by one temporary account, reverted twice
stories.summary: The 1008-byte churn on en:Pitch and putt comes from two edits by one temporary account (~2026-55820-40), each undone within minutes. The first edit (rev 1381068660) deleted the infobox and inserted "at St anne's little links" into the lead. Cannolis reverted it as vandalism. The second edit (rev 1381068961, comment "the winners") replaced the maximum-hole-length rule with "Previous winners: Jeb and Fraggy at Little Links St Anne's". Wolfwolfnuke reverted that through AntiVandal. This looks like a joke about a local course and its players. There is no sign of a real-world event, a content dispute or activity in other languages. The page is back to its earlier version.

stories.headline: Routine infobox tweaks on Ugly (UK band); one unsourced genre edit reverted
stories.summary: Three edits in about six minutes on the English article for the UK band Ugly, all to the infobox. One editor added an alias field ("Ugly (UK)"), and that edit still stands. A temporary-account editor added "progressive rock" to the genre list. A patroller using the WikiShield anti-vandalism tool reverted it about 30 seconds later as an "unsourced genre change". This is the usual genre-tinkering seen on music articles: there was one revert, no back-and-forth, nothing changed in the article text, and nothing points to a real-world event such as a release, a line-up change or a death. I didn't check whether pages for this band in other languages also changed.

stories.headline: Cornelius Vanderbilt (Simple English): small edits, one bot revert of a newcomer
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts made small edits to the Simple English Wikipedia article on Cornelius Vanderbilt, who died in 1877. One account added that he gave one million dollars when Vanderbilt University was founded, plus a pronunciation guide ("van-der-bílt"). The anti-vandalism bot ChenzwBot reverted both, taking the page back to the last version by Griffinofwales. That account then put the pronunciation back as "Fix pronouce". A second temporary account made four one-to-four-byte copy edits (punctuation, removing "the" and "a"); one carried the joke comment "boomshakalaka". The bot revert looks like a false positive on a good-faith addition, not a dispute. No other languages, no news hook and no back-and-forth reverting. I couldn't load the diffs for the later small edits, so those are judged from their comments and byte sizes only.

stories.headline: Routine: two new, unrelated dewiki articles (1975 DDR TV film, Fritz comedy channel)
stories.summary: Nothing new since the last brief. This cluster is still two unrelated German Wikipedia articles that were created around the same time. 'Die Überlebende' (rev 271505267, AnPa286) is about a 1975 DEFA/DDR-Fernsehen TV film by Christian Steinke, based on Kurt David's novella. 'Comedy Kollektiv' (rev 271505401, a temporary account) is about the Fritz/rbb YouTube channel behind 'Falsch aber Lustig'. Its mention of an ARD Mediathek spin-off cites an existing DWDL report, not anything new. The only link between the two pages is M2k~dewiki, a high-volume patroller who added categories and a references section to both. Since the last brief, the only new edit is from the film article's creator (rev 271505658): a Film Polski source and the Hungarian title. There were no reverts and no other languages, and nothing points to a real-world event. I recommend closing this story.

stories.headline: Grizzana Morandi: joke edits to festival list reverted on it-wiki; no news event
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-50582-61) made three edits to the "Tradizioni e folclore" section of the it-wiki article on Grizzana Morandi, a municipality in the Apennines near Bologna. The first edit added three local feast days with no sources: a 24 April procession at the war memorial, the parish feast on the first Sunday of August, and the 15 August "festa dello Zuccherino". The later edits added a mocking line saying the feast ends with people "in alcoholic comas" ("coma etilici vari", then "gente ai limiti del coma etilico"). Patroller Amirzat undid the last edit, and Yiyi then took the page back to its earlier version ("ripristino versione"), removing everything the temporary account had added. The graph does not flag these as reverts, but the diffs show they were. This is small-scale vandalism mixed with possibly genuine but unsourced folklore detail, cleaned up within about 25 minutes. Nothing points to a real-world event, and the account edited no other pages.

stories.headline: Kandahar article vandalized: infobox removed, then city relabeled as in Pakistan; reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism on the English Wikipedia article for Kandahar, not a real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-56036-30) deleted the whole settlement infobox, about 3,400 characters (rev 1381093315). A Human of Time reverted the deletion. The same account then edited the short description, hatnote, infobox type, pushpin map and province/district links to say Kandahar is in Pakistan instead of Afghanistan (rev 1381096133). Lemonaka rolled that back about an hour after the first edit, citing missing reliable sources. Nothing points to a news trigger: only one page moved, no other-language versions changed, and the account touched no other articles. It may be nationalist trolling tied to Afghanistan–Pakistan tensions, but nothing in the graph shows that.

stories.headline: Damping page vandalism reverted twice in 90 seconds; no new activity, no news
stories.summary: The "new cluster" the Scout flagged is the same four Damping edits this story already covers. Nothing new has happened since. Pocketjoe684 vandalised the cited opening sentence twice while claiming in edit summaries to be adding explanation. Rev 1381084068 added "We love damping!!!! PETER!!" and rev 1381084199 added "WE LOVE DAMPING! PETER!". ClueBot NG reverted the first, and Dr vulpes reverted the second with Interceptor (rev 1381084238, which restores the cited sentence). The Scout called this routine churn with no reverts, but that is wrong: the graph's revert flag is false, yet both follow-up edits are anti-vandalism reverts. I'm keeping the status as vandalism, not routine. I also corrected the earlier brief, which quoted both inserts with the same wording. The Barn owl part of the story is unchanged, and nothing points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Annabelle Rama wording cleanup and Chatbot link spam share a patroller; no news
stories.summary: This cluster holds two unrelated bits of routine upkeep on English Wikipedia. They are grouped only because one anti-vandalism patroller, Beyhive Navy, reverted edits on both pages. On Annabelle Rama, a temporary account added unsourced occupation wording, and Beyhive Navy reverted it. Celjski Grad then cut the infobox and lead down to "actress" and removed both "talent manager" and the "Spanish and Chinese descent" line, citing lack of support in the article and MOS:ETHNICITY, the style guideline on mentioning ethnicity (rev 1381152686). On Chatbot, the account Yapa1997 kept adding promotional "Character AI" external links (characteraifree.com, then charactersaichat.com; revs 1381151320, 1381151621, 1381152927). Beyhive Navy and Calmira90 reverted them as WP:SPAM. These edits contain no real-world event, news hook or link to other languages, so I agree with the Scout. I did not open every revert diff, but the edit summaries and the changes in size match what I describe.

stories.headline: zh.wiki film-company list: two blankings both reverted; no new edits since
stories.summary: This is the same vandalism incident on zh.wikipedia's 电影公司列表 (List of film companies) that we already track. I found no new activity beyond it. The graph has just four edits on the page, the latest at ts 1792488101, and all four were covered by the earlier brief. The scout's note about edits "continuing" seems to be the same set seen again. Two temporary accounts each deleted content: rev 95185480 cut the Germany, mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan distributor sections (−1,078), and rev 95185559 replaced the whole page with "{{]]" and a category (−6,188). Registered editor Làm Việc Thiện undid both as pure vandalism, and the diff of rev 95185577 shows the full text coming back. This is not a real-world event or an edit war, because nobody re-reverted. The one open question is whether new edits happen that the graph hasn't picked up yet.

stories.headline: New nl.wiki article on NTR docudrama 'Fri Fri Suriname' after Cinekid Award win
stories.summary: The large churn is one new article, not a rewrite. Glynis73 created 'Fri Fri Suriname' (+5,084 bytes). It describes a three-part NTR youth docudrama from 2025 about Suriname's independence on 25 November 1975, made for the 50th anniversary. The article says the series won the 2026 Cinekid Award for craftsmanship in a series production, citing Cinekid's 2026 winners page (accessed 2026-10-20). That award is the likely reason the page was created now. The three follow-up edits are routine cleanup by two established editors: RuedNL2 removed a duplicate title header, and PAvdK added wikilinks and a references section. There were no reverts and no other languages were involved. One thing to watch: the creator's username, 'Glynis73', matches the screenwriter named in the article (Glynis Terborg), so this may be a conflict of interest. That can't be confirmed from the edits alone. The award claim also hasn't been checked beyond the cited source.

stories.headline: "Try Everything" page: one temp account's unsourced label swap reverted twice
stories.summary: This is not a news hook. All non-revert activity on the enwiki article for Shakira's 2016 Zootopia song "Try Everything" came from one temporary account (~2026-55064-83), which made 7 edits over about 30 minutes. Each edit changed the record label from Walt Disney Records to Universal Music Group in the infobox, lead and category. The later edits also changed the runtime from 3:22 to 3:16, added "File Type = MP3" and created a "Universal Music Group soundtracks" category. One edit broke the infobox by removing the music-video field and closing braces. The edit summaries cite only "Universal Music Group" or a Zootopia Trailer #2 YouTube title. None of the edits added a source. Patrollers Jessicapierce and Discospinster each reverted the account once, restoring the Disney label. There is no back-and-forth between established editors and no activity in other languages. The edits don't point to a re-release, label change or other real-world event, though I can't rule out the editor sincerely misreading a streaming listing.

stories.headline: Vandalism on es-wiki Aureliano Blanquet page by one temp account, reverted twice
stories.summary: This isn't news. A single temporary account (~2026-56291-49) vandalized the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Aureliano Blanquet, the Huerta-era general who died in 1919. In its first edit it swapped "Guerra" in the infobox's "Secretario de Guerra y Marina" for an obscene word. Leonpolanco reverted that. The account then added garbled, unsourced wording about Blanquet's severed head being "macheteado", meaning cut off with a machete, and removed the {{Cita requerida}} (citation needed) tag. Jake Park reverted that with Huggle about four minutes later. The scout counted "no reverts" because the revert flag wasn't set, but both reverts show plainly in the edit comments and diffs. Only one page and one language moved, and no other editors joined, so there's no sign of a real-world trigger. The scout's anniversary idea is unconfirmed and unlikely.

stories.headline: Zevgolatio update: another new account adds unsourced "Services" section, reverted
stories.summary: This is an update to the Zevgolatio/Vochaiko story on Greek Wikipedia, and no real-world event is involved. Since the last brief there is one new edit. A sixth new account, Antwniaaa, added a "Services" section to the Zevgolatio article (rev 11886120, +594). The heading itself is misspelled ("Υπυρεσίες"), and the section describes the Velo-Vocha municipal Community Centre and the benefits and counselling residents can apply for. Unlike the earlier name-dropping pranks, this text is plausible, but it has no source and is badly spelled. Patroller Fotis A. reverted it in full about five minutes later (rev 11886126). The scout's "churn of 1762" comes from adding up these additions and their removals together with the earlier Vochaiko and Yuujgftyyu edits and their reverts, not from a new wave of vandalism. The pattern fits a group of local students, possibly on a class assignment, writing about their own village with throwaway accounts. That link is a guess; I have not confirmed it.

stories.headline: Emma closure: de.wiki adds lead-style line on Schwarzer's announcement; no new facts
stories.summary: This is a continuation of the tracked story about Alice Schwarzer closing the feminist magazine Emma, not a new story. Since the last brief there have been two more edits to the German Wikipedia article. Nicola added a one-line summary (rev 271503745): "In October 2026 Alice Schwarzer announced the magazine would be discontinued at the end of the year." Christof46 then fixed a typo in that sentence (rev 271503894). The main facts are unchanged and still sourced to Tages-Anzeiger, taz and Der Spiegel, all dated 21 Oct 2026 (rev 271503352). The print edition ends on 8 Dec 2026, the closure is said not to be for financial reasons (the team is "worn out", in the magazine's words to German news agency dpa), and the editorial archive has gone to the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, a major German literary archive. There are no reverts and no vandalism. One open question remains: the article says both "print edition" ending 8 Dec and the whole "magazine" ending at year's end, so it is still unclear whether anything will continue online.

stories.headline: New account keeps blanking Lalpura conviction, now says High Court quashed case without a source
stories.summary: Hotmani singh, a single-purpose account with 4 edits, has now made four removals on the en-wiki article on AAP MLA Manjinder Singh Lalpura. Three different patrollers have reverted them: Komethere, Dr vulpes and Pattersonuwu. The new edits go further than the earlier ones. Rev 1381214985 renamed the section "Convicted in molestation charges" to just "charges" and deleted its text: the Sept 11, 2025 conviction by a Tarn Taran court in a 2013 case about molesting and assaulting a Dalit teenager, the arrest, and the four-year sentence. That text cited Indian Express, Hindustan Times and Times of India. Rev 1381215856 removed the conviction sentence from the lead again. Its edit summary claims the Chandigarh High Court has quashed the FIR and acquitted Lalpura. Pattersonuwu restored everything in rev 1381215935. The quash/acquittal claim is the one possible news hook here, but the editor gave no source, and nobody else on any language wiki has picked it up. Treat it as an unverified assertion, not a reported event, though it's worth checking whether there's been a High Court ruling or appeal. The TMI Episcopal edits are unrelated. An anonymous temporary account added small unsourced bits, such as "College Like Campus" (rev 1381214307), and they were reverted. Dr vulpes patrolling both pages is the only link.

stories.headline: Vandalism on da.wiki page for football coach Nils Nielsen, rolled back twice
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. All four edits to the Danish article on football coach Nils Kromann Nielsen came from one temporary account (~2026-56139-04), each with the comment "ikke noget" ("nothing"). The edits added junk text above the infobox ("puhadada 67 67 67…", "johan stinker") and changed the infobox name to "67". Editors E-Turner and Hjart each rolled the account back, and the article is now back to its earlier clean version. None of the edits touch his career, his status or any recent event. Other language versions did not move. The trigger may be the "67" meme. There is no real-world news here.

stories.headline: Vandalism on 4 unrelated enwiki pages, incl. 24kGoldn, all reverted; Long Beach rant
stories.summary: This cluster is routine counter-vandalism on four unrelated English pages. No languages other than English and no shared topic. 24kGoldn: a temporary account (~2026-56137-42) added junk ("Ruby", "Ruby Rasmussen Violet", "24KGoldn") to the infobox, the discography table and the short description. I read Augmented Seventh's Interceptor revert 1381096896, and it puts back both the infobox and the broken discography rows. That answers the open question in the earlier 24kGoldn brief. A later revert (1381097075) removed the short-description prefix. Dumb and Dumber: CraverG added joke lines about Biden/Harris and "the women from The View". Smallestredboy reverted the first and ClueBot NG the second. Oxgangs (Edinburgh): Toji4 pasted anime quotes (Jujutsu Kaisen) and small "clean" edits, reverted by ClueBot NG and Augmented Seventh. Long Beach, Mississippi: a temporary account (~2026-55982-71) twice added unsourced complaints to the article's opening paragraph that the city became "one big HOA" through Ordinance 676, which limits where campers can be parked on residential property. RadioactOlive and Augmented Seventh reverted both. That suggests a real but small local dispute over a city ordinance, which the edits don't verify and which isn't news on a wire scale. All damage appears reverted, so no follow-up is needed.

stories.headline: Jackie Shroff article: birthplace naming tweak reverted; routine upkeep
stories.summary: A temporary account changed the infobox birthplace of Indian actor Jackie Shroff from "Bombay, Bombay State" to "Mumbai, Maharashtra" (rev 1381069988, "Fixed incorrect info"). Established editor Drmies reverted it within about a minute, noting that Bombay/Bombay State was the correct name at his 1957 birth. That follows the usual Wikipedia practice of using historical place names. Fylindfotberserk then made a small +24 "restored sourced" fix to the early-life paragraph (rev 1381070342). The diff I read shows the 1 Feb 1957 Bombay birth details unchanged, so the exact restored text is unclear from the excerpt. Nothing points to a real-world event, an edit war or a vandalism spree. It is a common place-name fix plus regular maintenance.

stories.headline: Richard Riehle's article updated after reported death at 78; editors refine details
stories.summary: Editors are tidying the English Wikipedia article on character actor Richard Riehle ('Office Space'). Before this burst of edits, the article already said he died in Los Angeles on October 15, 2026, aged 78. That line cites a TMZ report dated October 19, 2026. Of the three edits I read, the first (rev 1381069006) added "at his home" and "from natural causes", with no new source; the second (rev 1381069789) is a copyedit; the third (rev 1381070648) adds a 1975 uncredited role in Rooster Cogburn to his filmography, the usual career fill-in after a death. There are no reverts and no pages in other languages moving, and the edits come from three different accounts. What's uncertain: the death rests on one tabloid source in the article, the cause of death has no citation, and I could not see when the original death sentence was added.

stories.headline: Bots revert vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Mar Mediterráneo'; no new edits
stories.summary: This repeats the earlier brief, and nothing new has happened. The five edits on es:Mar Mediterráneo are one vandal and two bots cleaning up. They are not tied to any real-world event. In rev 175917641 (-4,459 bytes), user Michiuwuinsano deleted the hatnotes and infobox. They also changed the opening sentence to the self-referential "viste que se puede editar cata michiuwuinsano del mundo". Automoderador undid it in rev 175917644 about 10 seconds later. SeroBOT had already undone Michiuwuinsano's first two edits (rev 175917608). The scout saw "no reverts" because the revert flag wasn't set, but the edit comments show these were reverts. The graph shows no edits after the bot revert, and no other language versions or editors are involved. The page looks restored, though the account could come back.

stories.headline: De-wiki self-promo page "Eisbaer Records" in speedy deletion; edit history now gone
stories.summary: This repeats an already-tracked routine item. There is no news here. There are 5 edits on a single de-wiki page, with no reverts and no versions in other languages. The page was created by StefanDimitrij, a 3-edit account whose name matches the founder the article names. The article's intro says Eisbaer Records is a music label founded on 20.10.2026 by Stefan Dimitrij Porcio ("DJ resaca"). M2k~dewiki then added a category, and the experienced patroller Horst Gräbner filed a speedy-deletion request ("SLA"). There has been no new activity since the prior brief. When I tried to re-read revisions 271487144 and 271487245, Wikipedia said both no longer exist. That fits the page having been deleted, though I couldn't confirm it, since a cached page summary still loads. I'm citing no diffs because I couldn't read any. The description of the edits relies on the dossier's edit comments and the prior brief.

stories.headline: Vandalism on 'Mabel Freer' article reverted quickly; no news event
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Mabel Freer saw one burst of vandalism. She was a British woman kept out of Australia in 1936 on morality grounds. A new account, Occwarior (2 edits in total), changed the key year from 1936 to 1967, which also mislabelled the Immigration Restriction Act 1901 as 'Act 1967'. The same edit added a racial slur to a section heading, and a second edit renamed 'Relationship with Edward Dewar' to 'Relationship with Donald Trump.' Cannolis, an established patroller, reverted both edits within about a minute, citing WP:VANDAL. The only other edit, by ITBF about 15 minutes earlier, was a small rewording in the legacy section. None of this points to a real-world event about the historical subject. It looks like ordinary vandalism that has already been cleaned up.

stories.headline: Chido Obi page: two vandal edits reverted, no new activity
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened. The graph still shows only the same four revisions on en.wiki's Chido Obi article. In rev 1381151892, a temporary account changed his "commonly known as" name to "Mathias Hartling". Materialscientist reverted it about 40 seconds later. In rev 1381152110 (summary "vggkgnlrg"), a second temporary account deleted his bolded full name and added the Danish-language nonsense "karlpeterjuul er enn svensker" into the career paragraph. ClueBot NG reverted that about 4 seconds later. Neither edit changed any facts about his club or his loan (Willem II, on loan from Manchester United). No other languages or pages moved. This is low-level vandalism, not a news event.

stories.headline: Violent Typhoon Champi enters Philippine area, named "Rosal" by PAGASA
stories.summary: Editors of the English "2026 Pacific typhoon season" article added the local Philippine name "Rosal" for Typhoon Champi (29W/2630). The edit comment says the name was assigned by PAGASA, which normally means the storm has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility (rev 1381115946; the season table was changed to match in rev 1381117310). The table lists Champi as a "Violent typhoon" active since October 11, with 10-minute winds of 105 kn and a pressure of 935 hPa, affecting Micronesia and the Mariana Islands; damage and deaths are given as unknown. The storm history (rev 1381116026, a capitalization fix) traces its growth from a JMA depression on October 11 to a typhoon on October 16, with the US military forecaster (JTWC) reporting rapid intensification and 1-minute winds of at least 120 kn. The page is lively (3 editors, 5 edits, no reverts) but this is a real, developing weather event, not an edit war or vandalism. Some things are uncertain: no other-language pages have moved yet, the Philippine-entry inference rests on an edit comment rather than a quoted bulletin, and the edits so far are minor (naming and formatting), with no reported landfall or impacts.

stories.headline: Swedish Wikipedia vandal moves from Fidel Castro to Birán and Margaret Thatcher
stories.summary: This is vandalism by one person, not news. A single temporary account (~2026-56131-63) vandalised the sv-wiki Fidel Castro article twice. Rev 59783728 changed his name from "Alejandro" to "Dildojandro". Rev 59783741 added a crude ASCII phallus after the sentence about his death, under an edit summary that falsely said it added childhood information. Both edits were undone within about 1–2 minutes by Nirmos (rollback) and Harka (undo). The scout's note says there were no reverts, but that's wrong: the graph's revert flag is false, yet both edit summaries show they were reverts. The graph also shows the account spreading to other pages. It made two earlier edits to Birán, Castro's birthplace (revs 59783720/59783723). Those revisions can no longer be fetched, which suggests they were deleted or hidden, but I can't confirm why. Its latest edit, rev 59783758 on Margaret Thatcher, was labelled as fixing a small grammar error. In fact it added one ("kom att bli" → "kom till att bli"), and the graph shows no revert yet. There is no real-world event and no other language involved. The Thatcher edit is probably still live and may need reverting.

stories.headline: Sofía Casanova es-wiki: unsourced "Ameli Paz" pseudonym re-added, reverted again by bot
stories.summary: This updates the earlier vandalism brief. Since then, two more edits hit the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Sofía Casanova (Galician journalist, 1861–1958), and the page has once again been reverted to its previous state. The same temporary account that tried to add the pseudonym "AMELIA PAZ" to the infobox (rev 175916232) came back about 90 seconds later. This time it added a loose sentence, "Le llamaban Ameli Paz" ("They called her Ameli Paz"), with no source and no edit summary (rev 175916249). SeroBOT reverted it within two seconds (rev 175916251). The earlier temporary account changed her death year from 1958 to 2030 (rev 175916213) and then undid it itself. In total that makes six edits from two temporary accounts plus the bot, all on one page in one language, and all undone. The repeated pseudonym attempt is persistent but it is not a news event. I have nothing that supports or rules out the pseudonym.

stories.headline: Fa.wiki "Call of Duty" page: joke edits about a private gamer, auto-reverted
stories.summary: The large churn on the Persian Wikipedia article on the Call of Duty series (ندای وظیفه) came from vandalism that a bot reverted, not from a real rewrite. Within about 30 seconds, two temporary accounts added joke text naming a private person, "Mehdi Farhang Fard". One edit put him into the developer field of the infobox as "father of CoD" and called him "one of the best players". The other added a section calling him "father of CoD in Iran and the world" whose friend gave him the Milad Tower, cited to his "memoir book". The edit comments say he is a big CoD streamer. Dexbot's AI-based anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) reverted all of it 12 seconds later, which restored the earlier text. Nothing points to a real-world event. The two temporary accounts may be the same person or friends.

stories.headline: De-wiki 'Jean Zacklad': temporary accounts' hard-coded interwiki links rolled back
stories.summary: All four edits are about one interlanguage link, not the subject's life. Within about four minutes, two different temporary accounts (~2026-56165-19 and ~2026-56138-50) each added a hard-coded Spanish link to the German article: first [[es:Jean Zacklade]], then [[es:Jean Zacklad]]. Both edit summaries asked someone to add the link on Wikidata instead ("bitte auf Wikidata setzen"). Each time, Carol.Christiansen undid the edit with a rollback, which fits de-wiki's practice of keeping language links on Wikidata rather than in the article text. The graph did not mark these edits as reverts, but the diffs and rollback summaries show that they are. No article content changed and no biographical news is involved. This looks like a good-faith editor, or the same person on two temporary accounts, who wants a newly created Spanish article linked. It is not vandalism or an edit war.

stories.headline: Swedish list update: Moderates win outright majority in Staffanstorp; a Skåne seat count corrected
stories.summary: The same registered editor, Berneblads, made three more edits to the Skåne section of the Swedish Wikipedia list of municipal and regional governments for 2026–2030. In rev 59783221 a blank row becomes a Moderate (M) government in Staffanstorp with 22 of 41 seats, an outright majority. The source is a 100.se analysis titled "Egen (M)ajoritet i Staffanstorp", retrieved 20 Oct 2026. Revs 59783217 and 59783219 change a 51-seat row from "25 av 51" to "23 av 51 (minoritet)" and then to "24 av 51 (minoritet)". This is most likely Vellinge, which was entered earlier as M with 25 of 51, so that council would be a minority government, not a majority. The diffs don't show the municipality name, so the Vellinge link is my inference. There are no reverts and no other editors involved: this is routine filling-in and self-correction after the September 2026 local elections, and Staffanstorp is the only new fact.

stories.headline: New de.wiki bio of hip-hop journalist Niko Backspin tagged for speedy deletion
stories.summary: The large delta is not a rewrite. A temporary account created a new German Wikipedia article on Niko "Backspin" Hüls, a Hamburg hip-hop journalist and owner of Backspin magazine (+5,620 bytes, edit comment "page didn't exist yet, relevant entry"). The draft is badly formatted: section headings in capitals, bare [n] citation markers and only two real ref tags. It reads like a promotional profile, citing a Serviceplan newsroom post and the Innings baseball magazine site. Within about 2 minutes, patroller SK Sturm Fan added a speedy-deletion request ({{SLA|kein Artikel}}, meaning "not an article"). A third editor, Carol.Christiansen, followed with another edit marked "SLA"; I couldn't load that diff, so I don't know exactly what it changed. This is routine new-page patrol of a likely self-promotional or poorly formatted article, with no real-world news event behind it.

stories.headline: Adam Wolke article: style tussle over birth/death symbols; 18 Oct death date still unsourced
stories.summary: Since the last brief there have been only two edits to the de-wiki biography of streamer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV"), and both are about style, not facts. The temporary account that added the unsourced 18 Oct death date (~2026-56226-19) switched the lead from "geb. … †" to the standard German genealogical symbols "* … †" (271493181). Horst Gräbner undid this within about 4 minutes, saying the article had been created without those symbols (271493236). Neither edit touched the death date, so "18. Oktober 2026" has now been through several editors' hands without challenge. It still has no source, and the cited press reports are dated 20 Oct. A correction to the previous brief: Berghest's −5 edit (271493024) did not tidy the infobox. It turned "SkylineTV Live" in the body text into a wikilink to [[SkylineTV]]. There were no reverts tagged as such, everything is on one page in one language, and the same person reverting style changes looks like article ownership, not an edit war. The core claim (died October 2026, aged 36, brain haemorrhage) hasn't changed. Open question: the exact date of death.

stories.headline: Routine: one editor expands fa-wiki article on Iranian town Ajabshir; joke edit reverted by bot
stories.summary: The churn on Persian Wikipedia's article on Ajabshir, a town in East Azerbaijan province, Iran, is almost all from one registered editor, Ohmygod211112, who made about 30 edits. They are building out the article. One edit adds a census table for Ajabshir County covering 1385, 1390 and 1395 (2006, 2011 and 2016), with references (rev 44790376). Another adds a sourced section on local Shab-e Yalda (winter solstice night) customs (rev 44791099). The only other human edit was a joke from a temporary account: it rewrote the opening sentence as a pun on the town's name ("ajab" means wonder, "shir" means lion), with the edit summary "without surprise and without lion" (rev 44791073). The anti-vandalism bot Dexbot reverted it within about 30 seconds. Nothing in these edits points to a real-world event, and no other language versions or pages are involved.

stories.headline: Racist vandalism on Swedish 'Romer' (Roma) article cleaned up; no new edits since
stories.summary: No change since the last brief: the latest round of vandalism on svwiki "Romer" (the Roma people) has been rolled back, and nothing has been edited since. In rev 59783263, temporary account ~2026-56015-41 put a racial slur and nonsense text at the start of the lead under the comment "lite text". It changed this to "c4Romer" (rev 59783267), and Tekannan restored the clean lead in rev 59783274, which I read. A graph query found no edits to the page after that rollback (ts 1792481480). So the burst of about 15 minutes by three temporary accounts, each rolled back by established patrollers, seems to be over. This matches earlier briefs: it's targeted anti-Roma trolling with no real-world event behind it. Still unknown: whether the three accounts are one person, and whether the page will be protected. I suggest folding this story into the existing Romer vandalism story.

stories.headline: Lil Keed article: minor vandalism by one account, reverted twice
stories.summary: This isn't news. One account, "6ix9ine Diddy Lover", added unsourced text to the English Wikipedia article on the late rapper Lil Keed twice. Both edits were changes to the line about his family. The first called his brother Lil Gotit "younger and heavier", with the edit summary "needed extra details". The second invented a twin brother named "Christian Boultan". Two other editors, Rencoolguy and Smallestredboy, reverted each edit within minutes, and the article is back to its earlier text. No other language versions moved, and nothing in the edits points to a real-world event. Judging by the edits and the username, this is an attention-seeking or joke account, not an edit war.

stories.headline: US midterms page adds report that Iran stalled talks to sway the vote, plus GOP-distancing analysis
stories.summary: Three registered editors made four additive edits to en:2026 United States elections within about 17 minutes. There were no reverts and no activity on other pages or languages. Pachu Kannan added a report, credited to Reuters and published by the Times of Israel on 20 Oct 2026, that senior Iranian officials said Tehran deliberately dragged out talks with the US to weaken Trump before the November midterms. He also changed the lead to say the Iran war was driven partly by "prolonged diplomatic talks". In the same edit he changed "the ongoing conflict with Iran" to "the conflict with Iran". The new text also says officials expected fighting to resume, which may mean active hostilities have paused, but I have not confirmed this elsewhere in the graph. Emperorpenguinn extended a paragraph about vulnerable Republicans (Rogers, Hinson) distancing themselves from the war; their earlier text cites Trump's 32% Reuters/Ipsos approval. Re000searchist added material on Trump criticising his election advisers to a section on Democrats leading the polls. These are ordinary, sourced campaign-coverage updates rather than a breaking event or a dispute. The one fresh news item is the Iranian officials' claim, which is a single-source report of what the officials said.

stories.headline: 'Deaths in 2026' list adds Grimau, Kruusa, Suárez, Majidzadeh, Lee Kwan-young
stories.summary: This is routine upkeep of English Wikipedia's 'Deaths in 2026' list. Several editors (Rigg, Folengo, Normantas Bataitis, CAWylie and others) are adding obituary entries, each backed by a foreign-language news source. New entries: Argentine actor Antonio Grimau, 82 (Canal26, Oct 20). Estonian poet and translator Kalju Kruusa, 53 (Delfi, 20th). Mexican telenovela actor Carlos Miguel Suárez (López-Dóriga, 19th). Iranian archaeologist Yusef Majidzadeh, 90 (ISNA). South Korean taekwondo grandmaster Lee Kwan-young, 80 (French taekwondo federation). There are no reverts or disputes, only small cleanups. The -155 removal from the 19th and the +155 addition to the 17th by the same editor are probably Majidzadeh's entry being moved to the correct date, but I couldn't load that diff to confirm. None of these deaths shows a cluster of related page activity, so none looks like breaking news on its own.

stories.headline: Persian Wikipedia bio of Kermanshah academic rewritten in apparent self-promotion, then flagged for deletion
stories.summary: The page is a small Persian Wikipedia biography of Alireza Shahrestani, a literature researcher and university lecturer in Kermanshah. In rev 44793349, editor Saeedmgh replaced the sourced, modest stub with a promotional rewrite: a new infobox and a lead calling him a professor, author and media activist who writes on resistance literature and on statements by the Islamic Revolution's leaders. The pasted text still carried leftovers from a chat or messaging export, including a sender line "A Shahrestani, [29/07/1405 09:04]" and a note that the material had been formatted "so you can upload it directly to Wikipedia". That suggests the subject, or someone working for him, supplied it, i.e. a likely conflict of interest. Rev 44793350 then removed those leftover lines. About 15 minutes later, Golpeti nominated the article for timed deletion for lacking sources that show notability (rev 44793368). I see no real-world news event here, only a routine conflict-of-interest and notability cleanup with no reverts or edit war. I didn't read the two smaller follow-up edits (0 and −40 bytes).

stories.headline: Update: Amancio Ortega es.wiki vandalism continues, partly reverted; earlier damage remains
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked vandalism story on the Spanish Wikipedia article about Amancio Ortega. It is still not news. Temporary account ~2026-56117-82 made two more edits to "Vida personal". The first added the political taunt "VIVA ESSSSPÑA Y VOTA PISOE" (rev 175914213). The second replaced his mother's name with an obscene insult about a brothel (rev 175914226). Registered editor Geom reverted both about 26 seconds later (rev 175914235). The Scout's "no reverts" note is wrong again. Geom's revert only went back to the last version by the other vandal, ~2026-56131-46. So the diff of the revert still shows the father listed as "Antonio jackson Rodríguez" and the birthplace province as "provincia de peruanos". From the diffs, the heading and Filantropía insults reported earlier also appear to still be on the page, though I haven't checked the current page directly. The graph shows no edits after Geom's revert, which suggests the page needs a deeper revert to a clean version and possibly protection.

stories.headline: es:Balonmano vandalism reverted; infobox back to 'Balonmano', no new edits since
stories.summary: This updates the prior vandalism brief. It is not a news event. After DonMaiquol's last edit (rev 175930974), the infobox 'nombre' field read "Ñavi Chaquetero Calienta Banquillos", an insult aimed at a named person. Patroller LMLM then undid that edit and the one before it in rev 175930993, putting the field back to "Balonmano". The graph shows no edits to the page after that revert, so the page currently looks clean. The pattern hasn't changed: one vandal using two near-identical accounts (Domnmaiquol and DonMaiquol), insults aimed at what look like local Catalan handball players, and a single patroller reverting. It is still one page in one language. The page could still be hit again, since the graph doesn't show whether the account was blocked or the page protected.

stories.headline: 49ers reportedly release DL Naquan Jones; Wikipedia page updated
stories.summary: Two temporary-account editors updated the en-wiki page for nose tackle Naquan Jones to say the San Francisco 49ers have released him. The first edit (rev 1381234638, "Released by 49ers.") removed the 49ers as his current team and changed his tenure to 2026 only. That edit still stands. The second editor added a sentence saying he was released on October 20, 2026, and gave a NBC Sports/ProFootballTalk link ("49ers-release-dl-naquan-jones"), but only in the edit summary, not as a citation in the article. A patroller reverted that sentence as an "unsourced addition to BLP" (biography of a living person). That is a sourcing-procedure revert, not a dispute over whether the release happened. Jones had signed with the 49ers on September 23, 2026. This is a routine NFL roster move, not an edit war or vandalism. I haven't independently checked the ProFootballTalk link.

stories.headline: Tamil film "Ayodhya" article sees cooperative cleanup after speedy keep
stories.summary: This is routine Wikipedia upkeep with no real-world news angle. It continues the tracked story in which the 2005 Tamil film article was nominated for deletion and then closed as a speedy keep. After the keep, Kailash29792 brought back an empty Production section marked as needing expansion (rev 1381269569). Minutes later the nominator, DareshMohan, filled it with one sourced sentence: the film was R. Jayaprakash's directorial debut, and he had earlier co-produced Love Channel (2001). The sources are the Chennai Online review and a RajVideoVision YouTube clip (rev 1381269611). DareshMohan then made a small cast-list edit, adding a wikilink for Bava Lakshmanan (rev 1381269813). Three registered editors worked together, with no reverts, no anonymous edits and no other language versions involved, which matches the scout's read.

stories.headline: Pertes de Thémines (fr-wiki): editor expands karst sinkhole article; routine, nothing to report
stories.summary: The burst on the French article about the Pertes de Thémines, a set of karst swallow-holes in the Lot department, is routine article-building. Nearly all of the churn comes from Thierry46, who is filling in "Situation et accès" and "Risques" sections that had been placeholders ({{...}}). His additions are sourced to a 2006 CDS46 caving inventory and the CDS46 website. The new text covers where the site is (about 8 swallow-holes spread over 300 m, near the mairie). It also covers access rules: the site was protected by prefectoral order on 27 August 1986, a municipal order sets the access conditions, and visits are banned when the flood gauge is above 30 cm. It also notes the risks of falling and drowning in a flood. No text was removed except placeholders and a maintenance banner. Ariel Provost and Père Igor made small copyedits. There were no reverts and no sign that a real-world event, such as a flood or an accident, set this off. The flood-safety wording describes standing rules, not an incident.

stories.headline: Catalan Wikipedia bio of philosopher Fernando Savater hit by schoolyard vandalism
stories.summary: The four edits on the Catalan Wikipedia article on Fernando Savater are vandalism, not news. Two temporary accounts added crude Spanish-language insults about apparent schoolmates ("Nicolas", "gaddiel") to the opening sentence (revs 38981159 and 38981172). That sentence was already defaced before this cluster started: it renames him "Joan Pezza Martín", calls him a Peruvian from "67 BC" and adds scatological text. Editor Mmen6 reverted the first addition and then reverted their own revert 30 seconds later (rev 38981165). Because of that self-revert, and because the earlier damage was never touched, the vandalized lead is still live. No other language versions or real-world facts are involved. The edit graph didn't flag any of these as reverts, so the scout's "no reverts" was misleading. The page needs cleanup back to an older clean revision.

stories.headline: Helen Haines article now sources double amputation to 7News report quoting her husband
stories.summary: The open question from our last brief is now answered. MrActiniuM's rev 1381282053 ("Added reference", +416 bytes) attached a 7News report, via MSN and dated 21 October 2026, to the body sentence "Both her legs were amputated as a result of the attack". The report is headlined "Helen Haines' husband Phil reveals surgeons have amputated both of MP's legs injured in alleged attack". I confirmed this by reading the 'before' text of the next revision. That means the two-leg amputation is no longer unsourced: a named outlet reports it, citing her husband. Until now the claim rested only on temporary-account edits and an ABC headline saying "loses leg". MrActiniuM followed with rev 1381282561 ("Added more references", +428 bytes) in the same paragraph. That diff was cut off, so I can't say which extra sources it adds. There have been no new edits since then and no reverts, and no other language editions are linked in the graph. Remaining caveats: the 7News claim is secondhand (the husband, via MSN), and I have not read the outlet's text itself.

stories.headline: Routine cleanup of German Wikipedia bio of Japanologist Sven Saaler; no news hook
stories.summary: This is maintenance work on the German Wikipedia article about Sven Saaler, a German historian and Japanologist (doctorate from Bonn in 1999, later at the German Institute for Japanese Studies in Tokyo). Three established editors made 5 edits in about 9 minutes, with no reverts. I read four of the diffs. Tom md changed quotation marks and wiki links. Kurator71 cleaned up the formatting and redundant links, turned the career list into prose ("Liste ausformuliert"), and added a {{Belege fehlen}} tag, which flags the article for missing sources (comment: "Belege?"). AHZ made a small 8-byte follow-up that I didn't read. None of the edits add news, such as an appointment, award, death or controversy. The page has no linked articles in other languages, and the article reads like a recently created CV-style bio getting its first quality review. I'm not certain the article is new: the graph only shows edits from this session onward.

stories.headline: Hebrew 'First Zionist Congress' article hit by two vandalism edits, both reverted
stories.summary: The Scout's guess of a major expansion is wrong. This was two separate rounds of vandalism on the Hebrew Wikipedia article about the First Zionist Congress (Basel, 1897), and both were undone quickly. First, a temporary account (~2026-56263-10) put a crude word ("פלוץ", meaning "fart") into the lead sentence about the 208 delegates. Ori reverted it about 40 minutes later. Then Galmyst, an account with only this one edit, deleted about 4 KB of sourced background text: Herzl's choice of venue and the Munich Jewish community's opposition, cited to Avineri and Elon. Galmyst replaced it with keyboard mash ("sdcsccs", "dds", "njcrhu"). אריאל ר. restored the text in full about 9 minutes later. The "8153 churn" figure is just the 4,072-byte deletion plus the 4,072-byte restore, not new content. Nothing ties this to any real-world news, and no other-language versions of the article were part of the story.

stories.headline: Sergen Yalçın named Turkey coach; edits spread to national-team pages, contract now "signed"
stories.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked story; the editing activity is the same event, not a new one. Four registered tr-wiki editors (Hakanp, Eemirrgs, -Fatih-, 2020mustafat03) made 13 edits to Sergen Yalçın's biography, with no reverts. The added section cites a TFF announcement, "A Millî Takımımızın Yeni Teknik Direktörü Sergen Yalçın", saying the federation appointed him on 20 October 2026. Since the last brief, Eemirrgs changed the contract wording from "will be signed" to "imzalandı" (signed). That change is the editor's own and has no new source, so the signing is still not confirmed. Hakanp added an empty Turkey row (0 matches) to the career statistics. The update has also spread beyond the biography: Eemirrgs filled the empty coach field on the tr-wiki Turkey national team infobox, and on the 2026 season page added Yalçın "from 20 October 2026" after Vincenzo Montella, whose spell ended 9 October. That supports the earlier finding that the job was vacant. Coverage is still thin: no languages beyond tr and en, and I have not checked the TFF page itself.

stories.headline: New de-wiki article on Indian slide guitarist Barun Kumar Pal; routine cleanup follows
stories.summary: Toolittle created a new German Wikipedia biography of Barun Kumar Pal (rev 271491432 and earlier; creation rev 271491291, +3,752 bytes). It describes him as an Indian guitarist, born 1948 in Dhaka, a student of Ravi Shankar and a pioneer of the Hansa Veena / Indian classical slide guitar. It also includes a discography, sources and authority-control data. Within a few minutes, two experienced editors made small fixes. M2k~dewiki corrected a typo in the MusicBrainz ID (rev 271491425), and ZweiteWurzelAus16 made spacing changes. None of the text mentions anything happening right now, such as a death, award or event. It reads as a translated or compiled profile based on artist-profile sites. There are no reverts, and the graph shows no linked pages in other languages. The edits look like normal article creation and upkeep, not news. One caveat: something off-wiki could have prompted the article, but the edits show no sign of it.

stories.headline: Pfeffer obituary article: career detail added, unsourced birth date removed; no new event
stories.summary: These are follow-up edits to the new German article on former ZDF sports commentator Michael Pfeffer. Nothing new has been reported about his death. Berghest expanded the career section (+397): Pfeffer commentated the Olympic debut of ski cross at Vancouver 2010, citing the Allgäuer Zeitung, and covered boxing and cycling at Summer Games. Berghest then fixed typos. Fcsch added an exact birth date, 15 June 1959, citing "private knowledge" (private Kenntnis). Horst Gräbner reverted it to "1958 or 1959" a minute later, pointing to the biography guideline (WP:BIO) and asking for a reputable source. That was a single policy-based correction, not a back-and-forth, so I don't count it as an edit war. M2k added the standard person-data block (Personendaten), which records the death as September 2026 in Rio de Janeiro. The article now says September everywhere, but that date still rests mainly on a blog post (URL dated 2026/09), while the Stern source noted in the earlier brief is dated 21 Oct 2026. So the month is still not firmly confirmed.

stories.headline: Malala Yousafzai es-wiki churn is reverted vandalism; no new activity, no news
stories.summary: This is the same Spanish-language Wikipedia vandalism episode already on file. It is not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56153-82 typed keyboard-mash into the lead ("mhgcvbh") and garbled sentences (rev 175916488, -358 bytes). It then deleted the infobox and large parts of the biography (rev 175916540, -932). Patroller Arjuno3, SeroBOT and Automoderador undid every edit. Their edit comments say "Revertido/Revertida", so these were reverts even though the graph did not flag them. That explains the scout's "no reverts" note, and the 2,326-byte churn is just damage and repair cancelling out. Earlier, a separate temporary account (rev 175916304) changed a vandalised "877 hermanos" (siblings) back to "2". The same sentence still calls her mother "Torpe" ("clumsy" in Spanish), which looks like leftover vandalism; her mother's name is Toor Pekai. The graph shows no edits after Automoderador's final revert, and it holds no versions of this article in other languages, so nothing points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Colts sign Morstead and Mecole Hardman to practice squad, release Eli Pancol
stories.summary: On October 20, 2026, the Indianapolis Colts made a three-player practice-squad move. They signed punter Thomas Morstead and wide receiver Mecole Hardman and released wide receiver Eli Pancol. Jeffrey34555 added a new Colts section to Morstead's article (1381231275) and set his infobox to Colts, practice squad, 2026–present (1381231164). Bluppyt789 then cited a Colts.com piece titled "Colts sign WR Mecole Hardman, P Thomas Morstead to practice squad; release WR Eli Pancol from practice squad" (1381231495). Bluppyt789 also added the same citation to Hardman's article with a Colts section (1381231010) and to Pancol's article with a line saying he was released from the practice squad (1381230899). Dark Dreaming added Colts roster navboxes to both Morstead and Hardman. None of the edits has been reverted, all are by registered accounts, and three player pages tell the same story with the same source. The scout read this right: these are routine follow-up roster edits, and nothing new has happened since the last brief. I did not open the Colts.com article myself, so the details depend on the citation title.

stories.headline: Katie Zacharia 'CCP' vandalism reverted; Montserrat link is a shared patroller, not the vandal
stories.summary: This corrects the previous brief. The edit by ~2026-56098-08 that changed "international practice team" to "CCP massaging team" is no longer live. CreativeLibrary460 reverted it about 25 seconds later (rev 1381249498), returning the page to A. Randomdude0000's clean version. There have been no edits to Katie Zacharia since then. The Montserrat page is in this cluster only because the same anti-vandalism patroller, CreativeLibrary460, worked both pages. The vandal is not the same account. A different temporary account, ~2026-56262-12, twice added a string of Turkish city names ("Turkey Ankara Adana Tarsus Mersin Antalya İzmir") to Montserrat's short description (rev 1381249991). CreativeLibrary460 reverted it once and TonySt reverted it again with Interceptor (1381250125). Both pages are clean now. This is unrelated, low-level vandalism on English Wikipedia only, with no sign of a real-world event. The Zacharia news itself (her ouster after five days) was already in the article. Semi-protecting the Zacharia page is still a reasonable precaution.

stories.headline: No story: patroller reverts unrelated junk edits on Roxy Dekker and November 19 pages
stories.summary: These two pages are only connected because one anti-vandalism patroller, MakaylaHippo1998, worked on both. There is no real-world event behind it. On Roxy Dekker, a temporary account (~2026-55566-40) twice added short Dutch fan text ("en is samen met koen", "en zongen samen liedjes") to the existing 2024 line about her relationship with Koen van Heest. MakaylaHippo1998 reverted the first edit and ClueBot NG the second. On November 19, two separate accounts added the same unsourced line saying Grand Theft Auto VI comes out that day in 2026. MakaylaHippo1998 and Cannolis reverted it for having no reliable source. Nothing here points to a birthday or event for Dekker. The GTA VI date may reflect a rumour or announcement circulating among gamers, but no source was given and I can't confirm it from these edits.

stories.headline: Griezmann's Norwegian page hit by 'Stranda IL' prank, now fully undone
stories.summary: This is vandalism on the Norwegian (no) article for Antoine Griezmann. It is not transfer news. Temporary account ~2026-56049-48 changed the visible name of the Atlético Madrid link to "stranda il", a small Norwegian club, and deleted the citation (rev 26006506). Patandor rolled that back to the last good version (26006508). About four minutes later, second temporary account ~2026-56193-92 made the same joke with "Stranda IL" (26006514). Update since the last brief: that same account reverted its own edit about 4 minutes later (26006517), so the link now reads "Atletico Madrid" and the citation is intact. The page has no linked articles in other languages (SAME_AS) in the graph, and only three editors were involved, so nothing points to a real-world event. The two temporary accounts may be the same person, but that can't be confirmed.

stories.headline: Creator keeps polishing new article on 2004 album "Nothing Is Cool"; still not news
stories.summary: This is still routine, and it's the same story as the earlier brief. The only page is the en-wiki article "Nothing Is Cool", a 2004 album by Canadian rappers Mcenroe and Birdapres. Since the last brief, the article's creator, Splashmoney15, has made three small edits. One filled in infobox details: recorded "2003–August 2004" and a running time of 56:07. It also realigned the infobox and fixed a tracklist title. The other two fixed the link and citation for the review in Now (it's a newspaper, not a magazine), removed a "disambiguation needed" tag, and repaired a closing bracket. There were no reverts and no other language versions were edited, and nothing in the text points to a current event. The only other editors, Jonesey95 and Vitorperrut555, did cleanup work, which was covered in the earlier brief.

stories.headline: Vandalism on five unrelated enwiki pages, all reverted; ISA Brown "H5" line is not a bird-flu signal
stories.summary: This is not a news event. Five unconnected accounts vandalised five English Wikipedia pages (Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, June, ISA Brown, Vittoria Ceretti, Mangar-kunjer-kunja). Each account touched only one page, and routine patrollers (Discospinster, Jiltedsquirrel, Mochabearr, Perpetually Blooming Rose) reverted every edit within minutes. I read the ISA Brown diffs again. BnkvfdolABEL first inserted gibberish ("developed the biggest thing ever it hangs and every thing") into the History section, then added the unsourced line "they do not like H5 it make them sick". Both were reverted. The earlier edit by Thenillalenape (−9 bytes) is a good-faith grammar fix ("has been developed" → "developed"). The graph has no other-language versions of ISA Brown, so there is no cross-language sign of a bird-flu story behind the H5 text. The findings on the other four pages come from earlier briefs and edit comments; I did not re-read those diffs.

stories.headline: New fr.wiki bio of Beninese Fa diviner tagged as possible paid/AI-written article
stories.summary: This isn't news. The 3,114-byte change is a brand-new fr.wiki article. User Fredoan published it from their personal draft (rev 240539428). It profiles Bokônon Gbêmadoyômin, a Beninese practitioner and teacher of Fa divination and Vodoun. The article lists talks he gave in Abomey-Calavi (January and May 2024) and an October 2025 event at the Biennale Euro-Africa in Montpellier, plus three books. Its only sources are two Bénin Intelligent articles and the event's own web page. Within minutes, two experienced patrollers added maintenance tags. NicoV added an {{Autobiographie}} tag with the edit summary "Contributions rémunérées" (paid contributions) (rev 240539548). Bertrand Labévue added an {{IA générative}} tag, flagging possible AI-written text (rev 240539829). The rest of the churn is ordinary new-page patrol, with no reverts and no other languages involved. Nothing here points to a real-world event. The article may be nominated for deletion later because it rests on few sources and looks promotional.

stories.headline: Thai Hell's Kitchen season 3 page gets routine episode-3 recap edits
stories.summary: Three registered editors (Jeabbabe, S49 Sola, ChefAddicts) are working on one thwiki article, Hell's Kitchen Thailand season 3, and every recent edit is in the "Episode 3" section. The diffs I read are fan recaps of a reality show that is airing now: dinner-service results, a khanom krok-inspired amuse-bouche challenge, dishes sent back, contestants thrown out of the kitchen, and changes to how the score tables are laid out. S49 Sola rearranged the recap into per-team bullet points. They also cut a few details, including a line saying contestant Chin admitted letting Jiffy win, and criticism of the blue team's undercooked oats. An unsourced note, based on social-media posts, says the head chefs served the dessert themselves off-camera. None of the edits are reverts, no other languages are involved, and none of the editors touched other pages. This is ordinary entertainment upkeep with no news value outside the show.

stories.headline: Nordderby vandalism continues: unsourced edit adds 6 HSV wins, not reverted
stories.summary: Update to the earlier Werder fan vandalism on de-wiki "Nordderby". Only one edit is new since the last brief: rev 271481748, by a different temporary account (~2026-56111-34), with no edit comment. It looks like a spacing cleanup of the infobox. But it also raises total competitive matches from 158 to 164 and HSV wins from 55 to 61. Draws (43), Werder wins (60) and the last match date (18 April 2026) are unchanged. The old figures added up exactly (55+43+60=158). Six extra HSV wins with no new match since that date is implausible. Coming about 15 minutes after the pro-Werder vandalism, this looks like a hidden pro-HSV reply rather than a real stats update. Unlike the earlier edits, it has not been reverted, and no edits have followed it. Uncertain: it could be a good-faith correction (e.g. adding cup or historical matches), but there is no source and only HSV's count moved. A human should check the head-to-head figures against a reliable source and revert if they're wrong. Nothing suggests a real-world event behind this.

stories.headline: Andrea Farri page: unsourced family edits keep coming; still no news
stories.summary: This still looks like routine low-quality editing on the article about the Italian film composer. Nothing suggests a real-world event. Brenno GEnti's edit (rev 1381156842) added unsourced names for Farri's father and children and a claim that actress Valentina D'Agostino is his wife, with a list of her films. The same edit removed the sourced line about his uncle Paolo Poli. Strongshorts' revert (rev 1381157148) only changed "good looking" back to "acclaimed", so the unsourced family details stayed on the page. One new edit came in since the last brief: Iamthebest28142, the same account whose "good looking" change was reverted, added "both born in rome" about the children (rev 1381158289), which piles more unsourced personal detail on top. Three accounts edited one page in one language, with no other activity in the graph. The pattern points to fans or acquaintances, not an award, a release or a death. The unsourced claims about living people are a cleanup issue, not news.

stories.headline: es.wiki vandalism: Apolo 11 joke removed by its author; Mazarulleque quote still altered
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It is schoolyard-style vandalism on two Spanish Wikipedia pages, and the only link between them is the bot Automoderador. Update on Apolo 11: KIRK676's crude made-up sentence about Armstrong and Aldrin (rev 175914330) was removed by KIRK676 himself in rev 175914523, which also fixed the missing full stop. The lead looks clean now. The earlier worry that Automoderador's revert had put the joke back is resolved. On Mazarulleque, temporary account ~2026-55888-86 made rev 175914437, which changes the quoted 1840s Madoz text from "112 casas pequeñas y de mala construcción" ("112 small, badly built houses") to "112 casa contruidas" ("112 house built", misspelled). No bot reverted it and there are no later edits in the graph, so the altered quote is probably still live and a human should fix it. Correction to the scout's note: the cluster has 12 edits, not 3, including bot reverts by Automoderador and SeroBOT. The existing story s_ad29d774 covers Mazarulleque, not Apolo 11. I recommend merging this story into s_ad29d774 instead of tracking it on its own.

stories.headline: Routine sourcing work on far-right biographies; Linder death claim rests on own website
stories.summary: This is routine editing, not a news event. One editor, PARAKANYAA, is expanding articles on related far-right figures. A 1981 Atlanta Journal clipping added to both pages shows that Ed Fields and Michael Thevis went to the same school (Marist School) and lived near each other (revs 1381262626, 1381262388). On Alex Linder, EncycloDeterminate re-added a death date of 27 June 2025. The only source is a "RIP Alex Linder" notice on alexlinder.com, and the edit summary says "No consensus was present", which points to an earlier dispute over that source (1381259528). The same editor added personal background sourced to an audio file on Linder's own site, Vanguard News Network (VNN) (1381262838). PARAKANYAA then tagged the article for unreliable and primary sources (1381262892). The edits cite sources dated October 2026, so the reported death is more than a year old and not breaking news. The open question is whether the death date can stand on a self-published source. There are no reverts yet, but the dispute on the Linder article could flare up again and is worth watching.

stories.headline: Swedish Van Gogh article: joke 'Rainbow Six Siege' insertions rolled back twice
stories.summary: This is minor vandalism, not a real-world story. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but that is wrong. A temporary account (~2026-56293-57) twice added a false claim to the Swedish Vincent van Gogh article: that Van Gogh "invented the concept" of the video game Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. The first time it went into the early-life paragraph (rev 59785406, +73 bytes). The second time it went into the lead (rev 59785413, +82 bytes). Two established editors, Adville (rev 59785409) and Gotogo (rev 59785418), each undid it with the rollback tool within about 5 minutes. The changes are small, and no other languages or pages are involved. The graph credits the temp account with 3 edits, but I only saw and read two of them.

stories.headline: Eurovision 2027 page logs Serbia's confirmation; Azerbaijan claim reverted over sourcing
stories.summary: This is routine upkeep of the participant list on en-wiki's "Eurovision Song Contest 2027" article. Tanvavad added Serbia (broadcaster RTS) to the table, citing an ESCkompakt "exclusive" dated 20 Oct 2026 saying Serbia confirmed it will take part in the contest in Burgas. That edit raised the entry count in the infobox from 32 to 33 (rev 1381174224). A few minutes later an anonymous editor changed the prose to match ("thirty-three countries"), a 2-byte consistency fix rather than vandalism (rev 1381181024). SpaceInferno1211 added what their edit summary called an "unofficial confirmation" of Azerbaijan's participation. Tanvavad reverted it because the source, eurovisionfun, is listed as unreliable for this page. That makes it a single sourcing dispute, not an edit war. Caveats: the Azerbaijan diff was cut off, so its content comes from the edit summary, and Serbia's confirmation rests on one fan-site report that I haven't checked against RTS or the EBU.

stories.headline: Cs-wiki schoolyard vandalism reaches 5 pages, now incl. Humanismus and Software; all reverted
stories.summary: The low-level vandalism on cs-wiki has spread from 'Kraje v Česku', 'Velká čínská zeď' and 'Komprese dat' to two more articles, 'Humanismus (ideologie)' and 'Software'. Nothing points to a news event. On Humanismus, temporary account ~2026-56078-61 twice cut text from the lead. One edit blanked the bolded title word and part of a sentence; the other chopped off the opening sentences. Kendo13 undid both within about 20 seconds to 2.5 minutes, with the summary 'bezdůvodné odstraňování obsahu' (unexplained removal of content). On Software, ~2026-56266-83 renamed the section 'Škodlivý software' (malicious software) to 'zlý software' (evil software), and Kendo13 undid it 12 seconds later. On Komprese dat, the earlier vandal ~2026-56121-92 came back with 'tibor je frajer' (Tibor is cool) and a 729-byte removal, both reverted. I couldn't load the text of those two Komprese diffs, so I'm going on the edit summaries and size changes. Every vandal edit comes from a different throwaway temporary account, falls within the same burst of roughly 15 minutes, and was reverted, mostly by Kendo13. Nobody restored anything after a revert, so this is not an edit war. The pattern looks like a few people, possibly one classroom, acting at the same time, but that is a guess. No other language versions were involved.

stories.headline: Richard J. Aldrich bio: routine sourcing cleanup, no news event (same as tracked story)
stories.summary: No new activity: the same four edits on the en-wiki biography of intelligence historian Richard J. Aldrich that an earlier brief already covered. A temporary account added an unsourced line saying he is "currently a professor at the University of Warwick as of 2026". Strongshorts reverted it within about 20 seconds using the Interceptor tool (rev 1381168696). Celjski Grad then undid two older edits by Deewitz. One removed a claim about a 2019 Leverhulme Trust Major Research Fellowship, with the summary "No such source" (rev 1381168860). The other removed a claim that he co-edits the Studies in Intelligence book series with Christopher Andrew and Claudia Hillebrand, and moved the sentence about his Warwick professorship since 2007 back into place (rev 1381168912). There was no back-and-forth reverting, no other pages or languages changed, and no sign of a real-world event. I can't tell whether the removed claims are false or just badly cited, since both relied on reused citations ("Warwick", "Warwick2").

stories.headline: Swedish 'Fall of the Roman Empire' article hit by small vandalism, rolled back
stories.summary: This is a one-page, sv-wiki only incident with no real-world news value. One temporary account (~2026-56166-67) made three edits within about 4 minutes. Each one swapped "Roman" for "Mango": the {{Romerska riket}} template became {{Mango Riket}}, and the hatnote "Romarrikets fall" became "Mangorikets Fall" twice. Two established editors undid every change with rollbacks: Nirmos twice, then Lars Törnqvist. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but the graph's revert flag simply missed them; the edit comments show these were rollbacks ("Rullade tillbaka"). The article is back to its previous version and I found no activity in other languages.

stories.headline: Minor ru-wiki vandalism on Magneto pages, all reverted by bot within seconds
stories.summary: This is low-level vandalism, not news. A temporary account (~2026-56428-88) made small changes to three ru-wiki Magneto/Erik Lensherr pages. It put "Элекс Мерсер" (Alex Mercer, a character from the Prototype video game) into the infobox "full name" field on Магнето (Marvel Comics). It also swapped the alias "Магнитный парень" for the same name on the Ultimate Marvel page, and made a 1-byte change to the film-series page. EyeBot reverted every edit within about 15–20 seconds, flagged by ORES/LWA scores. The Nagiev page is not about an actor or a dubbing role, as the scout guessed: it is about Anatoly Nagiev, a Soviet serial killer executed in 1982. A different temporary account (~2026-56244-26) cut his first name from "Анатолий" to "Атолий", and EyeBot reverted that too. Only 3 editors were involved (two temporary accounts plus the bot), not 8. The link between the Nagiev page and the Magneto pages looks like a coincidence of timing, but I can't rule out that it's the same person on two accounts.

stories.headline: India Asian Para Games page: athletics schedule filled in for 21 Oct, tally still 35
stories.summary: The three edits since the last brief add no new medals. Mr Gupta 18's +603 edit fills the athletics results tables with "21 Oct" final dates and n/a markers for events with no heats, which tells us more Indian athletes compete on 21 October. It also changes one class label from T62/64 to T64 (rev 1381170601). Neeelzzz20 fixed the "Denvender Kumar" typo the last brief flagged, so the medalists table now reads Devender Kumar (rev 1381169926). Balagurunaadha Velavan filled in two blank cells in the swimming table with the numbers 8 and 6, probably heat or rank placings (rev 1381170186). Nothing was reverted, and the infobox tally of 9 gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze (35 total) is unchanged. Edits are in English only. This is good-faith live tracking with no sign of vandalism or an edit war. Still open: the discus bronze mark is longer than the gold mark, and none of this has been checked against outside sources.

stories.headline: Dan Moore bio vandalized with fake death date, reverted; no roster move evident
stories.summary: The activity on Dan Moore (American football) is vandalism, not a transaction. Temporary account ~2026-56263-78 made two edits (1381225131, 1381225551). They inserted the middle name "Stalin", set his weight to 100,495,938, added insults ("one of the worst left tackles", "Moore being trash as usual"), changed his jersey number from 75 to 67, and added a fake death date (28 Dec 2026) with Nissan Stadium as the place of death. Patroller AriuCH reverted all of it to the last good version (1381226375). The actual roster facts on the page were left as they were: the March 2025 four-year, $82M contract with the Titans. The Jung Jae-kwang edit (1381225555) was an unrelated, unsourced addition of a 2026 series, "Take charge of my heart" (role: Choi do yoon), by a different temporary account. AriuCH removed it as unreferenced (1381225761). The only link between the two pages is that one patroller. This edit history gives no sign of a death, injury, or roster move.

stories.headline: 17 October riots: no new edits; casualty and arrest figures still unsourced
stories.summary: The scout flagged a burst of 3 editors, 4 edits and 1 revert, all in English. These are the same edits the 1792507204 brief already covered, and nothing has been edited on either tracked page since. In rev 1381183464, Whitesin21 changed French civilian injuries from "2,600" to "400+" in the infobox. The edit summary says there were 2,400 arrests, not injuries. The diff gives no source, and the 2,400 doesn't match the 2,600 that was removed, so treat both casualty and arrest numbers as unverified. The revert is Jeffrey34555 undoing his own edit, which had added "in France" to the lede (rev 1381183362). It is housekeeping, not an edit war.
