The linked French article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026" (134 edits) was last edited at ts 1792504943, adding photo galleries for Limoges and Marseille, so other languages show no new developments. Story status stays developing. Whether the Limoges town hall survived is still disputed on its article.

stories.headline: Small fa-wiki edits to 1973 Tehran derby and symphony orchestra pages, bot-reverted
stories.summary: Two unconnected Persian Wikipedia pages got small edits from two different temporary accounts, and the anti-vandalism bot Dexbot (Shahbaz system) reverted every change within about a minute. The pages are the 13th Tehran derby, a historical Persepolis vs Taj match played on 7 September 1973 (16 Shahrivar 1352), and the Tehran Symphony Orchestra. On the derby page one account added +94 and +71 bytes (one in the section "Tension in Taj's camp"). Dexbot then reverted it (−165 bytes) as suspected vandalism. On the orchestra page another account added 46 bytes to the "Conductors" section, also reverted. No human editor touches both pages, no other-language versions moved, and a 50-year-old match has no news hook. This looks like low-grade unsourced or test edits, not a real-world event. Caveat: the diff text could not be fetched, so the content of the edits is unverified. This assessment rests on metadata, edit summaries and the bot's revert reasons.

stories.headline: Cube Entertainment threat vandalism stays reverted; no new activity, not news
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. No edits have hit Cube Entertainment or Dustin Poirier since 420yeahh's revert (rev 1381242810). I checked the graph for anything after that timestamp and found nothing. That revert took out temp account ~2026-56501-62's text: abuse aimed at company staff, plus a violent, sexual threat against executive Ahn Woohyung and his family. The account made four vandal edits in total, and all four were reverted. The Poirier activity is separate, minor vandalism. Rev 1381242601 by ~2026-56286-41 changed his 2019 UFC 242 loss to Khabib Nurmagomedov (a rear-naked choke submission) into a false knockout win, and it was reverted as unsourced. Only English Wikipedia is involved, with three patrollers and no sign of any real-world event. Still to do: block the account, delete the threatening revisions, and possibly have admins review the threat. The Poirier edit should be split off from this story.

stories.headline: Update: French protest curfews article stable; 'European Spring' rename pushed twice, reverted
stories.summary: There is no new reporting on the ground. The most recent substantive edit is still rev 1381164999 (+364, citing Anadolu, 19 Oct). It adds the Gironde department's curfew for unaccompanied minors, 10pm–7am until 26 October, after looting and vandalism on 17 October. That sits alongside the existing text on curfews in Paris (République/Les Halles, 10pm–6am, applying to everyone), Lyon (9pm–6am, Presqu'île) and Nice (minors only). What is new since the last brief: the same temporary account (~2026-56100-21) tried a second time to rename the infobox to "European Spring" (rev 1381170749). Its edit summary says the movement is "spreading throughout Europe", but it adds no source. VocalCat2207 reverted with "Discuss first" (rev 1381170899). That is two rounds between one newcomer and one patroller, so it is a minor naming dispute, not an edit war. The claim that the protests are spreading across Europe has no sources and should not be treated as a real-world signal. The French-language article has seen almost no activity, and confirmation still depends on the cited outlets.

stories.headline: Harry Chester reverts are part of one temp account's link-style sweep, not news
stories.summary: The Harry Chester page has nothing new since the existing routine brief, and nothing here points to a real-world event. Temporary account ~2026-54405-06 twice changed the piped links to the monarchs, e.g. [[George III of the United Kingdom|King George III]] became King [[George III]]. The first try (rev 1381240372) included the typo "Kinga". Both versions were reverted, by 420yeahh and then Thomasfan1916. The only new finding settles the open question in the prior brief: the account is running the same link change across many British-history pages. Rev 1381241090 on The Opening of New London Bridge shows the identical William IV relinking. In about 90 minutes the same account made small negative-delta edits to roughly 15 other articles, including Portsmouth Harbour (painting), 2nd Royal Surrey Militia, Hercules Langford Rowley and William Hay, 19th Earl of Erroll. I read only the one cross-page diff, so it is an inference that the others are the same change. So far it has been reverted only on Harry Chester. This is not an edit war or vandalism, and it should be merged into the tracked routine story.

stories.headline: it.wiki Almo Violin edit war goes on as a second editor reverts a softened Vajont/SADE line
stories.summary: The dispute on Italian Wikipedia's bio of engineer Almo Violin is still going. That contradicts the Scout's "no reverts" note: the revert is in the comment (rev 152984828) but the graph didn't flag it. This time the diffs loaded, so we now know what the fight is about. Temporary accounts first added a "Nei media" section citing a 2015 Vajont documentary (rev 152984211). They then inserted a clause saying that as head of Belluno's Genio civile (the state civil-engineering office) Violin "fu malleabile per la SADE" ("was pliable for SADE", the private power company behind the dam) at the Vajont dam. Its only citation is a 1960 journal that appears to cover just his appointment (rev 152984655). Sayatek reverted that version twice. Another temp account (~2026-56095-14) then softened it to "lavorò per la SADE alla diga del Vajont" ("worked for SADE at the Vajont dam"), calling this "more correct and not denigratory" (rev 152984785). A second registered editor, Titore, reverted that too (rev 152984828). The article's existing text on his manslaughter conviction at first instance and later acquittal for insufficient evidence was never touched. The fight is over an unsourced claim that he served SADE's interests, which is a BLP-style neutrality issue about the 1963 disaster, not new real-world news. Four temporary-account IDs are involved and may be one person, but I can't confirm that. One of them made a 1-byte edit to the Napoli 2026-27 season page, which is otherwise routine and unrelated.

stories.headline: Cambridge Regional College page hit by juvenile alumni-list vandalism
stories.summary: The activity on the en-wiki Cambridge Regional College article is vandalism, not a news event. One temporary account added the junk line "* Jdrj" (rev 1381183879). Patroller Pyrrhic victor reverted it as test edits with WikiShield (rev 1381183924). A second temporary account then added fake "alumni": "LeBron James, goat", "Benjamin Netanyahu, world admin" and "Frank Nyarko, saviour of the end of the world" (rev 1381184957). At last check that second edit had not been reverted. The 117 bytes of churn come from these joke additions and the revert. The edits touch only this one page in one language. This fits the school-related vandalism also seen on other UK school pages, but nothing links the editors.

stories.headline: Self-promotional ru-wiki page 'XqwzKOT' tagged for speedy deletion, now apparently deleted
stories.summary: This is not a news event. A temporary account created the ru-wiki article 'XqwzKOT' in one edit of about 18 KB. That single edit accounts for nearly all the churn. Per its edit summary, the page described a personal software project ('Kot-system', also called xqwz or KOT) and promoted a Telegram channel. Within about 4 minutes, a second temporary account and the patroller Alex NB IT each added a speedy-deletion tag (Критерии быстрого удаления). The second account then undid Alex NB IT's tag because the page already had one ("Тут уже есть один шаблон"). The page was created and tagged within minutes, and no other pages or languages are involved. I could not open any of the 4 diffs because Wikipedia says the revisions no longer exist. That fits the page having been speedily deleted, but this is inferred, not confirmed. Everything above comes from edit summaries in the graph, not from the article text.

stories.headline: NATO member-states page: one vandal table wipe, reverted in 84 seconds; nothing new
stories.summary: This is the same episode as the earlier brief, and nothing new has happened since. The graph shows only three edits on enwiki's "Member states of NATO". None of them is newer than the 16,256-byte revert, and the page has no other-language versions linked in the graph. Temporary account ~2026-56255-74 replaced the formatted member table with a plain wikitable, stripping out flags, maps, citations and links. Its edit summary was "I added my buddy richard". TruenoCity reverted it 84 seconds later as "unexplained removal of content", restoring the original table markup. In the part of the diff I could read (Albania's row), the facts were the same: same accession date, population and other figures. There's no sign of a real change in NATO membership. The earlier zero-byte edit to "Military expenditures" by another temporary account is still unresolved, because the diff cuts off before the change. A same-size edit is most likely a small wording or formatting fix. Each editor has touched only this page, and there is no back-and-forth reverting. I recommend merging this into the existing story and closing it.

stories.headline: It-wiki: patroller reverts navigation hatnotes; new Sa-Nur article unrelated to the rest
stories.summary: This cluster is not a news event. It is two separate pieces of routine editing that got grouped together. First, temporary account ~2026-56275-64 added "{{torna a|...}}" hatnotes (links pointing readers back to a parent article) to Montecassino (pointing to Cassino), Scauri (pointing to Minturno) and Tremensuoli. Patroller Sayatek reverted these, saying the pages are not "ancillary" entries. Separately, a different temporary account made a small Tremensuoli edit: it added a photo of the Chiesa di San Nicandro Martire and cleaned up some wording. Second, and with no link to the Lazio pages, Stefantiz created a well-sourced it-wiki article on Sa-Nur, a West Bank settlement evacuated in 2005 and officially re-established on 19 April 2026. Sources show Israeli approval in May 2025, and the article's access dates are October 2026, so this is an older development being written up now, not breaking news. Apart from the patroller rolling back an anonymous edit on Sa-Nur, nothing points to an edit war or coordinated vandalism.

stories.headline: Still routine: flag fix on ru.wiki Aleksey Baga bio holds, no new activity
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The dossier shows the same three edits. A temporary account changed the flag on the 2026 Torpedo-BelAZ career entry from Russia's to Belarus's (rev 155716511). The bot EyeBot reverted it automatically (rev 155716517). Then LNTG undid the bot (rev 155716535). I read LNTG's diff, which confirms the only change is {{Флаг России}} → {{Флаг Беларуси}} on the existing 2026 Torpedo-BelAZ line. That is correct, because Torpedo-BelAZ is a Belarusian club. There are no more edits, no other pages or languages involved, and no sign of a real-world event behind it.

stories.headline: Petty vandalism on German Wikipedia's Maria Magdalena article undone within seconds
stories.summary: This is not a news event, and nothing has changed since the earlier brief. One temporary account, ~2026-56028-91, added the phrase "deine vater" ("your father") to the German article on Mary Magdalene twice. The first time it was dropped into the middle of a sentence in the lead (rev 271479573, summary "ich wars", "it was me"). The second time it was stuck in front of the disambiguation template (rev 271479636, summary "halo wdkdkxkkkdkdkdldldldl"). Established editors Mützelzipfe and Logograph each undid one of these within about 20 seconds. The graph doesn't flag those undos as reverts, but their edit summaries say they are. That is the 46-byte churn the scout saw: two insertions and two undos. There have been no edits to the page since the second undo. The activity stayed on one page in one language, with no sign of anything happening in the real world.

stories.headline: Spanish Civil War airlift edit war (es-wiki) continues: fourth temporary account, Ontzak reverts
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked edit war on es-wiki "Guerra civil española". It is not a new event. The scout says there were no reverts, but that's wrong. The graph's revert flag is unset, but both new edits are undos, as their comments and diffs show. In rev 175925303 a fourth single-edit temporary account, ~2026-56186-91, put back the disputed 88-byte change to the lead. That change swaps "gracias a la rápida colaboración de la Alemania nazi y la Italia fascista" for "creado por los sublevados con la ayuda de sus aliados extranjeros", sourced to La Razón. Its comment says it is unrelated to "the other account", which it says cited a book by the Francoist activist Fernando Paz and talked about "méritos", and insists it does not deny the foreign help. Fifteen seconds later Ontzak reverted it (rev 175925307), restoring the stable text that names Germany and Italy. The change has now been inserted 4 times by 4 different temporary accounts, and removed 4 times by 3 registered editors. The temporary accounts deny being linked, but they push identical text, each makes only one edit, and they appear one after another, which points to one person rotating accounts. I can't confirm that. No edits have come in since 175925307, and there is no sign of a real-world news trigger. Page protection seems likely.

stories.headline: Oregon OC Drew Mehringer's page hit by antisemitic vandalism after Ducks' losses
stories.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56212-69) made five edits in about 35 minutes to the en-wiki biography of Oregon offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. The edits added criticism of his offense: a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State, a 17-15 home loss to UCLA with 7 turnovers and 1-of-13 on third down, and a claim that his hiring "is widely associated with the sudden decline" of the program. They also inserted an antisemitic "nickname". Three experienced editors reverted it. Celjski Grad used the anti-vandalism tool Interceptor, Grem833 removed a smaller addition as unsourced, and PhilKnight rolled back the whole day's edits. This is vandalism by an angry fan, not an edit war, and no edit claims he was fired, resigned or reassigned. The only possible news hook is indirect: the cited losses (ESPN and SI links dated around 2026-10-20) point to a rough Oregon season and fan pressure on the coordinator. I haven't checked those game results against any source outside the vandal's text.

stories.headline: Latvian vandal's insult spree spreads to 3 pages; school article edit still unreverted
stories.summary: The vandalism on lvwiki 'Zizma' was more than a one-page incident. It was part of a four-edit spree over about 4.5 minutes by temporary account ~2026-55989-48. The account swapped article names for a homophobic insult aimed at one "Normunds": first on 'Kroņauce' (rev 4537968; NDG reverted it as vandalism), then twice on 'Zizma' (rev 4537972 changed the lead to "normunds gejs"; NDG reverted it in rev 4537973). Its last and most specific edit, rev 4537975, added text to the name field of 'Kandavas Lauksaimniecības tehnikums', an agricultural school in Kandava. The added text says a "big gay named Normunds Balandis" studies there. That edit names an apparently real person, probably a student, and the graph shows no revert yet. So it's a live attack on a private individual. The school link suggests this is local schoolyard harassment, not a real-world news event. I don't know if the target is a real person, or whether the edit was reverted after the graph's last update. Next steps: check the school page and consider asking admins to hide the revision. No other languages are involved and there's no edit war.

stories.headline: Quokka vandal returns twice more, including a false 'extinct' status; both edits reverted
stories.summary: Since the last brief, the account "Rushymaster" has made two more vandal edits to the English Quokka article, bringing its total to four. The first changed the conservation status in the infobox from VU (Vulnerable) to EX (Extinct) and left the IUCN citation in place. DonnieNova reverted it in about 40 seconds. The second replaced the short description with a made-up "fun fact" about quokka reproduction. T430s reverted it in about 30 seconds as vandalism. The "extinct" change is the only edit that looks like news, and it is false: the cited 2020 IUCN assessment lists the species as Vulnerable, and no editor or other-language page backs the change. Mesoamerica and Artemis VI have had no new activity. The earlier vandalism there was already reverted. There is no real-world event and no content dispute. The only editors who appear on more than one page are anti-vandalism patrollers and ClueBot NG. Rushymaster has now been reverted repeatedly, so the account may be blocked or the page semi-protected, but the graph does not show that.

stories.headline: es-wiki 'Iglesia católica': two logged-out test/vandal edits, both bot-reverted; no event
stories.summary: I checked again and found no new activity on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Iglesia católica' page since the earlier brief. The graph has four edits in total, all already covered there. The Scout's count is a little off: it is 4 edits from 4 accounts, and 2 of those edits are reverts that the graph doesn't flag as reverts. Rev 175919671 came from a temporary (logged-out) account with no edit summary and changed the lead paragraph (+109 bytes). Automoderador reverted it 11 seconds later. Rev 175919780 came from a different temporary account. It deleted the three hatnote templates at the top of the page and added broken table markup ("{| cla…") into the lead. SeroBOT reverted it 12 seconds later. I could not see exactly what text the first edit added because the diff output was cut off. Even so, single-edit accounts, no summaries and instant bot reverts match test edits or minor vandalism, not a real-world event. I agree with the Scout's conclusion: there is no new story here.

stories.headline: Iranian archaeologist Yousef Majidzadeh, Jiroft excavator, reported dead at 90
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Yousef Majidzadeh, the Iranian archaeologist who directed excavations at Jiroft, Ozbaki and Qabristan, now gives his death as 19 October 2026, aged 90. Its source is an ISNA article titled "یوسف مجیدزاده درگذشت" ("Yousef Majidzadeh passed away"). Before any of the five edits in this cluster, the lead and the body already gave the death date, so the edit that first added the death happened before our window. The edits we can see are follow-up cleanup by three registered editors, with no reverts. Editrite! changed "is a native of Tabriz" to the past tense, Extended Cut added an infobox field, and Strattonsmith reworded the death sentence (±8-byte tweaks; that edit also left a stray apostrophe). The graph has no other-language pages linked to this article and no activity in other languages. I have not checked the ISNA report independently, but it is a mainstream Iranian news agency and the cleanup by several editors fits a real, recent death.

stories.headline: No news: another sock pastes GTA: SA article over redirect, Rhain reverts in a minute
stories.summary: This is the same ban-evasion pattern as before, with no real-world event behind it. A new temporary account, ~2026-56068-06, pasted the full ~205 KB Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas article over the "GTA: SA" redirect (rev 1381157199). Its edit summary, "Last edit no more but the current revision sucks", repeats the wording of earlier socks. A fourth patroller, Rhain, put the redirect back about 60 seconds later (rev 1381157273). I read both diffs, and the paste is just a copy of the existing game article, with no new content. That makes at least six accounts doing the same paste, and patrollers have cited WP:SOCK and "banned means banned". All of it is on English Wikipedia. At Osmanabad, the graph shows no edits after Rina komorin's rev 1381155408 putting "Dharashiv" first in the lead, so the earlier note still holds: a dispute over which name goes first, not news. The only open question is whether that edit is still live.

stories.headline: Chilean celebrity bios on es-wiki hit by family-detail vandalism; some edits still up
stories.summary: The new cluster isn't routine. A second wave of vandalism has hit Spanish Wikipedia bios of Chilean TV figures. On Patricia Maldonado Aravena, temporary account ~2026-56162-80 added a made-up third child, "HERNAN FLORES" (rev 175918276), and Automoderador reverted it within seconds. Four minutes later the registered account Reddizze, under the misleading edit summary "correcciones recientes", added the same name as her parent and changed her religion from Agnóstica to "Judia" (rev 175918361). Reddizze then edited Jorge Zabaleta: it swapped his partner's name (175918457), and its second edit changed his years active to "1967-presente" and his number of children to "67" (175918482). The graph shows no reverts of Reddizze's three edits, so they may still be live and patrollers should look at them. The repeated "Hernan Flores" suggests one person moved from a temporary account to a registered one, but that is inferred, not confirmed. The only link to the existing Luar la L story is the Automoderador bot, not shared editors. Luar la L's own vandal (~2026-56419-72) made one more name and birthplace swap (175918231), and Automoderador reverted it. Nothing points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: es-wiki: Two unrelated edits by temporary accounts reverted by bot; no news event
stories.summary: This story is two separate incidents on Spanish Wikipedia. The only link between them is the anti-vandalism bot Automoderador, which reverted both. No real-world event is suggested. On "Protestas de la generación Z", temporary account ~2026-56258-59 removed 4,330 bytes from the Colombia ("Petrotazo") section with no edit summary (rev 175925992). The removed material included sourced statements about Gustavo Petro's unpopularity, criticism of his government for negotiating with armed groups, and white-clothed protests in Bogotá and Medellín after the attack on Miguel Uribe. This looks like politically motivated removal, not an update. Automoderador fully reverted it 23 seconds later (175925997). On "Víctor Jara", temporary account ~2026-56380-23 vandalised the lead sentence by changing "director de teatro" to the slang phrase "farmeador de aura" ("aura farmer") (rev 175925798). Automoderador reverted it within seconds (175925800). The scout's "8660 churn" is just ±4,330 bytes from one removal and its revert. No content was expanded, there was no back-and-forth between editors, and no human editors were involved besides these two single-edit accounts.

stories.headline: Taekwondo pioneer in France Lee Kwan-Young reported dead in Seoul at 80
stories.summary: French Wikipedia now lists Lee Kwan-Young as dead. He was a Korean martial-arts master, an early pioneer of taekwondo and hapkido in France, and the founder of hoshin moosool. The article gives his death as 18 October 2026 in Seoul. Three registered editors updated the article within about 17 minutes, with no reverts. Jmax added the category "Décès en octobre 2026" (deaths in October 2026) and a source: a notice from the French taekwondo federation (FFTDA) titled "Disparition du Grand Maître Lee Kwan Young", dated 19 October 2026. A second editor added the "Mort récente" (recent death) template, and AnasthaseLeGrand only reworded the opening sentence. The death date was already in the text before these edits, so an earlier edit that isn't in our graph must have added it. The only source is the federation's news page, which I have not checked myself. The graph has no linked pages in other languages, so nothing else confirms the death yet. This looks like a niche obituary and nothing more.

stories.headline: Airport route-table edits are one unsourced editor and one patroller, not news
stories.summary: This story is just two editors, not eight. Between about 1792563717 and 1792568009, one temporary account (~2026-56454-57) made small edits to the "Airlines and destinations" sections of Corfu, Luton, Athens and Berlin Brandenburg airports on English Wikipedia. Each edit changed between -372 and +155 bytes. The graph shows the same account also editing Zakynthos, Karpathos, Warsaw Chopin and Vienna. A regular patroller, 10mmsocket, then followed the account from page to page and undid most of the changes, giving the reasons "Unsourced" and "Unexplained removal of content". 10mmsocket also reverted on Rhodes, Saarbrücken and Milan Malpensa. This looks like routine cleanup of unsourced route changes, not an edit war (no back-and-forth reverting) and not a real-world event: there was no second independent editor, no other language versions changed, and nothing was sourced. One possibility I couldn't rule out: the pages are mostly Greek and other holiday airports, plus Luton, and 10mmsocket also touched Duo Airways and Red Rose Travel. So the account may have been adding new seasonal routes or removing dropped ones from a single airline. The big caveat is that the diff tool failed on every revision I tried, so I never saw which airline or routes were changed. This brief rests only on edit comments, edit sizes and graph structure.

stories.headline: Lunchables article: brief vandalism swapping inventor's name, reverted within minutes
stories.summary: This was vandalism, not a content dispute or a news event. A temporary account (~2026-56200-06) made two small edits to the History section of en:Lunchables. They replaced the sourced creator "Bob Drane" with the handle "S1guylavaman" (rev 1381264677), then changed later mentions of "Drane" to "Lavaman" (rev 1381264751). Both edits were unsourced and plainly a joke username inserted into the article. Patroller GreyZoneLife undid the second edit about a minute later (rev 1381264816) and restored "Bob Drane" in the first sentence about five minutes after that (rev 1381265101). The article now matches the cited source (Moss, Salt Sugar Fat). The only leftover is a missing space before a reference tag. Two editors were involved, nobody re-reverted, and no other-language versions or other pages were touched, so there is no edit war and nothing happening in the real world behind it.

stories.headline: Swedish Wikipedia: patroller rolls back test edits on Two Sicilies order page
stories.summary: On sv.wikipedia, the article "Kungliga orden av Bägge Sicilierna" (the Royal Order of the Two Sicilies) got four edits in about 8 minutes. A temporary account (~2026-56469-57) added 407 bytes with the summary "Jag har skrivit en liten kort berättelse om orden" ("I wrote a short little story about the order"). A second temporary account then added 31 bytes with the summary "d". The first account came back with an edit summarised "KOlloll" (a nonsense or joke summary), and patroller EPIC rolled back that account's edits to the second account's version. EPIC made a similar rollback of a temporary account on "Paradisfåglar" (birds-of-paradise) shortly before, which looks like routine recent-changes patrolling. There was no activity in other languages and nothing links this to a real-world event. Caveat: Wikipedia returned "no such revision" for all four diffs, so I couldn't read the edited text. This call rests only on edit summaries, byte changes and the rollback, and the text may have been hidden or deleted after the fact. Recommend closing as low-grade vandalism or test edits.

stories.headline: Small vandalism on Indonesian party pages and CECOT, reverted by one patroller
stories.summary: The story is not a real-world event. It is a few low-level vandal edits by two temporary accounts, all undone within minutes by a single patroller, Perpetually Blooming Rose, using the UV tool. On Communist Party of Indonesia, ~2026-56200-41 changed native_name from "Partai Komunis Indonesia" to the joke "Partai Komputer Indonesia". The edit also reformatted the infobox, which explains the ±229 bytes and the "458 churn" (229 removed, then 229 restored). The same account added the chant "Hidup PDIP, Hidup PDIP!!" ("Long live PDIP!") to Puan Maharani's page, labelling it as her party role. A separate account, ~2026-56298-71, swapped "stated" for "whined" in CECOT's section on Venezuelan deportees. The three pages share only the patroller, and the two Indonesian pages share one partisan joker. Nothing points to a news event in Indonesia or El Salvador. We have edits in English only and no reverts going back and forth.

stories.headline: eMudhra certificate authority hit by reported trivially weak intermediate CA keys
stories.summary: The scout read this as routine company-page churn, but the diffs say otherwise. The newly patrolled en-wiki article on Indian certificate authority eMudhra has a section titled "2026 intermediate certificate compromise". It says that on October 20 researchers found the private key of one eMudhra intermediate certificate was "simply the number 4". A follow-up edit (rev 1381213362, refined in 1381213513) adds that seven other intermediate certificates used the private keys 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Four accounts made 10 edits in about an hour with no reverts: a new-page patroller adding a stub tag, category and short description, plus three editors copyediting and expanding the compromise section. That points to a newly surfacing event, not promotion or vandalism. Big caveat: the only sources cited are two Fediverse/Mastodon posts by individual researchers. We have no vendor statement, no browser or CA/B Forum response and no mainstream coverage, and the claim has not been independently confirmed. Only one page in one language is involved so far. Watch for the article being sent to deletion or pulled back for weak sourcing, and for related Mozilla, Chrome or CA/B Forum distrust activity.

stories.headline: Minor vandalism on de-wiki Röntgen article, both edits quickly reverted
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-55920-30) made two small edits to the German article on physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1845–1923). The first, with the comment "ja", deleted the † death symbol from the lead. The second added the stray text "glaubt nicht alles" ("doesn't believe everything") above an image comment. Patrollers Brettchenweber and Serols (the latter using Huggle) undid both edits within minutes. Nothing here points to a real-world event. It is a low-level test or vandalism episode that has already been cleaned up.

stories.headline: ruwiki: EyeBot reverts more small temporary-account edits; mini-repeat on Samosvat, no news
stories.summary: The story grew from three pages to five, but it is still routine anti-vandal cleanup. The Samosvat edit was made twice by the same temporary account (~2026-56315-19). The second try lined up the infobox fields again and added "ØMEN" to his bands, with the comment that this is his latest band. EyeBot reverted both within about 30 seconds. That is one person re-adding an unsourced claim, not two editors fighting over it. On "Абоба (интернет-мем)", another temporary account replaced the lead and its Ukrainska Pravda source with one line saying the meme came out in 2022 (the article says 2021). EyeBot restored the original, and it looks like low-level vandalism. On László Sólyom (Шойом, Ласло), a temporary account made a +44 edit that EyeBot reverted. I couldn't load that diff. The same account also edited Lee Teng-hui, Nausėda and Áder, and the Lee Teng-hui diff I did read is infobox realignment plus changing religion from "христианство" (Christianity) to "пресвитерианство" (Presbyterianism). That points to one cleanup-minded editor working through presidents' bios, not news about Sólyom. Still, I haven't seen that diff, so I can't fully rule it out, and no other-language Sólyom pages moved.

stories.headline: Indonesian 2026 quake list logs a claimed M6.6 near Luganville, Vanuatu; routine update
stories.summary: On Indonesian Wikipedia's 'Daftar gempa bumi tahun 2026' (list of 2026 earthquakes), editors raised the count of M6.0–6.9 quakes by one. One edit summary says it was a new M6.6 quake at Luganville, Vanuatu. A temporary account bumped the infobox total from 101 to 102 (rev 30092940). Editor 'Eearthquake 2026' then raised the October count from 11 to 12, citing the Vanuatu quake (30092945), and updated the year-comparison table (102; total 12,490→12,491, rev 30092974). Separately, another temporary account changed the 9.0+ count from 0 to 3. That was a bogus edit, and the same editor reverted it (30093002). It was a one-off revert, not an edit war. Nothing else in the graph backs this up: no other-language versions of the list, and no Vanuatu earthquake page is being edited. The magnitude and location come only from an edit summary, so they are unconfirmed. A mid-6 quake in Vanuatu is common and probably not big news unless damage reports show up.

stories.headline: Haber process: one temporary account's sneaky vandalism reverted twice
stories.summary: This is not a news event. It's small-scale vandalism on the English "Haber process" article, and other editors cleaned it up within minutes. Temporary account ~2026-56275-44 added a slur fragment ("niga") to the lead sentence with the misleading edit summary "i deleted som bad words" (rev 1381277361). Staticspector reverted it about 40 seconds later. The same account then made a second edit labelled "dates were wrong" (rev 1381278388). That edit changed the date in Carl Bosch's photo caption from 1927 to 1928 with no source, added a stray period, and slipped "iga2" into the chemical formula for nitrogen. A second temporary account reverted it about 5 minutes later. Only one page was edited, there was no activity in other languages, and the false edit summaries show the edits were made in bad faith rather than as a content dispute. No further action is needed unless the account comes back.

stories.headline: eMudhra CA-key compromise page: no new activity, only cleanup and one undone edit
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked story, and nothing has changed since the last brief. The four edits the scout flagged are the same four the previous brief covered, and no newer revisions exist in the graph. I read all four diffs. Merlin04 lightly rewrote the sentence on key entropy: per Ars Technica, the P-384 keys should have had 384 bits of entropy but had only 3–8, being the integers 4–237. Actualice added publisher details to the Mozilla blog and The Island citations. A temporary account changed "is" to "was", implying the company is defunct, and Pppery undid it about a minute later, citing no evidence. This is one revert, not an edit war. The incident facts already on the page are unchanged: notification on Oct 17, eight intermediates revoked on Oct 18, and Mozilla pulling the emSign roots from Firefox on Oct 20, cited to the Mozilla security blog, Ars Technica and The Hacker News. The page has no linked versions in other languages, and the graph shows no activity on related pages. I have not independently verified the cited sources.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) strengthens to 900 hPa, now the 2026 Pacific season's strongest
stories.summary: Editors of the 2026 Pacific typhoon season article raised Typhoon Champi's central pressure from 905 to 900 hPa. That edit also dropped Typhoon Sinlaku from the "strongest storm" slot it had shared with Champi, leaving Champi alone (rev 1381214471). Minutes later a different editor raised Champi's 1-minute sustained winds from 155 to 160, likely knots, which would be super-typhoon strength (rev 1381214861). A third editor swapped in a satellite image dated 2026-10-20 at 1700Z (rev 1381221959). Champi also has a Philippine local name, "Rosal", which suggests it is in or has entered the Philippine monitoring area. That is my inference; no edit mentions landfall, warnings or damage. The activity is small: 3–4 named editors, no reverts, and the other recent edits are just about chart width on mobile. The numbers were typed in by volunteers and the edit summaries cite no source, so treat them as unconfirmed. No separate Champi article or other-language pages showed up in the graph. Worth watching for landfall and impact edits.

stories.headline: New ja.wiki page on SEIKIN's "Wahō" meme created, redirected, then restored
stories.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. All the churn comes from one new Japanese Wikipedia page, わほー ("Wahō"), about an internet meme. A temporary account created it (+2717). The page says the word comes from a 2014 SeikinTV video in which YouTuber SEIKIN eats a large amount of Mintia mints. It also says the word went viral on TikTok in late 2025–2026, and that SEIKIN and HIKAKIN have reacted to it. About six minutes later, Kugelschreibers turned the page into a redirect to [[SEIKIN]] (−2697). This is a normal cleanup step for a new, thinly sourced article. Another editor, カカポが好きな人, then put the article back with headings, external links and a "needs sources" ({{出典の明記}}) tag (+2748). The page cites a single source, a Livedoor News article. The "8162 churn" is just the same ~2.7 KB of text added, removed and added again. So far it's a one-time disagreement over whether the page should exist, not an edit war, though another redirect or a deletion nomination is possible.

stories.headline: Fielder/Holmes doc 'You Can See Everything': box-office update, duplicate Wired text removed
stories.summary: Three editors made routine upkeep edits to the English article on the 2026 Nathan Fielder–Lance Oppenheim documentary about Elizabeth Holmes. Wikicarp added a paragraph (+515 bytes) citing a Wired interview published October 19. In it, Fielder describes a phone call from Holmes: she said she had not seen the film or its reception, and repeated that she trusted him. A temporary account removed the same paragraph about 14 minutes later (−515), explaining that the Wired piece was already covered two paragraphs earlier. That add-and-remove pair accounts for the 1,030-byte churn the scout flagged. It is cleanup, not a dispute: there was no reply or re-revert. Separately, Gabgoldv raised the infobox gross from $15.6M to $18.2M, citing The Numbers. That suggests the film is still earning in its run, but I have not checked the figure against the source. No conflict, no other languages involved, and nothing here counts as a new real-world event.

stories.headline: Routine sv-wiki cleanup of new article on Quebec poet Mélissa Labonté
stories.summary: Three established Swedish Wikipedia editors (Lgmka, Yger, Stigfinnare) made 11 edits to the article on Mélissa Labonté between 1792496819 and 1792497144, about 5 minutes. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors, and no other language editions were involved. The diffs show only maintenance work. Lgmka added and removed categories with HotCat, for example adding and then removing "Författare från Kanada" (Writers from Canada), which is one editor correcting their own choices, not an edit war. Yger moved the birth details (born 1989, Saint-Henri-de-Lévis, Quebec, with an existing Poetik Bazar citation) into the lead sentence and replaced "Poeter" (Poets) with "Kanadensiska poeter" (Canadian poets) and "Levande personer" (Living people). Stigfinnare added a references tag, a default sort key and the "Franskspråkiga poeter" (French-language poets) category. No new facts tied to a current event were added, so this looks like a newly created biography getting its first cleanup. It matches the earlier routine brief, and nothing has changed since. One uncertainty: the article's creation edit isn't in the graph, so the story behind its creation is unknown.

stories.headline: One editor keeps re-adding animal-rights opinion to de-wiki 'Göttliches Recht'; reverted
stories.summary: This is not a real-world event or a content rewrite. A single temporary account (~2026-56572-12) keeps adding one opinion sentence (223 bytes) to the lead of the German article 'Göttliches Recht' (divine law). The sentence says divine law "must be based on absolute morality" and that tolerating the killing of farm animals violates it. The account first undid an earlier removal by Stephan Klage (rev 271500299). Horst Gräbner reverted that, the account put the sentence back with the comment "must not be censored", and Logograph removed it again citing WP:TF (the German guideline against original research). The high churn figure comes from the same 223 bytes going in and out four times, and none of the edits were flagged as reverts. No other pages, languages or sources are involved. This is unsourced opinion-pushing by one account, cleaned up by three established editors, not a two-sided edit war. More re-insertions or a block are possible, but the newsroom doesn't need to watch this.

stories.headline: Nigel Ng (Uncle Roger) page hit by two unrelated vandal edits, both reverted
stories.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Malaysian comedian Nigel Ng ("Uncle Roger") had two separate vandal edits from two different temporary accounts, about 15 minutes apart. Patrollers reverted both within minutes. In the first edit (rev 1381236506), the bold name was replaced with "UNCLE ROGERS FUIYOH HAIYA", the birth date was changed to "SEPTEMBER,13 1991" and the character was renamed "Uncle RICKS". The edit summary claimed he had revealed "his name and legit info" on a podcast, but no source was given. GhostStalker reverted it. In the second edit (rev 1381238068, summary "nak"), the whole infobox was deleted (1,236 characters) and "Cantonese" was swapped for an obscene word. TonySt reverted it with an anti-vandalism tool. The ~2,500 characters of churn is just that one deletion and its revert. There is no sign of a dispute between regular editors or of any real-world news; the podcast claim looks like a cover for the joke edit, though I can't rule out that some podcast moment prompted the attention. Only this one language edition is involved and the page is back to its earlier version.

stories.headline: Russian-text spam spreads from 'Pete versus Life' to its cast and Channel 4 pages
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news, and it is the same incident already tracked for 'Pete versus Life'. The account Ggsrhrhs added the same 8,399-byte block to English Wikipedia pages linked from that article: Rafe Spall (3 times), Reece Ritchie (2), Channel 4 (2) and the show's page itself (3). I read the diffs on Channel 4 (1381290991), Rafe Spall (1381290651) and Reece Ritchie (1381290906). Each one is only the Russian phrase "Том и Джерри. 10 серия." ("Tom and Jerry. Episode 10") repeated over and over. Three patrollers, Andreworkney, Beyhive Navy and KH-1, reverted every insertion within about 1–2 minutes. The 9 reverts are clean-up of one spammer, not an edit war. The dossier lists only 4 editors, not the 12 in the Scout's note. According to the graph, the same account has also hit other pages linked from the article: cast members Chris Geere, Daniel Ings, Susannah Fielding, Philip Jackson, Joseph Kloska and Scarlett Alice Johnson, plus Objective Media Group, Sitcom, Single-camera setup, Embarrassment and Andy Gray (footballer). Its latest edit was about 3 minutes after the last revert in this cluster. I have not read those other diffs, and I can't tell whether the account has been blocked. There is no sign of any real-world event; this story should be merged with the existing one.

stories.headline: Petty vandalism on 'Nuclear power debate' and 'Euphoria' reverted by a patroller
stories.summary: This isn't a news event or a content dispute. It's ordinary vandalism cleaned up by one patroller on English Wikipedia. On 'Nuclear power debate', temporary account ~2026-55968-94 made two small edits to the lead sentence, ending with the article "about aiden patterson" (rev 1381277018), which looks like a personal name prank. Patroller APK reverted it as vandalism ("rvv") by restoring an older revision (1381277808). That rollback also wiped out a legitimate edit, so APK put it back a minute later (1381277946, "restore edit"). The restored edit changes decommissioning costs to US$500M–2B and cites an IAEA source. On 'Euphoria', a different temporary account added "kendrick Lamars song" to the top of the page (1381276978), and APK reverted that too. The pages have nothing in common except the same patroller. There was no back-and-forth reverting, no other languages involved, and no sign of anything happening in the real world. Recommend closing the story.

stories.headline: Czech Wikipedia: minor vandalism on Brno Dragon article undone twice
stories.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. This is small-scale vandalism on the cs.wiki article about the Brno Dragon, the stuffed crocodile in Brno's Old Town Hall, and it was cleaned up quickly. A temporary account (~2026-56333-38) changed "draka" to "kara" in the Původ (origin) section (rev 26315234). On a second try it made the same change and also slipped the nonsense phrase "Mg Granko" into the sentence about the crocodile being a gift from Turkish envoys (rev 26315239). Both edits were undone within about two minutes, by JirkaSv and then OJJ. Their edit summaries are standard rollback text. Note that the graph's revert flag says false for those two edits, but the summaries show they were reverts, so the scout's "no reverts" was wrong. I read only the vandal's two diffs, not the rollbacks. No sign of a wider campaign or a news hook.

stories.headline: Single account adds joke middle names to three pop-star bios; all reverted
stories.summary: This is a small vandalism spree, not a news event. One new account, HurricaneImelda2025 (4 edits in total), changed the English Wikipedia pages for The Weeknd, Dua Lipa and Kelly Rowland one after another over about 9 minutes. Each edit made up a middle name and put it in the infobox and/or the opening line: "Abel Beyoncé Makkonen Tesfaye", "Dua Jackari Lispa Jackson Lipa" and "Kelendria Transgénderaline Teresa Trene Rowland". None of the edits cited a source, and all had blank edit summaries. Nil NZ, an established editor, reverted all three within about 1 minute of each other, with summaries like "Unsourced". No other editors or languages were involved, so there is no sign of a real-world event behind the cluster. The 4th edit by the account is outside this story and I didn't check it.

stories.headline: No change: es-wiki 'Capraria' hatnote back-and-forth with bots has stopped; no news
stories.summary: There has been no new activity since the last brief. The graph shows no edits on 'Capraria' or 'Torneo de Doha' after rev 175923657, where SeroBOT undid the latest attempt. The pattern is the same as before. One temporary account (~2026-56151-66) kept adding "{{Distinguir|El Hierro}}", a note telling readers not to confuse the page with El Hierro, plus small spacing fixes. Rev 175923656, which I read again, is a typical example. SeroBOT and Automoderador undid each attempt within seconds. The scout's note says there were no reverts, which is wrong: the bots undid the newcomer about 7 times. This is a newcomer against anti-vandalism bots, not people fighting each other, and it has nothing to do with real-world events. The Doha tennis page has also been quiet. I recommend closing the story unless the editor starts again or a human editor joins in.

stories.headline: One account's sneaky vandalism across five ja-wiki anime pages, all reverted
stories.summary: This isn't routine maintenance. It's a small vandalism spree by one registered account, 堀江美都子かいけつゾロリ, which made five small edits to five unrelated ja-wiki anime, voice-actor and radio pages over about 19 minutes. The diffs show subtle false changes. On Orange, the radio show's title was rewritten with fake wikilinked names (柏尾誠一郎・柏尾川慎), under a misleading summary claiming it was manually adding a report because DragoBot was down. On あいうら, a nonsense voice credit "[[Mt.Asahdake]]" was added. On 声優と夜あそび, a made-up guest was added to an episode. On 博多豚骨ラーメンズ, a second voice actor was tacked on and a character was said to spend his time on "anime viewing and Wikipedia administration". The MELODY FLAG edit only reformatted a template line. Patrollers North Pacific (4 pages) and Syunsyunminmin (1 page) reverted all five within about 15 minutes, so no false content is left. There's no real-world event behind this, and it isn't an edit war, since nobody restored the edits.

stories.headline: Patroller reverts three unrelated bad edits; no news event behind them
stories.summary: These three pages have nothing in common except one recent-changes patroller, 49ersBelongInSanFrancisco. Within about 3 minutes, that editor reverted one bad edit by a different user on each page. On Times New Roman, a temporary account replaced the "Usage" section heading with "it's my birthday" (+15 bytes). On Scammer Payback, a temporary account filled the Twitch fields in the infobox with nonsense ("Fbi", "O'clock", "Chico box"). On Practical Magic 2, Pjtawney added an opinion paragraph to the Critical response section saying that male critics and Rotten Tomatoes users "never understood" the film and should "stay in their lane" (+391). That edit is not sourced, so it doesn't count as film news. It may only hint that early reviews are negative, but this edit doesn't show that. Each page has one revert and no back-and-forth, so this is routine vandalism cleanup, not an edit war or a real-world event.

stories.headline: Championship page logs Wolves 1–1 Portsmouth result; one unrelated clause reverted
stories.summary: This is routine upkeep of the 2026–27 EFL Championship season article during the season. It isn't fixture or squad news. CatCat67420 entered a 1–1 result for Wolverhampton Wanderers v Portsmouth in the results grid, moved the table's update date from 17 to 20 October 2026, and raised the season totals from 131 to 132 matches and from 378 to 380 goals. LDMDNP then added an attendance figure of 29,058 for that match and recalculated the season's average attendance. The only revert, by Bmf 051, removed a clause an unregistered editor had added saying the play-off expansion was the first "since the 2017–18 National League". The revert comment called it irrelevant, so this is a content cleanup, not an edit war. I haven't checked the score against any outside source, but three editors made consistent edits and nobody disputed them, so it is very likely accurate. There is no sign of any wider event.

stories.headline: Minor vandalism on en-wiki 'Mr. Big' and 'Crab' pages reverted within minutes
stories.summary: These two pages have nothing to do with each other, and nothing suggests a real-world event. They show up together only because both had small, quickly reverted vandalism around the same time. On 'Mr. Big (Sex and the City)', a temporary account added the slang insult "migajera" next to Carrie Bradshaw (rev 1381200133, edit summary "I said migajera"), and Joyous! reverted it. About 15 minutes later, a different temporary account deleted almost the whole article, about 17.9k bytes (rev 1381201932). ClueBot NG restored it within 10 seconds. That deletion is the large change the scout flagged. On 'Crab', another temporary account added a made-up claim that crabs were "named after popular YouTuber Crabman220" (rev 1381200612), and Joyous! reverted it. The same account's later +24 "more examples" edit was then adjusted by Hemiauchenia, which looks like normal editing. The three vandal accounts are different, and the only overlap between the pages is the patroller Joyous!, so this doesn't look like a coordinated attack.

stories.headline: De-wiki: Creator makes 1-byte spelling tweak to cabaret page up for deletion; still routine
stories.summary: Only one edit has come in since the last brief. In rev 271485044, the creator Klaus Ziemer changed the alternative spelling in the first sentence of "Die Stachelbär´n" from "Die Stachelbärn" to "Die Stachelbän". The edit comment says Stachelbär´n is the group's original name and is often misspelled. The change seems to bring in a new misspelling of its own, and it doesn't touch the YouTube-only source or answer the speedy-deletion requests already on the page (revs 271484892, 271484895). The Scout is right this time: it's cleanup by the page's author with no reverts and no sign of a real-world event. The Hanslbauer page, tracked in the same story, has had no new edits. Both pages are self-promotional, have been flagged for speedy deletion, and will probably be deleted.

stories.headline: Helen Haines attack remains the story; Fielder film page hit by unrelated vandalism
stories.summary: I checked whether "You Can See Everything" is linked to the Helen Haines story. It is not. It is a 2026 documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim about Elizabeth Holmes. The only recent activity is about 4 small edits from one temporary account (~2026-56184-09) within about 6 minutes. That account changed the short description to "The potatoes are aliens" (rev 1381171007) and changed the country from "United States" to "Israel" under the summary "Fixed grammar" (rev 1381171438). Three different patrollers undid these within minutes: T430s, Celjski Grad's anti-vandalism tool, and Skywatcher68. This is simple vandalism and says nothing about real-world news. The scout was right: the 9-editor cluster comes from anti-vandalism patrollers (T430s, Celjski Grad) who work across several pages. It does not tie the pages together. Adil, Xie Wanjun and Ika people are likewise separate clean-up jobs or disputes. The real news here is still Helen Haines (as described in earlier briefs): the article says she was critically injured in a deliberate vehicle attack in Wangaratta on 19 October 2026, and an unsourced claim that she died was reverted. I did not re-read the Haines diffs for this check. Recommendation: remove You Can See Everything (and the other unrelated pages) from this story.

stories.headline: Editors fine-tune 'validity' wording on article about OpenAI's 722-paper math release
stories.summary: The en-wiki article covers OpenAI's 7 Oct 2026 release on GitHub of 722 AI-generated manuscripts that claim results on open problems, including partial results on the Riemann hypothesis, BSD and Hodge conjectures. Its cited sources (Retraction Watch, 8 Oct; Quanta, 9 Oct) say three preprints were withdrawn within a day and 14 more revised. The three edits in this window are wording changes to the "Validity" section, not new developments. An unregistered editor (+84) made the Lean caveat clearer: about half the papers come with machine-checked proofs, but someone still has to check by hand that each proof matches its paper, and some formalizations prove weaker results than the papers claim. The one revert is a small dispute over wording, not an edit war. IlkkaP changed "could contain errors" to "could have issues" to match the quoted reference, and Eigenbra changed it back, citing WP:EUPH. The underlying event is real news and is covered elsewhere, but this activity is routine copyediting. No other-language versions are linked and nothing here is new, so it's low priority.

stories.headline: Hoax cartoon listings and a link-spam edit reverted on animation-studio and loyalty pages
stories.summary: I found no real-world event behind this cluster. It is two unrelated bits of bad editing, and patrollers cleaned up both. One temporary account (~2026-55341-25) added made-up TV listings to three animation-studio pages. On D'Ocon Films and Rainbow (company) it added a 2026 series called "The PRCG Northeastern Central and Southwest American Lesbian Sisters!" (shown as airing on Cartoon Network on D'Ocon), and on Soyuzmultfilm it added "The Waldo Kitty is Returning on September 1, 2026." JavaHurricane and DanGFSouza reverted all of it within minutes. Separately, a new account called Loyaltynest inserted promotional links to cfcs.co.in into the Loyalty program article, with an edit summary claiming to "improve references". JavaHurricane reverted that too. The only thing connecting the two is the patroller JavaHurricane, so the studio pages and the loyalty page don't share a real topic. I have not read the diffs of D'Ocon's earlier History/top-section additions (rev 1381275563, 1381275928) or DanGFSouza's follow-up removal of 271 bytes (rev 1381276537). Those are probably the same hoax and its cleanup.

stories.headline: dewiki patrol: deleted joke page 'Henry groß' recreated as 'Henry Louis Groß'; no news
stories.summary: Routine anti-vandalism work on German Wikipedia. Nothing here points to a real-world event. The new item is "Henry Louis Groß". Account "PMA special" created it (rev 271502184) with almost the same text as the deleted joke page "Henry groß": a 14-year-old player at VfB Heusweiler whose rival is "Leon Kachebowski". Horst Gräbner tagged it for speedy deletion (SLA) about six minutes later. That makes it a recreation, not a separate story. The scout called the other new pages routine churn, which is right. On Söll (Tirol), a temporary account listed a 13-year-old trail runner as a notable resident (rev 271502300), and Horst Gräbner reverted it. On Florentine Osche, he removed an irrelevant "Abitur grade 0.9" detail (rev 271502153). On Charlène Favier, someone added a 2025 photo (rev 271502117) and a Commonscat link. The earlier findings still stand: the Lennart Karl "gamer" joke was rolled back, and the Prague ranking mistake was reverted. The graph marks these rollbacks as revert=false, but the edit comments show they are reverts. The one open question is whether "PMA special" is the same person as temporary account ~2026-56320-91, who made the original "Henry groß" page. The matching text suggests it, but I can't confirm it.

stories.headline: Shinya Yamanaka article: one temp account's vandalism reverted, no new activity
stories.summary: Nothing has changed since the earlier brief. The graph still holds only four edits to the English Wikipedia article on Shinya Yamanaka (Q80917), and no other language versions have edits. All the bad edits came from one temporary account, ~2026-56209-78. Its first edit (rev 1381184972) added "charlie kirk" to the sentence about his residency. Its second (rev 1381185624) deleted the line about his 2012 Nobel and 2013 Breakthrough Prize, added a made-up "kirk award of honor" with an image captioned "tommy the runner up", and added the insult "like a bum". Two patrollers reverted the edits within about six minutes: Starlet147 using the Interceptor tool, and Komethere, who labelled it vandalism. The scout was right that this is vandalism cleanup, not news. There is no real award or event behind it. I didn't open the two revert diffs, but their edit summaries and size changes (-17 and +103 bytes) exactly match the vandal's two edits.

stories.headline: Ohio governor race: AP source says Ramaswamy team owns Acton-mother ad, plans $4M buy
stories.summary: Update to s_de966fb5. Temporary account ~2026-56241-92 rewrote the campaign section (+4,334 bytes, rev 1381254389) and added a new citation: an AP story by Julie Carr Smyth dated Oct 21. According to the quote copied from that story, Vivek Ramaswamy's team confirmed late Tuesday that it made the ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged birth mother, Donna Arthur, and will spend $4 million airing it despite "bipartisan rebuke." The quote also says the ad's origins were "initially murky." That clears up the attribution question I raised last time. The same account then split the old "Negative campaigning" section into "Canfield Fair Incident" and "Attacks on Amy Acton's upbringing" subsections (rev 1381255085). Established editors CaptainCanada (rev 1381256813) and ViewFromSomewhere (+482, rev 1381257128) followed with copyedits. Their visible changes are small; the +482 addition was cut off in the diff, so I couldn't see what it adds. There were no reverts in this round, so the earlier dispute seems to have settled into joint editing. This is still English Wikipedia only, and I haven't read the AP piece itself, just the quote in the citation. The wording still makes sensitive claims about a living person, so expect more trimming.

stories.headline: Dune: Part Three: talk-page plea pasted into article twice, reverted; no news
stories.summary: This is not news. All four edits are 41 bytes each. A temporary account (~2026-56017-43) twice added the line "respond to my question on the talk page" to the body of the article (revs 1381260193 and 1381260335; I read both diffs). TonySt removed the first one with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, and 420yeahh reverted the second. Nothing about the film itself changed: no release, cast or production details were touched, and no other language editions moved. Nobody has edited the page since the last revert. This is minor disruption that has already been cleaned up, and it matches the prior brief. One open question: what the user asked on the talk page, which I didn't check.

stories.headline: Unsourced Santa Marta withdrawal claim stays on es-wiki Señorita Colombia 2026 page
stories.summary: A single temporary account (~2026-56228-45) is editing the es-wiki article on Colombia's 72nd national beauty pageant. Its latest edit (rev 175920897) cuts the field from 27 to 26 candidates. It removes Señorita Santa Marta María Camila Valiente Ortiz, whose entry cited a 14 July El Informador article, and adds a "Retiro" (withdrawal) section saying she could not take part "for unknown reasons", with no source. A bot had reverted the account's earlier, broader version of this change. This latest edit has not been reverted and no other editor has backed it up, so the withdrawal is unconfirmed. It could be inside knowledge from a fan or simply wrong. The scout was right that Kirmen Uribe is unrelated. An anonymous editor made the same harmless link fix twice ([[Castellano]] → [[Idioma español|Castellano]], revs 175920920 and 175920933), and Automoderador and SeroBOT reverted it both times, which looks like bots overreacting rather than vandalism. DirecTV is also unrelated bot-revert noise. These pages are linked to the story only through the bots.

stories.headline: Cambridge school page hit by meme vandalism from temporary accounts; mostly reverted
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts added joke text to the Chesterton Community College (Cambridge, UK) article. The joke was the same meme in both cases: the school is "known for the meme 'Sh*t on it to assert dominance'". ClueBot NG reverted the first insertion (rev 1381174228). A second temporary account re-added it about three minutes later (rev 1381174504), and DonnieNova reverted that within seconds. The first account then added Tyler, the Creator as a "notable former pupil" (rev 1381174546), which is false. As of the last data I have, nobody had reverted that line. None of the edits gives a source or points to anything that happened in the real world. This is typical schoolkid vandalism, probably pupils sharing an in-joke, not a news event.

stories.headline: Vandalism on Czech Wikipedia's 'Cyril' name page, reverted by patroller within minutes
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The Czech Wikipedia page for the given name "Cyril" was hit by a short burst of joke edits. The account "JokerVeVězení67" ("Joker in prison 67") rewrote the opening to say a "Churaq Cyril" is a Czech rapper "in prison with Joker" (rev 26313427). A temporary account then added a made-up lawyer "David Kala" and the hashtag #FREECYRIL (rev 26313433). The first account came back and swapped the article's whole introduction for a line accusing a named private person, "Daniel Solik", of being a sexual predator (rev 26313434). That's a possible attack on a real person, which the oversight team may want to look at. About four minutes after the first edit, patroller OJJ used TwinkleGlobal to restore the last clean bot version (rev 26313436). The dossier's revert flags missed this rollback, and the Scout's "restructuring" guess was wrong. Nothing suggests a real-world event: no other languages were involved, and both vandal accounts edited only this page.

stories.headline: Jackson Goldstone page: no new edits since the reverted "ahoj" test edit
stories.summary: This update adds nothing new. The same three edits from the earlier brief are the only activity, and the graph shows no edits after rev 1381293718. A temporary account (~2026-56307-54) put the Czech word "ahoj" ("hi") into the bolded name in the lead (rev 1381293632; edit summary "dopsal jsem ahoj", "I added hi"). Komethere reverted it as vandalism about 40 seconds later. VocalCat2207 then removed a leftover leading space from the bolded name (rev 1381293718), which only changes formatting. The article's facts didn't change, including his 2021 junior world title, his 2022 junior World Cup overall title and his 2025 World Championship win in Champéry. The activity stayed on one page in one language, with no sign of a real-world event behind it.

stories.headline: De-wiki: Account removes JJ's Israel-ESC remarks as "harmful to artist"; quickly restored
stories.summary: An account called "Manifester Music", on its first and only edit, deleted the whole sourced section "Kritik an der Teilnahme Israels" from the German article on Johannes Pietsch (JJ, the 2025 Eurovision winner). The edit summary was "Schadet dem Künstler" ("harms the artist"). The deleted text covered his May 2025 call to exclude Israel from ESC 2026, his comparison of Gaza with Russia's invasion of Ukraine, criticism from Austrian officials including Van der Bellen and the IKG, and his partial apology. It cited Der Standard, Die Zeit, Kurier, ORF and others. Two minutes later, experienced editor Brettchenweber reverted it, saying that harm to the artist is not a reason to remove content. Ailura then made an 11-byte copyedit to the restored section. The account's name and edit summary point to a possible conflict of interest (management or label whitewashing), but I can't confirm who is behind it. There's no new real-world event here, and the large churn number is just the one deletion plus its undo. I didn't read the revert diff itself; its effect comes from its edit summary and the matching ±2657 bytes.

stories.headline: Argentine actor Antonio Grimau reported dead at 82, per es-wiki edits
stories.summary: Three separate editors updated the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Argentine actor Antonio Grimau (Antonio Rebolini, born 1944 in Lanús) within roughly 20 minutes to record his death. Wledao added a death date of 20 October 2026 (age 82) and later a place of death, Buenos Aires (rev 175917431, 175917586). A temporary account changed the lead to "1944–20 de octubre de 2026" (175917542). Ezarate, the most active of the three, added the current-event "fallecimiento" template with the comment "fallecio hoy" (175917719). None of the diffs I read added a source. Wledao says this was their first edit. The edits agree with each other and nobody reverted them, but no other-language Wikipedia page has moved yet. Treat this as a likely death report that has not been independently confirmed.

stories.headline: Liberal Party of Canada lead blanked twice and reverted; Nightcrawler vandalism also undone
stories.summary: The Scout read the 30,530 churn on en-wiki's Liberal Party of Canada page as a possible bulk edit. It is actually two section removals by one new account, both reverted, so each removal and its revert count twice. Harrylarrylivesinthequarry made both: rev 1381218018 removed 8,810 bytes with no edit summary, and rev 1381219722 removed 6,455 bytes with the summary "false information". Both diffs strip the sourced opening of the article: the party's name, its liberal ideology, its centre to centre-left position, and its standing as Canada's "natural governing party". Cannolis reverted the first ("unexplained content removal") and Alpha Beta Delta Lambda reverted the second through the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool. The page is restored, and the account has only these 2 edits. The second item in this story, already covered, was the infobox vandalism on Nightcrawler (character): the real name was twice changed to "Rainer Winkler" and twice reverted. Neither page shows a real-world event. These revert flags were not set, but the edit summaries make clear the edits were reverts. Nobody links the two pages except Cannolis, who patrols for vandalism. Watch only for more removals by the same account.

stories.headline: Catalan Wikipedia PSOE article vandalised by look-alike accounts, now reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Over about 10 minutes, two accounts with near-identical names ("Raul ayudas y becas" and "Raul becas y ayudas"), likely the same person, vandalised the Catalan Wikipedia article on PSOE. Rev 38981174 replaced the Ideology section's text on PSOE's purpose and its UGT ties with paragraphs about the Falange Española. Rev 38981179 changed the party's Spanish name in the lead to the slur "Partido Sexista Opresor Euskadi". Later edits, including 38981182, swapped in a vulgar version of the acronym ("Pvtas Sobre(s) Orgías Españolas"). Editor Docosong rolled back the last account's edits, then fully restored the original lead and Ideology text in 38981212 ("rv vandalisme"). Nothing similar showed up on the same article in other languages in this window. It doesn't point to any real-world event. Low priority; watch for the accounts coming back.

stories.headline: New itwiki article on Robert Hatem, ex-Hobeika bodyguard and author; no news hook
stories.summary: Stefantiz created a new Italian Wikipedia biography of Robert Maroun Hatem ("Cobra"). Hatem was a Lebanese Forces militiaman and bodyguard to Elie Hobeika, and wrote the 1999 book "From Israel to Damascus", which Lebanon banned. The article draws only on historical sources from 1999–2000 (The Nation, Middle East Quarterly, CPJ). It covers the book ban and the legal cases brought against journalists, including publisher Milhem Karam. Nothing in it points to a current event: no appointment, death, arrest or other recent development. The edits that followed were small cleanups: Stefantiz expanded the Bio template and added an approximate birth year of 1956, AndreA made a minor fix with the edit summary "epoca", and Lulo tidied the lead. There were no reverts. The page has no linked articles in other languages in the graph, and none of the editors worked on related pages. This looks like an ordinary new article, though we can't rule out that something offline prompted it.

stories.headline: Vandalism on Swedish Wikipedia list of Finnish islands; page blanking not yet reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not a news event. All the activity is on one page, svwiki "Lista över öar i Finland", and comes from two temporary accounts plus one established patroller. Temporary account ~2026-56229-96 first replaced the Kimitoön row with a broken row and the made-up entry "Lilla kimitoön" (rev 59785602). A second temporary account added a joke row with an area of "Lite mer än 5" ("a little more than 5"), "Kimito" and "Hav" ("sea") (rev 59785616). Patroller Tekannan rolled back the second account and then reverted the first (rev 59785624). After that, ~2026-56229-96 deleted the whole island table, more than 20 rows (rev 59785629), then the intro text (rev 59785631), then made one more removal (rev 59785633, not read). In the data I have, none of these deletions has been reverted, so the page may still be largely blank, though patrollers will probably restore it soon. Both temporary accounts targeting Kimitoön suggests the same person or a local prank, but I can't confirm that. No other languages or pages are involved.

stories.headline: JAXA's MMX Phobos sample-return probe launched on H3; en-wiki article cleaned up after launch
stories.summary: The English article on JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) already says the probe launched on 19 October 2026 at 19:41:03 UTC (20 Oct, 04:41 JST) from Tanegashima. It also says the launch vehicle flew as planned and spacecraft separation was confirmed. The cited sources are a JAXA launch-result press release, NASASpaceFlight and The Japan Times. The six edits in this window, made about a day after liftoff, are tidy-up work around that milestone, not new events. RickyCourtney named the rocket as an H3-24L (JAXA calls the flight H3 F10). Chattenoir added references for the instruments and spacecraft mass, and cut a long, off-topic Asterix aside in the IDEFIX rover section. Animalculum moved text around to create a History section. The one revert was Chattenoir undoing their own edit to fix a reference error, so this is not an edit war or vandalism. The edit that first added the launch text happened before this window and I did not read it. The graph shows no other-language versions of this page, so the launch rests on what the en-wiki article says and the sources it cites; I could not check it independently.

stories.headline: Vandalism on mn-wiki's The MongolZ and 'Information' pages, reverted in minutes
stories.summary: This is a short vandalism spree on Mongolian Wikipedia, not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-56126-27) made three edits in about four minutes. It blanked most of the general article Мэдээлэл ("Information") and put in obscene Latin-script Mongolian (revs 873851, 873852). It also replaced the intro of the esports team article The MongolZ with insults and renamed the team in its infobox (rev 873853). About 8–10 minutes later, established editor Zorigt rolled back both pages to their last good versions (revs 873854, 873855). The "large edit" the scout flagged is that rollback putting back about 4.7 KB of the Information article. None of these edits contain anything about tournaments, roster moves or any other real MongolZ news. No other editors or languages were involved and there was no back-and-forth reverting, so there's nothing worth watching further.

stories.headline: pt-wiki translates article on Germany's 2026 Merz government crisis; unrelated NGO page rewrite
stories.summary: This is translation work on Portuguese Wikipedia, not a breaking signal. Editor Leirbag reib created "Crise do governo alemão de 2026" (+6,345 bytes, rev 73259806). It describes an ongoing crisis around Chancellor Friedrich Merz that started on 14 July 2026, after a personnel scandal involving Jens Spahn and a badly received reshuffle. The article says it worsened after the 6 September Saxony-Anhalt state election, where the AfD won 43.8% and the CDU fell to 17.2%. It also cites an INSA/Bild poll in which 14% thought Merz was the right chancellor. Sources listed include Politico, the NYT, Die Zeit/dpa and Reuters, all with access dates of 20 Oct 2026. Daniel G Rego then tagged the page as "in translation" (rev 73259852), so it is a translation of an existing article in another language, not a new event. The second page, Centro de Liberdades Civis, is unrelated: Daniel G Rego rewrote it from the English article on the Ukrainian Nobel-winning NGO (rev 73259761), and another editor made a small tweak afterwards. The only link between the two pages is that one editor worked on both. There are no reverts or signs of conflict. The crisis described is plausible and well sourced in the text, but I have not checked any of it outside Wikipedia. The graph shows no other-language versions of the crisis article being edited right now, so I see no fresh trigger today.

stories.headline: US U-17 forward Maddie DiMaria credited with record 6 goals in 17-0 rout of Samoa
stories.summary: Nothing new changes the main story. The DiMaria biography hasn't been edited since the last brief: it still has 4 edits, the latest at ts 1792503249. It is still the only page here with real-world news, a sourced six-goal game in the US's 17-0 U-17 Women's World Cup win over Samoa on 19 Oct 2026. Since the last brief there is one new edit, rev 1381179303 on Barbara Strozzi. In it, DonnieNova put back "believed to be of Barbara Strozzi" in the infobox portrait caption, which Mariavanaalst had removed, and asked them to dispute it on the talk page. That makes three reverts of Mariavanaalst by three different patrollers. It is a slow-moving fight over who the portrait shows, not news. The graph still lists no other-language versions of the DiMaria page, so there is no sign of wider coverage. The "record at any level" claim remains unverified.

stories.headline: Japanese Wikipedia: style dispute over Invicta title names on two MMA bios, no news
stories.summary: The two pages share one subject: Virna Jandiroba (ビルナ・ジャンジロバ) and Yana Santos (ヤナ・サントス) are both former Invicta FC women's MMA champions. Two registered editors, Pikko 82 and TN Paak, were making formatting changes to both pages. Pikko 82 added "女子" (women's) to title names and shortened them to "IFC" (revs 111459603, 111459613, 111459628). TN Paak took "女子" back out and changed the label to "Invicta", explaining that "Invicta is itself a women's MMA promotion" (111459701, 111459723). In the latest edit, Pikko 82 adopted TN Paak's "Invicta世界バンタム級" wording in Santos's fight record (111459882), so the two seem to be settling on one style rather than reverting each other. None of the diffs I read add a new fight, result, signing or other current event, and no other language versions moved, so there is no sign of a real-world trigger. I'd suggest closing this or keeping only a low watch.

stories.headline: Italian 'Maranza' article: brief, resolved dispute over 'racist' label for 'anti-maranza' decree
stories.summary: Two established it.wiki editors argued over neutrality on the slang article 'Maranza'. One temporary account also made a small fix. There were no formal reverts. Sayatek added a paragraph saying Meloni-government majority parties picked up the term, and that one of the 2026 security decrees was nicknamed "anti-maranza". It cites Corriere della Sera (24 Jul 2026) and says this use highlights the term's discriminatory, racist side against second-generation people of North African origin, with support from L'Espresso, IDMO and a Il Fatto Quotidiano blog. Within about 10 minutes AnticoMu90 cut the 'racist' wording and the blog citation, saying Wikipedia cannot call a politician's decrees racist. About an hour later he put the wording back "come da richiesta" ("as requested"), which suggests it was settled on the talk page. Sayatek then restored the blog ref. That last edit also seems to have undone the temporary account's one-word grammar fix ("di") in the lead, probably by accident (edit conflict or editing an old version). The real-world facts were already known; they are not breaking news: the "anti-maranza" bill dates to July 2026. The page has no linked articles in other languages, and none of the editors worked on other pages. This is a routine NPOV disagreement that has calmed down, so we just need to watch for it starting up again.

stories.headline: De-wiki attack page about a 14-year-old flagged for speedy deletion; no news event
stories.summary: This is schoolyard vandalism, not a news story.
