A temporary account created the de-wiki page "Henry groß", which describes a 14-year-old boy in Saarland in mocking terms, says he is "weaker than Leon", and cites a Jimdo site as its source (rev 271499033). Established patroller RoBri tagged it for speedy deletion as "Zweifelsfreie Irrelevanz" (clearly not notable) about 5 minutes later (rev 271499346). A second temporary account then removed the "weaker/less intelligent" line, calling it insults and lies, but kept other disparaging text and left the deletion tag in place (rev 271500186). This looks like a dispute among teenagers playing out on Wikipedia. The page is likely to be deleted soon. Because it targets a named minor, we should not amplify it, and it needs no further monitoring.

stories.headline: Update: es-wiki 'Iglesia católica' vandalism burst fully reverted, no new activity
stories.summary: This is an update to the tracked vandalism story. It contains no new edits, and nothing points to a real-world event. I listed every edit on the page in the graph: the "3 editors, 6 edits, 5,504 churn" burst is the same incident already filed. Temporary account ~2026-55155-86 made three edits: inserting "I am the king of Joseon. Arrest all users using wikipedia." (+57), a 16-byte insertion, and deleting the 2.7 KB lead (-2,679). Patroller Jcfidy reverted the first two and the Automoderador bot reverted the third, each within about a minute. The churn figure is simply each edit plus its revert (57+57+16+16+2,679+2,679 = 5,504). It looks like "no reverts" because the revert edits aren't flagged as reverts, but their edit comments say they are. The diffs I read confirm the vandal text, the lead deletion and the bot's full restoration. The page is back to its earlier version. Two other temporary accounts appear in the dossier's editor list, but no edits by them show up in the page's edit history.

stories.headline: Rugrats pages hit by one temporary account swapping voice cast for rappers; reverted
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The cluster comes from one temporary account (~2026-56411-43), which made six edits in about 13 minutes to Tommy Pickles, The Rugrats Movie and Rugrats: A Live Adventure. In the two reverts I could read, the account had replaced the real voice actors E. G. Daily and Tara Strong with the rappers Young Jeezy and Rick Ross, including a made-up 'credited as ... Rozay' line. Three other editors (Staticspector, CantReadRunes and a second temporary account) undid every one of these edits within minutes, so the pages are back to normal. The 'large churn' on the live-show page was a +328/+78 edit by the same account, reverted as a 'grammar mess'. I couldn't load that diff, but its timing and author match the spree. The Creative industries edit (Inara1989, +23 'description', reverted by Staticspector) looks unrelated and was probably grouped in only because Staticspector reverted both. There is no sign of real cast or production news, and no other-language activity.

stories.headline: es-wiki Sydney/Adelaide tennis pages: cosmetic edits, Adelaide link break self-fixed; no news
stories.summary: This is still routine cleanup on the Spanish Wikipedia's Australian tennis-tournament articles, with no sign of a real-world event. The broken link my last brief flagged on the Adelaide page is fixed. In rev 175925172 the same temporary account (~2026-56281-91) changed the unclosed "[[Tenis|tenis" back to "[[tenis]]", so the lead displays properly again. The new activity is three edits to Torneo de Sídney, each from a different temporary account. Rev 175925713 (+523) adds photos to the titles section of four historical seven-time champions: Bromwich, Crawford, Court and Wynne Bolton. Rev 175925822 finishes a cut-off "ATP International Series ↓" table header. Rev 175925877 makes the same [[tenis]] to [[Tenis|tenis]] change seen earlier on the Marseille and Adelaide pages. Repeating that exact change suggests one person may be editing through several temporary accounts, but it is harmless and I can't confirm it. None of the edits add results, champions or schedule changes, and there are no reverts on these new edits.

stories.headline: Conductor Chaslin's it-wiki bio expanded by a new account; Epstein-files line moved down
stories.summary: Three edits on itwiki "Frédéric Chaslin" account for nearly all the churn. All three come from Unistage93, an account with 16 edits in total. Rev 152987995 adds a discography list using French-wiki citation templates. Rev 152988020 removes the sentence near the top that says his name appears in the 2026 "Epstein files" but that several elements quickly cleared him. The edit summary says the sentence was moved after "the final judgment" because the matter is no longer important. Rev 152989569 (+8 KB) rewrites the biography with promotional detail, including Genoese ancestry and a child-prodigy organ debut at Notre-Dame. Its summary says the Epstein matter was moved to the end "in light of the favourable outcome of judicial checks." Two experienced editors then did light cleanup: Maybe75 cut the ancestry line from the opening paragraph, and Egidio24 fixed citation template errors. There are no reverts and no activity on other language editions. This looks like a biography rewrite, possibly by someone close to the subject, and does not signal a new real-world event. One open point to watch: the edit summaries claim a "final judgment" and a "favourable outcome" in the Epstein matter, but nothing I read cites a source for that. The diffs were truncated, so I could not confirm where the Epstein sentence ended up or how it is now worded.

stories.headline: Self-described grandson's unsourced edits to Ponte Conde page reverted; no news signal
stories.summary: Two unrelated English biographies, each edited and then rolled back by the same patroller. No real-world event is evident. On Fernando Ponte Conde, user Fjponte made 6 edits in about 30 minutes. His Spanish edit notes say he is adding family details, life details, birth dates and a brother (Juan Ponte Conde) that he knows "as his grandson". That makes these personal, unsourced additions by a relative, a conflict of interest, not an article expansion driven by news. Patroller Vitorperrut555 then restored an earlier revision (net -991 bytes), citing "Added content without sources". Separately, on Jake Brimmer, a one-time editor (AvonRSC) added 120 bytes to "Personal life". The same patroller reverted it within a minute as an unsourced change to a biography of a living person. The diff tool failed for every revision, so the actual text is unconfirmed. This reading rests on edit summaries, byte sizes and timing.

stories.headline: Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything': one-word 'epic' edit reverted, then put back
stories.summary: The scout was right that this is routine. There were four edits to the en-wiki article on 'You Can See Everything' in about 15 minutes. The article covers the 2026 Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim documentary about Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans. Its own sources say the film was Telluride's secret screening on Sept. 7 and opens in theaters from A24 in October. ViewFromSomewhere fixed a link, changing 'Billy Evans (entrepreneur)' to 'Billy Evans (businessman)'. A temporary account (~2026-52170-33) added '[[Epic film|epic]]' to the opening line ('American epic documentary film'). T430s used a revert tool to undo that as vandalism, then undid his own revert less than a minute later, so the 'epic' wording stays for now. This is a dispute over one word, not an edit war, and none of the edits suggests a news event. The page has 75 edits over its life, so interest is steady because the film is new, but there is no sign of a spike right now.

stories.headline: ja-wiki #KAITO controversy article draws "not encyclopedic" tag on top of neutrality flag
stories.summary: Since the last brief, the new ja-wiki article 「＃KAITOを巡る騒動」 has had one more edit. It is about the fan clash between King & Prince's Kaito Takahashi, who uses "KAITO"/#KAITO as a solo name, and fans of Crypton's Vocaloid KAITO. Veteran editor 鈴音雨 added a {{百科事典的でない}} ("not encyclopedic") maintenance tag (rev 111463595, +52). Earlier, within about 10 minutes of each other, Syadosa added a neutrality tag and しみんかがく requested page protection. So three experienced editors have now flagged the article, and that points to a dispute over whether it should exist and how neutral it is, not to new facts about the real-world row. The page has 11 edits from 7 editors (3 of them temporary accounts) and no reverts, and nothing has been edited since about 1792582603. That doesn't fit the scout's reading of "ongoing expansion." What happens next is probably a deletion or merge debate. Caveat: none of the diffs would load this session, so this update comes from edit comments and graph metadata only. The content description is carried over from the prior brief.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) now listed as joint-strongest storm of 2026 Pacific season
stories.summary: Editors of the 2026 Pacific typhoon season article are updating it as Typhoon Champi (Philippine name Rosal) gets stronger. UNIDRAGON 734 changed the season's "strongest storm" field from Sinlaku alone to "Sinlaku & Champi" (rev 1381190476). StormL00ver then linked Champi's new standalone article, Typhoon Champi/Rosal (1381194778). MarioProtIV swapped in a newer satellite image dated 2026-10-20 14:20Z (1381183972, 1381194282). A separate Champi article is being built by StormL00ver. Its edit summaries (diffs not readable) say "JTWC updated pressure" and "JMA at 905 now", which would put Champi's central pressure at 905 hPa, a very intense typhoon. I couldn't confirm that figure or check landfall or impacts. The only reverts are routine fixes of broken redirects between MarioProtIV and StormL00ver, not a content dispute. Everything is on English Wikipedia so far, and other languages haven't picked it up.

stories.headline: Vandalism on UND football and coach Marv Helling pages reverted; no news event
stories.summary: Over about 13 minutes, one account (EditorKash) made five unexplained edits to two linked English Wikipedia pages. On 'North Dakota Fighting Hawks football' it deleted the whole conference-championships table (rev 1381237879, −1,431 bytes) and swapped the late coach Marvin Helling for a made-up 'Ajesh Rajesh' in the 1957–67 era section, linked to a Google redirect URL (rev 1381238425). On 'Marvin C. Helling' it removed his head-coaching record and his bowl wins from the lead (rev 1381237986). A second editor, LkL-70547, restored both pages within minutes, with edit summaries citing unexplained removal and spam links (revs 1381238727, 1381238855, 1381238944). This isn't a sports or obituary update: Helling died in 2014, and nothing here points to a real-world event. Contrary to the scout's note, the graph shows only two editors, and the 'restored revision' edits are reverts in practice. The graph shows EditorKash touching no other pages.

stories.headline: Lua Blanco pt-wiki: section merge, sibling links, new photo; 2026 death claim still unsourced
stories.summary: I read the four newest revisions to the Portuguese Wikipedia article on Lua Blanco, the Brazilian singer and actress from 'Rebelde'. They are all reorganisation and enrichment, with nothing new on her death. Guedexx merged the separate music and acting sections into one "Carreira" section with an "Estreia na atuação" subsection, and switched some mentions between "Lua" and "Blanco" (rev 73256786). Hernandofuente added a 2023 photo captioned "Lua em 2023" from Ibirapuera Park (rev 73256811), listed her brother Daniel Blanco in the infobox (rev 73256830), and linked his name in the biography (rev 73256848). There were no reverts. The three registered editors from the last update are still the only ones active, so this is ordinary collaborative cleanup, not an edit war. None of these diffs touch the 18 October 2026 death date or add a source or cause of death. The graph has no recent edits on linked articles in other languages, so I couldn't cross-check this round. The earlier caveat still applies: I haven't seen the edit that added the death or any citation for it.

stories.headline: Bots keep undoing temporary accounts' removal of Cuban/bolero roots from es-wiki 'Bachata'
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts kept deleting the same material from Spanish Wikipedia's Bachata article, and anti-vandalism bots put it back every time. Account ~2026-56073-77 made 7 edits. Rev 175921809 cut the lead sentence "Se considera un derivado del bolero" and the passage crediting Cuban son and Latin American tríos, with the summary "Ningún país debe tomarse atribuciones de la bachata que no le pertenece" ("No country should claim credit for bachata that isn't theirs"). A second account, ~2026-56242-59, made a nearly identical cut in rev 175921919: the lead line, the son/trío passage, and the etymology paragraph tying the word to 1920s Cuba (and Fernando Ortiz). It also added "República Dominicana" to the list of countries whose music influenced bachata. Its summary read "I think bachata doesn't derive from bolero nor is it a copy". SeroBOT and Automoderador reverted every edit within seconds to minutes. Those reverts appear only in the bots' edit summaries; the revert flag is false on all of them. There have been no edits since the last bot revert, no human editors took part, and this page has no linked pages in other languages in the graph. So this looks like a small, contained push about national origins that is now over, not a reaction to news. Because both accounts removed the same text with the same reasoning, they may be the same person, but I can't confirm that.

stories.headline: Oman sultan's page records UK honour swap with King Charles; banner vandalism cleaned up
stories.summary: The one new signal since the vandalism brief comes from a single editor, Walco1, and it points to a real event. Walco1 changed Sultan Haitham bin Tariq's foreign honours from "Stranger Knight Companion of the Order of the Garter" to "Honorary Knight Grand Cross of the Order of the Bath (GCB)", dated 20 October 2026 (rev 1381218344). The citation is an Oman Observer piece titled "HM, King of the United Kingdom exchange Orders". Two minutes earlier Walco1 undid their own earlier edit that had raised Charles III's Garter appointment count from 10 to 11 (rev 1381218095), and also touched the list of current Garter knights. Read together, the UK King and the Sultan of Oman appear to have exchanged orders today, and the sultan's award was first wrongly logged as the Garter. Caveat: this all rests on one editor and one cited source, and no other language or Oman page has moved yet. The es-wiki edit to Theyazin's honours that I read was routine: an April 2026 Kazakh Order of Friendship award (rev 175921291). The "Almighty God - the Nature11" banner spree on both Omani royal pages stays fully reverted with no new hits. On Akash Verma, temporary account ~2026-56246-79 undid Codename Noreste's revert once more (rev 1381217039), and Alpha Beta Delta Lambda reverted it. Pyrococcus furiosus got only a junk double comma from a different temporary account (rev 1381216309), reverted twice, and is unrelated.

stories.headline: Korean Wikipedia: blanking account keeps hitting sports council stub; Nt reverts again
stories.summary: This is still vandalism by one account, not a news event. After the first cleanup, the registered account 아정당모바일 blanked the new ko.wiki stub 전남광주통합특별시체육회 (the sports council for the merged Jeonnam-Gwangju special city) two more times. Each time it removed sections in steps and finished with the edit summary "문서를 비움" ("blanked the page") (revs 42687855, 42687865). Nt restored the full stub each time (e.g. rev 42687870). That makes three restorations of this page plus one of the Juche Tower article. The Juche Tower page (주체사상탑) has not been hit again since Nt restored it in rev 42687850. The scout counted no reverts because they are not flagged, but they show clearly in the edit summaries. The stub dates the council's founding to October 2026, which is around now, so a real body may have just been set up. Even so, it is one bare-bones page from a single creator and gives no sign of a wider news event. The account keeps coming back, so more blanking is likely unless it gets blocked.

stories.headline: Repeated '67' meme vandalism on German 'Klimaschutz' article, rolled back 3 times; no news
stories.summary: This is minor vandalism, not a news event. A temporary account (~2026-56272-14) changed the bolded lead term of de:Klimaschutz to "Klimaschutz 67" three times in about 4.5 minutes, adding 3 bytes each time. The section-heading edit summary on the first edit was misleading: the lead is what changed. Two established editors, Itti (twice) and Carol.Christiansen (once), undid each change with a standard rollback. The diffs I read show only the "67" being added and then removed. The "67" is most likely the "six-seven" meme. One correction to the scout's note: there were three reverts. The revert flag just wasn't set, but the rollback comments and diffs show them clearly. The page has had no activity since the last rollback, has no linked pages in other languages, and no involved editor touched any other page. This repeats the tracked Klimaschutz vandalism story and the earlier brief. I suggest merging it into that story and closing.

stories.headline: Penguin (character): same account makes 'Barnacott' name swap a third time
stories.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56288-75) has now changed the infobox real_name on en:Penguin (character) from "Oswald Chesterfield Cobblepot" to "Oswald Chesterfield Barnacott" a third time (rev 1381260584). Like the earlier tries, it has no source and an empty edit summary. Two different established editors (Rencoolguy, Bucket of Bubbles) reverted the first two within minutes. The graph shows no revert of the third edit yet, so the wrong name may be live for now. All of this is on one page in one language, with a single account pushing the change and nobody backing it. That points to persistent low-level vandalism, not a news event or a real content dispute. If it keeps going, page protection or a block is the likely next step.

stories.headline: Kyle Kennedy death entry on 'Kennedy curse' now cites USA Today, not just TMZ
stories.summary: The entry reporting the death of Kyle Francis Kennedy, granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy, at 42 at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, is holding on the English 'Kennedy curse' article. It now cites a stronger source. Temporary account ~2026-51450-31 replaced the original TMZ citation (rev 1381188198) with a USA Today report dated October 20, 2026 (rev 1381198959). They also added obituary wording saying her 2020 spinal cord injury caused "long-term paralysis, disability and other medical challenges" (rev 1381199488). The entry still says no cause of death has been announced. The scout's note was wrong on one point: nobody has disputed the death claim. The one revert was over a separate line about RFK Jr. and Cheryl Hines being at the 2026 White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting. Jpgordon removed it twice, Ivanhardybirt restored it once, and the matter went to the talk page. Still uncertain: the entry gives the death date as September 21, 2026, a month before both reports, and that has not been fixed or explained. The graph shows no separate article on her and no edits in other languages.

stories.headline: Chiikawa film page on ja-wiki protected after unsourced 'NHK Kōhaku' rumor insertions
stories.summary: This is not a release update. It is one account repeatedly adding an unsourced rumor. On the ja-wiki page for the film 映画ちいかわ 人魚の島のひみつ (Chiikawa: Mermaid Island Secret), the account 茶間田 kept adding text saying the film will appear on the 77th NHK Kōhaku Uta Gassen (the 2026 year-end show), with a medley and character appearances. The only source given is a claim that an "NHK insider" said so (rev 111457189 edit summary: "NHK内部の関係者より聞いた話", "heard from someone inside NHK"). The account also linked uploaded files it described as "NHK internal documents" and swapped the infobox logo for a "紅白R8-12.png" image. 茶間田 restored this text after 柏尾菓子 removed it (rev 111457150). The material was reverted again with Twinkle by 大夫将監, and 茶間田 restored it a second time (rev 111457379). 大夫将監 then filed a protection request (rev 111457399), and 柏尾菓子 added a pp-vandalism tag, which suggests the page has been semi-protected. Uncertainties: it's not clear whether the rumor text is still on the page, since the graph shows no revert after rev 111457379. I have no independent evidence that any Kōhaku booking exists, and the "internal documents" files may be fabricated or copyright violations. Before the war, an earlier version of the page said three characters were scheduled to appear on Kōhaku; I didn't check where that came from, so its origin is unverified.

stories.headline: Unsourced 'Andy Burnham' leader and left-wing edits reverted on Labour Co-op page
stories.summary: Two temporary accounts made three small infobox edits to the en-wiki "Labour and Co-operative Party" article within about 4 minutes. They changed the party's position from "Centre-left" to "Centre-left to left-wing" (rev 1381276923, edit summary: "Under Andy burnham… clearly shifting"), added "Democratic socialism" as an ideology (1381277031), and added "leader = Andy Burnham" (1381277425). The position change went against an in-page comment asking editors to discuss it on the talk page first. About 12 minutes later, experienced editor 10mmsocket undid all three as "unsourced / personal analysis" (1381278763), and nobody has re-added them, so this is not an edit war. Naming Burnham as leader implies a real change in Labour's leadership, but I found no sign of it elsewhere in the graph: no activity on pages for Burnham, Labour Party (UK) or Starmer, and no other languages moved. With no sources given and edits on one page only, this looks like speculative or partisan editing rather than a sign of real news. If Labour leadership pages start moving, it's worth checking again.

stories.headline: idwiki: 'anti-Chinese' tag on Kalla, Fadli Zon pages reverted; no new edits since
stories.summary: This is the same activity as the earlier brief. Nothing new has happened. User OnAir21 added [[Kategori:Tokoh anti-Tionghoa]] ("anti-Chinese figures") to the Jusuf Kalla and Fadli Zon articles. Henri Aja reverted both edits about five minutes later. The revert notes call the edits good-faith but say the category was "added without narrative explanation", meaning no sourced article text supports it. I checked the graph: neither editor has touched either page since the reverts, so the category has not been re-added and there is no back-and-forth. OnAir21 kept adding similar categories elsewhere (Khmer Merah, Bersiap, Apple Daily, Taiwanese party pages). Henri Aja has not reverted those. This is a dispute over category tagging on Indonesian Wikipedia, not a sign of a real-world event. It touches biographies of living people, so it is worth watching only if OnAir21 re-adds the tag.

stories.headline: Hidalgo infobox vandalism reverted; small Cavendish nationality dispute quiet
stories.summary: This isn't a news event. On Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, one temporary account (~2026-56397-03) made four junk edits to the infobox, for example changing his service years from "1810–1811" to "2077-638384". HMSLavender and TonySt (using the Interceptor tool) reverted each one within seconds to minutes. On Nicola Cavendish, another temporary account (~2026-56273-44) twice rewrote her as a "British actress": it switched the short description, the English-variant tag, the lead sentence and the categories from Canadian to British, and called her Canadian citizenship unsourced. HMSLavender restored the Canadian wording, citing MOS:NATIONALITY, Wikipedia's style rule on describing nationality. The only link between the two pages is HMSLavender, the same patroller. A graph check shows no edits on either page since the last revert, so this updates nothing in the earlier brief. The citizenship point could come back if someone produces a source, but there's no sign of anything happening in the real world.

stories.headline: es-wiki Caso Negreira and Reloj de sol: small vandalism, some still live, no news
stories.summary: I checked the earlier brief and found nothing new: neither page has been edited since SeroBOT's revert at ts 1792509455. On Caso Negreira, a temporary account put "Hala Madrid." at the start of the lead (rev 175919243), which is football-rivalry trolling. A second temporary account then deleted the infobox and changed the lead's first words to "." (rev 175919487). SeroBOT rolled the page back to the last edit by the first vandal, so "Hala Madrid." is still live. So is an infobox defendant entry, "-Adrián pozo berenguer", whose formatting doesn't match the other entries and may be an inserted private name. That entry was already there before this burst, and I haven't confirmed who added it. On Reloj de sol, a temporary account renamed the "Historia" heading to nonsense (rev 175919440) and SeroBOT reverted it. G.r.gddd then changed the heading to "Historia 67" (rev 175919479), the same "67" meme, and that edit has not been reverted. The two pages share no editors except the bot. There is no sign of a real-world event or of a coordinated campaign. A human patroller should clean up what's left.

stories.headline: German Amy Winehouse article: slang vandalism added twice, reverted twice; no news
stories.summary: This is the same vandalism incident already tracked, not a news event. A new account, Fuslimburgerotto, has two edits in total. Both times it added the joking slang sentence "Sie erzfitscherte an Alkohol" ("she drank herself to death") to the end of the lead in the German article on Amy Winehouse (rev 271487848, then 271487886). Patrollers undid it each time within about 20–25 seconds: Horst Gräbner first (271487855), then Serols using the anti-vandalism tool Huggle (271487898). One correction to the scout's note: there were two reverts. The graph doesn't flag them as reverts, but the edit comments and the diffs show they were. There are no other edits to this article and none to its versions in other languages in the graph, and nothing suggests a real-world trigger. I recommend closing this and merging it with the existing story.

stories.headline: Anonymous for the Voiceless vandalism reverted; no new activity since cleanup
stories.summary: This is the same set of 8 edits on one en-wiki page that the earlier vandalism brief already covered, and nothing has been added since. One temporary account, ~2026-55260-41, swapped "Cube of Truth" (the group's street-outreach method) for joke names like "Cube of Weed", "Cube of Kardashians", "Cube of Death eater" and "Cube of People that need a spanking". I read the diffs to confirm this. Patroller T430s used RedWarn to restore the last good revision and tagged it as vandalism (rev 1381203316). DonnieNova undid the account's last two attempts, the final one at rev 1381203696. A graph query found no edits to the page after that revert, and no other pages or languages were touched. It's one account vandalising and patrollers cleaning up, not an edit war, and nothing points to a real-world event. Unless the account comes back, this needs no more attention.

stories.headline: ruwiki: anti-vandal bot twice reverts accurate Aristotle citation on Plato's Unwritten Doctrine
stories.summary: This is not a news event. On the ruwiki article «Неписаное учение» (Plato's unwritten doctrine), a temporary account added a citation (+87 bytes) twice. The added text says Aristotle first used the term in the Physics (209b) and explains it in Book I of the Metaphysics. The anti-vandal bot EyeBot rolled it back automatically both times (ORES ~0.73), and a second temporary account then undid the bot's revert, putting the citation back. The scout's note is wrong on one point: the graph marks none of these edits as reverts, but three of the five are reverts (two by EyeBot, one undoing EyeBot). The edit itself is a sound scholarly correction: Physics 209b is the usual source for Aristotle's phrase 'agrapha dogmata'. It looks like an ordinary bot false positive, not vandalism or a real edit war. The two temporary accounts may be the same person, but I can't confirm that. If EyeBot reverts again it could turn into a small bot-vs-human loop, but nothing here points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Arabic 'Global warming' article: two low-quality edits undone by patroller
stories.summary: This isn't news. On Arabic Wikipedia's الاحتباس الحراري (Global warming, Q7942), two one-time accounts made pending (unreviewed) edits. One (77035657) mangled the lead sentence by inserting the word "مرتفع" ("high") with no space before it. The other (77035702) garbled a lead paragraph: it added the word "الخبيثه" ("malignant") and repeated a phrase, and its edit summary is a schoolbook-style definition. The regular editor باسم (48 edits) then undid both pending edits at once, restoring revision 77015983 (77035731). The scout's note said there were no reverts, but the diff and edit summary show 77035731 is a rollback. The churn of 254 is just these small changes (+15, +112) plus the −127 undo; nobody changed any substance. Nothing points to a real-world event, an edit war or organised vandalism. It looks like ordinary well-meaning but poor edits, possibly from students, caught by pending-changes review.

stories.headline: Kole Nedelkovski page quiet after second revert; Pan Radio and Mantis reverts unrelated
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The last edit to any of the four pages was SuperFastSpellChecker's restore of the ZackBot version of Kole Nedelkovski (rev 1381238303). I read that diff. It takes out the unsourced "Two brothers: Kiro, Slave", the misused native_name_lang field and the "Krstev"/"M'skavici" spellings, and puts the "Bulgarian" label back in the opening line. Temporary account ~2026-56256-86 has not come back to either Nedelkovski or Yoakim Karchovski, so this stays a stalled, one-sided push of national framing rather than an edit war. The Pan Radio edit (rev 1381237449) is a separate case: a user rewrote the infobox to say the Bijeljina station renamed itself "SIM Radio" (founded 22 Dec 2023, website simradio.net) and cut the sourced 1997 founding date. The renaming may be real, but it is old news, and the edit was reverted as unexplained content removal. The Mantis edit, an unsourced change to the species count, was also reverted. Neither is linked to the Macedonian dispute, and nothing here points to a current real-world event.

stories.headline: it-wiki new-page patrol: three unrelated new articles tagged by one patroller
stories.summary: There is no news event here. The only thing linking these three it-wiki pages is the patroller Cipintina, who tagged each of them within about 12 minutes while reviewing new pages. The pages are: 1) 'Studio Tecnico Lux', created by a first-time account and sent for speedy deletion as promotional ("IMO voce pubblicitaria"). It appears to have been deleted already; an earlier brief found its revisions unreadable, so I did not try again. 2) 'Gregor Seberg', a new biography of an Austrian actor (born Graz, 1967) translated by Fonn Jacopo. Cipintina added an {{NN}} notability-check tag to it (rev 152995880). 3) 'Chiesa di San Paolo Apostolo (Como)', a new article with sources about the parish church in Sagnino, built 1989–94. Its creator expanded it, and Cipintina did a small cleanup. None of the diffs mention any recent event. This is routine maintenance.

stories.headline: es-wiki self-promo bio of teen YouTuber 'Enix' tagged for speedy deletion
stories.summary: The four editors were all reacting to one new page, not to anything happening in the world. A temporary account (~2026-56093-11) created the es-wiki article 'Enix (Progamer537)' (rev 175919941, +3.4 KB). It is a biography of a Spanish content creator born in 2007, with personal details like a sister's name, social-media handles and follower counts. Nearly every sentence is marked {{cita requerida}} (citation needed), and the only source is a youth-football profile. About three minutes later, VietwaveTo9791 tagged it for speedy deletion as promotional, criterion G3 (rev 175919964). General de brigada Antonio swapped that tag for a milder 'needs references' tag (rev 175920073), and Casisgaal undid that and put the deletion tag back (rev 175920089). That was a single tag swap and an undo, not a back-and-forth edit war, and the page will most likely be deleted. I can't tell whether the editor who removed the tag is linked to the page's creator.

stories.headline: Spanish Wikipedia vandalism spreads to Sol LeWitt with antisemitic edits; reverted
stories.summary: The Scout called the new 'Sol LeWitt' page routine, but it is part of the same es-wiki vandalism run by temporary accounts. The edits are antisemitic. Temporary account ~2026-56135-31 made three changes: it set LeWitt's art movement to "Diarrea" (rev 175920123), changed his religion from Judaísmo to "Nacionalsocialismo" (rev 175920184), and rewrote "a family of Jewish immigrants" as "nazis" (rev 175920231). Letstown undid these (rev 175920235, and rev 175920241, which put the infobox back). A second account, ~2026-56209-76, then re-added the same changes and also changed "of Jewish origin" in the lead to "nazi" (rev 175920288). The repeat by a fresh account suggests the same person switching accounts, or people working together. Letstown undid rev 175920288 in rev 175920292, which is the page's latest edit. I could not load that diff, so I'm relying on its undo comment and its delta (−6, matching +6) to say the page is clean. The graph's revert flag shows false for all these undos, which is likely why the Scout saw "no reverts". The earlier vandalism on Computadora, Björk and Ariel Miramontes (covered in prior briefs) is all reverted. There is no real-world event behind any of this.

stories.headline: BBC Three, BBC Scotland channels now listed as "outgoing" after closure announcement
stories.summary: This updates the earlier brief. English Wikipedia editors are still writing up the BBC's 20 October 2026 announcement that the BBC Three linear channel will close for a second time. Benmathieson901 merged the closure text into a section now called "Reverting back to a Digital service". The merged text names BBC Scotland and BBC Radio 4 Extra as closing too, and adds "in spring 2027" as the timing (revs 1381224153, 1381224509, 1381224596). An editor without an account then changed the opening sentence of both the BBC Three and BBC Scotland (TV channel) articles to call each an "outgoing" channel (revs 1381226170, 1381226123). An earlier BBC Scotland edit by Abdullahi Mohamed 103 backs up the details: closure from spring 2027, part of cuts meant to save £500m, with the brand kept on iPlayer and Scottish programmes moving to BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland (rev 1381219612). The sources cited are still Deadline, The Standard and The Guardian. Activity is in English only, from a handful of editors, with no reverts. That looks like routine write-up of a real announcement, not a dispute. Still uncertain: no exact switch-off date, and I haven't read the Radio 4 Extra diff.

stories.headline: One patroller reverts three unrelated low-level edits; no news event
stories.summary: Three English Wikipedia pages are grouped here only because one recent-changes patroller, 420yeahh, reverted an edit on each within about 17 minutes. There is no shared real-world event. New since the last brief: on Balwyn High School (Melbourne), the account WikepediaDev108343 made three edits that added unsourced "notable alumni" who appear to be private individuals: "Luke Rizk - Basketballer", "Lucas Antonopoulos - Twitch Streamer" and a chef (rev 1381236513). One edit inserted self-promotion, "Follow lkings on Twitch", before that account removed the entries itself (rev 1381236998). 420yeahh then restored the earlier version, citing "No references provided" (rev 1381237473). That revert also undid a sports-field sentence and a typo fix. This looks like student or vanity editing, not news. The earlier findings still stand: a vanity tag on Twerking was reverted within about 100 seconds, and an unsourced lead rewrite on Yellowstone Schools was reverted as unexplained. I could not re-fetch those two diffs this round, so I am relying on the prior brief for them. Only English pages moved, and no other editors are involved.

stories.headline: Allen Bailey death claim now cites four X posts from ex-teammates and KC media; not confirmed
stories.summary: Temporary account ~2026-56257-93, which has pushed the October 20, 2026 death date from the start, edited the English Wikipedia article on former Chiefs/Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey again (rev 1381270478, +895). The edit puts "death_date=October 20, 2026" in the infobox and cites four X posts, all dated October 21: @JeffAllen71 (the Chiefs offensive lineman who wore No. 71 had this name; the edit summary calls him a Kansas City radio host), @Farzin21 (Farzin Vousoughian), @klseaboldt (Kurtis Seaboldt, Kansas City broadcaster) and @COLINMcCARTHY52 (Colin McCarthy, described as a college teammate). The edit summary also names Dwayne Bowe, Derrick Johnson and Cyrus Gray as former teammates who posted on Instagram/X. It tells editors not to remove the date "unless you have proof of him being alive" and admits there is no obituary yet. The diff adds the death_date line rather than just the references, so the earlier cited version was probably changed at some point. I couldn't pin down how. MakaylaHippo1998's rollback (rev 1381270300) removed only another temp account's "Died: October 20, 2026" line. As of the latest graph data, nobody has reverted the new edit in about 8 minutes. Several named people from Bailey's NFL and Kansas City circles all point to the same day, so a real death looks more likely than it did earlier today. Still, nothing comes from mainstream news, I haven't seen the text of the posts, social media doesn't meet Wikipedia's sourcing rules for living people, and there are no other-language articles to cross-check. The pressure-style edit summary also makes a new revert or edit war likely.

stories.headline: Larva (TV series) vandalism: no new edits since last brief, page still restored
stories.summary: There has been no new activity. The graph has the same four edits on Larva (TV series) as the earlier brief, and nothing after PhilKnight's revert at ts 1792513389. I re-read the second joke edit by temporary account ~2026-56223-58: it says Chuck was "on the pole dancing team" and "looks like jesus". PhilKnight's revert puts back the original Chuck entry, so the page is clean. One new detail: before the Larva edits, the same account made one edit to Christopher Auchter (rev 1381192453). It added "canada", a broken link label, and "one of the animations he created was The Mountain of Gaana, a great film." That reads as a clumsy good-faith edit with an opinion in it, not vandalism, and so far nobody has reverted it. This is low-level vandalism by one person with no link to anything in the real world. Merge with the tracked story or close.

stories.headline: pt-wiki Gaza War page: one user's disruptive edits reverted twice; no news
stories.summary: This is not a real-world news event. All four edits come from one editor, Ana Maria Gallizi Debetio, and two others reverting her. Her first edit (rev 73259522, −308) removed image captions from the 'Guerra de Gaza' article, including "a child wounded in Gaza," along with captions for two pro-Palestinian protest images. Daniel G Rego reverted it. Her second edit (rev 73259606, +661) added nonsense in all caps claiming to be "HIGHNESS ANA MARIA GALES OF UNITED KINGDOM" and "I was there and I'm not a child." It also added an unrelated 1975 biochemistry citation and a Facebook link in place of the caption. LupusLiber reverted that edit 57 seconds later. The scout's "no reverts" flag is wrong: both rollbacks say so in their edit comments. The 1,938 "churn" is just the add-then-revert cycle, and the article is back to where it was. One account, possibly with a personal grievance about the photo, is making disruptive edits. Watch for more attempts, but there is nothing to report.

stories.headline: No new edits since last brief; Ningning Jennie line stays out, Hopepunk hatnote back
stories.summary: The scout was right: nothing has changed since the previous brief. I queried the graph for edits on this story's eight pages after rev 1381257000 (ts 1792548895) and got zero results. I re-read the two latest diffs. On Ningning (1381257000), Adakiko removed the line saying she named Jennie as her role model, sourced to a 2020 Hankyung article, as "not found in source". He kept the Frank Ocean sentence, which cites Billboard. So for now the editor who kept deleting the Jennie line got the outcome they wanted, through a patroller's sourcing check rather than their own edits. On Hopepunk (1381256898), Pppery's main account put back the {{Distinguish|Hopecore}} hatnote that his Huggle alt had wrongly reverted. This is ordinary patrol churn, not vandalism, and the page has no other activity. Everything in the earlier brief still stands: the Azerbaijani Armed Forces article is back after an IDF page-replacement hoax, and Kibgkide's infobox vandalism has been reverted. All of this is en-wiki only, with no sign of a real-world event. The one open question is whether the temporary accounts on Ningning start a new dispute now that the line is gone.

stories.headline: PHP2Shell goes to German Wikipedia, which cites Reuters and CERT-EU on attacks and taking sites offline
stories.summary: The PHP2Shell story (CVE-2026-109618/109619) now has a second-language article. Berghest created a German page (de rev 271505582) that is stronger than the English one in both claims and sources. It cites a CERT-EU advisory, The Hacker News, Reuters ("Cyber agency warns websites may go dark as PHP prepares critical fix") and the UK NCSC. According to the German text, Cloudflare confirmed on 21 Oct that attacks using the exploit had started. The PHP Foundation's patches cover PHP 8.2 and later only. CERT-EU advises isolating vulnerable older applications and taking them off public networks. The release was moved up from 22 Oct because details had leaked on forums. On English Wikipedia, rev 1381293677 confirms Ca changed the embargo date from "22nd November" to "22nd October at 15:00 UTC", and rev 1381293746 is a one-word wording change. The English page has had no new edits since Padgriffin's Cloudflare edit, and later German edits by Berghest and M2k are category and typo fixes. There are no reverts and no vandalism. The Reuters, NCSC and CERT-EU citations make the exploitation-before-patch claim more credible than the single X post on English Wikipedia. However, I haven't checked those sources myself. Two references are dated "2016", clearly typos. The patch time doesn't match across pages: 14:00 CEST on German Wikipedia versus 14:00 UTC earlier on English. It is still unclear whether the patch has shipped.

stories.headline: Crumpet vandalism reverted; Clinton endorsements list page only got a citation fix
stories.summary: The English "Crumpet" article was vandalised by a temporary account (~2026-56204-31) and a new account (Henerythehippo). The last edit added "you need a diet by the way" to the history section. Patrollers EndTheWikiEditor, Pppery (alt) and Staticspector reverted every edit within minutes. The only reason the "List of Hillary Clinton 2016 presidential campaign celebrity endorsements" page is in this story is that patroller Pppery also edited it. It is not part of the vandalism. On that page, a temporary account tried in good faith to fix a broken <ref> tag on Hayden Panettiere's entry, which had been hiding other endorsements, but got the syntax wrong. Pppery (alt) reverted that, and Pppery then fixed the tag properly by changing "<ref/>" to "</ref>". The edit changed no content and doesn't point to any news. Every edit was on English Wikipedia, there were no edit wars between established editors, and nothing here points to a real-world event.

stories.headline: Norwegian 'Viktor' name page vandalized twice, fully restored; nothing new
stories.summary: This is vandalism, not news, and there has been no activity since the last brief. The page still has the same four edits. A temporary account (~2026-56143-85) twice replaced the name infobox and intro on no.wikipedia's 'Viktor' with a joke line about what looks like a private person. Edit 26007019 added "…er navnet til Viktor stølan aas, han bor på heistad", which includes a place of residence. Edit 26007026 added a shorter line without the place. Anne-Sophie Ofrim and Patandor rolled back each edit within minutes. I have now read Patandor's revert (26007030), and it restores the full infobox and intro, so the article is back to its last good version. Two corrections to the earlier brief: the graph shows 2 edits from the vandal account, not 3, and only the first joke line named the place. Because the vandal targeted an apparent private individual, admins may want to hide those revisions, but there is no news here.

stories.headline: Czech 'Operating system' article vandalized a third time by same account; reverted again
stories.summary: This is a third round of the vandalism already tracked on the Czech Wikipedia article "Operační systém". It is not a news event. The scout's note said there were no reverts this time, but that's wrong. The same temporary account (~2026-56242-41) made a third edit (rev 26315302, +8) to the Unix history section. It changed "Unix" to "onix", "operačních systémů" (operating systems) to "operačních operátorů" (operating operators), and "moderní" (modern) to "prehistorický" (prehistoric). About 90 seconds later MichalCZE fully restored JirkaSv's version (rev 26315304, −8). The graph doesn't flag that edit as a revert, but its comment and diff show it was one. So three vandal edits have now been undone by three different editors (OJJ, JirkaSv, MichalCZE). It's still one page in one language, and nothing points to a real-world trigger. The only open question is whether the account carries on, which could lead to page protection or a block.

stories.headline: India's Asian Para Games page logs more athletics finals; routine live results editing
stories.summary: This continues the tracked story on "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" (en only). Since the last brief, the same small group of registered editors has made a few more small edits, with no reverts and no anonymous disruption. Abesh2023's athletics edits (revs 1381288090, 1381288467) change sprint entries marked "21 Oct" into final results. Dilip Gavit is listed with gold in 10.69. One athlete is listed with silver in 10.72, marked as a Games record. Another is listed with gold in 12.02, also marked as a Games record. Pranav Desai is listed with bronze in 11.96. The edits also bold the names of finalists including Mohammed Basil, Simran Sharma and Preethi Pal. I couldn't load the diffs for the newer cycling and medalist edits (1381287945, 1381287647), so I can't confirm whether the medal table has been updated past 50. Event names and some athlete-to-time pairings aren't clear from the diffs, and none of these results have been checked against official sources.

stories.headline: es.wiki vandalism cluster quiet; Maracena unchanged, only a Freeform slogan edit is new
stories.summary: Nothing new has happened in the real world. This is the same es.wiki vandalism story, and it is winding down. Maracena has had no edits since Castellónenred's undo at 175931199, so the scout is right that it is continuation, not a new event. But Maracena's churn was vandalism that patrollers reverted by hand, not "no reverts". Across all five pages, the only edit since the last brief is on Freeform (175931239): temporary account ~2026-56292-24 added a Spanish gloss to the infobox slogan, "A little forward" → "(Un poco atrevido)". This is the same account's fourth or fifth try at adding translations (see 175931189, which glossed "A New Kind of Family" in the History section). Castellónenred and Automoderador have reverted similar edits before. It looks like a persistent good-faith edit, not vandalism, and it was not reverted as of the last event. Carmen Martínez-Bordiú, Río, Castor and Maracena are all quiet and clean, and no other language editions moved.

stories.headline: Indonesia Para Games page adds 400m T11 silver; India medal count jumps on a temporary account's edit
stories.summary: Editors are still adding results to "Indonesia at the 2026 Asian Para Games" on English Wikipedia, with no conflict. Yogwi21 added a silver for Taufik Abdul Karim in the men's 400 m T11, dated 21 October (rev 1381292297), and changed his name in the athletics table from "Taufik Karim" to his full name (rev 1381292208). The "2026 Asian Para Games medal table" page now has activity too, and that is the one thing to watch. A temporary account raised India's bronze count from 15 to 16 (rev 1381292418), which is a normal one-step update. Nineteen minutes later a different temporary account changed India's count from 12/11/16 to 14/20/24 (rev 1381292836). That is +2 gold, +9 silver and +8 bronze in one edit, with no edit summary and no source, which is out of line with the step-by-step changes elsewhere. A regular editor, Gol Golaby, edited the table 19 seconds later (rev 1381292854). The diff wouldn't load, so I can't tell whether it undid the jump, and the graph doesn't mark it as a revert. Nothing on the medal table has been checked against official results, and the Indonesia entries still have no citations.

stories.headline: Abel de Jesús eswiki vandalism turns defamatory: fake arms-trafficking and terror-link claims
stories.summary: The vandalism pile-on on the Spanish Wikipedia bio of Carmelite friar Abel de Jesús is still going, and it has gotten more serious. The page has 11 edits from 5 throwaway or temporary accounts in about 23 minutes. None of these accounts has edited any other page, and the graph shows no reverts. The largest new edit (rev 175930890, +1207) adds a fake lead paragraph. It calls him a "fictional character" tied to international arms trafficking and organized crime, and says he supplied weapons to real terrorist organizations. The only citation is an unrelated nursing-journal DOI. On a living person's biography, that is defamatory content, not just a joke. Another account (rev 175930878) adds an invented book praising Netanyahu, worded with the antisemitic "Masonic-Jewish" framing seen in earlier edits. One edit (rev 175930871) actually removes two earlier joke entries, the Google-thumbnail image and the "reborn as a dung beetle" death place. That looks like the vandals tidying up or competing, not a real cleanup. Nothing points to a real-world news event. The unverified housing-speculation and Israel themes may reflect an online controversy about him, but no sourced edit supports that. This needs patroller attention as a defamation risk.

stories.headline: itwiki: new Ehud Ya'ari article created with a different journalist's bio; no news hook
stories.summary: This is routine article creation on Italian Wikipedia, not news. The "Ehud Ya'ari" page was created by Stefantiz (rev 152998740, +4,076 bytes). The text is actually a biography of Eitan Haber, Rabin's aide, who died on 7 October 2020. It even names Ya'ari only as Haber's co-author on "The Year of the Dove" (1979), so it looks like a copy-paste error or the wrong title. Lulo then removed a link from the page to itself (rev 152998745). Stefantiz's follow-up edits, including adding a photo of "the journalist" on the Golan Heights, couldn't be fetched, so I can't confirm whether the content was fixed. Stefantiz's recent edits are a steady run of new Israel-related articles (Ze'ev Schiff, Noam Braslavsky, Robert Hatem, Homesh, Sa-Nur, Kadim), which fits a long-term writing project rather than a reaction to events. The second page, a new article on Ferdinand Bol's painting "Aeneas Crowning Cloanto" by a temporary account, is plain art-history work that Lulo tidied up. There are no reverts, no other languages involved, and nothing in the text that ties to current events.

stories.headline: Dewiki Brausewetter bio: duplicate wikilink undone; cleanup still routine
stories.summary: The only new edit on the German Wikipedia biography of Richard Brausewetter (1866–1916), the WWI officer and Kölnische Zeitung front correspondent, is a small revert. Gezeitengarten undid Fruchtjoghurt00's +21-byte edit (rev 271505561) with a matching −21-byte revert (rev 271505646). The edit summary gives the reason as "Weiter oben bereits verlinkt" (already linked further up). That points to a duplicate wikilink being removed under the usual style rule of linking a term only once, not a dispute over content. Neither diff would load this round. What I say about their content comes from the edit summaries, the byte counts and the previous brief's reading of rev 271505561. This is one page in one language, with one revert that nobody has reversed back. There's no sign of an edit war, vandalism or a news event. Why the page is getting this much attention is still unknown; an article-improvement or review push is the likeliest reason.

stories.headline: Vietnamese Michael Olise page restored again after third wave of prank vandalism
stories.summary: This updates the existing vandalism story on the Vietnamese Wikipedia "Michael Olise" article. It is not a new event. After the temporary-account edits in the last brief, account Tinhnguyenyt5 (75657951, +117) added one more fake item: a youth spell at Vietnamese club Hoàng Anh Gia Lai, 2018–2019, in the infobox. About a minute later Nguyenquanghai19 (75657952) rolled the page back to MrMisterer's clean version 75657842. That rollback removed the Hoàng Anh Gia Lai entry and the fake "born in Bình Dương, Vietnam" line, brought back the sourced paragraph on his birth in Hammersmith, London, and turned "Moiden" back into "Anh" ("he"). The diff shows the rollback also undid the earlier temp-account edits, including 75657911. I didn't read that edit's content directly. The graph has nothing after 75657952, so as of the last edit the page is clean. The scout said there were no reverts. That's only because the graph didn't tag them: 75657952 is clearly a rollback. All of this happened on one page in one language, with no real transfer or other news behind it. Another wave is possible, since this is the third burst; the page may need protection.

stories.headline: Luol Deng page: temp-account prank edits reverted; no real-world news
stories.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56303-83) made two prank edits to Luol Deng's English Wikipedia article. The first added "also friends with will hays" to the short description. The second added "also his friend will hays is now a player" to the end of the lead. Two patrollers reverted them within about a minute (Wafflerrs, then Komethere using VandalHandle, which tagged it as disruption). The same account's only other edit, a minute or two earlier, was on an unrelated article about a Ukrainian village, Fyholivka. It added "finley land" with the edit summary "because i own it", so this looks like a single prankster, not a dispute. No other editors, languages, sourced content, or later edits appear, so this isn't an edit war or a real event. It matches the earlier brief, and there's nothing new to report.

stories.headline: Likely company whitewash of Hebrew Wikipedia's Atraf article reverted by patroller
stories.summary: All three edits fall within about 16 minutes on the Hebrew Wikipedia article for Atraf, an Israeli LGBT dating app. They show sourced critical content being removed and then put back. Nothing here points to a new real-world event. A temporary account removed about 8.3k bytes (rev 44097212) with the comment "a few irrelevant entries – we are adapting the article for AI engines." That edit cut the Criticism and Crime sections (2009 credit-card theft, robbery and child-prostitution cases, sourced to Haaretz and Ynet) and the section on the 2021 Black Shadow hack of operator CyberServe. It also replaced the lead with brochure-style text and changed the website field to atraf.com. Registered user YAROMEGATRON then cut about 1.6k more bytes of the dating-history section as "repeated info" (rev 44097241) and added links to atraf.co.il in the lead. Patroller שיפוץ-ניק used TwinkleGlobal to restore the last good revision, calling it "massive removal without visible justification" (rev 44097258), so the net change is about zero. The "we" in the first edit summary suggests the company or someone working for it made the edit, but I can't confirm that. The graph doesn't flag the restore as a revert, though in practice it is one. Each editor has touched only this page, and no other language editions were checked.

stories.headline: VisionQuest page: small Paladin-sentence dispute between two editors flares up again
stories.summary: The prior brief said to check again if the Paladin sentence kept flipping, and it has. On the English VisionQuest article, Marco camino 10 removed for a second time the clause saying Paladin has met the Punisher, Werewolf by Night and Daredevil (rev 1381294759). The edit summary reads "Here we go again" and complains that the other editor restored it without explaining why. MillenniumGeneration had put the clause back with the comment "It is worth mention" (rev 1381294017). That makes two removals and one restore between the same two editors, about 20 minutes apart. It is still below the three-revert rule, and so far it is a content disagreement, not vandalism. Separately, MillenniumGeneration made a routine update (rev 1381294666): it renames the Human Torch entry to "J.I.M. / Synthetic Man" and credits Phineas Horton as his creator, sourced to a Polygon explainer dated Oct 20, 2026. This is ordinary fan upkeep of an airing show, not a real-world news event. Only one page and one language are involved. I'm calling it a low-level edit war to watch, not a news story. If the clause goes back in again, a talk-page discussion or page protection would be the next thing to look for.

stories.headline: ru-wiki: new 'Niamey airport attack' page is a 2023 coup retrospective, now a redirect
stories.summary: This is not news about a current event. A temporary account created the ru-wiki page «Нападение на аэропорт Ниамея» ("Attack on Niamey airport", rev 155731681, +4952 bytes). The text describes the July–August 2023 military coup in Niger: troops under Gen. Tchiani took Diori Hamani airport on 26–27 July 2023, and France and Italy ran evacuation flights on 1–2 August. It also covers the airspace closure on 6 August 2023. The draft looks like it was pasted from a rendered page (it even includes the "From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia" header line). About 6.5 minutes later a second temporary account replaced it with a redirect to «Захват международного аэропорта в Ниамее» (rev 155731778, −4860). An experienced editor then made a −1 byte fix that, judging by its size and edit comment, removes the stray brace in the redirect (I didn't read that diff). The 9,813 bytes the scout saw are just this create-then-redirect cycle: no new event was described, and no other languages or pages moved. Uncertainty: the redirect target isn't in the graph, so I can't confirm that it exists or has recent edits. I also can't rule out a current Niamey airport incident that someone mislabelled; nothing in these diffs suggests one.

briefs.headline: ru-wiki: temp user swaps "Белоруссия" for "Беларусь" in Nazi SS official's bio
briefs.summary: This is a naming-convention edit on a historical article, not a real-world event. The ru-wiki biography of Karl Zenner, the SS and Police Leader in Belarus in 1941–42, got three edits in about a minute. A temporary account (~2026-56034-98) changed "Белоруссия" to "Беларусь" twice: once in the infobox and once in the body (rev 155687030). The edit summary says "Белоруссия" sounds offensive, "as a reminder of the colonial past". EyeBot automatically reverted the change because it scored as likely vandalism. Patroller Beonus then undid the bot's revert (rev 155687057), so the "Беларусь" wording is what the page currently says. The same temporary account also edited another bio (Бабосов, Евгений Михайлович) seconds later with no edit summary. I didn't read that diff, but it may be the same terminology change. On ru-wiki the Белоруссия/Беларусь wording is a long-running style dispute, so the change could still be reverted. One undo of a bot doesn't make this an edit war between people. I didn't read EyeBot's revert diff; I'm relying on its edit summary for what it did.

briefs.headline: West Virginia vandal returns on two more throwaway accounts; admin Zzuuzz reverts both
briefs.summary: The vandalism on English Wikipedia's West Virginia article went on after our last brief. Two more new temporary accounts, ~2026-55927-35 and ~2026-56090-98, each made the same +160-byte edit. I read both diffs. Each swaps the nickname "Mountain State" for "Incest Capital of the world," swaps the motto for a line about sex with stepdaughters, adds three sentences claiming the state encourages incest and sexual abuse, and adds a stray Green Day link. That is exactly what ~2026-56094-99 posted earlier. Administrator Zzuuzz reverted each one within about 35 seconds; I read rev 1381077108, which puts the original text back. The edit summaries make the vandal's edits look like routine "Undid revision" clicks aimed at old patrol reverts by Crtbob and BriDash9000. That suggests the same material was added and removed once before, outside what the graph covers, but I haven't checked this. The same payload coming from many fresh accounts points strongly to one person dodging blocks, though I can't prove it. There are no edits after 1792445878, and that quiet period, plus an administrator now answering directly, may mean the page has been protected or the vandal's IP range blocked. I haven't confirmed either. This is all on one English page, it's one-way vandalism being cleaned up rather than a real dispute, and nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: West Virginia page hit by vandalism, then reverted; hidden edits suggest revision deletion
briefs.summary: This looks like a vandalism spree, not a content dispute or a news event. In about five minutes, two accounts added the same material to West Virginia over and over: the temporary account ~2026-56092-89 (+160 and +49 bytes) and then Dbdbah (+209). Patrollers Cannolis and 45dogs, then administrator Primefac, removed it each time, with edit summaries tagging it as vandalism. I couldn't read the West Virginia diffs because the text of the disputed revisions now returns 'missing content', which usually means an admin has hidden it (revision deletion) because it was offensive or harmful. So I can't say what the added text was. On the separate Ibrahim Isaac Sidrak page, a different temporary account twice changed the short description from 'Head of the Coptic Catholic Church' to 'Fake Coptic Patriarch' (diff read), and both changes were reverted. The only link between the two pages is patroller Cannolis, and there's no sign of a real-world event behind either.

briefs.headline: West Virginia vandalism has stopped; no new edits since admin's last revert
briefs.summary: Nothing has happened since our last brief. The graph shows no edits to English Wikipedia's West Virginia article, or to the linked Ibrahim Isaac Sidrak page, after Zzuuzz's revert at ts 1792445878. The four reverts the Scout flagged are the same churn we already covered. Throwaway temporary accounts kept re-adding one +160-byte block of sexual slurs, and patrollers 45dogs and administrator Zzuuzz removed it within seconds. I read Zzuuzz's rev 1381076764. It brings back the nickname "Mountain State," the real motto and the lead paragraph, and removes the incest-themed lines and a stray Green Day link. It's one-way vandalism cleanup on one English page, not a two-sided dispute, and nothing points to a real-world event. The quiet period suggests the page was protected or the accounts were blocked, but I haven't checked either. I recommend merging this into the existing West Virginia vandalism story and closing it.

briefs.headline: West Virginia article hit again by sexual slur vandalism; vandal taunts admin, change undone
briefs.summary: The vandalism on the English Wikipedia's West Virginia article has kept going, and it is not a news event. A new temporary account, ~2026-56094-99, made a +160-byte edit with the summary "[[User:Primefac]] There's nothing you can do to stop me." The diff, which I read, replaces the state nickname and motto with incest-themed slurs, adds lines claiming the state encourages sexual abuse of stepdaughters, and inserts a stray link to Green Day. Patroller 45dogs undid it within about 70 seconds and restored the original text. The new account taunting the administrator by name, the same +160 size as earlier edits by ~2026-56092-89, and the Dbdbah account all suggest one person switching accounts to get around blocks. That is likely, but I can't confirm it. Earlier versions of the disputed edits, such as Dbdbah's rev 1381074659, still return 'missing content', which fits an admin hiding them (revision deletion). All the edits are on one English page, the reverts are patrollers removing obvious vandalism rather than a real dispute, and there is no sign of a real-world trigger. Page protection may follow.

briefs.headline: Serie A: Fiorentina lose 1-3 at home to Como; it.wiki season page updated
briefs.summary: Four temporary accounts made five small edits to it.wiki's "Serie A 2026-2027" page on 18 Oct 2026. Together the edits record a Fiorentina–Como result of 1-3. One edit changed the fixture's kickoff time ("15:00") to "1-3" (rev 152957251). The other edits update the rest of the page to match that score. In the table, Como go from 11 to 14 points and 6 to 7 games played, with goals 9-6 changing to 12-7, and move up to 4th. Fiorentina stay on 4 points after 7 games, with 5 losses and goals 8-17, and stay in the red-shaded relegation band. The season infobox goes from 65 to 66 matches and from 188 to 192 goals. All of these numbers agree with each other, there are no reverts, and the changes match what a real match result would produce, so this looks like normal upkeep rather than vandalism. This is based only on the edits: no news source or second language confirms the score.

briefs.headline: Serie A: it.wiki records Fiorentina 1-3 Como; no new activity since last brief
briefs.summary: This is the same story as the earlier routine brief on it.wiki's "Serie A 2026-2027" page, and nothing has changed since then. The graph still shows five small edits by four temporary accounts on 18 Oct 2026, with no reverts. I re-read rev 152957251, which replaces the Fiorentina–Como kickoff time ("15:00") with a 1-3 result in the "Girone di andata" fixture list. I tried to re-check the other four diffs (152956574, 152957155, 152957171, 152957183), but none of them loaded.
