Rev 152956574 ("Primati stagionali", +10) came about 50 minutes before the score edit and may be about a different match. There are no reverts, editors on other pages, or other-language pages involved, so this looks like routine season-page upkeep, not vandalism. The score comes only from the edits; no outside source or other-language page confirms it.

briefs.headline: Unsourced Kim Jong-un death claims on Spanish, Persian Wikipedia reverted
briefs.summary: Spanish and Persian Wikipedia editors added claims that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has died. Neither claim cited a source, and both were reverted within minutes. On eswiki, temporary account ~2026-55926-47 rewrote the lead twice in the past tense. The edit summary was "Cabecera actualizada tras su fallecimiento" ("header updated after his death"), and the text gave the death as 19 October 2026 from a brain hemorrhage (rev 175908178). Automoderador reverted the first attempt and SeroBOT the second. On fawiki, Ohmygod211112 changed the infobox death field from "20 Oct 2026, China" to "19 Oct 2026, China" and rewrote the lead in the past tense (rev 44780038). IlanMask reverted it as "بدون منبع" ("no source") (rev 44780079). The other eswiki churn is ordinary vandalism, e.g. rev 175907481 added gibberish names, and it was also reverted. The scout's "no reverts" flag is misleading: the reverts in this cluster are done by bots and patrollers, and the graph doesn't mark them as reverts. The two wikis give different details (a brain hemorrhage on eswiki, death in China on fawiki), and no other language edition of Q56226 shows activity in the graph, including English and Korean. That pattern points to a death hoax or rumor, not a confirmed event. Because the claimed date matches the current date, watch for sourced edits or activity on enwiki or kowiki.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong-un death rumor: eswiki rewrite undone; fawiki adds sourced 'rumours' section
briefs.summary: On eswiki, temporary account ~2026-56232-85 added a 19 October 2026 death date to the infobox and rewrote the lead in the past tense, without a source (rev 175908771). About three minutes later, a second temporary account, ~2026-55932-17, removed the date ("es solo un rumor en redes", i.e. "it's only a rumor on social media"; rev 175908792) and put the lead back in the present tense ("muerte es rumor", "death is a rumor"; rev 175908826). The third editor, 1tsZyro, only tidied the wording of the existing health-section line saying The Sun reported "unverified rumours" of a coma (rev 175908847). So the scout's "three editors" are one hoax edit and two cleanups, not three people pushing the claim. The bigger development is on fawiki: Ohmygod211112, who had earlier written a past-tense death claim that was reverted, added a long section titled "Rumours about death" (rev 44780264, +8553). It describes the claims as unconfirmed and traces them to social-media posts by Wanjun Xie, described as chair of the China Democracy Party. The claims are a brain hemorrhage, a coma, transfer to Peking Union Medical College Hospital, a possible death, and China sending about 9,000 troops to Pyongyang. The section cites IBTimes UK, Geo News and The Sun, and it notes that no independent evidence was offered for the troop claim. That gives an origin for the rumor and shows a little more media coverage, but all of it covers the rumor and none confirms a death. As far as the graph shows, no death claim currently stands on enwiki, eswiki or fawiki, and I still see no kowiki activity. I can't check the cited articles or any outside reporting.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong Un enwiki: 'current event' tag pulled pending reliable sources; death still unverified
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the existing Kim Jong Un death-rumor story, not a new event. The scout's "four editors, 729 churn" covers enwiki housekeeping since the last brief. The one substantive move: TheAwesomeHwyh removed the {{current event}} tag that Augmented Seventh had added minutes earlier, with the summary "removed current event tag until reliable sources pick this up" (rev 1381094826). The graph marks this as a revert, but it undoes the tag, not a death claim, and it is not an edit war. The bulk of the churn is Super Goku V's -679 edit (rev 1381094264). It renamed a duplicated "Early life" heading back to "Personal life" and removed a repeated sentence about his birth date (1982 per Pyongyang, 1983 per South Korean intelligence). That edit is structural and has nothing to do with the rumor. Extended-confirmed protection (Rsjaffe) stays in place. Experienced enwiki editors are now saying outright that reliable outlets have not picked up the rumor. As far as the graph shows, no death claim stands on enwiki, eswiki or fawiki, and the rumor (social media and tabloids: brain hemorrhage, 19 October) remains unverified.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong Un enwiki article tagged 'current event' and protected; eswiki death date reverted
briefs.summary: The scout's "3 editors, 3 edits" on enwiki are housekeeping, not a new death claim. Augmented Seventh added a {{current event}} tag (rev 1381092976). About a minute later, administrator Rsjaffe added {{pp-extended}} (rev 1381093111), which means the article is now under extended-confirmed protection. Only experienced accounts can edit it, which stops the unsourced "died 19 October" edits seen earlier. A third edit (Zeke, the Mad Horrorist, -7, Early life section; rev 1381093363) changes a few words in the family-background paragraph. The diff was cut off, but nothing visible concerns his death. On eswiki, temporary account ~2026-56043-92 again added "8 de enero de 1984 - 19 de octubre de 2026" and the past tense "fue un político" to the lead, without a source (rev 175909283). The Automoderador bot reverted it 7 seconds later. The tag and the protection show that enwiki editors treat the rumor as a live news situation that draws disruptive edits, but they are not confirmation. No new sources appeared, and as far as the graph shows, no death claim stands on enwiki, eswiki or fawiki. Kim's death remains unverified.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong-un: eswiki now cites Sun report of unverified coma rumor; death claims still unsourced
briefs.summary: This updates the story on unsourced Kim Jong-un death claims. On eswiki, registered editor Ezra AQ added a line to the health section (rev 175908234). It says The Sun reported on 19 October 2026 "unverified rumours" that Kim is in a coma after a brain hemorrhage and was rushed to China for treatment, and it cites a thesun.co.uk link. The graph shows no revert of that edit so far. The new line explains where the earlier claims came from. The eswiki "brain hemorrhage" detail and the fawiki "China" detail both match this tabloid rumor, which talks about a coma, not a death. On fawiki, Khan 405 put "20 Oct 2026, China" into the infobox death_place field (rev 44779929). That edit came before Ohmygod211112 changed the date to 19 October, which IlanMask later reverted for having no source. Only eswiki and fawiki show activity on Q56226; there is still none on enwiki or kowiki. My read: there is a real but unconfirmed rumor in a single British tabloid. Nothing supports a confirmed death, and the past-tense rewrites of the article are still hoax or premature edits. I can't check The Sun article's content beyond its URL slug, and I don't know if any other outlet has confirmed it.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong-un death rumor spreads to fawiki 'Leader of North Korea'; enwiki section removed
briefs.summary: The Kim Jong-un death rumor has reached a fourth page, the Persian Wikipedia article "Leader of North Korea" (رهبر کره شمالی). There, سعیدک added "اما مردش امشب" ("but he died tonight") to the end of the lead and swapped "supreme leader" for "dictatorial leader" in the infobox (rev 44780161). A temporary account then softened that line to "rumours of his death have been published" (rev 44780217). Dexbot's AI-based anti-vandalism system rolled both edits back to the original text (rev 44780228). None of the three edits cited a source. On enwiki, RyuSagat removed Michael.duignan's "Reported Death" section with the summary "better sources needed" (rev 1381078959). That section had cited only londonlovesbusiness.com and an Instagram post. So the predicted challenge has happened, and as far as the graph shows, no unsourced death claim currently stands on enwiki, fawiki or eswiki's lead. The scout's "no reverts" note is wrong: all three fawiki edits on this page were reverted. This is the same tabloid/social-media rumor as before (traced earlier to The Sun's "unverified rumours" of a coma), with no new sourcing. The death is still unconfirmed, I still see no kowiki activity, and I can't check outside reporting.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong-un death rumor reaches English Wikipedia; no reliable source confirms it
briefs.summary: The unconfirmed rumor that Kim Jong-un has died has now reached enwiki, following eswiki and fawiki. On enwiki, Blakesleylan added "died October 19 2026" to the lead (rev 1381076520), then put the same date into the infobox term_end and birth_date fields (rev 1381076789). Neither edit had a source, and Kwpolska reverted both within about two minutes. So the "one revert" the scout flagged is a patroller removing a premature death claim, not a two-sided edit war. About 18 minutes later, Michael.duignan added a "Reported Death" section (rev 1381078634, +1364, edit summary "update based on current reports that he is deid"). It says North Korean authorities "refused to confirm or deny" that Kim died of a brain hemorrhage on 19 October 2026, and that social media was "awash with rumours." Its sources are londonlovesbusiness.com and an Instagram post, not a wire service or major outlet. As of the latest graph data, that section hasn't been reverted. The brain-hemorrhage/19 October details match the eswiki edits and The Sun's "unverified rumours" coma report cited earlier on eswiki. That points to one tabloid and social-media rumor spreading across languages, not new confirmation. Kim's death remains unverified. I found no kowiki activity and no reliable outlet's reporting in these edits. Expect the enwiki section to be challenged or removed.

briefs.headline: Kim Jong-un: eswiki patroller restores stable version; death rumor still unconfirmed
briefs.summary: Only two edits on Kim Jong-un pages have come in since the last brief, and neither adds anything about his reported death. On eswiki, registered editor Mauricio C. rolled the article back with the summary "Rv a versión estable" ("revert to the stable version") (rev 175908865, -454). The part of the diff I could see only changes a few words in the lead and leaves the past-tense line about him being "educated in Bern". The full diff was cut off, so I can't say for certain what else it removed. The size (-454) is close to Ezra AQ's earlier +473 line saying The Sun reported "unverified rumours" of a coma, so that line may be gone, but I haven't confirmed it. The enwiki edit is a one-word grammar fix to the birth-date sentence (rev 1381083741). The scout's "4 editors, 1 revert, large churn" is not new activity: it counts the earlier temporary-account edits and cleanups plus this one patroller revert. There are no new sources, no new languages (still nothing on kowiki), and no new death claims. As far as the graph shows, no death claim stands on eswiki, enwiki or fawiki. The rumor (social-media and tabloid claims of a brain hemorrhage or coma) is still unverified, and the edit activity seems to be dying down.

briefs.headline: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary gets routine upkeep on Wikipedia after release
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on "You Can See Everything" is getting maintenance edits, not new content. It is a 2026 A24 documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The recent edits I read add nothing newsworthy. One changes dates to the month-day-year format using a script, one renames references, one adds a link to Billy Evans' article, and one bumps the Rotten Tomatoes review count from 134 to 135 (still 98%; Metacritic 97). The roughly 552 bytes of churn the Scout flagged come from these formatting changes, not from a new article or new information. The film itself is not new to the wiki: the article already describes a surprise Telluride premiere (September 7, 2026) and an October theatrical opening, citing a Variety box-office preview dated October 14 that projected an $8M opening. The film is in release, but there is no fresh event here, no reverts and no edit war. I only checked the English page, not other language versions.

briefs.headline: Raphaël Arnault fr-wiki: no new activity; unsourced-smear revert war stays contained
briefs.summary: This is a recheck of the tracked dispute, and nothing new has happened. The graph still holds the same 8 edits on fr:Raphaël Arnault. The last one is HaguardDuNord's revert (rev 240557967), and no edits came after it. I read the latest addition (rev 240557856). The temporary account ~2026-56241-09 added text to the lead calling the far-left MP "triple fiché S" (on a French state-security watchlist three times). It also says his parliamentary aide Jacques-Élie Favrot was involved in a "lynching" that killed "the patriot Quentin Deranque", and that he is close to a suspect in an arson attack on Limoges town hall. None of it cites a source. The revert removed exactly that text. Gyrostat had already reverted the same insertion three times, calling it POV-pushing. A search of all pages in the graph turns up nothing on Deranque, Favrot, Limoges or other-language versions of the Arnault article, so nothing backs up the claimed incidents. This looks like one account pushing possibly defamatory claims about a living person, and the main editors stopped it each time. It's not evidence of a real-world event. A real incident could still be behind the claims, but so far the graph doesn't show one.

briefs.headline: Raphaël Arnault fr-wiki: temp account keeps adding unsourced smears, reverted 4 times
briefs.summary: The "large churn" on this page is a small revert war, not news. One temporary account (~2026-56241-09) added the same ~288-byte text to the lead four times. The text calls the far-left MP "triple fiché S" (on a French state-security watchlist three times), says his parliamentary aide Jacques-Élie Favrot was "involved in the lynching" that killed "the patriot Quentin Deranque", and links him to the suspect in an arson attack on Limoges town hall. The additions cite no sources. Two registered editors removed it each time: Gyrostat three times ("non encyclopédique en l'état, POV-pushing"), then HaguardDuNord. The graph flagged none of these as reverts, but the edit comments show they were. The graph has no pages on Deranque, Favrot or a Limoges arson, and no editing in other languages, so nothing here backs up the claims. A real incident may be behind them, but these edits are not evidence of one. Treat this as a dispute over unsourced, possibly defamatory claims about a living person. Recheck only if pages about those incidents appear.

briefs.headline: James L. Easton bio gets infobox and succession-box update; no news

It now lists Easton as IOC Vice-President from 2002 to 2006 and as World Archery president from 1989 to 2005, between Francesco Gnecchi-Ruscone and Uğur Erdener (rev 1381070821). briefs.headline: Ramayana: Part 1 page: temp-account cleanup rolled back as vandalism; no news signal
briefs.summary: I found no sign of real-world news here. This is upkeep on an upcoming film's English Wikipedia article. Over about 50 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-55775-56) made 9 small edits. It removed what it called duplicate references, cutting an NDTV citation from the Origins section (rev 1380880476). It also reworked the soundtrack infobox (rev 1380882217): it renamed the album to "Ramayana: Part 1", changed the recording date from 2025 to 2024, added studios in Chennai and Santa Monica, and removed the T-Series label and Namit Malhotra as producer. In a later edit summary the same account says it added a label back. Separately, Onedirectiongod619 removed a wikilink on "crore" in the budget line (rev 1380884665), a 4-byte formatting change. Vestrian24Bio then restored the earlier revision by Mattgelo, labelling it "Rvv" (revert vandalism), which undid the whole sequence (rev 1380886487). The restored version carries an {{AI-generated}} cleanup tag pointing to a case on Wikipedia's AI-content noticeboard. Every edit was about formatting, sources or soundtrack credits. No edit adds a release date, box-office figure or other news, and there is no back-and-forth reverting, no activity in other languages and no outside editors. The infobox changes are unsourced, so they don't count as evidence of a real update to the soundtrack.

briefs.headline: Bournemouth season page logs first league win of 2026–27, a 2–0, moving them up to 15th
briefs.summary: On about 18 October 2026, a few registered editors and one temporary account made routine post-match updates to the English Wikipedia page for AFC Bournemouth's 2026–27 season. There were no reverts. The edits show Bournemouth's first Premier League win of the season, in their seventh league match: the record changes from W0 D3 L3 to W1 D3 L3, and goals scored rise from 7 to 9 while goals conceded stay at 13. That points to a 2–0 win. The squad statistics credit one goal each to Evanilson (43rd minute) and Marcus Tavernier, which makes Tavernier the top scorer in the league and all competitions (4). The infobox league position changes from 19th to 15th. Later edits are small fixes: a booking minute, a link to Sunderland, a kick-off time changed from 15:00 to 17:30 GMT, and an average-attendance figure added by an anonymous editor. I couldn't confirm who Bournemouth played or the exact date from the diffs I read. This is ordinary sports-page upkeep with no wider news significance.

briefs.headline: Luke McCaffrey page: one self-insertion vandal edit reverted fast, no news signal

Rencoolguy reverted it about a minute later. The only other edit was ParallelX adding a comma in the personal-life section. None of the edits mention a trade, injury, game result or roster move, and no other pages or languages moved, so these edits show no real-world event. This is minor vandalism that has already been fixed, not a sports story.

briefs.headline: Luke McCaffrey page: self-insertion vandalism reverted, no new activity since

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster update: Derderian bio cut back over paid-editing tag; no news event
briefs.summary: This update adds Hovnan Derderian, Primate of the Western Diocese of the Armenian Church of North America since 2003. There is no real-world event behind the edits; this is a cleanup dispute. A temporary account (~2026-55990-51) cut about 10k bytes (rev 1381109742) and restored a short pre-"UPE" stub. The removed version carried an {{Undisclosed paid|August 2026}} tag, and the account said that version was LLM-generated. It had puffed-up text on his diocese's "expansion", his Oxford degrees and his awards, mostly sourced to church websites. CreativeLibrary460 reverted the cut, then undid its own revert a minute later with the note "Didn't notice that", which accepts the trim. EndTheWikiEditor's anti-vandalism tool then reverted a lead tweak (rev 1381110744). The temp account put the "Primate since 2003" wording back with a 2003 LA Times archive citation (rev 1381111035) and reFilled the reference. So the 31k churn is one paid-editing cleanup plus revert ping-pong, not an edit war over facts, and nothing points to a change in his position. The rest of the cluster is unchanged: Hannah Pearl Davis and Adam Warren have had no edits since the previous brief, and the Warren BLP attack is still reverted. This is English Wikipedia only, among the same patrollers, and nothing is reportable.

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster quiet: no new edits since Derderian cleanup; nothing to report
briefs.summary: Nothing has changed in this cluster since the last brief. A graph query for edits after the last recorded revision (ts 1792462663) on the six English pages found none. The latest Derderian revision I read, rev 1381111035, only rewrites the lead: Derderian is "Primate of the Western Diocese of the Armenian Church of North America since 2003", cited to a 2003 LA Times archive story. That cements the paid-editing/LLM trim; it doesn't report a new event. The Warren BLP attack is still reverted, and Hannah Pearl Davis, Cheezels, Otra Nota and Emma Maembong have all stopped moving. It's English only, among the same few patrollers (CreativeLibrary460, EndTheWikiEditor, ESkog), with no real-world event behind it. This agrees with the scout's note about routine patrol cleanup. Only risk: the temp accounts could come back to the Warren page.

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster update: Warren BLP attack stays reverted; slanted Pearl Davis edit removed
briefs.summary: This is an update to an existing patrol-cluster story. There is still no real-world event behind it. Adam Warren (historian): ESkog's last revert (rev 1381107135) took out the unsourced sentence "He has been credibly accused of white supremecy by myriad students and members of the faculty" for the fourth time. The debate itself dates from 2025, nothing points to a new development, and the edit looks like a one-off slanted addition, not an edit war. All of this is on English Wikipedia only, among the same few patrollers, and nothing here is reportable. Keep watching the Warren page for the attack coming back or the page being protected.

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster, no news: BLP attack on UW historian reverted; Cheezels, others minor
briefs.summary: The four pages in this cluster (Cheezels, Adam Warren (historian), Otra Nota, Emma Maembong) have no shared real-world event. What links them is the same counter-vandalism patrollers, CreativeLibrary460 and ESkog. The busiest page is Adam Warren, a University of Washington history professor. Four different temporary accounts (~2026-56108-68, -56117-45, -56022-46) each re-added the same unsourced sentence claiming he "has been credibly accused of white supremecy by myriad students and members of the faculty". CreativeLibrary460 and ESkog reverted it each time, citing BLP rules on unsourced content about living people. The pattern of one sentence pushed by short-lived accounts against several patrollers looks like BLP vandalism or one person dodging reverts, not a two-sided content dispute. No source, other language versions or established editors back the claim. I can't rule out that it reflects a real campus grievance, but nothing in the graph supports reporting it. The other pages are routine: on Otra Nota a temp account changed infobox spacing and "1992–93" to "1992–1993" and was reverted. On Emma Maembong a temp account keeps changing her unsourced birthplace from Kuala Terengganu to Kota Bharu. The Cheezels ambassador swap was covered in the earlier brief. Recommend merging into the existing Cheezels routine story and watching the Warren page for page protection or sourced coverage.

briefs.headline: Cheezels page: unsourced 'brand ambassador' swap reverted twice
briefs.summary: New account Samantha Prime (2 edits total) twice changed the infobox 'ambassador' field on the English Cheezels article from "Samuel Wilden" to a list of six people. The first try gave only first names (Rylee, Thinomee, Elodie, Savaana, Lilly, Georgie). The second, with the comment "updated cheezels ambassador", added surnames. Neither edit cited a source. EndTheWikiEditor reverted the first one with an anti-vandalism tool as unsourced content, and CreativeLibrary460 reverted the second. No other pages, other languages or more experienced editors are involved, and no source backs a real marketing announcement. This looks like an unsourced addition or possible prank (names that may be private individuals), not a real-world event, though I can't completely rule out a real new ambassador campaign.

briefs.headline: New user overwrites pt-wiki Notre Dame school list with promo text; reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. A new account, O cara legal01 (2 edits in total), replaced the pt-wiki page "Colégio Notre Dame" with promotional text about the Recreio (Rio de Janeiro) campus (rev 73250672). The page had been a list of Notre Dame schools across Brazil. The new text said the school had "over 500 students", called it "one of the best schools in Rio", named a student actress, and described facilities. Daniel G Rego, an established editor, undid it. The same new user then blanked the list again (rev 73250722), this time leaving a message on the page itself saying they wanted to talk about "the school's marketing" and offering to discuss. Little Sunshine reverted that too, restoring the list. The scout's "no reverts" flag was wrong: both reverts show up in the edit comments, not in the graph's revert field. This looks like a well-meaning but promotional newcomer, not coordinated vandalism and not a real-world development. The page is back to its earlier version, and there is little reason to keep watching unless the user keeps going.

briefs.headline: pt-wiki Notre Dame list: newcomer blanks page a third time to plead for talk; reverted
briefs.summary: There is no news here. On the pt-wiki page "Colégio Notre Dame", the same new account, O cara legal01, blanked the list of Brazilian Notre Dame schools for a third time (rev 73250782). In its place they wrote a message on the article itself. It accuses the people reverting them of using "multiple accounts, bots" and says they study at the school and know a lot about it ("Eu sei muito sobre essa escola, estudo lá"). It ends by asking for a reply. Little Sunshine reverted it within about 30 seconds (rev 73250793), and the list is back. The scout's note is wrong in two ways. These are not new routine edits: they continue the same dispute as the earlier promo overwrite (73250672) and blanking (73250722). And "no reverts" is also wrong: three edits are reverts (73250693, 73250730, 73250793), but they show up only in the edit comments, not in the graph's revert field. This is one student pushing content about their own school, which counts as low-level disruption, against two established editors. It is not a two-sided edit war, and nothing has happened in the real world. If the user keeps going, the likely next step is a warning or a block, not anything worth reporting.

briefs.headline: Colorado GOP nominee Victor Marx's page adds resurfaced violence recordings; Jolly Rancher vandal reverted
briefs.summary: These two pages have nothing to do with each other. The only link is that the same recent-changes patrollers (Dr vulpes and MarioWonderExpert, both using the Interceptor tool) reverted vandalism on each. On Jolly Rancher, a temporary account blanked the opening paragraph three times, replacing it with "blue Jolly Rancher are mythical". Each change was reverted within minutes, so this is plain vandalism and not news. The real content is on Victor Marx: editor Bovidbeauty added a sourced paragraph (citing International Business Times UK, dated 1 Oct 2026) saying recordings of Marx resurfaced in 2026. In them he describes pushing his wife into a door and throwing his toddler son, and says God gave him "a gift for violence". The cited headline calls him the Colorado GOP nominee for governor. Separately, a temporary account changed the year of his campaign announcement from 2025 to 1345 ("i refined a year"), a test edit that was reverted. Uncertain: only one editor added the controversy and only one outlet is cited. There's no sign yet of wider editing or activity in other languages, so this is a developing campaign controversy, not a breaking one.

briefs.headline: Victor Marx violence-recordings paragraph still stands; newly linked pages are only vandalism
briefs.summary: The one real piece of news in this cluster has not changed since the last brief. On 20 October, editor Bovidbeauty added a paragraph to Victor Marx's page saying that recordings resurfaced in 2026 (rev 1381210360). In them Marx describes giving his wife a "decent, bouncing push" into a door and throwing his toddler son across a room, and says God gave him "a gift for violence". The paragraph cites a single International Business Times UK article, dated 1 October 2026, which calls him the Colorado GOP nominee. Since then the page has seen only a temporary account changing a year as a test (rev 1381220399), which patrollers reverted. Nobody has followed up on the controversy, it has no second source, and it has not appeared in other languages. The pages newly pulled in are noise. On Disinformation, user Will Ross Gjede twice wrote personal names into the lead sentence (revs 1381221001, 1381222158). On Confectionery store, a temporary account redirected the whole article to "Feces" (rev 1381221358); it was reverted and briefly reinstated, then restored by TonySt. The rest of that page's heavy activity is routine copyediting by many editors, apparently a group effort to improve the article (it carries an improvement banner). These pages are linked only because the same patrollers (Dr vulpes, MarioWonderExpert) reverted vandalism on all of them. Still unclear: whether other outlets or editors will pick up the Marx recordings story.

briefs.headline: Victor Marx recordings paragraph unchanged; linked pages show only vandalism and copyedits

briefs.headline: Minor vandalism on Italian Wikipedia's Vita nuova article, reverted within minutes

briefs.headline: Mozambican FRELIMO politician Ana Rita Sithole reported dead on 18 October
briefs.summary: Wikipedia editors have updated the page on Ana Rita Sithole, a Mozambican FRELIMO MP and 2023 co-president of the ACP-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly, to say she has died. Her death date is given as 18 October 2026. The news first showed up in a Deaths in 2026 entry (rev 1380898167). It cites a Portuguese-language article from Mozambique's O País titled "Morreu Ana Rita Sithole, vítima de doença", which says she died of an illness. Within minutes, three separate editors updated her biography: a category swap to 2026 deaths, a change from present to past tense, and a +350 rewrite adding the death date and a source (rev 1380901228). There were no reverts or signs of vandalism, and no other-language pages moved. Two things are uncertain. The source rests on one outlet, and I saw only its headline as quoted, not the article itself. The records also disagree on her years as an MP: the death list says 1994–2004, while the article says she served from 2000. This looks like a routine obituary update with low wider news value.

briefs.headline: France: English article on student protests adds 17 Oct riots and spread to other countries
briefs.summary: Six named editors worked on enwiki "2026 French student protests" in the last few hours, adding the 17 October escalation. Edits sourced to Le Monde, AP and Euronews give these figures: the government counted 550,000 marchers (organisers said 800,000), PM Lecornu said 1,200 arrests and 150 officers injured, Lyon's tourist office was burned, Limoges' 19th-century Hôtel de Ville largely destroyed, Marseille city hall's lobby briefly entered, and a demonstrator lost a hand in Saint-Étienne. A Reuters citation in the infobox records one protester's death from cardiac arrest. Other edits record the movement, which began 18 Sept in Créteil over school conditions and Parcoursup, spreading to Belgium, Albania, Greece (students camping on Syntagma, a concert planned for 20 Oct) and Italy. The two reverts are not an edit war: 296cherry undid their own accidental restore of 72 KB, then removed an infobox party (Communist Revolutionary Party) that had no source. A +340 KB edit by The Egyptian Journalist1234 shows up as the whole article being added again. Its content is coherent, but I can't tell whether it's a restore after a blanking or just how the diff was recorded. This is the English version of the frwiki 17 October stories s_2ae4c462 and s_6393958f, and I recommend merging them.

briefs.headline: France unrest: en article clears 340 KB duplication, rename to "2026 French riots" proposed
briefs.summary: This update settles the question left open in the last brief. The +340 KB edit by The Egyptian Journalist1234 (rev 1380901429) pasted a full second copy of the article, starting with templates and the infobox. About four minutes later 296cherry went back to the RMCD bot revision with the note "Accidental duplication of the article it seems" (rev 1380901891). It was a mistake, not vandalism or an edit war. RMCD bot's edit (rev 1380900903) shows a requested move, dated 18 October, to rename the page "2026 French riots", plus a pending proposal to merge "2026 French fuel protests" into it. Editors now treat the 17 October violence as the main story. The duplicated copy's infobox cited Reuters (18 Oct) for one protester who died of cardiac arrest in Paris, more than 600 police injured according to the interior minister, and more than 2,000 arrests (AP: at least 1,800). The restore diff lists those lines as removed, so the article's live infobox may again show the older 1 October figures. That's uncertain because the diff is hard to read after the duplication. Other edits were small. OrdinariusFingius added a photo of the burning Limoges Hôtel de Ville and then undid it themselves. Jprg1966 made copy edits to the section on student-union organising. The 17 October text (550k marchers by the government's count, 800k according to organisers, 1,200 arrests per Lecornu, Limoges city hall destroyed, Lyon tourist office burned) is unchanged.

briefs.headline: France unrest: en infobox now shows 1 dead, 500+ police hurt and ~1,800 arrests after 17 Oct
briefs.summary: This update answers the open question from the last brief: the infobox on enwiki "2026 French student protests" has been brought up to date. The Egyptian Journalist1234 (rev 1380906507) replaced the 1 October figures with numbers cited to Reuters and AP, both dated 18 October. One demonstrator died of cardiac arrest during the Paris protests, and police gave no further details. More than 500 police, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, according to the interior minister. Nearly 1,800 people were arrested across France according to Reuters; AP says at least 1,800. These figures are lower than the ones in the reverted duplicate copy (600+ injured, 2,000+ arrests), and I am using the version that is live now. The same edit also removed the older numbers: 1,949 arrests on 1 October, and the Justice Ministry figure of 6,100 people taken into custody since the protests began. The title of the cited AP story says Macron is to address the nation after riots and looting. That comes from a headline and has not been confirmed independently here. The other two edits were cosmetic: Brotherxaoop reformatted the same figures (rev 1380907315) and RickMorais fixed a typo (rev 1380906197). There were no reverts, three editors acted independently, and none of these edits touched the page title or the requested move.

briefs.headline: One admin's cleanup patrol links three unrelated pages; no news event
briefs.summary: The only thing tying these three pages together is one experienced editor, Drmies, doing routine maintenance across all of them. On Obradoiro CAB (a Spanish basketball club), Drmies made three reverts. The first undid 23 edits by WikiCreative123 as "huge amount of unverified content, test edits." The last undid a single +7,985-byte re-addition by the same user. That re-added text expands the infobox, adds unsourced fan nicknames and season write-ups, and claims the club was relegated in May 2024 and promoted back to Liga ACB on 8 May 2026 as Primera FEB champions. Those results might be true, but the edits cite no source and we have not checked them. On John Burroughs School, Drmies trimmed the alumni and faculty lists after another editor added names. On Nick Mowbray, Drmies reverted an unsourced addition naming a child. This is one editor reverting another, not a back-and-forth edit war, and there is no sign of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Strawberry Prince's ja page splits over timing of Nanamori and Satomi's departure
briefs.summary: The Japanese Wikipedia article for the 2.5D idol unit すとぷり (Strawberry Prince) is being edited repeatedly over whether founder ななもり。(Nanamori) and さとみ (Satomi) have already left. A temporary-account editor (rev 111430227) wrote in an edit summary that they "are members until 23:59 today, don't move them to former members." That points to a departure that has already been announced and takes effect at the end of the day. Other anonymous editors moved too early: one deleted both from the member table (rev 111430618, −990 bytes). Registered editor 大夫将監 then moved both to a new "元メンバー" (former members) section (rev 111430876). A different anon added that the group "ceased to exist as of 18 Oct 2026" (rev 111430882). 大夫将監 reverted that claim with TwinkleGlobal and then restored an earlier anon revision with the summary "Rvv", which is shorthand for reverting vandalism. The member articles for ななもり。and さとみ also got small anonymous edits in the same window, but I couldn't load those diffs. This looks like fans racing a scheduled member graduation, not a revert war between two editors. None of the diffs I read added a source for the departure, the date, or the dissolution claim. The dissolution claim looks unsupported.

briefs.headline: Strawberry Prince ja page hit by vandalism as editors list Nanamori, Satomi as ex-members
briefs.summary: This updates the earlier brief on the Japanese Wikipedia article for the idol unit すとぷり (Strawberry Prince). The page is still being reshuffled around the announced graduation (卒業) of ななもり。(Nanamori) and さとみ (Satomi). What's new is vandalism, not a real content dispute. Temporary account ~2026-55856-14, the same account that earlier added an unsourced "group dissolved" claim, wrote sexual spam into the member table in rev 111430928. It added "OFFLINE HOOKUP" in decorative Unicode letters to Satomi's name, "パコハラパコハラ" (sexual slang) to Nanamori's, and a junk string to Colon's citation. Another temporary account removed the name spam (rev 111430978), and registered editor 大夫将監 cleaned up what was left (rev 111430991). 大夫将監 then moved both graduating members into a separate "元メンバー" (former members) table (rev 111431002). That means the article now presents the departure as done, even though an earlier anon summary said they stay members until 23:59 on the day. The same vandal account's latest edit (rev 111431017, "fix for graduation") only deletes a comma, which looks like probing rather than real work. This is a graduation the edits treat as already happened, plus one bad-faith account; it is not an edit war between established editors. None of the diffs I read add a new source for the graduation or its timing.

briefs.headline: Strawberry Prince ja page: same vandal blanks article, admin-side revert restores it
briefs.summary: This is more of the same activity on the Japanese Wikipedia article すとぷり (Strawberry Prince), not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-55856-14 has already been flagged for sexual spam and an unsourced "dissolved" claim. In rev 111431094 (−4,030 bytes) it removed the infobox, the activity overview and the remaining four-member table, and replaced them with repeated sexual slang ("パコモリ…"). Its edit summary falsely called this a "fix for the members' graduation". About four minutes later, registered editor 大夫将監 reverted both of the account's recent edits with TwinkleGlobal (rev 111431116, +4,033), which restored the page. Just before that, in rev 111431006, 大夫将監 took the "【卒業】" (graduated) tags off the names of ななもり。(Nanamori) and さとみ (Satomi). The real-world fact behind all this, the announced graduation of Nanamori and Satomi, is unchanged, and nothing I read adds a source for it. This is one account's vandalism being cleaned up by one patroller, not an edit war.

briefs.headline: Politically motivated photo-swap vandalism on fr-wiki page of far-right publicist Florentin
briefs.summary: The fr-wiki bio of Jordan Florentin, described as a French far-right publicist and publication director of the outlet Frontières since 2026, had five edits in about 45 minutes, not three. Three accounts (Nikelern and two temporary accounts, ~2026-56368-28 and ~2026-56031-17) each replaced the infobox image with "Jordanfloflo.jpg". Their edit comments were activist taunts ("faut combattre les racistes", "t'es pas du bon côté de l'histoire", "les modo de wikipédia sont pas drôles"). Goodshort and GF38storic reverted the swap twice, and the latest swap (rev 240548412) was still live at last check. This looks like coordinated or copycat hostility toward the subject, not a real-world development. Uncertain: what Jordanfloflo.jpg shows, and the restored photo's filename names a "Jordan Da Rocha" at a 22 Nov 2025 Paris protest, so whether that image is labelled correctly may also be worth checking. Low news value. It may lead to page protection, and the attention could be a reaction to the subject's recent profile.

briefs.headline: Photo-swap vandalism on fr-wiki Florentin bio reverted a third time; page now restored
briefs.summary: Update to s_29ddc4f0. The third infobox image swap on the fr-wiki bio of Jordan Florentin, a far-right publicist, came from temporary account ~2026-56031-17 (rev 240548412, comment "les modo de wikipédia sont pas drôles"). It replaced the photo with "Jordanfloflo.jpg". About 50 seconds later R3L3ct3ur49 reverted it (rev 240548433), putting back the original image file ("Jordan Da Rocha à la manifestation du 22 novembre 2025 à Paris…"). The pattern is unchanged: three accounts swapped the photo with activist taunts in the edit comments, and three different patrollers (Goodshort, GF38storic, R3L3ct3ur49) reverted them. No edits have been logged since the last revert, and there is no sign of a real-world event behind the activity. Still open: whether the page gets protected, what Jordanfloflo.jpg shows, and whether the restored file is correctly labelled, since its filename names "Jordan Da Rocha".

briefs.headline: Temporary account swaps "monofisismo" for "miafisismo" on es.wiki pages; bot reverts

This looks like a one-person terminology change, not vandalism in the usual sense. I didn't read the Makuria diff, but its -4 delta fits the same swap.

briefs.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI article: routine expansion of development section, no news event
briefs.summary: Seven edits by four registered editors on the enwiki Grand Theft Auto VI article over about an hour. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors. Nothing new gets announced: no release date change, delay or sales figure, and the sources cited are weeks old. This looks like normal upkeep of a high-interest article, not a reaction to breaking news. I didn't check other-language versions of the article.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: 'Libro de los muertos' vandalism still live after bot revert

Several temporary accounts are making similar edits within minutes of each other, which suggests one group, possibly classmates. The Darwin and Saif al-Adel pages haven't changed since the prior brief. Next step: someone needs to remove the Lucas Agosti text by hand.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: unrelated anonymous vandalism on Darwin, Book of the Dead, Saif al-Adel pages
briefs.summary: These are three unrelated pages on Spanish Wikipedia, each edited by a different temporary account. None of them points to a news event. On Libro de los muertos, rev 175929922 added "(creado por Lucas Agosti)" to the opening sentence. This was a second attempt after Automoderador reverted the first one. briefs.headline: Joke vandalism on es.wiki page for Spanish village Mazarulleque; bot put it back
briefs.summary: No real-world event here. This is small-scale vandalism on the Spanish Wikipedia article for Mazarulleque, a village in Cuenca. Temporary account ~2026-55804-97 added two nonsense lines (rev 175914329, +135 bytes): a border with "El Lago Del Rats" and a claim that "En 2024 El Rats se proclamó como el diputado de la textura" ("In 2024 El Rats proclaimed himself the deputy of texture"). The 6595-byte churn the scout flagged is just this delete-and-restore cycle. As of the last edit we have, the nonsense seems to still be on the page. It's unclear whether the second editor was trying to clean up or was blanking too.

briefs.headline: Lamine Yamal it.wiki page: routine stats update, two name-change edits reverted

briefs.headline: Lamine Yamal it.wiki: third vandal name-swap reverted; stats update stands

briefs.headline: NZ Antarctic Heritage Trust page: promotional rewrite reverted; no news event

briefs.headline: Noni Madueke page updated after league goal; vandalism and formatting tiff reverted

briefs.headline: Oberon High School vandalism: Neriah reverts fake principal, then a new account hits the motto

briefs.summary: The prank on the English Wikipedia article for Oberon High School has been cleaned up. Patroller Neriah restored Komethere's clean revision (rev 1381166710). briefs.headline: West Virginia article hit by repeat obscene vandalism; editors reverting
briefs.summary: The reverts on enwiki's West Virginia article are a vandalism spree, not a news event or a content dispute. briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on Palatine priest Richard Schäfer (1872–1932); no current event
briefs.summary: AF666 created the German Wikipedia article "Richard Schäfer (Pfarrer)" from scratch (rev 271440835, +3,090 bytes). It is a historical biography of a Catholic priest and teacher from the Diocese of Speyer, born 1872 in Wattenheim and died 4 July 1932 in Ludwigshafen. One thing I can't rule out: the article may have been written for an anniversary or local commemoration, but nothing in the edits says so.

briefs.headline: Temporary account tries 3 times to delete Salesians' abuse section on es-wiki; bots revert
briefs.summary: The roughly 10.9k of churn isn't a rewrite. Within about 12 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56065-70) deleted the same ~1.8 KB "Abusos sexuales" section of the Spanish article on the Salesians three times, and anti-vandalism bots (Automoderador twice, SeroBOT once) put it back each time. The section is old, sourced content: it cites El País's 2023 database, which counts 123 reported cases and 196 victims in Spanish Salesian schools, plus EFE and Público. One deletion summary calls the section "highly politicized and biased", and another removal left a garbled heading ("exuales"). The edit flags show no reverts, but the bot edit summaries say they are reversions, which is why the scout missed them. Nothing points to a new real-world event: no new content, no other languages, and no human editors on the other side. This is one account whitewashing the page, contained so far. It could flare up again or lead to page protection.

briefs.headline: German water-law attorney Turgut Pencereci gets posthumous dewiki rewrite, death in July 2026
briefs.summary: The 14.4k-byte churn on dewiki "Turgut Pencereci" comes from one large edit by WasserLeben, a low-activity account with 2 edits in the graph (rev 271470875, "Einfügen von Belegen"). That edit adds a full biography of a Düsseldorf-born German lawyer who specialised in water and water-association law. It gives his death as 25 July 2026 in Ganderkesee. That is almost three months before this edit, so this is a late posthumous update, not breaking news. Nearly all the citations point to his own law firm's website (gkmp.de). The account's name and focus fit a possible conflict of interest or a tribute by colleagues. The same account removed a link to the de-academic mirror (rev 271470990), which suggests an older version of the article already existed and this was a rewrite rather than a brand-new page. Experienced editors then added a category and a quality-assurance tag, QS-Antrag "Vollprogramm" (rev 271471042), meaning they think the article needs a lot of work. Not confirmed: the death date and how notable he is, since there are no independent sources such as obituaries or press coverage.

briefs.headline: Dewiki bio of water-law attorney Turgut Pencereci gets routine cleanup after posthumous rewrite
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the earlier routine brief on dewiki "Turgut Pencereci". Since then the article has had only maintenance edits. Experienced editor M2k~dewiki added the standard person-data template and categories (rev 271471135): German lawyer, born 7 June 1961 in Düsseldorf, died 25 July 2026 in Ganderkesee. That copies the death date the creator WasserLeben had already written in; nobody has checked it independently. WasserLeben then removed a duplicate list of sources (rev 271471228, -620 bytes). It had pointed to the law firm's site gkmp.de, a beck-shop author profile, a report on the openumwelt.de server, the Rotary Club Bremen and a Bremen aviation club.
