Uncertain: the exact meaning of the lowercase "a" status code, and I didn't check other language editions.

briefs.headline: Linus Torvalds es-wiki page vandalized by temporary account, reverted twice by bots
briefs.summary: The roughly 6.5k of churn on Spanish Wikipedia's "Linus Torvalds" page comes from vandalism and bot reverts. It is not a rewrite and does not point to anything happening in the real world. Temporary account ~2026-56158-52 made two edits with no summary, about five minutes apart. I read both diffs. The first (rev 175918433) deleted the infobox and changed the lead to call Torvalds "Gorila sabroso" ("tasty gorilla") and "un desconocido" ("a nobody"), with garbled text about "páginas raras" ("weird pages"). The second (rev 175918516) deleted the infobox and lead paragraph again. SeroBOT (rev 175918435) and Automoderador (rev 175918518) each restored the earlier version within about 10 seconds. I did not open those two diffs, but their edit summaries say they are reverts and their size changes (+1004 and +2265) exactly cancel out the vandal's edits. The graph's revert flag missed them, which is why the scout saw "no reverts". Only this one page and this one non-bot account are involved, and nothing points to a coordinated campaign or any news about Torvalds.

briefs.headline: France 17 October riots: death toll disputed on en-wiki; Macron to address nation
briefs.summary: The English '17 October riots' page is still being worked on, mostly through tidying. The one revert is about the death toll. A temporary account (~2026-56083-52) changed the infobox from "2 (1 police officer, 1 protester)" to "1 protester" with the comment "wrong", and OrdinariusFingius undid it, putting back 2 deaths. Neither edit cites a source, so treat the police officer's death as unconfirmed. In the body text, Limoges is still there, which settles a doubt from the last brief. The article says the 19th-century Hôtel de Ville was set on fire in the evening, burned into the next morning and was partly destroyed. It cites Euronews ("Spire collapses at historic Limoges town hall") and AP. The same text says Lyon's tourist office was burned, Marseille city hall's lobby was briefly entered, and a demonstrator lost a hand in Saint-Étienne. Interior Minister Nuñez said an investigation was open and did not confirm reports that a police grenade caused the injury. A Le Monde live-blog citation dated 18 October says Macron will address the French people at 8 p.m. London3Calling also removed causes from the infobox ("poor school conditions", "chronic underfunding of education", "police brutality", "reintroduction of conscription") with a comment that pushes back on the education-underfunding claim. That is a change of framing to keep an eye on, not a new fact. Other figures (1,200 arrests, 150 police hurt, 550,000 marchers) have not changed.

briefs.headline: en-wiki '17 October riots' updated: 1,200 arrests, 550,000 marchers; Limoges city hall fire
briefs.summary: This is the English-Wikipedia side of the French 17 October 2026 protests we already track. The en page is SAME_AS the frwiki pages in stories s_6393958f, s_2ae4c462 and s_f5473aad, so it should probably be merged into those. Six named editors made small edits with no reverts. London3Calling's "clean-up" (+4,326) rewrote the lead and cited Le Monde's live blog: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez counted 110 marches and 550,000 marchers (110,000 in Paris), while organisers said 800,000. Students joined protests called by unions and the yellow vests. AP reported about 400 arrests during the day, and PM Sébastien Lecornu later said 1,200 were arrested and 150 police and gendarmes hurt. The page also says around 1,500 shops were damaged and more than 1,500 fires were set. The old text said more than 500 police, gendarmes and firefighters were injured. In the visible part of this diff, that figure and the Limoges sentence were removed and not put back. They may have moved lower in the article, but I couldn't see that part. On the companion page, the Hôtel de Ville in Limoges (built 1883, listed monument) is described as badly damaged by arson on 17 October, citing France 24 ("largely lost") and Le Parisien. Its clock tower, 43 m tall before the fire, is reported elsewhere as having collapsed, and new photo captions show the fire and the day after. The article also covers related unrest abroad, including an Albania section (Tirana ministries attacked). Uncertain: the figures were copied from sources by editors and are still being edited, and the injury counts don't match each other (150 vs 500+).

briefs.headline: France national team page: old October 2025 qualifier results removed, reverted, removed again
briefs.summary: This is routine housekeeping, not news. Editor Chelsdog removed two old match boxes from the "Recent results" section of the English Wikipedia France national football team article: France 3–0 Azerbaijan (10 Oct 2025) and Iceland 2–2 France (13 Oct 2025), both 2026 World Cup qualifiers. TonySt reverted the first removal, which had no edit summary, calling it "unexplained content removal". Chelsdog then made the same removal again with the explanation "over one year": the edit timestamps put these edits in October 2026, so the matches had just passed the one-year mark. No match scores or facts were changed. Only two editors and one language edition were involved, there has been one revert, and nothing has happened since. This looks like the same kind of results-trimming already being tracked on the France U-21 page. It is not an edit war unless TonySt reverts again.

briefs.headline: Small revert fight over a bus-route citation on Santiago's Los Libertadores station page
briefs.summary: There is no real-world news here. The "large churn" is one 277-byte change being reverted back and forth on the es-wiki page for Estación Intermodal Los Libertadores, a transit hub in Santiago, Chile. The disputed text is a single <ref> on a bus route listing (Caletera Autopista Los Libertadores … Cerro Portezuelo). It cites a February 2023 DTPM "Programa de Operación" routes file. Two temporary accounts (~2026-56126-31 and ~2026-55933-43) removed it with undo edits. Aroblesm, who added it, put it back, and so did a patroller with many edits, Casisgaal. The graph now shows a fifth edit: ~2026-55933-43 removed it again (rev 175919561, which I haven't read). All edit comments are undos or rollbacks, even though the graph's revert flag is false. No reasons were given, so it's unclear whether the removals are disputes over an outdated 2023 source or just disruption. The fight is small, slow and limited to this one page.

briefs.headline: Revert loop over 2023 DTPM citation continues on Santiago Los Libertadores station page
briefs.summary: This is not a real-world event. It is the same small edit war already being tracked on the es-wiki article for Estación Intermodal Los Libertadores, a transit hub in Santiago, Chile. Temporary account ~2026-55933-43 again removed the single <ref> on the bus-route line "Caletera Autopista Los Libertadores … Cerro Portezuelo" (rev 175919561). That ref cites a February 2023 DTPM "Programa de Operación" routes zip file. 18 seconds later, Aroblesm, who originally added the ref, restored it with a rollback (rev 175919566). Counting both temporary accounts, the citation has now been removed three times and restored three times, each time a ±277-byte change. Every removal used the undo tool and gave no reason, and none of the removing accounts has edited any other page, which points to disruption or an unexplained objection rather than a sourced content dispute. It is unclear whether the two temporary accounts are the same person. If removals continue, the page may need protection or admin attention.

briefs.headline: Jasmine Sokko page: apparent label account rewrites bio, reverted as promotional COI
briefs.summary: An account called JSJFJ, with only 3 edits, made three edits to English Wikipedia's Jasmine Sokko article. Each had the comment "Official company update of artist bio to reflect recent changes." The name and the text point to her label, JFJ Productions (JJ Lin's company). The first edit (−11,283 bytes) removed her birth name "Jasmine Wong Chu Qing" and the sourced lead text. In their place it put marketing copy ("multi-hyphenate creative director... Draped in monochromatic ensemble"), her December 2024 debut as a JFJ artiste on JJ Lin's JJ20 tour, the album "Burnout Dynasty" (March 2025), her NDP2026 song "You'll Be Okay," and a single released 5 June 2026. Two experienced editors, APK and Celjski Grad, reverted all three edits as unsourced, promotional, conflict-of-interest changes. This is a common pattern of a label or PR account editing an artist's page. There is no new real-world event here: the facts it cites are already known or minor releases. Three reverts in about 20 minutes could become an edit war if JSJFJ keeps going. For now it's a one-sided COI cleanup, not a two-way edit war or malicious vandalism.

briefs.headline: Subtle factual tampering on Fergie's "Clumsy" article reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: Two temporary accounts made small, misleading changes to the English Wikipedia article on Fergie's 2007 single "Clumsy". ~2026-56033-76 changed the "Composition" section so that Digital Spy's comparison was to Cassidy's "I'm a Hustla" instead of Tweet's "Oops (Oh My)" (rev 1381134480). ~2026-56080-52 then credited an MTV News quote to BET, renaming the citation without changing its MTV source link (rev 1381135151), and made a -41 byte edit to the chart section; the visible part of that diff showed no clear change. Within about 10 minutes, the established editor Tbhotch reverted both edits by ~2026-56080-52 and then restored his own earlier revision, which undid the Tweet/Cassidy swap too (rev 1381135379). This looks like sneaky vandalism, not a news event or an edit war: the changes went one way, with no back-and-forth. Nothing points to anything happening in the real world. I didn't see exactly what the chart-section edit changed, and I didn't check whether these accounts were active on other pages.

briefs.headline: Simon Fraser vandalism reverted; pages quiet since, no news event
briefs.summary: The scout's read holds: this is minor vandalism, and nothing has changed since the last brief. I checked the graph and found no edits to Simon Fraser (explorer), Aye-aye or Paper Wars after Smallestredboy's revert (rev 1381234790). The last activity came from temporary account ~2026-56278-91. It renamed the subject in the lead "kurt kobain" (rev 1381234640) and changed the "Early life" heading to "late life" under the summary "fixed some minor mistakes" (rev 1381234718). EditWarCriminal and Smallestredboy undid both edits, each within about 40 seconds, and the diffs confirm the page is back to normal. The pages are linked only by anti-vandalism patrollers, and nothing points to a real-world event. The only loose end is the possibly mistaken proposed-deletion notice still on Paper Wars (rev 1381234046), which is wiki housekeeping, not news. I recommend folding this into the existing vandalism story and lowering its priority.

briefs.headline: Vandalism patrol links 3 unrelated pages; Paper Wars magazine article overwritten by novel
briefs.summary: These three pages are linked only by one anti-vandalism patroller, Equivalent-Text2598, who edited all of them. Nothing here points to a real-world news event. On Aye-aye, a temporary account rewrote the infobox and lead as SpongeBob SquarePants. ClueBot NG, Equivalent-Text2598 and EditWarCriminal reverted it (rev 1381233191). On Simon Fraser (explorer), a temporary account changed the name to "Sibbian Framer" under the edit summary "spelling error". Patrollers including Knitsey reverted it (rev 1381233704). The large churn on Paper Wars came from user Ellis McCracken, who replaced the whole article about the wargaming magazine with a plot summary of an "unpublished fantasy-adventure novel by Ellis McCracken" (+10,458 bytes). This looks like a conflict of interest or self-promotion. Cannolis restored the magazine version (rev 1381233960). One loose end: Equivalent-Text2598 then put a proposed-deletion (PROD) notice on the page (rev 1381234046), with a concern ("no sources at all") written about the novel text. That notice now sits on the restored magazine article, which does cite sources, so it may be a mistaken tag that another editor will remove.

briefs.headline: More vandalism on Simon Fraser page, reverted within minutes; still no news event
briefs.summary: This is an update to the vandalism story already being tracked on Aye-aye, Simon Fraser (explorer) and Paper Wars. Nothing new suggests a real-world event. Since the last brief, a second temporary account (~2026-56278-91) changed the subject's name in the Simon Fraser lead to "kurt kobain" (rev 1381234640). After that edit was reverted, the same account renamed the "Early life" heading to "late life" under the summary "fixed some minor mistakes" (rev 1381234718). EditWarCriminal and then Smallestredboy reverted both edits, each within about 40 seconds. Not every temporary-account edit was bad: earlier, ~2026-56167-26 correctly changed a vandalised birth year from 2005 back to 1776 (rev 1381233473). Aye-aye has had no new edits. Paper Wars also has no new edits, so the proposed-deletion notice (rev 1381234046) is still on the page. Its concern ("does not seem to have any sources at all") was written about the novel text that Cannolis has since removed. Whether that notice is removed is the only open question, and it is a wiki housekeeping matter, not news.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on English 'Uraeus' page is over: reverted, no new edits
briefs.summary: This repeats the vandalism story already on file. It is not a new event. The same six edits are involved. Temporary account ~2026-55935-45 vandalised the Symbolism section of the English Wikipedia 'Uraeus' article three times; the last edit (rev 1381088316) changed the opening sentence to "Poopie is uraeus,a symbol for the goddess Wadjet... :)". Patrollers SuperPianoMan9167 and Nil NZ reverted each edit within about a minute. Nil NZ's final revert (rev 1381088396, made with the WikiShield tool) brought the original text back word for word. The graph shows no edits to the page since that revert, no other language versions involved, and none of the three editors touching any other page. Nothing here points to a real-world event. Recommend merging into the existing vandalism story or closing this one.

briefs.headline: Juvenile vandalism on English 'Uraeus' article reverted three times; no news hook
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not a content dispute. A temporary account (~2026-55935-45) edited the Symbolism section of the English Wikipedia article on the Uraeus, the cobra emblem of ancient Egypt, three times in about four minutes. Each time it added the word "Poopie", in the last case with a ":)", and it also broke the opening sentence. Two patrollers, SuperPianoMan9167 and Nil NZ (using the WikiShield tool, with the comment "vandalism"), reverted all three edits within a minute or so each time, and the article is back to its earlier text. There were no edits in other languages and no sign of a real-world event. The only open question is whether the account will come back.

briefs.headline: Ana Brnabić article hit by vandalism from a temporary account; reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: A single temporary account (~2026-55895-21) made two edits to the English Wikipedia article on Serbian politician Ana Brnabić. Both were vandalism, and both were reverted within about 20 seconds by two different editors (Beyhive Navy, then Joyous!). The first edit tacked a private individual's name and what looks like a street address in Vršac/Zrenjanin onto the infobox term_start field. That looks like doxxing aimed at someone unrelated to the article, so the details are not repeated here, and suppressing that revision may be worth considering. The second edit inserted "worst country serbia" into the native_name field. This is not a content dispute or edit war: no new facts were added, the edits never stood, and no other languages or pages were involved. The existing "28 September 2026" term_start date was already in the article and was not changed by these edits.

briefs.headline: Ana Brnabić vandalism resumes from a second temp account; rest of cluster is unrelated patrol churn
briefs.summary: The anti-Serbia vandalism on the English Wikipedia article about Ana Brnabić has continued. Temporary account ~2026-55895-21 made a third edit, changing the infobox name to "from serbia and studied in UK? Not liked serbia edicational program ?", and ClueBot NG reverted it within 7 seconds. A second temporary account, ~2026-55886-45, then changed the name to "Hate Serbia and studied in UK Brnabić", swapped the photo for "Monkey eating.jpg" and added "ew" to the office line. Itsjuenyin reverted that within 14 seconds. The wording is similar enough that it is probably the same person, but I can't confirm that. All six vandal edits were reverted. Pages for this item in other languages show no activity, so I see no sign of a real-world event behind it. The infobox already listed her as "Acting President of Serbia", and none of these edits changed that. The other pages ended up in this cluster only because the same anti-vandalism patrollers (Materialscientist, ClueBot NG, Streetr4) worked on them. On Pixar, an editor blanked the Filmography timeline and it was restored. On Bosnian Cyrillic, Arolaq twice changed the language label from Serbo-Croatian to Bosnian, and Shadow4ya and Materialscientist reverted it each time. That is a small nationalist-labelling tussle, not news. The edits to Fifth grade, Lithobius forficatus and Problematic smartphone use were small and reverted, and I didn't read those diffs.

briefs.headline: Brnabić vandal pastes Diana conspiracy text; Bosnian Cyrillic label dispute hits third revert
briefs.summary: The vandalism on English Wikipedia's Ana Brnabić article is still going, but it no longer has anything to do with her. Temp account ~2026-55886-45 came back (rev 1380891652, +608) and pasted Serbian-language text into the infobox. The text sets out the conspiracy theory that MI6 killed Princess Diana on royal orders, and it ends with a chatbot-style offer to "tell you more", so it looks like pasted AI chat output. MarioWonderExpert reverted it within about 17 seconds. The real event in this cluster is on Bosnian Cyrillic: Arolaq made his third attempt (rev 1380891862) to change the infobox language from Serbo-Croatian to Bosnian. This time he also reworded the lead and argued in the edit summary that Serbo-Croatian is no longer official. Shadow4ya undid it within about 70 seconds. Three changes and three reverts in about 22 minutes (two by Shadow4ya, one by Materialscientist) is now a slow edit war on a nationalist sore point, though I see no talk-page or other-language activity. Nancy Ajram is incidental: temp account ~2026-56036-78 replaced "singer" in the lead with an apparent slur (revs 1380891926, 1380891998), and Paul Erik, ClueBot NG and Materialscientist reverted each attempt. Nothing here points to a real-world event, and every bad edit has been undone.

briefs.headline: Prank vandalism on German Burj Khalifa article reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-56116-74) vandalised the German Wikipedia article on Burj Khalifa twice in about 5 minutes, and two established editors reverted both edits within seconds. First (rev 271482534), it made "Leo Benning und sein Hund Lukas Kränzle" (Leo Benning and his dog Lukas Kränzle) the building's main tenant in the infobox. Der.Traeumer reverted that. Second (rev 271482647), it swapped the height-comparison image caption for a crude joke about "Leo", while its edit summary falsely claimed to be correcting misinformation. Carol.Christiansen reverted that. The graph did not flag the reverts, but the edit comments show they were standard rollbacks. Nothing happened on other pages or in other languages. The likely source is a schoolkid prank naming a friend. The Scout called this routine, but it's vandalism, and it's already contained.

briefs.headline: New Galician article on Gaza's Unknown Soldier Square translated from Spanish
briefs.summary: The edits on glwiki 'Praza do Soldado Descoñecido' are a new article being created, not a rework of an existing one. Wikimoder26 created the page (+1038) by translating the lead section of the Spanish article 'Plaza del Soldado Desconocido', and said so in the edit summary. The text describes the square on Omar Mukhtar Street in Gaza City's Rimal district and says Israeli forces bulldozed it during the war. Its one source is an NBC News article from December 2023, so this is old information, not a new event. MAGHOI then did routine cleanup: removed the 'uncategorized' tag and added an infobox, authority control and the Palestine category. Two small edits by Mark Gasoline (+10, +26), which I didn't read, finish the four-edit burst. There were no reverts and no sign of an edit war, vandalism or breaking news. This is routine translation work, though the article does use the contested label 'genocide' for the Gaza war.

briefs.headline: Galician Wikipedia gets two new translated articles: Gaza square and Malayan Communist Party
briefs.summary: Wikimoder26 created two new articles on Galician Wikipedia within minutes of each other. Both are translations of the lead sections of Spanish Wikipedia articles, and both edit summaries say so. One is 'Praza do Soldado Descoñecido', on the Unknown Soldier Square in Gaza City (rev 7731663, already covered in an earlier routine brief). The other is 'Partido Comunista de Malaisia', on the Communist Party of Malaya (rev 7731689). It gives encyclopedic background: the party was founded in 1930, played a role in the Malayan Emergency and gave up its weapons in 1989. Nothing in it is new or tied to a current event. The rest of the burst is cleanup by regular Galician editors. MAGHOI added categories and marked the Malaya article as too short. Breogan2008 added wikilinks and an authority-control template (rev 7731734), then added a History section to the Gaza square article, translated from the English article (rev 7731769). That section includes the square becoming a camp for displaced people in 2025, with a sourced report dated May 2025. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors, only four named editors, and only Galician pages changed. The pages have no clear link in the news beyond one translator's choice of topics. This is routine translation work, not a news event.

briefs.headline: Joke edits on ja.wiki page for former Hiroshima town Ōgaki reverted; no new activity
briefs.summary: This story is the same one as the earlier vandalism brief on 大柿町 (Ōgaki), a former town in Hiroshima Prefecture that merged into Etajima City in 2004. One temporary account (~2026-56244-55) made three small joke edits. I read two of them: one says the town's land "was launched by rocket and is now sea" (rev 111446241), and another adds "this is non-fiction" to the paragraph on where the name comes from (rev 111446275). Two established editors, Black Oar and Daiyamond (using TwinkleGlobal), reverted the edits within about 7 minutes. The graph shows no edits since the last revert, and no other pages, languages or editors are involved. Nothing points to a real-world event, and this can be closed as a duplicate of the earlier story.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on ja.wiki page for former Hiroshima town Ōgaki quickly reverted
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56244-55) made three small edits to the Japanese article 大柿町, a former town in Hiroshima Prefecture that merged into Etajima City in 2004. All three were joke text: that the town's land "was launched by rocket and is now sea", that the village of Kogoe "disappeared in 1548" (yet the same sentence has it joining the 1889 merger), and then "this is non-fiction." Two established editors, Black Oar and Daiyamond (the second using TwinkleGlobal), reverted the edits within minutes. All three bad edits were undone. No other pages, languages or editors were involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. This is routine vandalism that has already been cleaned up, so the story can be closed.

briefs.headline: Indonesia adds powerlifting and judo bronzes at 2026 Asian Para Games; tally at 17 bronze
briefs.summary: Results-tracking continues on English Wikipedia's "Indonesia at the 2026 Asian Para Games". Since the last brief, Yogwi21 added three bronze medals dated 20 October: Margono (powerlifting, men's −65 kg), Shebrioni (powerlifting, women's −61 kg) and Fajar Pambudi (judo, men's J1 −95 kg) (rev 1381167417). Kwetiau then raised the infobox bronze count from 16 to 17 (rev 1381167800). That leaves the tally at 4 gold, 4 silver and 17 bronze, and the rank was last given as 9th. The infobox now shows fewer bronzes than the medalist table implies, which suggests editors are not keeping the two in step. It does not look like a dispute: there are no reverts, all the editors have accounts, and edits are still coming in. Uncertainty: I have not checked the figures against an official medal table.

briefs.headline: Indonesia's 2026 Asian Para Games page updated with medals as Games continue
briefs.summary: Editors on English Wikipedia are updating "Indonesia at the 2026 Asian Para Games" with results as they come in. Several established accounts are doing the work, mainly Rahmadabduljaf20 and Yogwi21, with Kwetiau making one edit. None of the edits were reverts. Yogwi21 added bronze medals dated 20 October in table tennis (Komet Akbar, Barce Layaba) and athletics (Nanda Mei Sholihah, Alfin Nomleni, Rizal Bagus Saktyono) (revs 1381166745, 1381166171). Kwetiau filled in the infobox medal tally for the first time, at 4 gold, 4 silver and 16 bronze and a rank of 9th, citing 18:56 WIB (rev 1381166787). Rahmadabduljaf20 added draw and bracket entries for events such as mixed doubles and fixed a name spelling (rev 1381159792). This is routine results-tracking during a multi-sport event, not vandalism or an edit war. Uncertainty: I did not check the tally against an official source, and the rank will keep changing.

briefs.headline: Arsenal win 1–0 away in Premier League round 7, stay second (routine update)
briefs.summary: Three editors updated the en-wiki 2026–27 Arsenal F.C. season page with one Premier League round-7 result dated 18 October 2026. The match entry shows a 0–1 away score, an 80th-minute goal and a booking for Noni Madueke, a booking for Neco Williams, and an attendance of 30,893. The first editor marked the result as "L". Publicwalrus changed it to "W", which matches the 0–1 away score and the other edits: the away record went from 2 to 3 wins, the form string added a W, and points rose from 15 to 18. Alexthebat901 kept Arsenal 2nd in the league position row. The opponent isn't in the diffs I read. Williams's booking suggests Nottingham Forest, but I haven't confirmed that. The page logged no reverts and no other languages moved, so this is a routine match-result update, not a distinct news event.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on Ryūkyū princely houses (Udun) created; routine
briefs.summary: The churn here comes from one new article being created, not from news. Bosse Nor started the German article "Udun (Ryūkyū)" (rev 271488924, +11,575 bytes, comment "Neuanlage", meaning a new page). It is a sourced history article about the princely houses of the Ryūkyū Kingdom and their residences and mausoleums, citing Okinawan reference works. A few minutes later two other editors made routine cleanup edits: one added non-breaking spaces (rev 271489047), and M2k~dewiki added a category, judging by the edit summary; I didn't read that diff. There are no reverts and no signs of vandalism or a dispute, and nothing ties the article to a current event. It looks like a translation or expansion on a historical topic, possibly from the English or Japanese article, but that is a guess.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on Ryūkyū princely houses (Udun) gets images, cleanup; routine
briefs.summary: The only activity here is a new German article, "Udun (Ryūkyū)", being built out. It covers the princely houses of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, their residences and their tombs. Bosse Nor created it (rev 271488924, +11,575 bytes, "Neuanlage", meaning a new page) and has now posted one follow-up edit (rev 271489207, +274). That edit adds four images (Nakagusuku Udun, Shikina Udun, and the Ie and Ginowan Udun tombs) and fixes double periods in the list of houses. Two other editors made small cleanup edits: M2k~dewiki added the category "Königreich Ryūkyū" (rev 271488949), and another editor added non-breaking spaces (rev 271489047). The story still covers one page in one language, with 3 editors, 4 edits, no reverts and nothing tied to current events, so this is ordinary article growth, not news.

briefs.headline: New it-wiki article created on Rembrandt's 1637 Louvre painting of Tobias and the angel
briefs.summary: An Italian Wikipedia article on Rembrandt's 1637 panel "L'arcangelo Raffaele che lascia la famiglia di Tobia" (Louvre, Paris) was created from scratch. The first revision (152985552, +2147) built the stub: an infobox (oil on oak panel, 52×68 cm), a lead sentence, and categories. A second revision by the same temporary account (152986850, +3414) added Description, History (the painting entered Louis XV's collection in 1742) and "Tobias in other works" sections, with book citations. The remaining edits are small: a 9-byte tweak by a second temporary account, and a citation-template fix by an experienced editor (Egidio24, 219 edits). There are no reverts, no conflict, and no sign of any real-world news trigger. This is ordinary content creation, as the scout expected. I did not read the two smallest diffs.

briefs.headline: Kira Kosarin page hit by YouTube link spam, apparently from a sockpuppet; reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a news event and not routine biography editing. It is link spam. Over about 4.5 minutes, the account "Mark Goldstein" added a bare YouTube URL to the top of the Kira Kosarin article three times, each with the comment "Please Watch Video" (rev 1380903314 adds youtube.com/watch?v=krbeYGeyvOY). After those edits were reverted, a near-identical account, "Mark Goldstein1", added a different YouTube link with the comment "Please Watch Porya Video Thanks" (rev 1380903754). Every insertion was reverted within seconds to a minute, first by Streetr4 using the CVPI Interceptor anti-spam tool and then by SuperPianoMan9167. Neither spam account has edited any other page in the graph, and no other language versions of the article were touched. The second account looks like a sockpuppet made to dodge the reverts, but that's an inference from the name and timing, not something confirmed.

briefs.headline: Kira Kosarin YouTube link spam continues with a third numbered account; all reverted
briefs.summary: This is still vandalism, not a news event. Since the last brief, a third account in the same name series, "Mark Goldstein2", added the same bare YouTube link (watch?v=eNMzaV9P5N8) to the top of the Kira Kosarin article twice. Both edits carried the comment "Please Watch Video Sponsored by LTA" (rev 1380904106). On Wikipedia, "LTA" usually means "long-term abuse", which suggests a known repeat vandal, but I haven't confirmed that. Mark Goldstein1 had earlier added the same link (rev 1380903894). SuperPianoMan9167 and Ser Amantio di Nicolao reverted each insertion within about 40 seconds. The last revert was rev 1380904175, with the comment "rats, thought I could beat it to here". Across 16 edits there are 8 spam insertions by three accounts and 8 removals, but only 5 of the removals are flagged as reverts in the data. None of the accounts edited other pages in the graph and no other language versions were touched. This is spam being cleaned up by patrollers, not an edit war between two editors. More numbered accounts may follow until the page is protected or the accounts are blocked.

briefs.headline: Michael Rockefeller page: patroller reverts new account's edits; no news event
briefs.summary: Over about 3 minutes, a low-activity account (Olliebones23, 4 edits in total) made two edits to the English Wikipedia article on Michael Rockefeller. One changed the short description with no change in size. The other removed 13 bytes from a section and left a blank section comment. Vandal patroller Discospinster reverted both edits, the second time using the Huggle anti-vandalism tool (HG). This is not two editors trading reverts: the account did not push back after the second revert, and no other editor or language version moved. The same account made similar short-description and small edits to unrelated pages (Harry Houdini, Two-Face) in the preceding half hour, which fits unconstructive or test edits being cleaned up. I couldn't check what the text said because every diff fetch failed, so I'm calling this vandalism from the metadata pattern alone, and I don't see any sign of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Emoji vandalism on Turkish page for volleyball player İlkin Aydın, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56033-95) made two edits to the tr-wiki biography of volleyball player İlkin Aydın. Both edits only stuck heart and kiss emojis onto the start of the volleyball infobox ("Voleybolcu bilgi kutusu"). The first one also appears to have broken the infobox's opening line. Two different patrollers, DerinGök and SHIFT64, undid the edits within minutes (DerinGök's comment: "Yapıcı olmayan değişiklik", meaning "unconstructive edit"). No facts about the subject were changed and no other language versions were involved. This looks like low-level fan vandalism, not a real-world event. It is possible the fan was reacting to a match or other news, but the edits give no evidence of that.

briefs.headline: Third emoji edit on Turkish page for volleyball player İlkin Aydın, reverted in a minute
briefs.summary: The same temporary account (~2026-56033-95) came back for a third edit to the tr-wiki biography of volleyball player İlkin Aydın. Rev 38293949 replaced the "== Kariyeri ==" ("Career") section heading with heart and kiss emojis. Patroller SHIFT64 undid it about a minute later (rev 38293959), and the diff shows the heading put back. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but that is wrong. The graph's revert flag is false, yet SHIFT64's edit is a standard undo of that revision. As with the earlier edits, no facts about the subject were changed, no other language versions moved, and only one vandal and two patrollers are involved. This is persistent low-level fan vandalism, not a sign of a real-world event. If it keeps up, the page may get protection or the account a block, but nothing yet suggests news about the player.

briefs.headline: US 'No Kings' protests under way Oct. 17; Wikipedia article moves to past tense
briefs.summary: Editors on the English Wikipedia article "October 2026 No Kings protests" are treating the nationwide US rallies as happening now. An unregistered editor removed the {{Update}} tag, whose reason was "they have begun" (rev 1380888453). ItalianAce rewrote the Demonstrations section and changed it from future to past tense (rev 1380889445). The section that edit replaced said events were planned in many states, including Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas and Kentucky. It cited local outlets that describe Oct. 17 rallies tied to early voting before the midterms. Lorax added a photo dated 2026-10-17 of a No Kings protest at Friendship Heights on the Maryland/DC border (rev 1380890548), which is first-hand evidence that the events took place. Activity is light so far: 4 edits from 4 editors on one page, no reverts, and no other language editions checked. Turnout, size and any incidents have not appeared in the edits yet. This is a separate US event from the tracked France Oct. 17 protests, even though it falls on the same date.

briefs.headline: Vietnamese '2 Days 1 Night' page hit by mocking nickname vandalism aimed at Trường Giang
briefs.summary: The Vietnamese Wikipedia article for the show '2 ngày 1 đêm' is being hit by a wave of vandalism from several short-lived temporary accounts. The edits swap host Trường Giang's name for mocking nicknames: "chàng trai mét 6 em iu" (roughly "my sweet 1m60 guy"), "Join Làng M6", "mét sáu thích làm màu" (roughly "1m60 who loves showing off") and "Giang Lùn" ("short Giang"). One edit also tags cast member HIEUTHUHAI as having been "boosted by Join Land". Patroller Veritas Sapientiae is reverting the edits and labels them vandalism ("phá hoại"). One of the restored earlier versions still had a planted joke name ("Cristiano RonalGiango (M6)"), so the vandalism has been going on longer than this window. Contrary to the scout's note, this is not routine cast updates. Many different throwaway accounts focusing on one person suggests an online pile-on, possibly set off by recent buzz about Trường Giang. The edits themselves don't show any real-world event, and two diffs from earlier in the window couldn't be loaded.

briefs.headline: Vietnamese '2 Days 1 Night' page protected after nickname vandalism; et-wiki eKool hit with slurs
briefs.summary: Update. The vandalism wave on the Vietnamese Wikipedia article for '2 ngày 1 đêm' kept going. Temporary account ~2026-56131-10 put in more mocking names for host Trường Giang ("mét sáu thích làm màu", "Giang Đẫm bé bỏng") and renamed the criticism section to "Giang Lùn" ("Short Giang"). Patroller Veritas Sapientiae undid the edits and then added a {{pp-vandalism}} protection tag, which should slow the throwaway accounts down. The scout's note is wrong about the Estonian eKool page: this is not routine maintenance. Temporary account ~2026-54734-65 blanked the article three times in about five minutes, replacing it with racist slurs, number spam and a jab at a school. Veritas Sapientiae and Morkoz reverted each time. The two pages share no real-world event. They are linked only because one cross-wiki patroller (Veritas Sapientiae) cleaned up both, so the eKool part counts as separate, unrelated vandalism. None of these edits points to anything happening in the real world.

briefs.headline: Hebrew page for kids' show 'HaSidratiyim' sees cleanup edit reverted as season 2 airs
briefs.summary: The large churn on the Hebrew Wikipedia article for 'הסדרתיים' (a Kan Educational series) comes from one edit and its reversal. A temporary account (~2026-55928-69) copyedited the character list, cut about 2.5k bytes of plot detail (including an episode-17 detail about Ron), and added that Ron loses his powers in season 2 (rev 44084637). User חובב תחבורה ציבורית then undid it with the summary 'reverting vandalism', putting the removed text back plus a long episode-7 plot summary, net +4448 (rev 44084722). A third editor only added an explanatory-notes section (rev 44084710). The removed edit reads as a good-faith trim and copyedit, not vandalism. That makes this a small content disagreement on a fan-maintained page, not a news event. The one real-world fact on the page is that season 2 premiered on 18 October 2026, which probably explains why people are editing it now. There is one revert and no back-and-forth, so it isn't an edit war yet.

briefs.headline: CBS's Jan Crawford page draws partisan edits over her El-Sayed heckler post
briefs.summary: Four edits by three accounts in about 25 minutes added and then argued over a new Career sentence. It says that on October 18, 2026, CBS correspondent Jan Crawford praised a town-hall questioner who asked Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to denounce the Muslim Brotherhood. The only source for that sentence is Crawford's own post on X. The word used for the questioner keeps changing. One version said "white nationalist" (rev 1380869823), Muglug changed it to "heckler" and called the label unsourced (1380870739), and Gagaboatly then changed it to "Christian nationalist," citing a Handbasket story that names him as a former Hawley staffer (1380871914). A temporary account then added to the lead sentence that she is a "Trump administration shill masking as a television journalist" (1380873081), even though its edit summary said it "accurately described her current employment." That is vandalism, and it is still on the page. There is no sign she changed jobs. The news underneath appears to be a minor social-media controversy around a viral El-Sayed town-hall video. The graph shows no activity on the El-Sayed page or in other languages, so I can't confirm the event beyond the cited sources, and the page may need watching for biased or defamatory wording.

briefs.headline: Jan Crawford page: 'shill' vandalism reverted in 46 seconds; disputed El-Sayed line stays
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the earlier brief. The one new edit is a revert by Materialscientist using an anti-vandalism tool (rev 1380873182). It came 46 seconds after the edit it undid. That revert takes out the temporary account's addition to the lead sentence calling Crawford a "Trump administration shill masking as a television journalist" (1380873081), so the lead again simply calls her a television journalist, author and attorney. The earlier brief said the vandalism was still on the page; that is no longer true. The disputed Career sentence is still there. It says that on Oct 18, 2026, she praised a "Christian nationalist" for asking Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to denounce the Muslim Brotherhood. It cites her X post and a Handbasket article that names the questioner as a former staffer for Sen. Hawley (1380871914). The sentence's wording is loaded, and its main source is her own post. There are no edits after the revert, no new editors, and nothing on El-Sayed pages or in other languages. That points to a small online controversy that has calmed down, not a developing event.

briefs.headline: India's 2026 Asian Para Games page updated live with 21 October medals and results
briefs.summary: Two established editors (Neeelzzz20, Mr Gupta 18) are working together to update 'India at the 2026 Asian Para Games' (en) with results from the day's competition. There are no reverts and no conflict between them. The diffs I read add 21 October medalists to the table. Golds: Ayush Verma (men's shot put F53), Praveen Kumar (men's high jump T64) and Sachin Khiladi (men's shot put F46). Silvers include Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag (women's compound doubles), Banti, Bhagyashree Jadhav, Mohd Yasser and Manjeet Vyas. Bronzes include Anubhav Choudhary, Parveen and Rakeshbhai Bhatt. A separate badminton edit adds group-stage scores, with 22 October fixtures for players who advanced. The medal counts in the table went up step by step, to 12 gold, 16 silver and 18 bronze. This is normal, good-faith coverage of an event as it happens. I have only Wikipedia's word for these results and haven't checked them against an outside source, and only the English page was involved.

briefs.headline: India Asian Para Games page adds powerlifting silver for Kasthuri Rajamani; tally 12-17-18
briefs.summary: Live results editing continues on 'India at the 2026 Asian Para Games' (en). Mr Gupta 18 and Neeelzzz20, both established editors, are still working together, with no reverts. Since the last brief, Mr Gupta 18 added a 21 October silver for Kasthuri Rajamani in the women's 67 kg powerlifting (rev 1381266830). That raised India's silver count from 16 to 17 and its total from 46 to 47, with golds at 12 and bronzes at 18. A follow-up edit adds her lift attempts: 103, a failed 106 and a best of 108 kg (rev 1381266937). An earlier edit added a time of 11.50 marked as a personal best to Rakeshbhai Bhatt's bronze in athletics (rev 1381266161). This is normal good-faith updating during a live event. The results come only from Wikipedia and haven't been checked against outside sources.

briefs.headline: Hoax "Prayturnia" sleep condition twice inserted into Insomnia article, reverted
briefs.summary: This is a small hoax incident, not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-55799-03) twice added a paragraph to English Wikipedia's Insomnia article about a made-up related condition called "Prayturnia". The text claimed that people with it can go days without sleep with no ill effects, that about 1 in 173 million people have it (1 in 137 million in the second version), and that it is mostly found in mountainous areas like Nepal. Both versions cited a general Sleep Foundation page on sleep deprivation that doesn't back up the claim. Drchriswilliams reverted the first addition as nonconstructive, and MrOllie reverted the second as a hoax. Each revert came within about 10 minutes. There was no back-and-forth edit war, no other pages or languages were involved, and the 2,712 churn figure is just the two insertions plus their two reverts.

briefs.headline: New Hebrew Wikipedia biography of Virginia congressman Thomas W. Harrison (d. 1935)
briefs.summary: The heavy churn comes from a brand-new article, not from a rewrite of an existing one. Hebrew Wikipedia editor על הטוב created 'תומאס הריסון' (rev 44092987, +7,556 bytes, comment "creating new page"). It is a full biography of Thomas Walter Harrison (1856–1935), a Democrat who served in the Virginia Senate, as a state judge, and in the U.S. House for Virginia's 7th district (1916–22 and 1923–29). Its structure and sourcing look like a translation of the English article. The two follow-up edits are routine cleanup: YoavR changed a category using HotCat, and Assayas swapped one dash style for another (rev 44093051, −12 bytes). The subject died in 1935, nothing in the text points to anything happening now, and there are no reverts or edits in other languages. This is routine editing with no news hook.

briefs.headline: Neozapatismo label dispute continues; Moksha and Montezuma reverts are unrelated
briefs.summary: The Neozapatismo article on English Wikipedia is still in a small dispute over whether to label the EZLN "libertarian socialist." A temporary account and Rurugu twice removed a 477-byte block. Discospinster, using the Huggle anti-vandalism tool, restored it twice. Rurugu then made a -80 byte change, arguing that the EZLN reject Western political labels. Augmented Seventh reversed that change (+80, "Restored revision 1381099581 ... Observers have described"). Moksha and Carlos Montezuma are only grouped with this story because the same patrollers worked on them. Augmented Seventh and CreativeLibrary460 reverted a temporary account on Moksha, pointing to a dispute already open on the talk page. On Carlos Montezuma, ClueBot NG and CreativeLibrary460 reverted a different temporary account's one-word "not"/"nothing" edits, which look like vandalism. None of the three pages points to a real-world event, and none of the diffs could be loaded, so this rests on edit sizes and summaries only.

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster on 5 enwiki pages: San Sebastián page blanked, Neozapatismo spat cools
briefs.summary: This cluster is linked only by shared patrollers (Augmented Seventh on all 5 pages, plus CreativeLibrary460, Discospinster and ClueBot NG). It is not a real-world event. Two corrections to the scout: Long Beach is already covered by vandalism story s_6f43c0b1 and Moksha by s_2b6c075a, but no other story in the graph covers Carlos Montezuma. Caveat: no diff would load (all returned errors), so this rests only on edit sizes, summaries and who reverted.

briefs.headline: Neozapatismo article: small revert fight over 'libertarian socialist' label
briefs.summary: Over about 9 minutes the English Wikipedia article on Neozapatismo went through five edits. Each one added or removed the same 477-byte block, apart from a final -80 byte change. A temporary account undid an earlier edit by JalenBarks (rev 1378250640). Discospinster, using the Huggle anti-vandalism tool, put the text back as "unexplained content removal". Rurugu then removed it again, Discospinster restored it again, and Rurugu made a final edit with the summary that the EZLN "reject any idea of western politics" and should not be called libertarian socialists. From the edit summaries, this is a dispute over how to label the movement's ideology. It is not a real-world event or vandalism. It is one page, in one language, with no activity on other pages, and none of the editors worked on any other page in the graph. Caveat: none of the diffs could be loaded, so this brief relies only on edit sizes and summaries, and the exact wording in dispute is unconfirmed. It is possible, but not shown, that the temporary account and Rurugu are the same person.

briefs.headline: Patrol cluster: San Sebastián article blanked, Montezuma spam; no new event

The graph shows no revert of it yet, and the edit-by-edit dispute is already covered by story s_2b6c075a. Nothing here points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Zumbi dos Palmares (pt-wiki): one account's vandalism reverted twice; no new activity

There have been no edits since my earlier brief. I'd suggest closing it unless the account comes back.

briefs.headline: Zumbi dos Palmares (pt-wiki): small vandalism by one account, reverted twice

Black Consciousness Day (20 November) is a month away, so it may have drawn some extra attention to the page, but nothing in the edits ties them to it.

briefs.headline: One temporary account blanked big chunks of five articles, including the Serbian protests page; all reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Temporary account ~2026-56102-20 cut large blocks of text with no edit summary from five unrelated English Wikipedia articles in about 30 minutes: Phnom Penh (−10,150), GoDaddy (−3,578), Preply (−3,288), Suno (−16,844) and 2024–present Serbian anti-corruption protests (−37,192). The two diffs I read show the infobox, the lead and long sourced sections deleted in each case, with broken template pieces left behind. Nothing new was added and no real-world event is mentioned. Patroller KH-1 reverted both the Suno and the Serbian protests edits within minutes. There's no sign of other editors or other language versions moving, and this isn't a back-and-forth revert fight. The only reason Suno and the protests page were grouped together is that the same account hit both. One thing worth noting is a maintenance tag on the protests page saying it has no coverage of 2026 events. That points to an article that's falling behind, not to anything new happening right now.

briefs.headline: Reverted vandalism on Stefon Diggs and Hopi; It's Jeff redirect change is unrelated

The deleted infobox listing Diggs with the Washington Commanders for 2026 was already on the page before the vandalism, so it is not new information. Recommend merging this into the existing vandalism story and closing it.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Stefon Diggs and Hopi pages by one temp account, reverted; no news event
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56045-94) vandalised two unrelated pages. On Hopi it added the phrase "they were 67rizzers" (rev 1381088856). On Stefon Diggs it deleted the whole infobox and added "he was born in ohio and had 27 moms" (rev 1381089316, edit summary "hgjjg"). That deletion explains the -1,899-byte change the scout noticed. briefs.headline: Sonay Kartal loses Wuhan Open WTA 1000 final in three sets, page edits show
briefs.summary: Correction to the scout's note: Sonay Kartal is a British tennis player, not a politician. Within about six minutes, three editors updated her English Wikipedia finals table. They changed a WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open, China, from "Pending/TBD" to a loss, 6–2, 4–6, 2–6. That moves her WTA singles finals record to 1 title and 1 runner-up (revs 1380872784, 1380873034). The other edits only tweak formatting: cell colours under the WikiTennis style (1380873352, 1380873609). Nobody reverted anything and the editors didn't disagree, so this looks like normal results-tracking after a real match. The pattern of a final first marked pending, then filled in with a score, fits a final that has just been played. The opponent's name isn't in any diff I read, and I haven't checked other languages or sources.

briefs.headline: Maja Chwalińska beats Sonay Kartal to win Wuhan Open, her first WTA 1000 title
briefs.summary: This update names the opponent missing from the earlier Kartal brief. Maja Chwalińska of Poland appears to have beaten Britain's Sonay Kartal in the 2026 Wuhan Open singles final. Earlier diffs had Kartal losing 6–2, 4–6, 2–6. Chwalińska's English Wikipedia page now says she won the 2026 Wuhan Open, "a WTA 1000 level-event," as her one WTA Tour singles title (rev 1380873238). Her performance table marks Wuhan as a win ("W", 6–0 in matches) and counts a first WTA 1000 title (revs 1380873667, 1380874335). Kartal's page mirrors this: Wuhan is marked "F" (runner-up), with a 5–1 run at the event (rev 1380874651). A new prose section (rev 1380874064) cites Independent and Sky Sports reports for her path to her first WTA 1000 final, including wins over Bencic, Paolini, Svitolina and Ostapenko. Six named editors and one temporary account worked on both pages, with nothing reverted. Some edits only reformat the infobox (rev 1380872821). The edits match each other but this isn't checked against outside sources, and no other language editions have been looked at.

briefs.headline: Chwalińska's Wuhan win added to prose; early No. 11 ranking claim reverted
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked Wuhan Open story. The result hasn't changed: Maja Chwalińska beat Sonay Kartal in three sets in the 2026 Wuhan Open final. Since the last brief, Chwalińska's English article has added prose saying "She went on to win the final, beating Sonay Kartal in three sets," citing a Sky Sports highlights page. The section heading now says "first WTA Title" (rev 1380878695). That edit also says she rose to No. 11 the following week. The one revert is about that ranking, not the result. Kapnonian changed her infobox to No. 11 as of 19 October 2026 (rev 1380874767). Moscow Connection undid it with the note "Come back when the ratings are updated" (rev 1380877668), because the new ranking hasn't been published yet. That's normal housekeeping, not an edit war. Polish Wikipedia shows the same thing: an editor's comment reads "Ranking nie został opublikowany" ("ranking not published"), though I couldn't load that diff. Other new edits are formatting on Kartal's page (rev 1380875566) and a stats tweak (rev 1380880224). Treat the No. 11 ranking as unconfirmed until WTA publishes it; the prose still says No. 11, which contradicts the reverted infobox.

briefs.headline: Polish Wikipedia records Maja Chwalińska winning Wuhan Open 2026, her first WTA title
briefs.summary: Polish Wikipedia's article on tennis player Maja Chwalińska says she won the Wuhan Open 2026 final on 18 October, beating Sonay Kartal 2:6, 6:4, 6:2. The article calls it her first career WTA title. It also says she is the third Polish woman to win a WTA 1000-level event (or equivalent) and the first Polish player to win in Wuhan. Editor Mareczekkk added these lines (rev 80999998, 81000038), along with her route to the title: wins over Sherif, Bouzková, Jović, Sakkari, and Iga Świątek 7:5, 6:1 in the semifinal, described as her first win over a top-10 player. Editors are being careful rather than fighting. RafaEl030794 first added a one-line "tournament winner" sentence (80999973). Mareczekkk had earlier hidden an unsourced lead mention of reaching the Wuhan final (80999884), and later undid an early ranking update to No. 11, saying the new ranking had not been published yet (81000054). There were no reverts by other editors, and all three editors are named accounts. The only source cited for the final is a live-match page on Sport.pl, and no other language versions are moving in the graph, so the result is not independently confirmed here.

briefs.headline: Pope Leo XIV page on Italian Wikipedia: vandalism reverted, no further activity
briefs.summary: This update finds no new activity. The graph still shows the same 4 edits on it.wiki's "Papa Leone XIV" page, and nothing came after Titore's revert (rev 153000750). The scout called this routine editing, but it is vandalism: one temporary account (~2026-54751-20) and two editors who undid its changes. Its second edit (rev 153000718) changed "primo papa... proveniente dagli Stati Uniti" (the first pope from the United States) to "secondo papa" (the second). Titore restored "primo" in rev 153000750. The text of the first vandal edit (rev 153000669) and the content of Moderatore Automatico's revert of it (rev 153000677) can no longer be retrieved. The likeliest reason is that administrators hid the revision because it was offensive, which fits the prior brief's description of insults and drug slang, but I have not confirmed this. Nothing points to a real-world event. Watch for repeat attempts that might lead to page protection.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Italian Wikipedia's Pope Leo XIV article, reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. One temporary account (~2026-54751-20) made two edits to it.wiki's "Papa Leone XIV" page and both were undone within about two minutes. In the first edit (rev 153000669), it swapped the papal motto for a joke phrase and added insults and drug slang, calling him a "papa bastardo" and saying he spent his years in Peru "a pippare bamba" (snorting cocaine). The automatic anti-vandalism tool Moderatore Automatico reverted it nine seconds later. In the second edit (rev 153000718), the account changed "primo papa" to "secondo papa" proveniente dagli Stati Uniti, a quiet factual sabotage. Titore reverted it in rev 153000750. The edit comments describe these as reverts, even though the graph's revert flag didn't mark them. The edits came from one source, on one page, in one language, and nothing in them points to a real-world event. Watch only for repeat edits that might call for page protection.

briefs.headline: De-wiki housekeeping: Stratz bio tidied up; new Kirk T. McDonald page tagged for speedy deletion
briefs.summary: This is routine German Wikipedia maintenance, not a news event. Heinz Stratz is a writer and translator who lived 1897–1941. Experienced maintainers are tidying a new biography of him. M2k~dewiki added the Personendaten template, Normdaten IDs (GND/LCCN/VIAF), a sort key and categories (rev 271486638). Magipulus added categories and fixed links. According to his edit summary, Magipulus also changed the place of death because "Herzberg bei Murmansk" seems to have been a Wehrmacht nickname for a hill, not a real town. The big churn on Kirk T. McDonald (Wikidata Q105708212, probably the Princeton physicist) comes from one new article: Alexandre Vendryes, an account with 19 edits, created it at about 5 KB and then cut about 770 bytes. M2k~dewiki made a small fix, and Flossenträger then posted "SLA+", meaning a speedy-deletion request. None of the three McDonald revisions can be fetched any more and the page has no summary, so it was most likely deleted. That inference is my only uncertainty, and I could not read those diffs. There are no reverts, no other language versions involved, and nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on writer Heinz Stratz (1897–1941) gets routine cleanup
briefs.summary: The activity is standard maintenance on a new or newly finished German Wikipedia biography of Heinz Stratz, a German writer and literary translator born in 1897 in Łódź who was killed in 1941 near Murmansk. It is not a news event. The author, Dierp40 (a one-edit account), removed the {{Baustelle}} "under construction" tag. Then experienced maintainers took over. M2k~dewiki added the Personendaten template, Normdaten authority IDs (GND/LCCN/VIAF), a sort key, and birth/death-year categories. Magipulus added more categories and fixed quotation marks. The death date in the text is 23 June 1941, so there is no recent death or biographical development, and there are no reverts or disputes. The 748-byte figure flagged by the scout is just these six small additions added together.

I read the three insertions.

briefs.headline: BBC to close BBC Three linear channel in spring 2027 and take it back online-only, edits say
briefs.summary: Three registered editors updated the English BBC Three article within about 45 minutes, with no reverts. Benmathieson901 added a new section, "Reverting back to an Internet service". It says that on 20 October 2026 the BBC announced the linear BBC Three channel will close in spring 2027 and go online-only, along with the BBC Scotland TV channel and BBC Radio 4 Extra, as part of a plan to cut £500m by 2028. The section cites a BBC News article dated 20 October 2026, with an archived copy. VernardoLau then reworded the text and merged the duplicate citations, and Benjamintchip added "Spring 2027 (planned)" as a closing date in the infobox. The BBC Scotland (TV channel) and BBC Radio 4 Extra articles were also edited in the same window, which fits a joint announcement, though I didn't read those diffs. This looks like a real corporate announcement rather than a routine schedule change. Not yet confirmed: I haven't checked the BBC source itself, and the exact closure date is still only "spring 2027".

briefs.headline: BBC to close BBC Three, BBC Scotland channel and Radio 4 Extra in spring 2027, edits say
briefs.summary: Three registered editors (VernardoLau, Benmathieson901, Benjamintchip) edited the English BBC Three and BBC Scotland (TV channel) articles in parallel over about 50 minutes, with no reverts. The BBC Radio 4 Extra article was also edited in the same window by VernardoLau plus two other editors, which makes six distinct editors across the cluster. On BBC Three, Benmathieson901 added a section saying the BBC announced on 20 October 2026 that the BBC Three and BBC Scotland linear channels will close in spring 2027 and go online-only, as part of a plan to cut £500m by 2028. On the BBC Scotland channel page, VernardoLau rewrote the lead and History section to give the same news, adding that the content will move to BBC iPlayer and some programmes will air on the Scottish versions of BBC One and BBC Two. Benjamintchip added "Spring 2027 (planned)" as the closing date in both infoboxes. Every addition cites the same BBC News article dated 20 October 2026, with an archived copy and a byline later added as Steven McIntosh. This looks like a real corporate announcement. I haven't checked the BBC article itself or read the Radio 4 Extra diffs, and the exact closure date is still only "spring 2027".

briefs.headline: ALCS page wrap-up: Rays beat Guardians 4–2 to reach World Series vs. Brewers
briefs.summary: The 2026 ALCS article is getting wrap-up edits after the series ended, not live in-game updates as the scout guessed. BaseballFanatic1 added a Game 6 recap: Yandy Díaz hit a two-run homer in the eighth to make it 7–3, and Bryan Baker pitched a scoreless ninth. The same edit says the Rays are heading to their third World Series, citing an MLB.com piece headlined "Rays finish off Guards to set up World Series clash vs. Crew". That editor also bolded the Rays as winners (4–2) in the composite line score and raised total attendance from 197,475 to 207,475. Smitty Smitty added that Junior Caminero was named ALCS MVP, then removed it about 14 seconds later, so the MVP award is unconfirmed by these edits. The other changes are small copyedits and wikilinks, with no reverts between editors and no vandalism. The Brewers–Rays matchup already shows up in tracked stories about the 2026 World Series page (s_a9b43062, s_5a8fb50c), so this is follow-up to a known result rather than new news. That supports a routine, low-priority story, and it could be linked to the World Series story.

briefs.headline: Ivar Aasen article on no.wiki hit by schoolyard-style vandalism, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: Over about 20 minutes, two temporary accounts vandalised the opening sentence of the Norwegian Wikipedia biography of Ivar Aasen (1813–1896), the creator of Nynorsk. Neither edit relates to any real event. Account ~2026-56235-93 first changed his life dates to "1967–1969" (rev 26005573, labelled "En feil", meaning "an error"), then piped the link for "språkforsker" (linguist) to an insult meaning "sex offender" (rev 26005581). Patandor, an experienced patroller with 66 edits on the page, reverted both. Minutes later a second temporary account, ~2026-56144-51, swapped "språkforsker" for a vulgar phrase (rev 26005592), and Patandor reverted that within 5 minutes (rev 26005597). The scout read this as routine maintenance with no reverts, but that was wrong: the "no reverts" count came from the revert flag not being set on Patandor's rollbacks. Two separate temporary accounts doing the same thing could mean a classroom or coordinated prank, but nothing suggests a news hook. The article is clean now.

briefs.headline: Routine cleanup of de-wiki bio of MDR presenter Henriette Fee Grützner

briefs.headline: Philip Dwyer vandal returns; Birthmark film page sees repeated self-linking by namesake
briefs.summary: The temporary account ~2026-46936-96 came back to the English Wikipedia article on Philip Dwyer with two more edits. One changed the short description to "far-right anti-immigration "activist" and dole sponger" (rev 1380905651). The other changed the infobox name to "Angry Phil" (rev 1380905761). SuperPianoMan9167 reverted both in a single edit about 16 seconds later. This continues the vandalism already tracked on that page. The scout called Birthmark (film) one small addition, but it was actually three attempts, all reverted. An account named Vikram Shreedharan, the same name as the 2024 Tamil film's credited director, writer and producer, kept turning that credit into a link: first to User:Vikram_Shreedharan (rev 1380903538), then to Draft:Vikram_Shreedharan (rev 1380905847). IrisChronomia and SuperPianoMan9167 undid each attempt. This looks like conflict-of-interest self-promotion, with a low-level revert loop against patrollers rather than a real dispute, but we can't confirm the account is really the filmmaker. No other languages and no real-world event are involved on either page.

briefs.headline: Philip Dwyer article hit by infobox name vandalism, reverted within minutes

briefs.headline: 2026 World Series page: routine copyediting before Brewers–Rays Game 1
briefs.summary: The English article "2026 World Series" is getting small, low-stakes edits ahead of the series. briefs.headline: Temp account repeatedly strips Jewish-community content from Ioannina, Larissa pages
briefs.summary: The activity comes from one temporary account (~2026-56372-73) taking out Jewish-history material from two Greek city articles on English Wikipedia. It is not driven by any real-world event. On Ioannina, the account removed the whole 8 KB "Jewish community" section four times in about 55 minutes. The section covers the Romaniote synagogue and the 1944 deportation of 1,870 Jews to Auschwitz. The account's edit summary argues that covering only one minority is "political propaganda". Three different patrollers (TonySt, StephenMacky1, EndTheWikiEditor) put the section back each time. On Larissa, the same account removed a synagogue image three times, citing "unnecessary image and reference", and was reverted twice by EndTheWikiEditor and Discospinster. One reverter called the edits good-faith, but the pattern is one editor reverting against several others, which probably breaks Wikipedia's three-revert rule. The content was restored after each removal on both pages. No other languages or outside triggers are involved. Things could flare up again if the account keeps going or gets blocked, but as news this has little value.

briefs.headline: Temp account's push to remove Greek Jewish history fails as patrollers restore all four pages
briefs.summary: This is the same campaign we already track, now winding down, and not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56372-73 made one last round of removals on English Wikipedia between about 1792539099 and 1792539142. It cut the 8 KB Ioannina "Jewish community" section a fifth time (rev 1381244163). That section covers the 1829 Romaniote synagogue and the deportation of 1,870 Jews to Auschwitz in March 1944. This time the account argued that "religious texts are not valid historical sources". It also again removed the clause "reaches back two thousand years" from the opening of History of the Jews in Thessaloniki (1381244231), and again removed the synagogue image on Larissa. All three were reverted within about a minute: EndTheWikiEditor on Ioannina (1381244273), AriuCH on Larissa, and Discospinster on the Jewish-history article. The graph shows no edits on any of the four pages since then, so all the content stands restored and the account looks to have stopped, or been stopped, though we can't confirm a block from here. Over the whole campaign it was one account against six patrollers, with 18 edits by the remover across four pages, no other language editions affected and no outside trigger visible. News value is low; only watch for a renewed attempt or page protection.

briefs.headline: Temp account's removal of Jewish history spreads to Thessaloniki pages; patrollers revert it
briefs.summary: This adds to the existing Ioannina/Larissa story rather than being a new event. The same temporary account (~2026-56372-73) moved from Ioannina and Larissa to Thessaloniki and History of the Jews in Thessaloniki on English Wikipedia. On Thessaloniki, it first removed the whole roughly 12 KB "Jews of Thessaloniki" summary section (rev 1381237183), calling it "ethnic bias" and "political purposes". It then kept cutting the Romaniote/Paul the Apostle sentences (about 219 bytes) over and over (e.g. 1381243645). On the Jewish-history article, it cut the early-settlement section about Paul's Epistle to the Thessalonians (about 2.3 KB), saying "religious texts are not valid historical sources" (1381242761). It also repeatedly removed the opening clause "reaches back two thousand years" (1381244231). Seven distinct accounts were involved, not the 13 the scout counted: the one remover and six patrollers (EndTheWikiEditor, Discospinster, AriuCH, Dr vulpes, TonySt, StephenMacky1). They reverted every removal within minutes, so all content is currently restored. It is one account against many on four pages, well past the three-revert rule, with no other languages and no outside trigger visible. A block or page protection is the likely next step, and the news value is low.

briefs.headline: New ru-wiki stub on 1990s Moscow electronic band 'Spirali' tagged for deletion
briefs.summary: The churn comes from a page being created, not from anything happening in the world. On ru-wiki, user Дальных created 'СПИРАЛИ' (+1808 bytes), a page with nothing but infoboxes. It describes a Moscow electronic group (big beat, breakbeat, trip hop) active 1997–2003, with labels and members listed. It has a blank, duplicated infobox template and no prose. A temporary account (~2026-54331-87) then deleted the empty infobox and added a {{Db-nn}} speedy-deletion tag for lack of notability. EyeBot automatically reverted that edit based on an ORES score (+919). The bot's revert is not a revert pair between people, so this is not an edit war. The 3646 churn is just these three edits added up. I see no sign of a real-world event behind the page. The page will probably be re-tagged for deletion or cleaned up.

briefs.headline: Old Kharkiv war-crimes material restored to ruwiki page on Russian Gen. Makovetsky
briefs.summary: The ruwiki article on Lt. Gen. Oleg Makovetsky, commander of Russia's 6th Air and Air Defence Army, had five edits from three accounts. A temporary account added "Ukraine" to his combat record (rev 155689864) and a line saying he "is accused of war crimes in Ukraine" (rev 155689885). The anti-vandalism bot EyeBot reverted both, and neither edit cited a source. Then BFD-69 undid an older edit, 153404646 by Shluzzzoid (rev 155690163, +3494). That restored a lead sentence and a section saying Makovetsky ordered the bombing of Kharkiv and Kharkiv Oblast, and that Kharkiv regional prosecutors have named him a suspect. All of the restored sources are from March 2022 (LB.ua, Volynnews, Futura News). Nothing points to a new event such as a death, award, arrest or new charges. This looks like an ongoing content dispute over Ukraine-related allegations, not a news trigger. Uncertainty: one more removal and restore would make this an edit war, and a new development could still be behind the anonymous edits, but nothing in the text shows one.

briefs.headline: Lithuanian Wikipedia: patroller reverts new user's additions to business/marketing pages
briefs.summary: This is routine maintenance, not a news event. A new account, Mazasisatlas4s, made its only two edits to two Lithuanian Wikipedia pages about 13 minutes apart. On "Verslo administravimas" (Business administration) it added 614 bytes; the edit summary describes text about accreditation of study programmes. On "Rinkodara" (Marketing) it added 807 bytes; the summary describes text on how specialist training in Lithuania has developed since 1990. The patroller Homo ergaster undid both edits within about 2 minutes each. That account was doing the same to other pages at the time (Wii U, Mario, Lego, Imunoanalizė and others). Nobody re-added the text, so this is not an edit war, and there's no sign of an outside event. The topic and style suggest a student or someone adding material about their institution, but that's a guess: none of the diffs would load, so this account rests only on edit metadata and summaries, and I can't say why the text was removed. The scout's "four editors" doesn't match the dossier, which shows two.

briefs.headline: Minor test edits and vandalism on es-wiki Nelson Mandela page; no news hook
briefs.summary: Three edits in about 2.5 minutes on Spanish Wikipedia's "Nelson Mandela" article. All of them touch the opening sentence and none adds any facts. The first, by temporary account ~2026-56166-32, added a stray comma after the birth and death dates. The bot Automoderador reverted it automatically. About two minutes later a second temporary account, ~2026-55928-03, put the word "peo" (Spanish slang for "fart") in front of the birth date, with an edit summary that doesn't make sense. That edit was still standing when I last checked. The graph has no linked Mandela pages in other languages and no other recent activity, and the dates he was born and died (1918 and 2013) were not changed. This looks like ordinary schoolkid-style vandalism on a famous article, not a sign that anything happened in the real world. I can't tell whether both edits came from the same person using two accounts.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on es-wiki "Sexualidad" and "Nelson Mandela"; bots revert most of it
briefs.summary: This is vandalism by temporary accounts on Spanish Wikipedia. Nothing happened in the real world. I disagree with the scout's note on one point: the large change on "Sexualidad" (−1883 bytes) was not a cleanup. The account ~2026-56166-73 (edit summary "Errores") deleted most of the opening section, including cited text on animal sexual behaviour, and replaced part of it with "NUNJAMASSASSSSSSS USES WIKIPEDIA". Automoderador put the text back 8 seconds later. Earlier, the same account had swapped "técnicas" for "tung tun sahurr", a meme phrase, and SeroBOT reverted that within 8 seconds. On "Nelson Mandela", ~2026-56166-32 added a stray comma, which Automoderador reverted. ~2026-55928-03 then inserted "peo" before the birth date. The graph shows no revert of that edit, so it may still be live; that should be checked on the wiki itself. Mandela's dates (1918–2013) were not changed. The two pages are not about the same topic. The likely link is the editors: the temporary-account names ~2026-56166-32 and ~2026-56166-73 look very similar, so they may have been created close together, perhaps by the same person or the same place (e.g. a school). That link is a guess, and it does not extend to ~2026-55928-03.

briefs.headline: Barbera Thornhill page: small dispute over YouTube-sourced claim about her son
briefs.summary: On the en-wiki biography of Barbera Thornhill (US Ambassador-at-Large to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons since Oct 2026), a temporary account added one sentence: "She has a son named Hale Thornhill-Wilson." Its only source was a YouTube video titled "This Woman Eerily Appeared Out Of Nowhere" from the channel MinutesOfHorror (rev 1381173524). Realcosmixyt, a regular patroller, removed it as unsourced. A single-edit account (H1234ek) put it back, saying the information was correct but not the original source. Realcosmixyt removed it again because YouTube is not a reliable source (rev 1381175366). All the churn is that one 245-byte sentence going in and out four times within about 20 minutes. There's no sign of a real-world event and no movement on other languages or pages. Uncertain: it's a claim about a family member on a living person's biography, it's still unverified, and it could come back if more single-edit accounts keep pushing it.

briefs.headline: Student-style vandalism on zhwiki Our Lady's College (HK) page, reverted by patrollers
briefs.summary: This is school-page vandalism, not news. One account, Nickychinnnnnn, made four edits in about 10 minutes to the zhwiki article on 聖母書院 (Our Lady's College, Wong Tai Sin, Hong Kong). Two patrollers, BanSpdRunOrMaybeNot and XiaoFui, reverted each one, and the page is back to its earlier version. The edits were juvenile: the school name became the insult "聖母豬院 band 3" ("band 3" is a slang label for a low-ranked school), the campus size went from 6,600 to 100,000 m² with made-up playgrounds and "lucky swimming pools", and a "history department head" was added as a notable alumna. There is no edit war: both patrollers reverted the same vandal, and nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: zhwiki Our Lady's College (HK) page: school vandalism fully reverted, no new activity
briefs.summary: This is the same vandalism already tracked on the zhwiki article 聖母書院 (Our Lady's College, Wong Tai Sin, Hong Kong). It is not a news event. One account, Nickychinnnnnn, made four edits in about 10 minutes. Patrollers BanSpdRunOrMaybeNot and XiaoFui undid each one within about 1–5 minutes, and the page is back to its earlier version. The two diffs I read show the vandalism: one inflated the campus from 6,600 to 100,000 m², with 10 playgrounds, 30 labs and "lucky swimming pools", and the other added a current history department head as a notable alumna. A small correction to the scout's note: only one revert carries a revert flag, but the comments show all four edits were undone. The graph has no edits after the last revert (rev 95181665), and the pattern is two patrollers against one vandal, not an edit war.

briefs.headline: UFO sightings list: same temp account re-adds unsourced text after revert
briefs.summary: This is the same low-level churn on English Wikipedia's 'List of reported UFO sightings' that we are already tracking. Temporary account ~2026-56176-35 first added a +50-byte "sighting of two boys who saw a alein" (rev 1381290431). AndyTheGrump reverted it as "unsourced nonsense".
