A second temporary account's +7-byte edit was also reverted, as "rvv". After both reverts, ~2026-56176-35 came back with a new +112-byte, unsourced and ungrammatical sentence (rev 1381291325): "Since them there has been very few amounts of sightings if so a lot have been put online on different websites". The graph does not yet show that edit as reverted. There are only 3 editors, one page and no other languages, and no edit names a dated or sourced incident, so nothing points to a real-world event. It looks like persistent novice or test editing that will probably be reverted again. It is not an edit war: one experienced editor is reverting a temporary account that keeps re-adding content.

briefs.headline: Unsourced 'alien sighting' additions to UFO list reverted; no real-world event
briefs.summary: Two different temporary accounts each made one small edit to English Wikipedia's 'List of reported UFO sightings' (+50 and +7 bytes). Experienced editor AndyTheGrump reverted both within about two minutes, calling them "unsourced nonsense" and "rvv" (revert vandalism). The first editor's own edit summary says they "added another sighting of two boys who saw a alein". The diffs I could read were cut off, so I could not see the exact text that was added. Still, the edit summaries, the small sizes and the quick reverts all point to low-grade vandalism or test edits, not a real reported sighting. No other languages and no related pages moved, so I see no sign of a real-world event behind this.

briefs.headline: Swedish Wiki bio of Företagarna CEO Magnus Demervall: rewrite rolled back twice, no news
briefs.summary: The scout reported no reverts, but that's wrong. On sv.wikipedia, the temporary account ~2026-56289-70 replaced Magnus Demervall's biography with a shorter rewrite (rev 59785628, −4953 bytes). The rewrite removed the infobox, his birth name (Andersson), his home in Segersta and his Egyptian father, and the detailed Centre Party career section. It added a new lead and promotional-sounding material based on his member-magazine interview about Företagarna's priorities (rev 59785636). Patroller Yger rolled the account back. The account then put its version back (rev 59785656, −3548), and EPIC rolled it back again (rev 59785662). So this is a small, one-sided dispute between one newcomer and two patrollers, possibly with a conflict of interest, not a real-world event. The only facts in it (CEO of Företagarna since February 2025, succeeding Benjamin Dousa) are old news. It could start up again if the temp account comes back, but there's no sign of a news hook.

briefs.headline: Demervall sv-wiki bio: temp account's rewrite rolled back twice, page now quiet, no news
briefs.summary: Nothing has been edited since the last brief. EPIC's rollback (rev 59785662) is still the latest edit on sv:Magnus Demervall. The diffs confirm what happened. Temporary account ~2026-56289-70 put its shorter rewrite back (rev 59785656). The rewrite replaced the infobox and the detailed lead with a short "organisationschef" lead sourced to Riksdagen, and removed his birth name (Andersson), his home in Segersta, his Egyptian father and the Centre Party career section. EPIC then restored Yger's version (rev 59785662). This was one temporary account against two patrollers, two rollbacks in total. It looks like an attempt to tidy up or curate the biography, possibly with a conflict of interest. It is not a real-world event: the only facts in it (CEO of Företagarna since February 2025) are old news. The scout's 'no reverts' reading is wrong because the rollbacks aren't flagged as reverts in the graph. The scout is right that the story has no broader significance. Things to watch: whether the account comes back, or whether the rewrite turns up on other language versions.

briefs.headline: Cuti Romero (es): newcomer adds sources, two anti-vandal bots revert, edits restored
briefs.summary: The Spanish article on Cuti Romero had a short back-and-forth between one temporary account (~2026-44405-78) and two anti-vandalism bots (SeroBOT, Automoderador). The user's edits were reverted twice, and both times the user put them back. This is not news. The article already said Romero plays for Atlético de Madrid and captains Argentina before these edits. The diffs show the user adding press citations for those existing claims: Infobae (2026-10-18), Clarín (2026-10-13) and La Gaceta (2026-09-25), which report that Scaloni named him captain after Messi left. The user also rewrote the career list, removing the loan markers. That makes it less precise: Genoa is now listed as 2018-20, and the Juventus and loan entries are gone. The user also added a typo-ridden line saying he never played for Juventus. The bot reverts look like automated responses to an unregistered user's large changes, not a fight over facts. No other languages or human editors are involved. The weak point is that the career-list rewrite is lower quality and may still get reverted by a human patroller.

briefs.headline: Cuti Romero (es): no new activity; sourcing edits and bot reverts remain routine
briefs.summary: I re-checked the story and found no new edits since the prior brief. The page still has six edits from three accounts: temporary account ~2026-44405-78, SeroBOT and Automoderador. The user's edits were reverted twice by bots and restored both times. No humans pushed back and no other language editions changed. In rev 175884041 the user adds press citations to claims the article already made: that Romero plays for Atlético de Madrid and captains Argentina. The citations are Infobae (2026-10-18), Clarín (2026-10-13) and La Gaceta (2026-09-25), which say Scaloni named him captain after Messi's farewell. In rev 175884004 the user flattens the career list and removes the loan markers. That leaves Genoa as 2018-20, drops the Juventus row, and adds a typo-ridden claim that he never played for Juventus. The edits add no new real-world event. The open risk is that a human patroller undoes the lower-quality rewrite.

briefs.headline: Reformation vandalism reverted; fuel protests page sees routine upkeep
briefs.summary: This story is two unrelated threads. The only thing joining them is anti-vandalism patroller Celjski Grad, who reverted bad edits on both pages. On 'Reformation', temporary account ~2026-55860-40 added the same 27 bytes five times. The edits were reverted by ClueBot NG ("possible vandalism"), MattMauler, T430s and Celjski Grad, and the account's last re-add had the comment "suck it". That is a small vandalism spree, not a real content dispute. I read the first diff (rev 1380912591), but the tool cut off the text before the 27 bytes, so I can't confirm exactly what was inserted. On '2026 French fuel protests' (protests over fuel prices that began 15 September 2026), the work is routine: OrdinariusFingius added 418 bytes to the Reactions section and swapped the image, and a 12-byte unsourced addition by another temporary account was reverted. I couldn't load the diffs for those edits, so I can't say what the Reactions text says. Nothing here suggests a new real-world development beyond ongoing coverage of the protests.

briefs.headline: France fuel protests page logs 17 Oct riots and Macron crackdown vow; Reformation vandal reverted
briefs.summary: The scout called the fuel-protests edits "routine". The diffs show the opposite: enwiki '2026 French fuel protests' is recording a major escalation. Rev 1380921375 contains text, cited to AFP, CNN, ABC and Al Jazeera, saying that on 17 October 2026 protests spread to about 110 cities, joining student protests and a revived yellow-vest movement. Turnout figures are 550,000 from the Interior Ministry and 800,000 from the CGT union. PM Sébastien Lecornu reported 1,200 arrests and 150 police officers injured, and Limoges's Hôtel de Ville was firebombed and burned down. Rev 1380919091 adds that Macron promised a "firm response" to the rioting (KATV, dated 18 Oct). Most of this text was already on the page before these edits, which polish it (one editor is fixing the transcription of a slogan on a yellow vest). The page has only one active content editor (OrdinariusFingius) and no other-language pages linked in the graph, so the facts rest on the cited sources, not wide editor activity. Separately, '~2026-55882-34' tried to insert "Palestinian" into an image caption (rev 1380920053) and was reverted as unsourced. The Reformation thread is still plain vandalism: temporary account ~2026-55860-40 kept re-adding a 27-byte change ("suck it"; rev 1380920471, text cut off in the tool) and four patrollers/bots reverted it. The two pages are linked only by patroller Celjski Grad.

briefs.headline: Brazilian 'Rebelde' actress Lua Blanco dies of cancer at 39, Wikipedia edits indicate
briefs.summary: This doesn't look like routine article work. The Portuguese and English Wikipedia articles on Lua Blanco, the Brazilian actress and singer who played Roberta in 'Rebelde', are being updated to say she died on 18 October 2026, aged 39. Klebs1 expanded the ptwiki "Morte" (Death) section (rev 73240857) to say she had intestinal (colorectal) cancer and had kept her months of treatment private. That edit cites Quem, CNN Brasil and Jornal de Brasília. On enwiki, an editor changed the cause to "intestinal cancer in Rio de Janeiro" (rev 1380911241), citing Metrópoles. The ptwiki page has about 35 edits since activity started roughly 3.4 hours ago, from more than 15 named accounts. One unsourced change of the cause to Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (rev 73241364, Gozolinogozado) was undone within minutes because "the sources say cancer" (rev 73241381). The rest is cleanup: categories and wording. The death itself is not disputed. The exact cancer type comes from press reports cited in the article, and I have not checked those sources myself.

briefs.headline: Lua Blanco article: follow-up edits only tidy up; cancer death account unchanged
briefs.summary: This is the same ptwiki page as the breaking story on the death of Lua Blanco, the 'Rebelde' actress, and the new edits add nothing to it. They are housekeeping. Francisco Leandro made the death category more specific, changing it to "deaths from cancer in Rio de Janeiro state" (rev 73241414). Guedexx tidied the infobox and cut the family list down to the relatives who have their own articles (rev 73241172). Lord Zaxor fixed a spelling error ("descrição" to "discrição", meaning "privacy") and complained in his edit summary (rev 73241408): 79a's earlier undo of the Creutzfeldt-Jakob vandalism had also brought the typo back (rev 73241381). That summary was annoyed, but it was a single fix, not a back-and-forth edit war. The scout's "no reverts" note is slightly off because of that one undo, which was a correct one. The article still says she died on 18 October 2026, aged 39, of intestinal cancer, citing Quem, CNN Brasil and Jornal de Brasília. I have not checked those outlets independently. I suggest merging this into the tracked breaking story rather than treating it as a separate event.

briefs.headline: Estonia football page: old Oct 2025 results pruned, briefly reverted, then removed again
briefs.summary: This is routine maintenance on the English Wikipedia page for the Estonia national football team, not news. Chelsdog, an established editor with 335 edits, removed two match boxes from October 2025: the 1–3 home loss to Italy on 11 October and the 1–1 draw with Moldova on 14 October, both 2026 World Cup qualifiers. TonySt reverted this as "unexplained content removal". Chelsdog then removed the same 1,589 bytes again with the explanation "over one year", which fits the usual practice of keeping only the last 12 months of results in the recent-results section, since the edit timestamps fall about a year after those matches. The scout's 4,767 churn figure is just the same block counted three times, and no new facts were added. There was one revert and one re-removal, so this is not yet an edit war, but it could become one if TonySt reverts again. I didn't read the first removal (rev 1381261390), but its size matches the other two.

briefs.headline: Spanish Armada article hit by two schoolyard-style vandal edits, both reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. About 22 minutes apart, two different temporary accounts each replaced the lead paragraph of en-wiki's Spanish Armada article with nonsense. The first claimed the Armada "never happened" and talked about Alvin and the Chipmunks and Eric Cartman. The second was "RICARDO KILLLED HGENRY TYHE 8". Editor RFNirmala reverted the first within about 4 minutes, and ClueBot NG reverted the second within 10 seconds. The large churn the scout flagged is just these blankings and their reverts adding up. There's no real dispute and no sign of other language versions being touched. The pattern looks like classroom vandalism, possibly students working on a history lesson, but that's a guess. Worth a semi-protection watch, not a story.

briefs.headline: Wikipedia editors list Brock Purdy ahead of Lamar Jackson as NFL career passer rating leader
briefs.summary: This is not an edit war. The flurry on the Lamar Jackson article was a short, one-sided disagreement that settled itself, apparently prompted by a stats update. Tb101202 removed Jackson's "Career passer rating (minimum 1,500 attempts): 102.7" record line. GOAT Bones231012 restored it, calling it an unexplained removal, then undid their own restore within about two minutes. They then changed the lead from saying Jackson "ranks first" on the all-time regular-season career passer rating list to "ranks second." In the same few minutes, Tb101202 edited "List of NFL career passer rating leaders": they changed a rating from 105.4 to 105.6 and replaced the lead image and caption to say Brock Purdy "is the all-time leader in career passer rating for the regular season." This most likely means Purdy recently passed Jackson, perhaps after a game or after reaching the minimum number of attempts. But no edit cites a source or a specific game, only two editors were involved, and no other languages have moved, so the trigger is unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: ISL 2026–27 page updated after Match 10: East Bengal win 4–0 at Churchill Brothers
briefs.summary: Three registered editors made 8 small, non-reverted edits to the English 2026–27 Indian Super League page within about 12 minutes, updating it after Match 10. The infobox diff shows the matches count going from 9 to 10, total goals from 23 to 27, and a new biggest away win: Churchill Brothers 0–4 East Bengal (18 October 2026). Bipin Singh (East Bengal) joins Borja Martínez and Messi Bouli as joint top scorer on 2 goals, and the top-scorers table was changed to match. Other edits update the form and match-by-match tables, top assists, and make a cosmetic link change. This is normal result-tracking, not a dispute or vandalism. The match result and scorer come only from the diffs and were not checked against outside sources.

briefs.headline: ISL 2026–27 page updated after Match 10; East Bengal win 4–0 at Churchill Brothers
briefs.summary: This is the same set of 8 edits the prior brief covered, on the English 2026–27 Indian Super League page. Three registered editors (Sherifkk, Iampavan19, HelloWorld8800) made them in about 12 minutes, and none were reverted. No edits have come in since the last one at ts 1792331389. The infobox diff shows matches going from 9 to 10 and total goals from 23 to 27. It also adds a new biggest away win, Churchill Brothers 0–4 East Bengal (18 October 2026), and names Bipin Singh as joint top scorer on 2 goals. The latest edit only shortens a link label to "Mohun Bagan SG". This is ordinary result-tracking with no dispute or vandalism. The score and scorer come only from the diffs and were not checked against outside sources.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: temp account renames birthplace Poyo→Poio, likely good faith
briefs.summary: There has been one new edit to Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography since the last brief, and I read it. Temporary account ~2026-55802-76 changed the infobox birthplace from [[Poyo]] to [[Poio]], with the summary "correct name of city of birth" (rev 175887487). Poio is the official Galician name of the town, so this looks like a good-faith naming fix rather than trolling. It contains no insults or "Quintana" jokes. The edit also pulled several infobox fields onto the same lines as wikitext comments, and moved the club list onto the "equipos =" line. That is the same formatting side-effect as the earlier unsourced shirt-number edit (rev 175886406), so it may be an editor-tool artefact; it probably doesn't break how the page displays, but I haven't confirmed that. I agree with the scout that this isn't a new event. I disagree with "no reverts": Saloca's rev 175887360 just before this was a rollback, even though the graph doesn't mark it as one. As noted in earlier briefs, the infobox name "Rodríguez Parera" and the unsourced shirt-number change 32→20 may still be live; I haven't checked the current page. This is still small-scale activity on one page in one language, and the vandalism spree seems to be dying down into cleanup.

briefs.headline: Fan-rivalry vandalism hits es-wiki bio of Celta defender Javi Rodríguez
briefs.summary: In about four minutes, six temporary accounts (~2026-… IDs that are not otherwise anonymous) made six edits to the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Celta de Vigo defender Javier Rodríguez Galiano. Every diff I read is vandalism or junk swapped for other junk. One edit replaced "un tío tranquilo y educado" with the anti-Celta taunt "celtarra a segunda, forza Depor" (rev 175886045). Another removed that line but used the edit summary "volveréis a segunda turcos" (175886082). Other edits added "aupa atleti ostias" (175886100), replaced it with "miguel quintana el guapo" (175886109), and inserted crude remarks about the player's girlfriends and anatomy (175886113, 175886117), all under misleading summaries like "He añadido información". None of the edits adds factual content. The relegation taunts and the Deportivo and Atlético chants point to football-fan trolling, possibly set off by a recent Celta match, but nothing in the edits confirms any real-world event. The page still seems to hold vandalized text, which needs a rollback.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio cleaned up after fan-vandalism spree; no news found
briefs.summary: This is the same vandalism spree on Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography, and it is now over. The first brief covered the opening six edits. After that, more temporary accounts added junk: "Tiene un aura criminal" under external links (rev 175886142), longer crude insults about "miguel quintana" (175886122), and a "7 novias" line, which a later edit removed (175886127). One temporary account removed the insult line, but its edit also deleted the Transfermarkt citation (175886146). Patroller Geom undid a couple of edits one at a time, then used TwinkleGlobal to restore the page to revision 173795883 by Jekiwc (175886183). That restore removed all the vandal text and the joke infobox fields (apodo "Chino", color "blanquito", a fake 1.89 m height). The graph shows no reverts, but that is wrong: Geom's three edits are reverts. In total, nine temporary accounts made 10 junk edits over about 7 minutes, the spree stayed on one page, and no other language edition was touched. None of it adds facts, so I don't think there is a real-world event. A recent match may have set off the fan trolling, but nothing confirms that. Watch for more vandalism and possible page protection.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio hit again after cleanup; patroller reverts within 2 min
briefs.summary: This update adds a short coda to the vandalism on Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography. About 10 minutes after Geom restored the clean revision, a new temporary account (~2026-55716-17) edited the lead to say he "es un tio tranquilo y amable" (rev 175886310). That is the same joke as the spree's first edit, which replaced "un tío tranquilo y educado". Geom rolled it back about two minutes later (rev 175886333), and I read both diffs. The graph does not mark Geom's rollback as a revert, but it is one. Across the whole spree, 10 temporary accounts made 11 junk edits on one page in one language. No edit adds facts, so I still see no sign of a real-world event behind the fan trolling. A new account returning to the same joke suggests the vandalism may continue in short bursts until the page is protected.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: new temp account changes shirt number 32→20, no source
briefs.summary: One new edit since the last brief on Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography. About 4.5 minutes after Geom's rollback, temporary account ~2026-55861-29 changed the infobox squad number from "dorsal = 32" to "dorsal = 20" (rev 175886406, which I read). The edit also moved a few infobox fields onto the same lines as wikitext comments, which shouldn't change how the page displays. Unlike the earlier edits in the spree, this one adds no insults or chants. It could be a real squad-number change, or it could be a quiet piece of vandalism. It cites no source, the summary is blank ("/* */"), and it comes from a new temp account in the middle of an active trolling spree, so I'm not treating it as fact. Nobody has reverted it yet, and the graph shows no later edits. Overall the story is still small-scale fan vandalism on one page in one language, with no confirmed real-world event. A shirt-number change would be easy to check against the club's official squad list.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: new 'Quintana' vandalism wave, still not reverted
briefs.summary: Three more temporary accounts made three edits to Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography over about 7 minutes. None of them touches the shirt number. The scout note's "shirt-number dispute" framing is wrong: the only number change is still the unsourced 32→20 edit covered in the last brief (rev 175886406), and nobody has changed it since. Instead, the new edits continue the "Miguel Quintana" joke from earlier in the spree, which I read in all three diffs. One appended "y Miguel Quintana es soldado de el" to the lead sentence (rev 175886711). The next changed the infobox name to "Javier Rodríguez Parera" and added the nickname "El soldado de Quintana" (175886773). The last extended the lead text with "GRAN REAL CLUB CELTA DE VIGO" (175886832). The graph shows no reverts after these edits, so the page appears to still hold the vandal text and the unsourced number 20. Patroller Geom, who cleaned up the earlier waves, hasn't acted on these yet. This is still small-scale fan trolling on one page in one language, with no sign of a real-world event. Rotating temporary accounts keep coming back, so semi-protecting the page is the likely next step.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: vandal line toned down, stats updated, cleanup still pending
briefs.summary: There have been two edits to Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography since the last brief, and I read both. Neither is a proper cleanup. Temporary account ~2026-55809-50 replaced the lead's "y Miguel Quintana es soldado de el GRAN REAL CLUB CELTA DE VIGO" with "Y es un tio tranquilo y educado" (rev 175886916). That removes the insult but adds back a phrase that isn't in the clean version of the article. Registered editor Kirluu then changed the club-stats table's "updated to last match" date from 23 May 2026 to 18 Oct 2026 and edited the Celta row (rev 175887094). The diff looks like the appearances figure went from 88 to 95 and goals from 3 to 4, but the table markup is muddled, so those numbers are uncertain. Kirluu appears to be a routine stats updater: in the past hour the account edited about 14 footballer bios, mostly Bundesliga players. That means the update probably reflects a real recent Celta match, not vandalism. It also didn't revert anything. As far as the graph shows, the earlier junk is probably still live: the infobox name "Rodríguez Parera", the nickname "El soldado de Quintana" and the unsourced number change 32→20. I inferred this from the edit history and didn't check the current page. This is still small fan trolling on one page in one language. Geom or another patroller still needs to roll back to the clean revision, and semi-protection is likely.

briefs.headline: Celta defender's es-wiki bio: editors strip vandal lead and nickname, revert new jab
briefs.summary: Registered editor Kirluu has now cleaned up most of the vandalism on Javier Rodríguez Galiano's Spanish Wikipedia biography (rev 175887211). The edit removes the fake nickname "El soldado de Quintana", with the summary that no reliable source supports it, and deletes the leftover "Y es un tio tranquilo y educado" line from the lead. It also fixes the birthplace formatting (Poyo, Pontevedra, Galicia) and raises the infobox club goal total from 11 to 12, which fits Kirluu's earlier stats update. Two minutes later a new temporary account (~2026-55866-37) added "es un buen chaval" to the lead (rev 175887330). Registered editor Saloca reverted that within about 2 minutes, back to Kirluu's version (rev 175887360). The scout's "no reverts" note is wrong: Saloca's edit is a rollback, even though the graph doesn't mark it as one. I read all three diffs. They don't touch the infobox name "Rodríguez Parera" or the unsourced shirt-number change from 32 to 20, so both may still be live; I didn't check the current page. This is still small fan trolling on one page in one language with no sign of a real-world event, and temporary accounts keep coming back, so semi-protection is still possible.

briefs.headline: Edits say Tennessee Rep. Dennis Powers lost Aug. 6 GOP primary to Noah Smith (unsourced)
briefs.summary: The scout called the side pages in this cluster unrelated noise. One of them is actually the most newsworthy item here. Editor Easttnlover added a paragraph to Dennis Powers' article (rev 1381088112, comment "election results"). It says challenger Noah Smith beat Powers in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee House District 36, 8,034 votes (66.97%) to 3,963 (33.03%). That would end Powers' bid for a ninth term. Patroller F0malhaut42 reverted it for lacking a reliable source. Easttnlover then changed the infobox to show his term ending in November 2026, with Noah Smith as successor (rev 1381088402), and started a new "Noah Smith" article (3 edits, diff not readable). Everything comes from one low-edit account, with no citation and no other editors or languages backing it up, so I can't confirm it. That said, the vote totals are specific and add up, and the timing fits a primary night. The School District 43 Coquitlam edits are routine principal updates, as the earlier brief said. The LTE Advanced edits were a test edit (an email address added) that was reverted.

briefs.headline: Routine staff-table update on School District 43 Coquitlam article
briefs.summary: A new account (Ttowner8975, its only edit) changed the administrator names for Maple Creek in the schools table, replacing "Darren Macmillan" and "Ian Robertson" with "Sean Della Vedova" and "Jessica Eng" (rev 1381087688). Patroller F0malhaut42 reverted the change because it had no source. Within minutes, established editor Meters put back a version of the update, setting the principal to "Shawn O'Brien" based on the school's home page (rev 1381088194). Meters then refreshed the district citation with a 2026 access date (rev 1381088666). This looks like ordinary upkeep, probably a staff change at one school. It isn't a news event or an edit war. Only three editors touched the page and it exists only on English Wikipedia. I didn't read the revert diff, and I couldn't check the exact names or roles against the school's site.

briefs.headline: Malay actress Ruhainies' Wikipedia page hit by derogatory edits and gossip timeline
briefs.summary: Within about 6 minutes, three temporary accounts, each with only this one edit, vandalised the Malay Wikipedia biography of actress Ruhainies. None of the edits had been reverted when I checked. Rev 6987545 changed her name field to 'Rusak Rumah Tangga Org' ('wrecker of people's marriages') and added mocking notes to her occupations ('bland', 'barely a model'). Rev 6987549 added 'repeat sem' to her UiTM alma mater. The large edit, rev 6987548 (+3443), pasted in an unsourced year-by-year gossip timeline of Bella Astillah and Aliff Aziz's marriage, ending with the March 2024 khalwat (close-proximity) arrest of Aliff Aziz and Ruhainies and the couple's June 2024 divorce. That timeline describes 2024 events, not new ones, and there is no sign of a fresh real-world development. Still, the burst of hostile edits suggests public attention on the scandal has flared up again. This is a living-person page, so the anti-vandalism patrol should look at it. I can't tell whether the three accounts are one person or several.

briefs.headline: No new activity on Ruhainies page; the 3,540 "churn" is the same three vandal edits
briefs.summary: This is a re-flag, not new activity. The page has no edits since the prior brief. The graph shows only three edits on ms:Ruhainies: 6987545, 6987548 and 6987549, made by three single-edit temporary accounts in about 6 minutes. Their sizes (+62, +3443, +35) add up to the 3,540 churn the scout flagged. I re-read two of those diffs. Rev 6987545 changes her name to "Rusak Rumah Tangga Org" ("wrecker of people's marriages") and adds mocking notes to her occupations. Rev 6987548 pastes in an unsourced gossip timeline of the Bella Astillah and Aliff Aziz marriage, which ends with the March 2024 khalwat (close-proximity) arrest and the June 2024 divorce, so no new real-world event. None of the edits have been reverted, and no linked pages in other languages exist or moved. The earlier finding stands: targeted vandalism of a living person's biography that is still live. It needs patroller attention, but it isn't news.

briefs.headline: No new activity on Greek 'Hare' article; name-insertion vandalism still reverted
briefs.summary: This is an update on the earlier brief, and nothing has changed. The last edit to the Greek Wikipedia article Λαγός (hare) is still Fotis A.'s DEFAULTSORT edit (rev 11887251). No temporary account has edited the page since. I re-read two diffs. In rev 11887239, a temporary account added "Αγρια:Βασιλης / Επιθετικα:Σταυρος / Ηρεμα:Σωτηρης" ("wild: Vasilis / aggressive: Stavros / calm: Sotiris"). In rev 11887250, Fotis A. removed the names and labels that were still on the page. The graph shows the three temporary accounts edited only this page. Fotis A. was working through Greek film articles before and after, so the cleanup looks like routine patrolling, not a targeted dispute. There is no sign of a real-world trigger and no edit war. One small loose end: the editor totals for two temporary accounts (4 and 3 edits) are higher than the edits the graph shows. That may be a counting quirk, but it means some of their edits may be missing from the graph.

briefs.headline: Greek 'Hare' article hit by name-insertion vandalism, cleaned up by patroller
briefs.summary: Three temporary accounts made four edits to the Greek Wikipedia article Λαγός (hare). They added personal names (Γιωργος Ψαρας, Σταυρος Γεωργιου, Φωτης Χρυσανθου, Σωτήρης Κραμβης) to the species ("Είδη") section, along with labels like "Αγρια:Βασιλης" ("wild: Vasilis"), "Επιθετικα:Σταυρος" ("aggressive: Stavros") and "Ηρεμα:Σωτηρης" ("calm: Sotiris"). This looks like schoolyard joking, with classmates calling each other kinds of hare. Experienced editor Fotis A. (380 edits) then removed all of the remaining inserted text (rev 11887250, −164 bytes) and added a DEFAULTSORT key. The graph didn't flag that removal as a revert, but it was effectively one. This is not ordinary collaborative editing as the scout thought, and there is no real-world news trigger. It is low-level vandalism that has already been fixed. Confidence is high based on the diffs I read. The three temporary accounts may belong to the same small group, but I can't confirm that.

briefs.headline: Rivonia Trial article hit by apparent classroom vandalism, reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: This is a short burst of vandalism on the English article about the Rivonia Trial, not a news event. One temporary account (rev 1381291938) replaced the trial's location with joke text: the trial supposedly took place in "Miss Zhome's class room", lasted three and a half years and was linked to homosexuality "in the United States". About four minutes later a second temporary account (rev 1381292185) fixed the spelling of that joke text and also added Donald Trump, Joe Biden, Joseph Stalin and "Doctor Disrepsepct" to the list of people convicted. Within a minute, Lynch44 (rev 1381292210) restored the last good version by PhotographyEdits, which removed both edits. The edits aren't flagged as reverts and the scout's "routine" reading missed the vandalism, but the diffs make it clear. The mention of a teacher and the two temporary accounts acting in quick succession suggest students in a class, though that's a guess. No other language versions or related pages moved, and nothing points to a real-world trigger.

briefs.headline: Rivonia Trial vandalism reverted; no new edits since cleanup
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up on a vandalism burst already tracked on the English "Rivonia Trial" article. There is no news event. Re-reading the diffs confirms the earlier brief. In rev 1381291938, a temporary account replaced the trial's location (Pretoria's Palace of Justice and the Old Synagogue) with a joke: "Miss Zhomes class room", a trial lasting 3.5 years, and a line about homosexuality "in the United States". Four minutes later, in rev 1381292185, a second temporary account fixed the joke's spelling and added Donald Trump, Joe Biden, Joseph Stalin and "Doctor Disrepsepct" to the list of men convicted. In rev 1381292210, 21 seconds after that, Lynch44 restored PhotographyEdits' last good version, which removed both edits. The graph shows no edits to the page after the restore, no other language versions moved, and no related pages were involved. The mention of a teacher points to students, but that is a guess.

briefs.headline: Knecht page protected after Lakers release; latest edits are only formatting
briefs.summary: This is the same story as the tracked Lakers–Dalton Knecht waiver, with no new development. Since the last brief, which covered the New York Post citation added in rev 1381074631, only two edits have landed, not three. Vic Hawk changed how the infobox writes his Lakers years, from {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2026|start}} to {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} (rev 1381076221). That fixes the season notation and does not change the facts. Ymblanter then added a {{pp-protected}} tag (rev 1381076601). The tag suggests an administrator has protected the page, likely because several temporary accounts were editing it during the news spike, but I did not check the protection log. Nothing has been reverted since Bagumba's first revert, and the sourced waiver line still stands. The graph still shows no activity on the Lakers team or season pages or in other languages.

briefs.headline: Knecht page settles on 'free agent' after Lakers release; still no source cited
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Dalton Knecht, the Lakers' 17th pick in 2024, now lists him as a free agent. Editors are not fighting over this. After Bagumba reverted NullyD's line "On Monday October 19th, 2026 Knecht was waived by the Lakers" as unsourced (rev 1381072957, diff read), Char3290 changed the infobox team to "Free agent", ended his Lakers years at 2026 and changed the lead to "most recently played for" the Lakers (rev 1381073147). Char3290 later removed his jersey number, 4 (rev 1381073390). The other edits are cleanup. One temporary account inserted "is a FORMER American professional" (rev 1381073253), which looks like a joke or a misunderstanding, since he would be a free agent, not retired. A second account removed it (rev 1381073426) and a third fixed the grammar (rev 1381073887). No one has undone the free-agent version, including Bagumba, who reverted the first claim. Correcting the scout's note: nothing in the edits mentions a waiver claim by another team, and the activity is cleanup, not a dispute. The release itself is still unconfirmed. No edit cites a source, and the graph shows no edits to the Lakers page, a Lakers season page or any other-language article. The date, October 19, fits the NBA's pre-season deadline for cutting rosters, so the claim is plausible.

briefs.headline: Editors say Lakers waived Dalton Knecht; first claim reverted as unsourced
briefs.summary: Two separate editors updated the English Wikipedia article on Lakers guard Dalton Knecht (the 17th pick in 2024) to say he is no longer with the team. NullyD wrote "On Monday October 19th, 2026 Knecht was waived by the Lakers" and called him "formerly of" the Lakers. Bagumba, an experienced editor, reverted that edit as unsourced (rev 1381072957; I read only its edit summary, not the diff). About two minutes later Char3290 changed the infobox team to "Free agent", ended his Lakers years at 2026, and rewrote the lead to say he "most recently played for" the Lakers. That edit was still standing when I looked, and it also cites no source. The edit timestamps fall on October 19, 2026, which fits the pre-season deadline when NBA teams cut their rosters, so a waiver is plausible. Still, neither edit cites a source, there is no activity on the Lakers page or on other-language versions of the article, and one of the two claims has already been reverted. Treat this as unconfirmed until a reference is added or the Lakers or league pages pick it up.

briefs.headline: Lakers waive Dalton Knecht; Wikipedia now cites New York Post report
briefs.summary: The Dalton Knecht article now cites a source for his release by the Lakers. Dark Dreaming, the page's most active editor (10 edits), added this to the Lakers section: "On October 19, 2026, Knecht was waived by the Lakers." The citation is a New York Post article by Khobi Price dated October 19, 2026, headlined "Lakers cut Dalton Knecht, become compliant with roster rules" (rev 1381074631). That fills the gap behind Bagumba's earlier revert, which removed the same claim because it had no source. Char3290's earlier infobox change to "Free agent" with Lakers years ending in 2026 is still in place (rev 1381073147). It also left a typo in the lead, "player for who most recently played for." The page activity is now consistent: one article, seven editors, no reverts since the first one. The NYP headline ties the cut to the Lakers needing to meet roster limits before the season. I have not opened the NYP article itself. The graph still shows no edits to Lakers team or season pages, or to other-language articles. This is the same story as before, now sourced. It is not a separate event.

briefs.headline: K-pop singer Ejae reported married to Sam Kim in Seoul; Wikipedia adds Vogue source
briefs.summary: Two editors updated the English Wikipedia article on singer-songwriter Ejae (KPop Demon Hunters) to say she has married her fiancé, former music producer Sam Kim. First, a temporary account (~2026-56339-92) rewrote the Personal life section to say they married on October 17, 2026 at her grandfather's estate in Seoul. In doing so it removed a February 2026 Chosun Daily citation that had described a planned November 7 wedding in Los Angeles. The same account added no new source and changed the infobox from "partner" to "spouse". About 15 minutes later, registered editor Jamie Eilat cleaned up the infobox ({{marriage|Sam Kim|2026}}) and added a citation to a Vogue piece dated October 19, 2026, titled "Inside Ejae and Samuel Kim's Garden Wedding at Her Grandfather's Former Home in Seoul". The article now says simply "They married in October 2026." Uncertain: I have not checked the Vogue article myself, and the exact date (Oct 17) currently comes only from the unsourced edit. There are no reverts and nothing suggesting vandalism. This is celebrity personal news, so it is a low-stakes routine update.

briefs.headline: Vandalism spree on ko-wiki: artist page blanked, '케이팝모터스' page spammed
briefs.summary: The scout's guess of "routine expansion" doesn't hold up. The edit metadata shows coordinated vandalism, not content work. On 정은혜 (미술가), the user '아정당' made five removals in a row ending in "문서를 비움" (page blanked). After a +3665 restore by a temporary account, '에스아이네트 본사' removed text four more times. The page 케이팝모터스 has been created over and over with the text "반달" (Korean slang for vandal) repeated. It was also briefly made a redirect to 찰스 폰지 (Charles Ponzi). Several accounts are involved: '아정당' and '아정당모바일' (names that look like an impersonation pair), '에스아이네트 본사', and three temporary accounts. The same accounts also hit unrelated pages: 주체사상탑 (the Juche Tower), 전남광주통합특별시체육회 and 두일신풍연립. That pattern points to a vandal or sockpuppet campaign, not a real-world event. Two caveats: none of the revision diffs could be fetched (they may have been deleted by admins), so this rests on edit summaries, size changes and editor patterns. No language versions in other wikis moved.

briefs.headline: Troy Denning forum-feud vandalism with slurs reverted again; page clean for now
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The en.wiki biography of Star Wars novelist Troy Denning was hit twice by temporary accounts. Each one added an unsourced "2024 SI Controversy" section about a faked forum screenshot (UnuThul vs. Caedus). The section also named forum users and piped their names to slur articles (Faggot, Nigger, Retard (pejorative), Autism). BOZ removed the first insertion by hand as "obvious vandalism" (rev 1381116548). A second temporary account put it back (rev 1381116867). Admin PhilKnight then rolled that back (rev 1381118406, -1078); I read the diff and it removes the whole slur-laden section. The graph shows no edits after the rollback, so the page should be clean. The only remaining question is whether the same people come back, which could lead to page protection or revision deletion. The scout's note is correct: there are 2 vandal accounts and 2 reverts, all on one page in one language, and it continues the story already being tracked.

briefs.headline: Troy Denning page hit by forum-feud vandalism with slurs; reverted once, then re-added
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not a real-world event. Two temporary accounts each made one edit to the en.wiki biography of Star Wars novelist Troy Denning, adding unsourced fan-forum drama. The edits describe a 2024 "Suspect Insight" debate-forum "controversy" over a faked screenshot about UnuThul vs. Caedus, plus a claim that Denning runs Discord accounts that "debunk pro-Caedus arguments". The second insertion (rev 1381116867) also names forum users and links them to slur articles (e.g. the Faggot, Nigger and Retard (pejorative) articles). Long-time editor BOZ removed the first insertion by hand as "obvious vandalism" (rev 1381116548). The graph didn't flag that as a revert, which is why the scout saw "no reverts". About three minutes later a second temporary account re-added the section. The last edit in the graph is that re-insertion, so the offensive text may still be live. No other languages or pages are involved, and the scout's "routine bibliography update" reading is wrong. The likely next step is another revert, plus possible page protection or revision deletion.

briefs.headline: Timelash page re-protected after vandal account returns when protection lapses
briefs.summary: This is not a real-world news event or a content dispute. It is a short vandalism incident on the English Wikipedia article for the 1985 Doctor Who serial Timelash. A brand-new account, 'TheProtectionlashHasExpired', made its only edit (+169 bytes) right after the page's protection ran out. Its edit summary pinged several administrators (Yamla, Ponyo, Zzuuzz, Pppery, HJ Mitchell and others) to taunt them that "the protection has now expired", which is how a returning long-term abuser behaves. SuperPianoMan9167 reverted it within 7 seconds. About six minutes later Dualcerb added the {{pp-extended}} tag, which shows the page is under extended-confirmed protection again. I couldn't read the vandal's edit: Wikipedia returns no content for it, which suggests administrators have hidden it. So I can't say what was added. The incident is over unless the same pattern shows up on other pages.

briefs.headline: Timelash: vandal returns as protection lapses, reverted in seconds and page re-protected
briefs.summary: This is vandalism on the English Wikipedia article for the 1985 Doctor Who serial Timelash, not a news event. A new account, 'TheProtectionlashHasExpired', made one edit (+169 bytes) whose edit summary pinged admins (Yamla, Ponyo, Zzuuzz, Pppery, Staraction, HJ Mitchell) to say "the protection has now expired". That fits a returning long-term abuser. SuperPianoMan9167 reverted it 7 seconds later. About six minutes after that, Dualcerb added {{pp-extended|small=yes}}, which I confirmed in the diff and which signals extended-confirmed protection is back on. I couldn't read the vandal's revision or the revert diff because Wikipedia returns no content for them, which suggests admins hid (revision-deleted) the vandal's text, so I don't know what it added. A graph search found no other edits in this window with the same taunting summary, so it hasn't spread so far. This matches the prior brief, and nothing new has happened.

briefs.headline: Willards, Maryland: unsourced musician claim re-added once, reverted; page now quiet
briefs.summary: This is minor vandalism with no real-world event behind it. Temporary account ~2026-56394-08 restored the line that ~2026-56393-78 had added to the lead, which I confirmed by reading that diff. The line says Willards is "home of the famous guitarist and lead singer of 7 Spirits Rd, Fender Kottemann, who also created Neon", and it has no source. DonnieNova had reverted the first insertion. Komethere reverted the restore with VandalHandle, citing "unsourced". The page has had no edits since Komethere's revert, it is back to its stable census-based lead, and only this one English-language page is involved. The two temporary accounts have consecutive numbers and each made a single edit, so they are probably the same person. That is an inference I haven't confirmed.

briefs.headline: Willards, Maryland: unsourced 'famous local musician' claim added twice, reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is small-scale vandalism, not a news event or a real content dispute. A temporary account (~2026-56393-78) added a phrase to the lead of the Willards, Maryland article calling the town "home of the famous guitarist and lead singer of 7 Spirits Rd, Fender Kottemann, who also created Neon". The phrase had no source. Patroller DonnieNova reverted it. A second temporary account (~2026-56394-08), whose name is numbered right after the first, which suggests the same person, undid that revert. Komethere then reverted again, using VandalHandle and citing "unsourced". The "444 churn" the scout flagged is just the same 111-byte sentence going in and out four times, and the page is now back to its stable version. Each temporary account made one edit and touched no other pages, and no other language editions moved. I read the original insertion and the final revert. I didn't open the restore edit; its edit summary and its 111-byte size match the same text.

briefs.headline: New dewiki stub on 18th-century Hanoverian general Pufendorf; routine maintenance follows
briefs.summary: This is a brand-new German Wikipedia article, not a rewrite. User A1000 created "Georg Siegmund von Pufendorf" in one edit of +2,844 bytes (flagged new_page). The edit summary describes him as a Brunswick-Lüneburg major general (1715–1799). Over the next three minutes, five small edits followed (4 to 52 bytes): Scholless filled in missing details and fixed spacing in the literature section, experienced maintainer M2k~dewiki made a small fix and added authority-control data (Normdaten), and A1000 added a category. The live page intro says he was a major general, finally inspector of all the territorial regiments (Landregimenter), and was made a noble of the Holy Roman Empire with his brothers in 1756. There are no reverts, no other languages and no link to any current event, so this is normal article creation plus new-page cleanup. I couldn't read either diff I tried (the diff service returned an error), so this rests on edit metadata, edit summaries and the live page intro, not on the diff text.

briefs.headline: New dewiki article on 18th-century Hanoverian general Pufendorf; author copyedits
briefs.summary: This update adds one edit to the story: A1000, who created the German article "Georg Siegmund von Pufendorf", removed 13 bytes with no edit summary. The diff shows a grammar fix only: a duplicated "das Regiment" was dropped from the sentence about him handing the Wendish territorial regiment to Johann Friedrich von Quernheim in 1788. The creation diff (+2,844), which I could read this time, confirms the article's content. Pufendorf was a Brunswick-Lüneburg major general, born in Minden in 1715 and died in Döhren in 1799. He rose from ensign (1738) to inspector of all the territorial regiments (Landregimenter) in 1788 and was made a noble of the Holy Roman Empire with his brothers in 1756. The article cites Poten's 1902 list of Hanoverian generals and a 1796 state calendar. One small error: the creation edit put him in the death-year category "Gestorben 1759" while the text gives 1799. I haven't confirmed whether a later small fix (for example M2k~dewiki's "k" edit) corrected it. There are still only three editors, all logged in, no reverts and no other languages, and nothing links the article to any current event. This is routine article creation and cleanup.

briefs.headline: France imposes local curfews incl. Paris after weekend riots, per English Wikipedia edits
briefs.summary: The English article "2026 French student protests" was created about 32 hours ago. It already has 42 edits from 13 named editors, which is more activity than the scout's 3-edit window showed. The most important recent edit (rev 1381068920) added that curfews were imposed in several cities, including Paris, and that PM Sébastien Lecornu called them "partial" and "very locally limited". It cites a Yahoo News piece dated 19 Oct. The surrounding text, credited to the BBC and the Interior Ministry, says about 2,400 people were arrested and about 1,000 police were injured (seven seriously) during Saturday's demonstrations. It says about 550,000 people took part and that looting continued on a smaller scale in Paris and Lyon on Sunday. The one revert was a single wording dispute: one editor removed "mostly peaceful" (rev 1381077449) and another put it back (rev 1381078771). That is one back-and-forth, not an edit war, and the other recent edits are cleanup. Caveats: these figures come from what the article says its sources report, and I have not checked them independently. The page also has no other-language versions linked in the graph, which is surprising for an event this size in France and worth checking for a missing French article.

briefs.headline: Gwamba (Malawian rapper) article hit by self-promotional hijack; reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: The en-wiki page "Gwamba" is about Malawian rapper Duncan Zgambo. It is not an ethnic-group article, so the candidate headline is wrong. A new account, "Yahaya Usman Gwamba", made two edits replacing the subject's identity with his own. The first edit changed the infobox to give his birth name, a birth date of 27/7/2000, Argungu as birthplace, Kebbi State University as education, and "Billionaire Farmer" as occupation. The second changed the lead to name "YahayaUsmanGwamba" and removed "Malawi". F0malhaut42 reverted the first edit as self-promotion, and Itsjuenyin reverted the second with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, all within about two minutes. The edit counts are 2 by the hijacker and 2 reverts, even though the dossier marks no reverts. It looks like an isolated case of someone inserting themselves into an article that shares their surname, with no real-world event behind it.

briefs.headline: Gwamba rapper page: one-off self-insertion vandalism, already reverted; no new activity
briefs.summary: This story covers the same four en-wiki edits as the existing vandalism brief on "Gwamba", the page about Malawian rapper Duncan Zgambo. There has been no new activity since then. In rev 1381142938, the account "Yahaya Usman Gwamba" replaced the infobox details with his own: born 27/7/2000 in Argungu, studied at Kebbi State University, occupation "Billionaire Farmer". In rev 1381143102 the same account renamed the lead subject "YahayaUsmanGwamba" and deleted "Malawi". F0malhaut42 and Itsjuenyin (using the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool) reverted both edits within about two minutes. The graph doesn't flag these as reverts, but the edit comments show they were. No other pages, languages or editors are involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. I agree with the scout: this is minor, already-resolved churn and should be folded into the existing story rather than opened as a new one.

briefs.headline: Routine itwiki edits: Aeneid image swaps and a page move for astronomer Cassini IV
briefs.summary: Two unrelated Italian Wikipedia articles are getting ordinary maintenance edits, and nothing points to a real-world event. On 'Eneide', temporary account ~2026-52083-13 keeps rearranging and replacing illustrations (Ferdinand Bol, Pinelli and Carracci captions). M7 undid one round of these changes with a single revert. The editor then made the swaps again, and they are cosmetic, not vandalism. On 'Jean-Dominique Cassini (astronomo 1748)', Gambo7 finished a naming-convention move: the edit removed the {{Sposta}} move tag and stub tags, and the move comment points to a redirect from 'Jean-Dominique Cassini (1748-1845)'. One temporary account (~2026-56296-04) touched both pages, but only with 1-character whitespace fixes, so the overlap looks like chance. A small correction to the scout's note: there was one revert on Eneide, but it isn't an edit war.

briefs.headline: Theranos article gets routine short-description and template tidy-ups; no news signal
briefs.summary: Three registered editors made five small edits (deltas from -9 to +13) to the English Wikipedia Theranos article over about 90 minutes. No other language editions moved and nothing was flagged as a revert. GhostInTheMachine added the company's active years to the short description ("American health-technology company, 2003–2018"). Yedaman54 then changed it to "Defunct American health-technology company (2003–2018)" and re-dated the Use mdy dates and Use American English templates. GhostInTheMachine's next edit (-9, comment cites WP:SDDATES, diff not read) most likely returned it to the guideline's comma format. That is a small style disagreement, not an edit war. Hsw542 made a one-character grammar fix in the 2015–16 regulatory section without changing any substance. None of the edits adds new facts, sources, or current events, so this looks like ordinary maintenance. One caveat: I didn't read the -9 diff, so the exact wording that ended up on the page isn't confirmed.

briefs.headline: Former Swedish ambassador Sven Hirdman dead at 87, Swedish Wikipedia says
briefs.summary: The Swedish Wikipedia article on diplomat Sven Hirdman already says he died on 9 October 2026 in Stockholm. That claim cites a death notice in Dagens Nyheter and an SVT report headlined "Diplomaten Sven Hirdman är död" ("Diplomat Sven Hirdman has died"), dated 2026-10-18. Hirdman was a former ambassador and state secretary. The 2024 photo caption in the article shows him at a protest against the DCA agreement, which is presumably the Russia link the scout mentioned. The three edits in this window are follow-up cleanup, not the first report of the death. Belairroad2 added wikilinks (Sergels torg, Norge), Tekannan fixed a typo ("Stockolm" to "Stockholm") in the place-of-death field, and Disembodied Soul added the {{nyligen avliden}} ("recently deceased") template. There are no reverts and nothing suggests vandalism or a dispute. No other-language versions of the page are linked in the graph, so I couldn't check whether other wikis are reflecting the death. I didn't see the edit that first added the death, but it has two mainstream Swedish sources, so the death looks real. Coverage is low-intensity.

briefs.headline: German Wikipedia lists Russian boxer Denis Boytsov as dead in 2026; exact date unsourced
briefs.summary: The German Wikipedia article on Russian heavyweight boxer Denis Nikolajewitsch Boizow (Boytsov, Q327073) got three small edits. A temporary account changed the infobox death date from just "2026" to "17.10.2026" (rev 271435294). About two minutes later, Irraza1910 reverted it because the death date had no source (rev 271435362). Separately, ChickSR added the category "Sowjetbürger" (Soviet citizens), which is routine maintenance (rev 271435242). The year 2026 was already in the infobox before these edits, so his death had been recorded on the page earlier. That means the only new claim is the exact date, and it is unsourced. The graph has no other language versions, no other editors, and nothing else showing activity, so I can't confirm either the death or the date from here.

briefs.headline: Russian boxer Denis Boytsov dead; ruwiki cites Championat for 17 Oct 2026 date
briefs.summary: This update corrects the earlier brief, which said there was no corroboration from other languages. The Russian Wikipedia article on heavyweight Denis Boytsov (Q327073) already lists his death date as 17.10.2026. A revision by Vitedg (rev 155682928) shows that date and a citation to a championat.com article. The cited headline reads "Умер «русский Тайсон». Не стало Дениса Бойцова" ("'The Russian Tyson' has died. Denis Boytsov is gone"). The URL mentions his beating in Germany, a head injury, an induced coma and his recovery. That edit itself is a small cleanup: it unlinks some dates, and in the visible part of the diff the reference is taken off the death-date line. I couldn't confirm whether the reference was moved elsewhere or removed. On German Wikipedia, a temporary account added the same exact date, 17.10.2026 (rev 271435294). Irraza1910 reverted it within two minutes because it had no source (rev 271435362), not because it was wrong. The year 2026 stays in the German article. The two language versions now agree on the death, and Russian Wikipedia has a named sports-media source for it. I haven't checked the source directly, and the Russian page shows just this one edit, so there's no sign of a wave of editing.

briefs.headline: Nancy Ajram page: more infobox vandalism, reverted; still no news event
briefs.summary: Since the last brief there has been one more round on en-wiki's Nancy Ajram page. Temporary account ~2026-55806-20 replaced the infobox name and native name with "RANI yehya" (apparently a private person), swapped the photo for "Pegions.jpg", cleared her birth name and changed her number of children from 3 to 7 (rev 1380894211). PixelsRCool reverted it about 30 seconds later (rev 1380894255). This matches the earlier pattern: a different temporary account had already swapped "singer" in the lead for an offensive word (rev 1380891564), and ClueBot NG, Paul Erik and Materialscientist undid each attempt within minutes. The Mahmoud Ouertani side has had nothing new since Materialscientist's reverts of the unsourced "grandfather" claim. Only one language is involved, every edit was quickly reverted, and no edit adds sourced facts, so this is drive-by vandalism, not a real-world event. If it keeps going, the page may need semi-protection, but that is upkeep, not news.

briefs.headline: Nancy Ajram page quiet after vandalism; only link cleanup since last brief
briefs.summary: There has been no new vandalism on en-wiki's Nancy Ajram page since the last brief. The only two edits since then are wikilink tidying by established editors. PixelsRCool removed a duplicate link to "World Music Awards" on the "WMA winner" phrase and cut some links further down the article (rev 1380894703). Calmira90 then changed a piped link to point straight to "World Music Award", citing WP:NOPIPEDLINK (rev 1380896292). Neither edit changes any facts or adds new events. The page's only revert is still PixelsRCool's undo of the "RANI yehya" infobox vandalism covered before, and nothing new has happened on the Mahmoud Ouertani page. This was vandalism that has since stopped, followed by routine upkeep; there is still no sign of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: No linked event: separate low-level vandalism on Nancy Ajram and Mahmoud Ouertani pages
briefs.summary: The only thing tying these two en-wiki pages together is the anti-vandalism patroller Materialscientist, who reverted edits on both. They share no other editors and no content, so there is no real-world event behind this. On Nancy Ajram, temporary accounts vandalised the lead and infobox: one changed "singer" to nonsense (rev 1380891926), and another put a private person's name and village into the name fields (rev 1380892884). ClueBot NG, Paul Erik and Materialscientist reverted each edit within seconds to minutes. On Mahmoud Ouertani, a temporary account and the registered account AdemKrztos each added the same unsourced sentence, that he is "the grandfather of Skander Ben Sabbeh" (revs 1380892075, 1380892451). Materialscientist reverted it three times as unsourced; the matching text suggests one person may be behind both accounts. The "large churn" in the scout's note is just this ±45-byte add-and-revert cycle, not news. I can't verify the family claim, but nothing suggests an event that would make it newsworthy.

briefs.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured in alleged deliberate vehicle attack
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Helen Haines, independent MP for Indi (Victoria), has a "2026 attack" section. Edits sourced to ABC News, BBC, news.com.au and The Guardian (dated 19–20 Oct 2026) say she was struck by a 4WD outside her Wangaratta electorate office, reportedly rammed twice. The section says she had emergency surgery and was in critical but stable condition at the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne. According to rev 1381145377, the suspect is a 43-year-old man from Tarrawingee who is known to police. It says a member of the public detained him at the scene, he was carrying a knife, and he will have a mental health assessment. The 13 recent edits I looked at are calm follow-up work, not an edit war: biography expansion sourced to ABC's profile of her, including her maiden name, marriage date, policy positions and marathon running. There are no reverts. The scout undercounted the activity: the page has had 46 edits from more than 15 editors in about 12 hours, which fits a story that broke on 19 Oct. I didn't read the earlier edits that created the attack section. Details like motive and her condition come from early live-blog reports and could change. No other-language versions of the page are linked in the graph.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack: suspect details grow from cited reports; rest of page is restructuring
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked story on the alleged vehicle attack on independent MP Helen Haines (Indi) outside her Wangaratta office. Since the last brief there are two new non-revert edits on English Wikipedia. Rev 1381148162 by Neegzistuoja ("More info on attacker") edits the "2026 attack" section. That section now says the 43-year-old suspect from Tarrawingee was driving a white Toyota Land Cruiser and had a knife. It also says neighbours had earlier reported him over mental health concerns and that he had a mental health assessment after his arrest. One cited ABC piece (20 Oct) is headlined as naming the arrested man as Brendan Nugent and saying his online history shows he once praised her. That reference was already in the text before this edit, and the name is not in the article body. The section still says she is in critical but stable condition at the Alfred Hospital. There is no sign of charges, a court date or a change in her condition. The diff tool cut off the added text, so I can't separate exactly what this edit added from what PliskorCor's earlier edit 1381145377 put in. Rev 1381148557 by TarnishedPath only reorganises the page (merges paragraphs, moves sections, adds subsections). Editing stays cooperative, with no edit war. The details come from early news and live-blog reports and could change.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines vehicle attack: no new facts; edits since last brief are biography polish
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked story on the alleged deliberate vehicle attack on independent MP Helen Haines (Indi) outside her Wangaratta office. It is not a new event. Since the prior brief there have been 5 small, non-revert edits on the English Wikipedia page from 3 editors: Laterthanyouthink, Yourlocallordandsavior and one temporary account. I read three of them. One adds that in 2021 she spoke at the 90th anniversary of ABC Goulburn Murray radio (rev 1381146677). The other two are copyedits: a missing word fixed in the 2019-election paragraph (1381146878) and a grammar fix in the lead (1381147652). None of the edits touches the "2026 attack" section. So there is no new information on her condition (last reported as critical but stable at the Alfred Hospital), the 43-year-old suspect, or charges. Editing is slowing down and stays cooperative, with no reverts or edit war. The attack details still rest on early news reports and could change.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack: no new facts since suspect was named and charged
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked story on the alleged vehicle attack on independent MP Helen Haines outside her Wangaratta office. It is not a new event. The scout counted "three editors with sizeable churn", but MrActiniuM's and Neegzistuoja's edits were already covered in the last brief: suspect Brendan Nugent named and charged with three offences, per a single ABC report from 20 Oct. Since then there have been only two small edits on English Wikipedia, with no reverts. Rev 1381156862 by Laterthanyouthink only adds a wikilink for Chiltern Bush Nursing Hospital in her nursing background. Rev 1381156083 by Schestos (+1 byte, no edit summary) is in the attack section's opening paragraph, but the diff tool cut off before the change. At one byte it is almost certainly a typo or formatting fix, though I couldn't confirm that. The paragraph still says she was struck twice on 19 Oct at 15:35 AEDT, that PM Albanese called it deliberate, and that the AFP, ASIO and the joint counter-terrorism team are investigating. Nothing new on her condition, which stays critical but stable at the Alfred, or on court dates. I tried rev 1381154815 again, and the text of the "Pauline" reaction is still cut off, so it remains unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack: no new facts; latest edits are housekeeping on her biography
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked story on the alleged vehicle attack on independent MP Helen Haines (Indi). Since the last brief there have been 5 more non-revert edits on English Wikipedia, mostly by TarnishedPath plus one wikilink fix by Laterthanyouthink. I read three. Rev 1381148760 splits her career into a "Second term (2022–2024)" section and a new "Third term (2025–present)" section tagged for expansion. Rev 1381148823 is a script-run date and style cleanup. Rev 1381149138 renames references. Judging by their edit summaries, the other two (unpiping links, adding a nursing wikilink) are also housekeeping. None of these edits adds anything about the attack, her condition (last reported as critical but stable at the Alfred Hospital), the 43-year-old suspect, or any charges. Editing is cooperative, with no edit war. Attention seems to have moved from breaking details to cleaning up the article.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack: suspect named as Brendan Nugent, charged with three offences
briefs.summary: I disagree with the scout's note. The edits since the last brief are not housekeeping: MrActiniuM made five edits to the "2026 attack" section and Neegzistuoja made one. Rev 1381155752 adds that on 20 October the suspect, Brendan Nugent, was charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury, and the Commonwealth offence of causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. The source is an ABC report dated 20 Oct. Revs 1381150845 and 1381151239 change the article from "a 43-year-old man" to "43-year-old Brendan Nugent from Tarrawingee". Neegzistuoja's follow-up (1381155364, "now we're apparently naming him") shows editors agreed to name him. Rev 1381151056 adds that she was struck "twice", and the text quoted in the diffs also notes that the AFP, ASIO and the counter-terrorism team are investigating. The Guardian and news.com.au are cited for links between Nugent's family and Haines. Rev 1381154815 adds a reaction from someone called "Pauline", probably Pauline Hanson, but the diff tool cut off before the added text, so I can't confirm what it says. No edit reports a change in her condition, which stays critical but stable at the Alfred Hospital. There are no reverts, and edits come only from English Wikipedia. Cooperative editing. The charges come from a single cited ABC piece and haven't yet been cross-checked against a court listing.

briefs.headline: New page on a non-notable individual tagged for speedy deletion; not news
briefs.summary: A single-sentence English Wikipedia article was created by a new account (ARGFNorway, 1 edit) describing a private individual, apparently a teenage Norwegian high-school student, with a self-supplied portrait. A temporary account added only the note "(This article is currently under work)". New-page patroller DonnieNova reverted that and tagged the page for speedy deletion under CSD A1 (no context) and A11 (obviously invented or non-notable). The "revert" is ordinary page patrolling, not a dispute: no back-and-forth, no other language versions, no other pages involved. Nothing here points to a real-world event. The subject appears to be a minor, so the brief leaves out identifying details.

briefs.headline: VisionQuest article: routine fixes to air dates and sourcing, no edit war
briefs.summary: Four editors made a small burst of edits to the English article on Marvel's Disney+ series VisionQuest (which premiered in October 2026), all on the same day. Kucingb1rah moved every episode release date one day later (Oct 13→14 through Nov 10→11), saying the change matched Disney+. Trailblazer101 undid both edits as "Inaccurate, see cited sources." The article cites a release schedule giving a Disney+ premiere of October 13, after a BFI London Film Festival screening on October 12. The originally announced date was October 14. The one-day gap is most likely a time-zone difference (a US-evening release falls on the next day in Asia) or the old announced date, not a real schedule change. Separately, Marco camino 10 removed a 787-byte addition by MillenniumGeneration because it relied on Murphy's Multiverse, which the reverting editor said is not a reliable source. I only saw a truncated part of that addition, so I can't say exactly what it claimed. There's no back-and-forth reverting, no anonymous accounts and nothing in other languages. This is ordinary upkeep of an article about a show that's airing, not news.

briefs.headline: Corneille fr.wiki page: minor test edits by temporary account, cleaned up and reverted
briefs.summary: Four edits in about 15 minutes on the French Wikipedia biography of Pierre Corneille. There is no sign of any real-world news. A temporary account (~2026-56250-63) made two edits. In rev 240541362 it added a useful wikilink to "avocat" and, judging by the next cleanup diff, also put a 👍🏻 emoji after a bibliography entry. Csar62 removed the emoji (rev 240541448). The same temporary account then put the emoji back and replaced the "avocat du roi" wikilink with a raw Google search URL (rev 240541562). R3L3ct3ur49 reverted that, per the edit comment. This is low-grade test or vandal editing, typical of a student on a school-curriculum author's page, with no other pages or languages involved. I didn't read the revert diff itself; the description of it comes from its edit comment.

briefs.headline: Rays–Brewers World Series pages fill in after ALCS clinch; editors fix early errors
briefs.summary: This update adds to the existing story (Rays beat Guardians 4–2 in the ALCS; World Series vs. Brewers). Editing has moved from logging the result to filling in background, and the edits I read agree with the earlier brief. On the ALCS page, Smitty Smitty added a Game 6 photo caption: Junior Caminero went 2-for-3 with a home run and two runs scored, sending the Rays to their third World Series (1381118628). On the postseason page, SportsGamer257 noted it is the first World Series since 1980 between two teams still looking for their first title, and the sixth to match the No. 1 seeds from each league (1381118563). The World Series page now has a sourced "Small Market World Series" paragraph covering payrolls and the possible lockout (1381118590). Editors are also fixing mistakes as they go. A temporary account claimed this would be the first "all-indoor" World Series (1381118672), and DeMarcusCousinsCousin removed it because 2023 already holds that distinction (1381119070). KoRoBeNiKi's season-page summary wrongly names the Minnesota Twins as the opponent instead of the Brewers (1381118810), and that error had not been fixed in the edits I saw; Spanneraol's next edit there only changed an infobox field (1381119023). Activity is English-only (no linked pages in other languages turned up), with no reverts and about 15 named and temporary accounts. That looks like normal post-game updating, not vandalism or an edit war. The result still rests only on what editors wrote, not on an independent final source.

briefs.headline: Rays–Brewers World Series: Guardians page records ALCS exit; Rays "Twins" error fixed
briefs.summary: This update adds to the existing story, and the new edits agree with it: Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 4–2 in the ALCS and will play Milwaukee in the World Series. The Guardians season page has now caught up. Flyerssuperfan logged Game 6 as a 3–7 loss at Tampa Bay on October 19 (win to Peralta, loss to Armstrong, attendance 30,230), made the ALCS record 2–4 and removed the Game 7 row (1381118743). A temporary account rewrote the summary to say the Guardians lost in six games, "ending their season" (1381119200). That account kept an old October 11 ALDS citation, so the new sentence has no source of its own. The error flagged in the last brief has been fixed: Allen2 replaced "Minnesota Twins" with the Milwaukee Brewers on the Rays season page (1381119213). Allen2 also added background to the World Series page: Rays won the AL East, swept the Yankees, then beat Cleveland in six for their third pennant (2008, 2020, 2026) (1381119448). SportsGamer257 added a game-by-game ALCS recap on the postseason page. It says Game 6 was decided by Richie Palacios's two-run double and two-run homers from Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz, and calls it the Rays' first pennant won at home since 2008 (1381119688). He also noted that the Brewers' NLCS sweep of the Dodgers denied a rematch of the 2020 World Series (1381119985). Editing is still English-only with no reverts. It looks like normal post-game cleanup, not vandalism or an edit war. As before, the result rests only on what editors wrote.

briefs.headline: Rays beat Guardians 7–3 to win ALCS 4–2; World Series vs. Brewers set
briefs.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays appear to have won the 2026 ALCS four games to two, beating the Cleveland Guardians 7–3 at home in Game 6. That sets up a World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, the NL's top seed. Allen2 filled in the Game 6 box score ("Rays take Game 6 and win the ALCS!", rev 1381117655), and Smitty Smitty changed the series result to "(4–2) Tampa Bay Rays defeated Cleveland Guardians" and deleted the placeholder for a Game 7 on October 20 (1381117659). Within minutes, editors on the World Series and postseason pages swapped every "TBD/AL champion" slot for Tampa Bay, putting Games 3–5 at Tropicana Field (1381117904, 1381117911). Another editor added background on the matchup (1381117840): the two teams have never met in the postseason, both are still looking for their first title, and press coverage cited there calls it a "Small Market World Series" ahead of a possible lockout. About 14 named and temporary accounts made 27 edits over three pages with no reverts. That looks like normal live-event updating, not vandalism or an edit war. Caveats: the result rests only on what editors wrote during the game, not a final source, and only English Wikipedia has moved so far.

briefs.headline: Rays' Freddy Peralta named ALCS MVP, editor cites MLB.com; "Twins" error back on ALCS page
briefs.summary: This update adds to the existing story: the Rays beat the Guardians 4–2 in the ALCS and will face the Brewers in the World Series. The only new fact is that Freddy Peralta is listed as ALCS MVP. KoRoBeNiKi added a lead sentence naming Peralta MVP after he won Games 2 and 6, citing an MLB.com story dated October 19 headlined "ALCS MVP 'Fastball Freddy' pitches Rays to World Series, where his old team awaits" (1381121062). That is the first citation in this story tied to the result itself. The same edit also wrongly names the Minnesota Twins as the World Series opponent, the same mistake KoRoBeNiKi made on the Rays page earlier, and it is not fixed in the edits I read. Separately, Flyerssuperfan logged Game 6 on the Rays season page as a 7–3 win (Peralta W, Armstrong L) and added a World Series schedule. It runs October 23–31: Games 1–2 and 6–7 at American Family Field, Games 3–5 at Tropicana Field (1381120792). That entry has two small problems: it marks the game "@ Guardians" even though it was played at Tropicana Field, and it gives attendance as 40,230 where the Guardians page says 30,230, so the crowd figure is unsettled. Other edits are tidy-ups: Bananza76 removed the "current sport" banner from the ALCS page (1381119866), and a temporary account added Japanese broadcasters NHK BS and J Sports to the infobox (1381121431). Editing is still English-only with no reverts. This is routine post-series cleanup.

briefs.headline: World Series page: editors still arguing over dome-series trivia; latest fix leaves broken text
briefs.summary: This adds to the existing Rays–Brewers World Series story and doesn't change it. There is no new real-world event, and the Scout's call of routine upkeep holds. The new edits are back-and-forth over unsourced trivia in the Background section. RainbowRunner2000 changed the most recent all-dome Series from 2025 to 2023 (1381124652), which looks correct: Dodger Stadium has no roof, while both 2023 ballparks have retractable roofs.
