A temporary account added a line saying this is the first "-6" year Series since 1996 without a Central-vs-Central matchup (1381125030). A second temporary account deleted that line as "Misinformation corrected" and cut the dome count from "fifth" to "third", removing 1992, 1993 and 2020 (1381125280). That edit left garbled text: "(, an 2023)". On substance the "third" count may be right, because 1992 and 1993 each had games in open-air parks (Atlanta, Philadelphia), but the edit drops 2020 and breaks the sentence, so expect another fix. 杜沛克 changed "Domed" to "Dome" in the Game 4 infobox (1381124665), matching his Game 3 edits. Everything is English-only with no formal reverts, but the same sentence has now been rewritten about six times, so it's a slow-burning trivia dispute, not an edit war. The ALCS Game 6 attendance (40,230 vs 30,230) is still unresolved.

briefs.headline: World Series page: copyedits to Rays background on Peralta's Mets stint; no new event
briefs.summary: This adds to the existing Rays–Brewers World Series story and doesn't change it. The Scout is right: this is routine upkeep. Since the last brief, three named editors made four small edits to the 2026 World Series page, with no reverts and nothing outside English Wikipedia. DeMarcusCousinsCousin changed the description of Freddy Peralta's Mets stint from "poor season and a half" to "half a season" (1381135150, -4 bytes). That matches the cited Aug. 2, 2026 MLB.com trade story. CoDeX0206 then linked Peralta's name (1381135606) and made a further +18-byte tweak to the same paragraph (1381135789). I couldn't see that last change because the diff came back truncated. Allen2 made a "minor grammar fix + template tweak" to Background (1381135749). That paragraph now says this is the third World Series in which both teams play home games under a dome or retractable roof, after 2023, with a footnote explaining that the neutral-site 2020 Series doesn't count. This settles the trivia line editors fought over earlier in a sourced-adjacent form, but that sentence itself still has no citation. The ALCS Game 6 attendance (40,230 vs 30,230) is still unresolved.

briefs.headline: World Series page: Game 3 infobox now lists Tropicana Field as a dome; no new event
briefs.summary: This adds to the existing Rays–Brewers World Series story and doesn't change it. The Scout's call holds: there is no new event. Since the last brief, the only new edits are three small ones by 杜沛克 to the Game 3 infobox. They add a roof note to the "Other" field, change the link from "List of indoor arenas" to "List of indoor stadiums", and shorten the label from "Domed" to "Dome" (1381123745, 1381123934, 1381124644). This fits the Game 3 venue, Tropicana Field, which has a fixed roof. I re-read DeMarcusCousinsCousin's earlier "correction" (1381123313), but the diff was cut off again and still doesn't show what the 2-byte change was. It looks like a typo fix in a Background paragraph whose sourced claims were already there. That paragraph says Milwaukee (17th, $192M) and Tampa Bay (21st, $161M) have the lowest combined payrolls of any World Series pair since the 1994–95 strike. briefs.headline: France: 17 Oct protest day turned violent in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, frwiki edits say
briefs.summary: An existing frwiki article on a national day of protest in France on 17 October 2026 is being filled in after the event by 5 established, named editors (6 edits, no reverts). The article ties the protests to the 2026 high school and university student movement and the end of Macron's term. Harpocrate's edit (rev 240487827), sourced to Le Parisien, ici.fr and Le Monde, says the main Paris march drew about 110,000 people, with 195 arrests, wildcat marches trying to reach the Élysée, barricades on the Champs-Élysées and an "almost insurrectional" mood in the 8th arrondissement. Other edits add sourced photos and text on Lyon, where the tourist office on Place Bellecour was set on fire (rev 240486921), and on Marseille, where the Noailles police station was ransacked (rev 240487744). Edit timestamps work out to about 18 Oct ~13:30–14:00 UTC, so this is a write-up of yesterday's events, not a planned protest as the scout's note suggested. Limits: the activity is all on one language and one page (no SAME_AS pages in other languages in the graph), the edit count is low, and the figures come from the cited outlets via Wikipedia and have not been checked independently.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct protests: protester dies in Paris; Lille riots added; Limoges arson claim unsourced

The source is the Paris police prefecture as reported by CNews (18 Oct). This reads as a medical death, not violence. On Lille (rev 240488592), the article cites the Nord prefecture: a march of 24,000 people, about 2,000 violent individuals clashing with police from 12:30, and a McDonald's on the Grand-Place and a bar set on fire, sourced to ici and Horizon Actu. The text on how the day is being described (revs 240487961, 240488602) cites La Voix du Nord and Le Parisien using the word "insurrection", plus TF1 Info quoting foreign press on "urban guerrilla" scenes. Olevy added a Le Parisien report of police being overwhelmed by rioters and looters. One caution: the lead says Limoges's listed city hall was destroyed by arson, but Harpocrate removed its only citation (rev 240487990), which pointed to a Toulouse article. Treat that claim as unsourced until it is confirmed. Everything is still in one language on one page, and none of it has been checked independently.

briefs.headline: One temporary account's changes to two caste pages reverted by a patroller; no edit war
briefs.summary: This isn't a real dispute. One temporary account (~2026-56036-30) made poorly formatted edits to two small English Wikipedia caste/tribe pages within about 12 minutes. On Rajar (tribe), it removed 834 bytes (rev 1381092366), deleting the lead sentence, infobox and Rajasthan text and leaving loose citations. Its edit summary is in Sindhi and names one person as a member of the tribe. On Babbar (tribe), it rewrote the infobox (rev 1381091908) to add Hindu/Indian places and Punjabi, and removed the Baloch/Balochistan links. Patroller KuyaMoHirowo reverted both pages within minutes, citing an "ECR violation" (the restriction that limits South Asian caste topics to established editors; revs 1381092504, 1381092610). Each page has a single revert and the account didn't come back, so this is routine cleanup, not an edit war or a news event. What's unclear: whether the Babbar change reflects a real disagreement over the group's origins (Baloch vs. Rajput/Punjabi). But only one account was involved, so it doesn't count as evidence of a wider dispute.

briefs.headline: Footnote sections deleted from four ja-wiki animated film pages, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: Over roughly 2.5 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56447-07) made unexplained edits to four Japanese Wikipedia film pages: Frozen 3, Coco 2, the Shaun the Sheep pumpkin-patch film and Trolls Band Together. Each edit removed 26–49 bytes. The two diffs I read (Frozen 3, Trolls) show the account deleting the footnotes section heading (脚注), the help template and the reference list. Within about 7 minutes, patroller しのしん used TwinkleGlobal to revert all four edits as vandalism ("Rvv"), restoring the earlier versions. The scout counted 8 editors, but only two accounts were active in this burst. No release dates or other content changed, and nothing points to a real-world event. This is low-level disruptive editing that has already been cleaned up. I could not load the diff for the revert itself, but the edit summary and byte counts (+46 back against −46) match a full restore.

briefs.headline: Jeff the Killer page: unsourced sexuality claims added by temp account, reverted twice
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56097-97) made two edits to the enwiki article on the creepypasta character Jeff the Killer. Both added unsourced claims that the character is "LGBTQIA+"/"Homosexual": an infobox field, a change to the lead, and a rewrite of the backstory so it reads that he went on a killing spree after "coming out of the closet" and being burned by "homophobic bullies". The cited Pacer source was left as it was. Patroller Cannolis reverted the first edit for having no reliable source (WP:RS). ClueBot NG reverted the second as possible vandalism. The scout was wrong on one point: two of the four edits are reverts. But this is one person pushing unsourced content, not a back-and-forth edit war. Nothing points to a real-world event: no other languages or pages were involved, and no other editors joined in. This is low-level vandalism that was quickly handled, with no news value.

briefs.headline: Miami ranked No. 1 in new poll, editors set up its game against 5–2 Pittsburgh
briefs.summary: Three registered editors (Torlek, Blue Heron Football, KingSkyLord) made small, matching edits to the 2026 Miami Hurricanes and 2026 Pittsburgh Panthers football season pages. Rev 1380900061 adds Miami at No. 1 in the week-7 Coaches Poll, with what looks like 50 first-place votes. Rev 1380906970 adds the No. 1 rank to Miami's schedule entry. Revs 1380907866 and 1380907939 update the preview of the upcoming game on both pages to read "Pittsburgh Panthers (5–2) at No. 1 Miami Hurricanes (6–0)". There are no game results or scores in these edits, no reverts and no edits in other languages. This looks like routine weekly ranking and preview upkeep. The only newsworthy detail is Miami's unbeaten 6–0 start and No. 1 ranking, but I can't confirm that from outside sources. I couldn't read two of the diffs (1380907663, 1380907081), but their sizes and section names fit the same ranking updates.

briefs.headline: Notre Dame loses 28–24 at No. 8 BYU, drops in polls; Miami stays No. 1
briefs.summary: Notre Dame's 2026 season page now joins the Miami/Pittsburgh cluster, and these edits are more than routine upkeep: they record a game result. Rev 1380905124 by KingDLR2006 filled in the box score for "at No. 8 BYU". By quarter it reads Notre Dame 3-7-6-8 = 24 and BYU 7-14-0-7 = 28. BYU took the lead on a 6-yard Walker Lyons TD catch from Bear Bachmeier with 1:47 left. Some of the running-score labels inside that diff are garbled, so the result comes from the quarter totals. Later edits fit a loss: Notre Dame is listed at 6–1 in the Navy preview (rev 1380908351), and its AP rank went from 2 to 4 (rev 1380908224 by KingSkyLord; rev 1380907740 by Blue Heron Football). One oddity: Torlek's rev 1380900587 enters Notre Dame at No. 8 in the week-7 Coaches Poll, which is a big gap from the AP No. 4 and may be an error. On Miami, rev 1380907663 adds 40 first-place votes to its week-7 AP No. 1 ranking. All the edits are on English Wikipedia by a few regular college-football editors, with no reverts. This is upkeep of a real ranked-team upset, not an edit war, but I haven't confirmed the score outside Wikipedia.

briefs.headline: Italian 'Guerra d'Iran' article churn is cleanup, not news
briefs.summary: The 303-byte churn on itwiki's 'Guerra d'Iran' comes from six edits by three accounts, and none of them adds a new development. Registered editor Carlo Dani made link maintenance edits. One relinks the SIGINT article to skip a redirect in the section on CIA coordination with Israel before the 28 February strikes (rev 152959745). Another unlinks the IAEA article in the nuclear-background section (rev 152959922). Two temporary accounts reformatted the infobox's list of allied groups operating in Lebanon (Hezbollah, Huthi, PMF, Hamas, PIJ, PFLP, Amal and others). They added flag borders and merged the lines into one block; the existing sources were carried over and no new combatants were added (revs 152959752, 152959917). There are no reverts and no back-and-forth between editors, and no SAME_AS pages in other languages are tracked, so nothing points to an edit war or a breaking event. The underlying 2026 Iran war is clearly a live topic, but these particular edits contain no new facts.

briefs.headline: Chemist Douglas Stephan's page adds 2026 Davy Medal; other two pages are just patrol cleanup
briefs.summary: These three enwiki pages are grouped only because one patroller, CreativeLibrary460, touched all of them. They are not one story. Douglas Stephan: a temporary account added that he received the Royal Society's 2026 Davy Medal for chemistry (rev 1381251199). Another editor then added a citation to a University of Toronto news piece dated 2026-08-27 (rev 1381251519), and two style fixes followed. This is a real but small news item: an award announcement, now sourced. Utah Transit Authority: a temporary account changed "Salt Lake" to "Salt Leik" throughout the article (rev 1381250784). That is vandalism, and it was reverted twice by CreativeLibrary460 and Mochabearr. Otto Carius: the place where he studied pharmacy after the war was changed from Heidelberg to the University of Freiburg (rev 1381250990), with no source given. An earlier one-character attempt was reverted. This is a minor factual dispute, not news. I did not check the medal claim against anything outside the edits.

briefs.headline: Douglas Stephan update: 2026 Davy Medal entry holds steady, no new edits
briefs.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. There are no new edits on Douglas Stephan, Otto Carius or Utah Transit Authority after the last tracked revision (1381251999). The Stephan entry still says he won the Royal Society's 2026 Davy Medal for chemistry. It is cited to a University of Toronto Arts & Science news piece by Sean McNeely dated 2026-08-27 (rev 1381251519). That same edit moved the Order of Canada citation to the right sentence. The later edit only fixed a misspelled citation-needed tag on "He currently lives in Toronto" (rev 1381251999). Activity is small, all English-language, and no one has disputed or reverted the award claim. I have not checked the award against anything outside Wikipedia. The other two pages are still just routine cleanup by patrollers.

briefs.headline: Hoax Python Steering Council names repeatedly inserted, reverted on enwiki
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56033-10) made four edits to English Wikipedia's Python article. Each one attached five names (Findlay Noble, Quincy Ting, Noah Lima Grainger, Izaac Lye, Michelangelo Bianchi) to the sentence about the January 2019 Steering Council election, saying "the council came out public this morning". The real 2019 council was Barry Warsaw, Brett Cannon, Carol Willing, Guido van Rossum and Nick Coghlan, as set out in PEP 8100. The added names match none of them and look made up. Three established editors (Gadfium, Untamed1910, T8y) reverted the claim as unsourced or as contradicting PEP 8100. The account then added a "source": a Real Python glossary URL with an invented citation title ("Python Council changed to new members..."). Cleanup is incomplete. T8y's last revert (1381270716) removed the names but kept the fake Real Python citation, and the original PEP 8100/PEP 13 references appear to have been dropped. There is no sign of a real-world governance change. Only one page and one language are involved, and the activity is a single account's hoax or vandalism, not news.

briefs.headline: Two unrelated vandalism attempts on ru-wiki Blok and Transformers pages, both reverted
briefs.summary: These are two separate cases of low-level vandalism on Russian Wikipedia. They don't point to any real-world event. On the Alexander Blok biography, temporary account ~2026-55774-71 added a joke about the game "Block Strike" (Блок Страйк). It renamed the poet to "Блок Страйк" / "Блок страйкович" and wrote that he "began thinking about the game Block Strike back in the 19th century" (revs 155685834, 155685880). EyeBot automatically reverted the first edit and TheReallyThings rolled back the second. On the 1986 Transformers film page, Skyfire0 0 renamed the film "Transformers in Kazakhstan", gave it a Kazakh co-production and a Kazakh title, and then garbled the plot summary (revs 155685718, 155685746). EyeBot and Beonus reverted both edits. The two pages share only the anti-vandal bot EyeBot, and the edits came from different accounts with different themes, so the clustering is coincidental. No cross-language spread was checked, because nothing in the content suggests a real event.

briefs.headline: No story: two unrelated es-wiki vandal edits, linked only by anti-vandal bots
briefs.summary: This cluster is not a real-world event. Two separate temporary accounts edited different pages, and their edits were reverted within minutes. On Barcelona, ~2026-56374-47 twice inserted a political insult ("ciudad de rojos independentistas") into the lead sentence (revs 175920550, 175920579). Automoderador reverted the first and human editor Varondán undid the second. Nothing in the diffs points to sports broadcast rights or any other link between DirecTV and Barcelona. Recommend closing the story.

briefs.headline: Edit war on zh.wikipedia over Hakka origins and southward-migration pages
briefs.summary: This is an edit war on Chinese Wikipedia, not a news event. Over about 20 minutes, the temporary account ~2026-56323-48 and the registered user Cjsyr12345 repeatedly undid each other on three linked history pages: 客家民系 (the Hakka people), 建炎南渡 (the Jianyan southward migration) and 衣冠南渡 (the Jin-era southward migration). The temporary account kept restoring what it called the "stable version" (+5561 bytes on 客家民系, +82 on 建炎南渡, +16 on 衣冠南渡), with comments like "退回穩定版本，不要破壞" ("restoring the stable version, don't vandalise"). Cjsyr12345 undid every one within seconds or minutes, labelling them as reverting vandalism by an anonymous user, with some hostile comments such as "別像老鼠蟑螂一樣" ("don't act like rats and cockroaches"). Each side has gone well past three reverts per page. Earlier, another temporary account (~2026-56490-98) made almost identical restorations (+5558 and +82). That suggests the same person may be behind both accounts, but I haven't confirmed it. The fight is probably over contested claims about Hakka descent from northern Chinese migrants. I couldn't retrieve any diff text, so I can't say what the disputed 5.5 KB block contains or which version is better sourced. This brief rests on the edit metadata and comments only. The scout counted no reverts because the graph's revert flag is false on all of these edits, even though the comments show they are undos. The pages may need protection or admin review.

briefs.headline: zh.wikipedia Hakka-origins edit war ends in dispute protection; diffs show what was contested
briefs.summary: This is still a Wikipedia content dispute, not a real-world event, and it now looks paused. After more than 30 back-and-forth undos between temporary account ~2026-56323-48 and Cjsyr12345, user Manchiu (probably an admin) added {{pp-dispute}} templates to 客家民系 and 衣冠南渡. Both templates expire 2026-10-28, which suggests the pages are protected for about a week. The diffs show what the fight is about. The ~5.5 KB block on 客家民系 is a sourced section on Hakka origins: Luo Xianglin's "Central Plains Han migration" theory, Fang Xuejia's "southern Baiyue" theory, and genetic studies (Fudan 2003, Tianjin Normal, AJHG 2009) describing Hakka as mainly of northern Han descent. On 建炎南渡 the edit adds a claim that the Song-era migration formed the "客家人" group. On 衣冠南渡 it adds a "[[客家人]]" see-also link. Cjsyr12345 removes every one of these Hakka links. One comment on those removals uses an ethnic slur ("偷族客家族", roughly "thief-clan Hakka"), which points to a behaviour problem, not good-faith editing. The temporary account's version was the last edit on all three pages before protection, so the protected text includes the Hakka material. I haven't confirmed that 建炎南渡 was protected too, and I haven't checked whether the protection is technically enforced or only tagged.

briefs.headline: zh.wikipedia Hakka-origins dispute stays quiet after protection; no new edits
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity since the protection, so there is nothing to add to this story. Contrary to the scout's note, no edits to 客家民系, 衣冠南渡 or 建炎南渡 appear after Manchiu added {{pp-dispute}} templates (rev 95200461 at ts 1792568767, rev 95200468 at ts 1792568785). The diffs show each template expiring 2026-10-28. The graph has only 4 editors on these pages (Cjsyr12345, ~2026-56323-48, ~2026-56490-98, Manchiu), not 6. The last edit by either warring account was at ts 1792568623, and none of the four has edited any other page since then. The "no reverts" count is misleading: the graph's revert flag is false on all of these edits, but the comments show more than 30 manual undos before protection. 建炎南渡 was not given a template; Manchiu only tagged the other two pages. I still can't confirm whether the protection is technically enforced or only tagged. This is not a real-world event. I'd suggest closing this follow-up and re-alerting only if either party edits these pages again or the protection lapses.

briefs.headline: Two temporary accounts vandalize de.wiki electrical-meter pages; patroller reverts
briefs.summary: Over roughly 30 minutes, two temporary accounts (~2026-55970-25 and ~2026-55949-88) made small edits to three German articles on measuring instruments: Digitalmultimeter, Dreheisenmesswerk and Drehspulmesswerk. The diffs show juvenile vandalism. One edit inserts what looks like a name, "Pasci", plus a crude phrase ("Pascis Riesen Glied") and the nickname "Shelter" into the opening sentence. Another cuts the Quantisierungsabweichung section and part of a paragraph (rev 271476089). A third adds "zur befriediegung des Shelters" to Dreheisenmesswerk. The two accounts build on each other's edits, which suggests classmates, possibly during a physics lesson on these instruments. That is a guess. Patroller Ot reverted all three pages to clean versions within minutes. This is not a coordinated technical cleanup and there is no real-world news here. I did not read the Drehspulmesswerk diffs, but they follow the same pattern and were also reverted.

briefs.headline: Ex-Guatemalan prosecutor Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa reported killed, es-wiki shows
briefs.summary: The scout's low-priority call undersells this one. The Spanish Wikipedia biography of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa (a Guatemalan lawyer, former prosecutor and former head of the tax agency SAT) now has a "Muerte" (death) section and describes him in the past tense. That section cites DW ("Asesinan en Guatemala a exfiscal que denunció corrupción"; the URL says he was killed on a football field) and La Jornada (17 Oct 2026, "Mataron a exfiscal de Guatemala que denunció corrupción de políticos"). The three edits I read are follow-ups, not the first report of the death. One adds his father (Carlos López Arévalo, "comandante Camilo") with the La Jornada source (175886233). One cleans up formatting and loaded wording in the Muerte section (175886257). One fixes the broken citation (175886336). According to the section, the killing came two days after a Facebook video in which he questioned how the Arévalo government and the army handled a massacre of eight civilians in Huité, Zacapa, and suggested it was a failed US (CIA/DEA) operation. These are his own claims as the article reports them, not established facts. What's uncertain: the edit that first recorded the death is not in our graph, there are no other-language pages or reverts so far, and I haven't checked the sources myself. Still, two major outlets are cited and the editors aren't disputing the death, so it's likely real. It should be upgraded and watched for coverage of the Huité massacre and for en-wiki activity.

briefs.headline: Ex-Guatemalan prosecutor Solórzano Foppa reported shot dead at Guatemala City stadium; two held
briefs.summary: This follow-up backs up the earlier brief and adds detail. The Spanish Wikipedia biography of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa (former prosecutor and former head of the tax agency SAT) has a "Muerte" (death) section citing LA Times en Español, Publinews and Prensa Libre, alongside the DW and La Jornada sources reported earlier. According to that section, he was killed in a gun attack on the morning of Saturday 17 Oct 2026, aged 43, at the government-run "Campo Marte" stadium in zone 5 of Guatemala City, even though government security staff were protecting him. It also says a second person was found dead and five were wounded. Hours later the National Civil Police (PNC) reported arresting two suspects and recovering the weapon, which a preliminary report said was found in a "PedidosYa" delivery backpack. Editor Hard's two new edits (175886420, 175886400) only reword the casualty sentence and add an internal link; this text was added earlier, and that edit isn't in our graph. No editor disputes the death and there are no reverts. Uncertain: the page is still es-wiki only (no other-language versions, no en-wiki, no family pages or Huité massacre page moving in our graph), only 4 editors are involved, and I have not checked the cited outlets myself. The arrest and backpack details are preliminary police reports.

briefs.headline: No news: patrol reverts on two unrelated biographies (Staggie, Schall)
briefs.summary: These two English Wikipedia biographies have nothing to do with each other. What ties them together is one recent-changes patroller, F0malhaut42, who made 33 edits across many pages using the RedWarn tool. There is no new death or event. On Rashied Staggie, the Cape Town gang leader shot dead in December 2019, user RealtalkME cut about 125 bytes from the "Death" section, which already covers that killing. F0malhaut42 reverted it as unexplained removal, and RealtalkME then made a small, harmless wording change to "Early years" (noting the twin brother). On Roger Schall, the French photographer who died in 1995, Daisy61470 said she was a family member and added text giving credit to his brother Raymond Schall. F0malhaut42 reverted this for lack of reliable sources. The edits are a conflict-of-interest problem, not news. I couldn't see exactly what the Staggie removal cut because the diff text was truncated. Nothing here needs follow-up unless the Schall family edits keep coming back as an edit war.

briefs.headline: Account rewriting Dubai page with government sources reverted again; crime section kept
briefs.summary: This is an edit war on one Wikipedia page, not a news event. Assembly2026, an account that has edited only the English page Emirate of Dubai (6 edits), is trying to cut critical material from it and replace it with text sourced to the Dubai government. Its edit 1381158994 deleted the whole "International crime hub and criminal haven" section, which cites OCCRP's "Dubai Unlocked", the Carnegie Endowment and the press, calling it "highly inappropriate". Patroller IrisChronomia reverted that as a neutrality (NPOV) problem. Assembly2026 then made a bigger cut of 9,321 bytes (1381159862): it rewrote the lead, governance and geography sections around dubai.ae and digitaldubai.ae, with a 2025 population figure of 4.58M and "Arabian Gulf" wording. IrisChronomia undid that too (1381160591), so both sides have now reverted each other twice, and nothing has been edited since. Uncertain: the diff text I could see was cut off, so I can't confirm the second cut also removed the crime section, though the byte count suggests it did; and whether Assembly2026 has a conflict of interest is a guess, not proven. The other two pages share only the patroller and are small disputes: "Zionism" was added back to De Nederlandse Alliantie's ideology infobox after being reverted (1381159974), and a "marital rape" wording change on Arranged marriage was reverted.

briefs.headline: Single-purpose account repeatedly strips crime-hub section from Emirate of Dubai page
briefs.summary: The three pages share nothing except one patroller, IrisChronomia, who reverted edits on all of them. This is ordinary recent-changes patrolling, not a single real-world event. The only material dispute is on Emirate of Dubai. There, Assembly2026, an account that has edited only this page (6 edits), rewrote the lead and governance sections using "government sources". It then deleted the "International crime hub and criminal haven" section (−8,646 bytes) as "highly inappropriate". IrisChronomia reverted that for NPOV, and Assembly2026 then made a larger cut (−9,321) with the summary "added government sources... updated data of 2025". That pattern suggests a slow edit war and possible conflict-of-interest or reputation-management editing. The other two pages are small ideology/wording disputes: adding "Zionism" to De Nederlandse Alliantie's ideologies (reverted and then restored), and changing "marital rape" to "marital sexual violence" on Arranged marriage (reverted). Caveat: I couldn't fetch any diffs, so this relies only on edit summaries, byte deltas and graph metadata. No other-language versions of the Dubai page are linked or moving.

briefs.headline: New dewiki article created for ORF presenter Larissa Rausch; routine cleanup follows
briefs.summary: The activity comes from a brand-new German Wikipedia biography, not an update driven by news. Wikithunder1848, an account with only 4 edits, created the article (rev 271471883, +2,886 bytes). It describes Larissa Rausch (born 1997) as an Austrian lawyer, journalist and presenter who reports for ORF's magazine "Konkret" and has hosted its "Recht Konkret" segment since September 2024. Her sources are ORF Stars, her FHWien alumni profile, an ORF ON series page, and a Kleine Zeitung piece about the Bachmann Junior Preis. The other small edits, including AxelHH's, look like copyedits. Nothing here points to a news event: there are no reverts, no other languages and no breaking claims. One ORF reference URL still carries a "utm_source=chatgpt.com" tag, which hints the draft may have been written with AI help, and the subject's notability could be questioned later.

briefs.headline: Cleanup continues on new dewiki biography of ORF presenter Larissa Rausch; no news
briefs.summary: This is still a newly created German Wikipedia biography being tidied up. Nothing suggests a real-world event. Since the last brief, three editors have made only small cosmetic edits, with no reverts. AxelHH removed bold formatting from the section headings and linked the birth year (rev 271471993). AxelHH also swapped the broad "Journalismus" category for "Journalist (Österreich)" (rev 271472018). The article's creator, Wikithunder1848, added links to FHWien der WKW (rev 271472002) and Radio Arabella (rev 271472054). The -12/+12 byte pair from AxelHH is two unrelated edits, not a revert. Two problems remain: the ORF Stars citation URL still carries "utm_source=chatgpt.com", which hints the draft was written with AI help, and the subject's notability could be challenged later. Neither is newsworthy right now.

briefs.headline: Songtsen Gampo edit war on French Wikipedia has gone quiet after bot revert
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked frwiki "Songtsen Gampo" edit war. It is not a new event and has nothing to do with current news. Nothing has been edited since the last brief. The last two edits are still the garbled-name account's third swap (240570804) and Salebot undoing it 3 seconds later (240570805). That was about 20+ minutes before this check, and the page has been quiet since. The diff of 240570804 confirms the swap is the same as before. It deletes the passage sourced to Kuzmin, which says Taizong was "acculé" (cornered) by Gampo's conquests, and the Songzhou passage. It puts in "Old Tang Book 196" text instead, calling Tibet "un pays qui se soumet à la dynastie Tang" (a country that submits to the Tang dynasty) and the Wencheng marriage a "compromis mutuel" (mutual compromise). In 240570760, Rédacteur Tibet cited a China Intercontinental Press history of Tibet to support the contested invasion sentence. The scout's "no reverts" is wrong again. The revert flags are false, but the edit summaries show undo cycles. This page has no linked pages in other languages in the graph, so the dispute is limited to French Wikipedia. Earlier briefs suspected one person behind several accounts. That is still unconfirmed. The account may try again or move to the talk page, so the war may not be over.

briefs.headline: Songtsen Gampo edit war on French Wikipedia continues; anti-vandalism bot now reverting
briefs.summary: This is more of the tracked frwiki "Songtsen Gampo" edit war, not a new event, and no real-world news is behind it. The scout's "no reverts" is wrong. The revert flags are false, but the edit summaries and diffs show at least four undo cycles in about two hours. The new account with the garbled name ("WWiWi lWi…") made the same swap three times (240570594, 240570645, 240570804). Each time it removed the passage sourced to Kuzmin, which says Taizong was "acculé" (cornered) by Gampo's conquests and gave Princess Wencheng to stop an invasion. It replaced that with text citing "Old Tang Book 196", which calls Tibet "un pays qui se soumet à la dynastie Tang" (a country that submits to the Tang dynasty) and the marriage a "compromis mutuel" (mutual compromise) that "brought peace". R3L3ct3ur49 undid it once, Rédacteur Tibet undid it once, and the anti-vandalism bot Salebot undid the most recent attempt. Between attempts, Rédacteur Tibet strengthened the contested sentence (240570760) by citing a China Intercontinental Press "Concise General History of Tibet". That is a Chinese state-linked publisher, which seems meant to answer the other side with a source it would accept. Signs point to one person using several accounts: the earlier temporary account ~2026-56227-86 put back the same passage, and the new account was created for this dispute. This is not confirmed, and I did not check other language editions.

briefs.headline: French Wikipedia edit war over how Songtsen Gampo's article frames Tibet–Tang relations
briefs.summary: The scout read the churn on frwiki "Songtsen Gampo" as a rewrite. It is actually an edit war over historical framing, with no link to current news. One side keeps putting back the same passage, citing "Old Tang Book vol. 196". It says Tibet was "a country that submits to the Tang dynasty", that Songtsen Gampo apologised to Emperor Taizong after the battle of Songzhou, and that the marriage of Princess Wencheng was a mutual compromise that "brought peace". That version deletes the existing text, which is sourced to Kuzmin's "Hidden Tibet" and says Taizong was "cornered by Gampo's conquests" and gave up Wencheng to stop an invasion. The same text was added by four accounts in turn: Lili over (240557535), a temporary account (~2026-56227-86, whose edit summary accuses "Edit Tibet" of pushing a "subjective" version), and a newly created account with a garbled name (2 edits), which suggests a single person or a coordinated effort. Rédacteur Tibet and R3L3ct3ur49 undid it each time and pointed to the talk page. The revert flags are false, but the edit summaries and diffs clearly show undo cycles. I can't confirm sockpuppetry from these edits alone, and I didn't check other language editions.

briefs.headline: Man City season page logs 5–1 Champions League league-phase win on 20 October

briefs.headline: New de-wiki stub on 1920s songwriter Jesse Greer (d. 1970); not news
briefs.summary: Konrad Lackerbeck created a new German Wikipedia article on Jesse Greer, an American songwriter (1896–1970) known for "Just You, Just Me." The article is sourced to Wölfer's Lexikon der Unterhaltungs-Musik (2000). Three other edits followed: a whitespace fix, a minor change to the external links, and M2k adding Commonscat and authority-control templates (GND/LCCN/VIAF). The +1445 "large churn" is just the page being created, not a rewrite or a death update. He died in 1970, so nothing here points to a current event. There are no reverts and no other languages are involved. This is routine article creation.

briefs.headline: Unsourced death claim for Croatian singer Jakov Jozinović removed from hr-wiki
briefs.summary: On hr-wiki, editor Martin Kuljak added a death date and place to the lead of the article on 20-year-old Croatian pop singer Jakov Jozinović: "Beč [Vienna], 18. rujna 2026." (rev 7620284). The edit cited no source and did not link or mention the death anywhere else in the article. About seven minutes later a temporary account deleted the claim (rev 7620286), and a minute after that the experienced editor Ponor used Twinkle to restore the last good version (rev 7620287). The page is not linked to any other-language Wikipedia article, and no other pages show any matching activity. The edits came about a month after the claimed death date, with no source and no follow-up from other editors, so this looks like a death hoax or vandalism that was quickly reverted, not a real-world event. Some uncertainty remains: if real reports of his death appear, this page should be checked again.

briefs.headline: Unsourced Kim Jong-un death claims on it.wiki reverted; page protected
briefs.summary: Two temporary accounts on Italian Wikipedia added a death date for Kim Jong-un to his article, about 30 minutes apart. The first said he died on 20 October 2026 in Pyongyang (rev 152983744). The second gave the same date and place and added "brain haemorrhage" as the cause (revs 152984330 and 152984365). Neither edit cited a source. Editor Osnenzo removed each one, saying there was no source and no official confirmation (rev 152984468). Popsi then protected the page, and Osnenzo added a sourced birth year (rev 152984525), which is ordinary upkeep. The Scout's note said there were no reverts, but these were manual undos that the graph didn't flag as reverts. Nothing backs up the claim elsewhere: the only English edit was a date-format template (rev 1381140272). On Persian Wikipedia, a "death rumours" section that was described as AI-generated was cut, and a joke edit was reverted (rev 44784298). This looks like a hoax or rumour-driven vandalism, not news. The one open question is the timing: two separate accounts gave the same date, which could mean a rumour is going around off-wiki. It's worth checking again if other languages pick it up.

briefs.headline: Hashim Amla page: false parentage claim reverted; Ikhamanga honour suffix added without source
briefs.summary: Three edits to the English article on the retired South African batter Hashim Amla, all within about five minutes. A temporary account added an unsourced, false-looking claim that he is "the son of the famous South African cricketer Dabur Amla" (rev 1380894318). The anti-vandalism tool Interceptor, run by Materialscientist, reverted it two minutes later as unsourced content. Separately, the editor "User from Serbia" added the post-nominal letters "OIS" (Order of Ikhamanga in Silver, a South African national honour) to his name in the lead (rev 1380894908). That edit cites no source and has no edit summary, and the same editor's other recent edit was routine vandal patrol. No other languages and no other honour-related pages moved in the graph, so the edits don't by themselves show that a new national-orders announcement just came out. The likeliest reading is vandalism that was cleaned up, plus a routine tidy-up of an honour he may have received earlier. It's worth checking whether Amla really holds the OIS. If a fresh award is announced, it would show up as many recipients' pages being edited at once.

briefs.headline: Patrol cleanup across three unrelated en-wiki pages; no real-world event detected
briefs.summary: The only thing linking these three pages is one patroller, Materialscientist (using the Interceptor/rollback tools), cleaning up edits within about 15 minutes. They are not one news story. Hashim Amla: a temporary account's unsourced +63-byte addition (rev 1380894318) was reverted by Interceptor; separately, "User from Serbia" made an unexplained +44-byte edit (1380894908) that a prior brief describes as adding the "OIS" honour suffix. That honour is still unconfirmed, and no other honours-related pages moved. Fugazi: a temporary account blanked 298 bytes with no reason given (1380894591), and Interceptor restored them. Latin epsilon: I disagree with the scout's "routine churn" reading. An account named "Ɛ＝Ð Cum God the Second Attempt Ɛ＝Ð" (an offensive name, and "Second Attempt" points to a returning/sock account) undid an earlier editor's change (1380895438), then added content with the summary "Ɛ＝Ð" (1380895770). Both were rolled back to the earlier editor's version (1380895828), which fits a vandalism account more than a content dispute. Caveat: the diff fetch failed for every revision, so this rests on edit metadata only (comments, deltas, revert flags, usernames). No revisions are cited.

briefs.headline: Unsourced Kia-to-Hanwha team change on KBO outfielder Kim Ho-ryeong's page looks like vandalism
briefs.summary: A brand-new temporary account (~2026-56200-36) made four edits to the Korean Wikipedia page of Kia Tigers outfielder Kim Ho-ryeong (김호령). First it deleted the whole infobox (−1099) and relabelled the Kia link as "한화이글스" (Hanwha Eagles). Then it changed the club field, his 2015 draft team and his career line to Hanwha, and broke the markup in the process. None of these edits had a source or a summary. Changing his 2015 draft team can't be true even if he really had moved, which points to vandalism or a prank, not trade news. Experienced editor Nt reverted the edits twice. Ykhwong reverted once, then 16 seconds later undid his own revert (42687456), probably by mistake, so the page currently shows the false Hanwha version and needs fixing. The scout's "no reverts" flag is wrong: the edit summaries show three reverts. There are no other-language pages and no other activity backing up a real trade, but I can't completely rule one out.

briefs.headline: Kim Ho-ryeong page vandalism: false Hanwha version still live after self-undone revert
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity since the last brief. The newest edit on kowiki 김호령 is still Ykhwong's rev 42687456. The diffs confirm what we reported before. Temporary account ~2026-56200-36 left no sources and changed the Kia Tigers outfielder's current club, his 2015 draft team and his career line to "한화이글스" (Hanwha Eagles), and broke the markup doing it (rev 42687444). A real trade could never change a player's 2015 draft team, so this is vandalism, not trade news. Nt reverted twice. Ykhwong reverted, then 16 seconds later reverted his own revert (42687456). That put the vandal's text back word for word, so the live page wrongly says Hanwha and needs one more revert. The scout's note says "no reverts," which is wrong: there were three revert edits. Nothing in other languages or elsewhere backs up a real move.

briefs.headline: Routine copyediting of Polish Wikipedia article on the 'Rule 63' internet meme
briefs.summary: Over about 30 minutes, four registered pl-wiki editors (Xarys777, NiktWażny, Wcalenieja, IOIOI) made six small edits to "Zasada 63", the article on the "Rule 63" internet meme about gender-swapped versions of fictional characters. The diffs I read show only maintenance work. Wcalenieja fixed Polish inflection and capitalization, reformatted citations, wrapped English titles in templates, and removed the {{Przetłumaczony}} template marking the page as translated from en-wiki. IOIOI added a sister-projects box (Commons/Wiktionary) and the "Memy internetowe" category, and removed a red link from "See also". There were no reverts and no disputed content, and no other language versions or related pages moved. This looks like a recently translated article being tidied up through normal community cleanup, not a sign of any real-world event. The net churn is small (each edit changed fewer than 160 bytes), and I didn't read the first two minor edits.

briefs.headline: New pt-wiki biography of Haitian anthropologist Suzanne Comhaire-Sylvain created
briefs.summary: On Portuguese Wikipedia, user Oitocentistas created a new article (+5,482 bytes) on Suzanne Comhaire-Sylvain (1898–1975), described as Haiti's first Black woman anthropologist and an early linguist of Haitian Creole. The article cites 2023–2024 scholarship (Ethnologies, Archipélies). The creator then added categories. Two other experienced editors, Daniel G Rego and Leirbag reib, followed with small cleanups: infobox image and caption formatting, punctuation before refs, and naming a reused reference. There were no reverts and nothing contested. The subject died in 1975, and no edit points to a current event, so this looks like ordinary content creation, maybe tied to an editing campaign on women or Haitian figures. That last part is a guess the graph doesn't confirm. The 'large churn' the scout flagged is just the page being created; it isn't a rewrite.

briefs.headline: French Wikipedia gets new article on Norwegian cyclist Simen Evertsen-Hegreberg
briefs.summary: This is a routine new-article story, not breaking news. Zubeldia3764 created the frwiki biography of Simen Evertsen-Hegreberg (rev 240487498, +6.9 kB). He is a Norwegian rider born in 2004 in Würzburg, Germany, son of former pro Morten Hegreberg. He rode for Tirol-KTM from 2023 to 2025 and rides for Lucky Sport in 2026. The creator then added detail on his 2022 junior season (rev 240487843: second at Nokere Koerse juniors behind Jarno Widar; second in the Norwegian junior criterium championship). FromZeFild (rev 240488126) removed several infobox fields, which looks like infobox cleanup, possibly so the data comes from Wikidata instead; it is not a dispute. A third editor made a small edit to the rankings section. The newest source cited is an August 2026 local article saying he would ride the Arctic Race of Norway. The page has no reverts and no other language versions moving with it, and nothing in what I read points to a current news event. The likeliest explanation is a cycling-project editor writing up a rider before the 2026 season.

briefs.headline: es-wiki Total Drama page: user's redirect and deletion bids reverted by bot and patroller
briefs.summary: This is a low-stakes editorial fight on es:Drama Total Todos Estrellas, not a real-world event. Only three accounts edited the page. Brunocrac4 tried three times to replace the roughly 34k article with a redirect to "Drama Total: Todos Estrellas e Isla Pahkitew" (rev 175924261), along with smaller copyedits: "quinta temporada" became "primera parte de la quinta temporada" and "será lanzado" became "fue lanzada" (rev 175924090). Each time the anti-vandal bot SeroBOT restored the article. The scout said there were no reverts, but that is wrong: the edit comments record at least five revert actions, even though the revert flag was never set. Brunocrac4's own comments warn of an edit war and call it a bot that "no entiende" (doesn't understand). Brunocrac4 then added an {{Eliminar}} deletion tag, arguing the page is redundant and outdated (rev 175924345). Patroller Ontzak removed the tag. The merge question is a fair one, and it will probably be settled through a deletion or merge discussion. There has been no activity since the previous brief.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: user and anti-vandal bot trade reverts over Total Drama season page
briefs.summary: The scout read about 203k of churn on es:Drama Total Todos Estrellas as a big rewrite. It isn't. The edits come from one editor, Brunocrac4, going back and forth with the anti-vandalism bot SeroBOT, plus a final revert by Ontzak. The scout's "no reverts" was wrong: the edit comments show at least six reverts, even though the revert flag was never set. Brunocrac4 tried several times to turn the article into a redirect to "Drama Total: Todos Estrellas e Isla Pahkitew" (each try about −31k), saying a newer article already covers the whole fifth season. They also made small fixes, such as changing "es la quinta temporada" to "es la primera parte de la quinta temporada" and putting dates in the past tense. SeroBOT put the full roughly 34k-byte article back each time, and Brunocrac4 grew frustrated ("ese bot no entiende", "that bot doesn't get it"). Brunocrac4 then tried a formal deletion request ({{Eliminar}}), calling the page redundant and outdated, and Ontzak removed it. This is an editorial fight over merging two articles about a 2014 cartoon season. There is no real-world news here. It is a low-stakes edit war, and it could be settled on the merge or deletion process pages.

briefs.headline: Wake Forest, Wisconsin 2026 football pages get routine poll and schedule updates
briefs.summary: Five registered editors (no anonymous editors, no reverts) made small edits to the English Wikipedia pages for the 2026 Wake Forest and Wisconsin football teams. The changes are ordinary weekly upkeep. briefs.headline: Arch Manning stats show Texas QB's 6th start ended in loss; vandalism reverted
briefs.summary: Three edits to English Wikipedia's Arch Manning page in about 3 minutes. Marist72 updated the current-season stats table (rev 1380878386) from 5 games and a 4–1 record to 6 games and 4–2. The numbers it implies for the newest game: 14 of 20 passing for 173 yards, 1 TD and no interceptions, plus 10 rushes for 0 net yards. That suggests Manning started a sixth game for Texas and lost it. An unregistered account then renamed him and his family "Joe Smith"/"Smith" (rev 1380878646). An anti-vandalism tool user undid that a minute later (rev 1380878789). This was one-off vandalism with no back-and-forth, not an edit war. Uncertain: the opponent, score and date aren't in the edits, the stats come from a single editor with no source given in the diff, and no other-language pages or related Texas football pages were checked.

briefs.headline: Arch Manning page: stats now show 6th Texas start was a loss; one vandal edit undone
briefs.summary: I found no new activity since the last brief. The graph still holds only the same three English Wikipedia edits, all within about 3 minutes, and no Texas Longhorns pages moved. That suggests Manning started a sixth game for Texas this season and lost it. An unregistered account then replaced "Manning" with "Smith" for Arch and his relatives (rev 1380878646). briefs.headline: Torbeši article: small edit war over "Macedonian-speaking" vs "Slavic-speaking" wording
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on the Torbeši, a Muslim ethnoreligious group, saw a small revert cycle over how to describe them. A temporary account restored a version (rev 1381148599) that changes "Macedonian-speaking" to "slavic-speaking", adds Kosovo to the regions where they live (Podgora/Prizren, Sredačka Župa), replaces Romani with Vlachs in a list of other groups, and switches to the spelling "Torbeshi". A new account, Skorobishta12, then added unsourced lists of villages in Albania (Kukës/Luma) "with Torbesh roots" and removed "Macedonian" from the census wording (rev 1381149132). Established editors pushed back. Jingiby had already reverted these changes earlier ("not an improvement... gain a consensus", rev 1381139934), and StephenMacky1 put that version back, calling the changes "Disruption" (rev 1381149894). This is a familiar Balkan dispute over labels and identity, not a sign of any real-world event. It's low volume: one page, four editors, no other languages involved. The temporary account and the new account may be the same person, but I can't confirm that.

briefs.headline: Catherine Doherty article: second sneaky vandal edit reverted, no news event
briefs.summary: The English article on Catherine de Hueck Doherty (1896–1985), founder of Madonna House, is still drawing low-level vandalism. That account made its second bad edit (rev 1381263630), labeled "spelling error". The edit changed "He died in 1991" to "They died in 1991" in the line about her son George, which falsely implied other people died in 1991. Nil NZ undid it within about 80 seconds with WikiShield, noting "not a spelling error" (rev 1381263700). The page is back to its correct text. There are still only three editors on one page, no other-language activity, and nothing pointing to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Catherine Doherty article hit by juvenile vandalism, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: The English article on Catherine de Hueck Doherty (d. 1985), the Catholic activist who founded Madonna House, took a short burst of vandalism. Account LXR111 made two edits. One changed her "CM" post-nominal (Member of the Order of Canada) to "CUM". The other added a sexual insult to the end of the lead. Patroller Nil NZ reverted both together with WikiShield (-31 bytes, matching the +1 and +30 LXR111 added). This is not an edit war or a news event: the page has no other activity and no other-language edits, and neither vandal account has edited anything else.

briefs.headline: Lucas Digne page: repeated BLP vandalism to personal-life section, reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a transfer or club story. One temporary account (~2026-43477-40) made the same 8-byte change three times, inserting the word "traitor" before "girlfriend Tiziri" in the Personal life section of Lucas Digne's English Wikipedia biography. Three different established editors undid it each time: Ser!, Mattythewhite, and Cannolis, who cited the policy on biographies of living people (WP:BLP).
