The graph shows no linked pages in other languages and no activity on related pages. Status is vandalism. If the account keeps going, the page may get protected.

briefs.headline: JOA disambiguation page hit by repeated joke insertion; patroller reverted it twice
briefs.summary: This update adds the JOA disambiguation page to the existing Anubis vandalism story. Two different temporary accounts (~2026-56142-99, then ~2026-55884-90 about four minutes later) each added the same fake entry, "A gentleperson's club in the BD07 district." BD07 is a UK postcode area in Bradford, so this looks like a local in-joke. The first edit used the summary "brief addendum". Both times Materialscientist removed the line within about 90 seconds, using the Interceptor tool. The scout's note says there were no reverts on JOA, but there were two; the graph doesn't flag them as reverts. The same exact line coming back from a new account suggests one person switching accounts, though I can't confirm that. The only link to Anubis is that the same patroller cleaned up both pages, so these are probably separate incidents rather than a coordinated campaign. Both pages are back to their clean versions, no other languages were touched, and nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Anubis article hit by brief juvenile vandalism, reverted by ClueBot NG and patroller
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56243-13) made three edits to English Wikipedia's Anubis article over about three minutes. All three were vandalism: it added "yo yo yo", put "nico" in the middle of a word in the lead, and put "nico" again in front of the date template, with the edit summary "nice nico". ClueBot NG reverted the first two edits. Materialscientist undid the third about 30 seconds after it was made. I read all four diffs to confirm this. The scout said there were no reverts, but there were two; the graph just doesn't flag them as reverts. No other language versions were edited, and the diffs show no link to anything happening in the world. This is simple vandalism that has already been fixed, not news.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on ru-wiki red-lipped batfish article undone by bot and patroller
briefs.summary: This is two small acts of vandalism by one account, not article expansion. Note that "Нетопырь Дарвина" is the red-lipped batfish (Ogcocephalus darwini), a fish, not a bat. Editor Kaksska first deleted the whole species infobox with the comment "кактус" ("cactus"), a −310 byte change. EyeBot undid it automatically about 20 seconds later (ORES score 0.70). Kaksska then changed the body length from "25 сантиметров" to "10000 сантиметров" and the lifespan from 1 year to 10. Patroller Sand Kastle 17 undid that a minute later. The 630-byte churn is just these two edits and their undos. The graph's revert flag says false for all four, but both fixes are undos according to their edit comments. Kaksska has only 2 edits on record, and no other pages or languages moved, so there is no sign of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: More small tampering on ru-wiki red-lipped batfish page; unsourced size change still live
briefs.summary: This follows the earlier Kaksska vandalism on "Нетопырь Дарвина" (Ogcocephalus darwini, the red-lipped batfish). Three more edits came from new or temporary accounts. Temporary account ~2026-55329-30 added a duplicate red link ("[[нетопырёвые]] [[Нетопыревые|нетопыревые рыбы]]") under the comment "added a needed link", and patroller Sand Kastle 17 undid it about a minute later. First-time account Matveykakoyto then changed body length from 25 to 30 cm with the comment "update" and no new source. The source cited in that sentence still supports the old figure, and the change has not been reverted. Every account involved has one or two edits and no other pages, and no other languages moved, so this is low-level tampering rather than a real-world event. It is unclear whether the 30 cm edit was deliberate or careless, and the accounts can't be shown to be linked.

briefs.headline: ru-wiki: batfish tampering all undone; separate account edit-wars 1943 date on Polish WWII pages
briefs.summary:
This story contains two unrelated low-level problems on Russian Wikipedia. Neither is a real-world event.

(1) Batfish page ("Нетопырь Дарвина", the red-lipped batfish). Every bad edit is now undone. This corrects the previous brief, which said the 30 cm length change was still live. Sand Kastle 17 restored the length to 25 cm in rev 155684228. The same new account, Matveykakoyto, then retitled the lead to "Красногубый Нетопырь" and changed the sort key (rev 155684271). EyeBot undid that automatically about 20 seconds later.

(2) Yalta Conference ("Ялтинская конференция") and Operation Tempest ("Акция «Буря»"). The scout's note says there were no reverts here, but that is wrong: the graph's revert flag is false, yet the edit comments show undos. Temporary account ~2026-55727-16 changed the date of the Polish government-in-exile's instruction to the Home Army (Армия Крайова) from "1 октября 1943" to "26 октября 1943" on both pages (revs 155684394 and 155684439). There was no source and the comment was just "исправление, уточнение" ("correction, clarification"). Eniisi Lisika undid the changes. The account put them back, and DurbeK82 and Sand Kastle 17 undid them again. The same account also added an unsourced passage on the Home Army page arguing the Ukrainian nationalist (OUN/UPA) side (rev 155683851). On the page about the 1944–53 anti-communist movement in Poland it undid Eniisi Lisika's revert of its own edit (rev 155684299). That diff was cut off, so I couldn't see exactly what was restored.

This looks like one account slowly pushing a point of view or date changes on Polish WWII history, which patrollers are containing. The two halves share no editors except patroller Sand Kastle 17. The real date of the instruction is unverified, so the date change may be careless rather than malicious.

briefs.headline: ru-wiki 1943 date dispute spreads to "Poland" and "Home Army" pages; new edits still live
briefs.summary: This update adds two pages. Temporary account ~2026-55727-16 was reverted on the Yalta Conference and Operation Tempest pages; Sand Kastle 17's undo in rev 155684444 put back "1 октября 1943". The account then made the same one-figure change on two more ru-wiki pages. On "Польша" (Poland), rev 155684479 changes the date of the London government's instruction to the Home Army from "1 октября 1943" to "26 октября 1943", with no source and the same comment as before ("исправление, уточнение", "correction, clarification"). On "Армия Крайова" (Home Army), rev 155684530 (+1 byte, comment "исправление") targets the same passage. That diff was cut off: the old line "[[1 октября]] 1943" is visible but the new line isn't, so I'm inferring the 1→26 change from the matching byte count. Neither new edit had been reverted when the graph last updated. This is one account pushing a single date across four pages while patrollers undo it, not a real-world event. The scout's note of "no reverts" is wrong, as the earlier brief also found: the graph's revert flag is off, but the edit comments show the undos. One caveat: some historians date this instruction to late October 1943 (about 26–27 October), so the change may be a real correction made without a source rather than vandalism. Talk-page discussion with a source would settle it. The batfish half of this story has had no new activity.

briefs.headline: Romania: Parliament reportedly elects Luca Niculescu PM, ending months-long crisis
briefs.summary: On English Wikipedia's "2026 Romanian political crisis" article, editors added that on 20 October Parliament voted in Luca Niculescu as prime minister. The text says PSD, PNL and UDMR backed him, "effectively ending the crisis that held for nearly half a year" (revs 1381211296, 1381211915). The article now gives the crisis an end date of 20 October 2026. It traces the crisis back to the no-confidence vote that removed PM Ilie Bolojan, followed by failed bids by Eugen Tomac, Adrian Veștea and Siegfried Mureșan (rev 1381210422). Other wikis back this up: Niculescu cabinet pages were active in the same hours on fr, ro, pl and en, a new Polish page "Rząd Luki Niculescu" was created, and Niculescu's biography was edited on fr, pl, simple and cs. Uncertainty: almost all of the English edits came from one editor, VityaPeti, and the vote sentence I read has no reference attached. Materialscientist reverted one of VityaPeti's edits as unsourced, but what that revert touched was the start date (25 April vs 5 May). VityaPeti then put the 25 April date back (rev 1381214779), so there is a small open dispute over the start date, not a full edit war. There are no other reverts and no sign of vandalism.

briefs.headline: Karol G tour page on es-wiki: tour-date table reworked, unsourced cancellations added
briefs.summary: The candidate headline is wrong. "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour" is Karol G's concert tour, not a travel show. Three accounts made 7 edits with no reverts. Registered editor Paiap reformatted the tour-date table to show attendance and gross per show (for example, Chicago Soldier Field 85,300 and $18.0M; SoFi Stadium 139,000 and $34.1M, citing Billboard Boxscore). Paiap also changed the counts to 64 shows and 1 cancelled, and the edit comment says a Poland date was dropped because it isn't on sale or listed on Karol G's official site. Temporary account ~2026-55869-88 then moved Lyon (21 Jul 2027) in the cancelled-dates section, added Lisbon's Estádio da Luz (18 Jun 2026) as cancelled, and gave "logistics problems" (with a typo) as the reason for both. That account cited no source and also made small formatting edits that broke the España flag template. This looks like routine fan upkeep of the page. The only possibly newsworthy claim is the cancellations, and nothing in the edits confirms them, so I'd treat them as unverified.

briefs.headline: No new activity on Vincent Boesen page; reverted Samui United stats remain at 0/0
briefs.summary: This is the same set of edits the tracked story already covered, and nothing has happened since. The page's only edits are the four already logged on the German Wikipedia article for Vincent Boesen, a striker who joined Samui United FC in Thailand in 2026. I've now read the 0-byte edit by Zikrul Kari (rev 271484561), which the earlier brief skipped. It changed his Samui United record from 3 games and 3 goals to 1 game and 3 goals. RoBri's rollback (rev 271484579) undid the anonymous edit and both of Zikrul Kari's, restoring Siam.Soccer's version, which shows 0 games and 0 goals. The diff shows the rollback also put back the infobox formatting the anonymous edit had changed. One correction to the earlier brief: the rollback came about 38 seconds after the last edit and about 5 minutes after the first, not about 30 minutes later. The numbers never agreed with each other, no source was given, and nobody has tried again or edited the matching pages in other languages. It's possible Boesen scored a hat-trick in one match, but the edits don't confirm it. This is routine and needs no further follow-up unless the stats are re-added with a source.

briefs.headline: Unsourced stat changes on German footballer Vincent Boesen's page rolled back
briefs.summary: Vincent Boesen is a German striker from Trier who joined Samui United FC in Thailand's third division in 2026. An unregistered account (rev 271484470) reformatted his infobox and changed his Samui United record from 0 games and 0 goals to a garbled "0 {{1}}(3)". Registered user Zikrul Kari then changed it again, first to 3 games and 3 goals (rev 271484554). A further 0-byte edit that I didn't read apparently left it at 1 game and 3 goals. About 30 minutes later RoBri rolled back all three edits to Siam.Soccer's version, which shows 0 games and 0 goals (rev 271484579). The numbers don't agree with each other, no source was given, and the infobox still says it is current to the end of the 2025/26 season. So this was a rejected stats update, not a news event. Boesen may have started playing or scoring for Samui United, but nothing here confirms it.

briefs.headline: Pro Asyl article refreshed with 2025 figures; account named for the group adds a source
briefs.summary: A temporary account rewrote the English Wikipedia article on German refugee-advocacy NGO Pro Asyl. It updated the infobox to 25,000 members and a budget of €6,020,618 (2025), up from 25,209 members and €5.85m in 2022. The edit also copy-edited the lead and, according to its edit summary, deleted an "outdated" Positions section (net −649 bytes). Editor CantReadRunes did a partial "revert" that only fixed a duplicated bold name and a broken interlanguage link. The same editor then swapped a broken citation for a citation-needed tag. An account named "ProAsyl" then cited the organisation's own 2025/2026 activity report for the figures. The "reverts" were cleanup, not an edit war, and there is no sign of a real-world event. The only point worth noting is a possible conflict of interest: the new numbers rest on Pro Asyl's own report, and the account name suggests the organisation edited its own page. Removing the Positions section could also be read as image management, but I did not check what that section said.

briefs.headline: Prank edits on Cruz Alta (Córdoba) eswiki page spread to its history and notable-people sections
briefs.summary: This is still schoolyard vandalism, not a news event. Two temporary accounts kept going after the last brief. ~2026-56015-61 changed the 1966–69 mayor "Pratta" to "Fernández-Rosalez, Paul" (rev 175909866). It also added an "honorable mention" for a teacher at the Instituto Privado Diocesano San Luis and his greyhound "Galgo Salvaje" (rev 175909993), and slipped made-up names ("Valentin Bruno", "Bastian Martinez Miranda") into the colonial history section (rev 175910068). ~2026-56106-69 changed how the link to the singer Pablo Funes displays, so it now reads "giustiiix arda" (rev 175910013). It then described that name as an adult-website actress (rev 175910056). That is a crude and possibly defamatory joke, which makes it a cleanup priority. The history and notable-people text also contains other odd names ("Renzo Pratto", "ivo ilari", "Tanque massei", "Massi Fratta77", "ciudad de suiza") that look like earlier vandalism from the same group. I didn't check when those went in. No reverts have happened since SeroBOT's earlier one, so as of the last edit everything above is still live. The school reference suggests a group of students is behind this.

briefs.headline: Cruz Alta (Córdoba) eswiki page hit by joke edits and fake mayor names
briefs.summary: This is not a real-world event. Two temporary accounts are making prank edits to the Spanish Wikipedia article on Cruz Alta, Córdoba. Account ~2026-56015-61 added a joke line under "Otros datos de interés" about "our beloved greengrocer" Dylan "Mono" Zalazar donating bananas to a zoo. The same account also changed the historical list of mayors: an entry marked "no data" for 1940–43 became "Rosalez, Santino", and the 1966–69 mayor "Pratta" became "Fernández-Rosalez, Paul". The surnames look like inside jokes among friends. A second temporary account replaced the 2007–2011 mayor Diego Passerini with "Juan Martín crispina", and SeroBOT reverted that change. The other changes are still unreverted as of the last edit and need cleanup. I didn't read rev 175909727 (+22).

briefs.headline: Albanian protests page: temp account returns, swaps in new image and 'riots' subtitle
briefs.summary: This is a small follow-up, not a new story. About six minutes after Pattersonuwu restored PancakeGuy20's version (1381073858), the same temporary account (~2026-55646-41) edited the 2026 Albanian student protests infobox again (1381074423). It added the subtitle "2026 Albanian riots" and replaced the existing AlbProtest.png with "File:Flamingo Reveloutin.jpg", captioned "Craziest riots in Albania". This time it did not touch the casualty figures, and no one has reverted the edit so far. Calling the protests "riots" has no source, and the misspelled image name and the caption look like low-quality or joke editing rather than a report of escalation. The page has five edits in total, no other-language versions in the graph and no sources in any diff I read, so it says nothing reliable about what is happening on the ground. The protests themselves still look like a real, ongoing event. Expect a patroller to revert this edit.

briefs.headline: Vandal churn moves to charter school and Albanian protest pages; all reverted
briefs.summary:
The Dulce Maria Alavez attack has calmed down. The last change there remains Pattersonuwu's revert. Two new pages have joined the cluster.

On Collegium Charter School, temporary account ~2026-56075-06 made a run of nonsense edits. In 1381073665 it replaced the founders and CEOs with "Robert Loggia", moved dates to 2067 and swapped words for "pop". Cannolis reverted it twice, the last time in 1381073744. This is plain vandalism.

On 2026 Albanian student protests, temporary account ~2026-55646-41 raised the infobox casualty figures without sources (1381073651): injuries from 900 to 1000, arrests from 2000 to 2200, injured police from 400 to 500. It also added a forecast that "tomorrow said to get extremely violent". Ivebeenhacked cut the status text in 1381073826. Pattersonuwu then restored the earlier PancakeGuy20 version in 1381073858.

The page does cover protests that are still going on, but these edits don't show any new development. The higher numbers had no source and have been removed. The infobox numbers that were restored also cite no source in these diffs, so I can't confirm them.

Nobody edited both pages, so I can't say whether one person is behind both. Overall this is small-scale vandalism that patrollers have contained. I agree with the Scout.

briefs.headline: Alavez vandalism quiet; new cluster pages share only a patroller, Albania page is separate
briefs.summary: The Dulce Maria Alavez article has had no edits since Pattersonuwu reverted it in 1381072167. There's no new vandalism on it in this window. The Scout said the two new pages are tied in by the same editors. The graph doesn't support that: the only overlap is the patroller Pattersonuwu, and none of the vandal accounts touched them. On Collegium Charter School, a different temporary account (~2026-56075-06) made silly edits: it added "pop" to the text (1381072648) and replaced the founders' and CEOs' names with "Robert Loggia", with dates in 2067 (1381073665). Cannolis and Pattersonuwu reverted these. It looks like separate juvenile vandalism, not the Alavez long-term abuser. The 2026 Albanian student protests page is a real event that is still going on, not vandalism. Temp account ~2026-55646-41 raised the unsourced infobox figures (injured 900→1000, arrests 2000→2200, police injured 400→500) and added "Tomorrow said to get extremely violent" (1381073651). Ivebeenhacked trimmed this (1381073826) and Pattersonuwu restored the earlier version by PancakeGuy20 (1381073858), which places the protests mostly in Tirana. The Albania page has only 4 edits, no other-language versions in the graph and no sources in the diffs I read, so the casualty numbers aren't reliable. It should probably get its own story instead of being folded into this vandalism cluster.

briefs.headline: Missing-child article Dulce Maria Alavez hit by repeated sexualized vandalism
briefs.summary: This isn't news about the case. It's vandalism. A single temporary account (~2026-55994-91) added the words "sexy, curvaceous" to the opening sentence about Dulce Maria Alavez three times in about 45 seconds. She is the child who went missing in Bridgeton, NJ in 2019. The edit summaries ("revert", "socks") were misleading. The editors EndTheWikiEditor (using the Interceptor anti-vandal tool) and Joyous! undid it twice. Each of the three diffs I read adds the same 18 bytes of text and nothing else: no new facts, no sources, no change to the case. As of the vandal's last edit (1381071490), the vandalism was back in place. I haven't checked whether anyone has removed it since. No other pages or languages were involved, so there's no real-world development here.

briefs.headline: Dulce Maria Alavez vandalism continues via rotating temp accounts; reverted
briefs.summary: This is still vandalism, not news about the Alavez missing-child case. After the "sexy, curvaceous" edits I covered in the earlier brief, the attack switched to three new temporary accounts: ~2026-55995-51, ~2026-56084-38 and ~2026-55996-11. Each one changed the child's middle name in the opening sentence, to "Astra", "Elizabeth" and even "Pattersonuwu", which is the name of one of the editors reverting them. Their edit summaries ("reverting a sock", "rv lta", "rv") pose as anti-vandal work; this suggests one long-term abuser hopping between throwaway accounts, though I can't confirm it from the graph. Pattersonuwu and Komethere, using the Interceptor and VandalHandle anti-vandal tools, reverted each change, and the latest edit I read (1381072167) restores "Maria". The other pages in the cluster (Knights Templar School, Killing of Rayshard Brooks, East Germanic peoples) share some patrollers but have no editors in common with the vandals. From their summaries they look like ordinary small-scale churn (an unsourced headteacher edit, a redirect retarget, an article-title dispute), so I agree with the Scout. I couldn't load those pages' diffs, so that last point is based on edit summaries only.

briefs.headline: Albania student protests: no new facts since last brief, only cleanup on en-wiki
briefs.summary: The only edit to "2026 Albanian student protests" since the previous brief is rev 1381239682. In it, admin DMacks removed a duplicate "Flamingo Revolution" link from See also under the style rule against repeating links already in the article, so it changes no facts. The "1,347 churn" in the scout's note is the "Finished wip (up to 18 Oct)" edit (rev 1381238882), which the prior brief already covered. That edit dates the clashes from 13 October, adds rubber pellets to tear gas and water cannon as police methods, and says there have been daily Tirana protests since 31 May as part of the Flamingo Revolution, sourced to Top Channel and DW. The Prince Rupert's drop change is an unrelated grammar revert by DMacks of a one-comma edit by a temporary account. There are still no reverts on the protests page and no other-language versions of it in the graph, and most new content comes from one editor (Hduensixojnrwjzz). The underlying story is still developing, but this update adds nothing new. The cited news sources are still unchecked.

briefs.headline: Albania student unrest: en-wiki cites a seventh day of clashes, ~295 hurt, Rama says "state has fallen"
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article "2026 Albanian student protests" was created about 26 hours ago and has had 25 edits from roughly 11 accounts. None were reverts, but there has been some cleanup. The largest recent edit (rev 1381232477) adds a 14 October entry: about 1,000 protesters set fire to a government building and at least two banks, attributed to Reuters. It also says the riots reached their 7th straight day, with about 295 injured, 186 of them police, and protesters in Rinia Park prying up paving stones to throw. That figure is attributed to a BBC article dated 20 October. A Reactions section quotes PM Edi Rama on 18 October saying "The state has fallen" and calling it a "well coordinated attack". Other edits reorganise the infobox so the Opportunity Party, Lëvizja Bashkë and Lëvizja Shqipëria Bëhet are listed as supporters, with Albanian-language sources linking them to protests over Zvërnec that began in May (rev 1381233251). Other edits remove a live-blog line ("crazy fight… in Sheshi Skenderbej, Right Now") (rev 1381233400) and an image an admin called a licence failure or AI-generated, removed "again" (rev 1381234286). That points to eyewitness-style edits and quality problems, not vandalism. Caveats: I have not checked the cited Reuters and BBC articles. The casualty numbers and Rama quote come from a single editor's "wip" edit. No other-language versions of the page are in the graph.

briefs.headline: Albania student riots: en-wiki adds Rama refusing to resign; protests framed as 'Flamingo Revolution'
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article "2026 Albanian student protests" keeps filling in the timeline, mostly through one editor (Hduensixojnrwjzz). Rev 1381237190 adds a 15 October entry citing Reuters: PM Edi Rama rejected calls to resign as clashes went on, though he said he was willing to talk about rising education costs. Rev 1381238882, labelled "Finished wip (up to 18 Oct)", adds "rubber pellets" to what police used, alongside tear gas and water cannon. It also says the unrest has run "since 13 October" and ties it to the wider "Flamingo Revolution", with daily protests in Tirana since 31 May. That movement was set off by resort projects on Sazan Island and the Zvërnec coast linked to Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump, citing DW. Admin DMacks's edit (rev 1381237671) only removed maintenance tags and a see-also link. There were no reverts on this page, so this is not an edit war. The earlier figures still stand: day 7 of clashes and about 295 injured, 186 of them police (attributed to BBC). Caveats: I haven't checked the cited Reuters, BBC or DW articles, almost all new content comes from one editor, and the graph has no other-language versions of the page to cross-check against. The Prince Rupert's drop and potassium permanganate edits are unrelated routine fixes.

briefs.headline: Russian talk-show article 'Вопрос ребром' gets maintenance tags; anti-vandal bot reverts once
briefs.summary: The Russian Wikipedia article on the talk show 'Вопрос ребром' got six edits from two temporary accounts and the anti-vandal bot EyeBot. They were adding and re-adding maintenance templates: a 'no illustration/poster' tag and an empty 'Seasons and episodes' section marked {{Пустой раздел}} ("empty section"). EyeBot automatically undid one temp account's additions because of their ML score (ORES 0.62), not because the content was harmful. The same account then put the empty section back (rev 155688714), and a second temp account put the poster tag back (rev 155688744). There is no new factual content, no other language versions involved and no sign of a real-world event. It's formatting work, and the bot revert is a false positive rather than an edit war.

briefs.headline: Russian talk-show page 'Вопрос ребром': tag work continues, one 'See also' link undone
briefs.summary: This is still routine maintenance on the Russian Wikipedia article about the talk show 'Вопрос ребром'. It's on the same page as the routine story we're already tracking. Temporary account ~2026-55836-54 re-added the 'no poster image' tag to the infobox (rev 155688744). The same account then added a 'See also' section linking to [[MC Taxi]] (rev 155688809). The edit summary named the 'Резонансные выпуски' (notable episodes) section, but that section got no new text. Within a minute, experienced editor Skepsiz undid the link (rev 155688828), saying the linked article doesn't exist and its notability is doubtful. One undo isn't an edit war. No new facts were added, no other language versions changed, and nothing points to a real-world event. MC Taxi might be connected to a recent episode, but the edits give no evidence of that.

briefs.headline: Not a story: Nathan Tella vandalism and American Bitcoin ownership claim, linked only by a patroller
briefs.summary: The only thing tying these two pages together is the anti-vandalism patroller Materialscientist, who reverted unrelated edits on both pages within a few minutes of each other. There is no business or sports connection. On Nathan Tella, a temporary account added a made-up claim ("scoring 5 goals in 5 minutes against Bayern Munich") and then garbled the infobox stats (goals1 = 999, national goals = 900, years like "202222"). Both edits were reverted, by Materialscientist and then KuyaMoHirowo. On American Bitcoin, a different temporary account added that the company "was started, and trademarked by Christopher Connor in 2014. Eric Trump stole it". Materialscientist reverted that. Minutes later, an account named ChristopherJohnConnor added a softer version to the History section ("founded in 2014 by Christopher Connor, and taken in March 2025 by Eric Trump…"). That edit had not been reverted when I checked. It looks like a single person with a conflict of interest pushing an unsourced claim, not a news event, though I can't confirm the two accounts are the same person. Nothing points to a real-world development behind either page.

briefs.headline: Not a story: Nathan Tella vandalism, unsourced American Bitcoin claim; no new edits
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity since the earlier brief on these pages. The graph shows the same seven edits, and the latest is KuyaMoHirowo's revert on Nathan Tella. The only link between the two pages is patroller Materialscientist, who reverted unrelated edits on each. On Nathan Tella, a temporary account added a made-up line saying he "won a Bundesliga title… after scoring 5 goals in 5 minutes against Bayern Munich", then tampered with the infobox, and both edits were reverted. On American Bitcoin, a temporary account wrote that the company was "trademarked by Christopher Connor in 2014. Eric Trump stole it". Materialscientist reverted that. An account named ChristopherJohnConnor then rewrote the History section to say the company was "founded in 2014 by Christopher Connor, and taken in March 2025 by Eric Trump". That rewrite cites only the existing Wired source, which doesn't support it, and the graph shows no revert yet. This looks like an unsourced claim pushed by someone with a personal stake (the account is named after the person it credits), not a news event. The remaining open question is whether patrollers will remove that History edit.

briefs.headline: Callina Liang page: juvenile 'Chun-Li thighs' edits removed, page protected
briefs.summary: This is minor vandalism, not a news event. The 'Street Fighter' (2026) press cycle seems to be drawing attention to Callina Liang, the actress playing Chun-Li. Gadfium, an experienced editor, removed a sentence citing a Barstool Sports blog that said Liang "added 3 inches to her thighs" for the role, calling the source unreliable (rev 1381102757). A temporary account then added "thick legged" to the lead's description of Chun-Li (1381109545). ClueBot NG reverted it within seconds, and Gadfium then added a page-protection icon (1381112273), which means the page was semi-protected. There are no substantive biographical changes and nothing in other languages. A promotional or news hook for the film is likely behind the attention, but the edits don't confirm one.

briefs.headline: Fievel Goes West soundtrack page: patroller reverts unsourced Intrada reissue text
briefs.summary: This is routine page patrol, not an edit war. Over about 5 minutes, a temporary account (~2026-54338-41) made two additions to the enwiki article on the 1991 An American Tail: Fievel Goes West soundtrack. The first (+107) added "Intrada Records (2026)" to the label field and placeholder sections. The second (+5288) pasted what reads word for word like a label press release ("Intrada announces an expanded 2-CD set of James Horner's score... View the album trailer here."), along with a full track list for CD 1. Patroller Discospinster used Huggle to revert both edits for lacking a reliable source. The pasted text is promotional and probably copied from elsewhere, which also explains the large churn. The only real-world point is that Intrada may have announced an expanded 2-CD reissue of Horner's score. That is a minor niche release, and I haven't checked it outside Wikipedia. Only one page, one language and two editors are involved, with no back-and-forth so far.

briefs.headline: Kate, Princess of Wales page: vandalism spree reverted, no new edits since the restore
briefs.summary: This story covers the same 5 edits as the tracked vandalism story on the English Wikipedia article about Catherine, Princess of Wales. Querying the page's full edit history found nothing after MSincccc's restore (rev 1381125722). The account Ana Maria Gallizi Debetio emptied infobox fields and changed the royal navbox to read "HIGHNESS ANA MARIA GALES OF UNITED KINGDOM" (rev 1381125264, diff read). ClueBot NG reverted that. The account then gutted the infobox again and blanked about 175k bytes. MSincccc restored the bot's clean version, which brought back the title, image, spouse, children and mother fields and the article body (diff read). No other languages or pages moved, and nothing points to a real-world event. I'd fold this into the existing story rather than treat it as a new one. The Scout's "no reverts" reading came from the revert flag, which isn't set on these edits, but the edit summaries show two restorations.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Kate, Princess of Wales page; article blanked, then restored
briefs.summary: The large churn (~351k bytes) on the English Wikipedia article on Catherine, Princess of Wales comes from vandalism followed by cleanup. It is not a rewrite and not a news event. One registered account, Ana Maria Gallizi Debetio, made a series of edits that emptied infobox fields (title, image, birth date and place, spouse, children) and stuffed the royal-family navbox with the text "HIGHNESS ANA MARIA GALES OF UNITED KINGDOM" (rev 1381125264). ClueBot NG reverted that edit. The same account then gutted the infobox again (rev 1381125485) and blanked about 175k bytes of the article (rev 1381125613). Within about a minute, MSincccc restored the bot's clean version (+175k, rev 1381125722). There were 3 editors and the page is back to normal. Nothing points to a real-world development, and no other pages or languages are involved.

briefs.headline: Cube film series page: edit war over a release table, no news hook
briefs.summary: The activity on the English "Cube (film series)" page is an edit war over formatting. It does not point to any real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-56041-90) made about 20 small edits building a table of the four films: Cube, Cube 2: Hypercube, Cube Zero, and the 2021 Japanese remake. The table lists release dates, directors, writers and producers. It adds no new film, announcement or source (rev 1381068430, 1381078695). AriuCH and then Untamed1910 removed the table, calling it block evasion by the blocked user Didaka90. The temporary account restored it twice, with edit summaries that insulted the other editors (rev 1381080244). The big churn number comes from the same ~1.2k-byte table being added and removed again and again, not from new content. Whether this is really Didaka90 is the editors' claim and I haven't checked it, but the pattern points to a dispute that admins will handle, not a story.

briefs.headline: Cube film series page: block-evasion edit war over a films table, no news hook
briefs.summary: Still no real-world event here. There have been no new edits since Untamed1910's revert (rev 1381080244), and the article now reads as it did before the table was added. A temporary account (~2026-56041-90) spent about 20 edits building a table of the four Cube films: release dates, directors, writers and producers. The first draft (rev 1381068430) had empty rows plus a 2021 row with leftover details from an unrelated 2008 film, which were later replaced. The table adds nothing new, and the remake sentence and its Variety source were already in the article. AriuCH and then Untamed1910 removed the table as block evasion by Didaka90. AriuCH also undid an earlier edit by a different temporary account, ~2026-51961-07 (rev 1381078274), which suggests the same person may have come back more than once. The temporary account put the table back twice, with summaries attacking AriuCH (rev 1381079626). A correction: the previous brief said the insults were in rev 1381080244, but that is Untamed1910's revert. I haven't checked the sockpuppet claim itself.

briefs.headline: Arabic Wikipedia pastry war spreads: Tunisia claim now pushed on 'Mechmoum' too
briefs.summary: There is no real-world event here. The Arabic Wikipedia dispute over Maghrebi sweets that began on مقروض (maqrout) has spread to a second article, مشموم (mechmoum, an almond-paste sweet). The same four editors are involved on both pages, so the scout is right that this is one story, not a new one. On مشموم, Sarra69 changed the lead from "a type of Algerian sweet" (linked to حلويات جزائرية and sourced to an Algiers cookbook) to "Tunisian sweets" (revs 77025157 and 77025182, whose comment says "Tunisian sweets, jasmine mechmoum"). Each attempt was rolled back, by Kenshiro Taisho, Doaa970 and finally أوس (rev 77025188), and the graph shows about five attempts on this page. On مقروض, Sarra69 made a seventh and larger edit (rev 77025135, -791 bytes, comment "Aghlabid maqrout"). It again calls the pastry "Tunisian" in the lead. The diff was cut off, but أوس's rollback (rev 77025189) restores the food infobox, so that edit seems to have removed the infobox, which held the "unconfirmed" origin. Both pages are back on the neutral or Algerian wording, and the graph shows no edits after about 1792442993. I didn't check talk pages, page protection or any block on Sarra69.

briefs.headline: Arabic Wikipedia pastry war: Sarra69 tries again on both pages, reverted again; fifth editor joins
briefs.summary:

The scout said there were no reverts this window, which is wrong. Both new attempts were reverted, though the graph's revert flag is not set on either.

- **مشموم:** Sarra69 changed the lead from "Algerian sweets" to "Tunisian sweets" and removed the food infobox with its image captioned "gâteau algérien" (rev 77025228, -94). أوس rolled it back (rev 77025345).
- **مقروض:** Sarra69 changed the lead from "a Maghrebi pastry" to "a Tunisian pastry" (rev 77025252, -32). A fifth editor, بداح, undid this as an unsourced pending change (rev 77025305, comment "تعديل بلا مصدر", "unsourced edit").

Both pages are back on the neutral (maqrout) or Algerian (mechmoum) wording. The graph shows nothing after 1792443779. Across the two pages Sarra69 has now been reverted roughly 15 times by five editors in about 80 minutes. The rollbacks and the pending-changes review suggest the pages are watched, but I didn't check talk pages, page protection, or whether Sarra69 has been blocked or warned.

briefs.headline: Arabic pastry war: temporary account repeats Tunisia edit on 'Mechmoum' after Sarra69 rolled back
briefs.summary:
There is still no real-world event. This remains the Tunisia-vs-Algeria origin dispute on the Arabic Wikipedia articles مقروض (maqrout) and مشموم (mechmoum). The scout's "no reverts" is wrong again: there were two more rollbacks this window. The graph's revert flag is still not set on them.

- **مشموم:** Sarra69 changed the lead from "Algerian sweets" to "Tunisian sweets" again and removed the infobox with the "gâteau algérien" image (rev 77025400). أوس rolled it back (rev 77025539).
- **New account on مشموم:** About four minutes later, a temporary account (~2026-55998-36) made the same change (rev 77025607, -107). It drops the infobox and changes the lead to "Tunisian sweets", now linked to a "Gâteau tunisien" page. This is the account's only edit in the graph.
- **مقروض:** Sarra69 made another infobox edit, origin "unconfirmed"→Tunisia and creator "unknown"→Kairouan (rev 77025453). أوس rolled it back (rev 77025480).
- **أوس's content edits on مقروض:** أوس removed a large block of citations from the lead (rev 77025415, -1182, comment "مصدر يكفي", "one source is enough"). أوس then added "المقروط" as an alternate name in the lead, cited to a Sky News Arabia piece on Algerian maqrout (rev 77025491, comment "التسمية الجزائرية", "the Algerian naming"). So the reverting side is also shaping the content.

Current state: as of the last graph edit (ts 1792444731), مقروض is on the neutral wording, but مشموم shows the Tunisian version from the temporary account. Matching content and timing suggest Sarra69 may be continuing while logged out or through another account. That is an inference only: I can't link the accounts, and I didn't check talk pages, page protection or blocks.

briefs.headline: Arabic 'Maqrout' origin edit war escalates: Tunisia claim re-added five times, now stands

Editor Sarra69 keeps changing the infobox origin from "غير مؤكد" (unconfirmed) to Tunisia and the creator from "unknown" to Kairouan (revs 77024745, 77024919, each about -31 bytes). I didn't check the talk page or whether page protection or a block followed. The lead's sources still name Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, which suggests editors agree on a shared regional dish and the single-country origin is the contested point.

briefs.headline: Arabic 'Maqrout' pastry article: origin claim tilted to Tunisia, reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is not a real-world event. It is a small dispute over national origin on the Arabic Wikipedia article for maqrout/maqroud (مقروض), a semolina-and-date pastry eaten across the Maghreb. Editor Sarra69 changed the infobox origin from "unconfirmed" to Tunisia and the creator from "unknown" to Kairouan, and relabelled the caption "traditional Algerian maqrout" as Tunisian (rev 77023997). That edit also removed about 4.6 KB. The diff output was cut off, so I can't confirm what was removed, but the visible lead cites several Algerian sources that are likely candidates. Editor أوس undid it as a pending change (rev 77024437, +4629). Sarra69 then re-applied the Tunisia origin and caption changes in a smaller edit (rev 77024689, -33), and Doaa970 rolled that back (rev 77024700). The article is back to neutral wording. There was no blanking or vandalism, but this is the start of a Tunisia-vs-Algeria edit war, and the "very large churn" is just one removal and its revert.

briefs.headline: Arabic pastry war: Sarra69 tries again on both pages; sixth editor reverts
briefs.summary:

briefs.headline: Hiroshi Tsuchida article: only cosmetic fixes; death facts unchanged
briefs.summary: This adds to the existing story on the death of Japanese actor and voice actor Hiroshi Tsuchida (土田大). Nothing new has happened. The only edits since the last brief are two small ones by Mr. Toku on English Wikipedia. Rev 1381129950 changed "NinjaBlue" to "Ninja Blue" in three filmography entries. I still haven't confirmed whether the wrong "1954 births" category is on the English page. These diffs don't touch it.

briefs.headline: Voice actor Hiroshi Tsuchida's death on Oct 11 confirmed across Japanese, Chinese, English wikis
briefs.summary: This update adds to the existing story. Japanese Wikipedia had the death about 22 minutes before English did. Editor ロングベンチ (edit comment: "edit due to death") gave his death as 11 October 2026 from heart failure, aged 54 (ja rev 111447492). The edit cites two sources: an Oricon News article from 20 October, and an obituary notice on the website of his agency, 81 Produce, archived the same day. That notice says he died on 11 October of heart failure. An unregistered editor on Chinese Wikipedia then added the same date and cause, citing the same Oricon URL (zh rev 95180327). On English Wikipedia, the date mismatch from the last brief has been fixed. Sanpalm changed the lead from 20 October, which was the date the death was announced, to 11 October (rev 1381125780), so it now agrees with the infobox. Crboyer corrected the access date on the citation (rev 1381126094). One error remains: an unregistered editor added the category "1954 births" in rev 1381125630, but he was born in 1972. This is a small categorisation mistake, not vandalism. There are no reverts, and independent editors in three languages agree, so this is a real death being recorded, and the article updates are now routine cleanup.

briefs.headline: Hiroshi Tsuchida added to English 'Deaths in 2026' list under 11 October
briefs.summary: This update adds to the existing story; it does not reveal a new event. Crboyer added Japanese actor Hiroshi Tsuchida to the 11 October section of English Wikipedia's "Deaths in 2026" list (rev 1381126612). The entry gives his age as 54, his roles in Kakuranger, Attack on Titan and Soulcalibur III, and heart failure as the cause. It cites the same Oricon News article dated 20 October that the biography already uses. The two later edits to the list only tidied the entry: Crboyer fixed broken italics markup (1381126763), and Rusted AutoParts turned the citation into a bare link marked as a Japanese-language source (1381127808). On the biography, Sanpalm changed his occupation in the infobox from "Voice actor" to "Actor, Voice actor" (1381127164). The list's date, age and cause match the biography and the Japanese and Chinese articles described in the last brief. There have been no reverts. No later edit in the graph removes the wrong "1954 births" category (he was born in 1972), so it is probably still there, though I haven't checked the live page. This is routine follow-up work on a death that has already been confirmed.

briefs.headline: Japanese voice actor Hiroshi Tsuchida reported dead at 54, Wikipedia edits say
briefs.summary: Three registered editors updated the English Wikipedia article on Hiroshi Tsuchida within about 12 minutes, marking him as dead. Tsuchida, of 81 Produce, played Ninja Blue in Kakuranger and voiced Grisha Jaeger in Attack on Titan. Imranfreak added a death date of 11 October 2026 to the infobox (rev 1381124616). Another editor switched the article to past tense and changed years active to 1994–2026 (1381124964). Imranfreak then added a sentence saying he died of heart failure at 54 and that his agency announced the death on 20 October, citing an Oricon News article dated 2026-10-20 whose headline reports his death from heart failure (1381125224). There are no reverts and the editors agree, which looks like a real death being recorded, not vandalism. There are two problems. Bobasli's later edit put 20 October, the announcement date, as the death date in the lead (1381125512), so the article now contradicts its own infobox. And the graph has no other-language pages to check against, including Japanese Wikipedia, and I haven't seen the Oricon source myself.

briefs.headline: Horrid Henry hit by second vandal: "Nicholas Cruise" accounts spamming a YouTube link
briefs.summary: Still vandalism on English Wikipedia, and there's no real-world event behind it. Something new has started on "Horrid Henry (TV series)". After the temporary-account vandal who swaps words in article titles (see earlier briefs), a run of numbered registered accounts showed up: Nicholas Cruise, Nicholas Cruise1, 2 and 3. Each one pasted the same YouTube link (watch?v=DthG-J9HRko) at the top of the article, with comments like "Please Watch Video Thank You" and "Please Watch Masterpiece" (revs 1381231039, 1381231959). They also hit Horrid Henry, Horrid Henry: The Movie, Francesca Simon, ITV and several pages about children's or educational TV. Knitsey, Inzessin, 420yeahh, SimpleObjects-9ei and MakaylaHippo1998 reverted every edit, so none of the spam is live as of the last edit in the graph. These look like disposable accounts made one after another by a single person. Their method (link spam) is different from the title-swap vandal's, so I can't say whether the two are the same person. I mostly agree with the scout's note, with two corrections. Montrose, Colorado had separate juvenile vandalism from temporary accounts, such as "this is boring...i hate my job" added to the lead (rev 1381231607). It was reverted, and nothing connects it to the Henry vandals. On Nana (manga), a temporary account and then the new account Ihoopey made the same small wording change ("stage name" to "mononym", revs 1381230948, 1381231929). That looks like good faith, not vandalism, and it's probably one person. Separately, on Paulo Retre, AvonRSC has added the Rowville Secondary College line a third time, now with a citation to the school's own website (rev 1381231106). It hasn't been reverted yet, so a slow dispute over that line may continue.

briefs.headline: Horrid Henry TV page protected after link spam; Tina Batson edits are a separate birth-year dispute

That means the page has been protected, the same step taken earlier on Pororo. I disagree with the scout on Tina Batson, a Venezuelan pageant contestant: it is not part of the Henry vandalism. Equivalent-Text2598 reverted the first change and Inzessin the second, noting that the cited Globovisión source says 1999 (rev 1381232670). This is a small, unsourced factual dispute, not juvenile vandalism. The account's only other edit was to Miss Earth 2026, which fits a pageant follower rather than the Henry vandals. Nothing new happened on Montrose, Nana (manga) or Paulo Retre since the last brief. There are no other language versions involved. The Batson birth-year change may come back, but it isn't news.

briefs.headline: Pororo article title vandalized and reverted; Retre school edit unrelated, routine

briefs.headline: Pororo article vandalism resumes from a second temporary account; no news event

briefs.headline: Paulo Retre: unsourced school detail added twice, removed twice

briefs.headline: Pororo page protected after rotating-account vandal; same pattern jumps to Horrid Henry
briefs.summary: This is still one vandal working through disposable temporary accounts on English Wikipedia, not a news event. After the earlier ~2026-56488-42 and ~2026-56102-25 edits, two more temporary accounts kept changing the title in the opening line of "Pororo the Little Penguin". ~2026-56001-30 changed it to "Pororo the Little MCE89" with the comment "reverting an admin" (rev 1381230045). ~2026-56078-28 then changed it to "Pororo the Little MCE" with the comment "lta" (rev 1381230361). Both edits were reverted (rev 1381230799). The reused words "Astra" and "Staraction" and the fake revert comments strongly suggest the same person is behind all five accounts, but nothing in the graph proves it. briefs.headline: France U-21 page: year-old qualifier results pruned, briefly reverted, then removed again

Chelsdog then deleted the same 1,497 bytes again with the note "over one year" (rev 1381263060), meaning the results are more than a year old and no longer belong in the recent-results section. That is a common cleanup on national-team pages, and the edit dates fit those October matches being about a year old. The diffs only move the results around and don't change them, and no new result or squad news shows up. The second removal hasn't been challenged so far, so this looks like a one-time misunderstanding rather than an edit war. That could change if TonySt reverts again.

briefs.headline: Wu Kangmin (吳康民) zhwiki article gets routine early-life expansion, not death news
briefs.summary: Three registered editors (Gnonich, Will629, 919sth.) made seven edits to the Chinese Wikipedia biography of Wu Kangmin, the Hong Kong educator and longtime principal and supervisor of Pui Kiu Middle School. Almost all of the churn comes from one edit by Gnonich (+1640, rev 95148194), which expands his early life with sourced material: his birth in Shantou, his family's role in the anti-Japanese resistance, the anti-Japanese drama troupe he organised at age 12, his entry to Sun Yat-sen University at 16, and his alma mater Huilai No.1 Middle School. The sources are his own Wen Wei Po columns and a 2012 ATV/Chung Hwa book. The other edits are small: Will629 changed a wikilink (to 中國抗日戰爭) and added categories for Hong Kong educators and secondary-school principals. 919sth. added the "Hong Kong centenarians" category and removed it about three minutes later, which looks like a category correction, not a clash. None of the diffs I read add a death date, obituary wording, or any recent-event source, so there is no evidence of a death or other news hook. This looks like ordinary article improvement. I didn't read the two smallest edits (+4, +32), and I couldn't check the current lead because the page summary didn't load.

briefs.headline: Wu Kangmin (吳康民) zhwiki bio gets sourced early-life expansion; no news event
briefs.summary: This story covers the same burst of 7 edits as the earlier routine brief: three registered editors (Gnonich, Will629, 919sth.) working on the Chinese Wikipedia biography of Hong Kong educator Wu Kangmin, long-time principal of Pui Kiu Middle School. briefs.headline: French student protests: en-wiki says Lyon has joined Paris in night curfews

I don't count it as evidence of a real retirement event, though a Lufthansa A340-600 farewell could plausibly be what prompted it. The two reverts are routine anti-vandalism, not an edit war. When I checked, the latest vandal edit had not yet been reverted.

briefs.headline: Unrelated vandalism on Airbus A340, Dallas and Scott Novak pages, linked only by patrol bots
briefs.summary: These three en-wiki pages are tied together only by the anti-vandal patrollers ClueBot NG and Cannolis. No vandal account touched more than one page, so this is coincidence, not coordination. Dallas: Kevinvalles209 blanked large parts of the article twice (−33.5k, then −65.4k bytes), and ClueBot NG and Cannolis restored it both times. The scout's "no reverts" note is wrong: those restorations are reverts, even though they aren't flagged as such. Scott Novak (an NFL referee): temporary account ~2026-55776-01 replaced the lead with "sucks at being a referee", then added the nickname "holding on the offense". Both edits were reverted. That's typical fan anger after a game and hints that he worked a recent NFL game, but nothing here confirms which one. Airbus A340: on top of the vandalism in the existing story, Emirloves67chickennuggets added a farewell "editor message" thanking the A340-600 and naming "TC-JDM" (a Turkish registration). ClueBot NG reverted it. This one user's sentiment is weak evidence of a real A340-600 retirement, possibly at Turkish Airlines, and I can't confirm it. Recommend folding this into the existing A340 vandalism story. Dallas and Novak are separate low-value vandalism with no news event.

briefs.headline: Korean Wikipedia gets new article on Sept. 21 DMZ mine blast that injured three ROK soldiers
briefs.summary: On ~Oct 20, 2026, user Legacy of Justinian created a new kowiki article (+6,087 bytes, rev 42683042) on the "25th Infantry Division DMZ mine explosion." It says that on 21 Sept 2026, in the DMZ in Yeoncheon county, Gyeonggi province, a ROK Army reconnaissance team was clearing a path ahead of a UN Command site inspection when a mine went off. A second blast followed as others moved in to evacuate the injured; three soldiers were hurt. Citing a Ministry of National Defense/JCS joint task-force final report (korea.kr), the article says the mine was a North Korean-made plastic anti-personnel mine planted south of the MDL, and Seoul calls that deliberate. It also says Kim Yo Jong called the incident staged and threatened to reinforce against the 21st Division. A follow-up edit (rev 42683047) adds that the team had 3 officers/NCOs and 15 enlisted. The editor also added a DPRK military-incidents navbox to the article on North Korea's involvement in the Ukraine war (rev 42683068). That edit is housekeeping, not a separate development. This is a write-up of an incident about a month old, sourced to Korean press and government briefings, not breaking news. Only 2 editors appear (not the 4 the scout noted), there are no reverts, and no other-language pages have moved. I have not independently confirmed the facts beyond the article's cited sources.

briefs.headline: Patroller reverts two unrelated POV edits on Manusmriti and US racial unrest pages
briefs.summary: These two pages are not one story. The only thing connecting them is the patroller Tankishguy, who undid one edit on each page within about 11 minutes. On Manusmriti, temporary account ~2026-56112-88 added about 2,170 bytes of unsourced advocacy to the Controversies section (rev 1381113538). It argued that the text's offensive verses were inserted later "during the era of Muslim rule", and recast sati and the Shudra category in its own terms. The edit summary complains that earlier attempts had been removed, so this person has probably tried before, but it is a one-person push, not a two-sided edit war. Tankishguy reverted it about 2 minutes later (rev 1381113891). On United States racial unrest (2020–2023), a different temporary account, ~2026-56354-02, changed "murder of George Floyd" to "overdose death of george flloyd" (rev 1381115522). This was plain vandalism, reverted within a minute as such (rev 1381115583). Neither edit points to anything happening in the world, and no other languages or editors are involved.

briefs.headline: NZ 2026 election polling page: cleanup edits around recent Labour-led polls
briefs.summary:
This latest burst on the English Wikipedia page "Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election" is housekeeping. No new polls were added. AusYou and a temporary account (~2026-56089-54) made about eight small edits (deltas between −2 and +138 bytes), and none were reverts. The edits:
- Reordered the Whakaata Māori–Curia Te Tai Tokerau electorate poll (5–15 Oct, n=500, Te Ao Māori News, 20 Oct) so the party vote row comes first. That poll has Labour leading the party vote 27 to 25, and its source headline credits Hūhana Lyndon with leading the electorate.
- Corrected a publication name in the Ikaroa-Rāwhiti poll citation.
- Filled empty electorate table cells with n/a.
- Adjusted a 9–19 Oct national poll (n=1,458): AusYou changed the Labour lead row from 28.7 to 29.7, then put it back to 28.7. That is one editor correcting their own change, not an edit war.
The polls already on the page suggest Labour is narrowly ahead in mid-October 2026 polling, but this batch of edits adds no new information.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki biography of Stuttgart sculptor Herbert Gebauer (d. 2010) gets routine cleanup
briefs.summary: This is a newly created German Wikipedia article about Herbert Gebauer (1925–2010), a sculptor from Stuttgart-Sillenbuch. It was moved out of draft status, and veteran editors are now doing the usual cleanup a new page gets. Lutheraner swapped the "Baustelle" (under construction) tag for a quality-check request that asks for relevance to be confirmed. AHZ tidied the wording and formatting of the opening section, Kurator71 added categories (born 1925, died 2010, Stuttgart sculptor), and M2k added biographical metadata (Personendaten), a sort key and authority data. None of the edits mentions anything new: Gebauer died in 2010, and the main source cited is a 2024 publication from a private collection of his work. There are no reverts, no disputes and no activity in other languages, so this doesn't point to anything happening in the world. The open question is only whether the article will be kept, since the relevance check could lead to a deletion debate.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on sculptor Herbert Gebauer (1925–2010) still getting routine cleanup
briefs.summary: This is still the newly created German Wikipedia biography of Herbert Gebauer, a Stuttgart-Sillenbuch sculptor who died in 2010. Nothing in the text adds a new event: the death date is still 4 April 2010, and the main source is still a 2024 publication from a private collection of his work. The only open question is whether the article is kept after the relevance check.

briefs.headline: Boca Juniors win 3–1 away at Vasco da Gama to reach Copa Sudamericana 2026 final
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked Boca story on es-wiki "Copa Sudamericana 2026". The new edit, by AMBlanco25 (rev 175927508), adds the scorers for the semifinal leg: Rodríguez (66') for the home side, and Di Lollo (4'), Merentiel (34') and Paredes (88') for the visitors, who are Boca. That matches VicenteTGO99's result line of 1:3 (rev 175927496), the same edit that turned on the Final section with Boca Juniors (ARG) as the home side. One detail doesn't add up: two Boca goals came before half-time (4' and 34'), but the half-time score is listed as 0:1, so one of those entries is probably a typo. The aggregate score, the first-leg result and the final's opponent are still not confirmed in the edits. There are three registered editors, no reverts, no other languages and no sign of vandalism.

briefs.headline: Boca Juniors reach Copa Sudamericana 2026 final after beating Vasco da Gama, per es-wiki
briefs.summary: Three registered es-wiki editors made six non-reverted edits within about five minutes to "Copa Sudamericana 2026", filling in the result of a semifinal. VicenteTGO99 entered a semifinal result of 1:3 (0:1 at half-time), put Boca Juniors (ARG) into the final slot of the bracket, and un-commented the "Final" section, listing Boca as the home side (revs 175927496, 175927460). AMBlanco25 listed Vasco da Gama (BRA) as an eliminated semifinalist (175927459), and Lukas OG bolded Boca as the winner of the tie (175927493). Together the edits mean Boca Juniors knocked out Vasco da Gama and advanced to the final. The bracket's leg scores are hard to read: they look like 1–2 and 3–3, but it isn't clear which team each number belongs to, so the aggregate and how the tie was decided (for example on penalties) are not confirmed. The final's opponent isn't filled in, and no other-language pages are linked in the graph. The editors agree with each other and nothing suggests vandalism. This looks like a routine but real sports result.

briefs.headline: 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs page: wording edits undone in one revert, no new results
briefs.summary: Two temporary-account editors made four small edits to the English article on the 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs. Registered editor Conyo14 undid all four in one revert, giving the reason "unnecessary edits/unexplained removal of content". The diffs show rewording, not news. One editor kept changing the trivia line in the Vegas–Colorado Western Conference final about the last sweep of a Presidents' Trophy winner. The other rewrote the first-round write-ups for the Lightning–Canadiens and Penguins–Flyers series, and that rewrite added errors: it said Pittsburgh and Philadelphia had 106 points (the article says 98) and named Tampa Bay as winning the Metropolitan Division tiebreaker. The text saying Vegas swept Colorado and reached the Stanley Cup Final (Game 4 on May 26, 2026, citing NHL.com) was already in the article before these edits, so it isn't new here. This was one revert with no back-and-forth, on one page in one language, so it isn't an edit war or a real-world development.

briefs.headline: 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs page: wording edits undone in one revert, no new results
briefs.summary: Nothing has been edited on the English article on the 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs since the last brief. The latest revision is still Conyo14's revert (rev 1381209128), which undid four small edits by two temporary-account editors, giving the reason "unnecessary edits/unexplained removal of content". I read the first-round edit (rev 1381208555). It rewrote the Lightning–Canadiens and Penguins–Flyers write-ups, adding tiebreaker scores and two errors: it gave Pittsburgh and Philadelphia 106 points (the article says 98) and said Tampa Bay won the Metropolitan Division tiebreaker. The revert put the earlier text back. The text saying Vegas swept Colorado in the Western Conference final was already in the article before these edits and was not changed. This is one revert on one page in one language, with no back-and-forth, so it is routine upkeep rather than an edit war or a new real-world development.

briefs.headline: Lua Blanco's death spreads to en-wiki, which adds unsourced 'intestinal cancer' detail
briefs.summary: The death of Lua Blanco, the Rebelde actress, already tracked on pt-wiki, has now reached her English Wikipedia page. Five accounts made six edits there in about 37 minutes. The edits were additive, with no reverts, so this is not an edit war. Davi270 added an infobox death date of 18 Oct 2026, first in Portuguese and then reformatted it (revs 1380896699, 1380896838). Plbds rewrote the lead to "March 5, 1987 – October 18, 2026" and "was" (rev 1380899363). Strattonsmith fixed tenses, and in rev 1380900454 linked an already-present sentence saying she died at 39 "after months fighting against intestinal cancer". A temporary account added Rio de Janeiro as the place of death and updated the short description (rev 1380900884). Meanwhile, Leone Melo on pt-wiki set the infobox cause of death to "câncer" and cleaned up the tenses (rev 73240578). The two-language agreement, and pt-wiki's earlier citations to CNN Brasil and Quem, support the death being real. Caveats: none of the en-wiki edits I read add a news source; the new lead text reuses an old Caras profile ref. The "intestinal" cancer site appears only on en-wiki, while pt-wiki says the site was not disclosed. I did not see who first added that sentence, so treat it as unverified. The Rio place of death is still unsourced in both languages.

briefs.headline: Lua Blanco death: en-wiki and pt-wiki shift to cleanup, no one disputes the death
briefs.summary: This follow-up covers five edits to Lua Blanco's pages since our last brief. All are housekeeping, and none adds or removes facts about her death. On en-wiki, a temporary account swapped Category:Living people for Category:2026 deaths (rev 1380901463). Another temporary account turned the infobox death date into the {{death date and age}} template, which gives 18 Oct 2026 with a birth date of 5 Mar 1987 (rev 1380901641). The first account also changed years_active from "2004–present" to "2004–" (rev 1380902326) and then undid its own edit a minute later. That is the "revert" the scout flagged; it is not a dispute. On pt-wiki, Daniel G Rego made a "-421 byte" pass that tidies citation templates and formatting without touching the death content (rev 73240663). Moving her into the 2026 deaths category means editors are treating the death as settled in both languages. The earlier caveats still stand. The en-wiki "intestinal cancer" detail has no source. The Rio de Janeiro place of death has no source in either language. We have not opened the CNN Brasil or Quem articles that pt-wiki cites. Ana Rita Sithole appears in this dossier but is a separate tracked story (s_7fba917c) and is not covered here.

briefs.headline: Lua Blanco: en-wiki death claim reverted as unsourced, then restored still without a source
briefs.summary: This is the first pushback in this story. SuperFastSpellChecker rolled en-wiki back to an older revision from before the death, with the summary "Rv multiple edits without sources" (rev 1380902755). That removed the death date, the Rio de Janeiro place of death, the "1987–2026" short description and the past tense. About 3–7 minutes later the death came back. StarDeg re-added "March 5, 1987 - October 18, 2026" to the lead, though it still said "is" (rev 1380903071). Jkaharper then restored the infobox death date, "[[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil", years_active 2004–2026 and "was" (rev 1380903171). Neither restoring edit adds a news source, so the reverter's objection still stands on en-wiki. Nobody has reverted again yet. So far this is one challenge to sourcing, not a back-and-forth edit war, but it could flare up again. On pt-wiki the death is still cited to Quem and CNN Brasil. Individuo indigente changed the cancer line from "tumour site not disclosed" to "câncer no intestino" (intestinal cancer), still citing CNN Brasil (rev 73240698). The CNN headline says only "após câncer" (after cancer), so this may be en-wiki's unsourced claim moving into pt-wiki rather than new reporting. The same editor's other edits are cosmetic: infobox tweaks and adding a sister, Estrela Blanco (revs 73240708, 73240720). We have still not opened the Quem or CNN Brasil articles. The death looks real given the two cited outlets on pt-wiki, but the cancer site and place of death are still unverified.

briefs.headline: Lua Blanco: en-wiki dispute over death claim quiet; editors now only doing cleanup
briefs.summary: The scout's signal (a revert and 758 bytes of churn) mostly comes from edits we covered in our last brief: SuperFastSpellChecker's "unsourced" rollback and the restorations by StarDeg and Jkaharper. Since that brief there are two en-wiki edits we hadn't read, and neither one challenges the death. StarDeg changed the lead from "is" to "was", so it now reads "March 5, 1987 - October 18, 2026 ... was a Brazilian actress" (rev 1380903113). Seasider53, an experienced registered editor, copyedited the early-life section. He also removed the names of her non-notable siblings, citing WP:BLPPRIVACY, and left the death material in place (rev 1380904395). No one has reverted the death again since the rollback about 15 minutes earlier, so there is no edit war. Two caveats from earlier briefs still stand: en-wiki still has no news source for the death, and the "intestinal cancer" detail and Rio de Janeiro place of death have not been verified. pt-wiki still cites CNN Brasil and Quem, which supports the death itself being real.

briefs.headline: Unsourced claim of Brazilian actress Lua Blanco's death appears on pt-wiki
briefs.summary: Within about 3.5 minutes, four registered accounts edited the Portuguese Wikipedia page of Lua Blanco, the Brazilian actress and singer best known from the telenovela Rebelde, to report that she died. Lkjoker added "morte_data = 18/10/2026" to the infobox (rev 73240422). Letyffer then changed the lead from "é" to "era" (is → was) with the edit summary "ele morreu hoje 18/10/2026" ("he died today"; "ele" is the masculine pronoun) (rev 73240425). Neither edit cites a source, the dossier contains no edit to a "Mortes em 2026" category or any other related page, and no other language edition of the article (there are no SAME_AS pages) has moved. Diffs for the follow-up edits by Lustmoon and Assisensenga could not be fetched, and the graph does not flag any edit as a revert, but the summary of a sixth edit says Luiz79 undid Assisensenga's edit (rev 73240449, -32 bytes). This could be early reaction to real breaking news or a death hoax. Several accounts acting together point to news spreading, while the missing sources, the wrong pronoun and the undo point to a hoax. Treat as unverified: do not report the death without an outside source, and check whether the infobox death date survives.

briefs.headline: pt-wiki now cites CNN Brasil, Quem for death of 'Rebelde' actress Lua Blanco at 39
briefs.summary: Our earlier brief flagged an unsourced death claim. The claim has now firmed up. Nine registered pt-wiki editors made 13 edits in about 16 minutes, and none of them removed the death. Mjrocha2310 added that Blanco died on 18 Oct 2026, aged 39, "vítima de um câncer" (of cancer), citing a CNN Brasil article headlined "Morre Lua Blanco, estrela de 'Rebelde', aos 39 anos após câncer" (rev 73240484). Klebs1 added a "Morte" section citing Revista Quem ("Lua Blanco, a Roberta da novela 'Rebelde Brasil', morre aos 39 anos"). It says the cause was not disclosed, which contradicts the CNN Brasil citation (rev 73240521). Luiz79 changed the lead to give her death as Rio de Janeiro, 18 Oct 2026, and set her active years to 2004–2026 (rev 73240468). Abraão Feliciano formatted the infobox date with the {{Morte}} template (rev 73240461). Luiz79's earlier undo of Assisensenga (rev 73240441) wasn't a challenge to the death. Assisensenga had added the death date to an older version of the lead, and Luiz79 later added it himself. There is no edit war. Still uncertain: I could not open the cited URLs to confirm they exist. Mjrocha2310's text says cancer and Klebs1's says the cause wasn't disclosed. The Rio de Janeiro place of death has no source. No other language edition is linked in the graph.

briefs.headline: pt-wiki settles on cancer as cause of 'Rebelde' actress Lua Blanco's death
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to our developing brief, not a new story. Since that brief, one editor, Klebs1, has made three edits to Lua Blanco's Portuguese Wikipedia page. None is a revert, and no one else has edited. In rev 73240541, Klebs1 merged the two conflicting death passages into one. It says Blanco died on 18 Oct 2026, aged 39, citing Revista Quem. It then says she had been fighting a cancer found in recent months, with the tumour site not disclosed, citing CNN Brasil. The line saying the cause "was not disclosed" is gone, which resolves the contradiction we flagged earlier. Klebs1 then added the category "Mortes por câncer" (deaths from cancer) in rev 73240549, and shortened a section heading's year range to "2018–26" in rev 73240525. Still uncertain: we have not opened the CNN Brasil and Quem URLs, so we cannot confirm they exist or say what they report. The cancer detail now rests on one editor's reading of the CNN Brasil source. The Rio de Janeiro place of death is still unsourced, and no other language edition has picked up the story.

briefs.headline: Crown Jewel 2026 page: editors cut speculation that WWE may move event from Riyadh

The one edit that matters (rev 1381092140, -1,261 bytes) took out a "Security concerns" section. That section cited the "October 2026 attacks on Saudi airports" and "2026 Yemen offensives". That was one removal and one restoration, not yet an edit war. The page itself is routine event-card upkeep. The cut text hints at a bigger real-world story (attacks on Saudi airports, a possible relocation), but I can't find a page for those attacks anywhere in the graph, so the claim is unconfirmed here. Two diffs failed to load (JDC808, GodofDemonwars); both were small edits.

briefs.headline: Jamar, Gujarat: schoolboy vandalism by temporary account reverted twice

briefs.headline: Simple English 'Hello Kitty' article blanked repeatedly by one temporary account

It is not a real-world event or a content dispute. Over about 3.5 minutes the account made 7 edits deleting the article's body text in pieces (e.g. rev 11036545, -2.9k), and then blanked the whole page twice. briefs.headline: Simple English 'Hello Kitty' blanking vandalism continues; page restored for now
briefs.summary: This is still page-blanking vandalism by one temporary account (~2026-56234-44) on Simple English Wikipedia's Hello Kitty article. It is not a real-world event. briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on 19th-century Polish general Józef Rautenstrauch
briefs.summary: This is a new historical biography, not a news event. Asdrubal created the German Wikipedia stub "Józef Rautenstrauch" (rev 271439890, +1535 bytes). The stub describes a Polish general (1773–1842) who served under Józef Poniatowski in 1812 and at Leipzig, did not take part in the November Uprising of 1830, and then joined the Russian army. Mai 1773" to just "1773" (rev 271440097). Saliwo then fixed a one-character typo. There are no reverts, no other languages and no link to current events. briefs.headline: Drive-by vandalism on Sex shop and The Mask pages; one bad edit still live
briefs.summary: There's no real-world event here. Two unrelated English articles got low-quality drive-by edits, and the only link between them is one patroller, Beyhive Navy, who reverted bad edits on both. On Sex shop, temporary account ~2026-55931-55 inserted a joke alias, "also known as Di Dey Nick Her Shop (as of 2026)", into the first sentence (rev 1381080634), and Beyhive Navy reverted it. Four minutes later, registered account CYbr4983 changed the first sentence to say a sex shop "forces products related to sexual or erotic entertainment into the hands of children" (rev 1381081157). Its edit summary calls this a fix for a "severely wrong" description, but it's vandalism. As of my last graph check that edit had not been reverted, so it's still in the article. On The Mask (1994 film), the edits match the prior brief: a "67th" to "67" wording change that was reverted, then an unsourced lead sentence, "The film was also produced by Chuck Engelman" (rev 1381079643). As far as I know the credited producer is Bob Engelman, but I haven't checked that against a source. No other languages are involved, there's no back-and-forth between editors, and nothing in the edits points to news. Vandalism, not news.

briefs.headline: Sex shop article vandalised again after revert; new falsehood still live
briefs.summary: There's no real-world event here. This is a run of repeated vandalism on the English "Sex shop" article. F0malhaut42 reverted CYbr4983's line saying sex shops force products "into the hands of children" (rev 1381081715, cited as an NPOV violation), which put back the correct first sentence, "sells products related to sexual or erotic entertainment". The same edit also changed the date of Léon Vidal's Paris stores from the 1920s to the 1940s, which contradicts the cited book, "City of Pleasure: Paris Between the Wars" (rev 1381082174). A graph query shows no later edit on the page, so as of my check this edit is still in the article. That makes three bad-faith edits from three different accounts in about 16 minutes. The two most recent push the same "children" theme, which could mean one person switching accounts or simply copycats. I can't tell which from the graph. The Mask (1994 film) side has nothing new since the last brief. Only one language is involved, there's no back-and-forth between two editors, and there's no news hook.

briefs.headline: The Mask (1994 film): small unsourced tweaks and one revert; no news event
briefs.summary: Three edits in about two minutes on the English article for The Mask (1994 film). None of them points to a real-world event. Temporary account ~2026-56067-12 changed the displayed link text "67th Academy Awards" to "67 Academy Awards" (edit summary "fix number"), which made the wording worse.
