These are low-quality drive-by edits with no other languages involved and no sign of an edit war. I'm treating this as routine.

briefs.headline: Sex shop vandalism reverted by Drmies; article restored, no new edits since
briefs.summary: This is an update to the vandalism run on the English "Sex shop" article. The edit the last brief flagged as still live has now been reverted. Experienced editor Drmies reverted temporary account ~2026-56238-27 (rev 1381082476) about three and a half minutes after its edit. The diff shows the restore was complete: the first sentence again says the retailer "sells products related to sexual or erotic entertainment" instead of "forces kids to use products". Léon Vidal's Paris shops are back to the 1920s, which matches the cited book "City of Pleasure: Paris Between the Wars". A graph query shows no edits after this revert on either Sex shop or The Mask (1994 film), so the article looks clean as of this check. The full run was three bad-faith edits from three accounts in about 19 minutes, each reverted by a different patroller. There was no back-and-forth between two editors, only one language was involved, and nothing points to a real-world event. The "Chuck Engelman" producer line on The Mask (rev 1381079643) has no recorded revert in the graph. I haven't checked it against a source.

briefs.headline: Ota Jirák death entry trimmed to one source; place of death removed from article
briefs.summary: Update to the breaking story. Czech Wikipedia still reports that actor and presenter Ota Jirák died on 17 October 2026, aged 77. No one has disputed the death or reverted it. Experienced editor David V. (rev 26309576) has since taken out the temporary account's sentence saying Jirák died "on Saturday at his cottage in the Mladá Boleslav area." He also removed the Blesk.cz citation ("Legendární Hele přišlo o hlas. V 77 letech zemřel herec Ota Jirák"). His edit comment says he could not find the place of death in the source. The article now says only "Zemřel 17. října 2026 ve věku 77 let" ("He died on 17 October 2026, aged 77"), backed by the Novinky.cz piece "Zemřel herec Otakar Jirák" (18 Oct 2026). The other new edits are housekeeping: fixes to the Kinobox film-database link by Petrsv and Jindřich Rubeš. Taken together, the death and date are stable, but the place of death is unconfirmed. Earlier edits had said both Prague and the Mladá Boleslav area, and the article now gives neither. A graph query found no linked articles in other languages for this page.

briefs.headline: Czech actor Ota Jirák, voice of children's TV character 'Hele', dies at 77
briefs.summary: Czech Wikipedia's article on actor and presenter Ota Jirák (born 12 April 1949, Mladá Boleslav) was updated to report his death. Three accounts made six edits in about 11 minutes, with no reverts. A temporary account added the death first, giving the date as 18 October 2026 and the place as Prague, then changed the date. Experienced editor David V. rewrote the lead with the date of death as 17 October 2026, citing a Novinky.cz article titled "Zemřel herec Otakar Jirák" ("Actor Otakar Jirák has died", 18 Oct 2026). He also replaced the "living people" category with death categories. The temporary account then added a Blesk.cz report saying Jirák died on Saturday, 17 October, at his cottage in the Mladá Boleslav area. Two separate news outlets are cited, so the death looks well sourced. The place of death is still unsettled: the first edit said Prague, but the Blesk citation says the Mladá Boleslav area. I didn't check whether other language editions have been updated.

briefs.headline: Suvendu Adhikari page: two infobox blankings reverted, no net change
briefs.summary: The roughly 33,880 bytes of churn on en.wiki's Suvendu Adhikari article is the same 8,470-byte block deleted twice and put back twice, so the article ends up unchanged. Two different single-edit temporary accounts (~2026-53924-48 and ~2026-56119-04) each removed the whole infobox and opening section within about 4 minutes of each other, with an empty "/* */" edit summary. The anti-vandalism bot ClueBot NG undid the first removal 13 seconds later. Editor IrisChronomia undid the second about 40 seconds after it was made. The diffs show nothing replaced the deleted text, and no facts were changed. The restored text, which was already on the page, describes Adhikari as Chief Minister of West Bengal since 9 May 2026 and MLA for Bhabanipur. None of the four edits touches that claim, so this activity isn't news about him. What I can't tell: whether the two temporary accounts are the same person, and whether more blanking will follow, which might call for page protection.

briefs.headline: Suvendu Adhikari page: no new edits since two reverted blankings
briefs.summary: Nothing has happened on en.wiki's Suvendu Adhikari article since the last brief. The graph shows only the same four edits: two single-edit temporary accounts (~2026-53924-48 and ~2026-56119-04) each deleted the same 8,470-byte block, and ClueBot NG and IrisChronomia restored it within 13 and 42 seconds. The page ends up unchanged. Nothing has been edited since the last revert, so the blanking has not continued for now. I tried to read all four diffs again and none would load ("missing content"). That could mean an administrator has hidden those revisions, but I can't confirm it. So this update rests on edit history and summaries only, and I cite no diffs. This isn't news about Adhikari himself. I'd suggest folding this into the existing vandalism story rather than tracking it separately.

briefs.headline: Test-style vandalism on ja.wiki Elon Musk page reverted twice; no news event
briefs.summary: Over about 14 minutes, a temporary account (~2026-56073-43) made three small edits to the Japanese Wikipedia article イーロン・マスク (Elon Musk). The edit summaries were keyboard filler ("あ", "あいうえお", "おｎ"). One of these edits (rev 111446464) cut into the lead paragraph, which describes Musk's background, his role in the Trump administration and DOGE, and the companies he co-founded. Black Oar rolled back the account's first edit. Kugelschreibers then reverted the rest with Twinkle, tagging it "荒らしの差し戻し" (vandalism revert). The restored lead (rev 111446498) matches the earlier text and adds no new facts. The same Wikidata item (Q317521) has no edit activity in other languages over this period, so nothing points to a real-world trigger. This looks like isolated test edits or vandalism by one account, already cleaned up, not an edit war or breaking news.

briefs.headline: Routine upkeep on fa-wiki page for Iranian streaming series 'Taxi'; no news hook
briefs.summary: Three edits hit the Persian Wikipedia article on 'Taxi' (تاکسی), an Iranian 12-episode streaming series. It is directed by Hassan Nouri and adapted from a book by Soroush Sehat. A temporary/anonymous account added six cast names (Amir Nouri, Seyed Ali Salehi, Hamed Vakili and others; +209). Dexbot's AI anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) automatically undid that edit about a minute later. The graph does not mark this as a revert, but the bot's comment says it is one. Editor Carl then made a cleanup pass (−572): he trimmed long encoded reference URLs, removed a duplicate wikilink and emptied the IMDb template ID. The page already says filming ran from 17 Mordad to 29 Shahrivar 1405 (Aug–Sep 2026), and none of these edits add new real-world facts. The churn looks like ordinary maintenance, not a reaction to an event. The only open question is whether the cast addition was accurate, and the bot removed it without checking.

briefs.headline: Racist vandalism spree on Simple English ethnic-group pages, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a content dispute. One temporary account (~2026-56022-80) added one-line racist and sexually explicit slurs to Simple English Wikipedia's "Manx Americans" and "Cornish Americans" pages, twice on each, over about 7 minutes. Every insertion was reverted within seconds to minutes by patrollers Spiderone and NDG and by the anti-vandalism bot ChenzwBot, and Spiderone tagged them as vandalism. The diffs I read (11035821, 11035825, 11035835, 11035837) contain only abusive text, with no real claims and nothing citing a source. In the same short window the graph shows this account also touched Norwegian Americans, Irish Americans, Ku Klux Klan and Trumpism. I didn't read those diffs, but the pattern fits a single trolling spree rather than a reaction to any real-world event. There is no news signal here, and no more monitoring is needed unless the account or similar ones keep going.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: Rouen added to riot-hit cities in lead; Marseille church smoke from bin fires
briefs.summary:
Two small edits have come in since the last brief, both on fr-wiki's "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026", from registered editors and with no reverts. They are folded into this story rather than opening a duplicate.
- **Rouen in the lead (rev 240495881, Jerome misc):** Rouen was added to the list of cities with major riots and looting. This brings the lead in line with the Rouen looting section reported earlier.
- **Limoges:** the same lead sentence says Limoges's town hall, a listed historic monument, was "destroyed" by arson. That text was already there and this diff doesn't show its source, so treat it as unconfirmed until a citation is found.
- **Marseille (rev 240495930, Gottseidank):** a photo caption now says the black smoke around the Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul came from bin fires. That plays down any suggestion the church itself was attacked. It is only a caption, with no press source.
There are no new casualty, arrest or turnout figures and still no versions in other languages, so the story remains steady but quiet. Earlier open points still stand: the Vance quote and the looting summary have no source, the Magyar quote is cited to an article that predates it, and the Nancy figures depend on a single source.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct protests: 550,000–800,000 marched; one protester dead in Paris
briefs.summary: This is a small update to the fr-wiki article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026". There are 5 new edits from 3 registered editors (Thontep, Jerome misc, HaT59), with no reverts. Most of the work is copyediting and adding sources, but the edits I read show figures and events I hadn't reported before. On turnout, organisers claim 800,000 protesters nationwide and the Interior Ministry 550,000, including 110,000 in Paris across 110 marches (Linternaute, Le Parisien). The ministry had expected only 40,000–60,000 in Paris, and JDD quotes Laurent Nuñez saying the police deployment "was not undersized". The Bouches-du-Rhône police prefecture is cited (Le Figaro) as putting the crowd in Marseille at 30,000 looters, 8,000 of them rioters (rev 240493032). A "Mort" section, cited to CNews, says a protester collapsed on boulevard de Magenta in Paris's 10th arrondissement and died outside the rue du Château-d'Eau emergency station before he could be treated (rev 240493327, an edit that only fixed wiki links). Rouen looting gets a second source (ici.fr), and the article still notes a fire at a University of Rouen building on the night of 16–17 October (rev 240492998). HaT59's Paris edit only changes formatting (rev 240493342). Caveats: the death is single-sourced to CNews and described as a medical collapse, not violence, and the Marseille looter count is the prefecture's figure, cited second-hand through Le Figaro. There are still no arrest or injury figures and no versions in other languages.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct riots: Trump and Vance blame immigration, per fr-wiki; article retitled
briefs.summary: The fr-wiki article has been moved to "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026 en France". It keeps the same Wikidata item, and the new title is reflected in the lead (rev 240493745). That edit also added the categories "Émeute ou désordre civil en France" and "Émeute du XXIe siècle", so editors now classify the day as a riot, not just a protest. The largest new edit (+1316, DylanFR64, rev 240494063) starts a "Réactions étrangères" (foreign reactions) list. It quotes Donald Trump on Truth Social on 18 October ("La France brûle !", "France is burning!", blaming immigration and urging France to close its borders). It also quotes J. D. Vance on X, who blames Western migration policy, says he hopes France ends "this madness before more monuments burn", and draws a parallel with Democratic lawmakers in the US. No citation shows in the diff text I read, so both quotes are unverified for now. The editor marks the list "en cours" (in progress). Other edits are captions on a "Phase insurrectionnelle" (insurrectionary phase) gallery: burned cars on rue Saint-Denis and a looted, burned shop on boulevard Saint-Denis in Paris (rev 240493943), plus a copyedit of the lead (rev 240493459). There have been no reverts, and editors are still collaborating. Turnout and death figures are unchanged from the previous brief, and there are still no arrest or injury figures and no versions in other languages.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: 4,000 in undeclared Nancy march; mayor reports "guerrilla"; title move undone
briefs.summary: Six new edits came in on fr-wiki over about 8 minutes, from three registered editors (Guallendra, HaT59, DylanFR64). None were reverted, so this is ongoing article building. New fact: Guallendra added a Nancy section (+696, rev 240494276). Citing the Meurthe-et-Moselle prefecture, it says an undeclared march of 4,000 people left place de la République at 13:30. The source is a France 3 Régions article of 18 October in which Nancy's mayor describes "scènes de violences urbaines, de guérilla" (scenes of urban violence, of guerrilla fighting) and vandalism. HaT59 then only added wiki links and time formatting (rev 240494412). HaT59 also put the lead and infobox back to "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026", dropping "en France" (rev 240494248), and the latest edits are filed under that old title. So the move I reported last time seems to have been undone, though I have not seen the move log. DylanFR64 removed the "empty/incomplete section" tag from "Réactions étrangères" (foreign reactions) (rev 240494495). I did not see a citation added for the Trump and Vance quotes, so they remain unverified. Caveats: the Nancy figure is the prefecture's, and the citation names Hélène Geoffroy as author, which looks wrong (she is not Nancy's mayor). There are still no arrest or injury figures and no versions in other languages.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: 25 arrested in Nancy as shops looted; Bukele, Hungary's Magyar react
briefs.summary:
There are 8 new edits on the fr-wiki article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026" from the same 3 registered editors (Guallendra, HaT59, DylanFR64), with no reverts. This is the same story as before, so it stays folded into it.

**Nancy:** Guallendra expanded the section (rev 240494545), citing France 3 Régions. It says shops were looted on rue Saint-Dizier, rue Saint-Jean and rue des Ponts, the Secours catholique (a Catholic charity) was targeted, and 25 protesters, mostly adults, were arrested. These are the first arrest figures the article has given anywhere.

**Nancy injury count is unreliable:** the original text had a typo ("2\" personnes… dont deux grièvement", i.e. "2\" people injured, two of them seriously"). HaT59 rewrote it as "two injured, both seriously" (rev 240494577). The real figure may be higher, perhaps twenty-something, so I am not reporting a number.

**Foreign reactions:** DylanFR64 added two leaders (rev 240494652):
- El Salvador's Nayib Bukele posted "Démolition contrôlée" (controlled demolition) on X on 17 Oct. On 18 Oct he said France could fix in a week a problem El Salvador solved in a year. This is now sourced to Le Parisien (rev 240494709).
- Hungary's PM Péter Magyar, on Facebook on 18 Oct, linked the violence to Hungary's strict migration policy. He also distinguished peaceful protest from crime and expressed solidarity with the French people. No source is shown in the diffs I read.

**Still open:**
- The Trump and Vance quotes from earlier remain uncited in what I've seen.
- The Nancy citation still names Hélène Geoffroy as author, which looks wrong.
- There are still no pages in other languages.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: Trump quote now sourced to Le Parisien; Magyar citation doesn't fit
briefs.summary:
There are 9 more fr-wiki edits from the same registered editors (DylanFR64, HaT59, Guallendra; NDG only renamed a file). None were reverted, so this is still collaborative work on the article, and it mostly firms up sourcing.
- **Trump:** DylanFR64 added a Le Parisien link (dated 18 Oct) to the "La France brûle" ("France is burning") quote (rev 240494899). That gives it a press source for the first time, though the Vance quote is still uncited in the diffs I read.
- **Magyar:** the Hungarian PM's Facebook reaction was given a Euronews link dated 14 Oct, about Macron's planned 23 Oct visit to Budapest (rev 240494949). That article predates the 18 Oct post, so it doesn't support the quote, which stays unverified.
- **Tag removed:** HaT59 tagged the foreign-reactions section "à sourcer" (needs sources), commenting "zéro source 😱" (rev 240494765). DylanFR64 removed the tag less than six minutes later (rev 240494958), although sourcing is still thin. It's a mild disagreement, not an edit war.
- **Looting summary:** DylanFR64 added a line about "pillages massifs" (mass looting) in Marseille, Paris and Lyon, with no citation in that diff (rev 240495022).
- **Montreal:** a link fix (rev 240495053) shows an existing section on a solidarity rally of about 200 people. It was held at Square Phillips with student federations and La France insoumise present, cited to Le Devoir and Noovo. That paragraph also suggests the mobilisation was driven largely by lycéens (secondary-school students).
There are no new casualty or arrest figures, and still no pages in other languages.

briefs.headline: France: 17 Oct cost-of-living protest day turns to riots and looting in several cities
briefs.summary: The fr-wiki article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026" is being actively built out by about 12 registered editors (27 edits, no reverts), so this is collaborative real-time documentation, not an edit war. The lead describes a national day of action in France against the cost of living ("contre la vie chère"), linked to the 2026 high-school and university student movement and the end of Macron's second term. It says the worst clashes were in Paris, on rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honoré near the Élysée and on the Champs-Élysées, where protesters built barricades (rev 240489449, citing Le Parisien). Edits sourced to regional papers add damage elsewhere: shops looted in central Rouen (Paris-Normandie), a children's play centre burned and an apprentice training centre (CFA) ransacked in Valenciennes (La Voix du Nord), and a ransacked police station in Noailles, Marseille, shown in a Commons photo. The article also says similar protests took place in Italy and Belgium (TF1info), and the "ongoing event" banner was switched to "recent event", so the main day seems to be over. Nothing in the article mentions the US "No Kings" protests: the cause, country and sources are all different, so this should stay a separate story. I could not confirm casualty or arrest figures, and the graph shows no linked pages in other languages yet.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: 4,000 march in Aix-en-Provence; one group blocks A8 motorway
briefs.summary: Almost all of the new churn (~1,290 bytes) comes from one edit: Guallendra's +1204 (rev 240495413) adding an Aix-en-Provence section to fr-wiki's "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026". It cites a La Provence article dated 17 Oct. A march of 4,000 people set off at 14:00 from the fontaine de la Rotonde and went to the stade Maurice-David in the Jas-de-Bouffan district. The crowd then split: one group went to the city centre and the other blocked traffic on the A8 motorway. Unlike the Nancy and Marseille sections, it mentions no violence, looting or arrests, and the photo gallery shows marching crowds. The other edits only add links, a time template and a typo fix (revs 240495523 and 240495533 by Guallendra and HaT59). No reverts, the same small group of registered editors, and still no versions in other languages. Caveats: the 4,000 figure is from one local outlet, and the source's title says only "plusieurs milliers" (several thousand). How long the A8 blockade lasted isn't given. Earlier open points remain: the Vance and Magyar quotes have no sources, the Nancy injury count is unclear, and the looting summary has no citation.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: Nancy toll reads 23 injured; Rouen looting and Lille fires visible in context
briefs.summary:
Two copy edits have come in since the last brief, both on fr-wiki's "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026", from registered regulars and with no reverts. Gottseidank switched the Rouen and Nancy paragraphs to the present tense (rev 240495831), and HaT59 changed some punctuation (rev 240495634). Neither edit adds facts, but the surrounding text they display shows details I had not reported:
- **Nancy injuries:** the article now says 23 people were injured, two of them seriously, and that 25 people were arrested. This appears to settle the earlier "2\"" typo, but the figure has no separate citation; it rests on the same France 3 Régions article, which still wrongly names Hélène Geoffroy as author.
- **Rouen:** many shops selling trainers, appliances, jewellery and perfume were looted from late afternoon, cited to Paris-Normandie and ici.fr, both dated 18 Oct. A building of the Université de Rouen-Normandie burned during the night of 16–17 Oct, cited to actu.fr. The fire came before the march, and the article doesn't say it was caused by protesters.
- **Lille:** the shop Le Coin des Barons and the McDonald's on the Grand-Place were set on fire (named ref "Chaos à Lille").
There is still nothing in other languages and the story is quiet. Earlier open points remain: the Vance quote and the looting summary have no source, and the Magyar quote is cited to an article that predates it.

briefs.headline: France 17 Oct: only a link edit since last brief; caption says Marseille police station ransacked
briefs.summary: Only one edit has come in since the last brief: Gottseidank's rev 240495202 (+43, "liens", meaning links) on fr-wiki's "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026". It only adds wiki links to a photo caption in the Marseille section. The caption does show one detail I haven't reported before: the Noailles police station in Marseille was "saccagé" (ransacked), and residents met in front of it the next day. That detail comes only from a photo caption, with no press source in this diff, so treat it as unverified. There were no reverts, no new figures for casualties, arrests or turnout, and still no versions in other languages. The story is still active but quiet. Open points from earlier briefs remain: the Vance and Magyar quotes are unsourced, the Nancy injury count is unclear, and the looting summary has no citation.

briefs.headline: cs.wiki "Satanic panic" article: copy-paste move to Czech title undone
briefs.summary: The large churn is Czech Wikipedia housekeeping and does not point to anything happening in the world. Editor K.i.f copied the roughly 32 kB article "Satanic panic" into a new page, "Satanská panika" (+31,547), then replaced the original with a redirect (-31,944). The redirect carried a move-proposal template citing Czech media that use the Czech term. About six minutes later, OJJ used TwinkleGlobal to restore the full article under the old title (+32,021, summary "Špatně", meaning "Wrong"). OJJ then removed the move template from "Satanská panika" with the summary "Přesunuto" ("Moved"). The diff tool now labels these revisions under "Satanská panika", which suggests a proper page move that keeps the edit history replaced the copy-paste. Only two editors were involved, there was no back-and-forth reverting, and no other language versions changed. This is a disagreement over how to retitle the page, not an edit war or news. The one open question is the article's final title, which the history-preserving move seems to have settled.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on two ja.wiki pages (Manga Mura, Shuhei Kojima) reverted by patroller
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. It is low-level vandalism on two unrelated ja.wiki pages, and the same patroller, Black Oar, cleaned up both. On 漫画村 (Manga Mura), the defunct pirate-manga site, temporary account ~2026-56040-46 replaced the lead and several paragraphs with the name "黒柳徹子" (Tetsuko Kuroyanagi, a TV host), with the edit comment "くろや" (rev 111448499, −1918 bytes). Black Oar reverted it about 2 minutes later. So the "large churn" the scout flagged is one blanking and its revert, not real content change. On 小島脩平 (Shuhei Kojima, a retired baseball player), another temporary account added a line break in the lead. The joke phrase "応援歌が良いよ" ("his cheering song is good") was already in the article before that edit (rev 111448603), and Black Oar's rollback removed it (rev 111448623). The only link between the pages is Black Oar's patrol run: there are no other editors and no other languages involved.

briefs.headline: Bacchus Marsh Grammar cleanup partly done; same patroller reverts drive-by vandalism on 2 pages

briefs.headline: Same temp account vandalises Rohan (name) after Internet challenge; both edits reverted
briefs.summary: The scout was mostly right, with one correction: the Rohan edit was not random churn. Black" (rev 1381267730), most likely a name drop. Nil NZ reverted it about 2 minutes later (rev 1381267835). briefs.headline: Cmune dispute: temp account reverts a fifth time, adds YouTube source; patroller cleans up two pages

briefs.headline: Cmune 'key people' revert dispute continues; temp account now cites one SCMP link
briefs.summary: The low-stakes dispute over the infobox of the defunct UberStrike studio Cmune has gone another round. Temporary account ~2026-56221-40 has made four restorations in total. Adakiko reverted again with Huggle for lacking a reliable source (rev 1381263593). The temp account then restored four names (Lee Turner, Nad Chistie/Chishtie, Kostya Plutenko, Matti Lamberg) and attached the same 2017 SCMP article as an inline ref to several of them and to co-founder Shaun Lelacheur Sales (rev 1381264269). That makes about six reverts among three accounts on one page in roughly 80 minutes, and the temp account has passed the three-revert threshold. This is not a real-world news event and not malicious vandalism. It looks like a probable insider or fan pushing names that are hard to verify. I have not checked whether the SCMP article names these people. Most likely next steps are a 3RR warning, page protection, or a talk-page discussion.

briefs.headline: Small revert dispute over unsourced 'key people' names on defunct studio Cmune
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56221-40) added two names (Lee Turner, Nad Chistie) to the key_people infobox field of Cmune, the defunct UberStrike developer. The edit summary describes them as developers on UberStrike, Deadheads and the PayDay project. Adakiko reverted it with Huggle for lacking a reliable source. The temp account restored it, and Bucket of Bubbles reverted again. The temp account then restored it a third time, adding two more names (Kostya Plutenko, Matti Lamberg) and a 2017 SCMP link in an edit summary and as a bare URL. Four reverts in about 30 minutes among three accounts on one page makes this a low-stakes content dispute, possibly from a former employee or fan. It is not news or malicious vandalism. I haven't checked whether the SCMP article actually names these people.

briefs.headline: Cmune revert dispute quiet after restore; Métis hit by racist vandalism, reverted fast
briefs.summary: No new Cmune edits since Bucket of Bubbles restored Adakiko's version at rev 1381264659. The only link between the two pages is that one patroller worked on both. Neither is a real-world news event.

briefs.headline: Bacchus Marsh Grammar hit by school-kid vandalism; partial revert leaves junk; Cmune quiet
briefs.summary:
The scout called the Bacchus Marsh Grammar School edits routine churn. They are not: this is a vandalism run, probably by students. Temp account ~2026-56205-06 made five edits:
- turned the History heading into a full sentence, with "iji" in the edit summary (rev 1381265718)
- changed the 2015 transgender-uniform controversy to "In 2048" (rev 1381265790), even though the cited source in The Age is dated 2015
- replaced "gender-neutral bathrooms" with the misspelling "eqsuitute" (rev 1381265905)
- moved the school to "Dubai,UAE" and renamed the alumni section "Notable alumni Sigma" (rev 1381266126)
Between those edits, registered user ArmaanJagpal added a fake section heading: "The current principle of the school is Krish Patel" (rev 1381266027). Bucket of Bubbles rolled back only the last edit, to ArmaanJagpal's version (rev 1381266183). Going by the diffs, that leaves the 2048 date, the "eqsuitute" typo, the sentence-heading and the Krish Patel heading still on the page until someone does a fuller revert. I read the diffs but did not check the live page. Nothing new on Cmune: the graph shows no edits after the temp account's fifth restore (rev 1381265412), so that edit war is unchanged and still unreverted. None of this is a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Anti-government vandalism hits Indonesian pages; Satyam Audios link is a coincidence
briefs.summary: This cluster is two unrelated things, joined only because ClueBot NG reverted edits on all four pages. Within about four minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56076-24) added Indonesian-language insults to Prabowo Subianto (a fake death date and a "resign" rant), Government of Indonesia ("criticize it and you get silenced") and the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (complaining that critics' social-media accounts get taken down while online gambling sites stay unblocked). ClueBot reverted each edit within seconds. Earlier, a separate temporary account added "love epstein" to Prabowo's infobox, and KuyaMoHirowo reverted it. The vandalism complains about censorship and account takedowns, which may reflect current anger online at Komdigi, but the edits contain no factual claims, and the matching pages in other languages show no recent activity. The Satyam Audios churn (an Indian record label) is a good-faith cleanup by KlWI, who cut promotional text. ClueBot mistook it for vandalism and restored it, and KlWI reverted it again. That's a bot false positive, not an edit war, and it has nothing to do with Indonesia.

briefs.headline: No news: one editor's wikilink spree on footballer pages, partly reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a transfer or squad story. All six edits come from two accounts. "Aliyu baba goni" added small wikilinks (+4 to +33 bytes, with comments like "wiki link") across 13 football-related pages in about 17 minutes. Those pages include Nigerian figures (Osimhen, Lookman, Iwobi, Musa, Bala Mohammed) and Portuguese-league players (Tormena, Galeno, Lima, Rúben Micael), so this looks like editing practice rather than a reaction to something that happened. Experienced editor GiantSnowman reverted two of the links as "OVERLINK" and "inappropriate link" and reworded Galeno (−43). There are only two editors, no other languages involved, and no back-and-forth reverting, so it isn't an edit war or vandalism. One caveat: the diff text could not be fetched, so this conclusion rests on edit sizes, edit comments and the editor's history in the graph.

briefs.headline: New UK channel 5Drama's Wikipedia page gets tidied as its 21 Oct launch nears
briefs.summary: Three registered editors made routine improvements to the English Wikipedia article on 5Drama, a new Paramount UK/Channel 5 channel. According to the article, the channel was announced on 24 September 2026 and launches on 21 October 2026, taking over from 5Select and swapping programme-guide slots with 5Action. The article's sources are a Paramount press release and a Deadline story. Most edits came from Benmathieson901 (37 edits in total, all on this one page). They added the press-release citation, which replaced an 'unreferenced' tag, and added then removed a website link pointing to the 5Select page. Andreworkney made style fixes: switching to British spelling ('programme'), removing Freesat from the terrestrial channel list, and correcting bold text. EighteenFiftyNine added a wikilink. There were no reverts or conflicts, and nothing reads as vandalism. The page activity simply reflects the channel launch, which is minor news. Whether the single-page editor is linked to the broadcaster is unknown. The text is mildly promotional ('popular original British dramas') but has sources.

briefs.headline: Small dewiki content dispute over Helmut Neunzert bio ends in admin reset
briefs.summary: The four edits on the German article about mathematician Helmut Neunzert are a small content dispute, not a news event or a death update. In rev 271468785, editor Michael Hilden reverted an earlier removal by Horst Gräbner (rev 271428446) and restored about 1 KB of text. The restored text covers a reunion of Neunzert's doctoral students in Inzell after his 90th birthday (25–27 Sept 2026), a group photo, a claim of more than 250 academic descendants in the Mathematics Genealogy Project, and an upcoming talk on 21 Oct 2026 at the Fraunhofer ITWM's 30th-anniversary colloquium. Administrator Mpns then reset the page to the version before the edit war (rev 271469245) and removed that text again. Another editor followed with an image-size tweak. The graph has no revert flags on these edits, but the edit summaries show a back-and-forth over whether the material is notable enough. Only one page and language moved. Nothing suggests a change in Neunzert's status, and the text describes him as alive and scheduled to speak.

briefs.headline: Aaron Judge ja.wiki page hit by two vandal edits from a temp account, both reverted
briefs.summary: A single temporary account (~2026-56106-07) made two false edits to the lead of the Japanese Wikipedia article on Aaron Judge within about two minutes. The first changed "Yankees" to "Dragons" (Chunichi) and turned his AL single-season home run record into an NPB record. The second, misleadingly labelled "content correction," said he was manager of Samurai Japan at the 2026 WBC instead of captain of the US team. Daiyamond reverted the first with Twinkle and Black Oar reverted the second, both within a minute. Nothing in either diff points to real-world news: neither edit had a source, and the page was restored to its previous text. This is minor vandalism, not an edit war or a breaking story. Any link to baseball-season interest is a guess.

briefs.headline: Aaron Judge ja.wiki vandalism reverted; tie to new 'THE LUV BUGS' page is just a patroller
briefs.summary: This is minor vandalism, already cleaned up, with nothing new on the Aaron Judge page since the last brief. One temporary account (~2026-56106-07) made two false edits to the lead of the Japanese Aaron Judge article. The first (111447627) changed Yankees to Dragons and turned his AL home run record into an NPB record. The second (111447645), labelled "content correction," made him Samurai Japan's manager at the 2026 WBC. Daiyamond (via Twinkle) and Black Oar (111447653) reverted them within about a minute each. The scout's note says there were "more reverts," but there are none after 111447653. The only link to THE LUV BUGS is Daiyamond, a patroller who also tidied that page. It is a brand-new article about a Japanese music label (started September 2024, Shibuya WOMB events), created from a sandbox template by Todorokigotarou. It cites only the label's own sites, and its release list runs to 2026-09. Daiyamond removed leftover sandbox markup (111447688) and North Pacific tagged the page Uncategorized. That is routine work on a new page, not news, so the two pages should not be treated as one story.

briefs.headline: Schoolyard vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's Linus Torvalds page, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: I found no news here. Two new accounts, each with a single edit, made the same kind of prank edit to the opening of the eswiki article on Linus Torvalds within about 4 minutes of each other. One edit (rev 175931335) added a line saying he "married [a named private individual] yesterday". The other (rev 175931386, edit summary "se beso con una persona") put "he kissed [a named private individual]" in front of his name. The people named appear to be private individuals, probably classmates, so this brief leaves the names out. Patroller Castellónenred undid each edit within about 2–3 minutes (revs 175931365, 175931411). There are no sources, and no other language versions of the page were edited. The look-alike edits suggest one person or one group of friends. This is not an edit war or a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia vandalism hits Torvalds, Martínez-Bordiú pages; hoax death reverted
briefs.summary: This is a prank spree on Spanish Wikipedia (eswiki), not news. On the Carmen Martínez-Bordiú article, temporary account ~2026-56315-78 added a death date of 21 Oct 2026 and a death place of "Pionyang (Corea del Norte)" (rev 175930900, summary "Fecha"). The same account padded her full name with a long string of joke names (rev 175930971). Another account replaced Franco with "Adolf Hitler" as her grandfather and moved her birthplace to Beijing (rev 175930873). Dcaminop added "alias el tio Paquito de mi padre" and changed her birth year and place (rev 175931086). On Linus Torvalds, Holawe3e293 added "hola estrella" in front of his name (rev 175931445), following the "kissed/married" prank edits covered in an earlier brief. Every edit was undone within minutes by patrollers Castellónenred, Geom and Nuria, the witch. The death claim is the only edit that looks like news. I treat it as a hoax because the place is absurd, it cites nothing, the same account was making joke edits at the same time, and the graph tracks no other-language versions of her page, so there is no sign the change spread to other wikis. One gap: I have no outside confirmation that she is alive. The style, the new and temporary accounts and the timing fit one group of friends, probably at a school.

briefs.headline: Łukasz Gibała recorded as taking office as Kraków mayor on 20 October 2026
briefs.summary: Three editors updated Polish Wikipedia's list of Kraków mayors (Prezydent Miasta Krakowa) the same way, with no reverts. In rev 81016973, the current officeholder changes from Stanisław Kracik, marked "p.f." (pełniący funkcję, meaning acting), to Łukasz Gibała, with a term start of 20 October 2026. Rev 81017004 removes Gibała's "elekt" (mayor-elect) label, gives him a start date of 20 October 2026, and ends the acting period that began on 26 May 2026. Revs 81017063 and 81017124 add Gibała's photo to the infobox and start a days-in-office counter from 20 October. The graph shows matching edits on related pages within hours: plwiki "Stanisław Kracik" ("zakonczyl pelnienie funkcji", meaning his acting term ended), plwiki "Łukasz Gibała" ("objął urząd", meaning he took office) and dewiki "Łukasz Gibała" ("Aktualisierung", meaning update). I didn't read those diffs. Taken together, this points to a real and expected handover from an acting mayor to the elected one, not vandalism or an edit war. The edits don't explain why Kraków had an acting mayor from May or how Gibała was elected (possibly an early election), so that background is unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: Routine dewiki: AI-generated Koblenz ultras page recreated after deletion, tagged again
briefs.summary: This story adds a third page, 'Kamikaze Koblenz', to the routine story about the Sandhagen church article and the footballer bio tagged for speedy deletion. Nothing here points to a news event. The page describes 'Kammikaze Koblenz (KK06)', an ultras group of TuS Koblenz fans. The text says it was founded in 2006, broke up around 2013 and was refounded in 2026, citing only its own statements ('nach eigenen Angaben'). It also says the group is not an official TuS Koblenz fan club. A temporary account first created the page, and AsepTisch tagged it for speedy deletion. Neither of those revisions can be retrieved any more, which suggests the page was deleted. A different temporary account then recreated it (rev 271505001). AsepTisch tagged it again: 'still AI-generated, a recreation of a deleted page (Wiedergänger), please lock the title'. That means a page being recreated over and over, not a real-world event. There are no other language editions and no revert war. M2k~dewiki's category edits are the only link to the other two pages. The scout's note mostly holds, but this page is a repeat recreation, not a single new one. The text claims a 2026 refounding, but nothing independent backs it up.

briefs.headline: Routine dewiki: church article gets altar photo and link; Koblenz ultras recreation appears deleted
briefs.summary: This is an update to a story already rated routine, and nothing suggests a news event. The only edits since the last brief are two small, non-minor additions by EoNy to the new article 'Dorfkirche Sandhagen (Galenbeck)'. One adds an interior photo of the pulpit altar (Kanzelaltar) (rev 271505111). The other adds a footnote linking the altar to the 'Liste von Kirchen mit Kanzelaltären', a list of churches with pulpit altars (rev 271505215). This is normal article building. On 'Kamikaze Koblenz', AsepTisch's second speedy-deletion tag (rev 271505036) can no longer be retrieved. That suggests the recreated ultras page has been deleted again, the same way the first version was. I'm inferring this; I haven't confirmed it in a deletion log. Nothing new has happened on the footballer page 'Marcel Leon Gauss', which is still expected to be deleted. There are no reverts, no other language editions involved, and all the editors are familiar maintenance and author accounts. The scout's note holds.

briefs.headline: Routine dewiki activity: new village-church article; amateur footballer bio tagged for speedy deletion
briefs.summary: Two new German Wikipedia articles with nothing linking them except that the maintenance editor M2k~dewiki categorised both. Nothing here points to a news event. The 'Marcel Leon Gauss' page is a new biography of a regional amateur footballer (1. FC Nußbaum in the Kreisliga Pforzheim, SVK Beiertheim U19, and GSV Karlsruhe, a deaf football team). It was created in one ~5 KB edit by a temporary account, sourced only to FuPa and kicker amateur profiles. That one creation edit explains the 'large churn' the scout saw. Within about two minutes AsepTisch tagged it for speedy deletion as 'zweifelsfreie Irrelevanz' (clearly not notable), so it will probably be deleted. 'Dorfkirche Sandhagen (Galenbeck)' is a new article on an early-Gothic fieldstone church in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. EoNy is building it out with history and architecture details (1784 Baroque work, the pulpit altar), while others do formatting, categories and coordinates. There are no reverts and no interest from other language editions. I can't fully rule out that the footballer page is self-promotion, but the article itself claims nothing newsworthy.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's '19 de octubre' page reverted; no news event
briefs.summary: Over about 13 minutes, the account Vores452 made repeated juvenile edits to the opening line of the eswiki date page '19 de octubre', replacing the standard text with personal sexual remarks. A temporary account (~2026-55913-27) added a similar line once. Ontzak, SeroBOT and Gelo DemonPlayer reverted each one, and the last edit (rev 175906846, 'vandalismo eliminado') put back the standard intro text. None of the edits touched births, deaths or events, no other language versions changed, and nothing points to a real-world event. Vores452 and the temporary account may be the same person, but that is not confirmed.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on eswiki '19 de octubre' resumes; latest bad edit not yet reverted
briefs.summary: This is still the vandalism spree on Spanish Wikipedia's date page '19 de octubre'. It is not a news event. After Gelo DemonPlayer restored the standard intro (rev 175906846, 'vandalismo eliminado'), the account Vores452 came back about 7 minutes later (rev 175906908). It again replaced the opening sentence with the same personal sexual remark. No later edit shows up in the graph, so this vandalism may still be live on the page. All the edits come from one account plus one temporary account, which reverters Ontzak, SeroBOT and Gelo DemonPlayer have been undoing. No births, deaths or events entries were touched and no other language versions changed. The page needs another revert, and Vores452 is a likely candidate for a block.

briefs.headline: Hilltop High School (California) page: unsourced joke additions reverted, no news
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56136-17) made three unsourced additions to the Hilltop High School (California) article. The first claimed the swim team had won "over 30" state titles in a row under a coach named "Ethos Pathos-Pythagorean", which is clearly a made-up name. The second called the student body the "most reportedly islamic" public school in San Diego County. The third said a named student started the district's first mosque or Islamic club. Two experienced patrollers undid the additions. Nil NZ reverted them with the WikiShield tool as an unsourced addition, and Meters removed the last one because it was unsourced and Wikipedia doesn't name students who aren't notable. The edits only touched this one page in one language, nobody else joined in, and nothing points to a real event. This looks like low-level vandalism or student pranking, not a content dispute or news.

briefs.headline: Hilltop High School (California): prank edits reverted, no new activity, no news
briefs.summary: This is the same activity as the existing vandalism story. There are no edits newer than the last brief: the page has only six revisions in the graph, and the latest is Meters removing an empty History section. One temporary account, ~2026-56136-17, made three unsourced additions. The first said the swim team won state titles "over 30 times in a row under coach Ethos Pathos-Pythagorean", which is an obviously made-up name. The second called the student body the "most reportedly islamic" public school in San Diego County. The third said a named student started the district's first mosque or Islamic club. Patrollers Nil NZ (using the WikiShield tool) and Meters reverted the additions as unsourced, and Meters also cited the rule against naming students who aren't notable. The activity is on one page in one language, by one account, and nobody re-added anything, so there's no edit war and no sign of a real-world event. This should be merged with or closed as a duplicate of the prior story.

briefs.headline: Korean Wikipedia: new Bundaberg drinks stub blanked and redirected; Sprite article expanded
briefs.summary: Two editors account for all of this activity on Korean Wikipedia: a temporary account (~2026-56049-73) and the experienced editor Ykhwong. The scout's note said 4 editors, but the dossier shows only these two. The temporary account created a new page, 분다버그, about the Australian soft-drink brand Bundaberg Brewed Drinks. Over about 20 edits it added an unsourced overview, written in a promotional tone, with a list of flavours, a reference to the brand's 10 years in Korea, and serving tips (rev 42682403). It then cut the page down and blanked it itself (rev 42682535, "문서를 비움", page blanked). Ykhwong then made the page a redirect to the existing article on the town, 번더버그 (rev 42682545). On the Sprite page, Ykhwong added about 37 KB, apparently translated from English Wikipedia, with a 2026 logo, origin in 1959 in West Germany, and a marketing section (rev 42682468). The temporary account also added small "see also" links there. There are no reverts and no conflict between editors, and nothing in the edits points to a real-world event. This looks like ordinary article creation and cleanup with no news hook.

briefs.headline: CFB Wainwright fire: 7 dead per media sources, not officially confirmed; fire "being held"
briefs.summary: A new edit to the English article "CFB Wainwright fire" corrects how the death toll is sourced (rev 1380891851, Patternbuffered). The article had said Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed "at least seven" deaths. It now says he confirmed "both fatalities and injuries" but gave no numbers and no cause, citing CBC. The figure of seven is now credited to Global News, which cites unnamed military sources, and to a CBC report on October 18 based on its own sources. That CBC report says National Defence had not confirmed the number. The same edit replaces an outdated line saying it was unclear whether the fire was contained: around 10:45 pm on October 17, the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was "being held." The other recent edits are minor: Jukitaa added a Global News citation for the word "explosion" (rev 1380890189), and Slaughter-echo added a wikilink and fixed capitalisation (rev 1380890114). The article also says search-and-rescue technicians parachuted in, citing CTV and Canadian Press photos. There is no edit war or vandalism in this window. Still unconfirmed: the official death toll, the cause (the article's "accidental, not terrorism" line rests on one reference I have not opened), and the injury count. I have not checked any of the cited sources directly.

briefs.headline: Deadly explosion and fire at CFB Wainwright, Alberta; article cites CNN, Reuters
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article "CFB Wainwright fire" says that on the afternoon of October 17, 2026, an explosion in a training area at the Canadian military base in Wainwright, Alberta, set off a large fire. The article cites CNN ("Deadly fire breaks out after 'serious incident' at Canada military base") and Reuters via JPost ("Fatalities reported… Carney says"). Both cited headlines report deaths. The injury figure in the article's infobox is "24+", sourced to Global News. One editor (Jukitaa) added that the blast is believed to have been accidental and not terrorism, citing an existing reference. I did not open that source, so this is unconfirmed. An unsourced edit raising injuries to "150+" was reverted within about 4 minutes by Materialscientist, a regular anti-vandalism patroller. Other edits are small copyedits. Over about an hour there were 5 edits from 5 editors, with no edit war. The article existed before the window I looked at, and only the English page is tracked. I have not checked whether the death toll, the cause, or the details from the cited articles are accurate.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Travis Walton and Daryl Dixon pages reverted by one patroller
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Two unrelated temporary accounts made joke edits to two English Wikipedia pages. On "Travis Walton incident", ~2026-56092-76 renamed a heading from "allegations of a hoax" to "allegations of a fart" and changed the displayed name of Raymond E. Fowler to "Pharter". On "Daryl Dixon", ~2026-56012-91 rewrote the opening paragraph to call him "the worst" character, credit the role to Chadwick Boseman, and add partisan jokes. The same patroller, SuperPianoMan9167, reverted every one of these edits within about a minute. The patroller is the only link between the two pages. No other languages moved, and there was no back-and-forth over the reverts. Nothing here points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Lil Keed article vandalized; one bad edit reverted, a racial slur may still be live
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. In about two minutes, two temporary accounts made junk edits to the English article on the late rapper Lil Keed (died 2022). Rev 1381134668 changed "one daughter named Naychur" to a made-up son's name that contains a racial slur, and kept the original citation. Rev 1381134830 (comment "i fixed it") replaced his legal name, Raqhid Jevon Render, with a joke name. Theeverywhereperson used an anti-vandalism tool to undo only the name change (rev 1381134880, -4 bytes, which exactly cancels the +4). The graph shows no later edit that undoes the daughter/slur change, so it may still be on the live page, though I haven't checked the current article directly. Nothing points to a real-world event: no other languages, no other pages, and no sourced new content.

briefs.headline: Lil Keed slur edit still not undone; no cleanup edits found after the earlier revert
briefs.summary: The scout thought three editors might have cleaned up the slur. They didn't. These are the same three edits from the tracked vandalism story, and the graph has no other edits on the page. Rev 1381134668 by a temporary account changed "one daughter named Naychur" to a made-up son's name containing a racial slur, and kept the HotNewHipHop citation. Rev 1381134880 by Theeverywhereperson, using the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool, only put back the legal name "Raqhid Jevon Render" after a second temporary account's joke-name edit. It did not touch the personal-life sentence. Based on the graph, the slur is probably still live on English Wikipedia. I can't confirm that without checking the current page, and an edit the graph missed could have fixed it. This is vandalism, not news, and it should probably be merged with the existing tracked story. Someone should check the live article and revert if needed.

briefs.headline: Promotional push on Mike McGlone page continues from new temp account; no news event
briefs.summary: This is still routine English-only patrol work, and nothing points to a real-world event. On Mike McGlone (the actor known for the GEICO "rhetorical questions" ads), temporary account ~2026-55788-83 made a third attempt to add the uncited "Success Guidebook/Peace Guidebook" essay claims and the albums HERO, To Be Down and SPEED (rev 1381067184). This time the music source was a Google search link. A second temporary account, ~2026-56015-00, then added a link to michaelmcglone.com and swapped an internal wiki link for a long Google search URL (rev 1381068694). That suggests one person, possibly the subject or someone close to him, editing through rotating temporary accounts. Wolfwolfnuke reverted the 56015 edits with AntiVandal (rev 1381068826). But the diff shows the revert only rolled back to the 55788 version, so the promotional discography line with the Google link still appears to be on the page. On Moksha, the same temporary account re-added its uncited sentence on liberation from prakriti and samsara (rev 1381068529). JimRenge undid it ("try to convince fellow editors instead of edit warring"), as Joshua Jonathan had done before. This is a slow edit war against several patrollers, not a two-person ping-pong. I can't tell whether the two McGlone temporary accounts are the same person. That rests on the matching style and the Google-link habit.

briefs.headline: Patrol sweep grows to Mike McGlone page; still vandalism and unsourced edits, no news
briefs.summary: This story is still routine English-only patrol work. It now covers four pages that have nothing in common except the patrollers reverting them (Augmented Seventh, CreativeLibrary460, EndTheWikiEditor, Ivebeenhacked). On the King of the World disambiguation page, the vandalism continued: RORYALEXMIKES3 added "RORY" again, and a second account, Kiddler, added the name "jothanthan jones". CreativeLibrary460 reverted both. The new page is Mike McGlone. A temporary account added promotional claims, without sources, about essays in "The Success Guidebook" and "The Peace Guidebook" and albums named "HERO", "To Be Down" and "SPEED". It was reverted, re-added the claims while also stripping the page's {{distinguish}} hatnote (a note that tells readers apart from a similarly named person), and Interceptor reverted that edit too. On Moksha, the same temporary account is still at it in the long-running dispute over unsourced content. It has now added a new uncited sentence about liberation from prakriti and samsara, after Ivebeenhacked told it to get consensus on the talk page. Nothing points to a real-world event: the edits are in one language with no coordinated topic, and these are typical vandalism, promotional and unsourced additions.

briefs.headline: Patroller's sweep links three unrelated pages; no news event behind the edits
briefs.summary: The pages Chemise, Moksha and King of the World were grouped together only because one patroller, Augmented Seventh, reverted edits on all three in the same session using the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool. On the King of the World disambiguation page, a user added the word "RORY" (edit comment: "RORY GOES TO DR MONA JAIN MIDDLE SCHOOL"). That's schoolkid vandalism, and it was reverted again and again by Augmented Seventh and CreativeLibrary460. On Moksha, a temporary account kept re-adding one unsourced sentence ("oneness with supreme power…") despite talk-page discussion, with pleading edit comments. Patrollers removed it each time, which is a small dispute over unsourced content. On Chemise, a short text change was reverted and then restored. There is no topical link between the pages, no other languages are involved, and nothing suggests a real-world event. This is routine patrol and cleanup work.

briefs.headline: Unsourced category tag on two ja-wiki actress bios reverted citing WP:V
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56374-53) added the category "ハーフのAV女優" (mixed-heritage AV actresses) to two Japanese Wikipedia biographies, 夏木りん (AV女優) and 愛弓りょう, about a minute apart (revs 111456446, 111456454). Both edits added only that category line, with no source. Within about 4 minutes, registered editor 侵入者ウィリアム undid both. The revert of 111456446 (rev 111456471) cites WP:V, and I am assuming the second revert, 111456473, is the same kind of edit because its comment and size are identical. Neither side edited again, so this was not an edit war. Nothing points to a real-world event. The only thing that matters is the risk of putting an ethnicity label on living people without a source, and that was quickly fixed. One open question is whether the temporary account is adding this category to other pages too; I did not check.

briefs.headline: 2026–27 Primeira Liga page: matchday results plus unsourced coaching changes
briefs.summary: This is routine upkeep on the English 2026–27 Primeira Liga page by three editors, with no reverts. Wikizin entered the Braga–Vitória de Guimarães result as 1–2 and moved the "results updated" date to 19 October 2026 (rev 1381079354). A temporary account updated Porto's position-by-round, showing them still 1st after round 9 (rev 1381079670). The large 797-byte edit (rev 1381078065, also from a temporary account) changes the managerial-changes table. It says Rio Ave sacked Sotiris Sylaidopoulos on 4 October and hired Vasco Seabra, and that Arouca then appointed Vítor Severino to replace Seabra. It also adds unfinished rows for Estoril Praia and for Famalicão, marked "Sacked", 13th, with the outgoing manager left blank and the date commented out. The edit cites no sources and those rows are half-filled, so treat the coaching changes as unverified, especially Famalicão and Estoril. There is no sign of a major event; the coaching moves are worth checking against Portuguese sources.

briefs.headline: U-17 Women's World Cup group results logged live: 2–4 in Group A, Nigeria 2–0 Puerto Rico
briefs.summary: Several editors, mostly temporary accounts, are filling in match results on the English article for the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup as games end. In Group B, Embele moved the standings date to 20 October 2026 and recorded a 2–0 win with goals from Adegbuyi (25') and Oscar (90+2'). The standings table now gives Nigeria 1W 1L and Puerto Rico 0W 2L, 0–8 on goals, so the 2–0 match appears to be Nigeria vs Puerto Rico (rev 1381222103). In Group A, a temporary account entered a 2–4 result. Mouradi scored twice (64' and a 90+5' penalty) for the side that lost. Kleemann (27'), Martens (34'), Choisy (45+2') and Giesen (50' penalty) scored for the winners (revs 1381223919, 1381224768). TheArabizedHelper991 then only changed the formatting to use goal templates (rev 1381226046). The edits show no reverts, vandalism or disputes. The diffs I read don't name the teams in the Group A match, and the scores come from Wikipedia editors rather than official sources.

briefs.headline: Masked Singer Israel S5 page gets routine contestant-table updates after latest episode
briefs.summary: The Hebrew Wikipedia page for season 5 of Israel's "The Masked Singer" (הזמר במסכה) got about nine small edits from four registered accounts over roughly an hour. One account, שעה טובה, made most of them. The diffs I read are routine contestant-table changes. Cohoma23 added sources to two unmaskings: a Mako/Keshet 12 piece (17 Oct 2026) reporting that singer Eden Fines was the "fire ant" mask, shown to viewers at home first, and a Maariv piece about Maya Buskila. שעה טובה added a new "Elephant" (פיל) mask row in Group B. Another account then renamed that entry "Elephant in a china shop." There are no reverts, no other language editions and no editors working across other pages. This is fan upkeep after a broadcast, not a news event. The scout counted three edits, but there were about nine, and one diff (44091021) wouldn't load.

briefs.headline: Promi Big Brother 14 finale being logged live: Nadja Benaissa 4th, third place in flux
briefs.summary: Four registered editors made six edits in about 30 minutes to the dewiki page for Promi Big Brother season 14. The edits read like someone updating the page while the finale airs. Samuelgarcia22 (rev 271468247) put No Angels singer Nadja Benaissa in 4th place with an exit date of 19 October, and Frarenatin (rev 271468360) marked her "Viertplatzierte" (fourth place) in the nominations table. Third place is less clear. Frarenatin (rev 271469428, "Runde 3") marked Gia Georgina as third, but a Samuelgarcia22 edit made about 40 seconds earlier (rev 271469417) appears to give former boxer Axel Schulz the "3" in the contestant table, and ThorstenThorstig3 (rev 271469489) moved Axel's row above Nadja's in the nominations table. That could be a real contradiction or just a row swap that is hard to read in the diff. There are no reverts and no other languages involved, so this is ordinary live-show updating rather than a dispute. The winner isn't recorded yet, so expect more edits.

briefs.headline: Patroller reverts vandalism spree on pt.wiki Vandro Família page; real biography mostly restored
briefs.summary: The vandalism spree on the pt.wiki biography of former Rio state deputy Vandro Família has been reverted. Before that, Antônio Maecio added a line saying Família was raped by Adolf Hitler (rev 73251965). A new account, Rkieferbaum, took it out under the comment "Reversão de vandalismo" (rev 73251971). That edit left in place the earlier made-up claim of a 67-year prison sentence. Three seconds later DonJK replaced "Adolf Hitler" in the spouse field with group usernames such as "Mackenzie BE" and "Brandônia Neto" (rev 73251973). Rkieferbaum then undid the run of edits (rev 73251975). That brought back his real name (Vandro Lopes Gonçalves), his office as Rio de Janeiro state deputy, Magé, his 1977 birth date, Brazilian nationality, his party history up to PSDB in 2026, and the sourced lead and cassação text. The diff output was cut off, so I can't confirm the 67-year prison claim is gone. Someone should check the live page. No edits have come in since, and nothing points to a real news event. The page may still need protection, and the group could come back. The 2026 PSDB affiliation in the restored text is still sourced only to an Instagram reel.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on pt.wiki Vandro Família page grows as two accounts take turns, no reverts
briefs.summary: The vandalism we were already tracking on the pt.wiki biography of former Rio state deputy Vandro Família has kept going for about another 15 minutes. Two accounts are now taking turns, and nobody has reverted them. Kauan Varela 14 changed the infobox name to "BE, após fazer 15% em mais uma eleição", replaced his legal name with a string of nonsense words, and changed his birth year to 4267 (rev 73251853). The same account then changed the "known as" name to "Eu sonhando que o KV ganhou em primeiro turno" (rev 73251868) and his nationality to "now Bolivian", with an obscenity (rev 73251899). Dogee400OFC turned the accurate, sourced paragraph about his 2021 TSE cassação (removal from office), made official by Alerj in 2022, into sexual slurs (rev 73251878), then added more names to the fake legal name (rev 73251897). The edit comments are empty or one letter, and the in-jokes ("KV", "BE", Portuguese party labels) look like an online politics or election-sim crowd having fun. Nothing points to a real news event. This also clears up something the earlier brief left open: Kauan Varela 14's party-label edits now look like part of the same vandalism, not good-faith corrections. The page still shows defamatory text about a real person and a cited Instagram reel. It needs to be rolled back to its state before 73251167, and the accounts may need to be reported to pt.wiki admins.

briefs.headline: No new edits on pt.wiki Vandro Família page since patroller's rollback
briefs.summary: This is an update to the vandalism story we were already tracking on the pt.wiki biography of former Rio state deputy Vandro Família. There has been no activity since the last brief. The most recent edit in the graph is still Rkieferbaum's rollback of DonJK (rev 73251975, comment "Desfeita(s) uma ou mais edições de DonJK"), and a query for anything newer returned nothing. I read that diff again. It brings back the real infobox: name Vandro Lopes Gonçalves, office as Rio de Janeiro state deputy, Magé, born 1977, Brazilian, occupation politician, and the sourced lead. It also removes the vandal text: the "Alemanha Nazista" (Nazi Germany) title, the made-up legal names, the "boliviano" nationality line, the spouse field filled with group usernames, the fake "CDS" party and the "Prostituta" occupation. The diff output is cut off partway through the cassação paragraph, so I still can't confirm from the diff alone that Babinelson0512's made-up claim of a 67-year sex-abuse sentence is gone. Someone should check the live page. All of this is on one page in one language, nothing points to a real-world event, and the 2026 PSDB affiliation is still sourced only to an Instagram reel.

briefs.headline: Seven accounts now pile onto pt.wiki Vandro Família page; still unreverted, no news
briefs.summary: The coordinated vandalism of the pt.wiki biography of former Rio state deputy Vandro Família has picked up. The page now has 29 edits from seven registered accounts, all on this one page and in one language, and nobody has reverted any of them. In the last ~15 minutes, new accounts have joined in. DonJK filled the "primeira-dama" (spouse) field with a list of usernames, KVktz, Dogee and others, plus "ele era polígamo" (rev 73251944). Dogee400OFC then changed that field to "Adolf Hitler" (rev 73251962). ImCommunist changed his office to deputy of "Alemanha Nazista" (Nazi Germany) (rev 73251916). Antônio Maecio added more joke names to his legal name (rev 73251956). Kauan Varela 14 added a jibe about the UDN, NOVO and PP parties (rev 73251942). Most serious, Babinelson0512 added a made-up claim that he was sentenced to 67 years in prison for sexual abuse (rev 73251961). That is defamation of a real person. The usernames in the spouse field show this is one online group, probably an election-sim or politics community, vandalizing the page together. Nothing suggests a real-world event. The page needs to go back to its last clean revision, from before 73251167, and probably needs protection and admin action against the accounts.

briefs.headline: Vandalism hits pt.wiki page of Rio politician Vandro Família; party label keeps changing
briefs.summary: Over about an hour, the pt.wiki biography of Vandro Família, a former Rio de Janeiro state deputy and Magé politician, was edited 11 times by four registered accounts. Dogee400OFC made five edits with one-letter comments. They included an obscene line (rev 73251298) and a rewrite of the lead (rev 73251805) that swapped the 2012 militia-leadership accusation for a sexual slur against a named person. That is plain vandalism and possibly defamation, and it needs to be reverted. Mixed in with this, other accounts keep changing his party: EduardoPaes77 replaced PSDB with "CDS – Partido Popular" in an edit labelled "Reverti Vandalismo" (rev 73251167). Kauan Varela 14 then changed the 2018 party to the odd "Partido Progressista (PP) de Thomapper" (rev 73251652), and ImCommunist rewrote the infobox and lead several times (rev 73251777). "CDS – Partido Popular" is the name of a Portuguese party and "de Thomapper" makes no sense, so these labels may be jokes too. The only source cited for the 2026 party switch is an Instagram reel. The Wikipedia edits alone don't show any real news, such as a genuine 2026 party move. Treat this as vandalism on one page, with an unconfirmed party-affiliation claim to watch.

briefs.headline: JKT48 article hit by joke infobox edits from a temporary account, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: The English JKT48 article had two edits from the temporary account ~2026-56039-01, both with the edit summary "idk". The first changed the infobox name from "JKT48" to "Fufuritsu" (rev 1381125945). The second swapped the group's parent in the infobox from AKB48 Group to the Indonesian streamer Windah Basudara, and listed internet personalities as past members: Windah Basudara, DeanKT, Reza Arap and Luthfi Halimawan (rev 1381126143). Editor KH-1 reverted each edit within minutes. This is not an edit war between two sides. It is plain vandalism, probably a fan or meme joke, and it does not point to any real-world news. No other languages or pages were involved, so I don't think it needs watching beyond normal patrol.

briefs.headline: Small vandalism run on three ja.wiki biographies changed infobox names; all reverted
briefs.summary: In about 90 seconds, one registered account (デンジスパーク) made unexplained edits to the infobox name fields on three Japanese biography pages. It cut the last character off 水野貴雄 (→水野 貴) and 天神林ともみ (→天神林 とも), and changed ただの いっこ to ただの いつこ, swapping っ for つ. About six minutes later, a patroller (Syunsyunminmin) rolled back all three edits within the same second, restoring the earlier versions. In the graph, the account has touched only these three pages. There is no sign that the pages are connected to each other, there was no other editing activity, and no other language versions changed. This looks like low-grade vandalism or a test, not a news event or a shared template edit, and the Scout's 'six editors' really comes down to two people who matter here.

briefs.headline: Akmal Saleh page: infobox blanking reverted; editor tags and trims unsourced BLP content
briefs.summary: The latest edit is cleanup and does not signal a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56064-09 added {{citation needed}} tags to the Early life and political career text on the en-wiki biography of UMNO Youth chief and Malacca exco member Muhamad Akmal Saleh. It also removed 781 bytes it called "potentially libellous unsourced claims" (rev 1381179876). It did not change any office, term or status facts. This follows the pattern from earlier: a one-edit temporary account blanked the full infobox (rev 1381179085), Serols reverted it within about 30 seconds, and the same cleanup editor then removed an unsourced spouse/children line under WP:BLP. All of this is on one page in one language, and the single revert is part of anti-vandalism work, not an edit war. Caveats: the diff I read was cut off, so I can't confirm exactly what the "libellous" text was. Removing possibly defamatory claims could also be a sign of outside controversy around him, but the edits show no such event.

briefs.headline: Malaysian politician Akmal Saleh's page: infobox blanking reverted, BLP trim
briefs.summary: The activity on the en-wiki biography of UMNO Youth chief and Malacca state executive councillor Muhamad Akmal Saleh is routine maintenance. It does not point to a news event. A one-edit temporary account (~2026-56182-57) deleted the entire infobox (-3,032 bytes) with a blank edit summary. It added no new claims. Patroller Serols reverted it within about 30 seconds, and that revert is all of the 'churn' the scout flagged. A third editor then removed an unsourced Personal life line naming his spouse and children, citing WP:BLP. No office, term or status fields were changed, the edits are on one page in one language, and there is no back-and-forth reverting. One caveat: nothing in these edits explains the blanking. It could have been a reaction to something about him in the news, but the edits themselves show nothing of the kind.

briefs.headline: New YouGov poll put One Nation first on primary vote (27%) and Labor–Coalition level at 50–50
briefs.summary: A routine poll-table update on en-wiki's "Opinion polling for the next Australian federal election" includes a notable figure. Rev 1381157737 added a YouGov poll taken 13–20 Oct (1,500 respondents, online). It has One Nation first on primary vote at 27%, then Labor 24%, the Coalition 23%, the Greens 14% and others 12%. The two-party-preferred (2PP) split between Labor and the Coalition is 50–50, and a second matchup, most likely Labor vs One Nation, is 53–47. The cited headline reads "Albanese loses two-party-preferred lead as One Nation remains ahead in primary vote", which suggests One Nation already led earlier polls rather than this being a new first. The other two edits are cosmetic: one changed party abbreviations (L-NC→L/NP, etc.) and one fixed a dash in the date range. There are 3 editors, no reverts, one page, and no activity in other languages. Caveats: the citations point to "news24.com.au", which I could not confirm as an established Australian outlet. The edit comment ("You're all goving") is odd, and I am inferring the second 2PP matchup from the table layout. Treat the figures as unverified until a second source or editor confirms them.

briefs.headline: Dallas Brodie bio: unsourced spouse claim added twice, removed twice; no news signal
briefs.summary: On the English Wikipedia page for BC MLA Dallas Brodie (Vancouver-Quilchena), a temporary-account editor (~2026-56265-64) twice added an unsourced claim to the Personal life section naming a husband, "David ash" (rev 1381271959, then rev 1381274039). Katerdactyl removed the first addition as "incorrect information" (rev 1381273599). Fingray7 reverted the second as "removing unsourced information" (rev 1381274735). That is the only revert, and the page has just four edits from three editors. No other pages, languages, political or career content are involved. This looks like a small dispute over personal-life details, not a reaction to a real-world event. It is unclear whether the claim is true or a hoax, but either way it was unsourced and has been removed.

briefs.headline: Dallas Brodie bio: lone editor re-adds unsourced spouse claim five times; no news hook
briefs.summary: This has grown past the earlier routine dispute and past the scout's count. On the English Wikipedia page for BC MLA Dallas Brodie, temporary account ~2026-56265-64 has now added "spouse (David ash)" to the Personal life section five times in about two hours. Editors removed it each time: Katerdactyl once, Fingray7 three times (revs 1381274735, 1381278500, 1381280064, with comments like "Once again, this is unsourced"), and JavaHurricane with the WikiShield tool (rev 1381281185, labeled vandalism). That is four editors and four reverts, not three and two. In the latest re-add (rev 1381280210), the account points to family obituaries as proof in the edit comment, but the article text still cites no source. The reverts all go one way, a single account against several editors, so this is a slow edit war and likely a 3RR breach, not a two-sided ping-pong. There is still no sign of a news event: one page, one language, nothing about her politics or career, and no other editors joining in. I can't check if the claim is true. The likely next step is a warning or page protection, not news coverage.

briefs.headline: Hungarian Masked Singer season 5 page gets routine episode-table edits
briefs.summary: Nearly all the activity on huwiki's 'Álarcos énekes (5. évad)' (the Hungarian Masked Singer, season 5) comes from one editor, Ermic6666667, with 18 edits. They are rebuilding the tables for episode 1 (11 October) and episode 2 (18 October): moving duel rows, adding mask names such as 'Szupergomba' and 'Jégkirálynő' to the episode 2 table, and later adding a wiki link for Kovács István (filmproducer). A temporary account added Kovács István, filmproducer, to the 'Nyomozók' (panel/investigators) section. A third editor swapped one category for three: Álarcos énekes, 2026 in music and 2026 in television. There are no reverts, all edits are small, and none of the diffs I read reveal an unmasking or any other newsworthy event. This looks like ordinary fan upkeep of a TV season page while it airs. I did not read every one of the small table edits.

briefs.headline: Mehdi Tartar page on Persian Wikipedia vandalized, then automatically reverted
briefs.summary: The activity on the Persian Wikipedia article for football coach Mehdi Tartar is vandalism. It does not reflect real-world news. Temporary account ~2026-56228-07 inserted made-up infobox facts: birth year 1209 SH, made-up goal totals, and national teams (Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Spain) in place of his real coaching clubs (rev 44779872). A second temporary account then blanked the whole infobox, after it had been changed to list Barcelona, Real Madrid and Chelsea and a 3.45 m height (rev 44779918). Within seconds, Dexbot's AI anti-vandalism system (Shahbaz) reverted the page to the clean version (rev 44779920). The clean infobox lists Tartar as Persepolis head coach from 1405 SH. That entry was already there before this burst, so it is not new here. The large churn figure comes from the blank-and-restore pair, not from a real rewrite. Two small edits by the first account (revs 44779838, 44779859) were not read, but they come before the reverted state. No other languages or pages are involved.

briefs.headline: India's 2026 Asian Para Games page updated with 20 October results, table tennis bronzes
briefs.summary: The English article "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" is getting steady results updates, mainly from two editors (Neeelzzz20 and Mr Gupta 18). Davidindia fixed a link and Ansgar Slopsbane fixed a category. There are no reverts and no fighting between editors. The diffs swap '20 Oct' fixture placeholders for match scores. In para-badminton, Umesh Kumar won 2–0 (21-8, 21-8) and Kumar Nitesh lost 0–2 to Daisuke Fujihara. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre Sivan won their mixed doubles match against Taiwan, while another mixed pair lost to China. An Indian judoka lost by ippon to opponents from Japan and Kazakhstan.
