In the medal table, editors added four women's table tennis singles bronzes dated 20 October: Bhavinaben Patel (class 4/5), Sonalben Patel (class 3), Prachi Pandey (class 6) and Baby Sahana Ravi (class 9). This looks like ordinary live result-tracking during the Games, not breaking news. Caveat: the edits cite no sources, so the results come only from the editors, and I didn't check whether pages in other languages are changing too.

briefs.headline: India at 2026 Asian Para Games: results upkeep continues; one archery edit reverted
briefs.summary: Results-tracking on the English article "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" is continuing, almost all of it by Neeelzzz20. Since the last brief, Neeelzzz20 has edited the Archery, Badminton, Shooting and Medalists sections. The only new event is a single revert. Abesh2023, a newer account with 5 edits, filled the 20 October archery placeholders with opponent flags for Malaysia and Mongolia (rev 1381132803). About 14 minutes later Neeelzzz20 undid that edit (rev 1381134463), giving no reason. This is a one-off disagreement over an unconfirmed fixture, not an edit war. I couldn't check the newest additions because the diffs for revs 1381131559, 1381132036, 1381131605, 1381132602 and 1381134703 wouldn't load. So it's unclear whether more medals or results were recorded after the four table-tennis bronzes in the last brief. As before, the edits cite no sources.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt infobox "Inactive" flip reverted; quiet since, no sign of a real outage
briefs.summary: This is the same 5-edit cluster already covered by the routine brief on this story. A temporary account (~2026-56217-66) twice changed the English DeviantArt infobox from current_status = Active to Inactive, with the summary "Under maintenance means this site is inactive." Established editor Annh07 undid it both times. A second temporary account changed ipv6 from "No" to "end", and Annh07's restore (rev 1381274864) fixed both fields. The graph shows no edits after that restore on any language version of the page (Q46523), and no sources were added. The edits hint that DeviantArt may have been briefly under maintenance, but nothing confirms an outage, and nothing suggests the site has shut down. I agree with the Scout: this is minor content churn and doesn't need a separate story.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt shutdown push adds "folded into Google"; experienced editor restores Active
briefs.summary: This updates the tracked DeviantArt story; there is no new event. Temp account ~2026-56322-35 made the same "Closed" edit again with the summary "I don't care." It set the status to Closed with a dissolved date of 21 Oct 2026, changed "is" to "was", marked the planned languages as cancelled, and added the disestablished category (rev 1381284758). ~2026-54957-04 reverted it, and then a new temp account, ~2026-56298-14, made an identical edit with one new piece: "folded into [[Google]]" after the dissolved date (rev 1381284965). That claim is unsourced and implausible, since DeviantArt is owned by Wix. ~2026-56382-59 undid that. Then Celjski Grad, a registered editor with 288 edits in the graph, restored Suonii180's last good revision, "revert unsourced changes" (rev 1381285226). That put current_status back to Active and commercial back to Yes, which also removed the Inactive and commercial = No changes left from earlier rounds. No sources have been added at any point. The graph shows no edits to the English page after that restore and none in other languages since the last brief. This is one persistent editor rotating through temp accounts (my inference, not confirmed) against several reverters, so I'm calling it vandalism, not a real-world shutdown. A short maintenance outage is still possible but unconfirmed, and if the pattern continues the page will likely need protection.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt shutdown pusher adds "disestablished" category; infobox now reads Inactive
briefs.summary: Three more edits on English Wikipedia since the last brief, and they keep the same pattern: one side pushing an unsourced shutdown claim, the other pushing back. Temp account ~2026-56322-35, which made the "I don't care." Closed edit, added [[Category:Companies disestablished in 2026]] (rev 1381283355). ~2026-56061-30 then removed that category and the dissolved date of 21 Oct 2026, and changed current_status from Closed to Inactive (rev 1381283806). That is a partial walk-back, not a full restore to Active. ~2026-56322-35 then changed the infobox's planned "95+ languages (upcoming)" to "(cancelled)" (rev 1381283986). That edit is still on the page, as are the earlier "was an online community" wording and the commercial = No flip (I haven't re-checked whether the "was" wording is still there). No sources have been added at any point, and nothing new has happened on the French page or any other language version since the French blanking was reverted. The scout saw no reverts, but this is still the same slow tug-of-war between temp accounts, not a real-world event. Whether DeviantArt is actually offline for maintenance is still unconfirmed, and nothing supports a permanent shutdown.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt "Closed" claim reverted as unsourced; no new edits or other languages since
briefs.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The 4-edit cluster the Scout flagged is the same one already covered. Temp account ~2026-56217-66 twice set the English DeviantArt infobox to current_status = Closed, added dissolved = 21 Oct 2026, and changed "is" to "was" in the opening line. The second time it wrote "It is not a mainentance. It is the tombstone" (rev 1381279956). Two other editors undid this: ~2026-54957-04 first, then Suonii180, whose restore (rev 1381280071, "Unsourced") put the page back to Active. A graph check shows no edits after that restore on the English page or on any SAME_AS version (Q46523). The page has settled with three editors against one, and no sources were added at any point. DeviantArt may be under maintenance or showing an unusual landing page, but nothing confirms that it has shut down. Reopen only if sourced edits appear or other wikis start editing.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt "Closed" edit made again on enwiki, reverted within 74 seconds
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked DeviantArt story. There is no new real-world event. About seven minutes after Celjski Grad's restore, temp account ~2026-56322-35 made the full shutdown edit again with no edit summary (rev 1381285712). The edit set current_status to Closed, added a dissolved date of 21 Oct 2026, changed commercial to No, marked the planned languages as cancelled, changed "is" to "was" in the opening line, and added the "Companies disestablished in 2026" category. ~2026-56061-30 undid all of it 74 seconds later (rev 1381285803), so the page reads Active again. I read both diffs. No sources have been added at any point, and a graph check shows no edits to other-language versions (Q46523) since the last brief. This is a slow vandalism loop: one persistent pusher, probably the same person behind several temp accounts (my inference), against at least five editors reverting. The scout's "ongoing dispute" reading is right, but nothing here supports a shutdown. The page probably needs semi-protection. Whether DeviantArt is down for maintenance is still unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt "Closed" claim returns on new account, spreads to French wiki as page blanking
briefs.summary: The unsourced claim that DeviantArt has shut down is back after the last "settled" brief. Temp account ~2026-56217-66 set the English infobox to Closed a third time (dissolved 21 Oct 2026, "was an online community"; rev 1381281575). ~2026-56061-30 changed it back, saying "It is not closed, It is undergoing maintenance" (rev 1381282677), then set it to Active (rev 1381282738). A new temp account, ~2026-56322-35, then made the exact same Closed/dissolved/"was" edit with the summary "I don't care." (rev 1381283194). That looks like the same person on a fresh account, though I can't confirm it. Another new account flipped commercial from Yes to No (rev 1381283254). Nobody has reverted those last two yet, so the English page currently says Closed. The earlier brief was also wrong to say the claim stayed on English Wikipedia: ~2026-56217-66 blanked about 11 KB of the French article with the summary "DEVIANTART IS NO MORE!" (rev 240568827), and R3L3ct3ur49 reverted it within about 80 seconds. No sources have been added anywhere. Several editors keep pointing to a maintenance outage, so the site may really be down for maintenance, but any shutdown is unconfirmed. This is one persistent, unsourced pusher that is turning into vandalism, not a real-world event.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt infobox flipped to "Inactive" over maintenance, reverted twice
briefs.summary: Over about 8 minutes, a temporary account (~2026-56217-66) twice changed the English DeviantArt infobox from current_status = Active to Inactive. Its edit summary said "Under maintenance means this site is inactive." Established editor Annh07 undid it both times, the second time noting that maintenance "does not imply that it is not working anymore." A second temporary account also broke the ipv6 field (changing "No" to "end"), and the same restore fixed that. So the edits hint that DeviantArt may be down for maintenance right now, but there is no other sign of it: no other article pages moved, no other languages are editing, and no sources were added. This looks like a minor content dispute, not vandalism or real news. Any outage is unconfirmed, and nothing here shows the site has shut down for good.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt "Closed" push returns on enwiki, rolled back to Inactive by a third temp account
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked DeviantArt story, not a new event. Temp account ~2026-56322-35 again set the English infobox to current_status = Closed. It re-added the dissolved date (21 Oct 2026) and the "Companies disestablished in 2026" category, and marked the Italian language rollout as cancelled (rev 1381284060). It then changed "features" to "featured" in the opening line, which already said "was" (rev 1381284248). About three minutes later, a new temp account, ~2026-56382-59, undid all of it in one edit with the summary "It IS STILL UNDER MAINTENANCE, IT IS NOT DISSOLVED!!!!" (rev 1381284465). That edit set status back to Inactive, removed the dissolved date and the category, put the languages back to "upcoming", and restored "is an online community". The page now reads Inactive, not the original Active. No other language version of the article (Q46523) has been edited since the last brief, nothing has happened on the English page after rev 1381284465, and no sources have been added at any point. This is the same unsourced shutdown push by one persistent editor, probably on rotating temp accounts, which is closer to vandalism than to a real-world event. The repeated mentions of maintenance suggest the site may really be down for a while, but that is unconfirmed, and nothing supports a permanent closure.

briefs.headline: DeviantArt shutdown claim escalates: infobox set to "Closed" with Oct 21 end date, reverted
briefs.summary: The Scout said there was nothing new here, but that's wrong: the edits after the last brief go further. The same temporary account (~2026-56217-66) that earlier flipped the infobox to "Inactive" has twice set the English DeviantArt article to current_status = Closed. It also added dissolved = {{end date and age|2026|10|21}} and changed the opening line from "is" to "was an online community" (revs 1381279653, 1381279956). The second edit's summary says: "It is not a mainentance. It is the tombstone." That suggests the account believes the site now shows a farewell or closure page, not a maintenance notice. Two different editors reverted it: temp account ~2026-54957-04 (pointing to Annh07's view that maintenance is not a shutdown) and Suonii180 (rev 1381280071, reason "Unsourced"). No sources were added at any point, all the closure edits come from one account, and no other language version of Q46523 has moved. So this is one persistent, unverified claim that the site has shut down, against a consensus of three editors. It is not yet a confirmed event, and not a classic two-sided edit war. Earlier edits that mention maintenance hint that something is visibly happening on the site, so this deserves a short watch for sourced edits or other wikis joining in.

briefs.headline: Clifford the Big Red Dog film page: false studio credits reverted as suspected LTA
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. On the en-wiki page for the 2021 film 'Clifford the Big Red Dog', a temporary account (~2026-55856-82) replaced the production companies New Republic Pictures and Scholastic Entertainment with Universal Pictures and Illumination Entertainment. It also lowered the box-office gross from $117.8M to $107.4M and rolled back a reference access-date (rev 1380897378). CANthony0125 reverted this as vandalism (1380897955). The same account then made a two-edit run that partly reapplied the studio swap, including the misspelling "Illumination Entertainmen" (1380898910). Magitroopa undid it, tagging it "LTA" (long-term abuse) (1380898947). Nothing points to a real-world event: it's one page in one language with no matching edits in other languages, and the page is already back to the correct version. One caveat: the 'LTA' label is the patroller's judgement, and I didn't check the account's other edits.

briefs.headline: Clifford film page: third false Illumination credit reverted; account hit ~20 kids-TV pages
briefs.summary: This is still vandalism, not news. The same temporary account (~2026-55856-82) came back a third time to the en-wiki 'Clifford the Big Red Dog (film)' page. This time it swapped the production credit "Scholastic Entertainment" for "Illumination Entertainment" (rev 1380899042). Magitroopa, who had already flagged the account as LTA (long-term abuse), undid it 14 seconds later (1380899067), and the page is back to the correct credits. The graph shows that between about 1792340778 and 1792342217 (roughly 24 minutes), the account touched about 20 other en-wiki pages, mostly Nickelodeon/Disney kids' TV shows plus the pages for Illumination (company), Dan Povenmire and Kenny Loggins. That fits the spree pattern behind the LTA tag. I didn't read diffs on those other pages, so I can't say whether they were vandalised too. There is no real-world event: it's one language, the reverts are quick, and nothing has changed in the real credits.

briefs.headline: '9-1-1' season 9 split dispute escalates to second revert; page back to a redirect
briefs.summary: The fight over whether "9-1-1 season 9" should be its own article or a redirect has gone a step further. Since the last brief, Magical Golden Whip reverted JoyfullySmile's restored 36 KB article for a second time (rev 1381064049, "take to talk page"). Within about 45 seconds he made a self-revert that brought the article back (1381064095), then undid that too (1381064141). The self-revert looks like a misfired rollback, not a change of mind. The page is now a redirect to List of 9-1-1 episodes#Season 9 (2025–26) again. Lonniemitchell22 then added an italic-title template, a sort key and season categories (1381064333), which now sit on the redirect. Taken together, that's two content reverts by Magical Golden Whip and one by JoyfullySmile, all on English Wikipedia only, and nobody has said in the edit history that they've gone to the talk page. This is a small edit war about page structure between two editors, not real-world news. It's below the three-revert threshold, and it could die down or move to the talk page. Watch for JoyfullySmile undoing it again or creating other season pages.

briefs.headline: Editors dispute splitting out a standalone '9-1-1' season 9 article; not real-world news
briefs.summary: JoyfullySmile turned the redirect "9-1-1 season 9" into a full article (+36 KB): infobox, cast, an 18-episode table running from October 9, 2025 to May 7, 2026, plot summaries and ratings citations. Magical Golden Whip reverted it back to the redirect, saying the split should go to the talk page first and that the page "can't just have one season". JoyfullySmile undid that revert, saying all seasons will get their own pages, working backwards from season 10. Meanwhile Lonniemitchell22 made small cleanup edits, such as filling in missing ratings source URLs. So far that's one revert each way between two editors, all over how the pages are organised. It isn't a real edit war yet, and nothing in the diffs points to a new real-world event. One editorial slip: the new lead says the season "will premiere" on October 15, 2026, which clashes with its own 2025–26 air dates and looks like text copied from a season 10 draft. Worth watching only if the revert back-and-forth starts up again.

briefs.headline: NZ 2026 polling page: formatting fix to unsourced Mongrel Mob timeline entry
briefs.summary: The only new edit on the en Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election page is housekeeping. The temporary account ~2026-48399-43 added an unsourced 15 Oct timeline row (rev 1381065517) saying the Green Party and Te Pāti Māori were photographed with the Mongrel Mob at a wellbeing day. That row had been inserted by rewriting the existing 14 Oct row, which is probably why the system marked the edit as a revert. Its follow-up (rev 1381065762) corrects the sort date to 2026-10-15 and adds matching grey shading to the restored 14 Oct row, which records the NZ Herald leaders' debate between Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins. No new polls, no reverts by other editors and no sign of an edit war. The Mongrel Mob claim still has no source, and it is unclear whether other editors will keep it. The earlier poll additions (Freshwater Strategy national poll, Curia Te Tai Tokerau poll) stand as in the prior brief.

briefs.headline: NZ 2026 election polling page adds new national and Te Tai Tokerau polls
briefs.summary: This is routine upkeep of the en Opinion polling page for the 2026 New Zealand general election. Four editors made five edits in about 30 minutes. One editor added a Post/Freshwater Strategy national poll (fieldwork 9–19 Oct 2026, n=1,458) with Labour narrowly ahead on 28.7 against 27.6, a 1.1-point lead (rev 1381061897). Gadfium added a Whakaata Māori–Curia poll of the Te Tai Tokerau electorate (5–15 Oct, n=500), citing Te Ao Māori News: "Hūhana Lyndon leads Te Tai Tokerau poll as Labour tops party vote" (rev 1381064669). Gadfium then fixed misplaced numbers, and another editor fixed the poll order. A temporary-account editor added a 15 Oct timeline entry saying the Green Party and Te Pāti Māori were photographed with the Mongrel Mob at a wellbeing day and drew wide media attention. That entry has no source, and the editor invited others to revert it. The system flags this edit as a revert, but the diff shows new content, not a reversal, so I see no edit war. Uncertain: which party columns the national figures belong to (inferred from the shading and the usual table layout), and whether the Mongrel Mob entry survives.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki biography of 1901-born journalist Oswald Zenkner moved to main space
briefs.summary: This is a new German Wikipedia article on Oswald Zenkner (1901–1963), described as a German newspaper journalist, Wehrmacht war correspondent and book author. He was born in Josefstal near Gablonz in Bohemia and died in Schwetzingen. The six edits are routine work on a new page. Murkus69 moved the draft into the main article space ("Wurde in den ANR verschoben") and removed the {{Baustelle}} (under construction) tag. M2k~dewiki, a regular maintenance editor, added the person-data template, sorting key, categories and authority-file IDs (GND 116979976, VIAF 122298495). The author EposImages made small fixes to the references. There are no reverts, no activity on other language versions and nothing tied to current events. The subject died in 1963, so this is not a news trigger. One small gap: the person-data template has no death date, although the article text gives 1 August 1963.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki biography of journalist Oswald Zenkner (1901–1963) gets routine cleanup
briefs.summary: This is a new German Wikipedia article on Oswald Zenkner (1901–1963). The article describes him as a German newspaper journalist, Wehrmacht war correspondent and book author. Three registered editors made six edits, with no reverts and no activity in other languages. Murkus69 moved the draft into the main article space and removed the {{Baustelle}} (under construction) tag (rev 271440554). M2k~dewiki, a maintenance editor, added the person-data template, sorting key, categories and authority-file IDs GND 116979976 and VIAF 122298495 (rev 271440477). One small detail: Murkus69's move also wiki-linked the birth date, and the author EposImages removed those links a minute later (rev 271440574). That is a style difference, not an edit war. The person-data template still has no death date, although the article text gives 1 August 1963. The subject died decades ago and nothing points to a news trigger; this matches the earlier routine brief.

briefs.headline: ru-wiki 2026 deaths list adds Kyrgyz soprano Sartbaeva, geochemist Glazunov
briefs.summary: Routine upkeep of the Russian Wikipedia "List of deaths in 2026" by several editors, all logged in except one temporary account, with no reverts. Diffs add Kyrgyz opera soprano Kairgul Sartbaeva (90), a People's Artist of the USSR, sourced to a Lenta.ru item dated 20 Oct 2026 (rev 155721372). Two editors added Soviet/Russian geochemist Oleg Glazunov (99) within ten seconds of each other, citing baikal24.ru and VK (revs 155721686, 155721682). Krokusse then cleaned up formatting and removed one of the two Glazunov entries (rev 155721748). The same diff also shows Soviet dissident Boris Kochubievsky (90) and ex-Lokomotiv footballer Oleg Garin (60) already on the list. Garin's line is among the removed lines in that diff, probably because it was moved within the page, but I haven't confirmed that. None of these people's own pages show activity in the graph, so there's no sign that any of these deaths is driving wider editing. It's a regional notable-deaths story at most.

briefs.headline: Liechtenstein vandalism spree widens to four accounts; Cannolis restores clean version
briefs.summary: The activity on en:Liechtenstein is still a vandalism spree, not news. Since the last brief, three more bad edits came in, and Cannolis then rolled the page back to ClueBot NG's clean revision (rev 1381110647), which removed everything still outstanding. A new temp account, ~2026-56101-99, cut the GDP figures in the infobox down to nonsense, for example changing per-capita PPP from $210,600 to "$2.10" (rev 1381109172). Freyaconnolly123 swapped the coat of arms for an uploaded personal image, "Freyag123.jpg", with the comment "hello" (rev 1381110151). ~2026-56023-96 replaced the portrait of Johann I Joseph with a Rick Astley album cover, a rickroll (rev 1381110318), and Rencoolguy reverted it (rev 1381110432). Cannolis's restore also removed Freyaconnolly123's earlier flag swap, which had not been reverted at the last update, plus a change saying the country had "all of the debt" instead of "no debt". The debt change was probably part of rev 1381109172, but the diff text was cut off before that point, so I can't confirm it. The spree now covers four vandal accounts in about 40 minutes, and the shared style suggests a coordinated group. The page was clean as of the latest edit, and no real-world event is involved.

briefs.headline: Liechtenstein vandalism spree quiet after Cannolis rollback; page stays clean
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity on en:Liechtenstein since the last brief. The graph has no edits after Cannolis's rollback at rev 1381110647, so the page is still clean. That rollback put back the real flag and coat of arms, which Freyaconnolly123 had replaced with uploads named "Lp image.jpg" and "Freyag123.jpg". It also restored the infobox GDP figures, for example per-capita PPP from "$2.10" back to $210,600, and changed "all of the debt" back to "no debt". Rev 1381109172 by ~2026-56101-99 cut the GDP figures down and also edited the "no debt" sentence. The added text was cut off in the diff, but that is the only edit since ClueBot NG's revision that touched the sentence, and the rollback reverted it, so it was almost certainly the source of the "all of the debt" wording. Overall, four throwaway or temporary accounts made juvenile edits over about 40 minutes, and five patrollers and bots reverted them. Only this one page moved: no other language versions and no related articles, and there is no sign of a real-world event. The vandalism could start again, but for now it is over.

briefs.headline: Liechtenstein article hit by small vandalism spree; no news event behind it
briefs.summary: The edit activity on en:Liechtenstein is vandalism, not news. Three accounts made four bad edits in about 30 minutes, and the article's facts did not change. Temp account ~2026-56091-37 added "by Yusra Zeeshan" to the sentence on the country's 1719 formation (rev 1381104623; Oklopfer reverted it), then replaced the flag with an unrelated uploaded image (rev 1381105803; AntiCompositeNumber reverted it). Temp account ~2026-56023-96 replaced the Gutenberg and Vaduz Castle captions with personal messages ("I love my Mr. super supreme secretary"), labelling it "clarity" (rev 1381108632; ClueBot NG reverted it). Registered account Freyaconnolly123, which has no other edits, then swapped the flag for another unrelated image, "Lp image.jpg" (rev 1381109071). As of the latest graph data, nobody has reverted that last edit. The similar style suggests these accounts are linked, possibly a group of students, but that is unconfirmed. No other language versions or related pages moved.

briefs.headline: Hebrew 'Eggplant' bullying vandalism: one last hit reverted, page now looks clean
briefs.summary: This update covers the same schoolyard vandalism of the Hebrew Wikipedia articles חציל (Eggplant) and מגה-מוח (Megamind). It isn't news. After the main cleanup, temporary account ~2026-56318-51 came back one more time (rev 44096521). It changed the bolded subject at the start of the Eggplant intro from 'חציל' to the first name 'אביב' (Aviv), which looks like another jab at a peer. Idoiz rolled it back about 17 seconds later (rev 44096524), returning the page to שעה טובה's last version, which had already undone the earlier insults. The graph shows no Eggplant edits after that rollback. That answers the open question in the earlier brief: the latest revision appears clean. There are still no other languages involved, no tie to any real-world event, and no back-and-forth between established editors. The vandal could come back, and I haven't checked whether either page was protected or the temporary accounts blocked.

briefs.headline: Hebrew Wikipedia: two temp accounts vandalize 'Eggplant' and 'Megamind' with bullying
briefs.summary: This is schoolyard vandalism, not news. Two temporary accounts (~2026-56318-51 and ~2026-55421-39) took turns editing the Hebrew articles on the eggplant (חציל) and the film Megamind (מגה-מוח) over about 15 minutes. They added insults aimed at people named only by first and last name, who are probably private individuals such as classmates. The text calls them fat or ugly, makes claims about their sexuality, and says they are beaten at home. One edit summary falsely says it is "adding detail" (הוספת פירוט). Experienced editors Benbaruch, שעה טובה and Idoiz rolled back the edits on both pages, and Megamind was restored to its July 2025 version. The scout's note of "no reverts and no anonymous edits" is wrong. Temporary accounts are effectively anonymous, and several edits were rollbacks that the graph did not flag as reverts. I don't know of any real-world event behind this. The cleanup looks done, but I haven't confirmed that the latest eggplant revision is fully clean.

briefs.headline: FNaF 3 article: copied game transcript removed and revision-deleted; no news event
briefs.summary: On the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 article, StoopidPieForU added about 2.8 KB of text to the Plot section. Their edit summary says it was the full transcript of the night 1 phone call from the game, with more transcripts to come. About eight minutes later NegativeMP1 put the page back to the earlier revision by SleepyRedHair, saying a transcript is not what plot summaries are for and that it was a copyright violation. NegativeMP1 then added a {{Copyvio-revdel}} tag covering revisions 1381122139 through 1381122729 (I read this diff). An admin, Mfield, completed the revision deletion and removed the tag. I couldn't read the added text itself because those revisions now return "missing content", which fits the deletion. The large churn figure comes from this one add-and-remove, and the page is back where it started. This is ordinary copyright cleanup, not a real-world event or an edit war.

briefs.headline: ja-wiki sunflower festival article stripped of its sources, then its sourcing tag undone
briefs.summary: There have been no new edits since the earlier brief, and the diffs I re-read confirm it. Shin-Nippori created the Japanese article on the Akeno Sunflower Festival in Chikusei, Ibaraki (rev 111451078). Two minutes later the same editor removed every inline citation (local-government research institute, Ministry of Agriculture and Chikusei city PDFs) and the references section, leaving the text word for word the same (rev 111451098). そもそもーる added a "needs sources" tag ({{出典の明記}}). Geogie took it out with a pop-up undo (rev 111451166), so the article now has no sources and no warning. There are three named editors, one revert, no pushback, one language and nothing tied to a current event, so this is not news and not an edit war. It is unclear why the sources and the tag were removed; it looks like housekeeping on a new article, not an attempt to mislead.

briefs.headline: New ja-wiki article on Ibaraki sunflower festival; sources removed, tag reverted
briefs.summary: This is a new article being set up, not news. Shin-Nippori created the Japanese article on the Akeno Sunflower Festival (あけのひまわりフェスティバル), held every summer in Chikusei, Ibaraki (+6203, rev 111451078). It covers the festival's start in 1990, the switch to double-flowered sunflowers in 1993, venue changes in 2024 and 2025, and about 60,000 visitors in 2025, citing city and Ministry of Agriculture (MAFF) PDFs. Two minutes later the same editor deleted every citation and the references section (-1245, rev 111451098). The text stayed the same, so the article was left with no sources. そもそもーる then added a "needs sources" maintenance tag (rev 111451104), and Geogie removed it with a standard undo (rev 111451166), which is the single revert. It is not an edit war: there is one revert, nobody pushed back, and no edit points to a real-world event (the festival runs late August to early September). It is unclear why the sources were stripped and why the tag was removed.

briefs.headline: Es-wiki page on amateur Buenos Aires five-a-side team tagged for deletion; no news
briefs.summary: On es-wiki, user Elpibejanson created "Mantequinha", which the creation summary describes as an amateur football club founded in 2026 in Buenos Aires by a group of friends who play in "TIFA". Patroller CarlosEduardoPA added a deletion template with Twinkle Lite about 80 seconds later. After that the creator made two small edits ("puse un cuadro") and a new temporary account made one ("nada importante"), which look like tries to remove or work around the tag. I couldn't read any of the five diffs: Wikipedia says none of the revisions exist, which most likely means the page has already been deleted. So this rests on the graph's metadata and edit summaries only. It's a non-notable self-promotional page, not a real-world event, and there's no reason to keep watching it.

briefs.headline: Unsourced allegation about Cherokee councilor's family added twice and quickly reverted
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia stub on Daryl Legg, the Cherokee Nation tribal council member for District 6, got two near-identical additions within about three minutes. One came from a temporary account (rev 1380882650) and one from a new account, Stanleeew (rev 1380883112). Both added the claim that a named family member had driven drunk and caused a crash that killed a child, and that a "cover up" was under way. Neither cited a source. The anti-vandalism patroller Materialscientist reverted both within about 2.5 minutes (revs 1380882715 and 1380883347), so the page is back to its one-sentence stub. The 774 "churn" the scout flagged is just two additions and their two reverts, not a real expansion of the article. The edits read like the same person or a coordinated campaign pushing allegations from outside Wikipedia. This could mean there's a real local incident or rumour circulating, but nothing in the graph confirms it: there's no sourced edit, no other-language page activity and no related pages moving. We treat it as an unsourced attack on a living person's family, not as news, and we deliberately don't repeat the family member's name or details here.

briefs.headline: Cherokee councilor page: no new activity after unsourced allegation was reverted
briefs.summary: Nothing new has happened on the English Wikipedia page for Daryl Legg, the Cherokee Nation District 6 council member, since our last brief. The graph still holds only four edits. A temporary account (rev 1380882650) and a new account, Stanleeew (rev 1380883112), each added an unsourced claim that a family member caused a fatal drunk-driving crash and that a "cover up" was under way. The patroller Materialscientist reverted both within minutes (revs 1380882715 and 1380883347). I read the second addition and its revert, and the page is back to its one-sentence stub. No sourced edits, no other-language pages and no related pages have moved, so nothing confirms a real event. We're treating this as a BLP attack (unsourced claims about a living person) that has been contained, not as news. The scout was right not to open a new story; this one should stay merged with the tracked vandalism story.

briefs.headline: Genre edits by one temporary account on three pop pages, reverted; no news trigger
briefs.summary: This cluster comes from one temporary account (~2026-55473-37). It added "Teen pop" to the genre lists on Jessica Simpson (rev 1381271877) and Fantasy (Mariah Carey song) (rev 1381271460). On Cry Me a River (Justin Timberlake song) it went further, replacing "Funk" and "pop" with "Teen pop" (rev 1381269814). Tbhotch, an experienced editor, reverted the Simpson change ("Teen pop is pop") and the Cry Me a River change ("unsourced claim"). The Fantasy addition was still in place as of the last edit in the story. The rest is routine upkeep: Wherelovelives renamed a chart row to "Poland Airplay" on Fantasy (rev 1381272560) and made a similar "fix" edit on Cry Me a River. Nothing points to a death, anniversary or release: only English Wikipedia is involved, the changes are small, and no facts about a real-world event were added. This is a common kind of low-level unsourced genre editing, not news.

briefs.headline: fa-wiki adds unsourced "262 kg world record" claim to Iranian weightlifter Alireza Yousefi
briefs.summary: Seven edits in about 10 minutes on the Persian Wikipedia biography of Alireza Yousefi, an Iranian super-heavyweight lifter who won gold at the 2018 Youth Olympics. Editor "Guard active" added a photo of him in a Foolad Khuzestan shirt captioned "world heavyweight record holder" (rev 44791515). The same editor then added a lead sentence saying Yousefi holds the world heavyweight clean-and-jerk record at 262 kg (rev 44791527), with no new source. The other edits are punctuation fiddling by a temporary account. Dexbot's AI filter auto-reverted one of them, which only removed extra full stops (rev 44791577), so this is not an edit war or real vandalism. The 262 kg claim could point to a recent real result, such as a record in the new IWF weight classes, but I can't confirm it: no other language versions or related pages are moving, and the claim is uncited. Treat it as an unverified claim worth a quick check, not as confirmed news.

briefs.headline: Two unrelated new German Wikipedia articles: historic Neustadt mill and vendor 'Pakera Score'
briefs.summary: This cluster is two unrelated new articles on de.wikipedia, and neither is tied to a news event. First, AF666 created "Kronenmühle (Neustadt)" (rev 271442722), a sourced local-history stub about a medieval watermill on the Floßbach in Winzingen, Neustadt an der Weinstraße. It covers the mill's ownership by the Branchweiler hospital and later the Jesuits, and its 1823 auction. M2k~dewiki then removed the infobox status "abgerissen" (demolished) because it contradicts the article text saying the premises are now used commercially (rev 271443036). Zollernalb made small fixes. Second, the "Pakera Score" vendor article was already covered in the earlier brief. After it, Lutheraner added an edit with the comment "SLA+", which on de.wikipedia means a speedy-deletion request (rev 271442941). Wikipedia now reports that revision as missing, which suggests the promotional article has already been deleted. I couldn't read that diff, so this is inferred from the edit comment and the missing revision. There were no reverts, only one language and no outside hook, so this is routine wiki housekeeping.

briefs.headline: New German Wikipedia article on vendor's 'Pakera Score' packaging metric; no news event
briefs.summary: The 9.4k churn comes from one new article, not a rewrite or an event. MarleneR1984, an account with only 2 edits, created "Pakera Score" on de.wikipedia (rev 271442788). The article calls it a proprietary scoring system inside the Pakera packaging software that rolls logistics efficiency, safety, compliance and sustainability into one number. It sets the score against the EU Packaging Regulation (EU) 2025/40 (PPWR). Its main source for the product is the vendor's own help page (pakera.com), and the edit comment calls it "the first relevant logistics score in the EU", which reads as promotional. After that, regular editors M2k~dewiki and Lutheraner made small cleanup edits: adding a category (rev 271442847), formatting and a references section. There are no reverts, no other languages and no outside news hook. The article might get flagged for relevance or promotion, but that would be wiki housekeeping, not news.

briefs.headline: Persian Wikipedia's Kazan article hit by short-lived vandalism, not news
briefs.summary: All five edits to the fawiki article on Kazan (Q900) over about 4.5 minutes were vandalism and its cleanup, with no link to any real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-56063-54) tacked a derogatory phrase onto the lead paragraph saying the city "has many paid girls" (rev 44780314). Dexbot's Shahbaz AI anti-vandalism system reverted it automatically. Klaser35 then put a similar slur into the article's opening sentence ("Kazan, full of paid girls") under the misleading edit summary "typo fix" (rev 44780339), and took it out again in two steps (44780353, 44780356). The article now looks clean, apart from a leftover double space. There is no other-language activity in the graph and no factual content changed. The one open question is whether Klaser35 and the temporary account are the same person; the timing and wording suggest so, but that isn't proven.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Raúl Rangel page: fake club move to América and insults, reverted
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-55859-59) made three edits to the infobox of Chivas goalkeeper Raúl Rangel's en-wiki article, and two established editors (Ceilingbumps, Asukite) reverted them. The diffs show plain vandalism. The birthplace was changed from Zapotlán el Grande to "Tel Aviv, Israel", the height to "1.40 cm"/"1.50 cm", the caption to a Spanish insult ("El Pendejo Tala"), and the current club from Guadalajara to "Club Ametica"/"Club America" with made-up shirt numbers (67, 41). None of these edits had a source. The switch to Club América, Guadalajara's arch-rival, looks like rivalry trolling, not a real transfer. No other pages or languages were touched. I have no evidence of any real-world news about Rangel, and the page is back to the correct version.

briefs.headline: Raúl Rangel page vandalism reverted, but fake height of '1.50 cm' may still be live
briefs.summary: This is still plain vandalism, with no real-world news behind it. One temporary account (~2026-55859-59) made three unsourced edits to the infobox of Chivas goalkeeper Raúl Rangel on en-wiki. It changed his birthplace to "Tel Aviv", his height to "1.40/1.50 cm", the caption to an insult ("El Pendejo Tala") and his club to rival "Club America" with made-up shirt numbers 67 and 41. Ceilingbumps undid the first edit and Asukite rolled back the third. The earlier brief said the page was fully restored, which looks wrong. Asukite's rollback (rev 1380899712) restores the caption, birthplace, club and number but not the height. The middle edit (rev 1380899480, -50 bytes, height 1.90 m → "1.50 cm" with its source tag removed) was never reverted. The byte changes add up to -50, which fits that edit still being in place. I couldn't check the live page, and the diffs for 1380899480 and 1380899679 overlap oddly, so this is likely but not confirmed. It needs a manual check and a fix if the height is still wrong. Note: no other story is tracked on this page, so this task is about the tracked story itself, not a second incident. No other pages or languages were involved.

briefs.headline: es-wiki 'Frente Obrero' vandalism stays removed; no new edits since last check
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked cleanup and has no real-world news hook. The graph shows the same five edits on es-wiki 'Frente Obrero (España)' and nothing after Blitzo170's rev 175885172, so the anti-vandal bot SeroBOT has not put the text back a third time. I read all five diffs. Temporary account ~2026-55781-26 twice undid antisemitic changes to the lead: "organizaciones" had become "razas gentiles", and an added line spoke of the «goyim» of Núcleo Nacional and "Antisionismo" (revs 175885025, 175885087). Each time, SeroBOT restored the vandalised version within seconds (175885027, 175885091). Blitzo170 then made the same fix. The first removal was larger (−1313 bytes against −904 later), so it probably also cut some sourced text that the second fix kept. I can't confirm that because the diff output was truncated. Also unconfirmed: the source cited for "Antisionismo" is about a banner reading "Fuera el Islam", so the original word may have been changed too. This is a bot false-positive pattern, not an edit war between people. Close it unless the page moves again.

briefs.headline: Vandalism cleanup on es-wiki 'Frente Obrero' article; anti-vandal bot puts slurs back twice
briefs.summary: There is no real-world event behind this. It is vandalism and cleanup on one Spanish Wikipedia article about the Spanish group Frente Obrero. The lead had been altered with antisemitic wording: "organizaciones" became "razas gentiles" (gentile races), and a line was added about criticising the «goyim» of Núcleo Nacional and "Antisionismo" (anti-Zionism). The graph doesn't hold that earlier edit. The bot's revert comment points to temporary account ~2026-55760-26, but I couldn't read that diff. Temporary account ~2026-55781-26 removed the bad text twice (revs 175885025 and 175885087). Each time the anti-vandal bot SeroBOT reverted it within seconds and put the wording back (I read rev 175885091; I didn't read the first bot revert, 175885027). Registered editor Blitzo170 then made the same removal (rev 175885172). The article is clean as of the last edit in the graph. The large size changes come from repeated removing and restoring of the same paragraph, not a rewrite. There's no news hook, no other pages or languages, and no human edit war. It's worth a quick check that SeroBOT doesn't revert again.

briefs.headline: Small revert dispute over Air Canada route listing on BWI Airport page
briefs.summary: Two registered editors swapped one revert each on the English Wikipedia article for Baltimore/Washington International Airport, about five minutes apart. Mrgoggins90 undid an earlier removal by Danners430 (rev 1381197694) and put back a 345-byte destinations-table row saying Air Canada serves Toronto–Pearson and Montreal–Trudeau. That row cites a WBAL-TV story headlined "Air Canada to resume service at BWI-Marshall this spring". Danners430 then removed the same row again, saying "once again" unsourced content was being added "along with the good additions". The diff I could see shows only the cited Air Canada row, so it is unclear which part Danners430 considers unsourced. It may have been in the earlier edits that I could not see. This looks like a low-intensity content dispute between two people on one page, with no other languages or editors involved, not a breaking event. If the WBAL report is accurate, Air Canada restarting BWI flights is ordinary airline route news, and I have not checked it independently.

briefs.headline: Thai Wikipedia adds full royal title for Wat Arun abbot's Somdet elevation; other monk's 2569 entry cites Gazette
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked story. On Thai Wikipedia, an anonymous editor expanded the BE 2569 (2026) ecclesiastical-titles entry for Somkiat Kowito, the abbot of Wat Arun (rev 13355802, +831). The new text says he was raised to Somdet Phra Ratchakhana, the senior monk rank, and gives his full title as written on the royal appointment plate (suphannabat): "Somdet Phra Wachirakowitthamet ... residing at Wat Arunratchawararam, Bangkok". The same editor then removed a shorter duplicate line that another editor had added minutes before (13355793 added it, 13355805 removed it). This was cleanup, not a revert war. A later edit by อมฤตาลัย changed formatting only (13355808). On the "Somdet Phra Ratchakhana" list page, two other registered editors added him to the Mahanikai table with a BE 2569 date and a birth date of 6 Sept 1943 (BE 2486), and to the current-reign list (13355806, 13355809). The edits agree with each other and nobody reverted anything. New this round: someone edited the page of another monk, Somdet Phra Maha Wachirathibodi (Phi Suchato), whose own BE 2569 Somdet elevation was already listed. The edit (13355816) swapped a reused reference for a direct link to a Royal Gazette (Ratchakitcha) proclamation of title appointments. That suggests the abbot's elevation may be part of a wider royal batch in 2026, but I can't confirm that from the edits: the abbot's own entry still cites no source, and the activity is Thai-only.

briefs.headline: Thai Wikipedia: Wat Arun abbot shown elevated to Somdet rank, now Somdet Phra Wachirakowitthamet
briefs.summary: Within about 25 minutes, three editors on Thai Wikipedia updated pages to show that Phra Phrom Watcharamethi (Somkiat Kowito), abbot of Wat Arun in Bangkok and a member of the Supreme Sangha Council, has been raised to Somdet Phra Ratchakhana. That is the senior rank of Thai monks just below the Supreme Patriarch. His new title is Somdet Phra Wachirakowitthamet. Edits to his bio changed the infobox and lead to the new title and rank, switched his honorific to "Than Chao Prakhun", and added a 2026 (BE 2569) entry to the ecclesiastical-titles section. One edit quotes the full title as inscribed on the royal appointment plate (suphannabat). The same editors renamed him in Wat Arun's list of abbots and raised the count of living Somdets from 18 to 19 (Mahanikai sect 11 to 12). Edits on three related pages agree with each other, with no reverts, which looks like a real title appointment rather than vandalism. However, none of the new text cites a source, the date of the elevation isn't given, the activity is Thai-only, and no other monks' pages moved, so it's not clear whether this was a single appointment or part of a wider royal batch.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki articles on Harz mining ditch and a geologist who died in 2021; routine
briefs.summary: This story now covers two new German Wikipedia articles. Their only link is a new-page patroller, ZweiteWurzelAus16, who did small cleanup edits on both. The first is Ludengraben, the historic Unterharz mining ditch from the earlier brief. Since then there has only been a markup fix to the bold/italic formatting in the opening sentence (rev 271492486). The second is a biography of the GDR geologist Karl R. Wächter, created by Hejkal (rev 271492488, +4353 bytes). It covers his work at the Bergakademie Freiberg, the 1967 textbook "Historische Geologie" he co-wrote, and his work protecting geological sites around Staßfurt. It gives his death date as 15 November 2021, sourced to a published death notice, so this is not a fresh obituary and there's no current-event trigger. The follow-up edits are normal housekeeping by several experienced editors: categories, a sort key and a person-data (Personendaten) fix (rev 271492584). There were no reverts and no other language versions changed. The two pages have no topical link beyond both touching on central German geology and mining.

briefs.headline: De-wiki biography of GDR geologist Karl R. Wächter still getting small fixes; routine
briefs.summary: The new German article on geologist Karl R. Wächter (died 2021) has only had more small cleanup edits. Hejkal, who created the article, filled in the full citation for a publication on the Westeregeln clay-pit geotope: Dr. Ziethen Verlag, Oschersleben 2015, pages 406–421 (rev 271492867). That entry was cited as 2016 in the earlier brief, but the article says 2015. Guardian of Arcadia fixed an italic markup (lint) error in the citation of a 1970 paper on the tectonics of the Elbtalzone (rev 271492856). All editors so far are registered accounts. There have been no reverts, no anonymous edits and no edits in other languages. The companion page, Ludengraben, has had no new edits. Nothing ties these edits to a current event, which matches the scout's read.

briefs.headline: German Harz ditch article expanded; small revert fight over castle studio section
briefs.summary: The scout's note is out of date. Since the last brief, Ludengraben has been edited again, and a third German page, Schloss Bodenburg, has seen reverts. Sarkana, who created Ludengraben, greatly expanded it (rev 271493296, +3890 bytes). The article is now titled by its other name, Kochs-Graben, and gains an infobox (9.5 km long, built from the mid-1720s to 1745), plus a sourced history: mine director Koch built the ditch without permission from the Stolberg counts, and it only began operating in 1745. On Schloss Bodenburg, a temporary (effectively anonymous) account, ~2026-56092-95, deleted the section on the 2007 Corten-steel artist's studio twice with no explanation (revs 271493632, 271493710). It also changed the text to say visitors can see only "parts of" the castle park, not the whole park (rev 271493681). AxelHH and Aspiriniks reverted each change within minutes. It looks like a small edit war or unexplained-deletion vandalism by one account. Nothing ties it to a real-world event, though the park-access wording could reflect a local change I can't verify. No other languages moved, and the Wächter biography had no new edits.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on historic Harz mining ditch Ludengraben; routine cleanup
briefs.summary: Sarkana created a new German Wikipedia article on 'Ludengraben' (rev 271492398, +1856 bytes). It describes the Langen-Luden-Breitensteiner Graben, also called the Kochs-Graben: an artificial mining-water ditch in the Unterharz that forms part of the Silberhütter Kunstgraben. The article cites Christian Zacharias Koch's 1810 account of mining operations at Straßberg. Within about five minutes, two experienced editors made the usual follow-up edits. M2k~dewiki added the category "Graben des Unterharzer Teich- und Grabensystems" (rev 271492407) and made a small fix, and ZweiteWurzelAus16 moved a footnote after a comma (rev 271492472). There were no reverts, and nothing ties this to a current event. The "sizable churn" in the scout note is simply the article being created. I didn't read the last two zero-byte or minor revisions (271492415, 271492486).

briefs.headline: New de-wiki biography of GDR geologist Karl R. Wächter is still being tidied up; routine
briefs.summary: Since the last brief, the German article on geologist Karl R. Wächter (died 2021, created by Hejkal) has only had more housekeeping. Miebner added his GND authority ID (the German national library's identifier) and a category (rev 271492770). Hejkal, the creator, added a 2016 publication on the geology of a clay pit at the Kalkberg near Westeregeln to the list of selected works (rev 271492827). Other editors made small dash and lint fixes. All 9 editors are registered accounts, and there were no reverts, no anonymous edits and no edits in other languages. The companion page, Ludengraben (a historic mining ditch in the Harz), has had no further edits. Nothing points to a current-event trigger, which matches the scout's read.

briefs.headline: Student workshop on pt-wiki hearing-rehab article stops at 16 edits; one bad link remains
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity on pt-wiki "Habilitação e reabilitação auditiva" since rev 73259681. The UNINASSAU "Oficina Semana Ubíqua" class exercise, supervised by Profa Natalia Garcia, ended at 16 small edits by 8 registered accounts. The scout counted 4 editors, but the dossier shows 8, and none of them edited any other page. Diffs show wikilinking only. I can now answer the open question from the earlier brief: Melyssa Rodrigues first linked "linguagem oral" (spoken language) to "Língua brasileira de sinais" (Brazilian Sign Language) in 73259590, and Adriel Micael da Silva later removed that link. The one problem still standing is Weslem Henrique Lima Da Silva's 73259676, which links "linguagem" to "Linguagem brasileira de sinais". That is the wrong topic and probably a red link, so it is worth a quick cleanup. This is not a news event, not vandalism and not an edit war.

briefs.headline: University workshop adds wikilinks to pt-wiki auditory rehabilitation article
briefs.summary: Four registered accounts made ten small edits (+4 to +49 bytes) over about 11 minutes to the pt-wiki article "Habilitação e reabilitação auditiva". Every edit summary names a classroom exercise: "Oficina Semana Ubíqua - UNINASSAU - Supervisão Profa Natalia Garcia". One of the accounts, NatáliaGarciaFono, appears to belong to the supervising speech-therapy instructor. In the two diffs I read, the only change is new wikilinks on existing words ("acústicas" now links to Acústica, and "aparelho de amplificação sonora" now links to its own article). No prose was changed. There were no reverts, and none of these editors edited any other page. This is a supervised student editing workshop, not a news event. I only read 2 of the 10 diffs, but the other eight have the same summary and similar small sizes.

briefs.headline: Student workshop wikilinks pt-wiki hearing-rehab article; a few links point wrong
briefs.summary: The supervised UNINASSAU class workshop ("Oficina Semana Ubíqua", led by Profa Natalia Garcia, who appears to edit as NatáliaGarciaFono) has grown to 16 small edits by 8 registered accounts over about 20 minutes, all on pt-wiki "Habilitação e reabilitação auditiva". None of the accounts edited any other page. Diffs I read show wikilinking only, with no prose changes: "acústicas" now links to Acústica (73259681) and "aparelho de amplificação sonora" to its own article (73259651). The two negative-delta edits are housekeeping, not removals of content. Rayssa Maria removed the hearing-aid link and restored it a minute later (73259645/73259651). Adriel Micael da Silva removed a wrong link that sent "linguagem oral" (spoken language) to Brazilian Sign Language, and also dropped the "habilidades auditivas" link (73259654). One link still looks wrong: Weslem Henrique Lima Da Silva linked "linguagem" to "Linguagem brasileira de sinais" (73259676), the wrong topic and probably not a real article title. This is not a news event, not vandalism and not an edit war, but an editor may want to check link quality. Uncertainty: I read 5 of the 16 diffs and did not find out who first added the sign-language link.

briefs.headline: Raw milk article: lone editor's pro-raw-milk rewrite reverted twice by patrollers
briefs.summary: On English Wikipedia's "Raw milk" article, one account (Brazilianhistory, 2 edits total) made two edits to the lead. The first, about 6 minutes in, turned "Proponents have said that raw milk has better flavor, nutrition..." into a flat factual claim ("The raw (unpasteurised) milk has better flavor..."). The second edit, logged as "lait cru" (French for "raw milk"), did the same and also deleted the sourced sentences on medical consensus about milk-borne disease risk and on countries regulating raw milk sales. Two different patrollers reverted the edits within minutes: Leaf.Sheap ("Should not be in wikivoice") and Knitsey ("Unexplained removal"). This is a single editor pushing one point of view and being reverted by the usual patrollers. It is not a two-sided edit war and doesn't show any real-world news event. The scout's "1071 churn" is the same text being added and then removed again. I didn't read the two reverts' diffs; their edit summaries and size changes match the edits they undo.

briefs.headline: New id-wiki bio of streamer Reza Auditore used for religion-based meme vandalism
briefs.summary: Jengglot created a new Indonesian Wikipedia page on Kick/YouTube streamer Reza Auditore (rev 30093563). It reads like a fan profile, cites a single ggwp.id article, and includes a paragraph about a community joke that he is Jewish ("Yahuditore"). Later edits push the joke further. A temporary account added "Reza auditore beragama yahudi" ("Reza Auditore is Jewish") at the top of the page (30093602). Jengglot then captioned a generic stock-style "Traditional Jewish Portrait in Tallit and Kippah" image as "Foto Diri Reza Auditore" ("photo of Reza Auditore") (30093616). This looks like a fan community trolling the page with a religion-based meme about a living person, not a news event. Nothing has been reverted yet, and the page is likely to be deleted or need BLP cleanup. Two small diffs (30093610, 30093617) could not be retrieved.

briefs.headline: New Galician article on gay pride flags translated from Spanish, then tidied
briefs.summary: User Kd6awi25t created the Galician Wikipedia article "Bandeiras do orgullo gai" by translating the Spanish article "Banderas del orgullo gay" (+9,758 bytes). It covers the history of Gilbert Baker's rainbow flags from 1978 and gay men's flag designs proposed online since 2018. About two minutes later the same user removed 2,260 bytes: an image gallery whose file links were broken (the Spanish "Archivo:" prefix had been left in) and one paragraph about the Tumblr-designed gay men's flag. Since the creator made this cut to their own text, it reads as self-correction, not a dispute. After that, regular editor Breogan2008 (446 edits) and two others made small fixes, including adding a portal and an LGBTIQ+ category. There were no reverts, nothing points to a real-world event, and no other languages were involved. This is routine content creation and cleanup.

briefs.headline: Zh-wiki Ringling Bros. page: temp account keeps adding fake "2024 animal show" list
briefs.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. This is low-level vandalism or a hoax on the zh-wiki article 玲玲馬戲團 (Ringling Bros. circus). A temporary account (~2026-56261-74) added about 3.3k bytes. A patroller, Ghostingb, rolled it back with AdvancedRollback; Ghostingb's recent edits are quick single touches across many unrelated zh pages, which is how patrollers work. The account then re-added the same material, 3,250 bytes under the heading "Yes Lives World Of Animals (2024 Show)" (rev 95195558). That edit swaps out the page's existing related-films section (The Greatest Showman) for an English-language numbered list of roughly 200 wild species, including great white sharks, a sperm whale, a colossal squid and a narwhal, none of which a touring circus could plausibly show. The account's later edits (95195584, 95195612) just add and then remove two entries (Australian Pelican, Wisent). The Scout guessed a rewrite or translation, but this is neither: it's one account's repeated insertion, with no sources and no matching activity in other languages. Uncertain: I couldn't load the diffs for the first insertion, the rollback, or the final +33 edit by 外掛系統123 (rev 95195674), so I don't know whether the list was removed again or is still on the page.

briefs.headline: Brighton beat Crystal Palace 5–0 in Premier League round 7; season and league pages updated
briefs.summary: The edits now confirm the opponent that the earlier brief could only guess at. On the 2026–27 Premier League page, rev 1380884880 fills in the results grid as Brighton 5–0 Crystal Palace, linked through the Brighton–Palace rivalry article. Rev 1380884646 makes that game the season's biggest home win, dated 18 October 2026. The same edit adds two more results from that round: Bournemouth 2–0 Sunderland and Leeds 1–1 Manchester United. Another edit (rev 1380885607) logs a red card for Sunderland's Kevin Danso. On Brighton's season page, the summary table now shows three home wins and a draw (13 goals for, 1 against) and adds a seventh straight "W" to the form line (rev 1380884819). Six editors across two English Wikipedia pages made small, consistent edits with no reverts, so this is routine post-match upkeep. The only open question is a "pos4" position line extended with "16p". It may track another team, possibly Palace, and I couldn't work out what it refers to.

briefs.headline: Brighton logged as 5–0 winners in Premier League round 7, opponent apparently Crystal Palace
briefs.summary: Three registered editors updated the Matches section of the 2026–27 Brighton & Hove Albion season page within about three minutes, filling in a just-finished game. The first edit added a 5–0 win ("W") and goals from an own goal by Canvot (4'), plus Gómez (7'), Ayari (10'), Kostoulas (49') and Hinshelwood (84'), with Robert Jones as referee. The next two edits fixed the spelling of Jaydee Canvot's name, added attendance of 31,440, added the official premierleague.com match report link, and labelled the game round 7. The opponent isn't in the diffs I read. Canvot's own goal and the yellow card for Daichi Kamada suggest it was Crystal Palace, but that is my inference, not something the edits state. Nothing was reverted, the editors agree with each other, and only English Wikipedia changed. This looks like a routine post-match update, though a 5–0 derby result would get some sports coverage.

briefs.headline: Daniel Levy page: one unexplained edit reverted, no sign of news
briefs.summary: An edit labelled "HI" by temporary account ~2026-56112-43 added 50 bytes to the English article on former Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy (rev 1381150582). DoggieLicc undid it about 2.5 minutes later (rev 1381150784). Fourteen seconds apart, PhilKnight restored the edit by reverting DoggieLicc (rev 1381151719), then reverted his own change (rev 1381151743). The page now matches DoggieLicc's version. A revert followed almost at once by a self-revert looks like a misclick on the rollback button, not an edit war. The diff tool cut off the text before the changed part, so I couldn't see the 50 added bytes. Still, the "HI" summary, the quick undo and the lack of follow-up suggest a test edit or minor vandalism. The paragraph shown in the diffs already says Levy stepped down as executive chairman on 4 September 2025, which is old news. Only one language and one page are involved, so there's no sign of a new real-world development.

briefs.headline: Brandon McNulty recorded as 2026 Veneto Classic winner on three Wikipedias
briefs.summary: Editors on three Wikipedias recorded American cyclist Brandon McNulty as the winner of the 2026 Veneto Classic, all within about 15 minutes of each other. On enwiki, a temporary account added McNulty (USA, team UEX) to the Veneto Classic winners list under 2026 (rev 1380882587). About a minute later, Walterwiki updated nlwiki to make McNulty the latest winner of the race's 6th edition (rev 72094983). On frwiki, a temporary account added "Veneto Classic (2026)" to the main wins in McNulty's infobox, along with Tour de Croatie and Tour du Luxembourg wins (revs 240489041, 240489164). Philasc then cut the infobox back, citing the guideline on which races belong there (rev 240489290). Experienced editor FromZeFild re-added the Veneto Classic 2026 win in the year-by-year results instead (rev 240489379). That trim was a cleanup, not an edit war. Several separate accounts reported the same result in three languages, so this looks like a real race result. But I didn't check any source outside Wikipedia, and none of the edits I read cites one. This is a small sporting result, not breaking news.

briefs.headline: Routine cleanup on two Harry Bosch novel pages; no news hook
briefs.summary: Two registered editors made small maintenance edits to two English Wikipedia articles on Michael Connelly's Harry Bosch novels, The Concrete Blonde and Angels Flight. Lieutenant Cotton put each release date into the {{Start date}} template (1994-06-01 and 1999-01-28). The dates themselves did not change. Itzcuauhtli11 added a {{long plot}} cleanup tag to Angels Flight. The same editor's "revert" on The Concrete Blonde undid an earlier removal of an existing {{long plot|date=June 2026}} tag, which restores the tag. It is not a content dispute. There was no back-and-forth reverting, no anonymous or vandal activity, and no other languages were involved. These look like typical edits from people working through a series of novel articles, not a reaction to anything happening in the world.

briefs.headline: Persian Wikipedia: small vandalism run on three pages, all reverted by bot
briefs.summary: The three Persian pages are connected, but not by a news event. Each one got a single edit from a temporary account, and the anti-vandalism bot Dexbot (the Shahbaz system) automatically undid each edit within about 20 seconds. Temporary account ~2026-56088-79 made two of the edits. On the biography of Mohammad-Reza Jalali Naini, it dropped "Naini" from the name and image filename, changed the birthplace from Nain to Kashan, deleted the death date (1389 SH, i.e. 2010) and place, and changed his children to "none." On the TV series Ghoorbagheh (The Frog), it swapped cast member Houman Seyyedi for "Seyed Mohammad Reza Jalali." So both edits push the name "Mohammad Reza Jalali," which looks like someone writing in their own or a friend's name rather than reporting news. The third edit came from a different temporary account (~2026-55939-05): it renamed Noah to "Ali Laporta" in the infobox and lead sentence and added nonsense words, which is clear vandalism. No other sources and no edits in other languages back up any change, and since all three edits were reverted, there is nothing to report.

briefs.headline: Persian Wikipedia: bot-reverted vandalism run spreads to a fourth page, "Verse of Stoning"
briefs.summary: I'm updating this story with a fourth Persian page, آیه رجم (the "Verse of Stoning," a disputed Quranic verse). It fits the same pattern of single edits by temporary accounts, each auto-reverted within seconds by Dexbot's Shahbaz anti-vandalism system. A new temporary account (~2026-56049-84) deleted a sourced passage of 1,383 bytes. The passage cited al-Kafi and Majlisi's Mir'at al-Uqul, and reported that Shia scholars fall into three camps on the verse. The account replaced it with one unsourced line claiming "Shia scholars unanimously reject this" (rev 44781129). Dexbot restored the original text 15 seconds later (rev 44781131). This is a one-sided POV deletion on a religiously sensitive page, not a news event. The "large churn" is just one removal and its revert, and only two editors touched the page. Earlier in this story, unchanged and drawn from the prior brief rather than re-read diffs: edits on the Jalali Naini biography, Ghoorbagheh (The Frog) and Noah pages were self-insertion or nonsense vandalism, all reverted. This edit came from a different temporary account than those, so I see no sign of a coordinated campaign, though I can't rule out that the same person is behind more than one temporary account.

briefs.headline: It-wiki Vanvitelli University page: history section moved out after bot reverts

The removed text is sourced, uncontroversial background history, and no other pages or languages are involved. The removals look like cleanup, not vandalism, though nobody has confirmed the content was actually added to the target articles. This could turn into a small edit war if the bot or a human puts the section back.

briefs.headline: Bigg Boss Malayalam S8: Nilina evicted on Day 42, editors update the page

Routine fan editing of a TV show; all of it is unsourced on-air detail, so the eviction claim is likely but not independently confirmed.

briefs.headline: Confectionery store: four more copyedits, no vandalism, still no news event

briefs.headline: Shockley "Mario Shockley III" hoax returns a third time and is reverted; rest is cleanup

briefs.headline: Confectionery store: unexplained edit moves Googie-era decor from 1950s to \"1900\"

briefs.headline: Confectionery store gets routine copyedits after vandalism cleanup; no news event

briefs.headline: Confectionery store: page-blanking vandal reverted twice; copyedits continue; no news event

briefs.headline: 1 News–Verian NZ poll (15–19 Oct): preferred-PM row added after the party-vote row

briefs.headline: Luis Malagón page: vandal edit blanking infobox reverted within a minute

briefs.headline: Routine upkeep on article for Fielder–Oppenheim Elizabeth Holmes documentary

briefs.headline: NZ 'Moon Man' forecaster Ken Ring has died, family says; Wikipedia updated

The only source is one Stuff report I can see cited, and the exact date of death is unknown. Only English Wikipedia is involved, with three named editors.

briefs.headline: Scorpion stub on fr.wiki: wrong-photo cleanup settled; nothing new, no news

briefs.headline: Scorpion stub on fr.wiki: wrong photo removed after clumsy edits; no real-world news
briefs.summary: This is an image fix on the French article for Birulatus astartiae, a scorpion species described by Stathi & Lourenço in 2003. It is not news. briefs.headline: New es-wiki bio of Puerto Rican author Carlos Colón Rodríguez tagged for speedy deletion

briefs.headline: Suspect in Helen Haines attack remanded in custody after first court hearing

briefs.headline: Czech Wikipedia cleans up "Josef Polášek" disambiguation pages; no news trigger

All this happened within about 12 minutes, in one language. It looks like a disagreement over how to organise the pages, not an edit war or vandalism. I see nothing that points to a current event.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki biography of pianist Gabriele Baldocci, then routine cleanup

briefs.headline: Japan's MMX Mars-moon probe page shifts to past tense, hinting launch has happened
briefs.summary: Since about 19 Oct 2026 (UTC), nine named editors have worked on the English Wikipedia article for JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission over roughly 5.6 hours. There are no reverts. The edit comments point to a mission milestone, most likely the launch: one editor added an "elapsed mission duration" (+71), then added +508 bytes with no comment. Another added +781 bytes of citations. A third "changed some future tense to past/present tense." The remaining edits are small cleanups of typos and citation placement. This is still unconfirmed. So the launch claim, its date and whether it succeeded all rest on edit comments, not on the edits themselves. The next step is to re-pull the diffs (especially 1381092211 and 1381101312) and check jawiki.

briefs.headline: Japan's MMX Phobos probe page now says it "launched in 2026"; details unverified
briefs.summary: On 19 Oct 2026 (UTC), several registered editors updated the English Wikipedia article on JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which aims to return samples from Phobos. None of the edits were reverted. The current article intro describes MMX as a probe that "launched in 2026." The edit comments support that: one editor added an "elapsed mission duration" (+71 bytes) and then added +508 bytes with no comment, another added citations (+781), and a third "changed some future tense to past/present tense." Together these point to a launch that has just happened. One anonymous edit also hit the Japanese article (火星衛星探査計画, -1572 bytes, no comment) about 1.6 hours before the English activity. That edit could be a launch-related update or something unrelated. The edits on the Phobos article are style cleanups and have nothing to do with the launch. Every diff fetch failed again, including the Japanese one. So the launch date, time and early status (successful separation, contact with the probe) remain unconfirmed by edit text. The evidence is the article's current intro plus the edit comments.

briefs.headline: Explosion and fire at CFB Wainwright kills 4 soldiers; PM Carney orders flags lowered
briefs.summary: On the afternoon of Oct 17, an explosion in a training area at CFB Wainwright, a Canadian Forces base in Alberta, set off a large fire. That is the account in a new en-wiki article that several editors have been building, with citations to CBC live updates and Global News. The death toll in the article has moved. Global News first reported at least 7 dead and dozens injured, citing unnamed military sources. CBC later reported 7 from its own sources, which DND did not confirm. The latest edit (rev 1380902268) cuts the toll to 4 service members and cites a CBC item headlined "Carney confirms 4 deaths". Defence Minister McGuinty had earlier confirmed deaths and injuries but gave no numbers. The cause is officially "under investigation". A DND official told CBC there is no sign of terrorism, and an earlier claim in the article about ordnance hitting an underground gas line was removed because no source supported it. Carney gave a national address on Oct 18 ordering flags on federal buildings to half-mast. The base is under a communications lockdown, and the local municipal district said late on Oct 17 that the fire was being held. The edits look careful and well sourced, with no reverts or vandalism. One caveat: I have not opened the CBC links myself, and the official count of 4 is less than the 7 reported by the media, so the toll could still change.

briefs.headline: CFB Wainwright explosion: Carney confirms 4 soldiers dead, dozens seriously wounded
briefs.summary: Three editors made three new edits to en-wiki's "CFB Wainwright fire" article. Together they replace the earlier, unconfirmed media count of at least 7 dead with an official figure. Slaughter-echo (rev 1380901850) added that at a press conference on Oct 18, PM Mark Carney confirmed that 4 service members were killed and dozens seriously wounded. The citation is a CBC live-blog item titled "Carney confirms 4 deaths". Oustsync (rev 1380902268) then changed the infobox to deaths = 4, dropped the "unconfirmed" label on the injuries, and rewrote the lead. The earlier Global News and CBC reports of 7 are kept only as "initial reports". An anonymous editor (rev 1380901653) added categories, including "Gas explosions". That label goes beyond what the article's sources support, since the cause is still officially under investigation. There are no reverts and the editing looks cooperative. I have not opened the CBC source myself, and the gap between the media's 7 and the official 4 has not been explained, so the toll could still change.

The same editor changed the infobox from deaths = 4 to deaths = 4-7 (rev 1380911443); the edit summary admits the 7 comes from "anonymous sources". The official count is still 4 and these diffs don't show any new confirmation, so the article now gives more weight to the unconfirmed number than before. Other editors may challenge this, but so far there have been no reverts. The rest is routine: David O. Johnson removed an honorific and fixed date style (rev 1380916299), an anonymous editor fixed a typo (rev 1380915651), and Slaughter-echo added McGuinty's title as Defence Minister in Reactions (rev 1380917713).
