Caveats: I haven't opened the Global News or CBC sources, and nothing new about the cause appeared.

briefs.headline: CFB Wainwright: account now says munition-sparked grass fire caused blast; 4 dead stands
briefs.summary: Since the last brief, en-wiki's "CFB Wainwright fire" article has had a careful sourcing pass, with no reverts. In the largest edit (rev 1380905125), Patternbuffered rewrote the lead, now citing a DND press release titled "Incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright". The lead now says a fire ignited in a training area on Oct 17 and spread rapidly. It no longer says an explosion started the fire. The edit summary says Global News's military sources now describe a munition sparking a grass fire that then caused an explosion, with no gas line or well involved. The same edit removed the "Gas explosions" category that the previous brief had flagged as unsupported. The diff text I received was cut off before the revised cause sentence in the body, so that detail rests on the edit summary. The same edit made other corrections: the claim that the incident was "fully accidental" became DND's narrower statement that it is under investigation with no sign of terrorism. The communications lockdown is now attributed to posts by family members, and a former officer told CBC that such lockdowns are normal protocol. The edit summary also says the half-mast flag order came from a social media post, not the national address. The toll is unchanged at 4 service members killed and dozens seriously wounded, citing CBC's "Carney confirms 4 deaths". Tahbit (rev 1380907254) added, without a citation, that Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe is sending assistance. The remaining edits only fixed references.

briefs.headline: CFB Wainwright: Governor General issues statement; SAR techs from Winnipeg parachuted in
briefs.summary: Since the last brief, 4 editors (Tahbit, Hwy43, Kungjaada and Slaughter-echo) have made about 10 more edits to en-wiki's "CFB Wainwright fire" article. There were no reverts and the work was cooperative. Most of it was cleanup: citation formatting, past tense, and wording in the Background section, such as the exact 2021 census population of 6,606 and noting that the base borders Wainwright rather than sitting inside it. Two additions are new. Tahbit (revs 1380908235, 1380908411) added that Governor General Louise Arbour, as Commander-in-Chief, issued an official statement from Rideau Hall supporting military members, families and first responders, citing a bare gg.ca URL. Slaughter-echo (rev 1380907642) added that more than a dozen Search & Rescue Technicians from CFB Winnipeg parachuted into the area, citing CTV and a Yahoo News Canada repost of Global News. The Saskatchewan aid line from Premier Scott Moe is still there but still has no citation. None of these edits changed the death toll (4) or the cause (a munition-sparked grass fire, under investigation). Caveat: I have not opened the sources themselves, and the Yahoo source's headline still says 7 dead, the earlier unconfirmed figure.

briefs.headline: CFB Wainwright fire: citation cleanup only, toll still 4 dead; GG statement now properly sourced

DND says the incident is under investigation, with no sign of terrorism. Caveats: I did not open the sources. Earlier briefs noted that the Global News headline still says "7 dead", and I did not check again whether the Saskatchewan aid line has a citation yet. The newsworthy part: the article says she will become state secretary in Hesse's interior ministry under minister Roman Poseck. She replaces Martin Rößler, who is going to the Gießen regional government office from 1 November 2026. That claim cites a Stadt Hanau press release on presse-service.de, which I could not open to check. The follow-up edits were routine tidy-ups by regular editors (sort key, person data, categories, typo fixes — e.g. rev 271490970) plus one small edit by a temporary account, with no reverts. Treat this as a routine new article about a regional political appointment; confidence is moderate because the appointment rests on a single cited source.

briefs.headline: Unrelated low-level disruption on Pixar and 'Fifth grade' pages, reverted by patrollers

briefs.headline: Latvian singer's Wikipedia bio hit by defamatory rewrite, reverted twice by patrollers
briefs.summary: This is not a death or news update. It is BLP vandalism on the Latvian Wikipedia article about singer and teacher Indra Lintiņa-Lučka (b. 1961, Liepāja), who became known in the Atmoda period (1988–1992) performing with Eduards Rozenštrauhs. Nothing points to a real-world event. The motive may be a personal grievance, but that is unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines critically hurt in apparent deliberate car attack, page shows
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Helen Haines, the independent federal MP, has a "2026 attack" section. The edits in this cluster are tidying and adding to that section; the section itself was written earlier. The text says that on 19 October 2026 at 15:35 AEDT she was hit by a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta and taken to hospital with critical injuries (rev 1381086441). It says PM Anthony Albanese called it apparently "a deliberate act," and that the national joint counter-terrorism team (AFP and ASIO) has started investigating alongside state police. These claims are cited to Victoria Police, BBC, ABC, AAP and 7NEWS. Another edit says a 43-year-old man from Tarrawingee, known to police, was driving a white Land Cruiser, was arrested at the scene by a member of the public and had a knife on him; Albanese said later that Haines had surgery the night before (rev 1381080695, citing news.com.au dated 20 October). Four named editors made six edits over about 70 minutes, mostly copyedits plus a photo of the office (rev 1381087510). There were no reverts or disputes and no sign of vandalism. What I can't confirm: I have only the article text and its citations, not the sources. Haines's current condition, the suspect's motive and any charges aren't on the page, and the graph shows no other-language versions or separate article about the attack yet.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines car attack: page edits now copyedits only, no new facts

briefs.headline: Recent-changes patroller reverts low-level vandalism on three unrelated enwiki pages

briefs.headline: No new activity on it-wiki Ecuadorian Communist Party page; rewrite looks finished
briefs.summary: The scout's note says the history rewrite is continuing, but the graph shows no edits after the tracked story was filed. The page has 7 edits in total, and the last one, SurdusVII's "+categoria", came at ts 1792518990, before the prior brief. The only edit the earlier brief didn't describe is Jamessil's −4 byte rev 152992922. Its diff shows only formatting or markup changes, no change to the text. I re-read the main +7359 rev 152992834. It adds a table of presidential election results from 1940 to 2021, sourced to academic books and election archives. Nothing in it mentions a current event, though the access dates of "20 ottobre 2026" match when it was edited. The graph links this page to no other-language versions, so I found no matching activity elsewhere. It's still one page in one language: a single content editor plus two routine maintainers, no reverts and no anonymous editors. This is ordinary article improvement, and this story should be merged with or closed against the tracked routine one. Data-quality caveats remain: the 1944 row shows "91 votes / 91%", and the 1992 FADI candidate is given as Gustavo Jalkh. Both look doubtful, but I haven't checked them against sources.

briefs.headline: Italian Wikipedia's Ecuadorian Communist Party article gets a history rewrite, no news link
briefs.summary: Almost all the churn on it-wiki's "Partito Comunista dell'Ecuador" comes from one editor, Jamessil. In two large edits (+5485 and +7359 bytes) they rewrote the History section, covering the party's 1926–31 founding and the 1944 "La Gloriosa" uprising, and added a table of presidential election results from 1940 through the Correa, Moreno and Arauz years. There are no reverts, no anonymous editors, and only this one page in one language is involved. This looks like ordinary article improvement, not a sign of political news in Ecuador. I didn't check whether pages for the same topic in other languages changed. The new election table may also be incomplete: its 1944 row lists 91 votes (91%) for an assembly vote, which looks off.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on Jeff Parker ETA IVtet live album 'Happy Today'; routine

briefs.headline: Washington Post film critic Ann Hornaday reported dead at 66; Wikipedia updates her page

It cites a washingtonpost.com obituary whose URL is dated 2026/10/19 and titled "Ann Hornaday, longtime Washington Post film critic, dies at 66." Earlier items still stand, including the Ivorian politician Louis-André Dacoury-Tabley, 81 (rev 1381058661, single French source). No reverts and no edit war.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: schoolyard vandalism on Stumble Guys and Samurái pages, bots reverting

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia: Stumble Guys and Samurái vandalism; Samurái damage may still be live
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. It's schoolyard vandalism by temporary accounts on two unrelated Spanish Wikipedia pages, and this story is already the schoolyard-vandalism story. briefs.headline: NRA article vandalism stops after semi-protection; no further edits
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not a content dispute, which confirms the earlier brief. A temporary account (~2026-56319-52) and then the account Sbsbbab kept putting the same insertion into the English NRA article. It renamed the infobox to "Terrorist Organization" and added "mass murdering terrorist organization" to the opening sentence and the image caption (revs 1381071455, 1381071956). briefs.headline: Alberta independence vote: Wikipedia tally shows ~76% "Remain" with 73% reporting

These figures come only from Wikipedia editors and none of the edits name a source, so treat them as provisional until the official count. Activity is on one page, English only, with about 5 editors in the last few hours. Expect more updates as counting finishes.

briefs.headline: Alberta referendum: no new results since ~76% "Remain" at 73% reporting; edits are cosmetic

briefs.headline: Two unrelated vandalism edits on English Wikipedia, both reverted by one patroller

briefs.headline: Unrelated eswiki pages linked only by anti-vandalism bot; no news event

A graph query found no edits on Pledge of Allegiance, Kai or Sliced bread after rev 1381186163. On Pledge of Allegiance, Pickersgill-Cunliffe's revert (rev 1381186067) took out "yet useless," and put the lead back to "a patriotic recited verse". On Kai, Raptor123456 removed his own innuendo line (rev 1381186083). In the same edit he cut the last letter off "Khakassia", leaving "Khakassi" in an unrelated entry. Temp account ~2026-56185-92 then added a similar line (rev 1381186150), and ClueBot NG reverted it back to Raptor's version, so the typo is probably still on the page. Everything is in English, nothing is going back and forth between two editors, and there is no real-world news hook. The scout's call of continued churn rather than a new event holds.

briefs.headline: Pledge of Allegiance vandalism cleaned up; matching joke edits hit Kai, Sliced bread
briefs.summary: The "(yet useless)" line flagged as still live in the last brief has now been removed. Temp account ~2026-56181-12 took it out itself (rev 1381185803). Frogwings123 then put back "patriotic, yet useless," (rev 1381185987), and Pickersgill-Cunliffe reverted that (rev 1381186067), which leaves the lead clean as of the last recorded edit. There is no real-world news hook, no other language is involved, and each bad edit was reverted within minutes, mostly by other editors and once by its own author.

briefs.headline: Pledge of Allegiance: opinion edits on English Wikipedia, one reverted and one still live
briefs.summary: Within about 4 minutes, two editors added opinion to the English "Pledge of Allegiance" article. Jeppiz reverted that addition (rev 1381185065), but rolled the page back to Frogwings123's version, so the "(yet useless)" vandalism appears to still be live, based on the 3 edits recorded. Nothing points to a real-world event: it's a single page in one language, there's no back-and-forth between editors, and the edits are low-effort opinion insertions.

briefs.headline: Pitch and putt: minor vandalism by one temporary account, reverted twice
briefs.summary: The 1008-byte churn on en:Pitch and putt comes from two edits by one temporary account (~2026-55820-40), each undone within minutes. Wolfwolfnuke reverted that through AntiVandal. This looks like a joke about a local course and its players. There is no sign of a real-world event, a content dispute or activity in other languages. The page is back to its earlier version.

briefs.headline: Routine infobox tweaks on Ugly (UK band); one unsourced genre edit reverted
briefs.summary: Three edits in about six minutes on the English article for the UK band Ugly, all to the infobox. One editor added an alias field ("Ugly (UK)"), and that edit still stands. A temporary-account editor added "progressive rock" to the genre list. A patroller using the WikiShield anti-vandalism tool reverted it about 30 seconds later as an "unsourced genre change". This is the usual genre-tinkering seen on music articles: there was one revert, no back-and-forth, nothing changed in the article text, and nothing points to a real-world event such as a release, a line-up change or a death. I didn't check whether pages for this band in other languages also changed.

briefs.headline: Cornelius Vanderbilt (Simple English): small edits, one bot revert of a newcomer
briefs.summary: Two temporary accounts made small edits to the Simple English Wikipedia article on Cornelius Vanderbilt, who died in 1877. One account added that he gave one million dollars when Vanderbilt University was founded, plus a pronunciation guide ("van-der-bílt"). The anti-vandalism bot ChenzwBot reverted both, taking the page back to the last version by Griffinofwales. That account then put the pronunciation back as "Fix pronouce". A second temporary account made four one-to-four-byte copy edits (punctuation, removing "the" and "a"); one carried the joke comment "boomshakalaka". The bot revert looks like a false positive on a good-faith addition, not a dispute. No other languages, no news hook and no back-and-forth reverting. I couldn't load the diffs for the later small edits, so those are judged from their comments and byte sizes only.

briefs.headline: Routine: two new, unrelated dewiki articles (1975 DDR TV film, Fritz comedy channel)
briefs.summary: Nothing new since the last brief. This cluster is still two unrelated German Wikipedia articles that were created around the same time. 'Die Überlebende' (rev 271505267, AnPa286) is about a 1975 DEFA/DDR-Fernsehen TV film by Christian Steinke, based on Kurt David's novella. 'Comedy Kollektiv' (rev 271505401, a temporary account) is about the Fritz/rbb YouTube channel behind 'Falsch aber Lustig'. Its mention of an ARD Mediathek spin-off cites an existing DWDL report, not anything new. The only link between the two pages is M2k~dewiki, a high-volume patroller who added categories and a references section to both. Since the last brief, the only new edit is from the film article's creator (rev 271505658): a Film Polski source and the Hungarian title. There were no reverts and no other languages, and nothing points to a real-world event. I recommend closing this story.

briefs.headline: Routine: two unrelated new German Wikipedia articles, linked only by a new-page patroller
briefs.summary: This cluster is two separate German Wikipedia articles created around the same time. They have nothing to do with each other and point to no news event. 'Die Überlebende' (rev 271505267, by AnPa286) is a new article about a 1975 East German (DEFA/DDR-Fernsehen) TV film by Christian Steinke, based on Kurt David's novella. 'Comedy Kollektiv' (rev 271505401) is a new article about the Fritz/rbb YouTube comedy channel behind 'Falsch aber Lustig'. The comedy article mentions an ARD Mediathek spin-off, but cites an existing DWDL report, so it doesn't signal anything new. Recommend closing; no watch needed.

briefs.headline: Grizzana Morandi: joke edits to festival list reverted on it-wiki; no news event
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-50582-61) made three edits to the "Tradizioni e folclore" section of the it-wiki article on Grizzana Morandi, a municipality in the Apennines near Bologna. The first edit added three local feast days with no sources: a 24 April procession at the war memorial, the parish feast on the first Sunday of August, and the 15 August "festa dello Zuccherino". The later edits added a mocking line saying the feast ends with people "in alcoholic comas" ("coma etilici vari", then "gente ai limiti del coma etilico"). Patroller Amirzat undid the last edit, and Yiyi then took the page back to its earlier version ("ripristino versione"), removing everything the temporary account had added. The graph does not flag these as reverts, but the diffs show they were. This is small-scale vandalism mixed with possibly genuine but unsourced folklore detail, cleaned up within about 25 minutes. Nothing points to a real-world event, and the account edited no other pages.

briefs.headline: Kandahar article vandalized: infobox removed, then city relabeled as in Pakistan; reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism on the English Wikipedia article for Kandahar, not a real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-56036-30) deleted the whole settlement infobox, about 3,400 characters (rev 1381093315). A Human of Time reverted the deletion. The same account then edited the short description, hatnote, infobox type, pushpin map and province/district links to say Kandahar is in Pakistan instead of Afghanistan (rev 1381096133). Lemonaka rolled that back about an hour after the first edit, citing missing reliable sources. Nothing points to a news trigger: only one page moved, no other-language versions changed, and the account touched no other articles. It may be nationalist trolling tied to Afghanistan–Pakistan tensions, but nothing in the graph shows that.

briefs.headline: Damping page vandalism reverted twice in 90 seconds; no new activity, no news
briefs.summary: The "new cluster" the Scout flagged is the same four Damping edits this story already covers. Nothing new has happened since. Pocketjoe684 vandalised the cited opening sentence twice while claiming in edit summaries to be adding explanation. Rev 1381084068 added "We love damping!!!! PETER!!" and rev 1381084199 added "WE LOVE DAMPING! PETER!". ClueBot NG reverted the first, and Dr vulpes reverted the second with Interceptor (rev 1381084238, which restores the cited sentence). The Scout called this routine churn with no reverts, but that is wrong: the graph's revert flag is false, yet both follow-up edits are anti-vandalism reverts. I'm keeping the status as vandalism, not routine. I also corrected the earlier brief, which quoted both inserts with the same wording. The Barn owl part of the story is unchanged, and nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Barn owl article hit by minor vandalism, reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: The English "Barn owl" page (a disambiguation-style list of Tyto species) saw a short burst of schoolyard-style vandalism. It is not a content dispute and not a real-world event. A temporary account added "h guys" and account Nate313131676 added "hi will" (rev 1381083139). Staticspector reverted both. Nate313131676 then blanked about 1,200 bytes, including the species list and the See also section (rev 1381083263, comment "yes"). Dr vulpes restored the page with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool (rev 1381083335). All of this happened in about 5 minutes. The "high churn" the Scout flagged comes from blanking and restoring the same text, not from new content. Nothing suggests news involving barn owls.

briefs.headline: Barn owl and Damping pages hit by student-style vandalism, reverted quickly
briefs.summary: This is still a vandalism story with no real-world news hook. On "Barn owl", two accounts added greetings ("h guys", "hi") and Staticspector reverted both. Nate313131676 then blanked the page in two edits. Rev 1381083223 (comment "yes") removed the intro, and rev 1381083263 (no comment) removed the Tyto species list and See also section. Dr vulpes restored about 1,218 bytes with Interceptor within about 5 minutes. This corrects the earlier brief, which put the "yes" comment on the wrong revision. The new "Damping" activity is the same kind of thing. Pocketjoe684 claimed in edit summaries to be "adding info" but twice replaced the cited lead sentence with "We love damping!!!! PETER!!" (revs 1381084068, 1381084199). ClueBot NG reverted the first and Dr vulpes the second, within about 90 seconds. The two pages have different vandals, and the only link between them is patroller Dr vulpes, so this looks like unrelated, probably classroom, vandalism rather than one coordinated campaign.

briefs.headline: Annabelle Rama article: small dispute over occupation and ethnicity wording, no news
briefs.summary: Three edits to the English Wikipedia biography of Filipino actress and talent manager Annabelle Rama landed within about five minutes. They are routine cleanup and do not point to a real-world event. A temporary-account editor (~2026-56327-18) changed her occupation to "Talent Manager • Producer • Businesswoman • Actress" in both the infobox and the opening sentence, without sources. In the same edit they removed the "Spanish and Chinese descent" wording. Beyhive Navy reverted that edit as unsourced. Celjski Grad then cut the occupation down to "actress" and removed the descent line, citing lack of support in the article and MOS:ETHNICITY (the style guideline on mentioning ethnicity). Nothing added mentions a death, legal case, election or other news hook, and no other-language versions of the article were part of this cluster. One caveat: the diffs as displayed seem to be compared against an older version, so exactly what each edit changed is slightly uncertain, but the overall picture is clear.

briefs.headline: Annabelle Rama wording cleanup and Chatbot link spam share a patroller; no news
briefs.summary: This cluster holds two unrelated bits of routine upkeep on English Wikipedia. They are grouped only because one anti-vandalism patroller, Beyhive Navy, reverted edits on both pages. On Annabelle Rama, a temporary account added unsourced occupation wording, and Beyhive Navy reverted it. Celjski Grad then cut the infobox and lead down to "actress" and removed both "talent manager" and the "Spanish and Chinese descent" line, citing lack of support in the article and MOS:ETHNICITY, the style guideline on mentioning ethnicity (rev 1381152686). I did not open every revert diff, but the edit summaries and the changes in size match what I describe.

briefs.headline: zh.wiki film-company list: two blankings both reverted; no new edits since

briefs.headline: Chinese Wikipedia film-company list blanked twice by temporary accounts, reverted
briefs.summary: This is routine vandalism on zh.wikipedia's 电影公司列表 (List of film companies). It does not point to any real-world event. briefs.headline: New nl.wiki article on NTR docudrama 'Fri Fri Suriname' after Cinekid Award win
briefs.summary: The large churn is one new article, not a rewrite. Glynis73 created 'Fri Fri Suriname' (+5,084 bytes). It describes a three-part NTR youth docudrama from 2025 about Suriname's independence on 25 November 1975, made for the 50th anniversary. The article says the series won the 2026 Cinekid Award for craftsmanship in a series production, citing Cinekid's 2026 winners page (accessed 2026-10-20). That award is the likely reason the page was created now. The three follow-up edits are routine cleanup by two established editors: RuedNL2 removed a duplicate title header, and PAvdK added wikilinks and a references section. There were no reverts and no other languages were involved. One thing to watch: the creator's username, 'Glynis73', matches the screenwriter named in the article (Glynis Terborg), so this may be a conflict of interest. That can't be confirmed from the edits alone. The award claim also hasn't been checked beyond the cited source.

briefs.headline: "Try Everything" page: one temp account's unsourced label swap reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is not a news hook. All non-revert activity on the enwiki article for Shakira's 2016 Zootopia song "Try Everything" came from one temporary account (~2026-55064-83), which made 7 edits over about 30 minutes. Each edit changed the record label from Walt Disney Records to Universal Music Group in the infobox, lead and category. The later edits also changed the runtime from 3:22 to 3:16, added "File Type = MP3" and created a "Universal Music Group soundtracks" category. One edit broke the infobox by removing the music-video field and closing braces. The edit summaries cite only "Universal Music Group" or a Zootopia Trailer #2 YouTube title. None of the edits added a source. Patrollers Jessicapierce and Discospinster each reverted the account once, restoring the Disney label. There is no back-and-forth between established editors and no activity in other languages. The edits don't point to a re-release, label change or other real-world event, though I can't rule out the editor sincerely misreading a streaming listing.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on es-wiki Aureliano Blanquet page by one temp account, reverted twice
briefs.summary: This isn't news. A single temporary account (~2026-56291-49) vandalized the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Aureliano Blanquet, the Huerta-era general who died in 1919. In its first edit it swapped "Guerra" in the infobox's "Secretario de Guerra y Marina" for an obscene word. Leonpolanco reverted that. The account then added garbled, unsourced wording about Blanquet's severed head being "macheteado", meaning cut off with a machete, and removed the {{Cita requerida}} (citation needed) tag. Jake Park reverted that with Huggle about four minutes later. The scout counted "no reverts" because the revert flag wasn't set, but both reverts show plainly in the edit comments and diffs. Only one page and one language moved, and no other editors joined, so there's no sign of a real-world trigger. The scout's anniversary idea is unconfirmed and unlikely.

briefs.headline: Zevgolatio update: another new account adds unsourced "Services" section, reverted
briefs.summary: This is an update to the Zevgolatio/Vochaiko story on Greek Wikipedia, and no real-world event is involved. Since the last brief there is one new edit. A sixth new account, Antwniaaa, added a "Services" section to the Zevgolatio article (rev 11886120, +594). The heading itself is misspelled ("Υπυρεσίες"), and the section describes the Velo-Vocha municipal Community Centre and the benefits and counselling residents can apply for. Unlike the earlier name-dropping pranks, this text is plausible, but it has no source and is badly spelled. Patroller Fotis A. reverted it in full about five minutes later (rev 11886126). The scout's "churn of 1762" comes from adding up these additions and their removals together with the earlier Vochaiko and Yuujgftyyu edits and their reverts, not from a new wave of vandalism. The pattern fits a group of local students, possibly on a class assignment, writing about their own village with throwaway accounts. That link is a guess; I have not confirmed it.

briefs.headline: Prank vandalism spreads from Zevgolatio to neighboring Vochaiko on Greek Wikipedia
briefs.summary: This is an update to the Zevgolatio vandalism story, not a new event. The same temporary account (~2026-56023-51) that put personal names into the Zevgolatio article also edited the Greek article on Vochaiko, a village 2 km away. In rev 11886075 it inserted the name "Πρέντι" into the administrative text and swapped a link to the word "agha" for an insult. A second account, in rev 11886109 (+671), added an invented "aristocratic Bitsakos family" to Vochaiko, with a "palace" in the village centre plus named "kings" and a "princess". These look like private individuals named as a joke. A new edit on Zevgolatio (rev 11886108, by Yuujgftyyu) added an ungrammatical, childish sentence about youth centres and "smiling groups of friends". Patroller Fotis A. has already reverted the earlier edits on both pages. The tone and the local names point to the same group of schoolchildren. Nothing suggests a real-world event. I can't tell whether the Bitsakos names are real local people.

briefs.headline: Zevgolatio (Corinthia) Greek article hit by prank and inaccurate additions, not news
briefs.summary: Three accounts made non-news edits to the Greek Wikipedia article on Zevgolatio, a town in Corinthia, within about 10 minutes. No other pages or languages were involved. Rev 11886033 slipped personal names (Κένο, Χάρης, Βέρας, Σκεντέρ) into the existing geography and mythology text, for example renaming Perseus "the hero Χάρης". This is classic prank vandalism, probably by local schoolchildren. Rev 11886050 (+3083) added a long, oddly formatted "Geography" section that contradicts the article itself. The article says the town sits at 50 m on the coastal Vocha plain and is the seat of Velo-Vocha municipality; the new section puts it on the slopes of Mount Helmos in Stymfalia municipality, among chestnut forests. It reads like made-up, possibly machine-generated text. Rev 11886079 added a sloppy, informal sentence listing restaurants, clothes shops and schools. Nothing points to a real-world event. The three accounts may well be the same group of friends, but that is a guess.

briefs.headline: Emma closure: de.wiki adds lead-style line on Schwarzer's announcement; no new facts
briefs.summary: This is a continuation of the tracked story about Alice Schwarzer closing the feminist magazine Emma, not a new story. Since the last brief there have been two more edits to the German Wikipedia article. Nicola added a one-line summary (rev 271503745): "In October 2026 Alice Schwarzer announced the magazine would be discontinued at the end of the year." Christof46 then fixed a typo in that sentence (rev 271503894). The main facts are unchanged and still sourced to Tages-Anzeiger, taz and Der Spiegel, all dated 21 Oct 2026 (rev 271503352). The print edition ends on 8 Dec 2026, the closure is said not to be for financial reasons (the team is "worn out", in the magazine's words to German news agency dpa), and the editorial archive has gone to the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, a major German literary archive. There are no reverts and no vandalism. One open question remains: the article says both "print edition" ending 8 Dec and the whole "magazine" ending at year's end, so it is still unclear whether anything will continue online.

briefs.headline: Alice Schwarzer to close feminist magazine Emma after 50 years; final issue Dec 8
briefs.summary: The diff text was available this time, and it confirms what the last brief could only infer from edit comments. The German Wikipedia article on Emma now says that on 21 Oct 2026 it became known Alice Schwarzer is shutting the magazine down, with the last issue on 8 Dec 2026 (rev 271502509). Sources are cited inline: Tages-Anzeiger, taz and Der Spiegel, all dated 21 Oct. An anonymous editor's comment also cites a Welt article titled "Emma: nach 50 Jahren ist Schluss" ("Emma: after 50 years, it's over"). Aschmidt's additions (rev 271503352) say the closure is not for financial reasons: the team is "worn out", or in the magazine's words to German news agency dpa, "we are leaving because we think: enough!" They also say the editorial archive has gone to the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, a major German literary archive. Since then editors have mostly been tidying the article: removing a duplicate sentence (the anonymous editor's "December 2026" line), pruning dead web links, and adding a link to emma.de's full-text archive (rev 271503536). There are no reverts and no signs of vandalism. One open question: the current wording says the *print edition* ends on 8 Dec, while an earlier edit said the magazine itself ends, so it is unclear whether any online presence will continue.

briefs.headline: German feminist magazine Emma may be shutting down, de.wiki edits suggest
briefs.summary: The German Wikipedia article on Emma, the feminist magazine founded by Alice Schwarzer, has had 14 edits from 8 different registered editors in about 2.6 hours. That is more than the Scout counted, and there were no reverts. The key evidence is an edit comment by Schopper1305 under the "Entwicklung" (history) section: "Nicht nur die Herausgabe wird eingestellt, sondern die Zeitschrift selbst" ("it is not only the publishing that is being discontinued, but the magazine itself"). That suggests the article now says Emma is closing or ending its current form. After that, Aschmidt made several additions (+506, +198 web links, +447), Fossa trimmed the wording and removed a duplicate link, and JKowar edited a primary source in the same section. This looks like editors working together on news, not vandalism or an edit war. A big caveat: I could not get any diff text or a page summary (the fetch failed every time), so this rests only on edit comments, timing and editor counts. I have not seen exactly what is being discontinued or when. No other-language versions of the article are in the graph.

briefs.headline: New account twice blanks conviction line on AAP MLA Lalpura's page; patrollers revert
briefs.summary: Over about seven minutes, a new account, Hotmani singh (2 edits total), twice removed the lead's election citations and the sentence "He was found guilty and convicted of molesting a Dalit woman" from the en-wiki article on Manjinder Singh Lalpura, the AAP MLA for Khadoor Sahib in Punjab. The second edit also added unsourced praise: "military man before MLA and good shooter". Two established patrollers undid both edits within about a minute each. Komethere's revert was tagged as vandalism, and Dr vulpes reverted using the Interceptor tool. In all three diffs I read, the conviction sentence was already in the article, so this burst did not add it. It looks like a whitewashing attempt by one editor, not a sign of new real-world developments. Caveats: the graph only covers these 4 edits, so I can't tell when the conviction claim was first added, and in the version I saw it only has election-result citations, which is a possible BLP sourcing problem worth a look. The edits alone don't rule out a news hook outside Wikipedia, such as an appeal or a court ruling.

briefs.headline: New account keeps blanking Lalpura conviction, now says High Court quashed case without a source
briefs.summary: Hotmani singh, a single-purpose account with 4 edits, has now made four removals on the en-wiki article on AAP MLA Manjinder Singh Lalpura. Three different patrollers have reverted them: Komethere, Dr vulpes and Pattersonuwu. The new edits go further than the earlier ones. Rev 1381214985 renamed the section "Convicted in molestation charges" to just "charges" and deleted its text: the Sept 11, 2025 conviction by a Tarn Taran court in a 2013 case about molesting and assaulting a Dalit teenager, the arrest, and the four-year sentence. That text cited Indian Express, Hindustan Times and Times of India. Rev 1381215856 removed the conviction sentence from the lead again. Its edit summary claims the Chandigarh High Court has quashed the FIR and acquitted Lalpura. Pattersonuwu restored everything in rev 1381215935. The quash/acquittal claim is the one possible news hook here, but the editor gave no source, and nobody else on any language wiki has picked it up. Treat it as an unverified assertion, not a reported event, though it's worth checking whether there's been a High Court ruling or appeal. The TMI Episcopal edits are unrelated. An anonymous temporary account added small unsourced bits, such as "College Like Campus" (rev 1381214307), and they were reverted. Dr vulpes patrolling both pages is the only link.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on da.wiki page for football coach Nils Nielsen, rolled back twice
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. All four edits to the Danish article on football coach Nils Kromann Nielsen came from one temporary account (~2026-56139-04), each with the comment "ikke noget" ("nothing"). The edits added junk text above the infobox ("puhadada 67 67 67…", "johan stinker") and changed the infobox name to "67". Editors E-Turner and Hjart each rolled the account back, and the article is now back to its earlier clean version. None of the edits touch his career, his status or any recent event. Other language versions did not move. The trigger may be the "67" meme. There is no real-world news here.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on 4 unrelated enwiki pages, incl. 24kGoldn, all reverted; Long Beach rant
briefs.summary: This cluster is routine counter-vandalism on four unrelated English pages. No languages other than English and no shared topic. 24kGoldn: a temporary account (~2026-56137-42) added junk ("Ruby", "Ruby Rasmussen Violet", "24KGoldn") to the infobox, the discography table and the short description. I read Augmented Seventh's Interceptor revert 1381096896, and it puts back both the infobox and the broken discography rows. That answers the open question in the earlier 24kGoldn brief. A later revert (1381097075) removed the short-description prefix. Dumb and Dumber: CraverG added joke lines about Biden/Harris and "the women from The View". Smallestredboy reverted the first and ClueBot NG the second. Oxgangs (Edinburgh): Toji4 pasted anime quotes (Jujutsu Kaisen) and small "clean" edits, reverted by ClueBot NG and Augmented Seventh. Long Beach, Mississippi: a temporary account (~2026-55982-71) twice added unsourced complaints to the article's opening paragraph that the city became "one big HOA" through Ordinance 676, which limits where campers can be parked on residential property. RadioactOlive and Augmented Seventh reverted both. That suggests a real but small local dispute over a city ordinance, which the edits don't verify and which isn't news on a wire scale. All damage appears reverted, so no follow-up is needed.

briefs.headline: 24kGoldn article hit by vandalism from one temporary account; reverted
briefs.summary: All the activity on the English 24kGoldn page in this cluster comes from one temporary account (~2026-56137-42), and two patrollers reverted it: Zackmann08 and Augmented Seventh, the latter using the Interceptor tool. briefs.headline: Jackie Shroff article: birthplace naming tweak reverted; routine upkeep
briefs.summary: A temporary account changed the infobox birthplace of Indian actor Jackie Shroff from "Bombay, Bombay State" to "Mumbai, Maharashtra" (rev 1381069988, "Fixed incorrect info"). Established editor Drmies reverted it within about a minute, noting that Bombay/Bombay State was the correct name at his 1957 birth. That follows the usual Wikipedia practice of using historical place names. Fylindfotberserk then made a small +24 "restored sourced" fix to the early-life paragraph (rev 1381070342). The diff I read shows the 1 Feb 1957 Bombay birth details unchanged, so the exact restored text is unclear from the excerpt. Nothing points to a real-world event, an edit war or a vandalism spree. It is a common place-name fix plus regular maintenance.

briefs.headline: Richard Riehle's article updated after reported death at 78; editors refine details
briefs.summary: Editors are tidying the English Wikipedia article on character actor Richard Riehle ('Office Space'). Before this burst of edits, the article already said he died in Los Angeles on October 15, 2026, aged 78. That line cites a TMZ report dated October 19, 2026. Of the three edits I read, the first (rev 1381069006) added "at his home" and "from natural causes", with no new source; the second (rev 1381069789) is a copyedit; the third (rev 1381070648) adds a 1975 uncredited role in Rooster Cogburn to his filmography, the usual career fill-in after a death. There are no reverts and no pages in other languages moving, and the edits come from three different accounts. What's uncertain: the death rests on one tabloid source in the article, the cause of death has no citation, and I could not see when the original death sentence was added.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Mar Mediterráneo' reverted by bots
briefs.summary: The roughly 11k bytes of churn on es:Mar Mediterráneo is one vandal plus two automated reverts. It is not a rewrite and has no link to any real-world event. In three unexplained edits, user Michiuwuinsano replaced the lead with nonsense naming themselves ("michiuwuinsano, después del queque", rev 175917603). They then removed the infobox and hatnotes and inserted "viste que se puede editar cata michiuwuinsano del mundo" (rev 175917641; -4,459 bytes). SeroBOT reverted the first two edits (rev 175917608), and Automoderador reverted the third about 10 seconds after it was made (rev 175917644). The scout saw "no reverts" because the revert flag wasn't set, but the edit comments show they were reverts. No other language versions moved and no other editors are involved. The page appears to be restored, but the vandal could come back.

briefs.headline: Bots revert vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Mar Mediterráneo'; no new edits
briefs.summary: This repeats the earlier brief, and nothing new has happened. The five edits on es:Mar Mediterráneo are one vandal and two bots cleaning up. They are not tied to any real-world event. The graph shows no edits after the bot revert, and no other language versions or editors are involved. The page looks restored, though the account could come back.

briefs.headline: De-wiki self-promo page "Eisbaer Records" in speedy deletion; edit history now gone
briefs.summary: This repeats an already-tracked routine item. There is no news here. There are 5 edits on a single de-wiki page, with no reverts and no versions in other languages. The page was created by StefanDimitrij, a 3-edit account whose name matches the founder the article names. The article's intro says Eisbaer Records is a music label founded on 20.10.2026 by Stefan Dimitrij Porcio ("DJ resaca"). M2k~dewiki then added a category, and the experienced patroller Horst Gräbner filed a speedy-deletion request ("SLA"). There has been no new activity since the prior brief. When I tried to re-read revisions 271487144 and 271487245, Wikipedia said both no longer exist. That fits the page having been deleted, though I couldn't confirm it, since a cached page summary still loads. I'm citing no diffs because I couldn't read any. The description of the edits relies on the dossier's edit comments and the prior brief.

briefs.headline: New de-wiki page on one-day-old "Eisbaer Records" label tagged for speedy deletion
briefs.summary: This is not news. A brand-new de-wiki article says "Eisbaer Records" is a music label founded on 20 Oct 2026, the same day the article was created, by Stefan Dimitrij Porcio ("DJ resaca"). Its only source is a SoundCloud link (rev 271487144). The account that created it, StefanDimitrij, has made 3 edits in total and its name matches the founder's. That points to self-promotion or a conflict of interest. About five minutes later, the experienced patroller Horst Gräbner added a speedy-deletion request ("SLA") saying the label's notability isn't evident (rev 271487245). Between those edits, M2k~dewiki made a routine category edit and the creator made two small logo edits. There are no reverts and no other language versions, and the page is likely to be deleted soon. The scout's note called this "ordinary rewriting", but it's really a new self-promotional page going through normal deletion review.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on 'Mabel Freer' article reverted quickly; no news event
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Mabel Freer saw one burst of vandalism. She was a British woman kept out of Australia in 1936 on morality grounds. A new account, Occwarior (2 edits in total), changed the key year from 1936 to 1967, which also mislabelled the Immigration Restriction Act 1901 as 'Act 1967'. The same edit added a racial slur to a section heading, and a second edit renamed 'Relationship with Edward Dewar' to 'Relationship with Donald Trump.' Cannolis, an established patroller, reverted both edits within about a minute, citing WP:VANDAL. The only other edit, by ITBF about 15 minutes earlier, was a small rewording in the legacy section. None of this points to a real-world event about the historical subject. It looks like ordinary vandalism that has already been cleaned up.

briefs.headline: Two vandal edits to footballer Chido Obi's page reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: This is low-level vandalism, not a news event. Two different temporary accounts each made one edit to the en.wiki biography of Manchester United forward Chido Obi, who is on loan at Willem II. The first (rev 1381151892) changed his "commonly known as" name to "Mathias Hartling", apparently a joke name. Materialscientist reverted it within about 40 seconds. The second (rev 1381152110, edit summary "vggkgnlrg") deleted his bolded full name and inserted nonsense text ("karlpeterjuul er enn svensker"). ClueBot NG reverted it within seconds. Neither edit changed his club, his loan, or any other fact, and no other pages or languages moved. The Danish-flavoured jokes hint at pranksters who know each other, but that is a guess.

briefs.headline: Chido Obi page: two vandal edits reverted, no new activity

briefs.headline: Violent Typhoon Champi enters Philippine area, named "Rosal" by PAGASA
briefs.summary: Editors of the English "2026 Pacific typhoon season" article added the local Philippine name "Rosal" for Typhoon Champi (29W/2630). The edit comment says the name was assigned by PAGASA, which normally means the storm has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility (rev 1381115946; the season table was changed to match in rev 1381117310). The table lists Champi as a "Violent typhoon" active since October 11, with 10-minute winds of 105 kn and a pressure of 935 hPa, affecting Micronesia and the Mariana Islands; damage and deaths are given as unknown. The storm history (rev 1381116026, a capitalization fix) traces its growth from a JMA depression on October 11 to a typhoon on October 16, with the US military forecaster (JTWC) reporting rapid intensification and 1-minute winds of at least 120 kn. The page is lively (3 editors, 5 edits, no reverts) but this is a real, developing weather event, not an edit war or vandalism. Some things are uncertain: no other-language pages have moved yet, the Philippine-entry inference rests on an edit comment rather than a quoted bulletin, and the edits so far are minor (naming and formatting), with no reported landfall or impacts.

briefs.headline: Swedish Wikipedia vandal moves from Fidel Castro to Birán and Margaret Thatcher
briefs.summary: This is vandalism by one person, not news. A single temporary account (~2026-56131-63) vandalised the sv-wiki Fidel Castro article twice. Rev 59783741 added a crude ASCII phallus after the sentence about his death, under an edit summary that falsely said it added childhood information. The graph also shows the account spreading to other pages. It made two earlier edits to Birán, Castro's birthplace (revs 59783720/59783723). Those revisions can no longer be fetched, which suggests they were deleted or hidden, but I can't confirm why. Its latest edit, rev 59783758 on Margaret Thatcher, was labelled as fixing a small grammar error. In fact it added one ("kom att bli" → "kom till att bli"), and the graph shows no revert yet. There is no real-world event and no other language involved. The Thatcher edit is probably still live and may need reverting.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Swedish Wikipedia's Fidel Castro article, reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. One temporary account (~2026-56131-63) made two juvenile edits to the sv-wiki Fidel Castro biography. briefs.headline: Sofía Casanova es-wiki: unsourced "Ameli Paz" pseudonym re-added, reverted again by bot

Since then, two more edits hit the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Sofía Casanova (Galician journalist, 1861–1958), and the page has once again been reverted to its previous state. In total that makes six edits from two temporary accounts plus the bot, all on one page in one language, and all undone. The repeated pseudonym attempt is persistent but it is not a news event. I have nothing that supports or rules out the pseudonym.

briefs.headline: Sofía Casanova es-wiki page: small test edits undone by the editor and a bot, no news
briefs.summary: The four edits to the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Sofía Casanova (Galician journalist, 1861–1958) are small, low-quality changes that were all undone. Her birth (30 Sep) and death (16 Jan) dates don't match the timing, and only one language edition moved. This looks like casual test editing or mild vandalism that has already been cleaned up. I can't rule out that the pseudonym claim has some basis, but nothing on the page supports it.

briefs.headline: Fa.wiki "Call of Duty" page: joke edits about a private gamer, auto-reverted

briefs.headline: De-wiki 'Jean Zacklad': temporary accounts' hard-coded interwiki links rolled back
briefs.summary: All four edits are about one interlanguage link, not the subject's life. Within about four minutes, two different temporary accounts (~2026-56165-19 and ~2026-56138-50) each added a hard-coded Spanish link to the German article: first [[es:Jean Zacklade]], then [[es:Jean Zacklad]]. Both edit summaries asked someone to add the link on Wikidata instead ("bitte auf Wikidata setzen"). Each time, Carol.Christiansen undid the edit with a rollback, which fits de-wiki's practice of keeping language links on Wikidata rather than in the article text. The graph did not mark these edits as reverts, but the diffs and rollback summaries show that they are. No article content changed and no biographical news is involved. This looks like a good-faith editor, or the same person on two temporary accounts, who wants a newly created Spanish article linked. It is not vandalism or an edit war.

briefs.headline: Swedish list update: Moderates win outright majority in Staffanstorp; a Skåne seat count corrected
briefs.summary: The same registered editor, Berneblads, made three more edits to the Skåne section of the Swedish Wikipedia list of municipal and regional governments for 2026–2030. In rev 59783221 a blank row becomes a Moderate (M) government in Staffanstorp with 22 of 41 seats, an outright majority. The source is a 100.se analysis titled "Egen (M)ajoritet i Staffanstorp", retrieved 20 Oct 2026. Revs 59783217 and 59783219 change a 51-seat row from "25 av 51" to "23 av 51 (minoritet)" and then to "24 av 51 (minoritet)". This is most likely Vellinge, which was entered earlier as M with 25 of 51, so that council would be a minority government, not a majority. The diffs don't show the municipality name, so the Vellinge link is my inference. There are no reverts and no other editors involved: this is routine filling-in and self-correction after the September 2026 local elections, and Staffanstorp is the only new fact.

briefs.headline: Swedish editors fill in new municipal coalitions after 2026 local elections
briefs.summary: Three editors (one registered, two temporary accounts) are adding to the Swedish Wikipedia list of municipal and regional governments for 2026–2030. In each of the four edits, a blank table row becomes a named coalition with a seat count and a citation to local media. Vellinge: M, 25 of 51 seats (Sydsvenskan, 13 Oct). Tomelilla: M+KD+SD, 23 of 41 (Ystads Allehanda, 19 Oct). Degerfors in Örebro county: M+SD+C+KD, 17 of 31; Sveriges Radio calls this the right taking over an old left stronghold. A Västra Götaland municipality: an S+V minority government, 17 of 41. There are no reverts and no disputes, so this is the normal filling-in of results as local deals are announced weeks after the September 2026 election. The only small news item is the right-wing takeover in Degerfors. I didn't check the other-language versions or the full edit history, and the scout's 1390 churn figure is about the sum of these four edits (+1390 bytes).

briefs.headline: New de.wiki bio of hip-hop journalist Niko Backspin tagged for speedy deletion
briefs.summary: The large delta is not a rewrite. A temporary account created a new German Wikipedia article on Niko "Backspin" Hüls, a Hamburg hip-hop journalist and owner of Backspin magazine (+5,620 bytes, edit comment "page didn't exist yet, relevant entry"). The draft is badly formatted: section headings in capitals, bare [n] citation markers and only two real ref tags. It reads like a promotional profile, citing a Serviceplan newsroom post and the Innings baseball magazine site. Within about 2 minutes, patroller SK Sturm Fan added a speedy-deletion request ({{SLA|kein Artikel}}, meaning "not an article"). A third editor, Carol.Christiansen, followed with another edit marked "SLA"; I couldn't load that diff, so I don't know exactly what it changed. This is routine new-page patrol of a likely self-promotional or poorly formatted article, with no real-world news event behind it.

briefs.headline: German IRL-streaming pioneer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV") reported dead at 36
briefs.summary: A new de-wiki biography of Adam Wolke was created by Berghest (rev 271487726). It says he was a German web-video producer, born 3 Oct 1990, who died in October 2026 of a brain haemorrhage after an aneurysm burst. The article calls him a pioneer of "In Real Life" streaming in Europe, known for SkylineTV Live and for streams with Knossi, MontanaBlack and Trymacs. A follow-up edit (271488001) adds that he co-hosted Holger Kreymeier's "Netzprediger" from 2014 and was its main host from 2016 to 2018. The death claim cites stories dated 20 Oct 2026 in Die Welt, Focus and 20min/Blick. The page was created the same day, about 20 Oct 2026 by graph timestamps, and the graph shows no pages for him in other languages. Since then, 6 registered editors and 2 temporary accounts have made routine fixes (categories, links). One temporary account changed his age at death to 38 (271489294). Horst Gräbner put it back to 36 within minutes (271489408), which matches the 1990 birth date. That was a one-off fix, not an edit war. Caveats: I couldn't check the cited sources myself. The Focus citation is dated 2024, probably a typo. The 20min link is labelled Blick. This is a niche German internet figure, so the news is mostly of regional or community interest.

briefs.headline: Adam Wolke article: date and source tweaks; a Stern link giving age 38 added, then removed
briefs.summary: The de-wiki biography of streamer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV") is still being cleaned up, but this latest batch is more than commas, so the scout's note doesn't quite hold. Fruchtjoghurt00 made the death date more exact, changing "Oktober 2026" to "20. Oktober 2026" (271490358, 271490369). Horst Gräbner reverted that and asked editors to keep the article's original format (271490402). Fruchtjoghurt00 then cited a Stern article whose URL says Wolke died at 38 ("mit-38-ueberraschend-verstorben", 271490447). That clashes with the 36 given by the Welt and Focus citations and by his stated birth date (3 Oct 1990). About 45 minutes later Lulaci removed the Stern citation while converting the other references into proper citation templates (271491586). Other edits were wording fixes ("geplatztes" changed to "gerissenes" Aneurysma, 271491035) and a wikilink (271491490). The core claim hasn't changed: he died in October 2026, aged 36, of a brain haemorrhage. Open questions: the edits don't confirm the exact date of death, and the source disagreement over 36 vs 38 is still unresolved. It looks like a slow dispute over format and sourcing, not a fight over content and not an edit war.

briefs.headline: Adam Wolke article: style tussle over birth/death symbols; 18 Oct death date still unsourced
briefs.summary: Since the last brief there have been only two edits to the de-wiki biography of streamer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV"), and both are about style, not facts. The temporary account that added the unsourced 18 Oct death date (~2026-56226-19) switched the lead from "geb. … †" to the standard German genealogical symbols "* … †" (271493181). Horst Gräbner undid this within about 4 minutes, saying the article had been created without those symbols (271493236). Neither edit touched the death date, so "18. Oktober 2026" has now been through several editors' hands without challenge. It still has no source, and the cited press reports are dated 20 Oct. A correction to the previous brief: Berghest's −5 edit (271493024) did not tidy the infobox. It turned "SkylineTV Live" in the body text into a wikilink to [[SkylineTV]]. There were no reverts tagged as such, everything is on one page in one language, and the same person reverting style changes looks like article ownership, not an edit war. The core claim (died October 2026, aged 36, brain haemorrhage) hasn't changed. Open question: the exact date of death.

briefs.headline: Adam Wolke article: 18 Oct death date added without a source; 38-age edit reverted again
briefs.summary: This follows the tracked de-wiki story on the death of streamer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV"). Since the last brief there has been more cleanup, plus one new factual claim. A temporary account changed the death date from "Oktober 2026" to "18. Oktober 2026" with the comment "aktualisierung" (271492337). No source was added. Eastfrisian2 and The Lort then reformatted the date (271492947, 271493089), so it is still standing and nobody has challenged it. Earlier, Horst Gräbner removed an attempt to put "20. Oktober" in this spot. The 18 Oct date also differs from the 20 Oct press dates in the citations. The 36-vs-38 age dispute came back for the third time: a different temporary account set the age to 38 (271491886), and Horst Gräbner put it back within 2 minutes ("1990 bis 2026 macht 36 Jahre", 271491925). That same edit also corrected the Focus citation date from 2024 to 2026. Berghest added that Wolke last lived in Frankfurt am Main (271492613), with no new source. He also added a webvideo infobox (Twitch skylinetvlive, about 265k followers; YouTube about 132k subscribers, figures as of 20 Oct 2026) that at first had duplicated fields (271492930). A follow-up −5 edit probably tidied it, but I couldn't load that diff. This is all one page, with no other-language versions and no edit war. Open questions: the exact date of death (18 Oct is unsourced) and why 38 keeps coming back, which may echo the Stern headline.

briefs.headline: Adam Wolke death article: only copyedits since last brief, no new facts
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked breaking story on the reported death of German IRL streamer Adam Wolke ("SkylineTV") on de-wiki. The latest edits are all copyedits, not sourcing or confirmation work. A temporary account fixed a typo ("disztanzierte" → "distanzierte", 271489380). Dragilein fixed the grammar in the death sentence ("Aneurysmas" → "Aneurysma") and added a comma (271489504). Horst Gräbner then took that comma out ("kein Komma", 271489558). The core claim has not changed: he died in October 2026 at age 36 of a brain haemorrhage after an aneurysm burst. No editor has added or removed a source, and the Focus citation is still dated "20. Oktober 2024", which is probably a typo for 2026. There were no reverts and no fight over content, and the earlier back-and-forth over his age (36 vs 38) has not come back. The original story's confidence stands. I still have not checked the cited press reports myself.

briefs.headline: Routine: one editor expands fa-wiki article on Iranian town Ajabshir; joke edit reverted by bot
briefs.summary: The churn on Persian Wikipedia's article on Ajabshir, a town in East Azerbaijan province, Iran, is almost all from one registered editor, Ohmygod211112, who made about 30 edits. briefs.headline: Swedish 'Romer' (Roma) article hit by a third vandal account, racist edits rolled back

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Swedish Wikipedia's 'Romer' (Roma) article quickly rolled back
briefs.summary: The ~77k churn on svwiki "Romer" comes from vandalism, not a rewrite. Two temporary accounts were behind it, and patrollers rolled every edit back within minutes. The article is back on the last good version.

briefs.headline: Racist vandalism on Swedish 'Romer' (Roma) article cleaned up; no new edits since
briefs.summary: No change since the last brief: the latest round of vandalism on svwiki "Romer" (the Roma people) has been rolled back, and nothing has been edited since. This matches earlier briefs: it's targeted anti-Roma trolling with no real-world event behind it. Still unknown: whether the three accounts are one person, and whether the page will be protected. I suggest folding this story into the existing Romer vandalism story.

briefs.headline: Lil Keed article: minor vandalism by one account, reverted twice
briefs.summary: This isn't news. One account, "6ix9ine Diddy Lover", added unsourced text to the English Wikipedia article on the late rapper Lil Keed twice. Both edits were changes to the line about his family. The first called his brother Lil Gotit "younger and heavier", with the edit summary "needed extra details". The second invented a twin brother named "Christian Boultan". Two other editors, Rencoolguy and Smallestredboy, reverted each edit within minutes, and the article is back to its earlier text. No other language versions moved, and nothing in the edits points to a real-world event. Judging by the edits and the username, this is an attention-seeking or joke account, not an edit war.

briefs.headline: US midterms page adds report that Iran stalled talks to sway the vote, plus GOP-distancing analysis
briefs.summary: Three registered editors made four additive edits to en:2026 United States elections within about 17 minutes. There were no reverts and no activity on other pages or languages. Pachu Kannan added a report, credited to Reuters and published by the Times of Israel on 20 Oct 2026, that senior Iranian officials said Tehran deliberately dragged out talks with the US to weaken Trump before the November midterms. He also changed the lead to say the Iran war was driven partly by "prolonged diplomatic talks". In the same edit he changed "the ongoing conflict with Iran" to "the conflict with Iran". The new text also says officials expected fighting to resume, which may mean active hostilities have paused, but I have not confirmed this elsewhere in the graph. Emperorpenguinn extended a paragraph about vulnerable Republicans (Rogers, Hinson) distancing themselves from the war; their earlier text cites Trump's 32% Reuters/Ipsos approval. Re000searchist added material on Trump criticising his election advisers to a section on Democrats leading the polls. These are ordinary, sourced campaign-coverage updates rather than a breaking event or a dispute. The one fresh news item is the Iranian officials' claim, which is a single-source report of what the officials said.

briefs.headline: 'Deaths in 2026' list adds Grimau, Kruusa, Suárez, Majidzadeh, Lee Kwan-young
briefs.summary: This is routine upkeep of English Wikipedia's 'Deaths in 2026' list. New entries: Argentine actor Antonio Grimau, 82 (Canal26, Oct 20). Estonian poet and translator Kalju Kruusa, 53 (Delfi, 20th). Mexican telenovela actor Carlos Miguel Suárez (López-Dóriga, 19th). Iranian archaeologist Yusef Majidzadeh, 90 (ISNA). South Korean taekwondo grandmaster Lee Kwan-young, 80 (French taekwondo federation). There are no reverts or disputes, only small cleanups. The -155 removal from the 19th and the +155 addition to the 17th by the same editor are probably Majidzadeh's entry being moved to the correct date, but I couldn't load that diff to confirm. None of these deaths shows a cluster of related page activity, so none looks like breaking news on its own.

briefs.headline: Persian Wikipedia bio of Kermanshah academic rewritten in apparent self-promotion, then flagged for deletion
briefs.summary: The page is a small Persian Wikipedia biography of Alireza Shahrestani, a literature researcher and university lecturer in Kermanshah. In rev 44793349, editor Saeedmgh replaced the sourced, modest stub with a promotional rewrite: a new infobox and a lead calling him a professor, author and media activist who writes on resistance literature and on statements by the Islamic Revolution's leaders. The pasted text still carried leftovers from a chat or messaging export, including a sender line "A Shahrestani, [29/07/1405 09:04]" and a note that the material had been formatted "so you can upload it directly to Wikipedia". That suggests the subject, or someone working for him, supplied it, i.e. a likely conflict of interest. Rev 44793350 then removed those leftover lines. About 15 minutes later, Golpeti nominated the article for timed deletion for lacking sources that show notability (rev 44793368). I see no real-world news event here, only a routine conflict-of-interest and notability cleanup with no reverts or edit war. I didn't read the two smaller follow-up edits (0 and −40 bytes).

briefs.headline: Update: Amancio Ortega es.wiki vandalism continues, partly reverted; earlier damage remains

From the diffs, the heading and Filantropía insults reported earlier also appear to still be on the page, though I haven't checked the current page directly. The graph shows no edits after Geom's revert, which suggests the page needs a deeper revert to a clean version and possibly protection.

briefs.headline: Amancio Ortega es.wiki article hit by juvenile vandalism from two temporary accounts

Uncertain: at the time of the dossier, the four later vandal edits had not been reverted. The page may need cleanup or protection, but there is nothing newsworthy here.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Balonmano' page: insults aimed at local handball players
briefs.summary: This is not routine editing. It is a schoolyard-style vandalism spree, with the vandal and a patroller undoing each other's edits on es:Balonmano (the handball article). Two near-identical accounts, Domnmaiquol and DonMaiquol (probably the same person), kept rewriting the infobox 'nombre' field. The changes were a Catalan club taunt ("HANDBOL MOLINS NO HANDBOL COPERATIVA SANT BOI TOOPPP") and insults about named people ("Miuqle romeu calienta banquillos", "Oriol Montañes Chaquetero", "Ñavi Chaquetero Calienta Banquillos"). Patroller LMLM reverted about six times, with comments saying so, though the revert flag was not set. That explains why the scout's note said there were no reverts. The latest edit (rev 175930974) still showed vandalism when this was filed, so it may still be up. The named people look like local youth or amateur players from the Molins de Rei and Sant Boi area, not a real news event. The page and its insults could raise privacy and personal-attack concerns, so the page may need protection and the account may need blocking.

briefs.headline: es:Balonmano vandalism reverted; infobox back to 'Balonmano', no new edits since
briefs.summary: This updates the prior vandalism brief. It is not a news event. After DonMaiquol's last edit (rev 175930974), the infobox 'nombre' field read "Ñavi Chaquetero Calienta Banquillos", an insult aimed at a named person. Patroller LMLM then undid that edit and the one before it in rev 175930993, putting the field back to "Balonmano". The pattern hasn't changed: one vandal using two near-identical accounts (Domnmaiquol and DonMaiquol), insults aimed at what look like local Catalan handball players, and a single patroller reverting. It is still one page in one language. The page could still be hit again, since the graph doesn't show whether the account was blocked or the page protected.

briefs.headline: 49ers reportedly release DL Naquan Jones; Wikipedia page updated
briefs.summary: Two temporary-account editors updated the en-wiki page for nose tackle Naquan Jones to say the San Francisco 49ers have released him. The first edit (rev 1381234638, "Released by 49ers.") removed the 49ers as his current team and changed his tenure to 2026 only. That edit still stands. The second editor added a sentence saying he was released on October 20, 2026, and gave a NBC Sports/ProFootballTalk link ("49ers-release-dl-naquan-jones"), but only in the edit summary, not as a citation in the article. A patroller reverted that sentence as an "unsourced addition to BLP" (biography of a living person). That is a sourcing-procedure revert, not a dispute over whether the release happened. Jones had signed with the 49ers on September 23, 2026. This is a routine NFL roster move, not an edit war or vandalism. I haven't independently checked the ProFootballTalk link.

briefs.headline: 2005 Tamil film "Ayodhya" article kept within hours of deletion nomination
briefs.summary: This is internal Wikipedia upkeep, not a real-world event. On 21 Oct 2026, DareshMohan removed about 2 KB of material citing unreliable sources (rev 1381264115), including the Production section and a bbthots review. Minutes later they nominated the stub for deletion. Kailash29792 then added sources, including a 2005 Chennai Online review by Malini Mannath, and recategorised the film as an interfaith romantic drama (rev 1381269219). The nominator then added sourced detail on the director's debut (rev 1381269611), which suggests they accepted the outcome. There were no reverts, no anonymous edits and no other languages involved, and the editors cooperated, so this is not an edit war. The film's title refers to the holy city of Ayodhya, but nothing in the edits ties the activity to news about that city.

briefs.headline: Tamil film "Ayodhya" article sees cooperative cleanup after speedy keep
briefs.summary: This is routine Wikipedia upkeep with no real-world news angle. briefs.headline: Pertes de Thémines (fr-wiki): editor expands karst sinkhole article; routine, nothing to report
briefs.summary: The burst on the French article about the Pertes de Thémines, a set of karst swallow-holes in the Lot department, is routine article-building. Nearly all of the churn comes from Thierry46, who is filling in "Situation et accès" and "Risques" sections that had been placeholders ({{...}}). His additions are sourced to a 2006 CDS46 caving inventory and the CDS46 website. The new text covers where the site is (about 8 swallow-holes spread over 300 m, near the mairie). It also covers access rules: the site was protected by prefectoral order on 27 August 1986, a municipal order sets the access conditions, and visits are banned when the flood gauge is above 30 cm. It also notes the risks of falling and drowning in a flood. No text was removed except placeholders and a maintenance banner. Ariel Provost and Père Igor made small copyedits. There were no reverts and no sign that a real-world event, such as a flood or an accident, set this off. The flood-safety wording describes standing rules, not an incident.

briefs.headline: Catalan Wikipedia bio of philosopher Fernando Savater hit by schoolyard vandalism

briefs.headline: Helen Haines article now sources double amputation to 7News report quoting her husband
briefs.summary: The open question from our last brief is now answered. MrActiniuM's rev 1381282053 ("Added reference", +416 bytes) attached a 7News report, via MSN and dated 21 October 2026, to the body sentence "Both her legs were amputated as a result of the attack". The report is headlined "Helen Haines' husband Phil reveals surgeons have amputated both of MP's legs injured in alleged attack". I confirmed this by reading the 'before' text of the next revision. That means the two-leg amputation is no longer unsourced: a named outlet reports it, citing her husband. Until now the claim rested only on temporary-account edits and an ABC headline saying "loses leg". MrActiniuM followed with rev 1381282561 ("Added more references", +428 bytes) in the same paragraph. That diff was cut off, so I can't say which extra sources it adds. There have been no new edits since then and no reverts, and no other language editions are linked in the graph. Remaining caveats: the 7News claim is secondhand (the husband, via MSN), and I have not read the outlet's text itself.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack article: no new facts since last brief; 'both legs' claim still unsourced
briefs.summary: This follow-up adds nothing new. The only edit since our last brief is a 4-byte copyedit by GraziePrego in the board-roles section, which removes a stray "now" (rev 1381275046). It has nothing to do with the attack. The rest of the window is the same set of edits we already covered, all on the enwiki page, with no reverts. MrCryptoNerd added a Guardian report that the family of suspect Brendan Nugent says they have been friends with Haines for more than 20 years. Two temporary accounts changed the injury to 'both legs' amputated. One did it in the lead (rev 1381274408), with no source and the edit summary '/* */'. The other did it in the body (rev 1381273787), with an edit summary that credits AFP. The citation still in the article is the ABC headline 'Helen Haines loses leg', so the two-leg claim remains unverified, and nobody has reverted or sourced it yet. No other language editions or new editors appear in the graph. The story is still active, but this window is only maintenance.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines article: editors now treat 'both legs amputated' as settled; new source added
briefs.summary: Four new edits by registered editors landed on the enwiki Helen Haines article after our last brief. There were no reverts and no activity in other languages. In the lead, MrCryptoNerd (rev 1381280033) and then Liminal909 (rev 1381281725) changed the wording to "both of her legs were later amputated". Both edits are rewording only, with no new source. The 'both legs' claim was first added by temporary accounts, and these established editors are now keeping and polishing it rather than removing it. MrActiniuM's edit (rev 1381282053, +416 bytes, summary "Added reference") goes into the body sentence 'Both her legs were amputated', which until now cited only an ABC headline saying "loses leg". The diff I received was cut off, so I cannot confirm what the new reference is or whether it supports two amputations. Rhain (rev 1381281564) added that Haines ruled out joining a proposed teal-independent party in May 2026, citing the Border Mail, and removed the 'expand section' tag. This is background, not news about the attack. Overall the story is consolidating rather than breaking: the two-leg amputation is gaining editor consensus, but we still have not confirmed its source.

briefs.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines article tracks follow-up on alleged vehicle attack; 'both legs' claim unsourced
briefs.summary: This is not routine upkeep. The enwiki article on independent federal MP Helen Haines (Indi, Victoria) has a '2026 attack' section, and editors are adding follow-up details to it. The section says she was struck by a 4WD outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October 2026, that she is in critical but stable condition at the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne after surgery, and that a 43-year-old suspect, Brendan Nugent, was arrested at the scene by a member of the public. It also says he was charged on 20 October with Victorian state offences and a Commonwealth offence of causing harm to a public official, and was remanded in custody until 4 February 2027. These details cite ABC, the Guardian, BBC and news.com.au. The newest edits are the Guardian's report that Nugent's family has known Haines for about 20 years (MrCryptoNerd), and a rewording of the charges paragraph (Mhaot). Two temporary accounts changed the injury from one leg to 'both legs requiring amputation', citing AFP in an edit summary. The source already in the article (ABC) says she lost one leg, and the lead edit I read adds no source, so treat the 'both legs' claim as unverified. The graph only holds the last 4 edits (4 editors, about 80 minutes, no reverts) out of 121 page edits in total, so we are seeing the tail of a bigger story. No pages in other languages are linked in the graph. Also, the lead calls it a 'deliberate attack' while the body says 'allegedly', which may get changed.

briefs.headline: Routine cleanup of German Wikipedia bio of Japanologist Sven Saaler; no news hook
briefs.summary: This is maintenance work on the German Wikipedia article about Sven Saaler, a German historian and Japanologist (doctorate from Bonn in 1999, later at the German Institute for Japanese Studies in Tokyo). Three established editors made 5 edits in about 9 minutes, with no reverts. I read four of the diffs. Tom md changed quotation marks and wiki links. Kurator71 cleaned up the formatting and redundant links, turned the career list into prose ("Liste ausformuliert"), and added a {{Belege fehlen}} tag, which flags the article for missing sources (comment: "Belege?"). AHZ made a small 8-byte follow-up that I didn't read. None of the edits add news, such as an appointment, award, death or controversy. The page has no linked articles in other languages, and the article reads like a recently created CV-style bio getting its first quality review. I'm not certain the article is new: the graph only shows edits from this session onward.

briefs.headline: Hebrew 'First Zionist Congress' article hit by two vandalism edits, both reverted
