This was two separate rounds of vandalism on the Hebrew Wikipedia article about the First Zionist Congress (Basel, 1897), and both were undone quickly. First, a temporary account (~2026-56263-10) put a crude word ("פלוץ", meaning "fart") into the lead sentence about the 208 delegates. Ori reverted it about 40 minutes later. Then Galmyst, an account with only this one edit, deleted about 4 KB of sourced background text: Herzl's choice of venue and the Munich Jewish community's opposition, cited to Avineri and Elon. Galmyst replaced it with keyboard mash ("sdcsccs", "dds", "njcrhu"). אריאל ר. restored the text in full about 9 minutes later. The "8153 churn" figure is just the 4,072-byte deletion plus the 4,072-byte restore, not new content. Nothing ties this to any real-world news, and no other-language versions of the article were part of the story.

briefs.headline: Sergen Yalçın named Turkey national team head coach, Wikipedia edits indicate
briefs.summary: Three registered editors on tr-wiki updated Sergen Yalçın's biography within about six minutes. The edits say the Turkish Football Federation appointed him head coach of the Turkey senior national team on 20 October 2026. Hakanp added a new "Türkiye A Milli Takımı" section citing a TFF announcement titled "A Millî Takımımızın Yeni Teknik Direktörü Sergen Yalçın". It says a 4-year contract "will be signed" (future tense), so the contract may not be signed yet. -Fatih- ended his current Beşiktaş spell (2025–2026) in the succession box and added a new box naming him Turkey's 47th coach, succeeding Vincenzo Montella. Separately, an en-wiki editor changed the Turkey national team infobox coach from "Vacant" to Sergen Yalçın, so the post appears to have been empty beforehand. An editor added a contract end date of 2030, and Hakanp removed it. That looks like ordinary cleanup, not an edit war. There were no reverts or vandalism signals. I have not checked the TFF source itself, and coverage is still thin: no other language pages besides en-wiki have moved yet, and the Beşiktaş articles show no edits so far.

briefs.headline: Sergen Yalçın named Turkey coach; edits spread to national-team pages, contract now "signed"
briefs.summary: This is a follow-up to the tracked story; the editing activity is the same event, not a new one. briefs.headline: New de-wiki article on Indian slide guitarist Barun Kumar Pal; routine cleanup follows
briefs.summary: Toolittle created a new German Wikipedia biography of Barun Kumar Pal (rev 271491432 and earlier; creation rev 271491291, +3,752 bytes). The edits look like normal article creation and upkeep, not news. One caveat: something off-wiki could have prompted the article, but the edits show no sign of it.

briefs.headline: Pfeffer death article gets retirement source; Tewes page unrelated (new-page patrol)
briefs.summary: I found no new event here. Bernhard Tewes is not a ZDF sports figure. SeeMyWest created his German Wikipedia page as a new biography (+6340 bytes). It describes him as a Berlin-based alternative practitioner for psychotherapy (Heilpraktiker), a hypnotherapist ("Kiez Hypnose" practice in Friedrichshain) and the author of the 2025 Rowohlt book "Glimmer", citing Deutschlandfunk Kultur, taz and Perlentaucher. On the Pfeffer article, Berghest's latest edit (+226) only adds a Newsroom.de source (12 Aug 2024, "Generationswechsel im ZDF-Sport") for his retirement after Paris 2024. It adds nothing new about his death. The earlier brief stands: his death is reported, but whether it was in September or October 2026 is still unresolved.

briefs.headline: Longtime ZDF sports commentator Michael Pfeffer reported dead after sea accident off Rio
briefs.summary: A new German Wikipedia article on Michael Pfeffer (b. 1958/59) was created by Berghest (+2332 bytes). It describes him as a ZDF sports commentator for more than 30 years who covered alpine skiing, the Tour de France (1998–2011, alongside Peter Leissl) and several Olympics, and who retired after Paris 2024. The article says he died aged 67 from the effects of a sports accident in the sea off Rio de Janeiro, where his Brazilian wife's family lived. It cites a Stern piece headlined "ZDF-Sportreporter in Brasilien verstorben" (dated 21 Oct 2026) and an obituary by Leissl on the German sports journalists' association (VDS) site. The other edits are small: Karim fixed grammar and added a category, plus two typo fixes. Nobody reverted anything, and no other language pages moved. Open questions: the article first gave October 2026 as the date of death, but Berghest then changed it to September 2026, citing a blog post whose URL is dated 2026/09. The VDS citation is also dated 2025, probably a typo. So the death looks real and well sourced, but the exact date is not confirmed.

briefs.headline: Pfeffer obituary article: career detail added, unsourced birth date removed; no new event
briefs.summary: These are follow-up edits to the new German article on former ZDF sports commentator Michael Pfeffer. Nothing new has been reported about his death. Berghest expanded the career section (+397): Pfeffer commentated the Olympic debut of ski cross at Vancouver 2010, citing the Allgäuer Zeitung, and covered boxing and cycling at Summer Games. Berghest then fixed typos. Fcsch added an exact birth date, 15 June 1959, citing "private knowledge" (private Kenntnis). Horst Gräbner reverted it to "1958 or 1959" a minute later, pointing to the biography guideline (WP:BIO) and asking for a reputable source. That was a single policy-based correction, not a back-and-forth, so I don't count it as an edit war. M2k added the standard person-data block (Personendaten), which records the death as September 2026 in Rio de Janeiro. The article now says September everywhere, but that date still rests mainly on a blog post (URL dated 2026/09), while the Stern source noted in the earlier brief is dated 21 Oct 2026. So the month is still not firmly confirmed.

briefs.headline: Malala Yousafzai es-wiki page hit by temporary-account vandalism, reverted by bots

briefs.headline: Malala Yousafzai es-wiki churn is reverted vandalism; no new activity, no news
briefs.summary: This is the same Spanish-language Wikipedia vandalism episode already on file. It is not a new event. Temporary account ~2026-56153-82 typed keyboard-mash into the lead ("mhgcvbh") and garbled sentences (rev 175916488, -358 bytes). It then deleted the infobox and large parts of the biography (rev 175916540, -932). Patroller Arjuno3, SeroBOT and Automoderador undid every edit. That explains the scout's "no reverts" note, and the 2,326-byte churn is just damage and repair cancelling out. That edit raised the entry count in the infobox from 32 to 33 (rev 1381174224). A few minutes later an anonymous editor changed the prose to match ("thirty-three countries"), a 2-byte consistency fix rather than vandalism (rev 1381181024). SpaceInferno1211 added what their edit summary called an "unofficial confirmation" of Azerbaijan's participation. Tanvavad reverted it because the source, eurovisionfun, is listed as unreliable for this page. That makes it a single sourcing dispute, not an edit war. Caveats: the Azerbaijan diff was cut off, so its content comes from the edit summary, and Serbia's confirmation rests on one fan-site report that I haven't checked against RTS or the EBU.

briefs.headline: Schoolyard vandalism on cs-wiki Czech regions and Great Wall pages, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: This is low-level vandalism, not a news event. Over about two hours, temporary accounts and one new account (~2026-56155-46, ~2026-56162-49, ~2026-56137-46, Gerfgaefg) made small edits to 'Kraje v Česku' (Czech regions) and 'Velká čínská zeď' (Great Wall of China). They inserted insults aimed at named people ('vladik lox', 'sasha loxpendik'), swapped 'čínské úřady' (Chinese authorities) for a vulgar word, and typed gibberish into the history section. Patrollers OJJ, Kendo13 and JirkaSv reverted each edit within seconds to minutes, some with the summary 'revert vandalismu' (vandalism revert). It is not an edit war because no edit was restored after a revert. The 'churn of 64' is just the total of the small back-and-forth changes, not list maintenance. The insults use Russian-language slang and name individuals, which looks like a few people messing around together, maybe schoolkids. That part is a guess. No other languages were involved and nothing in the content points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Cs-wiki schoolyard vandalism reaches 5 pages, now incl. Humanismus and Software; all reverted
briefs.summary: The low-level vandalism on cs-wiki has spread from 'Kraje v Česku', 'Velká čínská zeď' and 'Komprese dat' to two more articles, 'Humanismus (ideologie)' and 'Software'. Nothing points to a news event. On Humanismus, temporary account ~2026-56078-61 twice cut text from the lead. One edit blanked the bolded title word and part of a sentence; the other chopped off the opening sentences. Kendo13 undid both within about 20 seconds to 2.5 minutes, with the summary 'bezdůvodné odstraňování obsahu' (unexplained removal of content). On Software, ~2026-56266-83 renamed the section 'Škodlivý software' (malicious software) to 'zlý software' (evil software), and Kendo13 undid it 12 seconds later. On Komprese dat, the earlier vandal ~2026-56121-92 came back with 'tibor je frajer' (Tibor is cool) and a 729-byte removal, both reverted. I couldn't load the text of those two Komprese diffs, so I'm going on the edit summaries and size changes. Every vandal edit comes from a different throwaway temporary account, falls within the same burst of roughly 15 minutes, and was reverted, mostly by Kendo13. Nobody restored anything after a revert, so this is not an edit war. The pattern looks like a few people, possibly one classroom, acting at the same time, but that is a guess. No other language versions were involved.

briefs.headline: Cs-wiki schoolyard vandalism spreads to 'Komprese dat' article; all edits reverted
briefs.summary: The low-level vandalism on cs-wiki's 'Kraje v Česku' (Czech regions) and 'Velká čínská zeď' (Great Wall of China) has spread to a third page, 'Komprese dat' (data compression). It is not a news event. A different temporary account, ~2026-56121-92, made three edits within about 7 minutes. It added schoolyard insults about named people: 'denis má erekci' ('Denis has an erection'), 'tibor ma rad sulina' ('Tibor likes Sulin'), 'tibor je špatný v r6' ('Tibor is bad at R6'). It also typed keyboard gibberish into the References section and finally replaced the lead paragraph with the single word 'KAARINA'. Patrollers JirkaSv and Kendo13 undid each edit within about 15 seconds to 4 minutes, some with the summary 'revert vandalismu' (vandalism revert), and the article is back to its earlier text. The larger edit sizes (±291, ±729) come from deleted paragraphs, not from real content work. Nobody restored the vandal text after a revert, so this is not an edit war. The vandal account didn't edit the other two pages, so linking it to the same group is a guess, based on matching timing, style, the same patrollers and the same wiki. The insults here are in Czech or Slovak, not the Russian slang seen on the other pages, so it may be a different person or several people (possibly schoolkids) acting at the same time. No other language versions were involved.

briefs.headline: Richard J. Aldrich bio: routine cleanup of unsourced claims, no news event
briefs.summary: I found no real-world news here. This is ordinary sourcing maintenance on the en-wiki biography of intelligence historian Richard J. Aldrich, and it isn't an edit war or vandalism. A temporary account added one sentence: "He is currently a professor at the University of Warwick as of 2026." Strongshorts reverted it within about 20 seconds using the Interceptor tool, citing missing sources (rev 1381168696). A few minutes later, Celjski Grad undid two earlier edits by Deewitz, an editor who doesn't appear in this burst. The first removed a claim about a 2019 Leverhulme Trust Major Research Fellowship, with the summary "No such source". The second removed a claim that Aldrich co-edits the Studies in Intelligence book series with Christopher Andrew and Claudia Hillebrand, and moved the sentence about his Warwick professorship back into place. No edit was reverted a second time, there was no back-and-forth, and no other languages or pages moved. I can't tell whether the removed claims are actually false or just badly cited.

briefs.headline: Richard J. Aldrich bio: routine sourcing cleanup, no news event (same as tracked story)

I can't tell whether the removed claims are false or just badly cited, since both relied on reused citations ("Warwick", "Warwick2").

briefs.headline: Swedish 'Fall of the Roman Empire' article hit by small vandalism, rolled back
briefs.summary: This is a one-page, sv-wiki only incident with no real-world news value. One temporary account (~2026-56166-67) made three edits within about 4 minutes. Each one swapped "Roman" for "Mango": the {{Romerska riket}} template became {{Mango Riket}}, and the hatnote "Romarrikets fall" became "Mangorikets Fall" twice. Two established editors undid every change with rollbacks: Nirmos twice, then Lars Törnqvist. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but the graph's revert flag simply missed them; the edit comments show these were rollbacks ("Rullade tillbaka"). The article is back to its previous version and I found no activity in other languages.

briefs.headline: Minor ru-wiki vandalism on Magneto pages, all reverted by bot within seconds
briefs.summary: This is low-level vandalism, not news. A temporary account (~2026-56428-88) made small changes to three ru-wiki Magneto/Erik Lensherr pages. It put "Элекс Мерсер" (Alex Mercer, a character from the Prototype video game) into the infobox "full name" field on Магнето (Marvel Comics). It also swapped the alias "Магнитный парень" for the same name on the Ultimate Marvel page, and made a 1-byte change to the film-series page. EyeBot reverted every edit within about 15–20 seconds, flagged by ORES/LWA scores. The Nagiev page is not about an actor or a dubbing role, as the scout guessed: it is about Anatoly Nagiev, a Soviet serial killer executed in 1982. A different temporary account (~2026-56244-26) cut his first name from "Анатолий" to "Атолий", and EyeBot reverted that too. Only 3 editors were involved (two temporary accounts plus the bot), not 8. The link between the Nagiev page and the Magneto pages looks like a coincidence of timing, but I can't rule out that it's the same person on two accounts.

briefs.headline: India's 2026 Asian Para Games page updated live with day's medals; one minor revert
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia page "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" is getting a steady stream of results updates from mostly one editor (Neeelzzz20), plus small edits by two others. The diffs add 20 October medals: gold for Pranav Soorma and silver for Ram Ratan Singh in the men's discus F51-53 (rev 1381157032); bronze for Himanshu Nandal in the men's 400m freestyle S11, which took India's bronze count from 10 to 11 and its medal total from 23 to 24 (rev 1381148410); and gold for Simran Sharma with a Games-record 24.80, plus bronze for Tejalben Damor, in a women's sprint final (rev 1381158522). The only revert was a good-faith formatting fix. Mr Gupta 18 had added a heat time and qualification mark, and Neeelzzz20 undid it, explaining that athletics heat results are recorded differently from swimming (revs 1381157121, 1381157356). This isn't an edit war or vandalism. It's normal live tracking of an ongoing multi-sport event. I haven't checked the results against outside sources, and the medal counts may change as the event goes on.

briefs.headline: India's Asian Para Games page adds Simran Sharma 200m T12 gold to medal table; routine
briefs.summary: The English page "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" is still being updated routinely during the event. Two edits have come in since the last brief. Mr Gupta 18 added Simran Sharma to the medalists table as a 20 October gold in the women's 200 m T12, which takes India's listed gold rows from 6 to 7 (rev 1381159093). That matches Neeelzzz20's athletics edit, which gave her a 24.80 Games record and gold and gave Tejalben Damor bronze with a personal-best 25.23 (rev 1381158522). A temporary account added a note to the badminton bracket that a match against Korea's Shin Kyung-hwan is set for 21 October (rev 1381158513), so India's badminton campaign continues. Nothing has been reverted since the earlier good-faith undo. The editors' work is consistent and there's no sign of vandalism or an edit war. I haven't checked the results against outside sources, and the medal tally will keep changing.

briefs.headline: India's Asian Para Games tally reaches 35 after discus and high jump medals added
briefs.summary: Live updating of "India at the 2026 Asian Para Games" (en) is still routine. Most of the new edits come from Mr Gupta 18, with small touches from Neeelzzz20 and Balagurunaadha Velavan, and nothing has been reverted. The diffs add 20 October athletics medals. Nishad Kumar won gold in the men's high jump T47 with 2.04, listed as a Games record. The men's discus F43/44/62/64 had three Indian medallists: Devender Kumar gold (49.71), Rakesh Kumar silver (49.35) and Pardeep Kumar bronze (51.15 PB) (revs 1381166386, 1381168701). The other medals added are a bronze for Hokato Hotozhe Sema in the men's shot put F56/57 (14.65), a bronze for Niranjan Mukundan in the men's 200m IM SM7, and Tejalben Damor's 200m T12 bronze in the medalists table (revs 1381168953, 1381165016). The infobox now reads 9 gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze, 35 in total. The intermediate edits got the totals wrong for a while (one table read 33 and another 34), and the discus results show the bronze medallist with a longer mark than the gold medallist. That could be a typo or a classification-based scoring quirk. There are also small typos ("Denvender Kumar", a broken Rakesh Kumar link). These are good-faith mistakes, not vandalism, and I haven't checked any of this against outside sources.

briefs.headline: India Asian Para Games page: athletics schedule filled in for 21 Oct, tally still 35
briefs.summary: The three edits since the last brief add no new medals. Mr Gupta 18's +603 edit fills the athletics results tables with "21 Oct" final dates and n/a markers for events with no heats, which tells us more Indian athletes compete on 21 October. It also changes one class label from T62/64 to T64 (rev 1381170601). Neeelzzz20 fixed the "Denvender Kumar" typo the last brief flagged, so the medalists table now reads Devender Kumar (rev 1381169926). Balagurunaadha Velavan filled in two blank cells in the swimming table with the numbers 8 and 6, probably heat or rank placings (rev 1381170186). Nothing was reverted, and the infobox tally of 9 gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze (35 total) is unchanged. Edits are in English only. This is good-faith live tracking with no sign of vandalism or an edit war. Still open: the discus bronze mark is longer than the gold mark, and none of this has been checked against outside sources.

briefs.headline: Dan Moore bio vandalized with fake death date, reverted; no roster move evident
