briefs.headline: 17 October riots: France-wide cost-of-living unrest; civilian injury count cut to 400+
briefs.summary: The English article "17 October riots" describes nationwide unrest in France on 17 October 2026 over living costs, fuel prices, public services and education. It escalated when student groups joined protests called by trade unions and the yellow vests. The article quotes Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez as saying 110 marches drew 550,000 people, 110,000 of them in Paris; organisers put it at 800,000. Its infobox also lists injured police in Belgium (5) and Italy (7). In the latest edits, Whitesin21 changed the French civilian injury figure from 2,600 to "400+", saying the 2,600 figure was really the number of arrests. That arrest figure is unsourced in the diff, and the comment says "2,400" while the old value was 2,600, so casualty and arrest numbers are unreliable for now. The other edits were housekeeping. Bill-Lee67 added "2026" and "in France" to the lede, and Jeffrey34555 added "France", then undid his own edit, which accounts for the cluster's one revert. That revert is not an edit war. On the Limoges Hôtel de Ville article, Dormskirk put the lead back in the present tense ("is a municipal building") and asked editors to discuss on the talk page first. The article still says the building was "set ablaze by arson", citing France 24 ("largely lost") and Le Parisien ("détruit"). Whether the building survived is still disputed.

briefs.headline: Limoges town hall reported badly damaged by arson in 17 October riots; wiki tweaks wording
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Limoges's Hôtel de Ville, a listed monument from 1883, now says the building was set on fire during the "17 October riots" in France. It cites France 24 ("Town hall in Limoges 'largely lost' to blaze set during French protests") and Le Parisien, which reports the town hall was destroyed by fire after a protest against the cost of living. The current burst is small. One edit added an image. One edit changed "France" to "Frinch", and Jeppiz reverted it within a minute; that was a typo or minor vandalism, not an edit war. Two editors then argued over how bad the damage was in the wording: Jabba550 changed "nearly destroyed" to "partially destroyed", and AnonymouslyFrench changed it to "set ablaze" and put the building in the past tense ("was a municipal building"). That suggests at least one editor thinks it is lost. The fire was already in the article before this burst, and a linked "17 October riots" article has 13 edits in the graph. The German article on the building got a 1-byte edit. How badly the building was damaged is still disputed in the text and needs to be checked against outside reporting. Treat this as a follow-on to a wider riots story, not a new event.

briefs.headline: 17 October riots: no new edits; casualty and arrest figures still unsourced
briefs.summary: The scout flagged a burst of 3 editors, 4 edits and 1 revert, all in English. These are the same edits the 1792507204 brief already covered, and nothing has been edited on either tracked page since. In rev 1381183464, Whitesin21 changed French civilian injuries from "2,600" to "400+" in the infobox. The edit summary says there were 2,400 arrests, not injuries. The diff gives no source, and the 2,400 doesn't match the 2,600 that was removed, so treat both casualty and arrest numbers as unverified. The revert is Jeffrey34555 undoing his own edit, which had added "in France" to the lede (rev 1381183362). It is housekeeping, not an edit war. The linked French article "Manifestations du 17 octobre 2026" (134 edits) was last edited at ts 1792504943, adding photo galleries for Limoges and Marseille, so other languages show no new developments. Story status stays developing. Whether the Limoges town hall survived is still disputed on its article.

briefs.headline: Small fa-wiki edits to 1973 Tehran derby and symphony orchestra pages, bot-reverted
briefs.summary: Two unconnected Persian Wikipedia pages got small edits from two different temporary accounts, and the anti-vandalism bot Dexbot (Shahbaz system) reverted every change within about a minute. The pages are the 13th Tehran derby, a historical Persepolis vs Taj match played on 7 September 1973 (16 Shahrivar 1352), and the Tehran Symphony Orchestra. On the derby page one account added +94 and +71 bytes (one in the section "Tension in Taj's camp"). Dexbot then reverted it (−165 bytes) as suspected vandalism. On the orchestra page another account added 46 bytes to the "Conductors" section, also reverted. No human editor touches both pages, no other-language versions moved, and a 50-year-old match has no news hook. This looks like low-grade unsourced or test edits, not a real-world event. Caveat: the diff text could not be fetched, so the content of the edits is unverified. This assessment rests on metadata, edit summaries and the bot's revert reasons.

briefs.headline: Cube Entertainment threat vandalism stays reverted; no new activity, not news
briefs.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief. No edits have hit Cube Entertainment or Dustin Poirier since 420yeahh's revert (rev 1381242810). I checked the graph for anything after that timestamp and found nothing. That revert took out temp account ~2026-56501-62's text: abuse aimed at company staff, plus a violent, sexual threat against executive Ahn Woohyung and his family. The account made four vandal edits in total, and all four were reverted. The Poirier activity is separate, minor vandalism. Rev 1381242601 by ~2026-56286-41 changed his 2019 UFC 242 loss to Khabib Nurmagomedov (a rear-naked choke submission) into a false knockout win, and it was reverted as unsourced. Only English Wikipedia is involved, with three patrollers and no sign of any real-world event. Still to do: block the account, delete the threatening revisions, and possibly have admins review the threat. The Poirier edit should be split off from this story.

briefs.headline: Cube Entertainment vandal comes back with worse threats, reverted again; Poirier edit unrelated
briefs.summary: The same temporary account (~2026-56501-62) came back to the English Wikipedia article on Cube Entertainment a third and fourth time. In rev 1381242630 it added abusive text about company staff and a violent, sexual threat against executive Ahn Woohyung. Rev 1381242757 extended the threat to his family. 420yeahh removed both edits about 30 seconds later (rev 1381242810), so the page is clean again. That makes four vandal edits from one account, all reverted. Because it keeps coming back, the account probably needs a block, and the threatening revisions should go to admins for revision deletion and possibly emergency/threat review. On Dustin Poirier, a different temp account (~2026-56286-41) made a harmless wording edit (rev 1381242166, undone by QuickPilot23). It then rewrote the 2019 Khabib Nurmagomedov fight as a Poirier knockout win (rev 1381242601), which is false because he lost by submission. "This is a hard decision" reverted it as unsourced. The only link between the two pages is that one patroller reverted both, so this isn't real-world news. I agree with the Scout: this isn't a new story. The Poirier edit should be split off or dropped from this story.

briefs.headline: Cube Entertainment page hit by vandalism from one temp account; both edits reverted
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56501-62) vandalised the English Wikipedia article on Cube Entertainment twice in about six minutes. The first edit (rev 1381241108) changed the company's name in the opening sentence to an insult. TonySt reverted it using an anti-vandalism tool. The second edit (rev 1381241654) added a line of violent and sexual threats against named company executives, and "This is a hard decision" reverted it within about 90 minutes. Neither edit pointed to any real company news, no other language versions moved, and the page is back to its stable version. The added text was abusive, so admins may want to look at it for possible revision deletion, but this is not a news story.

briefs.headline: Update: French protest curfews article stable; 'European Spring' rename pushed twice, reverted
briefs.summary: There is no new reporting on the ground. The most recent substantive edit is still rev 1381164999 (+364, citing Anadolu, 19 Oct). It adds the Gironde department's curfew for unaccompanied minors, 10pm–7am until 26 October, after looting and vandalism on 17 October. That sits alongside the existing text on curfews in Paris (République/Les Halles, 10pm–6am, applying to everyone), Lyon (9pm–6am, Presqu'île) and Nice (minors only). What is new since the last brief: the same temporary account (~2026-56100-21) tried a second time to rename the infobox to "European Spring" (rev 1381170749). Its edit summary says the movement is "spreading throughout Europe", but it adds no source. VocalCat2207 reverted with "Discuss first" (rev 1381170899). That is two rounds between one newcomer and one patroller, so it is a minor naming dispute, not an edit war. The claim that the protests are spreading across Europe has no sources and should not be treated as a real-world signal. The French-language article has seen almost no activity, and confirmation still depends on the cited outlets.

briefs.headline: French youth protest unrest spreads curfews beyond Paris to Lyon, Nice, Gironde
briefs.summary: The English article on the 2026 French student protests is still being updated. It was created about two days ago and has had 78 edits; the French article on the same topic has had 4. The most useful recent edit (rev 1381164999, +364) adds a 19 October update citing Anadolu. It says Paris set a 10pm–6am curfew for everyone around Place de la République and Les Halles and banned gatherings in some neighbourhoods. Lyon and Nice brought in curfews, Nice's for minors only. The Gironde department added a 10pm–7am curfew for unaccompanied minors, due to run until 26 October, after looting and vandalism on 17 October. Earlier text, which had a typo fixed (rev 1381169548), describes school blockades and fires at lycées across Paris and other cities on 2 October, with BBC, Le Figaro, Le Parisien and others cited. There was one piece of vandalism: rev 1381170269 renamed the infobox to "European Spring", and an anti-vandalism tool reverted it within a minute. That aside, there is no edit war. Uncertain: the claims rest on the cited outlets as summarised by editors, and the latest-day burst is small (three editors).

briefs.headline: Harry Chester: wikilink-style tweak to 19th-century biography twice reverted
briefs.summary: This is a cosmetic dispute on the en-wiki biography of Harry Chester, a Victorian civil servant in the Privy Council Office. It does not point to any real-world event. A temporary account (~2026-54405-06) twice changed the piped links to the kings his father served, turning e.g. [[George III of the United Kingdom|King George III]] into King [[George III]]. The first try also added a typo ("Kinga"). 420yeahh reverted that version as a "possible typo". The second, clean version was reverted by Thomasfan1916. No facts, dates or sources were changed. This was one round of back-and-forth, not a sustained edit war, and nothing was seen in other languages. The temp account has about 51 edits in total, so it may be making the same link change on other pages. That is unconfirmed.

briefs.headline: Harry Chester reverts are part of one temp account's link-style sweep, not news
briefs.summary: The Harry Chester page has nothing new since the existing routine brief, and nothing here points to a real-world event. Temporary account ~2026-54405-06 twice changed the piped links to the monarchs, e.g. [[George III of the United Kingdom|King George III]] became King [[George III]]. The first try (rev 1381240372) included the typo "Kinga". Both versions were reverted, by 420yeahh and then Thomasfan1916. The only new finding settles the open question in the prior brief: the account is running the same link change across many British-history pages. Rev 1381241090 on The Opening of New London Bridge shows the identical William IV relinking. In about 90 minutes the same account made small negative-delta edits to roughly 15 other articles, including Portsmouth Harbour (painting), 2nd Royal Surrey Militia, Hercules Langford Rowley and William Hay, 19th Earl of Erroll. I read only the one cross-page diff, so it is an inference that the others are the same change. So far it has been reverted only on Harry Chester. This is not an edit war or vandalism, and it should be merged into the tracked routine story.

briefs.headline: Small revert war on it.wiki bio of Almo Violin over his Vajont disaster role
briefs.summary: The Scout's "no reverts" note is wrong. Italian Wikipedia's article on Almo Violin is in a small edit war. Three temporary accounts keep adding text and the registered editor Sayatek keeps removing it: four exchanges in about 30 minutes, three of them undo-style reverts that were not flagged in the graph. Edit comments say the disputed sentence is "indispensable to understand his role in the Vajont disaster", answer that "this ... doesn't concern the media", and call a later rewording "more correct and not denigratory". It looks like a fight over how to describe the subject's link to the 1963 Vajont dam disaster. Nothing points to new real-world news. The Napoli 2026-27 season page is unrelated routine work (match/attendance updates). It is only grouped with the Violin article because one temp account made a 1-byte edit there. Big caveat: the diff fetches failed every time, so this rests on edit comments, byte sizes and editor patterns, not the actual text. I can't tell if the added wording is sourced or one-sided, or if the three temp accounts are one person.

briefs.headline: it.wiki Almo Violin edit war goes on as a second editor reverts a softened Vajont/SADE line
briefs.summary: The dispute on Italian Wikipedia's bio of engineer Almo Violin is still going. That contradicts the Scout's "no reverts" note: the revert is in the comment (rev 152984828) but the graph didn't flag it. This time the diffs loaded, so we now know what the fight is about. Temporary accounts first added a "Nei media" section citing a 2015 Vajont documentary (rev 152984211). They then inserted a clause saying that as head of Belluno's Genio civile (the state civil-engineering office) Violin "fu malleabile per la SADE" ("was pliable for SADE", the private power company behind the dam) at the Vajont dam. Its only citation is a 1960 journal that appears to cover just his appointment (rev 152984655). Sayatek reverted that version twice. Another temp account (~2026-56095-14) then softened it to "lavorò per la SADE alla diga del Vajont" ("worked for SADE at the Vajont dam"), calling this "more correct and not denigratory" (rev 152984785). A second registered editor, Titore, reverted that too (rev 152984828). The article's existing text on his manslaughter conviction at first instance and later acquittal for insufficient evidence was never touched. The fight is over an unsourced claim that he served SADE's interests, which is a BLP-style neutrality issue about the 1963 disaster, not new real-world news. Four temporary-account IDs are involved and may be one person, but I can't confirm that. One of them made a 1-byte edit to the Napoli 2026-27 season page, which is otherwise routine and unrelated.

briefs.headline: Cambridge Regional College page hit by juvenile alumni-list vandalism
briefs.summary: The activity on the en-wiki Cambridge Regional College article is vandalism, not a news event. One temporary account added the junk line "* Jdrj" (rev 1381183879). Patroller Pyrrhic victor reverted it as test edits with WikiShield (rev 1381183924). A second temporary account then added fake "alumni": "LeBron James, goat", "Benjamin Netanyahu, world admin" and "Frank Nyarko, saviour of the end of the world" (rev 1381184957). At last check that second edit had not been reverted. The 117 bytes of churn come from these joke additions and the revert. The edits touch only this one page in one language. This fits the school-related vandalism also seen on other UK school pages, but nothing links the editors.

briefs.headline: Self-promotional ru-wiki page 'XqwzKOT' tagged for speedy deletion, now apparently deleted
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. A temporary account created the ru-wiki article 'XqwzKOT' in one edit of about 18 KB. That single edit accounts for nearly all the churn. Per its edit summary, the page described a personal software project ('Kot-system', also called xqwz or KOT) and promoted a Telegram channel. Within about 4 minutes, a second temporary account and the patroller Alex NB IT each added a speedy-deletion tag (Критерии быстрого удаления). The second account then undid Alex NB IT's tag because the page already had one ("Тут уже есть один шаблон"). The page was created and tagged within minutes, and no other pages or languages are involved. I could not open any of the 4 diffs because Wikipedia says the revisions no longer exist. That fits the page having been speedily deleted, but this is inferred, not confirmed. Everything above comes from edit summaries in the graph, not from the article text.

briefs.headline: NATO member-states page: one vandal table wipe, reverted in 84 seconds; nothing new
briefs.summary: This is the same episode as the earlier brief, and nothing new has happened since. The graph shows only three edits on enwiki's "Member states of NATO". None of them is newer than the 16,256-byte revert, and the page has no other-language versions linked in the graph. Temporary account ~2026-56255-74 replaced the formatted member table with a plain wikitable, stripping out flags, maps, citations and links. Its edit summary was "I added my buddy richard". TruenoCity reverted it 84 seconds later as "unexplained removal of content", restoring the original table markup. In the part of the diff I could read (Albania's row), the facts were the same: same accession date, population and other figures. There's no sign of a real change in NATO membership. The earlier zero-byte edit to "Military expenditures" by another temporary account is still unresolved, because the diff cuts off before the change. A same-size edit is most likely a small wording or formatting fix. Each editor has touched only this page, and there is no back-and-forth reverting. I recommend merging this into the existing story and closing it.

briefs.headline: NATO member list hit by one apparent vandal edit, reverted within 90 seconds
briefs.summary: The "large churn" on enwiki's Member states of NATO comes from a single edit and its revert, not from a real-world change to NATO membership. Temporary account ~2026-56255-74 replaced the formatted member-state table with a stripped-down wikitable, removing about 16 KB (−16,256 bytes) including flags, maps, citations and links. Its edit summary was "I added my buddy richard", which reads as vandalism. TruenoCity reverted it about 80 seconds later as "unexplained removal of content", and the revert restored all 16,256 bytes. The truncated diff I read showed no change in which countries are listed or when they joined. An earlier zero-byte edit to the Military expenditures section by a different temporary account looks unrelated, but the diff I saw was cut off before the change, so I can't confirm what it altered. Each editor here has touched only this one page, there is no back-and-forth reverting, and no other pages or languages are involved. I recommend closing this.

briefs.headline: It-wiki: patroller reverts navigation hatnotes; new Sa-Nur article unrelated to the rest
briefs.summary: This cluster is not a news event. It is two separate pieces of routine editing that got grouped together. First, temporary account ~2026-56275-64 added "{{torna a|...}}" hatnotes (links pointing readers back to a parent article) to Montecassino (pointing to Cassino), Scauri (pointing to Minturno) and Tremensuoli. Patroller Sayatek reverted these, saying the pages are not "ancillary" entries. Separately, a different temporary account made a small Tremensuoli edit: it added a photo of the Chiesa di San Nicandro Martire and cleaned up some wording. Second, and with no link to the Lazio pages, Stefantiz created a well-sourced it-wiki article on Sa-Nur, a West Bank settlement evacuated in 2005 and officially re-established on 19 April 2026. Sources show Israeli approval in May 2025, and the article's access dates are October 2026, so this is an older development being written up now, not breaking news. Apart from the patroller rolling back an anonymous edit on Sa-Nur, nothing points to an edit war or coordinated vandalism.

briefs.headline: Routine fix on ru.wiki Aleksey Baga bio: Torpedo-BelAZ flag changed, bot revert undone
briefs.summary: This is a minor factual correction, not news. A temporary-account editor changed the flag in the infobox's 2026 career entry for Torpedo-BelAZ from Russia's flag to Belarus's (rev 155716511). Torpedo-BelAZ is a Belarusian club, so the change is correct. The anti-vandalism bot EyeBot automatically reverted it, likely because of the new account's risk score (ORES 0.72). Experienced editor LNTG then undid the bot and restored the Belarusian flag (rev 155716535). There was one revert and one restoration, no ongoing edit war, and no other languages or pages were involved. The 2026 Torpedo-BelAZ entry was already on the page before this cluster, so these edits don't show a new appointment or other event.

briefs.headline: Still routine: flag fix on ru.wiki Aleksey Baga bio holds, no new activity
briefs.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The dossier shows the same three edits. A temporary account changed the flag on the 2026 Torpedo-BelAZ career entry from Russia's to Belarus's (rev 155716511). The bot EyeBot reverted it automatically (rev 155716517). Then LNTG undid the bot (rev 155716535). I read LNTG's diff, which confirms the only change is {{Флаг России}} → {{Флаг Беларуси}} on the existing 2026 Torpedo-BelAZ line. That is correct, because Torpedo-BelAZ is a Belarusian club. There are no more edits, no other pages or languages involved, and no sign of a real-world event behind it.

briefs.headline: Petty vandalism on German Wikipedia's Maria Magdalena article undone within seconds
briefs.summary: This is not a news event, and nothing has changed since the earlier brief. One temporary account, ~2026-56028-91, added the phrase "deine vater" ("your father") to the German article on Mary Magdalene twice. The first time it was dropped into the middle of a sentence in the lead (rev 271479573, summary "ich wars", "it was me"). The second time it was stuck in front of the disambiguation template (rev 271479636, summary "halo wdkdkxkkkdkdkdldldldl"). Established editors Mützelzipfe and Logograph each undid one of these within about 20 seconds. The graph doesn't flag those undos as reverts, but their edit summaries say they are. That is the 46-byte churn the scout saw: two insertions and two undos. There have been no edits to the page since the second undo. The activity stayed on one page in one language, with no sign of anything happening in the real world.

briefs.headline: Minor vandalism on German Wikipedia's Maria Magdalena article, reverted within a minute
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. A single temporary account (~2026-56028-91) twice added the juvenile phrase "deine vater" to the German Wikipedia article on Mary Magdalene. The first time it went mid-sentence in the lead, with the edit summary "ich wars". The second time it went before the disambiguation template, with the summary "halo wdkdkxkkkdkdkdldldldl". Two established editors, Mützelzipfe and Logograph, undid each one within about 20 seconds. The other two edits were those undos, which the graph did not flag as reverts even though their summaries say so. Only this one page was touched, and no other languages show activity. The article is back to its earlier version.

briefs.headline: Spanish Civil War airlift edit war (es-wiki) continues: fourth temporary account, Ontzak reverts
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked edit war on es-wiki "Guerra civil española". It is not a new event. The scout says there were no reverts, but that's wrong. The graph's revert flag is unset, but both new edits are undos, as their comments and diffs show. In rev 175925303 a fourth single-edit temporary account, ~2026-56186-91, put back the disputed 88-byte change to the lead. That change swaps "gracias a la rápida colaboración de la Alemania nazi y la Italia fascista" for "creado por los sublevados con la ayuda de sus aliados extranjeros", sourced to La Razón. Its comment says it is unrelated to "the other account", which it says cited a book by the Francoist activist Fernando Paz and talked about "méritos", and insists it does not deny the foreign help. Fifteen seconds later Ontzak reverted it (rev 175925307), restoring the stable text that names Germany and Italy. The change has now been inserted 4 times by 4 different temporary accounts, and removed 4 times by 3 registered editors. The temporary accounts deny being linked, but they push identical text, each makes only one edit, and they appear one after another, which points to one person rotating accounts. I can't confirm that. No edits have come in since 175925307, and there is no sign of a real-world news trigger. Page protection seems likely.

briefs.headline: Spanish Civil War article (es-wiki): slow edit war over German and Italian role in 1936 airlift
briefs.summary: The six recent edits to es-wiki "Guerra civil española" are not routine. They are an edit war over one sentence in the lead, with the same 88-byte change put in and taken out again and again. The disputed version came from temporary account ~2026-56269-78 (rev 175923799). It drops the wording that the July 1936 airlift from Morocco happened "thanks to the rapid collaboration of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy". In its place it says the airlift was "created by the rebels with the help of their foreign allies", citing a La Razón article. The edit comment argues that the rebels had started the airlift before German and Italian help came. Registered editors Changes forever, Varondán and Ontzak removed the change three times ("Recupero la versión estable"). Two more temporary accounts, ~2026-56375-73 and ~2026-56089-38, put it back twice, one saying "argue before deleting referenced edits". Ontzak's revert (175925253) restored the version naming Germany and Italy. The scout's "no reverts" reading is wrong: the graph's revert flag is unset, but every edit after the first is an undo, according to the edit comments and diffs. Uncertain: the three temporary accounts made one edit each and push the same text, which suggests one person, but I haven't confirmed that. Nothing points to a real-world news event; this is a dispute over how the history is presented, and the page may get protected.

briefs.headline: Oregon OC Drew Mehringer's page hit by antisemitic vandalism after Ducks' losses
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-56212-69) made five edits in about 35 minutes to the en-wiki biography of Oregon offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. The edits added criticism of his offense: a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State, a 17-15 home loss to UCLA with 7 turnovers and 1-of-13 on third down, and a claim that his hiring "is widely associated with the sudden decline" of the program. They also inserted an antisemitic "nickname". Three experienced editors reverted it. Celjski Grad used the anti-vandalism tool Interceptor, Grem833 removed a smaller addition as unsourced, and PhilKnight rolled back the whole day's edits. This is vandalism by an angry fan, not an edit war, and no edit claims he was fired, resigned or reassigned. The only possible news hook is indirect: the cited losses (ESPN and SI links dated around 2026-10-20) point to a rough Oregon season and fan pressure on the coordinator. I haven't checked those game results against any source outside the vandal's text.

briefs.headline: Latvian river article 'Zizma' briefly vandalised by temporary account, quickly reverted
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-55989-48) replaced the name of the Zizma, a small river and tributary of the Lielupe in Latvia's Mežotne and Code parishes, with a personal insult aimed at a named individual. This happened twice: first in the infobox (rev 4537970), then in the lead sentence (rev 4537972). DJ EV undid the first edit within about 20 seconds. NDG reverted the second within a minute and labelled it vandalism. All four edits fell within about 90 seconds. There was no ongoing dispute, no sign of the same activity in other languages, and nothing points to a real-world event. Name-calling schoolyard vandalism like this needs no further follow-up unless the account comes back.

briefs.headline: Latvian vandal's insult spree spreads to 3 pages; school article edit still unreverted
briefs.summary: The vandalism on lvwiki 'Zizma' was more than a one-page incident. It was part of a four-edit spree over about 4.5 minutes by temporary account ~2026-55989-48. The account swapped article names for a homophobic insult aimed at one "Normunds": first on 'Kroņauce' (rev 4537968; NDG reverted it as vandalism), then twice on 'Zizma' (rev 4537972 changed the lead to "normunds gejs"; NDG reverted it in rev 4537973). Its last and most specific edit, rev 4537975, added text to the name field of 'Kandavas Lauksaimniecības tehnikums', an agricultural school in Kandava. The added text says a "big gay named Normunds Balandis" studies there. That edit names an apparently real person, probably a student, and the graph shows no revert yet. So it's a live attack on a private individual. The school link suggests this is local schoolyard harassment, not a real-world news event. I don't know if the target is a real person, or whether the edit was reverted after the graph's last update. Next steps: check the school page and consider asking admins to hide the revision. No other languages are involved and there's no edit war.

briefs.headline: Vandalism hits Quokka, Mesoamerica and Artemis VI; all reverted, no real-world event
briefs.summary: This is a pile-up of unrelated schoolboy-style vandalism on three English Wikipedia pages. Patrollers and ClueBot NG reverted all of it within minutes. On Quokka, "Mr. Cartoon Maker" made a second attempt. It deleted the lead and range sections and inserted fake claims ("weighs 500 pounds", a sexual-behaviour line, the heading "Description (Doh)"). Viewmont Viking undid it as vandalism. On Mesoamerica, temporary account ~2026-56183-24 blanked about 9.3 KB and added a heading reading "MICHAEL JAcksoN", which ClueBot NG reverted. A second temporary account, ~2026-56151-20, kept re-adding small changes, including "THIS ARTICLE IS FALSE INFORMATION". Serols and Celjski Grad reverted it four times. On Artemis VI, "Science it is" added an unsourced, chatty line ("I just googled it… supplying parts for the permanent moon base"), and ClueBot NG removed it. A correction to the scout's note: the "~2026-…" editors are Wikipedia temporary accounts, so they are effectively anonymous even though the graph doesn't flag them as anon. No editors overlap between the pages except the anti-vandal patrollers, nothing moved in other languages, and no content dispute is under way.

briefs.headline: Quokka article hit by two unrelated vandal edits, both quickly reverted
briefs.summary: On English Wikipedia, two separate low-activity accounts vandalised the Quokka article. The first, "Mr. Cartoon Maker" (an account with one edit), deleted the lead paragraph and range section, about 1,361 bytes. In their place it added a made-up claim about quokka sexual behaviour and changed a section heading to "Description (Doh)". DonnieNova reverted this within about 25 seconds. A few minutes later, "Rushymaster" (an account with two edits) added a nonsense line about a Maus tank "powered by 15,000 big macs", and Celjski Grad removed it with the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool. The high churn figure comes from that single blanking and its revert, not from a dispute between editors. No real-world event is involved, there was no back-and-forth reverting, and no other languages were affected. The revert summary mentions an earlier ClueBot NG revision, which suggests this page draws vandalism regularly.

briefs.headline: Quokka vandal returns twice more, including a false 'extinct' status; both edits reverted
briefs.summary: Since the last brief, the account "Rushymaster" has made two more vandal edits to the English Quokka article, bringing its total to four. The first changed the conservation status in the infobox from VU (Vulnerable) to EX (Extinct) and left the IUCN citation in place. DonnieNova reverted it in about 40 seconds. The second replaced the short description with a made-up "fun fact" about quokka reproduction. T430s reverted it in about 30 seconds as vandalism. The "extinct" change is the only edit that looks like news, and it is false: the cited 2020 IUCN assessment lists the species as Vulnerable, and no editor or other-language page backs the change. Mesoamerica and Artemis VI have had no new activity. The earlier vandalism there was already reverted. There is no real-world event and no content dispute. The only editors who appear on more than one page are anti-vandalism patrollers and ClueBot NG. Rushymaster has now been reverted repeatedly, so the account may be blocked or the page semi-protected, but the graph does not show that.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Quokka, Mesoamerica and Artemis VI all reverted; nothing new, no real event
briefs.summary: Nothing has changed since the last brief, and the graph shows no edits on any of the three pages after the last revert. On Quokka, "Mr. Cartoon Maker" made a second attempt. It deleted the lead and range sections and inserted fake claims ("weighs 500 pounds", a sexual-behaviour line, the heading "Description (Doh)"). Viewmont Viking reverted it. On Mesoamerica, temporary account ~2026-56151-20 kept adding small changes, including "THIS ARTICLE IS FALSE INFORMATION", which Serols and Celjski Grad reverted. Separately, ClueBot NG reverted a 9.3 KB blanking by another temporary account. On Artemis VI, "Science it is" added an unsourced chatty line ("I just googled it… permanent moon base"), which ClueBot NG removed. All of this comes from throwaway or temporary accounts with no content dispute, no editors shared across pages apart from anti-vandal patrollers, and no activity in other languages. I recommend closing the story or merging it into the existing vandalism tracking.

briefs.headline: es-wiki 'Iglesia católica': two temporary-account edits reverted by bots within seconds
briefs.summary: The activity on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Iglesia católica' page comes to two edits from new temporary accounts, and anti-vandalism bots undid both within about 11 seconds. Each account made only this one edit. Rev 175919671 (~2026-56025-48, +109 bytes) changed the lead paragraph. Automoderador reverted it 11 seconds later (rev 175919675). Rev 175919780 (~2026-56277-89, −114 bytes) deleted the hatnote templates at the top of the page and added broken table markup ("{| cla…") into the lead. SeroBOT reverted it 12 seconds later (rev 175919782). The diff output was cut off, so I can't see exactly what text was added in the first edit. Still, no edit summaries, single-edit accounts and quick bot reverts are the usual pattern for test edits or minor vandalism. They don't point to a real-world event. Pages on the same Wikidata item in other languages had no recent edits. Note for the Scout: the '~2026-…' editors are temporary (logged-out) accounts, so they are effectively anonymous. The bot reverts also count as reverts, even though they weren't flagged as reverts in the graph.

briefs.headline: es-wiki 'Iglesia católica': two logged-out test/vandal edits, both bot-reverted; no event
briefs.summary: I checked again and found no new activity on Spanish Wikipedia's 'Iglesia católica' page since the earlier brief. The graph has four edits in total, all already covered there. The Scout's count is a little off: it is 4 edits from 4 accounts, and 2 of those edits are reverts that the graph doesn't flag as reverts. Rev 175919671 came from a temporary (logged-out) account with no edit summary and changed the lead paragraph (+109 bytes). Automoderador reverted it 11 seconds later. Rev 175919780 came from a different temporary account. It deleted the three hatnote templates at the top of the page and added broken table markup ("{| cla…") into the lead. SeroBOT reverted it 12 seconds later. I could not see exactly what text the first edit added because the diff output was cut off. Even so, single-edit accounts, no summaries and instant bot reverts match test edits or minor vandalism, not a real-world event. I agree with the Scout's conclusion: there is no new story here.

briefs.headline: Iranian archaeologist Yousef Majidzadeh, Jiroft excavator, reported dead at 90
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Yousef Majidzadeh, the Iranian archaeologist who directed excavations at Jiroft, Ozbaki and Qabristan, now gives his death as 19 October 2026, aged 90. Its source is an ISNA article titled "یوسف مجیدزاده درگذشت" ("Yousef Majidzadeh passed away"). Before any of the five edits in this cluster, the lead and the body already gave the death date, so the edit that first added the death happened before our window. The edits we can see are follow-up cleanup by three registered editors, with no reverts. Editrite! changed "is a native of Tabriz" to the past tense, Extended Cut added an infobox field, and Strattonsmith reworded the death sentence (±8-byte tweaks; that edit also left a stray apostrophe). The graph has no other-language pages linked to this article and no activity in other languages. I have not checked the ISNA report independently, but it is a mainstream Iranian news agency and the cleanup by several editors fits a real, recent death.

briefs.headline: No news: another sock pastes GTA: SA article over redirect, Rhain reverts in a minute
briefs.summary: This is the same ban-evasion pattern as before, with no real-world event behind it. A new temporary account, ~2026-56068-06, pasted the full ~205 KB Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas article over the "GTA: SA" redirect (rev 1381157199). Its edit summary, "Last edit no more but the current revision sucks", repeats the wording of earlier socks. A fourth patroller, Rhain, put the redirect back about 60 seconds later (rev 1381157273). I read both diffs, and the paste is just a copy of the existing game article, with no new content. That makes at least six accounts doing the same paste, and patrollers have cited WP:SOCK and "banned means banned". All of it is on English Wikipedia. At Osmanabad, the graph shows no edits after Rina komorin's rev 1381155408 putting "Dharashiv" first in the lead, so the earlier note still holds: a dispute over which name goes first, not news. The only open question is whether that edit is still live.

briefs.headline: No news: more sockpuppet pastes on GTA: SA redirect; Osmanabad name dispute continues
briefs.summary: This is the same pattern as the earlier assessment, and no real-world event is behind it. On GTA: SA, another account, Porrsweas, again pasted a full ~205 KB copy of the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas article over what should be a redirect (rev 1381155635, edit summary "Last edit i swear no more"). Patroller Beyhive Navy turned it back into a redirect, citing WP:SOCK (rev 1381156085). That makes four or more accounts doing the same thing, which fits ban evasion through sockpuppets. Nothing about the game changed. At Osmanabad, a single editor (Rina komorin) keeps rewriting the lead to put "Dharashiv" first (rev 1381155408). The 2023 renaming is old news and the article already cites it. Two patrollers have reverted this, so it is a low-level dispute over which name the article uses. The open question from the earlier assessment remains: rev 1381155408 had no revert in the data I pulled.

briefs.headline: No news: banned-user evasion on GTA: SA redirect, separate name dispute at Osmanabad
briefs.summary: The two pages share only one editor, a patroller (Beyhive Navy), and are not connected by any real-world event. The large churn on GTA: SA is not a blanking. "GTA: SA" is a redirect to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Saresiop and two temporary accounts kept pasting a full ~205 KB copy of the game article over the redirect (rev 1381151198), and Beyhive Navy and StephenMacky1 kept turning it back into a redirect. One revert's edit summary cites "Banned means banned" (rev 1381155058), so patrollers appear to see this as a banned user dodging their ban. At Osmanabad, a single new editor (Rina komorin) kept making "Dharashiv" the city's main name in the infobox and lead (revs 1381154747, 1381155408). Two different patrollers reverted this, one of them calling it vandalism. The official renaming happened in September 2023, and the article already cites it, so this is a dispute over which name the page puts first, not news of a renaming. One open question: the latest Dharashiv edit had not yet been reverted when the data was pulled.

briefs.headline: No news: GTA: SA sockpuppet pastes reverted again; Osmanabad lead edit still stands
briefs.summary: Nothing has changed since the last two briefs, and no real-world event is behind this activity. On the GTA: SA redirect, Porrsweas pasted the full ~205 KB Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas article over the redirect once more (rev 1381156426, "Last change i swear no more"). A third patroller, IrisChronomia, put the redirect back within about 80 seconds (rev 1381156516). That makes at least five accounts doing the same paste, and earlier patrollers cited WP:SOCK and "banned means banned", so this looks like one banned user switching accounts. All edits are on English Wikipedia and the game article itself has not changed. At Osmanabad, Rina komorin's edit making "Dharashiv" the city's main name in the lead (rev 1381155408) is still the latest revision. The graph shows no revert after it. The rename itself is from 2023 and already sourced in the article, so this is a dispute over which name goes first, not news. A small uncertainty: the edit leaves a broken wikilink in an image caption, so a revert is likely but hasn't happened yet.

briefs.headline: Chilean celebrity bios on es-wiki hit by family-detail vandalism; some edits still up
briefs.summary: The new cluster isn't routine. A second wave of vandalism has hit Spanish Wikipedia bios of Chilean TV figures. On Patricia Maldonado Aravena, temporary account ~2026-56162-80 added a made-up third child, "HERNAN FLORES" (rev 175918276), and Automoderador reverted it within seconds. Four minutes later the registered account Reddizze, under the misleading edit summary "correcciones recientes", added the same name as her parent and changed her religion from Agnóstica to "Judia" (rev 175918361). Reddizze then edited Jorge Zabaleta: it swapped his partner's name (175918457), and its second edit changed his years active to "1967-presente" and his number of children to "67" (175918482). The graph shows no reverts of Reddizze's three edits, so they may still be live and patrollers should look at them. The repeated "Hernan Flores" suggests one person moved from a temporary account to a registered one, but that is inferred, not confirmed. The only link to the existing Luar la L story is the Automoderador bot, not shared editors. Luar la L's own vandal (~2026-56419-72) made one more name and birthplace swap (175918231), and Automoderador reverted it. Nothing points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Luar la L es-wiki page hit by identity-swap vandalism; reverted each time
briefs.summary: The Spanish Wikipedia page for Puerto Rican rapper Luar la L had 9 edits in about 15 minutes, all from one temporary account (~2026-56419-72) and the people undoing it: patroller Casisgaal and the Automoderador bot. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but in fact five of the nine edits were reverts. The diffs I read show the temporary account swapping the artist's real name for "Mateo Espinosa Cardenas". It also changed his birth date to "16 de abril de 21 A.C" and later 2000, invented a birthplace ("Parque placentero" / "Metropoli mercantil"), called him an "actor +18", and changed the genre to bachata. Every change was undone within minutes, and Automoderador restored the page after the last attempt. Nothing points to a real-world event like a release or announcement; this looks like a prank, possibly aimed at a real person named in the edits. It is contained, and the only open question is whether the account comes back.

briefs.headline: es-wiki: Two unrelated edits by temporary accounts reverted by bot; no news event
briefs.summary: This story is two separate incidents on Spanish Wikipedia. The only link between them is the anti-vandalism bot Automoderador, which reverted both. No real-world event is suggested. On "Protestas de la generación Z", temporary account ~2026-56258-59 removed 4,330 bytes from the Colombia ("Petrotazo") section with no edit summary (rev 175925992). The removed material included sourced statements about Gustavo Petro's unpopularity, criticism of his government for negotiating with armed groups, and white-clothed protests in Bogotá and Medellín after the attack on Miguel Uribe. This looks like politically motivated removal, not an update. Automoderador fully reverted it 23 seconds later (175925997). On "Víctor Jara", temporary account ~2026-56380-23 vandalised the lead sentence by changing "director de teatro" to the slang phrase "farmeador de aura" ("aura farmer") (rev 175925798). Automoderador reverted it within seconds (175925800). The scout's "8660 churn" is just ±4,330 bytes from one removal and its revert. No content was expanded, there was no back-and-forth between editors, and no human editors were involved besides these two single-edit accounts.

briefs.headline: Taekwondo pioneer in France Lee Kwan-Young reported dead in Seoul at 80
briefs.summary: French Wikipedia now lists Lee Kwan-Young as dead. He was a Korean martial-arts master, an early pioneer of taekwondo and hapkido in France, and the founder of hoshin moosool. The article gives his death as 18 October 2026 in Seoul. Three registered editors updated the article within about 17 minutes, with no reverts. Jmax added the category "Décès en octobre 2026" (deaths in October 2026) and a source: a notice from the French taekwondo federation (FFTDA) titled "Disparition du Grand Maître Lee Kwan Young", dated 19 October 2026. A second editor added the "Mort récente" (recent death) template, and AnasthaseLeGrand only reworded the opening sentence. The death date was already in the text before these edits, so an earlier edit that isn't in our graph must have added it. The only source is the federation's news page, which I have not checked myself. The graph has no linked pages in other languages, so nothing else confirms the death yet. This looks like a niche obituary and nothing more.

briefs.headline: Airport route-table edits are one unsourced editor and one patroller, not news
briefs.summary: This story is just two editors, not eight. Between about 1792563717 and 1792568009, one temporary account (~2026-56454-57) made small edits to the "Airlines and destinations" sections of Corfu, Luton, Athens and Berlin Brandenburg airports on English Wikipedia. Each edit changed between -372 and +155 bytes. The graph shows the same account also editing Zakynthos, Karpathos, Warsaw Chopin and Vienna. A regular patroller, 10mmsocket, then followed the account from page to page and undid most of the changes, giving the reasons "Unsourced" and "Unexplained removal of content". 10mmsocket also reverted on Rhodes, Saarbrücken and Milan Malpensa. This looks like routine cleanup of unsourced route changes, not an edit war (no back-and-forth reverting) and not a real-world event: there was no second independent editor, no other language versions changed, and nothing was sourced. One possibility I couldn't rule out: the pages are mostly Greek and other holiday airports, plus Luton, and 10mmsocket also touched Duo Airways and Red Rose Travel. So the account may have been adding new seasonal routes or removing dropped ones from a single airline. The big caveat is that the diff tool failed on every revision I tried, so I never saw which airline or routes were changed. This brief rests only on edit comments, edit sizes and graph structure.

briefs.headline: Lunchables article: brief vandalism swapping inventor's name, reverted within minutes
briefs.summary: This was vandalism, not a content dispute or a news event. A temporary account (~2026-56200-06) made two small edits to the History section of en:Lunchables. They replaced the sourced creator "Bob Drane" with the handle "S1guylavaman" (rev 1381264677), then changed later mentions of "Drane" to "Lavaman" (rev 1381264751). Both edits were unsourced and plainly a joke username inserted into the article. Patroller GreyZoneLife undid the second edit about a minute later (rev 1381264816) and restored "Bob Drane" in the first sentence about five minutes after that (rev 1381265101). The article now matches the cited source (Moss, Salt Sugar Fat). The only leftover is a missing space before a reference tag. Two editors were involved, nobody re-reverted, and no other-language versions or other pages were touched, so there is no edit war and nothing happening in the real world behind it.

briefs.headline: Swedish Wikipedia: patroller rolls back test edits on Two Sicilies order page
briefs.summary: On sv.wikipedia, the article "Kungliga orden av Bägge Sicilierna" (the Royal Order of the Two Sicilies) got four edits in about 8 minutes. A temporary account (~2026-56469-57) added 407 bytes with the summary "Jag har skrivit en liten kort berättelse om orden" ("I wrote a short little story about the order"). A second temporary account then added 31 bytes with the summary "d". The first account came back with an edit summarised "KOlloll" (a nonsense or joke summary), and patroller EPIC rolled back that account's edits to the second account's version. EPIC made a similar rollback of a temporary account on "Paradisfåglar" (birds-of-paradise) shortly before, which looks like routine recent-changes patrolling. There was no activity in other languages and nothing links this to a real-world event. Caveat: Wikipedia returned "no such revision" for all four diffs, so I couldn't read the edited text. This call rests only on edit summaries, byte changes and the rollback, and the text may have been hidden or deleted after the fact. Recommend closing as low-grade vandalism or test edits.

briefs.headline: Small vandalism on Indonesian party pages and CECOT, reverted by one patroller
briefs.summary: The story is not a real-world event. It is a few low-level vandal edits by two temporary accounts, all undone within minutes by a single patroller, Perpetually Blooming Rose, using the UV tool. On Communist Party of Indonesia, ~2026-56200-41 changed native_name from "Partai Komunis Indonesia" to the joke "Partai Komputer Indonesia". The edit also reformatted the infobox, which explains the ±229 bytes and the "458 churn" (229 removed, then 229 restored). The same account added the chant "Hidup PDIP, Hidup PDIP!!" ("Long live PDIP!") to Puan Maharani's page, labelling it as her party role. A separate account, ~2026-56298-71, swapped "stated" for "whined" in CECOT's section on Venezuelan deportees. The three pages share only the patroller, and the two Indonesian pages share one partisan joker. Nothing points to a news event in Indonesia or El Salvador. We have edits in English only and no reverts going back and forth.

briefs.headline: eMudhra certificate authority hit by reported trivially weak intermediate CA keys
briefs.summary: The scout read this as routine company-page churn, but the diffs say otherwise. The newly patrolled en-wiki article on Indian certificate authority eMudhra has a section titled "2026 intermediate certificate compromise". It says that on October 20 researchers found the private key of one eMudhra intermediate certificate was "simply the number 4". A follow-up edit (rev 1381213362, refined in 1381213513) adds that seven other intermediate certificates used the private keys 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Four accounts made 10 edits in about an hour with no reverts: a new-page patroller adding a stub tag, category and short description, plus three editors copyediting and expanding the compromise section. That points to a newly surfacing event, not promotion or vandalism. Big caveat: the only sources cited are two Fediverse/Mastodon posts by individual researchers. We have no vendor statement, no browser or CA/B Forum response and no mainstream coverage, and the claim has not been independently confirmed. Only one page in one language is involved so far. Watch for the article being sent to deletion or pulled back for weak sourcing, and for related Mozilla, Chrome or CA/B Forum distrust activity.

briefs.headline: Minor vandalism on de-wiki Röntgen article, both edits quickly reverted
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-55920-30) made two small edits to the German article on physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1845–1923). The first, with the comment "ja", deleted the † death symbol from the lead. The second added the stray text "glaubt nicht alles" ("doesn't believe everything") above an image comment. Patrollers Brettchenweber and Serols (the latter using Huggle) undid both edits within minutes. Nothing here points to a real-world event. It is a low-level test or vandalism episode that has already been cleaned up.

briefs.headline: ruwiki: anti-vandal bot undoes three small, unrelated temporary-account edits
briefs.summary: Three different temporary accounts each made one small edit to three unrelated Russian Wikipedia pages. EyeBot, an automated anti-vandalism bot, reverted all three within about 15–40 seconds based on its quality scores. On the bio of musician Maksim Samosvat, the edit lined up the infobox fields and added "OMEN" to his list of bands without a source. On the bio of Anatoly Safronov, a bare Rutube video link was pasted after an existing citation in the "Память" (memorial) section. On the "Бумажный дом" (La Casa de Papel) series page, the episode count was changed from 41 to 48. That could be a fan correction or an error; nothing in the edit or the graph points to a new season or other news. The editors don't overlap, nobody restored the edits, there's no back-and-forth reverting and no other languages are involved, so this looks like routine bot cleanup rather than an event or an edit war.

briefs.headline: ruwiki: EyeBot reverts more small temporary-account edits; mini-repeat on Samosvat, no news
briefs.summary: The story grew from three pages to five, but it is still routine anti-vandal cleanup. The Samosvat edit was made twice by the same temporary account (~2026-56315-19). The second try lined up the infobox fields again and added "ØMEN" to his bands, with the comment that this is his latest band. EyeBot reverted both within about 30 seconds. That is one person re-adding an unsourced claim, not two editors fighting over it. On "Абоба (интернет-мем)", another temporary account replaced the lead and its Ukrainska Pravda source with one line saying the meme came out in 2022 (the article says 2021). EyeBot restored the original, and it looks like low-level vandalism. On László Sólyom (Шойом, Ласло), a temporary account made a +44 edit that EyeBot reverted. I couldn't load that diff. The same account also edited Lee Teng-hui, Nausėda and Áder, and the Lee Teng-hui diff I did read is infobox realignment plus changing religion from "христианство" (Christianity) to "пресвитерианство" (Presbyterianism). That points to one cleanup-minded editor working through presidents' bios, not news about Sólyom. Still, I haven't seen that diff, so I can't fully rule it out, and no other-language Sólyom pages moved.

briefs.headline: Indonesian 2026 quake list logs a claimed M6.6 near Luganville, Vanuatu; routine update
briefs.summary: On Indonesian Wikipedia's 'Daftar gempa bumi tahun 2026' (list of 2026 earthquakes), editors raised the count of M6.0–6.9 quakes by one. One edit summary says it was a new M6.6 quake at Luganville, Vanuatu. A temporary account bumped the infobox total from 101 to 102 (rev 30092940). Editor 'Eearthquake 2026' then raised the October count from 11 to 12, citing the Vanuatu quake (30092945), and updated the year-comparison table (102; total 12,490→12,491, rev 30092974). Separately, another temporary account changed the 9.0+ count from 0 to 3. That was a bogus edit, and the same editor reverted it (30093002). It was a one-off revert, not an edit war. Nothing else in the graph backs this up: no other-language versions of the list, and no Vanuatu earthquake page is being edited. The magnitude and location come only from an edit summary, so they are unconfirmed. A mid-6 quake in Vanuatu is common and probably not big news unless damage reports show up.

briefs.headline: Haber process: one temporary account's sneaky vandalism reverted twice
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. It's small-scale vandalism on the English "Haber process" article, and other editors cleaned it up within minutes. Temporary account ~2026-56275-44 added a slur fragment ("niga") to the lead sentence with the misleading edit summary "i deleted som bad words" (rev 1381277361). Staticspector reverted it about 40 seconds later. The same account then made a second edit labelled "dates were wrong" (rev 1381278388). That edit changed the date in Carl Bosch's photo caption from 1927 to 1928 with no source, added a stray period, and slipped "iga2" into the chemical formula for nitrogen. A second temporary account reverted it about 5 minutes later. Only one page was edited, there was no activity in other languages, and the false edit summaries show the edits were made in bad faith rather than as a content dispute. No further action is needed unless the account comes back.

briefs.headline: eMudhra page tracks reported compromise of 8 CA keys; Mozilla pulls emSign roots
briefs.summary: This isn't promotional editing. The enwiki article on eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, is documenting a reported security incident. Existing article text, citing Mozilla's security blog, Ars Technica and The Hacker News (all dated 2026-10-20), says browser vendors and eMudhra were told on Oct 17 that intermediate certificates had been compromised. It says eMudhra revoked eight intermediates on Oct 18, and Mozilla removed the emSign root certificates from Firefox on Oct 20. The article reports that the private keys were tiny integers (4, 56, 66 ... 237), with only 3–8 bits of entropy instead of the 384 bits expected for P-384 keys. Of the latest four edits, two are copyedits and citation cleanup by Merlin04 and Actualice. The other two are a one-word change by a temporary account calling the company defunct ("is" to "was"), which Pppery undid within about a minute as unsupported. That single revert is not an edit war. The page has 24 edits from about 15 accounts in all, which points to active interest. The incident description comes from article text and citations I did not check independently, and no other related pages or language versions showed activity in the graph.

briefs.headline: eMudhra CA-key compromise page: no new activity, only cleanup and one undone edit
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked story, and nothing has changed since the last brief. The four edits the scout flagged are the same four the previous brief covered, and no newer revisions exist in the graph. I read all four diffs. Merlin04 lightly rewrote the sentence on key entropy: per Ars Technica, the P-384 keys should have had 384 bits of entropy but had only 3–8, being the integers 4–237. Actualice added publisher details to the Mozilla blog and The Island citations. A temporary account changed "is" to "was", implying the company is defunct, and Pppery undid it about a minute later, citing no evidence. This is one revert, not an edit war. The incident facts already on the page are unchanged: notification on Oct 17, eight intermediates revoked on Oct 18, and Mozilla pulling the emSign roots from Firefox on Oct 20, cited to the Mozilla security blog, Ars Technica and The Hacker News. The page has no linked versions in other languages, and the graph shows no activity on related pages. I have not independently verified the cited sources.

briefs.headline: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) strengthens to 900 hPa, now the 2026 Pacific season's strongest
briefs.summary: Editors of the 2026 Pacific typhoon season article raised Typhoon Champi's central pressure from 905 to 900 hPa. That edit also dropped Typhoon Sinlaku from the "strongest storm" slot it had shared with Champi, leaving Champi alone (rev 1381214471). Minutes later a different editor raised Champi's 1-minute sustained winds from 155 to 160, likely knots, which would be super-typhoon strength (rev 1381214861). A third editor swapped in a satellite image dated 2026-10-20 at 1700Z (rev 1381221959). Champi also has a Philippine local name, "Rosal", which suggests it is in or has entered the Philippine monitoring area. That is my inference; no edit mentions landfall, warnings or damage. The activity is small: 3–4 named editors, no reverts, and the other recent edits are just about chart width on mobile. The numbers were typed in by volunteers and the edit summaries cite no source, so treat them as unconfirmed. No separate Champi article or other-language pages showed up in the graph. Worth watching for landfall and impact edits.

briefs.headline: New ja.wiki page on SEIKIN's "Wahō" meme created, redirected, then restored
briefs.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. All the churn comes from one new Japanese Wikipedia page, わほー ("Wahō"), about an internet meme. A temporary account created it (+2717). The page says the word comes from a 2014 SeikinTV video in which YouTuber SEIKIN eats a large amount of Mintia mints. It also says the word went viral on TikTok in late 2025–2026, and that SEIKIN and HIKAKIN have reacted to it. About six minutes later, Kugelschreibers turned the page into a redirect to [[SEIKIN]] (−2697). This is a normal cleanup step for a new, thinly sourced article. Another editor, カカポが好きな人, then put the article back with headings, external links and a "needs sources" ({{出典の明記}}) tag (+2748). The page cites a single source, a Livedoor News article. The "8162 churn" is just the same ~2.7 KB of text added, removed and added again. So far it's a one-time disagreement over whether the page should exist, not an edit war, though another redirect or a deletion nomination is possible.

briefs.headline: Fielder/Holmes doc 'You Can See Everything': box-office update, duplicate Wired text removed
briefs.summary: Three editors made routine upkeep edits to the English article on the 2026 Nathan Fielder–Lance Oppenheim documentary about Elizabeth Holmes. Wikicarp added a paragraph (+515 bytes) citing a Wired interview published October 19. In it, Fielder describes a phone call from Holmes: she said she had not seen the film or its reception, and repeated that she trusted him. A temporary account removed the same paragraph about 14 minutes later (−515), explaining that the Wired piece was already covered two paragraphs earlier. That add-and-remove pair accounts for the 1,030-byte churn the scout flagged. It is cleanup, not a dispute: there was no reply or re-revert. Separately, Gabgoldv raised the infobox gross from $15.6M to $18.2M, citing The Numbers. That suggests the film is still earning in its run, but I have not checked the figure against the source. No conflict, no other languages involved, and nothing here counts as a new real-world event.

briefs.headline: Routine tidy-up of new sv-wiki biography of Quebec poet Mélissa Labonté
briefs.summary: Three established Swedish Wikipedia editors made 11 small edits to the article on Mélissa Labonté in about 5 minutes. All the changes were categories, a default sort key and copyediting. No new facts tied to any news event were added. The scout's note calls her a sports figure, but she isn't one. The article describes her as a Canadian poet, literary scholar and publishing editor, born in 1989 in Saint-Henri-de-Lévis, Quebec. Lgmka added and removed categories with HotCat; trying a category and then removing it is self-correction, not an edit war. Yger merged the birth details into the lead sentence and changed the categories to "Kanadensiska poeter" (Canadian poets) and "Levande personer" (living people). Stigfinnare added "Franskspråkiga poeter" (French-language poets) and a sort key. The pattern looks like a recently created article, possibly tied to a women-biographies project (category "Projekt Kvinnliga huvudpersoner"), being fixed up by other editors. Nothing suggests a real-world event, and no other language editions are involved.

briefs.headline: Routine sv-wiki cleanup of new article on Quebec poet Mélissa Labonté
briefs.summary: Three established Swedish Wikipedia editors (Lgmka, Yger, Stigfinnare) made 11 edits to the article on Mélissa Labonté between 1792496819 and 1792497144, about 5 minutes. There were no reverts and no anonymous editors, and no other language editions were involved. The diffs show only maintenance work. Lgmka added and removed categories with HotCat, for example adding and then removing "Författare från Kanada" (Writers from Canada), which is one editor correcting their own choices, not an edit war. Yger moved the birth details (born 1989, Saint-Henri-de-Lévis, Quebec, with an existing Poetik Bazar citation) into the lead sentence and replaced "Poeter" (Poets) with "Kanadensiska poeter" (Canadian poets) and "Levande personer" (Living people). Stigfinnare added a references tag, a default sort key and the "Franskspråkiga poeter" (French-language poets) category. No new facts tied to a current event were added, so this looks like a newly created biography getting its first cleanup. It matches the earlier routine brief, and nothing has changed since. One uncertainty: the article's creation edit isn't in the graph, so the story behind its creation is unknown.

briefs.headline: One editor keeps re-adding animal-rights opinion to de-wiki 'Göttliches Recht'; reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a real-world event or a content rewrite. A single temporary account (~2026-56572-12) keeps adding one opinion sentence (223 bytes) to the lead of the German article 'Göttliches Recht' (divine law). The sentence says divine law "must be based on absolute morality" and that tolerating the killing of farm animals violates it. The account first undid an earlier removal by Stephan Klage (rev 271500299). Horst Gräbner reverted that, the account put the sentence back with the comment "must not be censored", and Logograph removed it again citing WP:TF (the German guideline against original research). The high churn figure comes from the same 223 bytes going in and out four times, and none of the edits were flagged as reverts. No other pages, languages or sources are involved. This is unsourced opinion-pushing by one account, cleaned up by three established editors, not a two-sided edit war. More re-insertions or a block are possible, but the newsroom doesn't need to watch this.

briefs.headline: Nigel Ng (Uncle Roger) page hit by two unrelated vandal edits, both reverted
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Malaysian comedian Nigel Ng ("Uncle Roger") had two separate vandal edits from two different temporary accounts, about 15 minutes apart. Patrollers reverted both within minutes. In the first edit (rev 1381236506), the bold name was replaced with "UNCLE ROGERS FUIYOH HAIYA", the birth date was changed to "SEPTEMBER,13 1991" and the character was renamed "Uncle RICKS". The edit summary claimed he had revealed "his name and legit info" on a podcast, but no source was given. GhostStalker reverted it. In the second edit (rev 1381238068, summary "nak"), the whole infobox was deleted (1,236 characters) and "Cantonese" was swapped for an obscene word. TonySt reverted it with an anti-vandalism tool. The ~2,500 characters of churn is just that one deletion and its revert. There is no sign of a dispute between regular editors or of any real-world news; the podcast claim looks like a cover for the joke edit, though I can't rule out that some podcast moment prompted the attention. Only this one language edition is involved and the page is back to its earlier version.

briefs.headline: Russian-text spam spreads from 'Pete versus Life' to its cast and Channel 4 pages
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news, and it is the same incident already tracked for 'Pete versus Life'. The account Ggsrhrhs added the same 8,399-byte block to English Wikipedia pages linked from that article: Rafe Spall (3 times), Reece Ritchie (2), Channel 4 (2) and the show's page itself (3). I read the diffs on Channel 4 (1381290991), Rafe Spall (1381290651) and Reece Ritchie (1381290906). Each one is only the Russian phrase "Том и Джерри. 10 серия." ("Tom and Jerry. Episode 10") repeated over and over. Three patrollers, Andreworkney, Beyhive Navy and KH-1, reverted every insertion within about 1–2 minutes. The 9 reverts are clean-up of one spammer, not an edit war. The dossier lists only 4 editors, not the 12 in the Scout's note. According to the graph, the same account has also hit other pages linked from the article: cast members Chris Geere, Daniel Ings, Susannah Fielding, Philip Jackson, Joseph Kloska and Scarlett Alice Johnson, plus Objective Media Group, Sitcom, Single-camera setup, Embarrassment and Andy Gray (footballer). Its latest edit was about 3 minutes after the last revert in this cluster. I have not read those other diffs, and I can't tell whether the account has been blocked. There is no sign of any real-world event; this story should be merged with the existing one.

briefs.headline: Spam vandalism on 'Pete versus Life' article reverted by patrollers
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. In about 14 minutes, the account Ggsrhrhs made three edits to the English Wikipedia article on the sitcom 'Pete versus Life'. Each edit added the same block of about 8.4 KB. I read two of them (1381289594 and 1381290590): both contain only the repeated Russian phrase "Том и Джерри. 10 серия." ("Tom and Jerry. Episode 10"). Two patrollers removed it: Beyhive Navy reverted the first two edits, and KH-1 reverted the third. That explains the large churn and the two reverts. There was no back-and-forth over content and no sign of any real-world event. The page is back to its earlier version, and the account may get blocked.

briefs.headline: Petty vandalism on 'Nuclear power debate' and 'Euphoria' reverted by a patroller
briefs.summary: This isn't a news event or a content dispute. It's ordinary vandalism cleaned up by one patroller on English Wikipedia. On 'Nuclear power debate', temporary account ~2026-55968-94 made two small edits to the lead sentence, ending with the article "about aiden patterson" (rev 1381277018), which looks like a personal name prank. Patroller APK reverted it as vandalism ("rvv") by restoring an older revision (1381277808). That rollback also wiped out a legitimate edit, so APK put it back a minute later (1381277946, "restore edit"). The restored edit changes decommissioning costs to US$500M–2B and cites an IAEA source. On 'Euphoria', a different temporary account added "kendrick Lamars song" to the top of the page (1381276978), and APK reverted that too. The pages have nothing in common except the same patroller. There was no back-and-forth reverting, no other languages involved, and no sign of anything happening in the real world. Recommend closing the story.

briefs.headline: Czech Wikipedia: minor vandalism on Brno Dragon article undone twice
briefs.summary: Nothing happened in the real world here. This is small-scale vandalism on the cs.wiki article about the Brno Dragon, the stuffed crocodile in Brno's Old Town Hall, and it was cleaned up quickly. A temporary account (~2026-56333-38) changed "draka" to "kara" in the Původ (origin) section (rev 26315234). On a second try it made the same change and also slipped the nonsense phrase "Mg Granko" into the sentence about the crocodile being a gift from Turkish envoys (rev 26315239). Both edits were undone within about two minutes, by JirkaSv and then OJJ. Their edit summaries are standard rollback text. Note that the graph's revert flag says false for those two edits, but the summaries show they were reverts, so the scout's "no reverts" was wrong. I read only the vandal's two diffs, not the rollbacks. No sign of a wider campaign or a news hook.

briefs.headline: Single account adds joke middle names to three pop-star bios; all reverted
briefs.summary: This is a small vandalism spree, not a news event. One new account, HurricaneImelda2025 (4 edits in total), changed the English Wikipedia pages for The Weeknd, Dua Lipa and Kelly Rowland one after another over about 9 minutes. Each edit made up a middle name and put it in the infobox and/or the opening line: "Abel Beyoncé Makkonen Tesfaye", "Dua Jackari Lispa Jackson Lipa" and "Kelendria Transgénderaline Teresa Trene Rowland". None of the edits cited a source, and all had blank edit summaries. Nil NZ, an established editor, reverted all three within about 1 minute of each other, with summaries like "Unsourced". No other editors or languages were involved, so there is no sign of a real-world event behind the cluster. The 4th edit by the account is outside this story and I didn't check it.

briefs.headline: Newcomer keeps re-adding El Hierro hatnote to es-wiki 'Capraria'; bots revert it; no news
briefs.summary: Nothing has happened in the world here. Since the last brief, nothing new has happened on 'Torneo de Doha'. On 'Capraria' (a genus of plants), one temporary account (~2026-56151-66) has put back a "{{Distinguir|El Hierro}}" note five more times (revs 175923551, 175923588, 175923656, among others). The note tells readers not to confuse the page with El Hierro. Some of those edits also tidied up spacing. SeroBOT and Automoderador undid every attempt within seconds to minutes. The same account has also edited about 30 other pages, all ancient names for the Canary Islands and their people: Pliny's island names (Ombrion, Junonia, Ninguaria, Pluvialia, Planasia, Canaria, Capraria) and spelling variants of Tenesor Semidán. That looks like an honest, organised attempt to add "do not confuse with" notes to these pages. It does not look like vandalism or a response to news. The scout said there were no reverts, but there were: this is a slow back-and-forth between one newcomer and anti-vandalism bots, not a dispute between people. It will probably end once the account gives up or someone talks to them on their talk page. I did not check whether the editor's other pages were also reverted.

briefs.headline: Routine tidy-up on es-wiki Doha tennis and Capraria pages; no news event
briefs.summary: There is no news event here. The two pages have nothing to do with each other and were only grouped because they were edited at the same time. On 'Torneo de Doha', temporary-account editors renamed the section "Temporada inaugural" to "Historia" without changing its text (history from 2009–2012 about Nadal and Federer). They also swapped the Federer photo and changed its size settings (revs 175923182, 175923199, 175923511, 175923545). Nothing about results, a 2026 edition or a new champion was added. On 'Capraria', one temporary account added a "{{Distinguir|El Hierro}}" note at the top of the page, which tells readers not to confuse the two (rev 175923536). SeroBOT and Automoderador undid it twice. The scout's note said there were no reverts, but the edit comments show anti-vandalism bots undid newcomer edits about four times. These look like low-level bot cleanup, not a fight between editors, and only one or two humans touched each page.

briefs.headline: No change: es-wiki 'Capraria' hatnote back-and-forth with bots has stopped; no news
briefs.summary: There has been no new activity since the last brief. The graph shows no edits on 'Capraria' or 'Torneo de Doha' after rev 175923657, where SeroBOT undid the latest attempt. The pattern is the same as before. One temporary account (~2026-56151-66) kept adding "{{Distinguir|El Hierro}}", a note telling readers not to confuse the page with El Hierro, plus small spacing fixes. Rev 175923656, which I read again, is a typical example. SeroBOT and Automoderador undid each attempt within seconds. The scout's note says there were no reverts, which is wrong: the bots undid the newcomer about 7 times. This is a newcomer against anti-vandalism bots, not people fighting each other, and it has nothing to do with real-world events. The Doha tennis page has also been quiet. I recommend closing the story unless the editor starts again or a human editor joins in.

briefs.headline: One account's sneaky vandalism across five ja-wiki anime pages, all reverted

briefs.headline: Patroller reverts three unrelated bad edits; no news event behind them

briefs.headline: Championship page logs Wolves 1–1 Portsmouth result; one unrelated clause reverted

I haven't checked the score against any outside source, but three editors made consistent edits and nobody disputed them, so it is very likely accurate. There is no sign of any wider event.

briefs.headline: Minor vandalism on en-wiki 'Mr. Big' and 'Crab' pages reverted within minutes

briefs.headline: De-wiki: Second self-written page (Berlin youth cabaret) tagged for deletion; patrol overlap only
briefs.summary: This is routine new-page patrol, not news. The new cluster is the German page "Die Stachelbär´n" (rev 271484803). It was created by an account called Klaus Ziemer, and the text names him as the group's leader, so it looks like another page written by its own subject. The page describes a 1984–91 East Berlin youth cabaret group that broke through in 1987 with a Puhdys parody on GDR television. Its only sources are YouTube clips. Two patrollers tagged it for speedy deletion as "kein Artikel" (not an article) within minutes: Erastophanes (rev 271484892) and SK Sturm Fan (rev 271484895). The Scout's link to Hanslbauer is weak. The two pages share no subject, only the same patrollers (SK Sturm Fan, and M2k, who adds categories). It's wrong to say this cluster "belongs with the same story" in any real-world sense. On the Hanslbauer page, the edit war has gone quiet. Patroller Bumblebee Tights posted a deletion note (revs 271484818, 271484955) citing an Augsburger Allgemeine article about a re-release of "König von Mallorca". The note still argues for deletion and says the wording may be AI-generated. Rev 271484955 also seems to have accidentally added a typo to the article text ("laumten"). Neither page shows signs of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: De-wiki: Author of self-written bio keeps re-adding unsourced bike-crash claim; reverted twice
