So it's a small one-against-two revert fight over unverified self-promotion, not a real news event. I can't confirm any accident happened. The subject doesn't appear to be notable, and the page will most likely be deleted, which ends the dispute. The news value is very low.

briefs.headline: De-wiki: Creator makes 1-byte spelling tweak to cabaret page up for deletion; still routine

briefs.headline: De-wiki: Self-written Schlager songwriter bio tagged for speedy deletion minutes after creation

Selbstdarstellung" (beyond doubt not notable; self-promotion; rev 271484520) and "eindeutige Irrelevanz" (clearly not notable; rev 271484528). A routine maintenance edit added a category. briefs.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines hit by car in deliberate attack; unsourced death claim added
briefs.summary: This is not routine biography upkeep. The Helen Haines article (independent MP for Indi, Victoria) has had 78 edits from 30 editors in about 17 hours. The text describes an attack: on 19 October 2026 she was hit by a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta "in a deliberate attack" and taken to hospital with critical injuries (rev 1381163396). The attack section cites ABC, BBC and Guardian Australia coverage dated 19–20 Oct. It names the suspect as Brendan Nugent, 43, of Tarrawingee, who was arrested by a member of the public at the scene, had a knife, was known to police, had a mental health assessment, and whose family reportedly knew Haines (rev 1381162846). At 1792499990 a temporary account (~2026-55684-09) changed the article to say she died on 20 October 2026, in the past tense, with no source (rev 1381170836). A registered editor only added a full stop to that sentence and did not revert it (rev 1381170913). Treat the death as unconfirmed until a sourced edit or other editors back it up, and check again soon. One earlier revert was a minor dispute over keeping the attack in the lead section, not an edit war. Other edits are minor clean-up (e.g. rev 1381170178). No other-language versions of the article are linked in the graph.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines: unsourced death claim reverted; article says critically injured after attack
briefs.summary: Update: the claim that MP Helen Haines died has been removed. Registered editor Jjamesryan reverted the temporary account's edit (rev 1381170836) with the summary "Rm unreferenced" (rev 1381171328). The lead is back in the present tense ("born 21 September 1961", "is an Australian politician"), and the sentence "She passed away in hospital" is gone. The article now says only that on 19 October 2026 she was hit by a vehicle outside her Wangaratta electorate office in a deliberate attack and taken to hospital with critical injuries. A follow-up edit put back a small grammar fix (rev 1381171398). No sourced report of her death has appeared, so the attack itself is still the breaking story and the death claim should be treated as false or premature. The other two pages are not connected to this story. You Can See Everything had small edits from a temporary account that were reverted as vandalism. Ika people is flagged for a separate check. It is a content dispute, not news: the single-purpose account "Ika socials" has repeatedly cut sourced text tying the Ika to the Igbo (scholarly classification, colonial records, the Ekumeku movement; rev 1381171843). It was reverted as vandalism by T430s and Komethere (rev 1381171907) and kept removing material afterwards. That looks like an identity-POV edit war, not bulk maintenance.

briefs.headline: Ika people page: one-account campaign to remove Igbo links reverted again
briefs.summary: The activity on the Ika people page is an identity dispute between editors, not news. Almost all of it comes from one single-purpose account, "Ika socials". In rev 1381172191 and rev 1381172582 it cut the sourced Language section down to one line, removing citations that call Ika a dialect of Igbo or part of the western Igbo group (Uguru 2015 in JIPA, Williamson 1968, Onyeche 2002, Forde & Jones 1967, Blench 2019, and a 2022 paper in African Identities). In rev 1381172347 it changed the lead label from "Ika-Igbo" to "Ika". Four registered editors have now reverted it: T430s, Komethere, DonnieNova and, most recently, Jauerback (rev 1381172634), who restored the full text. The pattern is one person pushing a point of view against several patrollers, not two sides going back and forth. Page protection or a block is the likely next step, but I am inferring that; no edit shows it yet. Two other pages in this story are unrelated noise. Adil had its name-list page overwritten with a self-promotional profile of an 18-year-old influencer, "Adil Khokhar", which was reverted by Drmies and Celjski Grad (rev 1381173105). You Can See Everything had minor vandalism. Helen Haines has had no new edits since the last brief, so that brief still stands: the article reports a deliberate vehicle attack with critical injuries, and the unsourced death claim has been removed. The Haines part is still the only real-world story here.

briefs.headline: Helen Haines attack remains the story; Fielder film page hit by unrelated vandalism

briefs.headline: Editors fine-tune 'validity' wording on article about OpenAI's 722-paper math release
briefs.summary: The en-wiki article covers OpenAI's 7 Oct 2026 release on GitHub of 722 AI-generated manuscripts that claim results on open problems, including partial results on the Riemann hypothesis, BSD and Hodge conjectures. Its cited sources (Retraction Watch, 8 Oct; Quanta, 9 Oct) say three preprints were withdrawn within a day and 14 more revised. The three edits in this window are wording changes to the "Validity" section, not new developments. An unregistered editor (+84) made the Lean caveat clearer: about half the papers come with machine-checked proofs, but someone still has to check by hand that each proof matches its paper, and some formalizations prove weaker results than the papers claim. The one revert is a small dispute over wording, not an edit war. IlkkaP changed "could contain errors" to "could have issues" to match the quoted reference, and Eigenbra changed it back, citing WP:EUPH. The underlying event is real news and is covered elsewhere, but this activity is routine copyediting. No other-language versions are linked and nothing here is new, so it's low priority.

briefs.headline: Ohio governor race: AP source says Ramaswamy team owns Acton-mother ad, plans $4M buy

Temporary account ~2026-56241-92 rewrote the campaign section (+4,334 bytes, rev 1381254389) and added a new citation: an AP story by Julie Carr Smyth dated Oct 21. According to the quote copied from that story, Vivek Ramaswamy's team confirmed late Tuesday that it made the ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged birth mother, Donna Arthur, and will spend $4 million airing it despite "bipartisan rebuke." The same account then split the old "Negative campaigning" section into "Canfield Fair Incident" and "Attacks on Amy Acton's upbringing" subsections (rev 1381255085). There were no reverts in this round, so the earlier dispute seems to have settled into joint editing. briefs.headline: Ohio governor race: attack ad featuring Acton's estranged mother lands on Wikipedia
briefs.summary: The 2026 Ohio gubernatorial election article (Ramaswamy vs. Acton) is getting active editing focused on a new controversy. Editors added text, citing NYT, Washington Post and National Review pieces dated 2026-10-20, saying the Ramaswamy campaign ran an attack ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother. According to that text, the ads questioned Acton's upbringing despite records showing she was abused as a child (rev 1381246299). A temporary account then expanded the passage with more lurid detail it said it had copied from Acton's biography (rev 1381252333). An established editor reverted that within about 2 minutes as unnecessary detail (rev 1381252479). That was a single good-faith revert over wording, not an edit war or vandalism, and the core paragraph about the ad is still in the article. Separately, a routine polling update moved the aggregates to Oct 20 and shows Acton's lead narrowing to about 3.4–4.6 points, down from about 4.3–5.5 (rev 1381249352). I'm sure the article reflects a real, freshly reported news event. I haven't checked the cited articles themselves, and the edits came from only a few editors on English Wikipedia.

briefs.headline: Ohio governor race: temp account puts back reverted detail on Acton attack ad
briefs.summary: Update to s_de966fb5. About 4 minutes after Aesurias reverted its expanded passage (rev 1381252479), temporary account ~2026-56241-92 put a similar 2,722-byte version back, saying it "merits mention in the introduction" (rev 1381252701). The new text says the Ramaswamy campaign's ads portrayed Democrat Amy Acton as "sexually promiscuous" and mentally ill after Republican operatives found evidence she had been sexually abused as a child. It adds that one ad featured her estranged mother and that her stepfather was charged with raping her. It cites the NYT, National Review and Washington Post (all dated Oct 20), and the copied text also cites Politico and ABC News. The same account then cut 184 bytes, "didn't mean to do that" (rev 1381252746), and 1,329 bytes of accidentally duplicated biography text (rev 1381252882). The Biggest BOTW Fan fixed the "Ramawamy" typo (rev 1381252968). The fuller wording is in the article now and nobody has reverted it again yet. One revert and one re-insertion between two editors looks like an early content dispute, not an edit war or vandalism yet. Caveats: who made the ad is muddy. The article text pins it on the Ramaswamy campaign, but the copied ABC citation calls the ad "unattributed" and the text also says "Republican operatives". The wording also makes sensitive claims about a living person (BLP), so expect more trimming. The real-world event, a widely reported Oct 20 ad featuring Acton's mother, still looks solid, but I haven't checked the cited articles myself.

It cut the field from 27 to 26 candidates, removed the official-endorsement asterisks, deleted the table of upcoming departmental pageants (Casanare, Córdoba, Cundinamarca, Meta, Nariño, dated 18–24 Oct 2026), and removed Señorita Santa Marta María Camila Valiente Ortiz, whose entry has an El Informador source (rev 175920856, 175920862). Contrary to the scout note, there was a revert: Automoderador undid these changes (rev 175920863). The same account then re-added the Santa Marta removal as a "Retiro" (withdrawal) note saying she withdrew "for unknown reasons", with no source (rev 175920897). Veteran editor Casisgaal only reformatted the dates in the restored departmental table, and in doing so appears to have changed Meta's date from 23 to 21 October by mistake (rev 175920886). This looks like a fan editor updating the roster without sources, possibly with inside knowledge. It is not clearly vandalism, and the Santa Marta withdrawal is unconfirmed. The DirecTV page is unrelated: an anonymous editor changed the listed owner back to AT&T 70%/TPG 30%, SeroBOT reverted it, and the page is linked to this story only through the bots.

briefs.headline: Cambridge school page hit by meme vandalism from temporary accounts; mostly reverted
briefs.summary: Two temporary accounts added joke text to the Chesterton Community College (Cambridge, UK) article. The joke was the same meme in both cases: the school is "known for the meme 'Sh*t on it to assert dominance'". ClueBot NG reverted the first insertion (rev 1381174228). A second temporary account re-added it about three minutes later (rev 1381174504), and DonnieNova reverted that within seconds. The first account then added Tyler, the Creator as a "notable former pupil" (rev 1381174546), which is false. As of the last data I have, nobody had reverted that line. None of the edits gives a source or points to anything that happened in the real world. This is typical schoolkid vandalism, probably pupils sharing an in-joke, not a news event.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Czech Wikipedia's 'Cyril' name page, reverted by patroller within minutes
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The Czech Wikipedia page for the given name "Cyril" was hit by a short burst of joke edits. The account "JokerVeVězení67" ("Joker in prison 67") rewrote the opening to say a "Churaq Cyril" is a Czech rapper "in prison with Joker" (rev 26313427). A temporary account then added a made-up lawyer "David Kala" and the hashtag #FREECYRIL (rev 26313433). The first account came back and swapped the article's whole introduction for a line accusing a named private person, "Daniel Solik", of being a sexual predator (rev 26313434). That's a possible attack on a real person, which the oversight team may want to look at. About four minutes after the first edit, patroller OJJ used TwinkleGlobal to restore the last clean bot version (rev 26313436). The dossier's revert flags missed this rollback, and the Scout's "restructuring" guess was wrong. Nothing suggests a real-world event: no other languages were involved, and both vandal accounts edited only this page.

briefs.headline: Jackson Goldstone page: single test-edit vandalism reverted, no news signal
briefs.summary: A temporary account (~2026-56307-54) put the Czech word "ahoj" ("hi") at the start of the lead of the English article on Canadian downhill mountain biker Jackson Goldstone. Its edit summary, "dopsal jsem ahoj", means "I added hi". Komethere reverted it as vandalism with VandalHandle about 40 seconds later. VocalCat2207 then removed a stray leading space in the bolded name, which is cosmetic cleanup. None of the edits changed any facts: the lead still lists his 2021 junior world title, his 2022 junior World Cup overall title and his 2025 World Championship win in Champéry. There was only one page, no other languages, and no sign of a real-world event behind the edits.

briefs.headline: Jackson Goldstone page: no new edits since the reverted "ahoj" test edit
briefs.summary: This update adds nothing new. The same three edits from the earlier brief are the only activity, and the graph shows no edits after rev 1381293718. A temporary account (~2026-56307-54) put the Czech word "ahoj" ("hi") into the bolded name in the lead (rev 1381293632; edit summary "dopsal jsem ahoj", "I added hi"). Komethere reverted it as vandalism about 40 seconds later. VocalCat2207 then removed a leftover leading space from the bolded name (rev 1381293718), which only changes formatting. The article's facts didn't change, including his 2021 junior world title, his 2022 junior World Cup overall title and his 2025 World Championship win in Champéry. The activity stayed on one page in one language, with no sign of a real-world event behind it.

briefs.headline: De-wiki: Account removes JJ's Israel-ESC remarks as "harmful to artist"; quickly restored
briefs.summary: An account called "Manifester Music", on its first and only edit, deleted the whole sourced section "Kritik an der Teilnahme Israels" from the German article on Johannes Pietsch (JJ, the 2025 Eurovision winner). The edit summary was "Schadet dem Künstler" ("harms the artist"). The deleted text covered his May 2025 call to exclude Israel from ESC 2026, his comparison of Gaza with Russia's invasion of Ukraine, criticism from Austrian officials including Van der Bellen and the IKG, and his partial apology. It cited Der Standard, Die Zeit, Kurier, ORF and others. Two minutes later, experienced editor Brettchenweber reverted it, saying that harm to the artist is not a reason to remove content. Ailura then made an 11-byte copyedit to the restored section. The account's name and edit summary point to a possible conflict of interest (management or label whitewashing), but I can't confirm who is behind it. There's no new real-world event here, and the large churn number is just the one deletion plus its undo. I didn't read the revert diff itself; its effect comes from its edit summary and the matching ±2657 bytes.

briefs.headline: Argentine actor Antonio Grimau reported dead at 82, per es-wiki edits
briefs.summary: Three separate editors updated the Spanish Wikipedia biography of Argentine actor Antonio Grimau (Antonio Rebolini, born 1944 in Lanús) within roughly 20 minutes to record his death. Wledao added a death date of 20 October 2026 (age 82) and later a place of death, Buenos Aires (rev 175917431, 175917586). A temporary account changed the lead to "1944–20 de octubre de 2026" (175917542). Ezarate, the most active of the three, added the current-event "fallecimiento" template with the comment "fallecio hoy" (175917719). None of the diffs I read added a source. Wledao says this was their first edit. The edits agree with each other and nobody reverted them, but no other-language Wikipedia page has moved yet. Treat this as a likely death report that has not been independently confirmed.

briefs.headline: Nightcrawler article hit by twice-reverted infobox vandalism; not a news event
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not a news event or a real content dispute. In about four minutes, two accounts changed the infobox real_name field on en-wiki's Nightcrawler (character) article from "Kurt Wagner" to "Rainer Winkler". One was a temporary account (rev 1381218421) and the other a brand-new account, Luiz2212 (rev 1381218857), whose edit summary claimed in German that early X-Men comics give that as the character's real name. Both changes were reverted quickly, by Codename Noreste and then by Cannolis (rev 1381219017, "not providing a reliable source"), and the page is back to Kurt Wagner. The two vandal accounts each have one edit and no other activity on the graph. Two accounts making the same change with German-language framing could mean one person or a coordinated joke. "Rainer Winkler" also appears to be the real name of a German internet personality who has been the target of a long-running harassment meme, which could raise privacy concerns about a living person. That last point is outside knowledge, not something the edits show. Low significance: watch for repeats or similar edits on other pages, but nothing to report.

briefs.headline: Liberal Party of Canada lead blanked twice and reverted; Nightcrawler vandalism also undone
briefs.summary: The Scout read the 30,530 churn on en-wiki's Liberal Party of Canada page as a possible bulk edit. It is actually two section removals by one new account, both reverted, so each removal and its revert count twice. Harrylarrylivesinthequarry made both: rev 1381218018 removed 8,810 bytes with no edit summary, and rev 1381219722 removed 6,455 bytes with the summary "false information". Both diffs strip the sourced opening of the article: the party's name, its liberal ideology, its centre to centre-left position, and its standing as Canada's "natural governing party". Cannolis reverted the first ("unexplained content removal") and Alpha Beta Delta Lambda reverted the second through the Interceptor anti-vandalism tool. The page is restored, and the account has only these 2 edits. The second item in this story, already covered, was the infobox vandalism on Nightcrawler (character): the real name was twice changed to "Rainer Winkler" and twice reverted. Neither page shows a real-world event. These revert flags were not set, but the edit summaries make clear the edits were reverts. Nobody links the two pages except Cannolis, who patrols for vandalism. Watch only for more removals by the same account.

briefs.headline: Catalan Wikipedia PSOE article vandalised by look-alike accounts, now reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Over about 10 minutes, two accounts with near-identical names ("Raul ayudas y becas" and "Raul becas y ayudas"), likely the same person, vandalised the Catalan Wikipedia article on PSOE. Rev 38981174 replaced the Ideology section's text on PSOE's purpose and its UGT ties with paragraphs about the Falange Española. Rev 38981179 changed the party's Spanish name in the lead to the slur "Partido Sexista Opresor Euskadi". Later edits, including 38981182, swapped in a vulgar version of the acronym ("Pvtas Sobre(s) Orgías Españolas"). Editor Docosong rolled back the last account's edits, then fully restored the original lead and Ideology text in 38981212 ("rv vandalisme"). Nothing similar showed up on the same article in other languages in this window. It doesn't point to any real-world event. Low priority; watch for the accounts coming back.

briefs.headline: New itwiki article on Robert Hatem, ex-Hobeika bodyguard and author; no news hook
briefs.summary: Stefantiz created a new Italian Wikipedia biography of Robert Maroun Hatem ("Cobra"). Hatem was a Lebanese Forces militiaman and bodyguard to Elie Hobeika, and wrote the 1999 book "From Israel to Damascus", which Lebanon banned. The article draws only on historical sources from 1999–2000 (The Nation, Middle East Quarterly, CPJ). It covers the book ban and the legal cases brought against journalists, including publisher Milhem Karam. Nothing in it points to a current event: no appointment, death, arrest or other recent development. The edits that followed were small cleanups: Stefantiz expanded the Bio template and added an approximate birth year of 1956, AndreA made a minor fix with the edit summary "epoca", and Lulo tidied the lead. There were no reverts. The page has no linked articles in other languages in the graph, and none of the editors worked on related pages. This looks like an ordinary new article, though we can't rule out that something offline prompted it.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Swedish Wikipedia list of Finnish islands; page blanking not yet reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not a news event. All the activity is on one page, svwiki "Lista över öar i Finland", and comes from two temporary accounts plus one established patroller. Temporary account ~2026-56229-96 first replaced the Kimitoön row with a broken row and the made-up entry "Lilla kimitoön" (rev 59785602). A second temporary account added a joke row with an area of "Lite mer än 5" ("a little more than 5"), "Kimito" and "Hav" ("sea") (rev 59785616). Patroller Tekannan rolled back the second account and then reverted the first (rev 59785624). After that, ~2026-56229-96 deleted the whole island table, more than 20 rows (rev 59785629), then the intro text (rev 59785631), then made one more removal (rev 59785633, not read). In the data I have, none of these deletions has been reverted, so the page may still be largely blank, though patrollers will probably restore it soon. Both temporary accounts targeting Kimitoön suggests the same person or a local prank, but I can't confirm that. No other languages or pages are involved.

briefs.headline: JAXA's MMX Phobos sample-return probe launched on H3; en-wiki article cleaned up after launch
briefs.summary: The English article on JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) already says the probe launched on 19 October 2026 at 19:41:03 UTC (20 Oct, 04:41 JST) from Tanegashima. It also says the launch vehicle flew as planned and spacecraft separation was confirmed. The cited sources are a JAXA launch-result press release, NASASpaceFlight and The Japan Times. The six edits in this window, made about a day after liftoff, are tidy-up work around that milestone, not new events. RickyCourtney named the rocket as an H3-24L (JAXA calls the flight H3 F10). Chattenoir added references for the instruments and spacecraft mass, and cut a long, off-topic Asterix aside in the IDEFIX rover section. Animalculum moved text around to create a History section. The one revert was Chattenoir undoing their own edit to fix a reference error, so this is not an edit war or vandalism. The edit that first added the launch text happened before this window and I did not read it. The graph shows no other-language versions of this page, so the launch rests on what the en-wiki article says and the sources it cites; I could not check it independently.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on mn-wiki's The MongolZ and 'Information' pages, reverted in minutes
briefs.summary: This is a short vandalism spree on Mongolian Wikipedia, not a news event. One temporary account (~2026-56126-27) made three edits in about four minutes. It blanked most of the general article Мэдээлэл ("Information") and put in obscene Latin-script Mongolian (revs 873851, 873852). It also replaced the intro of the esports team article The MongolZ with insults and renamed the team in its infobox (rev 873853). About 8–10 minutes later, established editor Zorigt rolled back both pages to their last good versions (revs 873854, 873855). The "large edit" the scout flagged is that rollback putting back about 4.7 KB of the Information article. None of these edits contain anything about tournaments, roster moves or any other real MongolZ news. No other editors or languages were involved and there was no back-and-forth reverting, so there's nothing worth watching further.

briefs.headline: pt-wiki translates article on Germany's 2026 Merz government crisis; unrelated NGO page rewrite
briefs.summary: This is translation work on Portuguese Wikipedia, not a breaking signal. Editor Leirbag reib created "Crise do governo alemão de 2026" (+6,345 bytes, rev 73259806). It describes an ongoing crisis around Chancellor Friedrich Merz that started on 14 July 2026, after a personnel scandal involving Jens Spahn and a badly received reshuffle. The article says it worsened after the 6 September Saxony-Anhalt state election, where the AfD won 43.8% and the CDU fell to 17.2%. It also cites an INSA/Bild poll in which 14% thought Merz was the right chancellor. Sources listed include Politico, the NYT, Die Zeit/dpa and Reuters, all with access dates of 20 Oct 2026. Daniel G Rego then tagged the page as "in translation" (rev 73259852), so it is a translation of an existing article in another language, not a new event. The second page, Centro de Liberdades Civis, is unrelated: Daniel G Rego rewrote it from the English article on the Ukrainian Nobel-winning NGO (rev 73259761), and another editor made a small tweak afterwards. The only link between the two pages is that one editor worked on both. There are no reverts or signs of conflict. The crisis described is plausible and well sourced in the text, but I have not checked any of it outside Wikipedia. The graph shows no other-language versions of the crisis article being edited right now, so I see no fresh trigger today.

briefs.headline: US U-17 forward Maddie DiMaria credited with record 6 goals in 17-0 rout of Samoa
briefs.summary: Nothing new changes the main story. The DiMaria biography hasn't been edited since the last brief: it still has 4 edits, the latest at ts 1792503249. It is still the only page here with real-world news, a sourced six-goal game in the US's 17-0 U-17 Women's World Cup win over Samoa on 19 Oct 2026. Since the last brief there is one new edit, rev 1381179303 on Barbara Strozzi. In it, DonnieNova put back "believed to be of Barbara Strozzi" in the infobox portrait caption, which Mariavanaalst had removed, and asked them to dispute it on the talk page. That makes three reverts of Mariavanaalst by three different patrollers. It is a slow-moving fight over who the portrait shows, not news. The graph still lists no other-language versions of the DiMaria page, so there is no sign of wider coverage. The "record at any level" claim remains unverified.

briefs.headline: US U-17 forward Maddie DiMaria credited with record 6 goals in 17-0 rout of Samoa
briefs.summary: The only real news here is still the Maddie DiMaria update. Her en-wiki biography now says she scored six goals on October 19, 2026 as the US beat Samoa 17-0 at the U-17 Women's World Cup, citing The Athletic/NYT. Rev 1381176193 shows that sourced passage still in place. A 65-byte addition from a temporary account was reverted as unsourced, but the sourced text was left alone. The other two pages are in this cluster only because the same anti-vandalism patrollers (Celjski Grad, Materialscientist) touched them, not because of a shared event. On Barbara Strozzi, Mariavanaalst replaced the infobox name with a painting title ("The Viola da Gamba Player"), and Celjski Grad reverted it (rev 1381177777). That is minor disruption, not news. On the Charles III state-visits list, temporary accounts moved Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq's 20–22 October 2026 visit from "upcoming" into the main list, which suggests the visit is under way. Materialscientist then restored the "upcoming" table as an unexplained deletion. That is housekeeping about a long-scheduled visit, not breaking news. Still not checked: the "record at any level" claim and whether pages in other languages have moved.

briefs.headline: US U-17 forward Maddie DiMaria credited with record 6 goals in 17-0 rout of Samoa
briefs.summary: Nothing new changes the main story. The only real-world news in this cluster is still the sourced edit to Maddie DiMaria's biography: six goals in the US's 17-0 U-17 Women's World Cup win over Samoa on 19 Oct 2026. That passage has not changed since the last brief. The new activity is noise pulled in by shared patrollers (DonnieNova, Celjski Grad, Materialscientist). On the List of Jim Crow law examples by state, a temporary account renamed the "Oklahoma" heading to "jose is the best" (rev 1381178605), and DonnieNova reverted it. A second temporary account is making small, low-quality edits: stripping punctuation from a quotation in the Oregon section (1381178101) and adding a stray period in the Oklahoma section (1381178811). That is vandalism and sloppy editing, not news. On Barbara Strozzi, Mariavanaalst keeps changing the infobox after being reverted twice. The latest edit (1381178774) removes the claim that the portrait is "believed to be of Barbara Strozzi," a disputed-attribution question rather than an event. On the state-visits list, a temporary account added Oman to the table of countries that have made state visits (1381177298), which fits the 20–22 Oct 2026 visit by Oman's sultan. The visit was long scheduled. The "record at any level" claim and pages in other languages are still unchecked.

briefs.headline: US U-17 forward Maddie DiMaria credited with record 6 goals in 17-0 World Cup win over Samoa
briefs.summary: Editors updated the en-wiki biography of Maddie DiMaria, a US youth forward born in 2009. The new text says that on October 19, 2026 she scored six goals in a U-17 Women's World Cup match against Samoa, which the US won 17-0. It also calls this the most goals ever scored in a single World Cup match at any level. Benjamintchip added the passage (rev 1381174007), citing a dated article from The Athletic/NYT. The full diff was cut off, but the sentence appears in the page text that the next revision (1381176193) edits, and the only edit in between changed infobox fields. Chris1834 then raised her U-17 record from 10 caps/4 goals to 19 caps/18 goals, dated October 19, 2026. A 65-byte addition from a temporary account was reverted as unsourced by an anti-vandalism tool. I couldn't see what that addition said, but the sourced passage stayed on the page. This is a small, consistent, sourced cluster, which suggests a real sports result. Not checked: the 'record at any level' claim, the 17-0 score beyond the cited headline, and whether pages in other languages moved.

briefs.headline: Japanese Wikipedia: style dispute over Invicta title names on two MMA bios, no news
briefs.summary: The two pages share one subject: Virna Jandiroba (ビルナ・ジャンジロバ) and Yana Santos (ヤナ・サントス) are both former Invicta FC women's MMA champions. Two registered editors, Pikko 82 and TN Paak, were making formatting changes to both pages. Pikko 82 added "女子" (women's) to title names and shortened them to "IFC" (revs 111459603, 111459613, 111459628). TN Paak took "女子" back out and changed the label to "Invicta", explaining that "Invicta is itself a women's MMA promotion" (111459701, 111459723). In the latest edit, Pikko 82 adopted TN Paak's "Invicta世界バンタム級" wording in Santos's fight record (111459882), so the two seem to be settling on one style rather than reverting each other. None of the diffs I read add a new fight, result, signing or other current event, and no other language versions moved, so there is no sign of a real-world trigger. I'd suggest closing this or keeping only a low watch.

briefs.headline: Italian 'Maranza' article: brief, resolved dispute over 'racist' label for 'anti-maranza' decree
briefs.summary: Two established it.wiki editors argued over neutrality on the slang article 'Maranza'. One temporary account also made a small fix. There were no formal reverts. Sayatek added a paragraph saying Meloni-government majority parties picked up the term, and that one of the 2026 security decrees was nicknamed "anti-maranza". It cites Corriere della Sera (24 Jul 2026) and says this use highlights the term's discriminatory, racist side against second-generation people of North African origin, with support from L'Espresso, IDMO and a Il Fatto Quotidiano blog. Within about 10 minutes AnticoMu90 cut the 'racist' wording and the blog citation, saying Wikipedia cannot call a politician's decrees racist. About an hour later he put the wording back "come da richiesta" ("as requested"), which suggests it was settled on the talk page. Sayatek then restored the blog ref. That last edit also seems to have undone the temporary account's one-word grammar fix ("di") in the lead, probably by accident (edit conflict or editing an old version). The real-world facts were already known; they are not breaking news: the "anti-maranza" bill dates to July 2026. The page has no linked articles in other languages, and none of the editors worked on other pages. This is a routine NPOV disagreement that has calmed down, so we just need to watch for it starting up again.

briefs.headline: De-wiki attack page about a 14-year-old flagged for speedy deletion; no news event
briefs.summary: This is schoolyard vandalism, not a news story. A temporary account created the de-wiki page "Henry groß", which describes a 14-year-old boy in Saarland in mocking terms, says he is "weaker than Leon", and cites a Jimdo site as its source (rev 271499033). Established patroller RoBri tagged it for speedy deletion as "Zweifelsfreie Irrelevanz" (clearly not notable) about 5 minutes later (rev 271499346). A second temporary account then removed the "weaker/less intelligent" line, calling it insults and lies, but kept other disparaging text and left the deletion tag in place (rev 271500186). This looks like a dispute among teenagers playing out on Wikipedia. The page is likely to be deleted soon. Because it targets a named minor, we should not amplify it, and it needs no further monitoring.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on Spanish Wikipedia 'Iglesia católica' by one temporary account, reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. Over about 4 minutes, a single temporary account (~2026-55155-86) made three edits to the Spanish Wikipedia article on the Catholic Church. The first inserted "I am the king of Joseon. Arrest all users using wikipedia." The second inserted "I love Vandallism." The third deleted about 2.7 KB of the lead paragraph. Each edit was reverted within about a minute, by patroller Jcfidy for the first two and by the Automoderador bot for the third, so the article is back to its earlier version. The scout's "no reverts" flag missed this because the revert edits weren't tagged as reverts, though their comments say so. No papal or church event shows up here: the vandal's text doesn't mention one, the story covers only this one page, and there's no sign of related edits in other languages.

briefs.headline: Update: es-wiki 'Iglesia católica' vandalism burst fully reverted, no new activity
briefs.summary: This is an update to the tracked vandalism story. It contains no new edits, and nothing points to a real-world event. I listed every edit on the page in the graph: the "3 editors, 6 edits, 5,504 churn" burst is the same incident already filed. Temporary account ~2026-55155-86 made three edits: inserting "I am the king of Joseon. Arrest all users using wikipedia." (+57), a 16-byte insertion, and deleting the 2.7 KB lead (-2,679). Patroller Jcfidy reverted the first two and the Automoderador bot reverted the third, each within about a minute. The churn figure is simply each edit plus its revert (57+57+16+16+2,679+2,679 = 5,504). It looks like "no reverts" because the revert edits aren't flagged as reverts, but their edit comments say they are. The diffs I read confirm the vandal text, the lead deletion and the bot's full restoration. The page is back to its earlier version. Two other temporary accounts appear in the dossier's editor list, but no edits by them show up in the page's edit history.

briefs.headline: Rugrats pages hit by one temporary account swapping voice cast for rappers; reverted
briefs.summary: This is vandalism, not news. The cluster comes from one temporary account (~2026-56411-43), which made six edits in about 13 minutes to Tommy Pickles, The Rugrats Movie and Rugrats: A Live Adventure. In the two reverts I could read, the account had replaced the real voice actors E. G. Daily and Tara Strong with the rappers Young Jeezy and Rick Ross, including a made-up 'credited as ... Rozay' line. Three other editors (Staticspector, CantReadRunes and a second temporary account) undid every one of these edits within minutes, so the pages are back to normal. The 'large churn' on the live-show page was a +328/+78 edit by the same account, reverted as a 'grammar mess'. I couldn't load that diff, but its timing and author match the spree. The Creative industries edit (Inara1989, +23 'description', reverted by Staticspector) looks unrelated and was probably grouped in only because Staticspector reverted both. There is no sign of real cast or production news, and no other-language activity.

briefs.headline: es-wiki Adelaide tennis page: one temp account's link edits leave broken markup; no news
briefs.summary: There's no real-world event behind this. The new activity is all from one temporary account (~2026-56281-91), working on two Spanish tennis-tournament articles over about 10 minutes. On Torneo de Marsella it changed [[tenis]] to [[Tenis|tenis]] (rev 175925044). SeroBOT reverted that edit about four seconds later (rev 175925045), so the scout's note that Marseille had no reverts is wrong, although the change itself was harmless. The account then made the same link change on the Adelaide page (rev 175925143). Its next two edits removed one closing bracket each (revs 175925153 and 175925166), which leaves the lead with an unclosed "[[Tenis|tenis" link that will break how the opening sentence displays. That looks like clumsy or test editing more than deliberate vandalism, but the article is broken as of the last revision and needs a fix or revert. The earlier edits by other temporary accounts were routine cleanup. That includes the -4 Palmarés edit (rev 175924312), which only resizes the Barty photo caption box. None of the edits add results, champions or schedule changes.

briefs.headline: es-wiki Sydney/Adelaide tennis pages: cosmetic edits, Adelaide link break self-fixed; no news
briefs.summary: This is still routine cleanup on the Spanish Wikipedia's Australian tennis-tournament articles, with no sign of a real-world event. The broken link my last brief flagged on the Adelaide page is fixed. In rev 175925172 the same temporary account (~2026-56281-91) changed the unclosed "[[Tenis|tenis" back to "[[tenis]]", so the lead displays properly again. The new activity is three edits to Torneo de Sídney, each from a different temporary account. Rev 175925713 (+523) adds photos to the titles section of four historical seven-time champions: Bromwich, Crawford, Court and Wynne Bolton. Rev 175925822 finishes a cut-off "ATP International Series ↓" table header. Rev 175925877 makes the same [[tenis]] to [[Tenis|tenis]] change seen earlier on the Marseille and Adelaide pages. Repeating that exact change suggests one person may be editing through several temporary accounts, but it is harmless and I can't confirm it. None of the edits add results, champions or schedule changes, and there are no reverts on these new edits.

briefs.headline: es-wiki Adelaide International page gets copyedits; no news event
briefs.summary: Five small edits from five different temporary accounts went into the Spanish article on the Adelaide International tennis tournament over roughly an hour. There were no reverts. The diffs I read are all cleanup. Rev 175924819 (+383) rewrites the lead to give the tournament's tiers (ATP 250 men's, WTA 500 women's) and notes that Barty and Keys each have two titles. Rev 175924921 splits the history paragraph into shorter ones and writes "$10 millones" as "diez millones" instead. Rev 175924991 fixes an accent, and rev 175924241 swaps the Barty photo. None of the edits add new results, champions or schedule changes, and the edit pattern doesn't look like an event or vandalism. briefs.headline: New ja-wiki article covers fan dispute over King & Prince's Kaito Takahashi using "#KAITO" as solo name
briefs.summary: A new Japanese Wikipedia article, 「＃KAITOを巡る騒動」 (the #KAITO controversy), was started roughly three hours before this check and has had about 10 edits since. It describes a fan dispute that is still going on. King & Prince member Kaito Takahashi (髙橋海人) released solo music from 5 October under the name "KAITO" and used the hashtag #KAITO. Fans of Crypton Future Media's Vocaloid KAITO, which has existed since 2006, objected that idol posts were flooding their hashtag ("tag pollution"). According to the article, Takahashi apologised on 15 October in a paid fan-club blog and asked fans to switch to "#KAITO_SALTBOY". Criticism continued afterwards, because he kept the artist name and the apology sat behind the fan-club paywall. The sources cited are Japanese entertainment and tabloid outlets syndicated on Yahoo! News (KAI-YOU, Shūkan Josei PRIME, Josei Jishin, SmartFLASH, Pinzuba), dated 7–19 October, and one edit mentions a Crypton statement around 5 October. In the diffs I read, editors are disputing wording: one stressed that the blog is paid, and another replaced "had kept silent" with "10 days after Crypton's statement". Going by edit comments only (I didn't read those diffs), one editor requested page protection and another added a neutrality tag. There are no reverts so far. This is a soft-news entertainment dispute, not a hard-news event, and everything rests on tabloid-tier sources. Activity could grow if the neutrality dispute heats up, but it isn't an edit war.

About 12 minutes later, experienced editor 10mmsocket undid all three as "unsourced / personal analysis" (1381278763), and nobody has re-added them, so this is not an edit war. Naming Burnham as leader implies a real change in Labour's leadership, but I found no sign of it elsewhere in the graph: no activity on pages for Burnham, Labour Party (UK) or Starmer, and no other languages moved. With no sources given and edits on one page only, this looks like speculative or partisan editing rather than a sign of real news. If Labour leadership pages start moving, it's worth checking again.

briefs.headline: idwiki: 'anti-Chinese' tag on Kalla, Fadli Zon pages reverted; no new edits since
briefs.summary: This is the same activity as the earlier brief. Nothing new has happened. User OnAir21 added [[Kategori:Tokoh anti-Tionghoa]] ("anti-Chinese figures") to the Jusuf Kalla and Fadli Zon articles. Henri Aja reverted both edits about five minutes later. OnAir21 kept adding similar categories elsewhere (Khmer Merah, Bersiap, Apple Daily, Taiwanese party pages). Henri Aja has not reverted those. This is a dispute over category tagging on Indonesian Wikipedia, not a sign of a real-world event. It touches biographies of living people, so it is worth watching only if OnAir21 re-adds the tag.

briefs.headline: Indonesian Wikipedia: 'anti-Chinese' category added to Kalla, Fadli Zon pages, then reverted

User OnAir21 added [[Kategori:Tokoh anti-Tionghoa]] ("anti-Chinese figures") to the Jusuf Kalla and Fadli Zon articles. Adding a label like this to living politicians without sources is a BLP (biographies of living people) sensitivity issue. I see no sign of a real-world trigger. It could escalate if OnAir21 re-adds the categories or Henri Aja reverts their other additions.

briefs.headline: Patroller links two unrelated pages: Hidalgo vandalism, Cavendish nationality dispute
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. The only thing tying the two pages together is anti-vandalism patroller HMSLavender, who worked on both within about 20 minutes. On Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, a single temporary account (~2026-56397-03) made four nonsense edits to the infobox. HMSLavender restored the Canadian wording, citing MOS:NATIONALITY. This is a small two-person back-and-forth over how to describe her nationality, not a sign that anything happened in the real world. Both pages are now back to their earlier versions. Worth watching only if the Cavendish dispute flares up again.

briefs.headline: Hidalgo infobox vandalism reverted; small Cavendish nationality dispute quiet
briefs.summary: This isn't a news event. On Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, one temporary account (~2026-56397-03) made four junk edits to the infobox, for example changing his service years from "1810–1811" to "2077-638384". A graph check shows no edits on either page since the last revert, so this updates nothing in the earlier brief. The citizenship point could come back if someone produces a source, but there's no sign of anything happening in the real world.

briefs.headline: Vandalism on es-wiki Caso Negreira and Reloj de sol pages; no news event
briefs.summary: This is low-level vandalism on two unrelated es-wiki pages. There is no sign of a real-world event. The 1,669 "churn" on Caso Negreira is not new content. It is one temporary account deleting the infobox (-828, rev 175919487) and SeroBOT putting it back (+828, rev 175919489). Before that, another temporary account had added "Hala Madrid." to the start of the lead (rev 175919243), which is football-rivalry trolling. Because SeroBOT reverted to that version, the "Hala Madrid." text and a suspicious name in the infobox's defendants list ("-Adrián pozo berenguer", which I couldn't verify and looks like an inserted private name) appear to still be live. On Reloj de sol, a temporary account renamed the "Historia" heading to nonsense ("67676767 mi moto alpina derrapante", rev 175919440) and SeroBOT reverted it. Then user G.r.gddd changed the same heading to "Historia 67" (rev 175919479), which has not been reverted. The two pages share only SeroBOT as an editor and look like they were edited by chance at the same time, not as part of one campaign. A human patroller should clean up the leftover vandalism.

briefs.headline: es-wiki Caso Negreira and Reloj de sol: small vandalism, some still live, no news
briefs.summary: I checked the earlier brief and found nothing new: neither page has been edited since SeroBOT's revert at ts 1792509455. On Caso Negreira, a temporary account put "Hala Madrid." at the start of the lead (rev 175919243), which is football-rivalry trolling. A second temporary account then deleted the infobox and changed the lead's first words to "." (rev 175919487). briefs.headline: Vandalism on German Amy Winehouse article reverted twice; no news event
briefs.summary: This is low-level vandalism. It is not a news event. A new account, Fuslimburgerotto (2 edits in total), twice added a mocking slang sentence to the lead of the German Wikipedia article on Amy Winehouse. The sentence, "Sie erzfitscherte an Alkohol", is joking slang for "she drank herself to death". Both times experienced patrollers undid it within about 20–25 seconds: first Horst Gräbner, then Serols using the anti-vandalism tool Huggle. The reverts were not flagged as reverts in the graph, but their edit comments and diffs show they were. The edits added no new facts, no other language versions were involved, and nothing points to an anniversary or news hook. Winehouse died on 23 July 2011, which the article already states. I recommend closing this.

briefs.headline: German Amy Winehouse article: slang vandalism added twice, reverted twice; no news
briefs.summary: This is the same vandalism incident already tracked, not a news event. A new account, Fuslimburgerotto, has two edits in total. Both times it added the joking slang sentence "Sie erzfitscherte an Alkohol" ("she drank herself to death") to the end of the lead in the German article on Amy Winehouse (rev 271487848, then 271487886). I recommend closing this and merging it with the existing story.

briefs.headline: Vandal swaps in joke names on Anonymous for the Voiceless page; patrollers revert
briefs.summary: One temporary account (~2026-55260-41) made five small edits in about five minutes to the en-wiki article on the animal-rights group Anonymous for the Voiceless. Each edit replaced "Cube of Truth", the group's street-outreach method, with joke names such as "Cube of Weed", "Cube of Kardashians", "Cube of Malware" and "Cube of People that need a spanking". Two established patrollers undid every change. T430s used the RedWarn tool and labelled the edit vandalism; DonnieNova reverted twice more, and the page is back to its earlier text. This is not an edit war or a content dispute: only one account was adding text, it gave no reasons, and the reverts were routine cleanup. Nothing here points to a real-world event involving the group, and no other pages or languages were touched.

briefs.headline: Anonymous for the Voiceless vandalism reverted; no new activity since cleanup
briefs.summary: This is the same set of 8 edits on one en-wiki page that the earlier vandalism brief already covered, and nothing has been added since. One temporary account, ~2026-55260-41, swapped "Cube of Truth" (the group's street-outreach method) for joke names like "Cube of Weed", "Cube of Kardashians", "Cube of Death eater" and "Cube of People that need a spanking". I read the diffs to confirm this. Patroller T430s used RedWarn to restore the last good revision and tagged it as vandalism (rev 1381203316). DonnieNova undid the account's last two attempts, the final one at rev 1381203696. A graph query found no edits to the page after that revert, and no other pages or languages were touched. It's one account vandalising and patrollers cleaning up, not an edit war, and nothing points to a real-world event. Unless the account comes back, this needs no more attention.

briefs.headline: ruwiki: anti-vandal bot twice reverts accurate Aristotle citation on Plato's Unwritten Doctrine
briefs.summary: This is not a news event. On the ruwiki article «Неписаное учение» (Plato's unwritten doctrine), a temporary account added a citation (+87 bytes) twice. The added text says Aristotle first used the term in the Physics (209b) and explains it in Book I of the Metaphysics. The anti-vandal bot EyeBot rolled it back automatically both times (ORES ~0.73), and a second temporary account then undid the bot's revert, putting the citation back. The scout's note is wrong on one point: the graph marks none of these edits as reverts, but three of the five are reverts (two by EyeBot, one undoing EyeBot). The edit itself is a sound scholarly correction: Physics 209b is the usual source for Aristotle's phrase 'agrapha dogmata'. It looks like an ordinary bot false positive, not vandalism or a real edit war. The two temporary accounts may be the same person, but I can't confirm that. If EyeBot reverts again it could turn into a small bot-vs-human loop, but nothing here points to a real-world event.

briefs.headline: Arabic 'Global warming' article: two low-quality edits undone by patroller
briefs.summary: This isn't news. On Arabic Wikipedia's الاحتباس الحراري (Global warming, Q7942), two one-time accounts made pending (unreviewed) edits. One (77035657) mangled the lead sentence by inserting the word "مرتفع" ("high") with no space before it. The other (77035702) garbled a lead paragraph: it added the word "الخبيثه" ("malignant") and repeated a phrase, and its edit summary is a schoolbook-style definition. The regular editor باسم (48 edits) then undid both pending edits at once, restoring revision 77015983 (77035731). The scout's note said there were no reverts, but the diff and edit summary show 77035731 is a rollback. The churn of 254 is just these small changes (+15, +112) plus the −127 undo; nobody changed any substance. Nothing points to a real-world event, an edit war or organised vandalism. It looks like ordinary well-meaning but poor edits, possibly from students, caught by pending-changes review.

briefs.headline: Temporary account re-adds Macedonian framing to Kole Nedelkovski page; second editor reverts
briefs.summary: This continues the Bulgarian–Macedonian identity churn already being tracked. After StephenMacky1 rolled back its first changes (rev 1381236661), temporary account ~2026-56256-86 went back to the Kole Nedelkovski article. It first changed the birth-name transliteration from "Krastev" to "Krstev" and the title "Mӑskavici" to "M'skavici" (rev 1381237196). About eight minutes later, under the summary "Just changed to the right things, without mistakes", it again removed the "Bulgarian" label from the opening line, re-added the unsourced relatives "Two brothers: Kiro, Slave" and added a misused native_name_lang field (rev 1381238040). This time it did not re-add the Macedonian language/ethnicity or the resting place. A different established editor, SuperFastSpellChecker, restored the last ZackBot revision with the summary "Rv unsourced edits" (rev 1381238303). That makes two reverts by two editors against one account that reinstated its changes once. This is a slow, one-sided push of unsourced national framing, not a two-sided edit war, and nothing points to a real-world trigger. No other languages or pages are involved. If the account reinstates the edits again, it could be reported or blocked for edit-warring.

briefs.headline: Temporary account's Macedonian-identity edits to two biographies quickly reverted
briefs.summary: Within about 10 minutes, one temporary account (~2026-56256-86) made three edits to two English Wikipedia biographies. Each edit shifted the national framing from Bulgarian to Macedonian. On Yoakim Karchovski, the account renamed the subject "Joakim" and changed "one of the early figures of the Bulgarian National Revival" to "the Macedonian national revival", leaving the cited sources as they were, including Sampimon's "Becoming Bulgarian" (rev 1381235783). On Kole Nedelkovski, it removed the Bulgarian-language label from the opening line, added "Macedonian" as his language and ethnicity in the infobox, plus an unsourced resting place and brothers, and changed the transliteration of his birth name (revs 1381236460, 1381236544). The edit summaries ("changed things to the truth") cite no sources. Established editor StephenMacky1 reverted every edit within minutes (revs 1381236661, 1381236695), and the account has not re-reverted, so this is not an edit war. It looks like routine unsourced nationalist POV-pushing in the long-running Bulgarian–Macedonian dispute over historical figures, not a sign of any real-world event. I did not read the two revert diffs themselves; their summaries and deltas match a straight rollback.

briefs.headline: Kole Nedelkovski page quiet after second revert; Pan Radio and Mantis reverts unrelated
briefs.summary: Nothing new has happened since the last brief. The last edit to any of the four pages was SuperFastSpellChecker's restore of the ZackBot version of Kole Nedelkovski (rev 1381238303). I read that diff. It takes out the unsourced "Two brothers: Kiro, Slave", the misused native_name_lang field and the "Krstev"/"M'skavici" spellings, and puts the "Bulgarian" label back in the opening line. Temporary account ~2026-56256-86 has not come back to either Nedelkovski or Yoakim Karchovski, so this stays a stalled, one-sided push of national framing rather than an edit war. The Pan Radio edit (rev 1381237449) is a separate case: a user rewrote the infobox to say the Bijeljina station renamed itself "SIM Radio" (founded 22 Dec 2023, website simradio.net) and cut the sourced 1997 founding date. The renaming may be real, but it is old news, and the edit was reverted as unexplained content removal. The Mantis edit, an unsourced change to the species count, was also reverted. Neither is linked to the Macedonian dispute, and nothing here points to a current real-world event.

briefs.headline: New it-wiki page 'Studio Tecnico Lux' tagged for speedy deletion as promotional
briefs.summary: This was not a company-page rewrite by three editors. It was one new page followed by routine maintenance. A first-time account (~2026-56252-17, 1 edit) created 'Studio Tecnico Lux' on it-wiki with about 5.6 KB of text. Its edit summary says the page gives background for an earlier article, 'Le Acciaierie di Cortenuova', and insists the author has no ties to any for-profit company. About 4 minutes later Saverio Grumaio added a missing-source tag (+27). Two minutes after that, Cipintina, an experienced patroller with 57 edits, asked for speedy deletion: "IMO voce pubblicitaria" ("in my opinion, a promotional page"). So I couldn't read any diffs, and everything here comes from edit summaries and graph metadata. The graph has no page for 'Cortenuova', so I couldn't check the related article. I see no sign of a real-world event.

briefs.headline: it-wiki new-page patrol: three unrelated new articles tagged by one patroller
briefs.summary: There is no news event here. The only thing linking these three it-wiki pages is the patroller Cipintina, who tagged each of them within about 12 minutes while reviewing new pages. The pages are: 1) 'Studio Tecnico Lux', created by a first-time account and sent for speedy deletion as promotional ("IMO voce pubblicitaria"). It appears to have been deleted already; an earlier brief found its revisions unreadable, so I did not try again. 2) 'Gregor Seberg', a new biography of an Austrian actor (born Graz, 1967) translated by Fonn Jacopo. Cipintina added an {{NN}} notability-check tag to it (rev 152995880). 3) 'Chiesa di San Paolo Apostolo (Como)', a new article with sources about the parish church in Sagnino, built 1989–94. Its creator expanded it, and Cipintina did a small cleanup. None of the diffs mention any recent event. This is routine maintenance.

briefs.headline: es-wiki self-promo bio of teen YouTuber 'Enix' tagged for speedy deletion
briefs.summary: The four editors were all reacting to one new page, not to anything happening in the world. A temporary account (~2026-56093-11) created the es-wiki article 'Enix (Progamer537)' (rev 175919941, +3.4 KB). It is a biography of a Spanish content creator born in 2007, with personal details like a sister's name, social-media handles and follower counts. Nearly every sentence is marked {{cita requerida}} (citation needed), and the only source is a youth-football profile. About three minutes later, VietwaveTo9791 tagged it for speedy deletion as promotional, criterion G3 (rev 175919964). General de brigada Antonio swapped that tag for a milder 'needs references' tag (rev 175920073), and Casisgaal undid that and put the deletion tag back (rev 175920089). That was a single tag swap and an undo, not a back-and-forth edit war, and the page will most likely be deleted. I can't tell whether the editor who removed the tag is linked to the page's creator.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia's 'Computadora' article hit by small vandalism, mostly reverted
briefs.summary: This is not a news event and not a rewrite. It is low-level vandalism and test edits on the Spanish Wikipedia article 'Computadora' (computer). One temporary account replaced the article's opening paragraph with the word "Yeruti" (rev 175920132, −850). The Automoderador bot reverted it within seconds (rev 175920135). Minutes later a second temporary account inserted "Yeruti" at the start of another paragraph (rev 175920162). That edit had not been reverted when this data was taken. Earlier, editor Jh38 undid a well-meant but unneeded change that expanded "(CPU)" to "(CPU(Central Processing Unit))". The scout's 1,732 churn figure comes from the 850-byte removal plus its restoration, not from new content. Three different temporary accounts were involved, which may be one person or schoolroom-style testing. I can't tell which from the graph. There is no sign of an edit war or of any real-world event.

briefs.headline: Spanish Wikipedia vandalism spreads to Sol LeWitt with antisemitic edits; reverted
briefs.summary: The Scout called the new 'Sol LeWitt' page routine, but it is part of the same es-wiki vandalism run by temporary accounts. The edits are antisemitic. Temporary account ~2026-56135-31 made three changes: it set LeWitt's art movement to "Diarrea" (rev 175920123), changed his religion from Judaísmo to "Nacionalsocialismo" (rev 175920184), and rewrote "a family of Jewish immigrants" as "nazis" (rev 175920231). Letstown undid these (rev 175920235, and rev 175920241, which put the infobox back). A second account, ~2026-56209-76, then re-added the same changes and also changed "of Jewish origin" in the lead to "nazi" (rev 175920288). The repeat by a fresh account suggests the same person switching accounts, or people working together. Letstown undid rev 175920288 in rev 175920292, which is the page's latest edit. I could not load that diff, so I'm relying on its undo comment and its delta (−6, matching +6) to say the page is clean. The graph's revert flag shows false for all these undos, which is likely why the Scout saw "no reverts". The earlier vandalism on Computadora, Björk and Ariel Miramontes (covered in prior briefs) is all reverted. There is no real-world event behind any of this.

briefs.headline: Vandalism by temporary accounts on three Spanish Wikipedia pages, all of it reverted
briefs.summary: Temporary accounts vandalized three Spanish Wikipedia articles: 'Computadora', 'Björk' and 'Ariel Miramontes'. There is no real-world event behind the edits. The 'Computadora' insertion of "Yeruti" (rev 175920162), which the previous brief listed as still live, has now been reverted by R2d21024 (rev 175920198). One temporary account, ~2026-56275-49, links two of the pages. It blanked the lead of 'Computadora' (rev 175920132, reverted by Automoderador). On 'Ariel Miramontes' it renamed the actor in the infobox to "Alejandro De Dios Cataño" (rev 175920178). It then made a second edit there that changed his birthplace to Perisur, changed his years active to "67", broke a citation and renamed his famous character Albertano (rev 175920215). Casisgaal and Letstown reverted both edits. On 'Björk', another account changed the singer's birth name to "Augusto Pinochet" (rev 175920112). Letstown and SeroBOT reverted it and a repeat. The Scout's call of routine churn underestimated these edits: they are deliberate vandalism, but small and already cleaned up. I can't tell from the graph whether the three temporary accounts are the same person or a group, such as a classroom.

briefs.headline: BBC to close BBC Three linear channel again; BBC Scotland, Radio 4 Extra also axed
briefs.summary: Editors on English Wikipedia's BBC Three article are adding a same-day announcement (20 October 2026) that the BBC will shut the BBC Three broadcast channel from spring 2027 and make it online-only again. This would be its second closure, after the channel went off air in 2016 and came back in 2022. The diffs say BBC Scotland (TV channel) and BBC Radio 4 Extra will also close, as part of a plan to save £500m over two years. They also quote Director-General Matt Brittin saying the brand will stay on iPlayer. The added text cites BBC News, Deadline, The Standard and The Guardian. There are no reverts. The churn comes from several editors merging duplicate "second closure" sections and copyediting the lead (ViperSnake151, -1044 bytes). It is not an edit war or vandalism. The BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra pages each got a couple of edits at the same time; I haven't read those diffs. Uncertain: the exact closure date. The diffs say "spring" or "next year" but give no specific date.

briefs.headline: BBC Three, BBC Scotland channels now listed as "outgoing" after closure announcement
briefs.summary: This updates the earlier brief. English Wikipedia editors are still writing up the BBC's 20 October 2026 announcement that the BBC Three linear channel will close for a second time. Benmathieson901 merged the closure text into a section now called "Reverting back to a Digital service". The merged text names BBC Scotland and BBC Radio 4 Extra as closing too, and adds "in spring 2027" as the timing (revs 1381224153, 1381224509, 1381224596). An editor without an account then changed the opening sentence of both the BBC Three and BBC Scotland (TV channel) articles to call each an "outgoing" channel (revs 1381226170, 1381226123). An earlier BBC Scotland edit by Abdullahi Mohamed 103 backs up the details: closure from spring 2027, part of cuts meant to save £500m, with the brand kept on iPlayer and Scottish programmes moving to BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland (rev 1381219612). The sources cited are still Deadline, The Standard and The Guardian. Activity is in English only, from a handful of editors, with no reverts. That looks like routine write-up of a real announcement, not a dispute. Still uncertain: no exact switch-off date, and I haven't read the Radio 4 Extra diff.

briefs.headline: One patroller reverts three unrelated low-level edits; no news event
briefs.summary: Three English Wikipedia pages are grouped here only because one recent-changes patroller, 420yeahh, reverted an edit on each within about 17 minutes. There is no shared real-world event. New since the last brief: on Balwyn High School (Melbourne), the account WikepediaDev108343 made three edits that added unsourced "notable alumni" who appear to be private individuals: "Luke Rizk - Basketballer", "Lucas Antonopoulos - Twitch Streamer" and a chef (rev 1381236513). One edit inserted self-promotion, "Follow lkings on Twitch", before that account removed the entries itself (rev 1381236998). 420yeahh then restored the earlier version, citing "No references provided" (rev 1381237473). The earlier findings still stand: a vanity tag on Twerking was reverted within about 100 seconds, and an unsourced lead rewrite on Yellowstone Schools was reverted as unexplained. I could not re-fetch those two diffs this round, so I am relying on the prior brief for them. Only English pages moved, and no other editors are involved.

briefs.headline: Patroller reverts two unrelated edits; one is a vanity tag, one a possibly real school update
briefs.summary: The only thing linking these two pages is one recent-changes patroller, 420yeahh, who reverted a single edit on each within about 15 minutes. That is not a shared event. On Twerking, a one-off account added "Created by Jillian Fardella" to the top of the article (rev 1381236753). That is a vanity tag, i.e. vandalism, and it was reverted about 100 seconds later. The Yellowstone Schools edit (rev 1381235402) is not vandalism. A temporary account rewrote the lead: "Yellowstone Academy" and "Yellowstone College Prep" become a "lower school" and "upper school", the secondary grades are now run "through IDEA", "African-American" becomes "Black", and the article now says a high-school building was added. No other languages moved and nobody else is editing either page, so this is routine and not a news story.

briefs.headline: Unsourced Allen Bailey death claim re-added by temp accounts, reverted again
briefs.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Allen Bailey, a former Chiefs and Falcons defensive end, got another round of unsourced death edits. Two separate temporary accounts were involved. ~2026-56311-61 changed "is" to "was" in the opening sentence (rev 1381267014). ~2026-56257-93 then added a death date of 10/20/2026 to the infobox (revs 1381267136/1381267217). GreyZoneLife reversed both changes about three minutes later as "removing unsourced death dates" (rev 1381267436). This follows the earlier cycle: Elirbosley added the same October 20, 2026 date, moved him into "2026 deaths" and wrote "Hearing that AB has died" (rev 1381263340), and Yankees10 reverted that for lack of a source. Across about an hour, four different accounts have said he died, all giving the same date. That suggests a report is going around, but none of the edits cites a source, nothing has happened in other languages, and established editors keep removing it. The death is still unconfirmed. No new edits have shown up since GreyZoneLife's revert.

briefs.headline: Unsourced claims that ex-NFL lineman Allen Bailey died keep getting reverted
briefs.summary: Within about an hour, three different accounts added a death date of October 20, 2026 to the English Wikipedia article on Allen Bailey, a former Chiefs and Falcons defensive end born in 1989. That date matches the day of the edits. Elirbosley added the death date and moved him to the "2026 deaths" category with the comment "Hearing that AB has died." Yankees10 reverted it, writing "can't just say someone died without a source." A temporary account (~2026-56257-93) then added the same date again, and GreyZoneLife removed it as "unsourced death dates." None of the edits cited a source, and Bailey has no articles in other languages to cross-check. Several editors independently giving the same date makes it plausible that a death report is circulating, but it is unconfirmed rumor until reliable reporting appears. The other page in this cluster, Wendy (singer) of Red Velvet, has nothing to do with Bailey. It got simple vandalism (a Young Thug photo swapped in, "Height: 6'1", a name change), which GreyZoneLife reverted. That editor is the only link between the two pages.

briefs.headline: Allen Bailey death date re-added a third time, now credited to teammates; still unsourced
briefs.summary: Temporary account ~2026-56257-93 put an October 20, 2026 death date back into the infobox of the English Wikipedia article on Allen Bailey, a former Chiefs and Falcons defensive end (revs 1381268360, 1381268472). This time the edit summary says "Several former teammates and colleagues have confirmed his passing." No citation was added. GreyZoneLife removed the date about four minutes later, saying reliable sources need to be cited before such a change (rev 1381268766). This is the third cycle of add-and-revert in about 90 minutes. Four accounts have now made the claim, all with the same date. The new detail about teammates hints that tributes may be circulating on social media, but that has not been confirmed. Bailey's article has no other-language versions to cross-check, and no established editor has accepted the claim, so the death remains unconfirmed. Eggs Benedict and Wendy (singer) are unrelated vandalism or churn, linked only through the patroller GreyZoneLife.

briefs.headline: Allen Bailey death date now cited to X posts and has not been removed; still unconfirmed
briefs.summary: On its fourth try, temporary account ~2026-56257-93 re-added the October 20, 2026 death date to the infobox of the English Wikipedia article on former Chiefs/Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey, this time with citations (rev 1381269095, +683, "sources posted"). The sources are two posts on X: one by Colin McCarthy (the name matches a former NFL linebacker, possibly a college teammate from Miami, but I have not checked that) and one by Farzin Vousoughian (apparently a sports reporter). Unlike the three earlier attempts, nobody has reverted this edit in roughly 18 minutes. Later, a new temporary account (~2026-56303-79) set "status = deceased" and added a "Died: October 20, 2026" line (revs 1381270145, 1381270285). MakaylaHippo1998 rolled those back as unsourced BLP content (rev 1381270300). Because a rollback only undoes the last editor's changes, the cited death date appears to still be in the article. Five accounts have now given the same date, and the claim is now tied to named people posting about it publicly, which makes a real death more likely than before. Still, social media posts are not reliable sources under Wikipedia's rules for living people, there are no other-language articles to cross-check, and I don't have the text of the X posts, so the death is still unconfirmed until mainstream news reports it.

briefs.headline: Allen Bailey death claim now cites four X posts from ex-teammates and KC media; not confirmed
briefs.summary: Temporary account ~2026-56257-93, which has pushed the October 20, 2026 death date from the start, edited the English Wikipedia article on former Chiefs/Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey again (rev 1381270478, +895). The edit puts "death_date=October 20, 2026" in the infobox and cites four X posts, all dated October 21: @JeffAllen71 (the Chiefs offensive lineman who wore No. 71 had this name; the edit summary calls him a Kansas City radio host), @Farzin21 (Farzin Vousoughian), @klseaboldt (Kurtis Seaboldt, Kansas City broadcaster) and @COLINMcCARTHY52 (Colin McCarthy, described as a college teammate). The edit summary also names Dwayne Bowe, Derrick Johnson and Cyrus Gray as former teammates who posted on Instagram/X. It tells editors not to remove the date "unless you have proof of him being alive" and admits there is no obituary yet. The diff adds the death_date line rather than just the references, so the earlier cited version was probably changed at some point. I couldn't pin down how. MakaylaHippo1998's rollback (rev 1381270300) removed only another temp account's "Died: October 20, 2026" line. As of the latest graph data, nobody has reverted the new edit in about 8 minutes. Several named people from Bailey's NFL and Kansas City circles all point to the same day, so a real death looks more likely than it did earlier today. Still, nothing comes from mainstream news, I haven't seen the text of the posts, social media doesn't meet Wikipedia's sourcing rules for living people, and there are no other-language articles to cross-check. The pressure-style edit summary also makes a new revert or edit war likely.

briefs.headline: Larva (TV series) vandalism: no new edits since last brief, page still restored

briefs.headline: Larva (TV series) page: joke character edits by one temp account, reverted twice

briefs.headline: pt-wiki Gaza War page: one user's disruptive edits reverted twice; no news

briefs.headline: Update: vandalism on Archbishop Sample page reverted; Ningning role-model line restored

briefs.headline: No new edits since last brief; Ningning Jennie line stays out, Hopepunk hatnote back
